Important Upgrade Notes for VCF 9.1 and vSphere Foundation 9.1
Upgrading your environment to version 9.1 requires a strict component upgrade sequence.
Follow the upgrade guidance based on your current environment:
Upgrading from VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.x or 9.0.x to 9.1
For upgrading from VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.x or 9.0.x to 9.1, see the following documentation:
• Upgrading from VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.x to 9.1
• Upgrading from VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.x to 9.1
Upgrading to vSphere Foundation 9.1
For upgrading from vSphere Foundation 5.2.x or 9.0.x to 9.1, see the following documentation:
• Upgrading to vSphere Foundation 9.1
Upgrading vSphere 8 and Aria Operations 8 to 9.1
As a first phase to upgrade your vSphere 8 and Aria Operations 8 virtual infrastructure to 9.1, follow the order of upgrade
and deployment procedures as described:
• Upgrading vSphere 8 and Aria Operations 8 to 9.1
Common Related Issues
Incorrect upgrade sequence results in errors. See the most common scenarios described in the following documentation:
• vCenter known issues
• VCF Operations known issues
• Licenses could not be assigned to vCenter, license assignment failure on VCF 9.1
What's New
Following are the key features and capabilities of VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1:
• Enhanced NVMe Memory Tiering. Hypervisor tiers active pages to DRAM and cold pages to local NVMe, expanding
effective memory capacity without additional DRAM and adding software-based mirroring and cost savings analysis.
• Extended vSAN Deduplication, Compression. Inline data reduction broadened across cluster types and workload
profiles, lowering raw storage footprint per logical TB. Adding dedupe support for data-at-rest encryption, and improved
compression.
• vSphere Elastic Provisioning (Zero Touch). Automatically bootstrap and configure ESX on bare metal servers using
network-based imaging (UEFI, HTTP/S) with no manual intervention.
• VCF Management Services. VCF 9.1 adds a common runtime and set of components that unifies the architecture of
lifecycle and operational capabilities: VCF management services. For more information, see Components in VCF and
vSphere Foundation.
• VKS and VM Fast-Deploy. Significantly faster deployment and upgrading of VKS and VM clusters using linked clone
technology, significantly improving operational agility and time to value.
• Simplified Container-as-a-Service. Self-service namespace provisioning with registry, ingress, quotas, and identity
inherited from VCF constructs; simpler, faster way to provision a few containers without full K8s management.
• Native Object Storage (Tech Preview). Self-service S3 object storage for developers, with IT keeping the guardrail;
deploy, scale, and manage object storage with the same workflows as block and file.
• Live Patching for ESX for TPM-enabled hosts. Patches applied to running kernel memory; VMs continue running
with no maintenance window, covering up to 80% of patches.
• Continuous Compliance Enforcement. Advanced Cyber Compliance now supports continuous compliance
remediation and unified security posture management for the VCF stack.
Broadcom 77

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• On-prem Ransomware Recovery. Integrated cyber recovery to on-premises VCF isolated clean rooms.

• SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 10 SP4: Terminated
• SUSE Linux Enterprise Desktop 12: Terminated
• Debian 7.x: Terminated
• Flatcar Container Linux 3033 LTS: Terminated
• Asianux 3.x: Terminated
• Asianux 4.x: Deprecated
Windows Guest OS Pending Reboot Reporting with VMware Tools 13.1.0:
With VCF 9.1, VMware Tools 13.1.0 adds a vCenter UI and API restart status indicator that allows you to monitor and
identify virtual machines with pending restarts after a VMware Tools upgrade. This status allows you to efficiently schedule
the pending restarts. For more information, see Monitor the Guest Operating System Reboot Status.
ESX New Features
Installation
Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) for ESX installation:
VCF 9.1 introduces Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP), using a secure UEFI and HTTPS-based network boot to provision
ESX images on hosts at scale. ZTP simplifies and modernizes the way ESX hosts are installed and prepared for VCF
consumption, avoiding the configuration of PXE infrastructure and the use of additional network services such as TFTP
configurations. With VCF 9.1, you can boot multiple servers from a single HTTPS URL using a static network configuration
on bare metal. ZTP serves as a forward-looking replacement for legacy Auto Deploy, which is deprecated in VCF 9.0. For
more information, see Using Zero Touch Provisioning.
Storage
RDMA Observability Еnhancement:
With VCF 9.1, you can use the command for packet analysis and the
pktcap-uw --capture RDMASniffer
tool to validate network readiness for RDMA-based applications such as vSAN over RDMA or NVMe
rdmaperf-uw
over RDMA. With the capability for native packet capture and the built-in utility, you can
RDMA Sniffer rdmaperf
troubleshoot RoCEv2 connections, verify end-to-end connectivity between nodes, and evaluate throughput and latency
metrics directly within the ESX hypervisor.
API
Guest Customization APIs:
VCF 9.1 introduces updates to the Guest Customization APIs, focusing on network configuration flexibility and improved
automation:
• For Powered-Off VMs:
– IPv6-Only Support: You can explicitly deacivate IPv4 to configure IPv6-only networking in guest customization by
both the UI and API. This capability avoids the need to maintain a parallel IPv4 configuration.
– Partial Network Customization: You can customize network settings by providing only network-related fields
to Guest Customization API. This capability streamlines operations by avoiding the need to supply the full
customization profile when only network changes are required.
• Expanded Account Management:
– Linux: Adds support for setting the root account password during customization.
– Windows/Linux: Adds support for resetting root (Linux) and Administrator (Windows) passwords on existing VMs.
– Script Execution: Enhanced support for executing customization scripts within Windows guest environments.
• For Powered-On VMs:
– Live Network Customization: The Guest Customization API supports updating guest network settings for powered-
on VMs. This capability facilitates real-time network changes without the need to power off the VM.
Broadcom 79

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
For more information, see Guest Operating System Customization.
ESX Host Client
Updated ESX Host Client:
VCF 9.1 provides improved experience in the ESX Host Client, similar to the vSphere Client, to manage compute, storage
and networking at the single ESX host level. The updated ESX Host Client provides full feature parity with previous
versions.
Snapshot Operations
Change Block Tracking (CBT) Enhancement:
VCF 9.1 adds an enhancement to CBT enablement that removes the unresponsiveness of VMs during snapshot
operations. The overall operation for taking a snapshot is not reduced in time, but the VM unresponsiveness is resolved,
as opposed to an undefined period of unresponsiveness for VMs with larger disks before the change.
Virtual Machine Management
Linked Clones of First Class Disk:
As of VCF 9.1, you can make linked clones of first class disk (FCD). You can use such clones for fast provisioning of
container storage volumes in VMware Kubernetes Service (VKS). For more information, see Linked Clone First Class
Disk.
I/O
Enhanced DirectPath for Operational Flexibility:
• NVIDIA Mellanox ConnectX-7 and BlueField-3: ESX 9.1 adds support for NVIDIA Mellanox ConnectX-7
and BlueField-3 with Enhanced DirectPath, delivering high performance for AI/HPC workloads in passthrough
architectures. This enablement elevates raw performance but also operational flexibility for using vSphere vMotion,
Storage vMotion, Live Patch, and Hot-Add/Remove virtual hardware.
• AMD MI350: ESX 9.1 adds support for the AMD MI350 GPU, with Enhanced DirectPath, advancing AI/HPC workloads
in passthrough architectures to deliver high-performance speeds for faster training and inference. This enablement
facilitates virtualization capabilities such as Live Patch, Storage vMotion, and Hot-Add/Remove virtual hardware,
and enhances operational flexibility. Strategic partnerships with Hugging Face and participation in key open source
consortiums (PyTorch, OPEA, UALink) ensures optimized performance and accelerate AI adoption.
Support for Intel NIC E825 for Xeon Gen 6 (Granite Rapids-D):
ESX 9.1 expands hardware compatibility by adding support for Intel NIC E825, which is integrated into the Intel Xeon Gen
6 (Granite Rapids-D) platform and functions as a LAN on Motherboard (LOM) NIC.
IOMMU Virtualization Support for AMD Hosts with DirectPath Devices:
ESX 9.1 introduces IOMMU virtualization support for AMD hosts with DirectPath devices to deliver significant performance
gains and near-native hardware access for critical virtual machines while improving security and memory isolation.
Security
Quick Boot Support for ESX Hosts with Confidential VMs:
With ESX 9.1, Quick Boot supports ESX hosts running confidential VMs, bypassing the time-consuming full power cycle
and firmware initialization required by a regular reboot. Quick Boot support speeds up maintenance operations and
significantly reduces the upgrade time for the ESX server.
User-Level Monitor (ULM) for Enhanced Security:
VCF 9.1 introduces User-Level Monitor (ULM) as the default monitor for all virtual machines. ULM completely
reimplements the virtual machine monitor (VMM) for ESX. The monitor is responsible for running your virtual machines
and significantly reduces the amount of hypervisor code running in privileged mode in the ESX kernel, hence reducing the
potential of guest escapes compromising the host.
General Availability for AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP):
Broadcom 80

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
With ESX 9.1, AMD SEV-SNP for confidential VMs is general availability, after being introduced as a limited availability
release with ESX 9.0. AMD SEV-SNP provides a hardware-based Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) for critical
workloads, ensuring data integrity, confidentiality, and verifiable authenticity. The latest version of SEV-SNP adds memory
integrity protections to prevent hypervisor-based attacks like data re-play and memory re-mapping. The latest SEV-SNP
release also enables remote attestation to ensure the integrity of confidential VMs are not compromised. It is compatible
with AMD EPYC Zen 3 (Milan) and later processors. For more information, see Securing Virtual Machines with AMD
Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging.
General Availability for Intel Trusted Domain Extensions (TDX):
With ESX 9.1, Intel TDX for confidential VMs is general availability, after being introduced as a limited availability release
with ESX 9.0. Intel TDX provides a hardware-based Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) for critical workloads, ensuring
data integrity, confidentiality, and verifiable authenticity through attestation. It is compatible with Intel Xeon Gen 5 (Emerald
Rapids) and later processors, see Securing Virtual Machines with Intel TDX. For more information, see Securing Virtual
Machines with Intel TDX.
System Services
Improved Syslog Service Performance:
ESX 9.1 optimizes the syslog service, vmsyslogd, to handle a greater volume of logging messages for the TCP, SSL, and
UDP protocols, ensuring more efficient and reliable logging in high-demand environments. This enhancement delivers
improved performance and stability for system monitoring. For more information, see ESX Syslog Options.
Memory Tiering
Memory Tiering Configuration Enhancements:
• Simplified deployment: Memory Tiering configuration, including enablement and device selection, does not require a
host reboot, reducing deployment time and the maintenance window, and resulting in cost savings.
• Support for all VM types: ESX 9.1 removes limitations for the types of VMs you can power on in memory tiered host,
such as low-latency, security, and monster VMs.
Resiliency for Memory Tiering by Using Software RAID Mirroring:
ESX 9.1 improves resiliency for Memory Tiering by allowing for a mirrored device, without impacting performance. With
the enablement, if a device fails, the secondary device performs memory tiering to ensure continued operations. With a
second NVMe device using RAID1 mirroring, memory tiering cannot fail, regardless of NVMe device lifetime, reliability,
and wear-out.
vCenter New Features
File integrity monitoring capability:
VCF 9.1 adds a File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) capability, aligned with NIST SP 800-115, which detects changes by
malware or malicious actors to static files or binaries installed by vCenter. FIM is turned on by default and runs every four
hours to detect malicious or unintentional changes or corruption of the installed files . You can get a FIM report by using
API or stream FIM logs to VCF Operations by using the syslog service.
Pre-installed Logs Management Agent:
vCenter 9.1 comes with a pre-installed Logs management agent that pushes logs to VCF Operations and persists across
upgrades. For more information, see Configure Log Insight Agent to Send Custom vCenter Logs to log management.
Upgrade of the vCenter Virtual Machine Hardware Version to vmx-17:
With VCF 9.1, vCenter VM hardware version is upgraded from vmx-10 to vmx-17. For more information, see Manually
update the vCenter VM's hardware version in vCenter 9.1 and above if its updated from 9.0.
On-demand Pre-checks for RDU:
With vCenter 9.1, you can run on-demand pre-checks for RDU, similar to the regular vCenter patching pre-checks. For
more information, see Perform Upgrade Prechecks.
Automating Download of Payloads for vCenter Reduced Downtime Upgrade (RDU):
Broadcom 81

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
With vCenter 9.1, you can download payloads automatically by using RDU as opposed to downloading an ISO image and
mounting it for RDU workflow. For more information, see Download Updates from the Broadcom Online Repository.
vCenter Quick Patch:
With VCF 9.1, you can use the vCenter quick patches to upgrade vCenter with zero to 5 minutes of downtime. Quick
patches carry security or critical bug fixes and cannot be used for major upgrades. Based on the services included in the
patch payload, three groups of services are determined: zero, zero to 3 minutes, and 3 to 5 minutes of downtime. For
more information, see the section v Center Quick Patches.
vSphere Lifecycle Manager
Configure Global Remediation Settings for Clusters with vSphere Configuration Profiles Enabled:
With VCF 9.1, you can configure how ESX hosts and VMs behave before and during the remediation of a cluster that you
manage with an image and has vSphere Configuration Profiles enabled. For more information, see Configure the Global
Remediation Settings for Clusters That Have vSphere Configuration Profiles Enabled.
Integrity Verification of Customized and Exported ESX Images:
VCF 9.1 introduces validation of image integrity for customized ESX images. Large enterprises often customize ESX
images that require a review and sign off by internal compliance teams before use. Such validation ensures that the
image has not been modified and that administrators are consistently using the compliance-approved image. For more
information, see Verifying Image Integrity with SHA-256.
Skip Reserved VIBs During Remediation:
Starting with VCF 9.1, vSphere Lifecycle Manager improves remediation efficiency by skipping the transfer of reserved
VIBs that are not part of customized ESX images, saving bandwidth and reducing task duration.
vSphere Client
Memory Tiering Improvements:
With vCenter 9.1, the vSphere Client adds the following improvements for Memory Tiering:
• Memory pane:
– Shows tier 1 stats at host and cluster level in a summary page with a memory card.
– Streamlines the configuration at cluster level into a single flow that includes device selection.
– Enhances monitoring by plotting graphs with tiering-specific metrics.
• Cluster workflows:
– Memory Tiering cluster configuration allows for device selection and selection of Memory Tiering parameters.
Improved Interface for GPU Passthrough Devices:
With vCenter 9.1, the vSphere Client adds enumeration in human-readable form for GPU passthrough devices, simpler
names in English, and filtering capabilities to enumerate the passthrough device list.
VPC Transit Gateway, Traceflow, and Live Traffic Analysis available from the vSphere Client:
With vCenter 9.1, you can configure an external connection for a Transit Gateway, use Traceflow to inspect the path of a
packet, and get insight about tracing live traffic and bi-directional packet tracing by using Live Traffic Analysis (LTA) from
the vSphere Client. To provide complete VPC configuration capabilities, vCenter 9.1 adds:
• integration with external connections, which can define VPC connectivity policy. The Transit Gateway can connect to a
single centralized external connection or multiple distributed external connections.
• port mirroring (SPAN), which allows you to set up the range of inventory objects covered by the VPC network under the
same Transit Gateway.
• Virtual Network Appliance Clusters (VNAC), which enable VPC connectivity services.
• IP management capabilities for IP allocation and DHCP setup.
For more information, see Managing Virtual Private Clouds in vCenter.
vSphere Client Usability Improvements:
Broadcom 82

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VM tagging: When you create, clone or deploy a VM from a template, you can assign tags to the VM as part of the
workflow. Adding tags is a separate step in the Create VM wizard.
• Virtual scrolling: You can virtually scroll the grids of all managed objects, which prevents switching between pages to
browse object lists with large number of entities.
• Automatically adjustable columns in object lists: The column width for long strings in object lists automatically
adjusts to avoid text wrapping on multiple rows. You can switch to automatic adjustment and other options by using the
settings menu at the top of the Inventory tree section.
• CSV export of vCenter roles and permissions: From the vSphere Client, you can export vCenter roles and
permissions as a CSV file. The option is available for the global permission list and for the permission lists on inventory
objects level such as vCenter instance, cluster, and ESX host.
• Alphabetic order of all roles and permissions lists, including configuration views.
• Automatic propagation of user permissions: User permissions set for a particular inventory object are automatically
propagated to the object children by default.
• Alphabetic order of object selection views: In the OVF deployment wizard, objects are sorted alphabetically to
simplify configuration.
• 900 rows limit per page: In the consoles for tasks and events, you can increase the row limit to 900 from the default
of 300.
• Live refresh of the list of events.
Event Tracking:
VCF 9.1 adds an Event Tracking page in the vSphere Client, which visualizes the full sequence of events when an
ESX host fails and HA initiates recovery actions. The page provides a clear timeline that correlates ESX host failures,
failover decisions, restarts, and recovery steps, all in one console. For more information, see Monitor and Analyze High
Availability Events.
vCenter
Common objects identifiers between NSX and vCenter:
Starting with VCF 9.1, the maximum length of the object name is increased from 80 tо 255 chars for compatibility
Folder
with NSX network management to enable common object identifiers between NSX and vCenter. In previous releases,
NSX folder names could be too long for vCenter. For more information, see Folders in the Hierarchy.
Enhanced scalability in extra-large environments:
VCF 9.1 allows for up to 20% faster vCenter operations per minute. As a result, management tasks on virtual machines
and ESX hosts, such as power on/off, run significantly faster.
Content Library
Convert Subscribed Content Library to Published Local Library:
With VCF 9.1, to avoid loss of content in case the original published local library is not available, you can convert a
subscribed content library to a published local content library. For example, when you decommission a vCenter instance
that hosts a published library serving subscribed libraries, the capability allows a subscribed library on another vCenter
instance to convert to a published library, becoming the new content distributor and maintaining content availability.
Storage
VAAI-NAS support for Unmap with NFS v4.1:
VCF 9.1 supports space reclamation for VMs running on thin-provisioned NFS v4.1 datastores with VAAI-NAS Unmap.
For more information, see vSphere Hardware Acceleration on NAS Devices.
Increased Host Scale for NFS Datastores:
VCF 9.1 supports up to 256 hosts per NFS v3 or NFS v4.1 datastore. This enhancement improves storage flexibility and
allows for larger cluster configurations. For more information, see VMware Configuration Maximums.
Partner-supported NVMe stretch cluster solutions:
VCF 9.1 introduces NVMe dispersed namespaces which enable storage partners to validate and support NVMe-based
stretch cluster solutions. For more information, see Requirements for VMware NVMe Storage.
Broadcom 83

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
iSCSI support for the iSNS service:
VCF 9.1 introduces automated discovery, configuration and management of iSCSI connections with the Internet Storage
Name Service (iSNS) service. For more information, see Using iSNS with ESX iSCSI.
vSphere High Availability
Enhanced Failover Alarms:
VCF 9.1 introduces fully reworked logic for vSphere High Availability failover alarm that ensures accurate, stable, and
reliable failover notifications. In previous releases, HA failover alarms might intermittently toggle on or off, leading to
misleading signals about cluster health.
API
vCenter Support for OAuth 2.0 API Tokens:
With VCF 9.1, vCenter supports OAuth 2.0 API tokens, which help you manage API clients and emergency access clients
to support secure automation. For more information, see Managing API Clients and Tokens.
Tech Preview of FIPS API:
VCF 9.1 launches a tech preview of an API that allows you to retrieve information about the FIPS cryptographic modules
used by each VCF component, including version number, CMVP certificate, and CAVP certificate. For more information,
see Using the FIPS API to Query FIPS Status of Components.
Query API for Efficient Data Access:
VCF 9.1 adds a new Query API as extension of the already existing Search Index API that delivers a fast, flexible, and
scalable way to retrieve vSphere inventory data such as virtual machines and clusters.
The Query API enables:
• Server-side filtering based on user-defined criteria
• Efficient data access with pagination, property selection, and projections
• Lightweight, stateless queries without server-side state or client-side caching
• Entity counts and filtered results without retrieving full datasets
Designed for high-frequency automation use cases, the Query API simplifies data access.
Single, unified API endpoint for managing all vCenter instances in a vCenter group:
VCF 9.1 adds the vCenter group federated API (VGFA), a single, unified API endpoint for managing all vCenter instances
in a vCenter group. VGFA allows you to view and manage inventory across multiple vCenter instances as if they were
one, without changing any of the existing API integrations. VGFA becomes available with the configuration of VCF SSO
in VCF Operations. After activation, you gain seamless access to a consolidated inventory and operations experience,
consistent with the grouping capability under VCF Operations.
Utilization API:
VCF 9.1 adds Utilization API, which monitors vCenter capacity and usage metrics, including:
• The number of active connections compared to the maximum allowed connection limit.
• The endpoints through which these connections are established.
• The number of requests sent to vCenter services relative to the maximum request capacity supported by those
services.
Building on this API, new alarms are available in the vSphere Client. These alarms are triggered when:
• Active connections exceed a configured threshold, and/or
• Service request volume surpasses the defined limit.
You can configure threshold values by using Advanced Settings.
Snapshots
Enhanced snapshot operational efficiency and reliability:
Broadcom 84

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF 9.1 adds the following enhancements to snapshot operations:
• Resumable Consolidation: You can resume snapshot consolidation for powered-on VMs, eliminating the need to
restart the process from scratch if canceled. For more information, see Consolidate Snapshots.
• Disk Chain Integrity: New safeguards detect disk chain mismatches. In the vSphere Client, you see respective alerts.
The new safeguards block unsafe VM operations to prevent potential data corruption, while providing guided self-
service steps to resolve the issue.
• Capacity Planning Visibility:
With VCF 9.1, infrastructure admins can track the Max Data to Consolidate metric for better planning and resource
estimation for snapshot consolidation tasks. The metric is available in the Snapshots tile under the VCF Operations
diagnostics and in the VM file, under the parameter . For more information,
RuntimeInfo consolidateWorkTotal
see Virtual Machine Snapshots Health inVCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Metrics
vMotion Downtime Estimates with Enhanced DirectPath:
In vCenter 9.1, configuring a workload with an Enhanced DirectPath device provides you with increased visibility into the
estimated downtime for a vSphere vMotion operation, enabling better workload planning and management.
GPU Power Metrics for Virtual Machines:
With vCenter 9.1, the Advanced Performance charts include Power Capacity Usage - GPU metrics for real-time
insights into GPU power consumption at the workload level for virtual machines using NVIDIA GPUs.
Distributed Resource Scheduler
Intel QAT Offload for Encrypted vSphere vMotion Operations:
• CPU Efficiency: QAT offloads the majority of encryption cycles, reducing Source CPU utilization by nearly 67% and
reducing Destination CPU utilization by nearly 22%.
• Predictability: With QAT, you see significantly lower variance in 'Total Migration Time' and 'Oracle Performance
during vMotion' metrics as compared to the software-based encrypted vSphere vMotion that is sensitive to the
microarchitectural interference, including cache pollution, memory bandwidth contention, and scheduler jitter.
• Workload Performance: The reduction in microarchitectural interference due to QAT offload correlates to an 14%
increase in Oracle transaction throughput during the migration window.
vSphere Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) Enhancements:
• Optimized DRS VM selection logic to remediate CPU and memory contention faster, prioritizing the migration of high-
impact VMs and bucketing VMs to ensure that migrations directly address the most constrained resources rather than
defaulting to random, low-impact moves.
• Non-disruptive maintenance mode, which ensures that no workload disruptions occur during the host evacuation
process. Instead, DRS notifies you why a VM cannot be evacuated when a forceful evacuation can result in
performance degradation.
• Streaming vMotion Orchestrator:
– Streaming vMotion Execution: Removes the requirement to wait for an entire batch of migrations to complete before
starting the next to ensure that the migration pipeline remains at peak saturation, preventing a single slow migration
from stalling the overall progress.
– Adaptive Host-Pair Distribution (Progressive Pair-Sum): To prevent resource contention on key ESX hosts, a new
adaptive algorithm prioritizes the selection of distinct source and destination host pairs. By intelligently spreading
the migration load across all participating hosts in the cluster before loading any single host a second time, the
scheduler ensures balanced network and CPU utilization, reducing the risk of delays and NIC saturation.
– Dynamic Concurrency Control: You can move beyond the static cluster-wide limit of eight concurrent migrations.
You can use new advanced configuration options to fine-tune vSphere vMotion concurrency based on specific
hardware capabilities such as 25/100GbE networks and cluster size, enabling the system to scale throughput
linearly with the number of available hosts.
vSAN
This document contains the following sections
Broadcom 85

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• vSAN 9.1 New Features
vSAN 9.1 New Features
vSAN ESA Auto RAID 6:
In VCF 9.1, vSAN clusters use RAID-6 as the default RAID level. vSAN automatically configures RAID-6, removing the
need for manual selection and ensuring superior data protection without impacting performance. For more information,
see Selecting the Best RAID Configuration for a vSAN Storage Cluster.
Cyber Recovery vSAN Storage Clusters:
VCF 9.1 introduces a cyber recovery vSAN storage cluster that you can deploy through vCenter Quickstart. It optimizes
recovery from a cyber event using VCF Protection and Recovery and provides alerts to ensure that the cyber recovery
cluster is healthy and secure. For more information, see Deploy a vSAN ESA Storage Cluster for Cyber Recovery.
Seeding for vSAN Replication:
VCF 9.1 optimizes data transfer by using existing replicas to avoid full synchronization. When you create new replications,
this seeding capability saves time and bandwidth by syncing only incremental changes. For more information, see Use
vSAN Snapshots and Replication.
Tag Based VM Membership for vSAN Protection Groups:
VCF 9.1 simplifies administration by allowing you to define protection group membership using VM tags. This automation
protects new workloads instantly based on their assigned metadata, without manual intervention. For more information,
see Create a vSAN Protection Group.
Multiple Retention Schedules for vSAN Snapshots:
VCF 9.1 enhances retention management by allowing you to create daily, weekly, and monthly snapshot schedules. This
flexibility supports long-term cyber recovery strategies and day-to-day operational recovery needs. For more information,
see Create a vSAN Protection Group.
Cyber Recovery Using On-premises Clean Room:
VCF 9.1 introduces integrated cyber recovery workflows that use vSAN snapshots to recover from events. Baked-
in recovery processes, combined with integrated Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and vDefend push-button
network isolation, significantly reduce downtime during a security breach. For more information, see Using Cyber
Recovery.
vSAN Replication from Any Source Site:
VCF 9.1 extends vSAN replication to support workloads running on any storage by using vSAN ESA as the target. You
can now take advantage of vSAN replication capabilities such as dynamic protection groups, immutable snapshots, and
an integrated vCenter User Interface across a broader set of workloads.
vSAN ESA Compression Enhancements:
VCF 9.1 improves vSAN ESA compression to deliver better storage efficiency. You can expect increased space
savings compared to previous releases, helping reduce storage consumption without impacting performance. For more
information, see Using Global Deduplication and Compression in a vSAN ESA Cluster.
vSAN ESA Global Deduplication:
VCF 9.1 introduces vSAN ESA Global Deduplication, a cluster-wide and post-processing setting with encryption
support. Deduplication increases storage efficiency while providing data-at-rest security without reducing deduplication
effectiveness. For more information, see Using Global Deduplication and Compression in a vSAN ESA Cluster.
RWX File Volume Support:
VCF 9.1 extends RWX file volume support to VM Service VMs and adds support for multiple clusters within a single
vSphere Zone.
Fast Clone Volume Support:
VCF 9.1 introduces Fast Clone Volume support, adds snapshot and shared-disk capabilities for VM Service VMs, enables
non-disruptive VM migration to Supervisor Clusters, and allows storage policy updates by reprovisioning volumes from
snapshots.
Broadcom 86

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
CNS/CSI Scalability:
VCF 9.1 increases CNS/CSI scalability to 50,000 volumes per vCenter, supports shared-disk clustered workloads on
Supervisor Clusters, and adds unified monitoring of Persistent Volume Claims through VCF Operations.
Improved vSAN File Services Performance for SMB Workloads:
VCF 9.1 improves vSAN File Services performance, delivering up to 2 times faster metadata operations optimized for
SMB workloads. For more information, see vSAN File Service.
Clustered Applications Support on vSAN:
VCF 9.1 extends vSAN support for clustered applications and provides the capability to expand VMs with clustered disks
without shutting down the clustered application, such as WSFC or Oracle RAC. This capability supports both Oracle RAC
multi-writer and shared VMDK in Windows Server Failover Clusters. For more information, see Clustering Applications on
vSAN.
vSAN Stretched Storage Across vCenter Instances:
VCF 9.1 adds flexibility by allowing vSAN stretched storage clusters to provide storage across vCenter boundaries. This
includes sharing storage across workload domains within a VCF install or across multiple VCF deployments. For more
information, see Mount Remote vSAN Datastores.
Shared vSAN Storage Cluster Support:
VCF 9.1 allows vSAN storage clusters to mount and use both vSAN OSA and vSAN ESA clusters. vSAN compute-only
clusters can also mount vSAN OSA and vSAN storage clusters at the same time. For more information, see Sharing
Remote vSAN Datastores.
End-to-End Encryption for Disaggregated vSAN:
VCF 9.1 enables end-to-end encryption support for vSAN by providing data-in transit encryption between client clusters
and vSAN storage clusters. Combined with local data-in-transit and data-at-rest encryption, this capability fully protects
disaggregated vSAN deployments.
Site Maintenance in a vSAN Stretched Cluster:
VCF 9.1 introduces support for placing a site in maintenance mode in a vSAN stretched cluster. vSAN automates
promotion of the surviving data site and the witness sites during a site failure, enabling seamless data recovery. For more
information, see Manage the Site Maintenance for a vSAN Stretched Cluster.

Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Networking
AVI Integration: VPC and Distributed Transit Gateway (DTGW) with Distributed VLAN Connections
Broadcom 87

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
This release introduces support for AVI load balancers with VPCs and and Transit Gateways with distributed VLAN
connection. For more information, see the Avi Load Balancer documentation.
Distributed VLAN connection support for Supervisor and VCF Automation
By integrating the Virtual Network Appliance (VNA), we’ve added the essential services needed to enable Distributed
Transit Gateway for the Supervisor. This capability allows VCF Automation environments to connect to the data center
using only a simple VLAN removing the need for more complex networking prerequisites.
Enhanced NSX UI experience around VPC and IPAM
Due to importance of VPC for VCF networking, the following enhancements have been made for improved NSX user
experience:
• Extended VPC section with views per features (such as subnet and NAT) in addition to the view per VPC
• Full IP allocation and management workflow to ease IP management with IP allocation to services shortcuts (such as
NAT and External IP). For more information, see Assign External IPs to a VPC.
• Re-organization of the Networking tabs to clearly delineate objects leveraged by VPC Networking (like Transit
Gateway) versus objects that are part of Segment Networking (such as Tier-1s and segments)
Extend VPC and Transit Gateway consumption from vCenter
• Transit Gateway visible and fully configurable from vCenter
• Ability to extend Subnets to a VLAN in vCenter
• Full IPAM visibility and IP allocation mechanisms
• Extended Topology views and Traceflow available directly in vCenter for VPC VM
• DHCP server and DHCP relay options fully configurable from vCenter
Terraform extended coverage for Transit Gateway and VPCs
The Terraform Provider evolves in line with the new features added to VCF Networking by exposing new capabilities
available on Transit Gateway (multiple TGW, advanced connectivity options., and so on) and VPC (improved IPAM, VLAN
Extension, and so on). More details on NSX Terraform Page.
VPC Services: Load Balancer on Virtual Network Appliance
VPCs now support Load Balancer (LB) functionality through a solution deployed on top of a Virtual Networking Appliance
(VNA). Layer 4 (L4) load balancing service is fully supported and runs within this dedicated VNA ensuring scalability,
flexibility, and enhanced service isolation within your virtual network infrastructure.
VPC Services VPN support on Centralized Transit Gateway
IPSec VPN services support for VPC using centralized external connectivity - With VCF 9.1, IPSec VPN service is now
supported for VPC using centralized external connectivity enabling secure and encrypted communication across diverse
network environments. The release includes support for both Policy-Based and Route-Based (static route only) VPNs
offering flexibility to meet various connectivity and security requirements.
For more information, see Enabling an IPSec VPN Service on a Centralized Transit Gateway.
1:N SNAT service support for VPC with distributed external connectivity
VCF 9.1 added support for 1:N SNAT when using the Transit Gateway with distributed connection. This feature enables
multiple internal VMs to share a single external IP address through Port Address Translation (PAT), optimizing public IP
usage and simplifying outbound connectivity for workloads. For more information, see Register Add a NAT Rule for a
VPC.
Introduction of Virtual Network Appliance in VCF 9.1
VCF 9.1 introduces the Virtual Network Appliance (VNA) which is designed to run and support network services within
distributed VPC environments. This new appliance provides a flexible and scalable foundation for deploying advanced
networking services. For more information, see Create a Virtual Network Appliance Cluster.
VLAN extension for VPC subnets
VPC VLAN extension provides capability to extend VPC subnets to an existing VLAN in the fabric. It enables on-boarding
of VMs connected to DVPG to VPC subnets with a distributed VLAN extension. For more information, see Extending VPC
Subnet to VLAN and Onboarding DVPG VMs to VPC Subnets.
Broadcom 88

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Centralized Transit Gateway Advanced Connectivity Types
This feature delivers the following advanced connectivity options for Transit Gateways with a centralized external
connectivity:
• Provision of multiple gateway external connections per Transit Gateway
• Deployment of multiple Transit Gateways within a single Project
• Configuration of independent choice high-availability modes and flexible edge node placements for a centralized
Transit Gateway.
• Enablement of Proxy-ARP in Tier-0 for Transit Gateways and VPC subnets.
For more information, see Transit Gateways.
Multiple distributed Transit Gateways per Project
This release introduces support for multiple Transit Gateways with a Distributed VLAN Connection within the same
project. For more information, see Transit Gateways.
Distributed Transit Gateway with EVPN VXLAN connectivity
This release introduces Distributed EVPN-VXLAN that enables direct workload integration with EVPN-VXLAN fabrics
using BGP EVPN and VXLAN without centralized gateway appliances in the traffic path.
Forwarding is distributed closer to workloads and the BGP EVPN control-plane connectivity is provided by the VCF Route
Controller peering with the fabric EVPN Border Gateways (BGWs)—delivering improved scale, performance, and simpler
operational alignment across virtual and physical networks.
For more information, see External Connections.
Tenant networking support for services and multiple Transit Gateways
VCF Automation networking 9.1 allows a tenant to have:
• Distributed Connection to VLAN for both TGW and direct VLAN extension
• Multiple Transit Gateways with multiple connections
• Self Service NAT, VPN, Grouping, Firewalling (Stateful GFW and both stateful and stateless DFW require a vDefend
Firewall License)
• Create subnets shared across Namespaces.
Support of native Infoblox integration with VPC
VCF networking IPAM can now optionally integrate with Infoblox to:
• Discover Infoblox Network Views, DNS Views, and Network Containers
• Use Infoblox Network Containers to create subnets and update VM IP/FQDN information
You can configure the feature in NSX: pairing with Infoblox, External IP Block to Infoblox Network Container mapping that
can be discovered and used as VCF Automation External IP Block. For more information, see Register Infoblox NIOS DDI
with NSX.
Ability to define Span for Transit Gateway and VPC
The span of VPCs can now be defined directly from vCenter or from NSX letting VPCs be restricted to specific clusters or
have them span across all vCenter instances of the networking domain. For more information, see Add a Network Span.
New VPC Connectivity Policy
VPC communication can now be easily defined with a new feature, Connectivity Policy, that can group VPCs under the
same Transit Gateway which are meant to communicate with each other. Different grouping options are available, such as
communities of VPCs (for instance mapped to connected applications), isolated VPCs (for more restricted cases like DMZ
and the like), and promiscuous VPCs that host services and are connected to all other VPCs. For more information, see
Configure Connectivity Policies.
Edge Platform
New UI for Edge Node creation in NSX
Broadcom 89

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF 9.1 is introducing a new, user-friendly, and simplified UI workflow for defining Edge Node and Edge Cluster
configurations through NSX Manager. This enhancement streamlines setup and management that makes deployment
of edge infrastructure faster and more intuitive. For more information, see Create an NSX Edge Cluster and Add Edge
Nodes.
Broadcom 574X/575X and Mellanox CX6 LX support for BM Edge datapath NIC
VCF 9.1 supports Broadcom 574X and 575X and Mellanox CX6 LX NICs for Datapath of BM Edge. For more information,
see NSX Edge Bare Metal Requirements.
Edge Control Plane Prioritization
VCF 9.1 is introducing Control Plane Prioritization (CPP) on Edge Uplinks to ensure that all control plane packets
are prioritized. This enhancement applies to both RX (receive) and TX (transmit) packets, providing greater reliability
and stability for control plane operations. CPP is implemented for both the Bare Metal Edge (BME) and Edge VM
deployments.
Edge VM VLAN and MTU health check
As part of the new UI for Edge node creation and new UI for edge cluster creation workflow, VLAN and MTU pre-check for
the Edge node have been added. It validates that the VLAN and MTU configurations on the physical TOR switches have
been properly configured to ensure successful deployment of VCF Networking Edges. For more information, see Create
an NSX Edge Cluster and Add Edge Nodes.
Enhanced Data Path and Performance
FPO Hardware Steering for NVIDIA Accelerated NICs
This release introduces an asynchronous queue-based hardware steering engine to increase flow programming rates and
scalability for UPTv2 and Enhanced DirectPath I/O. This capability is available on NVIDIA Accelerated NICs (ConnectX-6
DX, ConnectX-7, BlueField-2, BlueField-3).
Uniform Passthrough (UPT) for Accelerated NICs
Uniform Passthrough (UPT) enables near line-rate networking performance through the standard VMXNET3 interface
by offloading the data path to NVIDIA ConnectX-7 or BlueField-2, BlueField-3 (NIC mode) hardware. This technology
removes the requirement for proprietary guest drivers and supports core features like vMotion making it ideal for high-
performance general workloads that require operational flexibility and simplified image management.
• Best Use Case: High-performance general enterprise workloads that require a balance of speed and operational
flexibility.
• Key Benefit: High-speed throughput without sacrificing vMotion or guest OS portability.
For more information, see Enhanced Network Offloads and Advanced NIC Passthrough.
Enhanced Direct Path I/O for Accelerated NICs
Enhanced direct path I/O (EDPIO) delivers the highest possible throughput and lowest latency by providing virtual
machines with direct hardware access to NVIDIA ConnectX-6 DX, ConnectX-7, or BlueField-3 (NIC mode) adapters.
This mode is specifically optimized for AI, machine learning, and distributed computing that offers support for GPUDirect
RDMA to facilitate high-speed direct communication between GPUs across the network.
• Best Use Case: AI/ML training, large-scale distributed computing, and high-frequency trading environments.
• Key Benefit: Maximum hardware-level performance and advanced RDMA capabilities for compute-intensive
applications.
Enhanced Data Path (EDP) Optimizations
EDP Standard features several deployment and performance enhancements:
• Improved Deployment: Utilizes an updated sequence to maintain data path up-time in multi-uplink environments
during orchestrated maintenance.
• Latency & Throughput: Adds posted interrupt support for lower VMXNET3 latency, enhanced multicast Fast Path
performance, and VMKAPI checksum offloading.
• Expanded Feature Support: Introduces SR-IOV for EDP Standard, RDMA parity with pkthandle, and LRO for Antrea-
based deployments.
Broadcom 90

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Platform Optimization: Optimized for vSAN performance via multi-world VMKnics and AMD architectures through
TLB optimizations.
GRE traffic scale for Cloud Service Providers (physical NIC and vNIC RSS Hashing)
GRE vNIC RSS hashing enhancements for Edge Node VM appliance improves the traffic scale. Inspection of the inner
packet will distribute the traffic among multiple CPUs that increases the traffic performance.
Platform Security
Non-Disruptive Certificate renewal for VCF components that consume NSX services
With VCF 9.1, VCF components that use NSX services have adopted the standardized Non-Disruptive Certificate
architecture that will allow them to maintain trust with NSX even when the NSX server certificates change.
RSA & SSH-ED algorithms support for NSX Backup and Restore
Experience better security and consistency as NSX Backup and Restore now support RSA and SSH-ED hostkey
algorithms. For more information, see Configure Backups.
Note:
If you wish to use ssh-ed25519 hostkey algorithm, configure NSX Backups from the NSX Manager UI/API only.
New password to be different from the old password in case of the Reset Password operation in NSX
Starting with VCF 9.1, a user cannot provide the old password during the Reset Password operation of a local account.
For information about resetting password, see Resetting User Passwords.
Make regular user accounts created by NSX internal accounts on ESXi
Starting with VCF 9.1, NSX no longer creates and uses the following regular users on ESX hosts for its own operations:
mux_user, da-user, nsx-user, and lldpVim-user. Instead, it uses special accounts not visible to users.
NSX Transition to Ubuntu 24.04 and Chiseled Containers
All NSX appliances have been upgraded to Ubuntu 24.04 that leverages chiseled containers to minimize the attack
surface, optimizes deployment efficiency, and simplifies patch management through a unified and enterprise-supported
stack.
VCF Integration
Workflow to make domains VPC-ready
In VCF 9.1, you can configure vNetworking service (Tunnel EndPoint - TEP) even if it was not configured initially during
creating or importing your VCF domain. You can also configure the default Transit Gateway as part of the default project.
Overlay service configuration in vCenter
In VCF 9.1, overlay Tunnel EndPoint (TEP) can now be configured directly from vCenter like other vmkernel NICs. This
provides a central place to configure all the services running on ESX hosts.
UI support for Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) on VCF workflows
VCF installer and VCF Operations offer the option to configure Link Aggregation Groups (LAG) with Link Aggregation
Control Protocol (LACP) directly in the UI.
Sharing NSX Managers between Management and Workload Domains
VCF Management Domain can now share NSX Managers with other VCF workload domains. This reduces the resources
to run NSX and the overhead for the NSX lifecycle.
Network Visibility
VDS IPFIX adopt ConnTrack module
Update IPFIX module (Netflow) in VDS to the ConnectionTrack-enabled module to improve performance and standardize
on a single module for all IPFIX implementations (DFW IPFIX, Switch IPFIX, & VDS IPFIX). As a result, IPFIX for uplink
port groups will not be supported. For more information, see Add a Switch IPFIX Profile.
Broadcom 91

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Network Observability
Port mirroring policy API support
This feature enhances Policy API and UI to support Local SPAN as well RSPAN. Policy API only supported ERSPAN and
Logical SPAN in prior releases. As a result, all SPAN types are configured centrally in one location. For more information,
see Add a Port Mirroring Session.
IP Address Management
IP Address Management (IPAM) for Cloud Consumption
• IPAM for Cloud Consumption: The IPAM becomes more flexible and powerful by extending the IP Block. It now
allows one IP Block to support up to 10 CIDRs, 10 IP ranges (from one previously), and to exclude specific IPs. This
allows to populate CIDRs and IPs without disrupting VPC consumers. If an IP Block to go to the Internet is full, some
new IPs can be added and consumers have nothing to change as it is the same IP block and same quota.
• IP Address Management (IPAM) improved Provider Control: It is now possible to share the IP Blocks to the tenant
while limiting the visibility on the content of the IP Block. For instance, it allows the Provider to share an IP Block
internet "Internet" to the Organization in VCF Automation with a quota of two IPs without exposing the Internet IPs
generally owned by the Provider.
• IPAM Allocation, Usage, and Visibility: The IPAM offers enhanced IP allocation and IPAM management capabilities
across the UIs consuming VPCs (VCF Automation, vCenter, and NSX)
For more information, see Add an NSX IP Address Block.
VPC Distributed DHCP Server enhancements
VCF 9.1 introduces automatic detection of static IP addresses that are now automatically excluded from the DHCP pool.
This enhancement ensures seamless IP address management by preventing conflicts between statically assigned and
dynamically allocated IPs, thus improving network stability and reducing manual configuration errors.
Load Balancer
Distributed Load Balancer decoupling from Distributed Firewall
The Distributed Load Balancer is now independently managed and decoupled from the Distributed Firewall (DFW). This
separation provides greater flexibility allowing users to configure and operate load balancing services without dependency
on DFW configurations. For more information, see Distributed Load Balancer.
Operations
SSH Login Banner Customization for NSX Appliances
An SSH Banner can now be configured on the NSX Manager and Edge appliances. Users will now see a configurable
message from their administrator before logging into either of these appliances.
VKS Multi-Interface Networking
Provide Istio Service Mesh for VKS workloads
Istio Service Mesh is now available at a per-VKS cluster level for Supervisor based workloads. Key functionalities include:
• mTLS between container workloads within a single VKS cluster
• Both Sidecar and Istio Ambient (Sidecar-less) modes are available
• All Istio Security and Traffic Management APIs are available
• Both L4 and L7 routing are enabled (Waypoint Proxy included)
Dual-Network support for VKS cluster
This enables any VKS cluster to be deployed with a secondary network interface (vNIC) as well as Pods within the cluster
to be deployed with secondary network interfaces when running Antrea CNI. Both VKS cluster nodes and secondary NICs
of Pods are mapped to VLAN or overlay backed subnets in NSX VPC. This addresses a number of customer use cases
such as traffic isolation from primary networks, multicast traffic to and from container workloads, direct access to physical
systems such as NFS storage.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Brownfield/Import
Out-of-band networking changes to not impact SDDC Manager
SDDC Manager now supports network configuration changes done directly in vCenter or NSX Manager to be
synchronized in its database.
Bare Metal Edge support in VCF import
In VCF 9.1, existing non-VCF deployment with NSX Bare Metal edge nodes can now be imported in VCF.
Installation and Upgrade - LCM
VDS support for VCP Autobootstrap
VDS capabilities and enhancements to support the NSX - vSphere Config Profiles integration.
Move NSX Edge/SVM Upgrades to the End of Upgrade Sequence to Complete Aligning NSX Upgrade Process
with vSphere
• Easier and faster upgrades - Consolidated maintenance windows for NSX and vSphere management plane and data
plane.
• Latest VMX version on your NSX Edges as part of the upgrade process. No post upgrade manual intervention or extra
reboot needed.
DPDK Upgrade to 24.11
Upgraded Data Plane Development Kit (DPDK) to version 24.11, bringing performance improvements, enhanced
stability, and support for the latest hardware and features. This ensures better efficiency and future compatibility for high-
performance networking workloads. For more information, see NSX Bare Metal Requirements.
Routing
Dynamic BGP Peering for Auto-Scaling applications
This feature provides dynamic BGP peering support on Tier-0 gateways and Tier-0 VRFs. With this feature, users can
define a range of IP addresses that will be used to determine when a Tier-0 gateway should establish BGP peering with
external routers. For more information, see Configure BGP.
Increased L3 Networking Scale
In this release, the configuration maximums for a number of aspects of VCF Networking (including L3 Networking scale)
has been increased. For more information about limit increases, see the VMware Configuration Maximums tool.
VCF Installer
This document contains the following sections
• What's New in VCF Installer
• What's New in SDDC Manager
What's New in VCF Installer
Starting with VCF 9.1, the following configurations are supported for convergence and import operations:
• Existing VMware vCenter 8.0 Update 3а or later environment with NSX Manager 4.2 or later, without manual
component upgrades.
• Existing VMware vCenter 8.0 Update 3а or later environment without NSX Manager, only by manually upgrading your
vCenter instance to version 9.1.
• vCenter instances without ELM and with existing NSX Local Managers that are part of an NSX Federation
configuration.
• If an existing VCF instance is configured to use dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) networking, existing vCenter environments
that use dual-stack networking.
Default Component Deployment
Broadcom 93

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Starting with VCF 9.1, VCF Installer deploys a default set of VCF management services components during new
deployment. The components included are VCF services runtime, fleet lifecycle, identity broker, software depot, Salt
RaaS, telemetry, and license server. This standardized deployment ensures that critical services are available from Day
0 without requiring additional configuration. For more information, see Deploy VCF Management Services and License
Server as Part of Upgrade to 9.1.
UI Support for LACP Configuration
VCF 9.1 introduces native UI controls for configuring Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) on vSphere Distributed
Switches. You can now configure LACP directly during the deployment of management domains in VCF Installer.
Previously an API-only capability, this feature also includes validation prechecks to ensure the physical network fabric is
correctly configured for LAG prior to deployment.
Auto-Generated Passwords During Deployment
To improve security during deployment, VCF Installer now supports auto-generation of complex passwords for system-
managed and break-glass accounts. These credentials can be retrieved post-deployment, reducing the risk associated
with static or shared passwords during the initial configuration phase.
UI Support for Flexible Network Configuration for deployment of VCF Operations and VCF Automation
VCF Installer UI now supports the deployment of VCF Operations and VCF Automation on custom network configurations,
including separate vSphere Distributed Switches (VDS), Distributed Virtual Port Groups (DVPGs), virtual private clouds,
and NSX Segments. For more information, see Deploying VCF Operations and VCF Automation on Custom Networking.
Integrated Planning Workflow
VCF Installer now features an integrated planning workflow that allows you to define your deployment topology and
component selection directly in the UI. Based on these inputs, VCF Installer generates a list of CPU, Memory, Storage,
VLAN, and FQDN requirements which are then validated against the target infrastructure to ensure resource sufficiency
prior to deployment. For more information, see Start a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance Deployment by Using the
VCF Installer Deployment Wizard.
What's New in SDDC Manager
Out of Band Operations
You can now perform the following tasks in vCenter without impacting SDDC Manager:
• Changes to vSphere Distributed Switch (add, remove, teaming policy, MTU, PNICs)
• Change primary datastore
• Changes to datastore
• Manual upgrade in vCenter
The following objects can be modified in NSX:
• Transport Zones
• Transport Node Profiles
• Uplink Profiles
Support for Dual Stack (IPv4 and IPv6) Networking
VCF 9.1 introduces native support for Dual Stack (IPv4/IPv6) networking for management and workload domains. For new
deployments, you can configure management or workload domains with either IPv4 or Dual Stack networking. For existing
environments, after you upgrade to VCF 9.1, you can configure SDDC Manager for Dual Stack networking, facilitating the
deployment of new workload domains in Dual Stack mode. For more information, see Configure Dual-Stack Networking
for SDDC Manager.
