VCF Operations UI Experience
VCF Operations now features an enhanced, intuitive experience structured around the functional pillars of VCF: Build,
Manage, Operate, and Protect the private cloud. All capabilities are aligned with these operational pillars.
UI Support for LACP Configuration
VCF 9.1 introduces native UI controls for configuring Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) on vSphere Distributed
Switches. You can now configure LACP directly during the deployment of workload domains in VCF Operations.
Previously an API-only capability, this feature also includes validation prechecks to ensure the physical network fabric is
correctly configured for LAG prior to deployment.
Workload Domain without a vSphere Cluster
VCF 9.1 introduces a new workflow for creating a workload domain without a vSphere cluster. The workflow deploys and
configures a vCenter instance and deploys and configures a new or joins an existing NSX Manager instance. You cannot
patch or upgrade the components in the workload domain before adding a vSphere cluster. All workload domains that
share an NSX Manager with a workload domain without a vSphere cluster cannot be patched or upgraded unless you add
a vSphere cluster to the domain without a cluster. For more information, see Create a New Workload Domain without a
vSphere Cluster Using VCF Operations.
Logging in to VCF Operations
While logging in to VCF Operations, use or FQDN.
https://<IP>
Build
The Build capability provides the ability to deploy and manage the lifecycle of your private cloud. It orchestrates the
complete platform lifecycle from the initial deployment, converging your existing infrastructure into the VCF private
cloud, to the ongoing lifecycle management of your private cloud by providing the ability to patch and upgrade your
infrastructure. Beyond deployment and lifecycle capabilities, this workspace acts as the central hub for managing software
binaries using the software depot and running lifecycle updates to keep the platform current. It also enables extensibility
by providing developers with access to APIs and SDKs through the developer center.
Broadcom 95

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Fleet lifecycle
In VCF 9.1, the standalone VCF Operations Fleet Management Appliance no longer exists and is replaced by fleet
lifecycle, a management component to streamline the lifecycle management of the VCF management components. The
inventory of the Fleet management appliance is fetched and leveraged by fleet lifecycle when the component is deployed.
The remaining functionalities, such as service registry, user imported certificates, certificate signing requests, and so on
are converged into VCF Operations 9.1.
The fleet lifecycle component provides a unified framework to install, upgrade, patch, backup, restore, and maintain the
various management components that constitute the VCF environment:
• Identity broker
• VCF Operations
• VCF Operations for networks
• Real-time metrics
• Real-time metrics store
• Salt master
• Salt RaaS
• VCF Automation
• Telemetry
• SDDC lifecycle
• Software depot
• Log management
• Migration service engine
• VCF services runtime
For more information, see Deploy Log Management, Deploy VCF Operations for networks, Deploy Real-time metrics,
Configure Backup Schedules for VCF Automation and VCF Management Services, In Place Restore of VCF Management
Services Components, Performing Post Deployment Actions on Components, Scale up VCF Management Components.
Domain lifecycle management
Optimized NSX Manager and vCenter Maintenance Window
You can schedule an update scenario that reduces the required maintenance window downtime. The vCenter reduced
downtime update (RDU) preparation stage is performed first and does not require downtime. Then, in the maintenance
window, the NSX Manager nodes are updated followed by the vCenter instance switchover stage. For more information,
see Perform an Optimized Upgrade of vCenter and NSX Manager.
NSX Edge Upgrades at the end of Domain Upgrade Sequence
NSX Edge clusters are now upgraded at the end of the domain upgrade process, following the upgrade of the
management domain components and ESX clusters. This reordering aligns the NSX upgrade process with vSphere best
practices, ensuring NSX Edges are upgraded on the hosts with the expected version. The NSX finalize process starts
after the NSX Edge clusters are upgraded, streamlining the maintenance window and reducing manual intervention. For
more information, see Upgrade the NSX Edge Cluster and Finalize NSX Upgrade.
Support for Imported Standalone Hosts and Single Host Clusters
Added support for the lifecycle management of standalone hosts and single host clusters.
Select Hosts during Cluster Upgrades
During a cluster upgrade, you can now select specific hosts rather than the entire cluster. If there are issues or errors
with certain hosts, these hosts can be removed from the selection and skipped during the cluster upgrade. For more
information, see Upgrade ESX to 9.1.
Improved Various Prechecks
Prechecks are now conducted using native VCF component capabilities rather than relying solely on SDDC Manager.
This enhancement includes support for vCenter Reduced Downtime Upgrade (RDU) prechecks following upgrade
configuration. Additionally, error and remediation messages have been updated, invalid or redundant prechecks have
Broadcom 96

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
been removed, and precheck results can be exported to a CSV file for analysis. For more information, see Perform
Upgrade Checks.
Component Versions
VCF centralizes version information and displays current and target versions for all supported components that are
managed by VCF Operations on the Component Versions tab. For more information, see Lifecycle Management in VCF.
Developer center
Prometheus Support for Management Pack Builder
Prometheus support is now added to the Management Pack Builder in VCF Operations. You can create your own
Management Pack using metrics from Prometheus Servers. This enables you to reuse your existing metrics and bring
them into VCF Operations without writing new integrations using the SDK. For more information, see Designing a
Management Pack Using Prometheus.
VCF Operations HCX
Support for VCF Operations HCX
Added support for the lifecycle management of VCF Operations HCX. For more information, see Deploy VCF Operations
HCX and Import Existing VCF Operations HCX to a VCF Domain.
SDDC Manager Scale
Manage a maximum of 5000 hosts per VCF Instance
• Per Instance level number of hosts scale support has been increased by 2x from VCF 9.0.
• You can now perform streamlined management of DNS, NTP at scale.
• Parallelization of operations has been enhanced, allowing for 256 simultaneous cluster upgrades and concurrent
workflows for domain creation and host commissioning.
• Revamped UI and API for brownfield imports and pre-checks to perform these operations in a scaled environment.
Manage
The Manage capability acts as the administrative control plane dedicated to maintaining fleet hygiene, governance, and
resource efficiency. It streamlines complex operational tasks by unifying certificate lifecycle management, identity and
access controls, and license entitlement into a centralized workflow. Along with fleet governance, it also provides financial
and operational insights through capacity planning and cost metering tools, ensuring the environment is both efficient and
cost-effective.
License management
Automatic License File Download in Connected Mode
If your VCF Operations is in connected mode, a new license file is now automatically downloaded to VCF Operations
every 24 hours. This keeps your licenses updated and you do not need to manually request license updates. If you want
to manually update licenses in connected mode, you can turn off this feature. For more information, see Change License
Updates Mode.
Override License Support
You can now assign licenses directly to individual assets that consume license capacity, such as ESX hosts and vSAN
clusters, if they are connected to a licensed vCenter instance. The licenses you assign directly to assets are called
override licenses. To assign an override license to an asset, the override license must have enough available capacity and
must be compatible with the license assigned to the vCenter instance. For example, you can assign a VCF license to a
vCenter instance, and VCF Edge licenses to some of the ESX hosts in that vCenter instance. For more information about
override licenses, see What is an Override License.
Aggregated License Usage for Hosts of Version 8.x and 9.x
License usage reporting is now unified for ESX hosts of versions 8.x and 9.x. The number of cores of ESX hosts of
version 8.x is included in the version 9+ license usage. With the combined view in VCF Operations and the Business
Services console, you can track your total license consumption. For more information, see License Usage Analytics.
Broadcom 97

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Operations License Server
Your licenses are now stored in a license server, instead of in VCF Operations. A license server is automatically installed
during the installation of VCF Operations 9.1. For more information, see Registering VCF Operations with VCF Business
Services Console.
Fleet management
Identity and Access Management
VCF introduces streamlined Identity and Access Management capabilities, enabling generic OIDC identity provider
support, centralized VCF level role assignments, and OAuth 2.0 API tokens.
• VCF Roles: Create custom VCF roles by mapping to specific component permissions. VCF roles can be assigned to
users and groups when you configure VCF SSO. For more information, see Managing VCF Roles.
• SSO-Centric Management: Manage the VCF SSO lifecycle at the identity broker level rather than from a VCF
Instance for better operational granularity.
• vCenter Role Sync and Remediation: Provision vCenter custom roles across multiple vCenter instances and
VCF Instances. VCF Operations automatically detects and remediates configuration drift. For more information, see
Provisioning vCenter Custom Roles.
• OAuth 2.0 API Tokens: Help users with appropriate permissions to generate standard OAuth 2.0 tokens for VCF
components. As an admin, you can also manage API clients and emergency access clients to support secure
automation. For more information, see Managing API Clients and Tokens.
• Migration from embedded to instance deployment of the identity broker: Support for the migration of the identity
broker from embedded mode to instance mode in VCF Operations. For more information, see Migration of Identity
Broker (Embedded) to Identity Broker (Instance).
• Migration from VMware Identity Manager to Identity Broker: Support for script-based migration of data from
VMware Identity Manager to identity broker. For more information, see Migrating VMware Identity Manager to Identity
Broker.
• IAM Settings: Allow administrators to define global limits for token lifecycle and security settings, and to enable or
disable entities such as the group. For more information, see Identity and Access Management Settings.
all_users
• Symantec Identity Security Platform. Support for Symantec Identity Security Platform as an identity provider. For
more information see, Configure Symantec Identity Security Platform as an Identity Provider.
• Generic OIDC: Supports any OpenID Connect (OIDC) compatible identity provider. For more information, see
Configure an Identity Provider using Generic OIDC.
Certificate Management
VCF Operations introduces comprehensive certificate management capabilities. You can now manage certificates for
VCF 5.2.x components in your environment, such as vCenter, NSX, and ESX hosts. In addition, you can now manage
standalone vCenter and ESX host certificates from version 8.0 U3 and later. Key functionalities in this release:
• User Interface: VCF Operations UI now offers improved functionality and bulk certificate operations.
• API support: You can now use VCF Operations API for third-party integration and automation of certificate
management for all VCF components.
• Expanded scope: You can now manage certificates for HCX and Advance Load Balancer.
• Certificate expiry tracking: You can now track intermediate certificate expiry for vCenter and ESX.
For more information, see Managing Certificates in VMware Cloud Foundation.
Password Management
VCF Operations expands password management capabilities. Key functionalities in this release:
• Password Policy: You can now manage account passwords across VCF components by using fleet or instance
password policies. A password policy defines password length, password complexity, account lockout, password
change interval, and password history.
Broadcom 98

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Expanded Scope: You can now manage account passwords for VCF 5.2.x components in your environment, such as
vCenter, NSX, and ESX hosts. In addition, you can manage passwords for standalone vCenter and ESX hosts from
version vSphere 8.0 U3 and later.
• Simplified Management: Password operations are now streamlined. Manual prechecks, previously required during
VCF Operations password updates, are no longer necessary.
• Enhanced Security: VCF Operations 9.1 no longer stores break-glass account passwords, eliminating the need for
password remediation.
• Integration Ready: VCF Operations 9.1 offers new APIs that allow you to integrate with third party tools, such as
Enterprise Vault.
For more information, see Managing Passwords for VMware Cloud Foundation Components.
Configuration Management (Earlier Known as Configuration Drifts)
Configuration management configuration templates are now available for vSphere Configuration Profile (VCP) enabled
clusters in VCF Operations. You can monitor, detect configuration drift, and schedule drift detection on ESX Clusters
across your VCF Fleet. You can also identify, view, and download host and cluster drift information from VCF Operations.
For more information, see Creating Configuration Management Templates for Clusters and Detecting Drifts and and
Downloading Drift Reports for Clusters.
Centralized vCenter Tag Management from VCF Operations
VCF Operations offers the following features:
• You can assign tags on any object across vCenter instances in your VCF fleet from VCF Operations.
• You can view and manage all your vCenter tag assignments across the VCF fleet in a single pane of glass in VCF
Operations.
For more information, see Tags and Categories Overview.
Fleet Settings
You can configure the following:
• Password Policies
For more information, see Create a password Policy for VCF Components.
• IAM Settings
For more information, see Identity and Access Management Settings.
• DNS and NTP Settings
– VCF Operations now has a consolidated interface for DNS/NTP settings configurations.
– DNS/NTP settings can be assigned at the fleet level.
– The global settings ensure uniform and consistent DNS/NTP settings across all components in the management
components hierarchy.
For more information, see Managing External Infrastructure Services for VCF Components.
Cost and capacity management
Cost Driver Enhancements
• Server Hardware Expense Management. You can now use the intuitive spreadsheet like interface to update
the server hardware cost drivers. You can also use the new fields and filters to manage multiple server hardware
effortlessly.
• Additional Cost Driver. Additional Cost Drivers now extend beyond VMs to clusters, hosts, and datacenters. You
have more options to capture your miscellaneous expenses. You can allocate costs using tags, performance metrics,
or fixed amounts.
• Customizable Cost Ratio. You can take control of your cost distribution strategy and define custom cost ratios.
This helps to determine how infrastructure cost is split between CPU and memory resources. You can also align the
allocation models with your organization's unique consumption patterns.
• VM Cost Visibility. You can now filter costs within the Organization and Projects Showback dashboards by specific
service types: Regular VMs, VKS, and DSM.
• Reclamation Dashboard. Use this dashboard for a detailed, centralized view of your cost savings achieved from
reclaimed idle VMs, snapshots, orphaned disks, and powered-off resources.
Broadcom 99

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Application Showback and Chargeback. You can view the total running costs of your applications and tiers, as well
as the corresponding charges for the same.
For more information, see Editing Server Hardware : Traditional, Editing Server Hardware: Hyper-Converged, Editing
Additional Costs, and Cluster Cost Overview.
VKS Cost Management
VCF Operations now delivers comprehensive costing capabilities across your entire Kubernetes ecosystem, including
nodes, clusters, vSphere namespaces, projects, and organizations. For more information, see Cost Overview.
Chargeback
• Upfront Pricing: VCF now delivers real-time pricing estimates when you deploy virtual machines and Kubernetes
nodes in VCF Automation. For more information, see Configuring Provider Pricing Details.
• Tenant Reports and Alerts:
– Immediate email notifications to tenants regarding capacity thresholds, pricing and other relevant information across
organizations and regions.
– Comprehensive reporting of infrastructure consumption, resource utilization, and cost breakdowns tailored by the
providers for tenants and delivered directly to the tenant’s email.
For more information, see Creating Notification Rules for Tenant in VCF Operations.
• Bill PDF Export and Emails: Streamlined billing communication with automated PDF delivery that makes it easier for
tenants to access, review, and manage their bills anytime and from anywhere. For more information, see Download
and Publish Bills.
• VKS Chargeback: VCF Operations now offers powerful tools to implement transparent, granular chargeback models
specifically for VMware Kubernetes Service (VKS) nodes in addition to the traditional VM pricing. For more information,
see Configuring Provider Pricing Details.
Workload Optimization
• Storage based eviction:
VMware Cloud Foundation now dynamically assesses your cluster stress and moves workloads across clusters. In
addition to the existing Compute stress, Storage stress can now be configured as a criterion for eviction and placement
of workloads in other clusters, using the Workload Automation policy.
• Network port group support:
Virtual Machines are now placed across equivalent port groups for All Apps organizations.
For more information, see Optimizing Capacity in VCF Operations.
Capacity Enhancements
• Enhanced Storage Capacity Visibility. Improved visibility into storage usage across vSAN, VMFS, NFS, and vVol
datastore types on clusters, hosts, and VMs.
• Multiple Recommendations per VM. Delivery of multiple, simultaneous recommendations, such as rightsizing and
snapshot reclamation, for a single VM regardless of its state (idle, powered off, or oversized).
• Automation Central Enhancements. Inclusion of idle and powered-off VMs when scheduling automated jobs for
snapshot deletion and rightsizing in Automation Central.
• Orphaned Disks Deletion. Identification and deletion of orphaned disks to optimize system hygiene and storage
reclamation.
• Exclusion Enhancements in Optimize. Options to exclude VMs from rightsizing and reclamation recommendations
based on property tags, VM age, and history, along with automatic exclusion of Broadcom appliances.
• Scale Improvements for What-if Analysis.Increased limits for What-if analysis scenarios to support up to 10,000
VMs and 200 TB of storage capacity.
For more information, see Optimizing Capacity in VCF Operations.
Improved Capacity Recommendations and Forecast
Updated capacity algorithms to improve the accuracy and explainability of forecasts and recommendations are available.
The configuration process for managing conservative workloads is simplified. For more information, see Optimizing
Capacity in VCF Operations.
Broadcom 100

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Operations orchestrator
Repository improvements for Python and PowerShell environments
You can now configure up to two repositories for your Python and PowerShell scripting environments. This allows you to
achieve a more efficient separation between development and production code.
Improvements to the default error handler
Previously, the default error handler workflow element could only catch and handle errors in the main workflow elements
of the workflow schema. With VCF 9.1, the default error handler can now also catch and handle errors in the default error
handler element itself. Users can also reconfigure the number of re-entries that the default error handler can perform
when it encounters an error. These improvements enhance the debugging and recovery functionality for workflow runs.
Configurable session timeout
Administrators can now configure the session timeout of the VCF Operations orchestrator UI in minutes. By configuring
a custom session timeout, users and workflow developers can avoid losing unsaved changes because of a short timeout
limit. This change is only applicable to external VCF Operations orchestrator instances. Session timeout for embedded
VCF Operations orchestrator instances is managed by VCF Automation.
Workload Mobility
Feature Deprecation
PhotonOS Based Appliances
Support for self-managed PhotonOS appliances in VCF Operations HCX is deprecated as of version 9.1.0.
Rationale: The NSX Edge stack offers superior performance and eliminates the redundancy of maintaining two
functionally equivalent network stacks. An automated migration workflow is introduced in HCX 9.1 to move PhotonOS
appliances to the NSX Edge architecture.
Timeline: Target for full removal is VCF 10.0.0.
Expanded OS Support
The following operating systems are now supported for Guest OS customization and OS Assisted Migration (OSAM):
• Guest OS Customization / Bulk Migration now supports Windows Server 2022.
• OS Assisted Migration (OSAM) now supports Windows Server 2022, Windows Server 2025.
Security and Compliance
• FIPS 140-3 Certification: HCX is now FIPS 140-3 certified, meeting rigorous security standards.
• Non-Disruptive Certificate (NDC) Management: New HCX Manager REST APIs enable managing HCX certificates
without disrupting client trust.
• Network Security: HCX ports are added to the Distributed Firewall (DFW) exclusion list. Standard IPsec traffic between
enhanced IX and NE instances.
VCF Integration and Management
• Lifecycle Management (LCM): HCX Manager is now deployed, managed, and upgraded via VCF Operations.
Manually deployed HCX Manager instances can be onboarded and managed from VCF Operations.
• VCF Operations HCX Management Pack: A new management pack is available for installation in VCF Operations,
enabling critical services like password rotation for local users and certificate rotations, log bundle collection. Note:
This pack is incompatible with the legacy vRealize Operations management pack for HCX.
• Identity and Access: Support for VCF Single Sign-On (SSO) and VCF Roles for unified authentication and
authorization on the HCX Manager Web UI and API.
Migration and Interconnect Enhancements
• WAN Optimization: Re-introduction of an efficient WAN optimization functionality embedded directly within the HCX
Interconnect service mesh configuration. This feature is exclusive to enhanced service meshes and is not available for
OSAM and HAV migrations.
Broadcom 101

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Local Site Migrations: Support for appliance-less migrations within a single vCenter instance with HCX Assisted
vMotion (HAV), enabling source and destination to be the same instance.
• Advanced Storage and Rules Support:
– Support for non-default storage policies in Cold migrations.
– Ability to select multiple destination datastores for a single virtual machine (VM), except for OS Assisted Migration
(OSAM).
• VLAN Network Extensions: Support for extending VLAN networks to native Distributed Virtual Port Groups (DVPGs) at
the destination.
• Enriched and refreshed Web UI.
Optimized Appliance Architecture
• Enhanced Architecture: A new, optimized enhanced architecture is introduced for HCX Interconnect (IX) and Network
Extension (NE) appliances, providing superior performance.
• Default for New Service Meshes: Starting with version 9.1, all new service meshes are automatically created using
the enhanced architecture. Existing appliances from previous versions will maintain their legacy architecture unless
migrated via the Migrating Network Extensions workflow.
Operate
Designed as a comprehensive observability hub, the Operate capability delivers a single pane of glass for monitoring
operational health and performance. It synthesizes critical information—including system metrics, logs, and network
traffic flows—to enable proactive troubleshooting and rapid root-cause analysis across the entire infrastructure and VCF
deployment. Additionally, it incorporates environmental analytics through sustainability scores, allowing organizations to
align infrastructure performance with energy efficiency goals.
Real-time metrics
Real-Time Data
The Overview page displays real-time or historical data for critical performance indicators—including CPU usage, memory
utilization, disk I/O, and network throughput—on the Overview page. You can configure the granularity of real-time
metrics, which defaults to 20 seconds, to as low as 2 seconds for ESX metrics via policy-based configuration.
• TopN Charts. Identify top-ranked objects, such as VMs, hosts, or datastores, based on specific metrics like CPU or
memory utilization.
• Custom Query. Use PromQL-based search queries to derive operational insights. You can also create and save
dashboards based on these PromQL queries.
• Flows. Explore and analyze network flows by traffic, volume, session count, or flow count.
• Actions. Execute command-line tools—including ipconfig, nslookup, iptables, netstat, tcpdump, route, arp, and dig—
directly from the Actions tab to identify and resolve network issues.
• Notes. Document your findings and insights directly in the Notes section during an investigation.
• Troubleshooting Session Lifecycle. Save your troubleshooting sessions as investigations to track their lifecycle.
• Collaboration. Share investigations with other users to improve collaboration.
For more information, see Real-time Data in the Workbench.
Findings
Log Assist enhancements
VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1 adds automatic log bundle generation for the following VCF components:
• Full support bundle for the VCF Operations cluster
• VCF management services
• Cloud proxies
• Log management
• Identity broker
Log Assist 9.1 also allows you to generate bundles for selected VCF Operations nodes, not only the cluster-level bundle
option. For more information, see Use Log Assist to Accelerate Your Support Cases..
Broadcom 102

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Public APIs for Findings
Starting with VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1, you can use a set of public APIs that allow you to integrate
diagnostic findings into your internal reporting and monitoring workflows such as risk management or ticketing. The
Findings API allows you to centralize monitoring of real-time findings or get data for trend analyses. For more information,
see Diagnostics Public REST API.
vSphere High Availability metrics in VCF Operations health and diagnostics
VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1 adds vSphere High Availability metrics that help proactive identification of
issues and preventive resolution from a single view that lists all high availability clusters with their operational state. For
more information, see vSphere High Availability Health in VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Organizations
Enhanced Monitoring of Organizations
This release introduces a capability to view details about Organizations that have been provisioned. The Organizations
page provides details of workloads created using the following managed services:
• VMware Kubernetes Service
• Virtual Machine Service
• Data Services
VCF health
Monitor ESX health and operational state with VCF Health
With VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1, you can monitor all ESX hosts in your environment, diagnose all aspects
of operation and performance, and proactively resolve issues. ESX Health under VCF Health summarizes the critical
issues that impact availability and connectivity of ESX hosts, grouped in the following categories:
• Reachability
• Connectivity
• Services Hardware (Memory and SSD)
• Purple Diagnostic Screen failures (PSOD count, active partition or dump file config status, and free space)
• Utilization
For more information, see ESX Health in VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Monitor vCenter health and operational state with VCF Health
In the vCenter health metrics, VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1 adds the following enhancements:
• Endpoint monitoring, replacing the ping reachable/unreachable check to the vSphere Client and APIs.
• Extends the list of vCenter services to 18 from 6.
• Adds the VM Operations Task ID parameter that allows a drill down to the backtrace of a particular task.
• Adds the Error Stack panel to analyze the logs in case of VM failure.
• Highlights VMs with fast-growing snapshot sizes and the biggest VMs in terms of snapshot size.
For more information, see vCenter Health in VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Monitor NSX health and operational state
VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1 provides the key metrics for NSX building blocks that help you track points of
failure to prevent overutilization and optimize performance in your system. NSX metrics in VCF Operations diagnostics
covers all operational aspects of the underlying infrastructure and appliances. For more information, see NSX Health in
VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Monitor vSAN cluster health and performance
VCF Operations health and diagnostics 9.1 gives you a single pane of glass for any vSAN-related monitoring, issue
detection, and troubleshooting tasks. Storage Operations is integrated with the Diagnostics capability to add value by
combining health scores and metrics with the means of accessing vCenter instances from the same screen. With the
combined capability, you can spot a negative health condition in the vSAN Health screen, follow up on the root cause and
Broadcom 103

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
take guided remediation steps in the vCenter instance. For more information, see vSAN Health in VCF Operations Health
and Diagnostics.
Log management
The following features have been added:
• Unified Log Management. Log management capabilities are integrated within VCF Operations, including log
masking, filtering, forwarding, partitioning, and the import of archived logs. Centralized agent configuration for efficient
management is available in VCF Operations.
• Upgrade and Deployment Support. Initial deployment of log components and upgrade paths from VCF Operations
for Logs 8.18 and VCF Operations 9.0 to VCF Operations 9.1 is supported.
• Centralized Log Configuration. Viewing and configuration of log collection across all VCF components is possible in
VCF Operations, eliminating the need for manual configuration on individual components.
• There is a standalone UI to access logs in cases where VCF Operations becomes unavailable. The log capabilities
limited to read-only with no configuration view, add, update or delete. For more information, see Accessing Logs when
the VCF Operations Console is Inaccessible.
• Analyse Logs. Log management features are natively integrated into VCF Operations console. To view and analyze
logs, log into the VCF Operations UI and navigate to Operate > Logs.
– VCF Operations supports searching and filtering log messages, performing analysis and visualizing search results,
working with alert queries, and dynamic field extraction from log messages based on customized queries. Navigate
to VCF Operations > Operate > Logs to view and analyse logs.
• Log Control and Filtering. Centralized options to manage log volume, including the ability to enable, disable, and
filter logs to suit specific environments, such as production or non-production endpoints is supported.
• Standardized Log Collection. Log collection processes are standardized by utilizing the Log Insight agent for
appliances and Fluentbit for Kubernetes environments.
• Scalability. You can increase the log management capacity by adjusting size and replicas. See VCF Operations >
Log Management in Config Max. Use the VCF Operations Sizing Estimator for the Log Management deployment size.
It is recommended to use total EPS (event per second) across all hosts from the existing Aria Operations for Logs
UI as the baseline for the upgraded Log Management. In the Aria Operations for Logs UI, go to System Monitor >
Statistics.
• Health Overview. The Log Management Health Overview dashboards are available to assist you in determining the
appropriate course of action when a system alert is triggered. Available dashboards are:
– Log Management Health Overview
– Log Management Health Drilldown (disabled by default)
For more information, see Log Management Health Overview Dashboard.
For more information, see Configuring and Analyzing Logs.
VCF Operations for networks
Infrastructure visibility to VCF admins
VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics provides infrastructure visibility to VCF admins. Infrastructure related critical
issues around appliances and capabilities are captured in simple dashboards. You can resolve issues quickly with the
right information. All NSX health issues related to appliances and capabilities are captured in the dashboard for each
NSX instance. NSX edge and ESX host networking capacity monitoring is critical, as it can impact connectivity and
performance of the applications hosted on the VCF infrastructure. The out-of-the-box dashboards provide detailed metrics
of NSX edge and ESX host networking. For more information, see NSX Health in VCF Operations Health and Diagnostics.
Note:
Edge monitoring is only accessible from the Edge dashboards in VCF Operations. You cannot access edge
monitoring from VCF Operations for networks.
Network Assessment and Value
The Network Assessment and Value feature helps users to evaluate their current network infrastructure and see the value
of VCF networking capabilities. Users can benefit by utilizing VPC networks and achieve capital expenditure (CAPEX) and
Broadcom 104

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
operational expenditure (OPEX) savings. This assessment focuses on deployments with only virtual networking (VDS).
Existing VPC networking configurations are not taken into account in the assessment. For more information, see Network
Assessment and Value Analysis.
Expanded IPFIX Functionality for VKS Clusters
This feature allows for the application of container IPFIX flows on VKS clusters deployed with Antrea to be exported
to the VCF Operations for networks collector. Flows are activated on all VKS clusters after Antrea IPFIX is enabled
on the vCenter data source. Flows are then parsed and aggregated to produce dashboards in VCF Operations.
These dashboards focus on traffic patterns, such as pod-to-pod and pod-to-external traffic between clusters. For more
information, see Using Antrea IPFIX for VKS Flows.
VPC Planning
The VPC planning feature provides users with guidance in transitioning from vSphere networking to VPC networking. After
selecting a vCenter server and Distributed Switch (VDS). for analysis, users are presented with a table with information
and subnets and the details required to create a VPC. The generated VPC design can be exported as a CSV file. For
more information, see VPC Planning.
NSX Inventory Objects and Relationship
The following changes to the NSX inventory dashboard have been introduced:
• Enhancements to VPC support.
• The NSX transverse spec is now moved from the Integrations tab to the Networks tab.
• Legacy dashboards are deprecated which streamlines the main NSX inventory dashboard.
Expanded Migration Planning Functionality
The migration planning feature for VCF Operations for networks is enhanced to support the automatic generation of
migration waves and groups. This functionality clusters workloads based on flow, latency and bandwidth data. The
enhanced migration plan summary provides a centralized source of information on the latest status of the migration
planning progress in VMware HCX and precise resource calculations for the destination site of the migrated workloads.
These enhancements remove the guesswork from complex migrations allowing for the migration of workloads with greater
confidence and less manual effort. For more information, see Create a Migration Plan and Export Migration Waves.
Storage operations
vSAN Storage Performance
Performance insights extend the existing reactive capabilities to proactively to monitor vSAN performance metrics against
a set of predefined rules. If any deviations from regular performance patterns are detected, it generates actionable
insights in VCF Operations, which include the plausible causes and the steps to remediate the issues. For more
information, see Monitoring Storage Operations.
vSAN Diagnostics
VCF Operations can now expose detailed health findings and specifics from the vSAN Health Service, going beyond the
overall health score. The vSAN Health Service analyzes the cluster's status to generate a health score (100 is best) and
provides detailed health findings with remediation guidance in vCenter. This allows for better identification of problematic
clusters and provides the ability to launch directly to the respective vCenter for detailed remediation steps.
vSAN Effective Capacity
vSAN Effective Capacity provides a clear and accurate view of usable storage capacity by way of abstracting the
complexities of RAID policies and system overhead. It highlights data reduction from advanced efficiency features,
such as deduplication and compression, and reflects efficiency gains from thin provisioning and snapshot savings. This
reporting aligns with the storage industry and helps promote the benefit of major ESA features. For more information, see
vSAN Cluster Summary Tab.
Workload monitoring and observability
Load Balancing for cloud proxies that are a part of HA enabled collector groups
Broadcom 105

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You can now activate load balancing for all cloud proxies that are a part of HA enabled collector groups for both product
managed and open source Telegraf agents. For more information, see Monitoring Application Services using Product
Managed Telegraf and Monitoring Application Services and Operating Systems using Open Source Telegraf.
Monitoring Data Service Workloads with VCF Operations
VCF delivers a cloud-native Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) experience through Data Services. As the unified platform
for database provisioning and lifecycle management, Data Services now integrates with VCF Operations to provide out-of-
the-box monitoring for these database workloads. For more information, see Monitoring Data Services in VCF Operations.
Notifications

${SYMPTOMS}
In 9.1, the placeholder was redesigned from a plain string to a structured JSON object representing
${SYMPTOMS}
symptom sets, conditions, and related context. As a result, can no longer be embedded inline with other
${SYMPTOMS}
variables or text within the same JSON value.
For correct usage, place as a dedicated key-value pair: . Embedding
${SYMPTOMS} "symptoms": "${SYMPTOMS}"
the placeholder within a larger text string, such as

, is no longer supported.
${ALERT_DEFINITION_DESCRIPTION} \n\nSymptoms: ${SYMPTOMS}"
Protect
Serving as the platform's security command center, the Protect capability focuses on ensuring cyber resilience and
rigorous regulatory adherence. It provides continuous, real-time assessment of the infrastructure's security posture by
monitoring encryption readiness and critical security advisories. This defensive stance is reinforced by robust auditing and
compliance validation against industry benchmarks.
Security and compliance
Confidential Computing
Confidential computing capabilities in Security Operations help you profile your datacenter hardware and discover hosts
that are capable of running confidential VMs. Gain visibility into your confidential VM environment along with the potential
opportunity to host confidential VMs on supported hardware. For more information, see Infrastructure Security.
Audit Records and Audit Trail
Investigate user actions across various VCF components using a centralized, time-sliced view which is available in VCF
Operations. You can leverage aggregated action summaries to easily navigate your audit log data and quickly identify key
events in your environment. For more information, see Audit Records and Audit Trails.
Security Posture Management
Assess the compliance of your VCF environment against the VCF Security Configuration Guide and PCI DSS v4.0.1
standards. Remediate non-compliant findings using a revamped experience that includes out-of-the-box assessment,
remediation, and reporting capabilities. For more information, see Security Posture Management.

Cloud Administration
Provider Management
Migration Tool
Broadcom 106

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In VCF Automation 9.1, you can use the Migration Tool to perform an in-place migration from VMware Cloud Director to
VCF Automation. For more information, contact your Broadcom representative.
Support for vDefend Distributed Firewall and Gateway Firewall
VCF Automation 9.1 introduces vDefend Distributed Firewall and Gateway Firewall support directly within VCF
Automation. Provider administrators can now delegate vDefend Firewall services to organization administrators to
control their own vDefend Gateway for the Transit Gateway Firewall and Distributed Firewalls. In addition, out-of-the-
box security profiles have been created to allow uniform vDefend Firewall security for new and existing VPCs along with
role-based access control labeling for dynamic security groups. For more information, go to the official vDefend Firewall
documentation.
Setting for default Private VPC and Private TGW IP Blocks
Starting with VCF Automation 9.1, providers can use the Provider Management UI to configure a default private VPC and
private TGW IP blocks that are configured in the organization itself after the organization's regional networking is set up.
These settings can also be overridden for each organization when its regional networking is provisioned.
Support for Avi Load Balancer
VCF Automation 9.1 introduces full self-service support for Avi Load Balancer. From the provider management portal,
administrators can delegate load balancing creation and management rights to the All Apps organization, ensuring
operational autonomy. Providers can set quotas (e.g., service engine limits, application limits) on organizations to manage
resource consumption and capacity. Organizations can provision namespaces with Avi load-balancing and create
allocations with necessary load-balancing components such as VIP, pool, health monitors, persistence profiles, and other
features.
Avi Load Balancer is also supported for VM Apps organizations.
For more information, go to the official Avi Load Balancer for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 documentation.
Multiple External Connections (Formerly Provider Gateways)
VCF Automation 9.1 introduces expanded flexibility for outbound traffic by supporting multiple external connections per
organization. Provider administrators can now use the Provider Management UI to configure multiple external connections
and associate them with organizations. This way, organizations have multiple exit points for external communication. VCF
Automation 9.1 supports both centralized connections (formerly called Provider Gateways), which are based on NSX
Tier-0 or Tier-0 VRF, and distributed VLAN connections.
For more information, see Managing External Connections in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
Shared VLAN Extension Subnets
Starting with VCF Automation 9.1, provider administrators can use the Provider Management UI to configure a VLAN
extension NSX subnet and share that subnet with one or multiple organizations to enable the workloads in those
organizations to establish direct connectivity to devices on the VLAN.
For more information, see Managing VLAN Extension Subnets in VCF Automation.
External IP Blocks with Multiple CIDRs
In VCF Automation 9.1, IP spaces from earlier releases are renamed to external IP blocks. External IP blocks enable
provider administrators to configure multiple CIDRs and to specify included or excluded custom IP ranges, inline with
NSX. Leveraging the newly introduced integration between NSX and Infoblox External IPAM, providers can now tie an
Infoblox network container to VCF Automation IP blocks. Also, providers can hide the entire content of an external IP
block from the organizations that consume the IP block through an external connection.
For more information, see Managing IP Blocks in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
Fully Allocated and Multi-Supervisor Region Quota for Organizations
Starting with VCF Automation 9.1, provider administrators can grant organizations quota across multiple supervisors in
any given region. In addition, providers can also share the capacity of the entire region across all available supervisors
with multiple organizations to simplify quota management.
Organization Management
Change Namespace Allocation Limits
Broadcom 107

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In VCF Automation 9.1, application teams can adapt to the changing resource needs of their applications by performing
day 2 actions on namespaces like changing resource limits, VM classes, storage classes, and shared subnets.
Project Content Libraries
VCF Automation 9.1 supports the ability for project teams to maintain content libraries that are specific to their project.
This capability gives project teams additional flexibility and removes their dependency on the organization administrator.
Project content libraries can also span across multiple projects. See Create a Project Content Library in VCF Automation.
Canonical Content Libraries
In VCF Automation 9.1, organizations can now have subscribed content libraries for Canonical Ubuntu VM OS images.
The Ubuntu LTS images are validated and supported by VCF. Organization administrators or advanced users can
synchronize the Canonical subscribed content library to fetch new sets of images. See Subscribe to Ubuntu OS Images
from a Canonical Content Library in VCF Automation.
Support for Shared NSX Subnets in Organizations
VCF Automation 9.1 allows organization administrators to configure organization-wide NSX subnets and share them with
one or more namespaces within the organization.
NSX Transit Gateways Configurations in Organizations
In VCF Automation 9.1, organization administrators can create multiple NSX Transit Gateways and configure NAT, IPsec
VPN, and vDefend Gateway Firewall on those gateways. See Create a Transit Gateway in VCF Automation.

VCF APIs
Real-Time Metrics APIs (VODAP)
The new Real-Time Metrics APIs deliver a modern, centralized observability platform for VMware Cloud Foundation.
Key Capabilities:
• High-Granularity Visibility: These Prometheus-compatible Edge APIs allow users to query real-time, high-granularity
(up to 2-second) metrics across the unified SDDC stack, including ESX, vCenter, vSAN, and NSX.
• Seamless Grafana Integration: Native PromQL support enables the APIs to function as a direct data source for
Grafana.
• Simplified Configuration: A single API call now accesses built-in collection profiles (Essentials, Standard, and
Verbose), replacing the complex legacy configuration model. As part of this transition, the legacy vStats Tech-Preview
APIs are deprecated.
For detailed information, see What's changed in Realtime Metrics API in the API Reference documentation.
Introduced the Utilization API, which monitors vCenter capacity and usage metrics.
Introduced the API, which monitors vCenter capacity and usage metrics, including:
Utilization
• The number of active connections compared to the maximum allowed connection limit.
• The endpoints through which these connections are established.
• The number of requests sent to vCenter services relative to the maximum request capacity supported by those
services.
Broadcom 108

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Building on this API, new UI alarms have been added. These alarms are triggered when:
• Active connections exceed a configured threshold, and/or
• Service request volume surpasses the defined limit.
Threshold values are fully configurable through Advanced Settings.
The vCenter Group Federated API (VGFA) introduces a single unified API endpoint for managing all vCenter
instances in a vCenter group.
It allows clients to view and manage inventory across multiple vCenter instances as if they were one—without changing
existing API integrations.
VGFA can be enabled directly from the VCF Operations UI once SSO and vCenter group configuration are in place. After
activation, users gain seamless access to a consolidated inventory and operations experience, consistent with Linked
Mode in the UI.
This simplifies multi-vCenter automation, reduces integration complexity, and delivers a more streamlined management
experience at scale.
Introduced a new Query API as extension of already existing Search Index API. that delivers a fast, flexible, and
scalable way to retrieve vSphere inventory data such as virtual machines and clusters.
The Query API delivers a fast, flexible, and scalable way to retrieve vSphere inventory data such as virtual machines and
clusters.
The Query API enables:
• Powerful server-side filtering based on user-defined criteria.
• Efficient data access with pagination, property selection, and projections.
• Lightweight, stateless queries without server-side state or client-side caching.
• Entity counts and filtered results without retrieving full datasets.
Designed for high-frequency automation use cases, the Query API simplifies data access. This capability is now available
to customers and partners, improving performance, reliability, and ease of automation across vCenter environments.

VMware Cloud Foundation PowerCLI
Introduction
VCF PowerCLI 9.1 introduces highly requested capabilities centered around high-performance storage, advanced
networking, and critical security compliance. This release focuses on giving administrators more granular control over the
SDDC stack while ensuring the underlying toolset remains modern and secure.
Core infrastructure and host management
The following list of top customer requests to improve host-level configuration and hardware optimization are addressed:
• CPU Topology Management: Support for Assigned at PowerOn, providing precise control over virtual machine CPU
layouts.
• NVMe over TCP: Added support for enabling NVMe over TCP for VMkernel adapters, catering to high-performance
storage requirements.
• Active Directory Integration: Enhanced host management by allowing hosts to join an AD domain via a proxy server.
vSAN enhancements
New cmdlets and methods are added to streamline storage reporting and remote datastore management:
• Effective Capacity Reporting: New cmdlet for better visibility into usable storage.
• vSAN Max: Support for client network enablement.
• Remote Datastore Management: Capability to add/remove remote datastores and cross vCenter remote datastores
using both desired state and incremental methods.
Advanced VPC networking
The VPC module receives a massive expansion in 9.1, offering deeper integration for transit gateways and connectivity
policies:
• DHCP & IP Management: Extended DHCP configurations for VPCs/Subnets and the ability to define IP Blocks for
services or external IPs.
• Transit Gateway & Connectivity: New tools to manage Transit Gateway lifecycles and Connectivity Profiles to define
how VPCs attach to gateways and IP blocks.
• Connectivity Policies: Introduced the ability to define logical VPC Groups with specific communication policies:
– Community: Inter-VPC communication within the group.
– Private: Isolation from other VPCs.
– Promiscuous: Communication across all VPCs.
• Visibility: New support for retrieving VPC NAT configurations and viewing VPC-specific alarm information.
Broadcom 110

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Image Builder and lifecycle security
To ensure compliance with the latest security standards and modern environments:
• Python 3.13 Support: The Image Builder module now officially supports Python 3.13, enabling customers with strict
compliance rules to continue patching and updating safely.
Important:
Deprecation Notice: Support for Python 3.7 and 3.8 is now deprecated due to these versions reaching End
of Life (EOL). While they remain functional in 9.1, support will be completely removed in the next release. We
strongly recommend migrating to Python 3.9 or higher immediately.

The functionality of VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA is delivered as a combination of components. Some
are bundled within the VCF software bits, while others are delivered separately.
The following components are a part of the VCF software:
– Guided deployment workflow in the vSphere Client
Broadcom 500

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
– AI catalog items in VCF Automation
The following components are delivered separately from VCF 9.1:
– VMware Deep Learning VM 9.1 Build 25217931
For more information about VMware Deep Learning VM image releases, see the VMware Deep Learning VM
Release Notes.
– Private AI Services 2.0.89
For more information about Private AI Services releases, see the VMware Private AI Services Release Notes.
• Third-party products from the VCF ecosystem maintain their existing dependencies at the component level. For
example, OEM driver add-ons, ESX device drivers, and UI plugins.
• VCF versioning is not applicable to any component with external dependency for the version, such as the Kubernetes
version.
• Clusters that don’t have active VMware Supervisor are supported, but do not support key capabilities of VCF, such as
VCF Automation workflows.

Introduction
See key product support notes for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 listed within each component:
Broadcom 501

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF-level
Deprecation of SHA1-based cryptographic algorithms:
Usage and dependencies on SHA1-based cryptographic algorithms are deprecated and will be removed in a future VCF
release.
ESX
Deprecation Notes
ESX System Storage Deprecations:
Starting with VCF 9.1, support is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release for the following:
• USB and SD boot devices
• ESX without a persistent system storage device for OSDATA partition
• ESX with system storage device of less than 32 GB
• APIs for reconfiguring the system storage locations
Deprecation of suspend-to-RAM option during ESX upgrades:
Support for the suspend-to-RAM option during ESX upgrades is deprecated and will be removed in a future VCF release.
You can use suspend-resume or vSphere vMotion in maintenance mode as a less complicated and state-preserving
alternative.
Deprecation of Marvell/Aquantia (Atlantic) NIC devices and drivers:
VCF 9.1 deprecates Marvell/Aquantia (Atlantic) NIC drivers for VMware ESX that enable 10GbE networking for USB-
based and PCIe devices commonly used in home labs. Support for the Marvell/Aquantia (Atlantic) NIC devices and
drivers will be removed in a future VCF release.
Deprecation of AMD Solarflare 8000 and X2 series Ethernet adapters:
With VCF 9.1, AMD Solarflare 8000 and X2 series Ethernet adapters are deprecated and support will be removed in a
future VCF release.
Marvell E3 and E4 Drivers Deprecation:
Support for Marvell's Converged Network Adapters (CNAs) FastLinQ 57800/57810/57811 series and FastLinQ
41000/45000 series is deprecated in VCF 9.1 and will be be discontinued in a future major release.
Cisco Virtual Interface Card (VIC) 1200 and 1300 Series Deprecation:
Support for Cisco Virtual Interface Card (VIC) 1200 and 1300 series devices is deprecated in VCF 9.1 and will be
discontinued in a future major release due to lack of support for Enhanced Data Path (EDP).
Other Notes
Expiration of Microsoft 2011 Secure Boot Certificates:
Microsoft UEFI and KEK CA 2011 certificates, which affect the Secure Boot capability for ESX hosts and Linux guests,
expire in June 2026, while the Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate, which affects the Secure Boot capability for
Windows guests, expires in October 2026. The expiration of the 2011 certificates only prevents Microsoft from creating
new signatures with them; it does not invalidate existing signatures created prior to the expiration. Therefore, any version
of ESX that can Secure Boot on a host machine before the expiration can still do so afterward, unless you actively remove
the expired certificate from the machine's firmware, which is not generally recommended.
ESX 9.1 is multiply signed by:
• Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 certificate
• Microsoft UEFI CA 2023 certificates, including certain components that require the Microsoft Option ROM UEFI CA
certificate
• VMware Secure Boot Signing certificate
Broadcom 502

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Therefore, host Secure Boot of ESX 9.1 generally is not affected by the 2011 certificates expiration. The 2011 certificates
expiration has more complex effects on virtual machines running Windows and Linux guests. For more details, see KB
article 423893.
Deprecated use of First Class Disk in NFS v.3 datastores shared by more than 128 ESX hosts:
The use of First Class Disk (FCD), also known as an Improved Virtual Disk (IVD), in NFS v.3 datastores that are shared by
more than 128 ESX hosts, is not supported.
vCenter
Deprecation Notes
Deprecation of Internet Protocol Flow Information Export (IPFIX):
With VCF 9.1, the following options are deprecated and will be removed in a future major release:
• Using IPFIX on a VMware vSphere Distributed Switch (VDS) Uplink Port Group.
• Use the class, which defines the IPFIX configuration of the Link Aggregation Control Protocol
LagIpfixConfig
(LACP) group. is in the VMware Storage Policy API.
LagIpfixConfig
• Set Override port policies for IPFIX on a VDS to enable monitoring on uplink port groups. If IPFIX is already active
on uplink port groups or LACP ports, vCenter upgrade is blocked. You see an error message to remove the IPFIX
configurations before proceeding with the upgrade.
End of Support Notes
Blocking port 514:
Starting with vCenter 9.1, the unencrypted port 514 (UDP/TCP) is blocked for use and any syslog data transfers to
vCenter by port 514 are no longer supported. You can use port 1514, which supports secure, TLS-encrypted connections,
for all syslog traffic to vCenter. If you are using the option for scripted CLI installations, you must
syslog.ext.port
switch to using the option.
syslog.ext.tls.port
Removal of vSphere Cluster Services:
Starting with vCenter 9.1, vSphere Cluster Services (vCLS) is deactivated by default and you cannot re-activate the
capability. All remaining APIs and configurations are not supported and will be removed in the next major release.
Other Notes
Extended vCenter API that sets the global policy for local accounts:
VCF 9.1 extends the vCenter API that sets the global policy for local accounts, (
PUT /api/appliance/local-
) to change existing user configurations, along with its current functionality to configure
accounts/global-policy
password expiration for new users. If you need to set the configuration of a certain user as different from the global policy,
you can create an exception by using another local accounts API (
PATCH /api/appliance/local-accounts/
).
{username}
vSAN
None
NSX
Deprecation Notes
Deprecation announcement for “LagIpfixConfig” and “overwrite port policy Netflow”
VDS IPFIX will be backed with NSX Connection Track based IPFIX data path to export TCP connection information.
However, the Connection Track based IPFIX does not support uplink port due to performance constraints. As IPFIX will
not be supported on the uplink port group, the dependent “LagIpfixConfig” and “overwrite port policy Netflow” will not be
supported.
Broadcom 503

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
End of Support Notes
Removal of Logical MP API for port mirroring
Logical MP API for port mirroring is no longer supported.
VCF Installer
End of Support Notes
Removal of all vSphere Cluster Services functionality from VCF Installer UI and SDDC Manager UI
In VCF 9.0, vSphere Cluster Services (vCLS) is decoupled from Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) and vSphere High
Availability (HA). In VCF 9.1, all vCLS functionalities available in SDDC Manager UI and VCF Installer UI are removed.
vCLS will be deprecated in a future release.
VCF Operations
Deprecation Notes
Compliance feature is now deprecated and replaced by Security Posture Management
Security Posture Management offers enhanced assessment and remediation capabilities for VCF. For more information,
see Security Posture Management.
Deprecation announcement for the support of PhotonOS-based appliances in VCF Operations HCX
A new stack based on NSX Edge is being introduced that has a better performance than the PhotonOS stack. Therefore,
the PhotonOS-based appliances in VCF Operations HCX is being deprecated.
Deprecation of the legacy cluster expansion method in VCF Operations 9.1
In VCF Operations, the legacy method for expanding an existing cluster via the newly deployed node is deprecated in
VCF 9.1.
Deprecation of Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services as data sources in VCF Operations for networks
Azure and AWS data sources are now deprecated.
Deprecation of bundled OpenSSL in VCF Operations for logs Agent
The VCF Operations for logs Agent fails to function on host systems that do not have OpenSSL version 3 or higher
installed. Starting with VCF Operations for logs Agent 9.1.0, the OpenSSL library is no longer bundled within the agent
package. Instead, the agent has transitioned to using the system's default OpenSSL library to handle cryptographic
operations. To ensure the agent functions correctly, you must either update their host system to a version that includes
OpenSSL 3 or higher or continue utilizing an older version of the agent that includes the bundled library.
End of Support Notes
Removal of vCenter Assessment report feature
The vCenter Assessment report is removed from VCF Operations for networks.
End of General Support for VCF Operations for logs (previously known as VMware Aria Operation Logs) Content
Packs
Starting with VCF 9.1 , you will not be able to use VMware Aria Operation for logs (VCF Operations for logs ( previously
VMware Aria Operation Logs) content packs in VCF Operations. For all 3rd party content packs, you must convert your
content packs into management packs. These converted management packs can then be used in VCF Operations. For
more details, see Converting Content Packs to Management Packs.
Effective with the VCF 9.1 release, direct vCenter authentication for VCF Operations has been removed
The list of vCenter instances is no longer available on the VCF Operations login screen, and API authentication using
vCenter user credentials is no longer supported.
The Network Share plugin has been removed starting from version 9.1
Broadcom 504

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
During an upgrade to VCF 9.1 or later, any existing Network Share plugin, its configurations, and related data are
automatically removed. This is because beginning with VCF 9.1, FIPS compliance is enabled by default and cannot be
disabled. The Network Share plugin relies on components that are not compatible with FIPS requirements and is therefore
no longer supported. As an alternative, use the Standard Email plugin to deliver generated reports as email attachments
to specified recipients instead of copying them to a network share.
VCF Operations Configuration Drifts functionality has now been incorporated into the new VCF Operations Fleet
Configuration Management service
Standalone Management Pack Builder Appliance
The standalone Management Pack Builder appliance is no longer supported or actively maintained. To ensure continued
updates and technical support, please transition to the in-product Management Pack Builder introduced in VCF
Operations 9.0.
Other Notes
Support for Windows log agent
VCF 9.1 adds Fluent Bit as a supported version for Windows to collect Windows Event Logs, including System and
Security logs. Download the supported Fluent Bit MSI file from here.
Support for open source Telegraf agents:
VCF 9.1 adds support for the installation of open source Telegraf agents for configurations required for VCF Operations
cloud proxies. Support extends to the initial configuration, which provides a consistent flow of metrics to endpoints with
no common failure patterns observed on VCF Operations. For queries on agent operations beyond this scope, use the
Telegraf open source community. For more information, see Monitoring Application Services and Operating Systems using
Open Source Telegraf and Open Source Telegraf Troubleshooting.
Important Upgrade Guidance for VCF Operations
• Customers planning to upgrade to VCF Operations 9.0.x:
Do not upgrade to VCF Operations 8.18.6. Instead, upgrade directly to VCF Operations 9.0.x.
• Customers who have already upgraded to VCF Operations 8.18.6:
To continue the upgrade path to the 9.x stream, you must wait for a subsequent release, such as VCF 9.1 or VCF
Operations 9.0.3, or a later version.

VMware Cloud Foundation Java SDK
Compatibility Notes
The SDK is compatible with the following Java LTS versions: 11, 17, 21, 25. It is strongly recommended to use one of
those versions when integrating the SDK into custom applications and when running the samples.
VMware Cloud Foundation Python SDK
Compatibility Notes
All modules of the VCF SDK for Python are compatible and verified with the supported versions of Python at the time
of their release. Once a Python version reaches EOL (End-Of-Life), it no longer receives security patches. VCF SDK
releases which happen after this moment will not provide compatibility guarantees for the EOL-ed Python version. As
generally good practice and for best security posture, it is recommended to use the VCF SDK with an actively maintained
version of Python and keeping your environment on the latest patch provided by the Python Software Foundation (PSF).
For VCF release 9.1.0.0, the supported Python versions are 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
Broadcom 509

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VMware Cloud Foundation PowerCLI
Deprecation Notes
Support for Python 3.7 and 3.8:
Starting with VCF 9.,1, support for Python 3.7 and 3.8 is deprecated due to these versions reaching End of Life (EOL).
While they remain functional in 9.1, support will be completely removed in the next release. We strongly recommend
migrating to Python 3.9 or higher immediately.
