ESX Known Issues:
Memory Tiering Issues
In rare cases, during migration or upgrade some virtual machines in clusters with Memory Tiering and DRS might
fail to power on
In clusters with Memory Tiering, if Tier-0 (physical DRAM) VMs occupy a significant portion of the DRAM, in rare cases,
DRS might fail to place additional VMs correctly during migration or upgrade tasks. Consequently, such VMs might fail to
power on after the respective operation.
Workaround: Avoid placing non-tiered (DRAM-only) VMs that occupy a significant portion of the DRAM on memory-tiered
hosts.
In the vSphere Client, you see an alarm that a NVMe Memory Tiering device is not healthy
In an ESX host with Memory Tiering and a single NVMe device, if the NVMe device fails and the VM on which the device
resides migrates out of the host, the ESX host might also fail. In the vSphere Client, you see an alarm
<ESX host>
suggesting that you need to replace the device.
NVMe Memory Tiering device is not healthy
Broadcom 510

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: Place the ESX host in maintenance mode, replace the NVME device, and use the command
esxcli
to set the Memory Tiering configuration.
memtier config set -d <new_device>
You see an alarm for failed vSphere HA failover for some virtual machines in clusters with Memory Tiering
If Tier 0, physical DRAM, resources are insufficient on any ESX host in a cluster with Memory Tiering to satisfy the
requirement of VMs with memory reservation to power on, you might see the alarm
vSphere HA virtual machine
in the Summary tab of the vSphere Client. As a result, you might see some VMs, either with memory
failover failed
reservation or not, in a powered off state. vSphere HA might report the alarm even if the overall memory resources in the
cluster are sufficient. You might also see the alarm
vSphere HA stopped trying to restart this VM because
for such VMs with failed failover. The issue occurs only in clusters
the maximum VM restart count was reached
in which some virtual machines use only Tier 0 memory, such as Low Latency VMs, Prealloc VMs, and Fault Tolerant
VMs.
Workaround: If a virtual machine failover fails in a cluster with Memory Tiering, provide sufficient DRAM resources. You
can either add hosts for additional DRAM capacity or reduce current usage, powering off some VMs consuming DRAM
for example. Sufficient DRAM resources allow VMs with memory reservation on all ESX hosts to power on. vSphere HA
might have stopped trying to restart such VMs and you must manually power them on.
Miscellaneous Issues
ESX host might fail with a purple diagnostic screen due to a rare memory overcommitment scenario
In a rare memory overcommitment scenario, where an ESX host transiently enters a low memory condition and an invalid
machine page number (MPN) is accessed during a swap-out operation, the host might fail with a purple diagnostic screen
with an error such as . The issue occurs only in a combination of the
ASSERT bora/vmkernel/mem/swap.c:1201
following conditions:
1. Low Memory State: The ESX host is in a low memory state, defined as typically having less than 2% free ESX
consumed memory.
2. Encrypted VMs: The issue only affects encrypted VMs.
3. Trigger Event: An encrypted VM is powered on, or an operation like vSphere vMotion migration, VM-resume, or Fast
Suspend and Resume (FSR) is executed on the encrypted VM while the host is in the low memory state.
Workaround: When you power on encrypted VMs or plan operations such as migration, FSR, or VM-resume on encrypted
VMs make sure that the ESX host is not in a low memory state that might lead to memory overcommitment.
ESX virtual host IP address unexpectedly changes during VM suspend, resume, or snapshot revert operations
In some environments, nested ESX hosts using DHCP-based IP configuration might experience unexpected IP address
changes during VM suspend, resume, or snapshot revert operations. The issue occurs when NTP time synchronization
introduces a significant time drift, causing the DHCP lease renewal to fail before lease expiration. As a result, the DHCP
lease expires and the IP address is released and reassigned, leading to a temporary loss of connectivity .
Workaround: Use a stable NTP server and configure longer DHCP lease duration and renewal timers to ensure sufficient
margin for successful lease renewal during transient network events.
You cannot turn on the disk LED by using the command 'esxcli storage core device set -d naa.xxx --led-state
error' on lsi_mr3, lsi_msgpt3, lsi_msgpt35, and bcm_mpi3 controllers
The operation is not supported for the lsuv2-lsiv2-drivers-plugin. When you use the command
ERROR LED esxcli
on lsi_mr3, lsi_msgpt3, lsi_msgpt35, and
storage core device set -d naa.xxx --led-state error
bcm_mpi3 controllers, you get an error such as:
Not supported':[root@xxx:~] esxcli storage core device set -d naa.xxx --led-state error
Unable to set LED state for device naa.xxx: Not supported!
This issue does not impact turn on/off LED operations from the vSphere Client.
Workaround: You can turn on the LED from the vSphere Client or use the following command:
LOCATOR LED
[root@xxx:~] esxcli storage core device set -d naa.xxx --led-state locator --led-duration
100
Intel Xeon 6 processors utilizing QAT accelerators might see increased boot times on ESX 9.1
Broadcom 511

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
On Intel Xeon 6 processors systems using QAT devices, in some cases, the boot time for ESX hosts might increase.
Workaround: None. This issue will be fixed in a future patch release.
vSphere vMotion Issues
You cannot migrate an NVIDIA Enhanced DirectPath I/O device from one distributed virtual switch to another if
the switches have a different number of uplinks
NVIDIA firmware does not support vSphere vMotion operations between configurations that use different uplink settings.
As a result, you cannot migrate an Enhanced DirectPath I/O device from one switch to another if the switches have a
different number of uplinks. The issue affects only Enhanced DirectPath I/O devices backed by NVIDIA's BlueField-3 and
ConnectX-7.
Workaround: None
Drivers
In rare cases, an ESX host might fail with a blue screen due to a IOMMU fault or traffic connection timeout
In a setup of two ESX hosts connected by a Cisco N9K switch, the target node in an RDMA Write operation might trigger
an IOMMU fault or a traffic connection timeout. As a result, the target host fails with a blue screen and an error such as
. The issue occurs only under specific conditions:
PTE not set to allow Write
1. RDMA write operations use DMA-based memory regions (DMA MR)
2. The network QoS of the switch are not properly configured
Workaround: None.
To prevent the issue, follow these best practices:
1. Use a supported N9K switch model with up-to-date firmware.
2. Properly configure QoS for RoCE on the N9K switch, following the Cisco configuration guides.
3. Avoid using DMA MR–based RDMA write operations. The Cisco nenic driver supports only NVMe over RoCEv2, which
uses FRMR for RDMA write operations.
Networking Issues
Loss of network traffic for VMs connected with Virtual Functions (VF) from NVIDIA ConnectX-7 four ports adapter
Due to a hardware limitation of NVIDIA ConnectX-7 four port cards preventing support for hardware LAG, VF configured in
LAG might experience traffic loss. In the , you see error messages such as:
vmkernel.log
2026-03-10T02:21:57.741Z -ALERT vmkalert - [esx@4413] cpu0:1001391606) <NMLX_ERR> 0000:46:00.0:
nmlx5_CoreCreateLag:56 command failed, status bad parameter(0x3), syndrome 0xf460ff
2026-03-10T02:21:57.741Z -ALERT vmkalert - [esx@4413] cpu0:1001391606) <NMLX_ERR> nmlx5_core: 0000:46:00.0:
nmlx5_CoreCreateLag:59 - Create LAG command fails with error: Failure
2026-03-10T02:21:57.741Z -ALERT vmkalert - [esx@4413] cpu0:1001391606) <NMLX_ERR> nmlx5_core: 0000:46:00.0:
nmlx5_en_LagInit:237 - Unable to create lag: Failure
Only LAGs with matching number of ports are supported, for example for a four-port Host Channel Adapters (HCA), only a
four-port LAG is supported.
Workaround: None.
Mounts on an NFS v4.1 server fail with a NFS4ERR_CLID_INUSE error
Each NFS v4.1 client instance is represented by a client ID and each NFS v4.1 server instance is identified by a server
owner which is a combination of server major and server minor and uniquely identifies a server in a cluster. When
NFS v4.1 client mounts a share, it creates a session per server owner and associates the TCP connection with the
session. Each session is associated with a client ID provided by the NFS v4.1 server. The server keeps the state of
the authentication mechanism for the existing client and the session and rejects any new security mechanism for the
existing client. A change in vmknic binding or nConnect, or mounting a new datastore from same NFS v4.1 server with a
different security flavor might lead to the creation of additional connections with a different security flavor. As a result, such
operations might fail with an error.
NFS4ERR_CLID_INUSE
Broadcom 512

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: Use the same security mechanism and vmknic binding with which a cluster was created for all connection
and mounting requests. For more details, see KB 370714.
vCenter Known Issues:
vSphere Client and vCenter Issues
Lost password sync between vCenter and SDDC Manager
In a VCF environment, you can change the local user password either under
administrator@vsphere.local
Administration > Users and Groups in the vSphere Client or by using the vCenter API. However, when you change the
password of a vCenter instance, the password sync with the SDDC Manager and
administrator@vsphere.local
VCF Operations might be lost. As a result, you see status for the vCenter instance in the vCenter grid
Disconnected
under Security > Password Management in the SDDC Manager interface.
Workaround: In the vCenter grid under Security > Password Management in the SDDC Manager interface, select the
vCenter account and click Remediate Password.
vSphere Client shows an error that the vCenter instance is not connected to a license server
During an upgrade to vCenter 9.1, in the vSphere Client you might see a banner with the following error:
One or more vCenter instances are not connected to a license server. To avoid service
interruption, verify that the vCenter instance is connected to a license server.
The banner triggers when the connected VCF Operations is not yet upgraded to 9.1 and the license server is not yet
deployed. This behavior is expected.
Workaround: To upgrade to version 9.1, strictly follow the upgrade order of components as documented in the 9.1 product
documentation:
• Upgrading to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1
• Upgrading to vSphere Foundation 9.1
• Upgrading vSphere 8 and Aria Operations 8 to 9.1
The vpxd service might fail with an error "Memory exceeds hard limit. Panic"
In rare cases, on very large virtual machines, the vpxd service might fail with an out-of-memory condition after around
3 days of uptime. As a result, some running operations in the vCenter instance might fail. The service recovers
automatically and vCenter resumes normal operations.
Workaround: None
In very rare cases, you might see a false positive alarm "License assignment failed for this host"
Due to a difference in the license entitlement formats in VCF 9.0 and VCF 9.1 and later, after an upgrade to vCenter
9.1, in the vSphere Client you might see the alarm . This is a false
License assignment failed for this host
positive alarm, because a license is provided but not auto-acknowledged upon successful licensing. The alarm does not
indicate a broken workload or function.
Workaround: Confirm that the host is licensed and acknowledge the alarm.
Some files, including the OVA image, remain staged on the source vCenter even when an CLI upgrade fails
The CLI installer does not support a user-initiated cancel operation during an upgrade and cancellation occurs only
when the upgrade fails. When an upgrade fails, some staged files, including the OVA image, on the source vCenter are
preserved by design, because:
1. When an upgrade fails, you usually resolve the issue and retry.
2. During the retry, the OVA file, which might weight 9 GB for example, is transferred to the source vCenter, which is time
consuming.
Keeping the OVA file staged saves significant load time.
If you use a different ISO, the existing OVA is deleted.
Broadcom 513

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: If you need to reclaim disk space after a failed upgrade that will not be retried, you can manually delete the
staged files from the source vCenter from the location:
/storage/lifecycle/vlcm/
Virtual machine templates might fail to sync when vCenter instances are linked by using vCenter grouping in VCF
Operations
With VCF 9.1, you link vCenter instances in vCenter Groups under Operate > Administration > Configurations >
vCenter Linking in VCF Operations, instead of using the vCenter Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM), which is deprecated.
After you create a vCenter group, if you create a content library on one of the vCenter instances, add a VM template,
and try to create a new subscription, the VM template sync might fail. In the vSphere Client, you might see either of the
following errors:
•
A general system error occurred: Failed to publish library <source library> to
subscribed library <target library> on vCenter Server XYZ. Reason: The operation failed
due to Permission to perform this operation was denied.
•
Permission to perform this operation was denied: You do not hold privileges... VM
template sync works if the vCenter instances are linked in ELM.
Workaround: For all linked vCenter instances, run the following commands:
1. To retrieve the machine id:
/usr/lib/vmware-vmafd/bin/vmafd-cli get-machine-id --server-name
localhost
Output example: eac8395e-f676-4358-a8aa-79e3668ddfa7
2. To add content library user:
/usr/lib/vmware-vmafd/bin/dir-cli group modify --name
vSphereClientSolutionUsers --add content-library-user-<machine-id> --login <vCenter
Server SSO administrator login id>
For example:
/usr/lib/vmware-vmafd/bin/dir-cli group modify --name
vSphereClientSolutionUsers --add content-library-user-eac8395e-f676-4358-
a8aa-79e3668ddfa7 --login administrator@vsphere.local
Enter password for administrator@vsphere.local:
Output example: Account [content-library-user-eac8395e-f676-4358-a8aa-79e3668ddfa7] added to group
[vSphereClientSolutionUsers]Group member [content-library-user-eac8395e-f676-4358-a8aa-79e3668ddfa7] added
successfully
You do not see linked vCenter instances in the vSphere Client after removing them from a vCenter group in VCF
Operations
When you remove vCenter instances from an existing vCenter group in VCF Operations, you might not see such
instances in the vSphere Client after you add them to a new group.
Workaround: Log in to SSH as root and run the command .
service-control --restart vsphere-ui
You cannot select options to preserve MAC-addresses and include extra configuration when cloning a VM
template
In the vSphere Client, when you right-click a virtual machine template and select Clone to Library, you do not see an
option to select the following parameters:
• Preserve MAC-addresses on network adapters
• Include extra configuration
Workaround: You can set either option by using API or the vSphere Client:
1. API: Use backend API https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/vsphere-automation-api/latest/api/vcenter/ovf/library-
item/post/ with the export flags in the CreateSpec https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/vsphere-automation-api/
latest/data-structures/Vcenter%20Ovf%20LibraryItem%20CreateSpec/
For example:
curl --location 'https://<vCenter IP>/api/vcenter/ovf/library-item' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Cookie: vmware-api-session-id=xxxxx' \
--data '{
"source": {
"type": "VirtualMachine",
Broadcom 514

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
"id": "vm-xxxxx"
},
"target": {
"library_id": "xxxxx"
},
"create_spec": {
"name":"<your_spec>",
"flags" : ["EXTRA_CONFIG", "PRESERVE_MAC"]
}
}
Get the export flags with this command:
curl --location 'https://<vCenter IP>/api/vcenter/ovf/export-flag' \
--header 'Cookie: vmware-api-session-id=xxxxx' \
--data ''
[
{
"description": {

},

},
{

]
2. vSphere Client:
a. Right click on a VM template and select Convert to Virtual Machine. You see a new VM created.
b. Right-click the new VM and click Clone > Clone as Template to Library.
c. In the Clone as Template to Library modal, select OVF as Template type.
Opening vCenter tasks in a new tab in the vSphere Client takes long
When the vSphere Client runs on a low-resource virtual machine, such as a Windows jumpbox, opening a vCenter task
in a new tab might take long, sometimes more than three minutes. This issue is more likely to occur during periods of
high activity, such as vCenter processing more than 5,000 parallel operations per hour. In such cases, the vCenter Task
Console also responds with a significant delay.
Workaround: Run the vSphere Client on a machine with higher resource availability to ensure responsive performance.
In the vSphere Client, you see tasks with name OvfManager.deployVm.label under Recent Tasks
In the vSphere Client, when deploying a virtual machine by using vCenter OVFS API, in Recent Tasks you see tasks with
name and the Initiator column shows an incorrect user name. The task name should
OvfManager.deployVm.label
read Deploy OVF template and the initiator should show the actual user name logged into the vCenter Client.
Workaround: None
After breaking Enhanced Link Mode (ELM), linking to some vCenter instances in VCF Operations fails
In a 9.x environment, after breaking ELM and setting up VCF Operations, linking to some vCenter instances might fail with
the message . The issue
An error has occurred. Please retry the linking process after some time
occurs because breaking ELM removes the service accounts associated with an already used token which sometimes
Broadcom 515

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
makes such tokens stale and no longer valid, causing vCenter API calls to fail. To confirm the issue, SSH into the affected
vCenter instance and check the following log file: . Look for the
/var/log/vmware/vapi/endpoint/endpoint.log
error:
Request is invalid: ns0:InvalidRequest: 'ActAs' token is invalid!
Workaround: To restore connectivity to vCenter API calls:
1. SSH into the affected vCenter instance.
2. Use the command to restart the following services:
service-control --restart <service name>
– vmware-vapi-endpoint
– vmware-vpxd
3. In VCF Operations, remove the affected vCenter instance from vCenter linking.
4. Re-add the vCenter instance. Confirm that vCenter linking status shows as Active.
Pods on VKS 3.6.0 might run out of memory during scaling
During scaling of a VCF 9.1 environment, some pods on VKS 3.6.0 might run out of memory.
Workaround: Upgrade to VKS 3.6.1.

tar file: %s" % self.getFilePath()).
Due to a rare race condition between read and write tasks, tar creation during the generation of the vCenter support
bundle might fail with an error such as . In the backtrace, you see logs similar to:

You cannot log in to the vSphere Client with Google Chrome after generating a VMCA certificate with key size
larger than 15 KB
Due to a limit on the maximum size of a TLS/SSL certificate chain that Google Chrome and other Chromium-based
browsers can process, you might not be able to log in to the vSphere Client after generating a VMCA certificate with a key
size larger than 15 KB.
Workaround: None
Upgrade Issues
A reset of the vSphere Lifecycle Manager database might cause data loss in the Supervisor
If the vSphere Lifecycle Manager database in your environment is reset before upgrading vCenter from versions 8.0
Update 3 and later or 9.0.x to 9.1.0 or 9.1.1, the upgrade might cause data loss in the Supervisor. To avoid data loss,
before a vCenter upgrade, you must first check your environment and take mitigation steps, if necessary.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 455737 for instructions how to check if your environment is affected
and for mitigation steps.
Broadcom 516

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
vCenter upgrade to 9.1 might fail with a pre-check error for NetFlow enabled on distributed portgroups
When upgrading vCenter Server to version 9.1, the upgrade pre-check might fail with an error in the vSphere Client such
as:
Some uplink distributed portgroup(s) on the source vCenter Server have NetFlow enabled.
Make sure NetFlow is disabled and NetFlow Override port policies is disabled in the
following uplink distributed portgroup(s) list.
Using Internet Protocol Flow Information Export (IPFIX) on a vSphere Distributed Switch (VDS) uplink port group is
deprecated in VCF 9.1.
This error typically occurs in environments managed by VCF Operations for networks, formerly vRealize Network Insight
(vRNI), which automatically re-enables NetFlow on VDS.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 441813.
In VCF Operations, you see completed status under Configuration Upgrades for all ESX hosts even though some
upgrades are still in progress
If a vCenter instance has both standalone ESX hosts and clusters, in VCF Operations under Build > Lifecycle >
<workload> > Configuration Upgrades, you might see a confirmation that the upgrade has completed. At the same
time, under Tasks, you might see that some upgrades have completed, for standalone ESX hosts for example, while
cluster upgrades are still running. The issue occurs because after the upgrade of standalone hosts completes, the bundles
API might consider the task complete on bundle level and not track tasks on the individual resource level.
Workaround: Monitor the running tasks to ensure that all upgrades complete.
After an in-place upgrade to vCenter 9.1, you see two disks backing /storage/dblog and /storage/lifecycle
A change in the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) usage in PostgreSQL can cause the partition to reach
/storage/dblog
100% capacity during certain scenarios such as long-running uptime, which might affect vCenter availability or database
operations. To avoid such issues, the partition size is doubled across all deployment sizes in vCenter
/storage/dblog
9.1. For example, from 25 GB to 50 GB on large deployments. When you perform an in-place upgrade from vCenter 9.0
to 9.1 and later, the former storage is repurposed and its capacity is added to ,
/storage/vtsdblog /storage/dblog
so the dblog partition is effectively doubled. As a result of this repurposing, you see two disks backing
/storage/dblog
and two disks backing after the update. This is expected and does not require any action.
/storage/lifecycle
Workaround: None. When you update from vCenter 9.0 to any 9.1 release, the upgrade automatically repurposes
/
and adds it to . No additional action is required.
storage/vtsdblog /storage/dblog
If you use the vCenter GUI installer, update to vCenter 9.1 from an earlier 9.x version fails
If you try to upgrade a vCenter instance from version 9.x to 9.1 by using the vCenter GUI installer, you see the following
error message:
Source version is 9.0.0 and the installer version is 9.0. Supported version
.
for upgrade is 8.0.
Workaround: Use the vCenter GUI installer only for upgrades of vCenter from 8.x to 9.0 and later. Use the Virtual
Appliance Management Interface (VAMI) for updates between versions of VCF 9.0, for example vCenter 9.0 to vCenter
9.0.x or vCenter 9.1.
Miscellaneous Issues
OpenLDAP login to vCenter fails after upgrade to VCF 9.1 due to a missing attribute
vCenter requires the attribute for OpenLDAP providers and if such is missing, OpenLDAP login fail
serviceAccount
after an upgrade to VCF 9.1.
Workaround: Remove and readd the identity source on the vCenter instance.
If ESX hosts of a 9.1 vCenter run versions earlier than 8.0 Update 2, some hardware compatibility checks fail
When running hardware compatibility checks on a vCenter of version 9.1 with ESX hosts on versions earlier than 8.0
Update 2, in the vSphere Client, you might see the following errors:
1. vSphere Lifecycle Manager Hardware Compatibility check on cluster level:
There was a problem connecting
to the hosts in the cluster.
Broadcom 517

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Discover and Plan (D&P) Hardware Compatibility check on host level:
There is a problem connecting
to the host 'host-XX'. Make sure that the vCenter Server Appliance has network
connectivity to the ESXi host.
3. Cluster Remediation: If the option Prevent remediation if hardware compatibility issues are found is active,
remediation fails to proceed on vSAN clusters due to the failed vSphere Lifecycle Manager Hardware Compatibility
check.
Workaround: Manually verify hardware compatibility according to the Broadcom Compatibility Guide and considering if
your cluster is a vSAN cluster. After the verification, you can uncheck Prevent remediation if hardware compatibility
issues are found and proceed with the remediation.
During RDU upgrade, you see an error "Unable to connect to the given vCenter or ESXi [] on its SDK endpoint"
In the Source Location step of the Target VM deployment wizard in the vSphere Client during RDU upgrade, you see
an error such as . This error
Unable to connect to the given vCenter or ESXi [] on its SDK endpoint
usually occurs because of incorrect username, password, or user certificate prompts.
Workaround: Check the username and the password, and retry.
Revert snapshot operation fails with the error 'The operation is not allowed in the current state.'
If a virtual machine has a chain of snapshots, which contains snapshots of both the VM and Improved Virtual Disks (IVD),
also known as First Class Disks (FCD), reverting to a VM snapshot is not supported. If you try such an operation, in the
logs you see a message such as:
The virtual machine cannot be reverted when crossing an Improved-Virtual-Disk snapshot.
or an error such as:
The operation is not allowed in the current state.
Workaround: None. The operation is not supported.
Auto Deploy Issues
Booting stateful ESX hosts on a vSphere Configuration Profile (VCP) cluster fails with error "Error copying /
downloading file"
When you use Auto Deploy to provision ESX hosts in a VCP cluster at scale, if you do not provide a ready configuration,
booting hosts fails with the message .
Error copying / downloading file
Workaround: Before you start using Auto Deploy with VCP, you must have a ready configuration, either in a file or
.json
imported from a reference host. The best practice is to:
• Create a VCP cluster.
• Manually configure the desired settings on an existing ESX host that you select as a reference host.
• Import the reference host configuration to create a draft, make changes, precheck, and apply it.
Successful provisioning of hosts in VCP clusters requires a valid, non-empty desired configuration document. If the cluster
configuration lacks networking details, Auto Deploy rules might fail, because hosts cannot come online. Always validate
the configuration before you create Auto Deploy rules and attempt to provision hosts.
API Issues
Deploying an OVF by using vAPI on ESX hosts of version earlier than 9.0 fails
The vAPI for deploying an OVF, https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/vsphere-automation-api/latest/api/
vcenter/ovfs__action=deploy__vmw-task=true/post/, is only supported for ESX 9.0 and later releases. If an
ESX host of version earlier than 9.0 is a target of OVF deployment by this API, the deployment fails with an
error.
vmodl.fault.InvalidRequest
Workaround: Use an ESX host of version 9.0 and later for OVF deployment by vAPI.
vSAN
This document contains the following sections
Broadcom 518

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• vSAN Known Issues
vSAN Known Issues
Data component utilization is greater than 95% on vSAN ESA disk partitions, preventing creation of new pod VMs
vSAN ESA limits the maximum number of components per disk to 3000 (for hosts with more than 64GB memory and disk
sizes greater than 1TB).
With only two disks per-host, the component limit is approximately 6000 components, which is reached before disk
capacity is used up.
Workaround:
For full component capacity, use hosts with at least 9 disks per-host (IMK 9 disks are supported per-host)
Deduplication store UUID not displayed in Virtual Objects view
When you enable global deduplication on a vSAN ESA cluster, the Deduplication store appears in the Virtual Objects view
but does not display its UUID or placement details. The UUID exists in the system and can be verified through command-
line tools, but it is not visible in the vSphere Client UI.
Workaround:
To view the Deduplication store UUID, use the ESXi command line:
esxcli vsan dedup dedupstore get
This command displays the backend UUID and other Deduplication store details that are not shown in the vSphere Client
interface.
vSAN ESA with VMware VSS (Volume Shadow Copy Service) quiesced snapshots are inconsistent
If you are using vSAN ESA with VMware VSS (Volume Shadow Copy Service) to quiesce your snapshots, from either
VMware's own or 3rd-party data protection tools that use VADP, the virtual disks on the running VM might become
inconsistent.
Specifically, guest files that are deleted only from the snapshot during VSS quiescing may get zeroed out in the running
VM. Observed at-risk guest files include edb.log transaction logs and DataStore.edb, both from the Windows Update
service.
If those files are affected and the Windows Update service restarts for any reason, the problem may manifest as the
following record in the Window Event log:
wuaueng.dll (288) SUS20ClientDataStore: Unable to read the header of logfile C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution
\DataStore\Logs\edb.log. Error -501.
Manually restarting the Windows Update service by running this command "net start wuauserv" should regenerate
the inconsistent files and fix the problem.
Workaround
To prevent this inconsistency from happening for Windows Update and other VSS-quiesced services, disable trim/unmap
support for individual VSS-protected VMs. Trim/unmap for the VM can be re-enabled when a future patch is released
that fixes this issue. If you see this issue before being able to disable trim/unmap, you can restore the affected VM from a
recent snapshot (including the VSSs napshot that triggered that problem).
Stretching a vSAN cluster using the SDDC Manager API fails with the error "Failed to validate IP address pool"
When you attempt to stretch a vSAN cluster using a JSON specification that includes DHCP IP assignment for host TEPs
and provides a network spec in the input spec, then the stretch cluster workflow fails at during the "Validate IP Address
Availability for Edge Overlay (TEP) IP Assignment" action.
Workaround: See KB 399582.
NFS server leaks memory when clients mount shares using UDP protocol
Using UDP to mount NFS shares causes memory leaks, resulting in FSVM reboot.
Workaround: NFS clients must use TCP protocol to mount NFS shares.
Broadcom 519

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Auto-downloading the OVF file is disabled during vSAN File Service enablement or upgrade
With the VCF product unified releases, the auto-downloading of the OVF file in vSAN File Service enablement or upgrade
is disabled in the user interface of vCenter instances.
Manually download and install the vSAN File Service OVF file on the vCenter. See Broadcom knowledge base article
390237.
Performance impact when listing directories with many files
Listing files in a directory with many files takes more time.
Workaround: None
You cannot use the option "Install on a new vSAN cluster containing the target host" when deploying a vCenter
instance
Due to a known technical limitation, you cannot use the option Install on a new vSAN cluster containing the target
host when deploying a vCenter instance by using the GUI installer. If you use this option, the deployment fails with the
error on the step Install - Stage 2: vCenter Server setup is in
VMware vSAN Health service failed firstboot
progress.
Workaround: Do not use the option Install on a new vSAN cluster containing the target host when deploying vCenter.
You can activate vSAN from the vSphere Client after the vCenter deployment completes.
Mounting remote datastores from vSAN stretched clusters with unsupported vSAN versions is allowed
Missing guardrails allow mounting remote datastores from vSAN stretched clusters running unsupported vSAN versions,
leading to undesired behavior.
Workaround: None.
Host might get PSOD error after adding a new host into a compute client cluster
vSAN VCenter Management Service gets restarted when a compute client cluster has mounted a vSAN ESA or vSAN
storage cluster from a remote vCenter. The newly added host might get PSOD error when there is an I/O activity triggered
on the host.
Workaround: Perform one of the following:
• Before adding a new host, mount a new vSAN ESA or vSAN storage cluster to the client cluster.
• Move the host into maintenance mode and then add the new host. Use the script "fixhostmount.py" to remediate the
host.

NSX Known Issues
On a transit gateway and tier-0 gateway, users can see the stale advertised prefix from a deleted VPC static route
for AVI. The prefix used in deleted AVI VPC static route is reused for a different service like NAT, but the traffic
doesn't work for the new service.
Broadcom 520

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
User traffic can be affected for a new service like NAT when a deleted VPC static route for AVIs public IP/prefix is reused
in the new service.
Workaround: Call the following API on NSX Manager to remove the duplicate route:
POST /policy/api/v1/orgs/<orgId>/projects/<projectId>/vpcs/<vpcId>/force-resync
For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 445154.
When a load-based teaming policy is configured, a teaming failover is triggered when the load is increased.
Datapath outage happens for VNICs and(or) VMKNICs that were migrated.
Outage of existing and new connections.
Workaround: Move to "Route based on originating virtual port" Teaming policy.
Workload VMs experience packet drops when co-located on the same ESX host as the edge node. The issue
persists when all the following three conditions are met: i) the Edge Uplink Profile transport VLAN is unset or set
to 0. ii) The Edge VTEP fastpath (fp-ethx) interface is connected to a non-trunk Distributed Virtual Port Group
(DVPG). iii) Both the Edge VTEP and management/VLAN Host Switch interfaces are connected to VLAN-tagged
DVPGs.
Customers using the specific configuration described above will experience datapath traffic interruptions due to packet
drops for workload VMs residing on the same host as the edge node.
Workaround:
Refer the following KB article to address this issue:
https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/445209/packet-drops-are-seen-when-edge-connecte.html
BFD Tunnel sessions are not coming up with Intel E810C NIC.
Customers using the Intel E810C NIC on their Bare Metal Edge nodes will be impacted. The tunnels fail to establish due
to the incorrect VLAN handling that renders the overlay network non-functional for those segments. There is no graceful
recovery from this issue.
Workaround:
Use the ice_comms-1.3.24.0.pkg package. Use the following steps to change the ice package:
1. cd /lib/firmware/intel/ice/ddp
2. Download ice_comms-1.3.24.0.pkg
3. sudo ln -sf ice-1.3.24.0.pkg ice.pkg
4. Check that link inside the container has also changed by running the following command:
docker exec -it service_datapath ll /usr/lib/firmware/intel/ice/ddp
Changing the Span field value unexpectedly resets the External Connection field when specific Connectivity
Types are selected.
When a user modifies the Span field, any previously entered or selected data in the External Connection field is
automatically cleared. This behavior occurs specifically when the Connectivity Type is set to Centralized, Distributed, or
VXLAN.
Workaround:
• From UI: Ensure that the Span field value is finalized before entering any information into the External Connection
field.
• From API: Use Update TGW API to update Span value.PUT: /policy/api/v1/orgs/{org-id}/projects/{project-id}/transit-
gateways/{transit-gateway-id}
Warning message is missing when tier-0 does not have "Transit Gateway Static advertisement" configured after
an NSX 4.2 upgrade.
Users configuring a gateway connection and centralized Transit Gateway have no indication that the associated tier-0 is
missing TGW_STATIC route redistribution, which leads to a silent routing misconfiguration after NSX 4.2 upgrades.
Workaround:
Broadcom 521

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
None.
IP Block statistics page shows CIDR allocated to a subnet and VM IPs connected to that subnet as two
allocations.
Customers see VM IP addresses listed twice in the allocation details, once as part of the subnet CIDR allocation and
again as individual VM IPs. This double-counting leads to inconsistency between the overall usage statistics and the
detailed IP/CIDR listings.
Workaround:
No available workaround.
When a tier-1 gateway's edge cluster is changed from one edge cluster to another (cross-cluster reallocation),
the VLAN conflict validation is ineffective. This allows segments with the same VLAN ID , Transport Zone, and
the uplink teaming policy from different tier-1 gateways to land on the same edge node causing edge Datapath
Configuration Failure.
Edge datapath configuration failure blocks all new configuration pushes to the affected edge node potentially impacting
traffic for workloads routed through tier-1 gateways on that edge.
Workaround:
Before changing a tier-1 gateway's edge cluster, manually verify that no segments connected to the tier-1 (through service
interfaces) have the same VLAN ID, Transport Zone, and the uplink teaming policy as segments already hosted on the
target edge cluster's edge nodes. If a conflict exists, move the conflicting tier-1 to a different edge cluster that does not
have overlapping VLAN segments on its edge nodes.

VCF Installer Known Issues
When converging to VCF or vSphere Foundation, the operation fails during VCF management services
deployment phase
When converging to VCF or vSphere Foundation, if the existing vCenter instance was upgraded from version 8.x to 9.0
or 9.1, then the VCF management services deployment task might fail to bootstrap VCF services runtime and return
the following error message: The VCF Installer and SDDC
Failed to bootstrap VCF services runtime.
Manager logs show the following error message:
Bootstrap failed during stage INIT0001 - Validating
configuration: INGRESS_PLATFORM_FQDN XXX could not be resolved via nameserver(s):
127.0.0.1.
Workaround: Perform one of the following tasks.
• Before starting the convergence process, perform the following tasks.
1. SSH to the vCenter instance.
2. Change to .
su
3. Open the file.
/etc/resolv.conf
4. Check for more than one line that contains and remove the duplicate lines.
nameserver 127.0.0.1
5. Open the file.
/etc/systemd/network/10-eth0.network
6. If or a similar combination is present in the file, delete the entry.
DNS=127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1
7. Restart the service by running the command.
systemd-networkd systemctl restart systemd-networkd
• After a convergence to VCF has failed, perform the following tasks.
1. SSH to SDDC Manager component and switch to the root user.
2. Check for more than one line that contains and remove the duplicate lines.
nameserver 127.0.0.1
Broadcom 522

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Save the file and retry the failed VCF convergence.
• After a convergence to vSphere Foundation has failed, perform the following tasks.
1. SSH to the vCenter instance.
2. Check for more than one line that contains and remove the duplicate lines.
nameserver 127.0.0.1
3. Save the file and retry the failed vSphere Foundation convergence.
When specific component FQDNs contain upper case characters, VCF deployment fails
If the following FQDNs contain upper case characters, VCF deployment fails:
• Fleet components FQDN
• Instance components FQDN
• Identity broker FQDN
• VCF services runtime FQDN
• VCF Automation FQDN
• VCF services runtime FQDN of the VCF Automation cluster
Workaround: Start the VCF deployment with lower case FQDNs for the listed components.
NFS Datastore Configuration validation fails for ESX hosts with a single physical network interface card (pNIC)
When deploying VCF 9.1 on ESX hosts with a single pNIC, the NFS Datastore Configuration validation step fails with
the following error message:
Failed to validate NFS configuration. NFS datastore mount failed on
host esx01.raipole.io: An error occurred during host configuration.
This validation failure prevents the deployment from proceeding even when NFS connectivity is actually functioning
correctly. The issue occurs because the validation check expects multiple physical NICs for redundancy.
Workaround: This is expected behavior and the configuration is unsupported. To proceed with the deployment, use 2 or
more pNICs.
Fleet lifecycle service produces workflow inconsistencies due to transient database connectivity issues
• Symptom 1: After a VCF deployment workflow completes successfully, certain component deployment tasks or
monitoring sub-tasks may remain displayed in an In Progress state in the VCF user interface, even though the
deployment has finished and the components are fully operational. This is a display issue only and does not indicate
any functional problems with the deployed infrastructure or services.
• Symptom 2: During a VCF deployment a component installation is triggered more than once. The subsequent
execution of the installation step fails because the component is already installed.
• Symptom 3: One or more steps within a VCF lifecycle task display no progress updates for more than two hours,
indicating the task is failed or stuck.
Workaround for symptoms 1 and 2: None. If the overall VCF deployment is reported as successful and the deployed
component is accessible and operational, ignore the task statuses. Alternatively, to verify that the deployment completed
successfully, perform the following tasks.
1. Verify the overall deployment status and if marked as successful, the deployment is complete.
2. Manually log into the deployed component's management interface.
3. Verify that all services are running and operational.
Workaround for symptom 3: To determine whether a task is stuck and which service to restart, see Broadcom knowledge
base article 435569.
Converging a vCenter instance that is already connected to a SDDC Manager, destroys existing Fleet
components
When converging existing infrastructure to a VCF Instance, if you select a vCenter instance that is already managed by
SDDC Manager, the new deployment destroys the fleet components of the first VCF Instance. During VCF management
services bootstrap, the second SDDC Manager deletes the shared vCenter folder used by the first VCF deployment,
resulting in the destruction of the primary VCF management services cluster and workers. The second VCF deployment
fails too.
Broadcom 523

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Important:
A warning message is displayed during the deployment workflow indicating that an existing SDDC Manager
extension is found on the vCenter instance. This warning does not prevent the deployment from proceeding.
Workaround: None. Redeploy the VCF Instance or restore it from backup.
During deferred components deployment, error messages appear in Depot settings and binary management
After deploying VCF, converting VCF Installer to SDDC Manager, and attempting to deploy deferred components (VCF
Operations and VCF Automation), the Depot settings and binary management page displays error messages, such as:
.
This API is no longer supported from VCF 9.1" along with depot connection errors
Workaround: Disregard the error messages. The Binary Management section functions correctly and allows you to
download required binaries and complete the deferred component deployment workflow.
Converging or importing an existing vCenter instance fails during validation with an error indicating that the NSX-
T Manager install image cannot be found for the required NSX version
When converging or importing an existing vCenter instance that is not connected to NSX, SDDC Manager automatically
deploys a new NSX Manager. The system selects the latest compatible NSX version based on your vCenter version and
VCF release. If the install image (bundle) for the selected NSX version is not available in the SDDC Manager depot, the
validation phase fails with an error message indicating which NSX version's install image is required.
Workaround: Download the NSX install image and retry the operation.
1. To identify the required NSX version, review the error message.
2. Download the required NSX-T Manager install image.
3. Retry the convergence or import operation.
Converging an existing vCenter instance with a non-compliant root password, fails
When converging an existing vCenter instance 8.0 Update 3 by using VCF Installer, the vCenter root user property is
mandatory in VCF Installer and the password must be between 15 and 20 characters now, even when the root password
is allowed to be between 8 and 20 characters in vCenter 8.0 Update 3.
Workaround: Change the vCenter root password. The password must be between 15 and 20 characters inclusive, have at
least 1 lower case letter, 1 upper case letter, 1 digit, and 1 special character, be made only of ASCII characters, and have
no white space.
SDDC Manager Known Issues
Initiating SDDC Manager upgrade pre-checks from the instance in Lifecycle tab in VCF Operations or from the
Available Upgrades tab in SDDC Manager Lifecycle Management UI fails with a
Triggering SDDC Manager
upgrade bundle failed
When you initiate upgrade pre-checks for SDDC Manager in VCF Operations (Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instances
> instance > SDDC Manager Upgrades tab) or SDDC Manager UI (Lifecycle Management > SDDC Manager >
Available Upgrades tab), the operation fails with a
Triggering SDDC Manager upgrade bundle failed.
A problem has occurred on the server. Please retry or contact the service provider and
error.
provide the reference token
Workaround: Initiate the upgrade pre-checks either from the Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instances > instance > domain >
Upgrades tab in the VCF Operations UI or the Inventory > Workload Domains > domain > Upgrades tab in the SDDC
Manager UI.
When converting a Virtual Volume (vVol) primary datastore to vSAN HCI, the add host operation fails when
validating L3 network data if the operation is performed before the client cluster is converted to vSAN HCI.
When converting a primary datastore from vVol to vSAN, the add host to the server cluster operation fails if it is performed
before the client cluster is converted to vSAN. Both the client and the server clusters must use the same storage
architecture.
Workaround: None.
Broadcom 524

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Deleting a vSphere cluster in SDDC Manager fails with error:
Error occurred while generating input for
.
remove workload for NSX Environment in NSX environment
If ESX hosts are NSX prepared out of band with some transport node profiles configured without an uplink profile, SDDC
Manager cannot delete the vSphere cluster.
Workaround: Reconfigure all transport node profiles with an uplink profile and restart the delete workflow in SDDC
Manager.
After SDDC Manager reboots during an upgrade to version 9.1, SDDC Manager core services fail to start
automatically
After the reboot operation of SDDC Manager during upgrade to version 9.1, the core services fail to start, which results in
prolonged service downtime and the user interface is also not accessible.
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
1. Log in to the virtual machine of SDDC Manager by using SSH, obtain root permissions and run the following
command:
for s in domainmanager operationsmanager lcm commonsvcs sddc-manager-ui-app; do echo
"--- $s ---"; systemctl status $s | grep -E "Active:|Loaded:"; done
2. In the command output, verify that the status for , , , and is
domainmanager operationsmanager lcm commonsvcs
inactive.
3. Reboot the appliance by running the command.
reboot
When management domain upgrade process is incomplete, VCF Operations user interface displays incorrect
upgrade status for the workload domain
When the management domain has pending upgrades, workload domains with fully completed upgrades to the target
Bill of Materials (BOM), might display AVAILABLE instead of UP TO DATE upgrade status. Fleet lifecycle incorrectly
calculates the upgrade availability, which results in displaying incorrect values in the user interface. The actual upgrade
operations through the user interface and API endpoints function correctly and are not affected by the display issue.
Workaround: Perform one for the following tasks.
• Complete the management domain upgrade to remove all pending bundles. Once the management domain completes
all pending upgrades, workload domains report upgrade status correctly.
• In the workload domain, verify that the NSX, vCenter, and ESX component versions match the target BOM versions. If
these versions match the target BOM, treat the AVAILABLE upgrade status as a false-positive.
When attempting an upgrade of SDDC Manager in an isolated workload domain configuration, the process might
fail
During SDDC Manager upgrade in a VCF 9.1 environment where vCenter instances of management and workload
domains are not linked and have dedicated Single Sign-On, when attempting to establish an SSH connection to a
management vCenter instance, the upgrade process might fail with the following error message:
Failed to SSH into
even when credentials are correct and SSH access is properly configured.
VCenter using root credentials
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
1. Log in to the SDDC Manager appliance.
2. Edit the file and add or modify the
/opt/vmware/vcf/lcm/lcm-app/conf/application-prod.properties
following parameter:
lcm.vcenter.ssh.precheck=false
3. Restart all SDDC Manager services by using the following command:
sh /opt/vmware/vcf/
operationsmanager/scripts/cli/sddcmanager_restart_services.sh
4. Retry the SDDC Manager upgrade.
SDDC Manager deployment with single uplink DVS configuration and NFS datastore fails
Using a single physical network adapter (pNIC) configuration for the distributed virtual switch (DVS) in combination with an
NFS datastore for SDDC Manager deployment is not supported and the operations fails.
Workaround: None.
Broadcom 525

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When performing pre-checks or an upgrade of selected ESX hosts, Hardware Compatibility List (HCL) checks are
performed on all hosts in the cluster
When performing pre-checks or upgrading selected ESX hosts in straddle state deployments, where SDDC Manager is at
version 9.1 and vCenter and ESXi are at version 9.0 or earlier, the HCL checks run on all hosts in the cluster, instead of
only on the selected hosts. Only the selected hosts are upgraded.
Workaround: None.
SDDC Manager does not reflect completed NSX dataplane upgrade status
After a successful NSX upgrade, SDDC Manager's inventory and lifecycle management cache might not reflect the
updated NSX-T dataplane version due to timeout or synchronization issues.
Workaround: The automatic version synchronization process resolves the discrepancy within 24 hours.
Alternatively, perform the following tasks to manually trigger version synchronization and update SDDC Manager inventory
immediately.
1. Confirm the NSX upgrade completed successfully on NSX Manager.
2. In the configuration file, set the
/etc/vmware/vcf/operationsmanager/application-prod.properties
flag to .
check.lcm.isVersionSyncRequired false
3. In SDDC Manager API, trigger version synchronization by executing a POST request to
/v1/resources/version-
with set to .
syncs resourceType SYSTEM
4. Wait approximately 5 minutes for the lifecycle management inventory refresh cycle to complete.
Optionally, trigger a manual lifecycle management inventory cache refresh using .
POST /lcm/inventory/refresh
5. Verify the bundle status reflects the correct NSX-T dataplane version by querying
GET /v1/bundles/domains/
and checking the entity status.
{domain-id} nsx_t_dataplane
On environments with enabled Persistent Memory (PMem), SoS health check shows Cluster vSAN Status and
Cluster Disk Status as RED.
In environments with Persistent Memory (PMem) enabled, the SoS health check can incorrectly report a status for
RED
and . This is a reporting issue specific to Persistent Memory (PMem)
Cluster vSAN Status Cluster Disk Status
enabled storage and can result in false health states during SoS storage health checks. Note that Persistent Memory and
all the associated features are deprecated and are not supported starting with VCF 9.0.
Workaround: None.
In the VCF Operations UI, log bundle generate, download, and delete operations are not available for VCF
Operations and VCF Operations for networks
In the VCF Operations user interface, the options to generate, download, or delete logs are not available for VCF
Operations and VCF Operations for networks.
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
• To generate a support bundle for VCF Operations, see Create a VCF Operations Support Bundle.
• To generate a support bundle for VCF Operations for networks, see Create a VCF Operations for networks Support
Bundle.
VCF Download Tool
VCF Download Tool displays incorrect .net URL after executing the generate --software-depot-id command
The output of the command contains a typographical error in the hardcoded string,
generate --software-depot-id
pointing to an incorrect domain instead of the public Broadcom domain. As a result, you cannot reach the direct access
page displayed by Use this link to register, such as:
$./bin/vcf-download-tool configuration get --software-depot-id
*********Welcome to VCF Download Tool***********
Version: 9.1.0.0.25172051 Use this link to register https://vcf.broadcom.net/vcf/clm/download-manager/
register?serviceId=######-####-####-####-######.
Alternatively login at https://vcf.broadcom.com, select Software depot Registration and use this Software
depot ID: ######-####-####-####-######
Broadcom 526

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 441033.
When Internet access is routed through a proxy server, the and
vcf-download-tool esx metadata vcf-
commands fail to authenticate
download-tool esx download
When network access to the Internet requires a proxy server, the and commands fail
esx metadata esx download
and return an authentication error. The VCF Download Tool does not apply the configured proxy settings to the OAuth
token request it sends to the Broadcom authentication endpoint. As a result, the tool attempts to reach the authentication
server directly, bypassing the proxy, and the request fails in environments where direct Internet access is not available.
Workaround: Download ESX binaries manually from the Broadcom Support Portal, then import them to software depot
or VCF Installer by using the command. For more information, see Broadcom
vcf-download-tool esx import
knowledge base article 442226.

Deployment and Upgrade
During upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1, after deployment of VCF management services, the remaining management
components do not appear in the VCF Operations inventory
During VCF upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1, after successful upgrade of VCF Operations and SDDC Manager and deployment
of VCF management services, the remaining existing management components are not migrated to the fleet lifecycle
component and do not appear in the VCF Operations inventory. No error messages or banners indicate that the import
failed. This issue occurs if a proxy server with SSL termination is configured in VCF Operations. The proxy server
prevents VCF Operations from communicating with the fleet lifecycle component.
Workaround: Follow the guidance for option 2 from Broadcom knowledge base article 441858.
Upgrading VCF Identity Broker in appliance mode from 9.0.x to 9.1 fails during validation
After upgrade of VCF Operations and SDDC Manager to 9.1, upgrading VCF Identity Broker 9.0.x in appliance mode
to identity broker 9.1 fails during the validation phase. With VCF 9.1, VCF Identity Broker transitions to being hosted by
VCF management services. As a result, to successfully upgrade to identity broker 9.1, VCF Identity Broker 9.0.x and VCF
management services must be deployed on the same network and on the same datastore. This issue occurs because one
of the following conditions is met:
• VCF Identity Broker in appliance mode is deployed on an NSX overlay segment. You cannot deploy VCF management
services on an NSX overlay segment.
Broadcom 527

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VCF Identity Broker in appliance mode is deployed on a different network than VCF management services.
• VCF Identity Broker in appliance mode is deployed on a different datastore than VCF management services.
Workaround: See Broadcom Knowledge Base Article 444734.
Upgrade from VCF 9.0.x to VCF 9.1 fails during the task
Deploy VCF Management Components
During upgrade from VCF 9.0.x to 9.1, the task fails at the
Deploy VCF Management Components Import VCF
step. The task fails due to invalid certificates, stale data in VCF Operations 9.1
Operations in Fleet Lifecycle
(for example, incorrect credentials), or connectivity issues for components previously managed by the VCF Operations
fleet lifecycle appliance.
Workaround: See Broadcom Knowledge Base Article 441858.
Upgrade from VCF Operations 9.0.1 or 9.0.2 to VCF Operations 9.1 fails at step 9 of 14:
Applied Operating
System Update
The upgrade to VCF Operations 9.1 might fail at step 9 of 14 with the following error message:
Failed resource
key=pak_manager.action_failed, resource args=[run master postgres db upgrade].
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 440200.
The Binary Management tab in VCF Operations lists the 9.1 VCF version option, but no 9.1 binaries appear as
available for download
This is expected behavior at this point, because the upgrade to version 9.1 starts with upgrading your VCF Operations to
version 9.1 by using a PAK file.
Workaround: To upgrade VCF to version 9.1, strictly follow the upgrade order of components as documented in the 9.1
product documentation: Upgrading to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.
After a VCF Operations upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1, VCF Automation, VCF Identity Broker, VCF Operations for
networks, or VCF Operations for logs might not appear in the VCF Operations UI
If VCF Automation, VCF Identity Broker, VCF Operations for networks, or VCF Operations for logs are deleted and then
imported in VCF Operations 9.0 prior to upgrading to VCF 9.1, these components do not appear in the inventory of VCF
Operations 9.1.
Workaround: See Broadcom Knowledge Base Article 441858.
When incorrect input is provided, vSAN Stretched Cluster expansion fails
vSAN Stretched Cluster expansion fails at step Add ESX Host(s) to vSphere Distributed Switch with the following error
message:
No available vmnic found on the host.
Workaround: Perform the tasks in kB 427183.
The Broadcom Support Portal link for cloud proxy download in the VCF Operations UI redirects to an incorrect
version (8.18) instead of the intended VCF 9.1
In the VCF Operations UI, the Broadcom Support Portal link used for downloading the cloud proxy OVA incorrectly
redirects users to version 8.18 instead of the expected 9.1 release. This could lead to deployment of an unsupported
cloud proxy version and potential compatibility issues.
Workaround: Manually navigate to the Broadcom Support Portal and download the correct cloud proxy OVA version (9.1)
by selecting it explicitly from the available versions list.
Licensing
After you upgrade a vCenter instance to version 9.1.0.0300, the vCenter instance does not appear on the
Licensing page in VCF Operations
After you upgrade a vCenter instance from version 9.0.x to version 9.1.0.0300, the vCenter instance does not appear
in the VCF Operations UI under Manage > Licensing, so you cannot assign a license to the vCenter instance. In the
vSphere Client, no licenses are displayed on the Administration page. There is no banner to indicate that there are
unlicensed assets.
Broadcom 528

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
A stale or orphaned vSphere+ subscription license in the vCenter LDAP database prevents the vCenter instance from
appearing in the VCF Operations UI.
Identify the stale vSphere+ license and manually delete the license from the vCenter LDAP database. For more details,
see Broadcom knowledge base article 455886.
The license server does not work properly and after the appliance boots, in the console you see a black screen
The license server uses the and IP address ranges for internal communications.
172.16.0.0/12 172.17.0.0/16
If you deploy the license server on the network or configure the license server to use a gateway that
172.16.0.0/12
advertises a routable path of , a network conflict occurs. As a result, you see only a black screen in the
172.17.0.0/16
license server console after booting.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 441526.
This issue is resolved starting with version 9.1.0.0200.
Build
Lifecycle
Pre-check functionality is not supported for upgrades of Log Management 9.x to 9.1
In the VCF Operations UI, the option to trigger a pre-check on the log management component might appear available for
the 9.0 to 9.1 upgrade path. Fleet lifecycle does not support pre-check for log management when upgrading from version
9.0 to 9.1.
Workaround: If pre-check is initiated, the task will result in a failure. You can safely ignore the pre-check task failure and
proceed with the upgrade.
Operate
vCenter adapter
vCenter data collection fails following an upgrade to VCF Operations 9.1
If a vCenter integration was originally configured using an IP address or FQDN that included trailing slashes or sub-paths
(for example, ), the collection mechanism in VCF 9.1 fails to
vcenter.example.com/, vcenter.example.com/ui
initialize. The new version requires a clean IP or FQDN without any trailing slashes or URL paths.
Workaround: Prior to upgrading to VCF 9.1, review all existing vCenter integration settings. Verify that the vCenter field
contains only the IP address or FQDN, and remove all trailing slashes or trailing URL paths.
Log Management
vCenter and ESX events or tasks show "Update parameter values" errors approximately every two minutes when
there is an HCX Migration Agent (MA) host in the vCenter
vCenter and ESX events/tasks display false positive errors such as "Update option values" and "A general system error
occurred" when there is an HCX Migration Agent (MA) host in the vCenter. This occurs because the log management
component attempts to configure ESX hosts, specifically enabling audit logs by default. But ESX HCX Migration Agent
(MA) hosts do not support this option. This does not affect the actual log collection process.
Workaround: To stop the frequent error messages, you can disable audit log collection for the corresponding vCenter,
though this will affect all ESX hosts managed by that vCenter.
1. Navigate to the Log Collection configuration page in the VCF Operations UI.
2. Edit the corresponding vCenter.
3. In the ESX section at the bottom of the page, uncheck the Audit checkbox and save the configuration.
4. The new configuration may take up to five minutes to apply, after which attempts to configure audit logs will be
suspended.
Log Collection Delay after Updating Adapter Hostnames from IP to FQDNSymptom
After updating the hostname configuration from an IP address to a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for NSX,
vCenter, Supervisor, or HCX adapter instances, it can take up to one hour for log collection to resume. Hostname
Broadcom 529

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
configuration changes in adapter instance settings are synchronized to the Log Management component every hour.
Consequently, when these hostnames are updated from an IP to an FQDN, log collection may not start working until the
next scheduled synchronization occurs.
Workaround: To immediately trigger log collection after a hostname update, manually disable and then re-enable log
collection from the adapter instance configuration page.
VM Log Tagging Discrepancy after vCenter Re-integration
VM logs retain an outdated {{vmw_vr_ops_id }}tag after a vCenter is deleted and subsequently added back to VCF
Operations. These logs fail to be correctly indexed or viewed via the Inventory page under the new vCenter object. When
a vCenter is removed and then added back to the same VCF Operations instance, the mapping mechanism on associated
VM logs continues to use the previous vmw_vr_ops_id. VCF Operations does not automatically update these logs with the
new identifier while an active agent continues to stream logs during the transition.
Workaround: Manually restart the Log Processor nodes to clear cached metadata and force a refresh of the ID
mappings. Use the following command:
kubectl rollout restart sts/log-processor -n ops-logs
SSO login to the VCF Operations for logs 9.0 UI fails after upgrading VCF Identity Broker to version 9.1
When VCF Identity Broker is upgraded to version 9.1, you cannot perform an SSO login to the VCF Operations for logs
9.0 user interface. This issue occurs because identity broker 9.1 transitions to a VCF services runtime instance that
hosts VCF management services, which uses the Server Name Indication (SNI) TLS extension to identify the correct
service certificate. When running in FIPS mode, the TLS stack utilized by VCF Operations for logs 9.0.x fails to send the
required SNI extension. Consequently, the gateway returns a default, untrusted certificate to the appliance, causing the
SSO authentication to fail. This issue specifically affects FIPS-enabled deployments, while non-FIPS deployments remain
unaffected.
Workaround: You can bypass by logging into the VCF Operations for logs 9.0 UI using a local, non-SSO account. Full
SSO functionality is completely restored after VCF Operations for logs is upgraded to version 9.1, as authentication is
then handled through VCF Operations and the updated UI.
VCF Operations for Logs Agent version 9.0.x fails to auto-upgrade to newer versions
VCF Operations for Logs Agent version 9.0.x is unable to perform automatic upgrades to newer versions. This issue is
caused by changes in the versioning scheme and the deprecation of SysV init systems.
Workaround: Manually install a newer version of the Log Management Agent.
A "Log Store Health Warning" alert appears for healthy single-node clusters
Single-node Log Store clusters are not recommended for production because they create a single point of failure. If you
use this configuration, the cluster health status remains "Yellow" in the VCF Operations administrative alert section. This
occurs because replica shards cannot be assigned to the same node as their primary shards. The system interprets this
as an availability issue and triggers a "Log Store Health Warning" on the dashboard.
Workaround: You can safely ignore this warning if you are intentionally running a single-node cluster.
Log forwarder SSL connections enforce strict certificate validation
Log forwarder fails to establish SSL connections and logs are not forwarded to configured destinations. SSL handshake
errors regarding hostname verification are displayed. If you are upgrading from earlier versions, you may experience
connection failures if existing log forwarder destinations use certificates that lack Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries,
even if the certificates contain valid Common Name (CN) fields. Starting in version 9.1, the log forwarder enforces strict
hostname verification during the SSL handshake. Connections fail if the destination's certificate lacks a valid SAN entry
matching the hostname, as the system no longer falls back to the Common Name (CN) for verification.
Always occurs when using SSL-enabled log forwarders with certificates that lack SAN fields after upgrading to version 9.1.
Workaround: Regenerate or update certificates for all log forwarder destinations to include valid SAN entries that
match the destination hostname or IP address. If using self-signed certificates, ensure the SAN field is populated during
certificate generation.
Data transfer from legacy clusters initiates for archived buckets only
Broadcom 530

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When initiating data transfer from legacy clusters, data from all archived buckets is copied to the target cluster, potentially
overlapping with the specified time interval. Only the most recent write buckets are active (non-archived) and data is not
migrated from these active buckets. You can verify bucket states on the legacy cluster using the command:
/usr/lib/
.
loginsight/application/sbin/bucket-index show
Workaround: None
Log Analysis page displays empty or partial results without error messages
The Log Analysis page in VCF Operations may display partial or empty results. Related alerts and dashboards are also
affected. If the backend experiences exceptions (such as CorruptIndexException or CircuitBreakingException), VCF
Operations handles these silently without displaying an error message to the user, making it unclear that the results are
incomplete.
Workaround: A fix has been introduced for CircuitBreakingException; however, there is currently no workaround for other
index-related exceptions.
Log collection should only be enabled in one VCF Operations instance for vCenter, NSX or other VCF
components
Enabling log collection for vCenter, NSX or other VCF component in a new VCF Operations instance overrides the
existing configuration of other instances. Log collection should only be enabled in one VCF Operations instance for
vCenter, NSX or other VCF components. Enabling it across multiple instances results in undefined behavior where only
one instance receives logs at a time.
Workaround: None
VCF Operations for Logs UI displays an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when pods are shut down
The user interface displays an "HTTP 500 Internal Server Error" when the service pods are scaled to zero or
ops-logs
shut down. When all pods are removed (during maintenance or shutdown), the Envoy Gateway returns an
ops-logs
HTTP 500 error instead of the expected HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable). Envoy Gateway proactively detects the lack
of healthy endpoints and programs a direct 500 response. If at least one pod exists (even if terminating), the gateway
correctly returns 503.
Workaround: None. This is cosmetic and does not indicate a functional failure. The service will resume normal operation
once pods are scaled back up.
Workbench
Real-Time Analysis displays "No data" for supported object types when core components are not upgraded to 9.1
During an upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, the Real Time Analysis tab in the Workbench may incorrectly display "No data"
for supported object types. This occurs in brownfield scenarios where management components have been upgraded,
but core components remain at a previous version. The Real Time Analysis tab does not currently provide a compatibility
warning or notification to indicate that core components require an upgrade to display metrics.
Workaround: None. This is a transient state during the upgrade process. Ensure all core components are upgraded to
version 9.1 to restore Real Time Analysis data visibility.
Real-time metrics
Real-time metrics data ingestion fails and data gaps appear in charts when the ClickHouse database reaches disk
capacity
When the ClickHouse storage becomes full, the system is unable to process or store incoming real-time metrics, resulting
in data loss. This occurs when the ingestion volume exceeds the provisioned disk space for the Real-time metrics
component.
Workaround: Increase the storage size for the Real-time metrics component by navigating to Build > Lifecycle > Real-
time Metrics > Increase Storage Size.
High ingestion loads cause real-time metrics pods to restart, resulting in intermittent data gaps in metric charts
During periods of significantly high data ingestion, real-time metrics pods may encounter instability and restart
unexpectedly. This behavior leads to temporary data loss or "holes" in metric charts for the duration of the restart period.
Broadcom 531

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: None.
Real-time metrics charts do not load when real-time metric data collection is not started
Real-time metrics charts fail to load in VCF Operations when a vCenter or NSX-T adapter instance under the VCF adapter
has never been started since configuration. This happens because the real-time metric data collection is not started. This
results in an ERROR status for the real-time metric adapter and prevents real-time metrics charts from loading.
Workaround: Manually start all instances of vCenter and NSX-T adapters under the VCF Adapter. The Real-time metrics
adapter will sync and return to a healthy status within 48 hours of enabling collection for all domains.
Real-time metrics data collection fails after a vCenter upgrade
Data collection fails if the real-time metrics component was deployed before upgrading vCenter to version 9.1. If vCenter
is upgraded after the real-time metrics component is already deployed, the system fails to enable data collection post-
upgrade.
Workaround: From the real-time metrics Day-2 actions menu, stop the service and then start the service to resume
collection.

bootstrap-launcher.bat
When running t during the UAC agent installation flow, the installation fails with the

following traceback:

The status for content upgrades of product-managed Telegraf agents may intermittently show as failed following
the upgrade of VCF Operations and cloud proxies
After upgrading VCF Operations and Cloud Proxies from 8.18.6 or 9.0.2 to 9.1.0.0, the content upgrade operation on
product-managed Telegraf agents may intermittently report a "Content Upgrade Failed" status in the UI. The actual agent
content upgrade on the endpoint completes successfully; however, a post-upgrade step ("maintain-agent-status") can time
out due to an asynchronous Salt Minion service restart, causing the overall operation to be marked as failed. This is more
frequently observed on application monitoring HA-enabled collector groups with multiple monitored VMs.
Workaround: Retry the content upgrade on the affected agents. The Telegraf agent content on the endpoint is already
upgraded to the target version; only the status in the UI is incorrect.
Audit Records
Audit record counts might not match the left navigation filters
In high-volume environments with large numbers of audit records (auditIDs) within a specific time period, the underlying
query engine (Log Management) may encounter limitations when returning large aggregation totals. As a result, certain
audit record counts may be excluded from the Category or Object Type filters.
• To address this, No Object and No Category Type fields have been added to the user interface to display missing
data counts.
• These fields are for display purposes only and are disabled for selection in queries.
• The system enforces a cap of 50 aggregations for audit records. Consequently, the Category and Object Type filters
will only display the top 50 audit record counts.
• The line chart on the Audit Trail page does not dynamically update when a filter is changed due to a UI framework
restriction. To improve clarity, the chart title has been updated to Total Records Timeline by Result.
Workaround: Deselecting VMSP can provide more accurate count displays.

Broadcom 532

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VKS 1.35.0+ clusters are not being discovered by VCF Operations for networks. Consequently, users cannot see these
clusters and the Antrea flows associated with them in VCF Operations for networks. These flows are also missing from the
Operate > Flows section in the VCF Operations.
Workaround: None
Existing VCF Operations for networks collector nodes are not imported or managed by fleet lifecycle
In VCF 9.1, fleet lifecycle does not import existing VCF Operations for networks collector nodes. As a result, these nodes
do not appear in the fleet lifecycle inventory and cannot be managed for lifecycle tasks through VCF Operations.
Workaround:Day-N actions and management tasks for VCF Operations for networks collectors can be performed by
following VCF Operations for networks guidance. For detailed, step-by-step instructions about performing these actions,
see Network Inventory.
Support Bundle generation for VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks is not available in Fleet
Lifecycle
The ability to generate and download support bundles for VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks components
is not available directly within the fleet lifecycle interface in VCF 9.1. Support bundle generation and download for VCF
Operations and VCF Operations for networks components is not integrated into fleet lifecycle for VCF 9.1.
Workaround: To collect support bundles, users must log in to the respective native product console for generation and
download. Refer to the product-specific documentation for instructions:
• For VCF Operations, please see Create a Support Bunde in VCF Operations.
• For VCF Operations for networks, please see Create a Support Bundle in VCF Operations for Networks.
Developer Center
The PowerCLI card on the APIs & SDKs page under Developer Center displays an outdated install command,
directing users to install the legacy VMware.PowerCLI 13.3 module instead of the current VCF.PowerCLI 9.x
On the APIs & SDKs page (Build > Developer Center > APIs & SDKs), the PowerCLI card instructs users to install
PowerCLI by running "Install-Module -Name VMware.PowerCLI". This installs VMware PowerCLI 13.3, which only
supports vSphere 8 and earlier versions. The current module has been renamed to VCF.PowerCLI starting with version
9.x, which supports both legacy versions and VCF 9.0 and later versions. The legacy module does not support VCF
Operations and lacks a smooth transition path to VCF 9.0.
Workaround: Users can manually install the correct module by visiting https://developer.broadcom.com/powercli to
download and install VCF.PowerCLI 9.x instead of following the command shown on the PowerCLI card.
Workload Mobility

is not compatible with VMware Operations HCX version 9.
The PowerCLI module for HCX Manager (VMware.VimAutomation.Hcx) included in all versions of VCF.PowerCLI is
compatible with HCX version 4.11 and no later.
