Multicast traffic on extended network in trunk mode fails to reach the other side.
Multicast traffic across an overlay to overlay extended network in trunk mode does not work.
Workaround:
Switch the bridge mode from trunk (multiple extensions per vNIC) to single extension per vNIC.
Option-1:
1. Create a new service mesh SM2 with overlay to overlay container pair in trunk mode.
2. Update SM2's bridge mode from "trunk-bridge" to "single-bridge"
Broadcom 533

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Transition the affected network from SM1 to SM2.
Option 2:
1. Un-extend all the extensions from SM1 with overlay to overlay container pair in trunk mode
2. Update SM1's bridge mode from "trunk-bridge" to "single-bridge" for appliances having overlay to overlay network
container pair
3. Extend all the networks back on SM1.
For an existing appliance pair, the bridge mode can be changed by running the following command at respective HCX
managers:/opt/vmware/bin/interconnectDebugUtils.sh modifyBridgeMode <local-appliance-id> single.
Redeploying the HCX Edge appliance with the local=true flag results in the tunnel going down.
Redeploying the HCX Edge appliance with the local=true flag results in the tunnel going down.
Perform the redeploy via API by explicitly setting the local=false parameter to ensure proper state synchronization, or use
the HCX Manager UI which, by default, maintains symmetry by redeploying both the local and remote peer appliances
simultaneously.
Downtime of in-service redeployment of an edge based NE mesh took more than 10 sec.

minute.

Force power off is not allowed from API when bulk migration is in progress.

Fleet Management
Batch precheck of upgrade plan for all VCF management components fails with the validation error
VCF_LCM_FLEET_UPGRADE_400_COMPONENT_NOT_NEEDED_USER_INPUT_SPEC_PROVIDED
This issue occurs when a component's user input specification remains configured after the component has already been
upgraded to its target version. If you then click Run Prechecks (ALL), or use Select All on the VCF Management >
Upgrade page without selecting individual components, the precheck runs against the full upgrade plan. Because the plan
includes a user input spec for a component that no longer requires one, the validation fails and returns the error above.
Workaround: Do not use the Run Prechecks (ALL) option. Instead, select the checkbox for each component you want to
precheck individually, and then run the prechecks.
Deletion of an existing folder causes Day-N actions that provision new VCF services runtime nodes to fail
If you use the vCenter UI to move VCF services runtime or VCF Automation VMs from a folder or resource pool to another
folder or resource pool after deployment, then delete the old folder or resource pool, any day-N operations that trigger
VCF services runtime node rollouts will fail.
Workaround: Before deleting the old folder or resource pool, update deployment values in the VCF services runtime
package to reference the new folder or resource pool to which VMs are being moved. This action triggers a rollout of the
VCF service runtime nodes and will create new VMs in the newly specified resource pool or folder.

scheduled RoleSync job (running on a 1-hour interval) re-establishes connectivity and syncs role data.

The following known issues impact the functionality included in the VCF Automation 9.1 Provider Management UI.

Namespace creation might fail due to an image synchronization timeout when a content library contains many
VM images
When a project-scoped content library contains a large number of VM images, the image registry might take longer than
the default 15-minute timeout to synchronize. This delay causes the namespace creation to fail.
Workaround: Increase the maximum number of readiness check attempts to 60 by running a script on the VCF
Automation host.
1. Back up the VCF Automation appliance.
2. Set the kubeconfig environment variable to point to the VCF Automation cluster.
export KUBECONFIG=vcfa.kubeconfig
3. Run the following command to apply the workaround script.
base64 -d <<<
""
| bash
4. Access the cell management tool and verify that the timeout value is .
60
kubectl -n prelude exec tenant-manager-0 -- bash
/opt/vmware/vcloud-director/bin/cell-management-tool
manage-config -l vcfa.contentLibrary.namespace.attach.readiness.check.max.attempts
Imported users and groups cannot log in to the VCF interface
Users and groups successfully imported into VCF Automation cannot log in to the VCF interface, even though they appear
in the Access Control list. This problem occurs when there is a format mismatch between the identity provider (IDP)
attribute mappings and the credentials that the user enters. If the IDP returns an attribute, such as an email address or
UPN, in a format that does not exactly match the login string or group name, the authentication handshake fails.
Workaround: There is no workaround available in the VCF Automation user interface. You must correct the attribute
mappings in your IDP configuration so that the returned attributes exactly match the user credentials and group names.
Region quota updates fail when a content library is in a Partially Ready state
When a backing vCenter content library is deleted directly in vCenter, VCF Automation retains a dangling reference to
that library. This state causes the content library to appear as in the Organization UI and prevents
Partially Ready
successful updates to the region quota for the organization. Region quota updates fail with an error:

messages = [LocalizableMessage (com.vmware.vapi.std.localizable_message) =>

b880-498c-885f-90ac585bcc36 not found., args = [8132d356-b880-498c-885f-90ac585bcc36], params =
<null>, localized = <null> }
],
Workaround: Delete the affected content library from the Organization UI. After you remove the dangling reference, region
quota updates proceed successfully.
Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) operations time out and fail
If you remove a vCenter instance from VCF Automation without first deleting its associated key providers, the system
retains the key providers in a failed state. This accumulation of failed key providers causes resource contention and
blocks communication. As a result, BYOK operations, such as registering a key provider, generating an encryption key, or
publishing a key provider to a tenant, fail with a timeout error.

Runtime Defined Entities (RDEs) associated with the removed vCenter instance.

2. Identify and delete the following encryption management CRs for the failed key provider registration:
–
SystemKeyProvider

–
KeyProvider
–
OrgKeyProvider
3. Identify and delete the following encryption management RDE instances for the failed key provider registration:
–
KeyProvider
–
KeyProviderStatus
–

High API load on VCF Automation during data collection
In large-scale environments, VCF Operations might overwhelm VCF Automation with frequent API calls. By default, the
system attempts to fetch entity information every 5 minutes. In high-density configurations, the API requests can overlap
and potentially destabilize the environment.
Workaround: To reduce the VCF Automation load in large-scale environments, manually adjust the collection intervals and
thread pool settings.
1. Use the VCF Operations UI to set the collection interval to 40 minutes and the Advanced Metrics Collection Interval to
240 minutes.
2. Modify the adapter configuration.
a. Log in to the VCF Operations node.
b. Edit the
/usr/lib/vmware-vcops/user/plugins/inbound/automation_adapter/conf/
file.
automation.properties
c. Update the thread pool and timeout properties as follows:
RESOURCE_COLLECT_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=5
RELATIONSHIP_COLLECT_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=5
METRICS_COLLECT_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=10
RESOURCE_COLLECTION_TIMEOUT_IN_MS=3600000
RELATIONSHIP_COLLECTION_TIMEOUT_IN_MS=3600000
METRIC_COLLECTION_TIMEOUT_IN_MS=3600000
3. To apply the changes, restart the adapter instance collection.

Deactivating the Provider Outbound NAT setting does not remove the NAT IP block reference in the database
When you deactivate the Provider Outbound NAT setting as a Day-2 operation, the corresponding NAT IP block does

When you create a centralized connection for shared services and you select the Provider Outbound NAT checkbox, the

Avi load balancer instance deployed via SDDC manager is automatically registerd to VCF Automation at next

Organization Management
The following known issues impact the functionality included in the VCF Automation organization UI.
Clicking Templates or Deployments in a VM Apps organization redirects the user to VCF Automation Provider
Management UI
In VM Apps organizations, when a user who has both an Organization Administrator role and a System Administrator role
attempts to access resource pages like Templates, Deployments, Custom Resources, Resource Actions, or Actions under
Infrastructure > Projects, the browser navigates away from the organization. The user is redirected to the VCF Automation
Provider Management UI instead of the intended page within the organization UI.
Workaround:
1. Log in directly to the VM Apps organization UI with the organization administrator credentials instead of accessing the
organization through the VCF Automation Provider Management UI as a System Administrator.
2. Ensure administrative activities within the organization are performed using dedicated organization accounts.
Create known issue document regarding issue UBMVCFA-25345
Sample:
Known Issue: Redirect to Provider Portal when clicking Templates or Deployments in VCF Automation 9.1.0
Article Metadata
• Document Type: Known Issue Article
• Products Affected: VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Automation 9.1.0 (classic soft tenancy)
• Severity: High (UI / Navigation — Loss of Tenant Context)
• Status: Resolved in Main / Target Fix Version 9.1.2
• Date: September 23, 2026
Symptoms
In VCF Automation 9.1.0 classic (soft) tenancy environments, when a user who holds both an Organization Administrator
(or First User) role and a System Administrator role attempts to navigate project resources, clicking resource links such as
Templates, Deployments, Custom Resources, Resource Actions, or Actions under Infrastructure > Projects results in an
unexpected redirection:
1. The browser navigates away from the active organization context (/tenant/$org/automation).
2. The user lands directly on the Provider Portal (/provider) instead of the requested Templates or Deployments page
within their organization.
Cause
This issue occurs due to cross-context HTML navigation link handling:
Broadcom 539

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• The resource-count navigation links under Infrastructure > Projects were rendered as absolute anchor tags (<a
href="..." target="_top">) that omitted the /tenant/$org/ URL segment.
• Clicking these links forces a full browser reload rather than an in-app Single Page Application (SPA) route update,
discarding the active organization context.
• During the subsequent OIDC re-authentication without an organization hint, users with dual roles (Organization
Administrator and System Administrator) default to the System organization, causing VCF Automation to automatically
redirect the browser to the Provider Portal (/provider).
Workaround
To avoid unexpected redirects to the Provider Portal:
1. Log in directly to the Tenant Portal (e.g., https://<vcf-automation-host>/tenant/<org-name>) using tenant-scoped
user credentials rather than accessing tenant resources through the Provider Portal as a System Administrator.
2. Ensure administrative activities within a tenant organization are performed using dedicated tenant organization
accounts without system-level role ambiguity.
Resolution & Fix Information
This issue is permanently addressed in code (PR #45348) by updating the navigation handlers to use in-app SPA routing
and preserving tenant context across all project navigation links.
• Target Fix Version: VCF Automation 9.1.2

Blueprint deployment fails with the Counter Exhausted error
By default, when a new custom naming has a template with , this indicates that the maximum digits that the naming
${##}
template can have is 99. If a VM reaches the 99 digit limit, the next request fails with the error .
Counter Exhausted
When the custom naming needs a counter appended at the end of the template, for example, , it generates
myvm-${##}
a counter that is incremented each time a new number is needed. Once the max limit is reached, the deployment fails with
the error . Names are in the range from to .
Counter Exhausted myvm-01 myvm-99
Workaround: Increase the template counter size.
1. In the existing custom name template, delete the specific resource template, for example, the template.
Machine
Important:
Do not delete the entire custom name template.
2. Create a new resource template for the specific resource with a larger counter size. For example, change
myvm-
to so you get a maximum of 999 counters.
${##} myvm-${###}
3. Set the starting counter to 99. By setting the starting counter to 99, the next counter starts from 100 onwards so that
existing VMs with counters from 01-99 can maintain the same name, avoiding conflicting counters.
Broadcom 540

Approval request emails not sent to approvers
In approval policies, if the approval is assigned to a project administrator which is an AD group, group members do not get

Selecting a namespace class and region before selecting a project causes a 404 error when creating a
namespace
When creating a namespace, if the user selects a namespace class and a region but does not select a project, VCF

Workaround: Clear the namespace class and region selection, select a project, and then reselect the namespace class
and/or region.
Upfront pricing is not supported for vSphere Supervisor version 9.0.x
Upfront pricing is only supported for VCF Automation 9.1 when integrated with vCenter 9.1 and VCF Operations 9.1.
Trying to fetch upfront pricing for deployments in a region on a vSphere Supervisor 9.0.x fails with an internal server error.
Workaround: Upgrade vSphere Supervisor to version 9.1.
IP Allocations UI fails with a 504 Timeout error in scaled organizations with over 500 IP blocks
In the VCF Automation organization UI, users cannot access the IP Allocations page to view or release IP block allocation
states. This issue specifically affects scaled organizations that contain more than 500 IP blocks within a single region.
When attempting to load the page, the request eventually fails and displays a timeout error message.
This issue is caused by a combination of UI data-fetching behavior and pagination limitations within the underlying
NSX API. To render the IP Allocations page, the UI attempts to fetch the allocation states for all IP blocks in a region
simultaneously. However, the maximum page size supported by the NSX IPBlockAllocationState API is 10 items per
request.
In a scaled environment with more than 500 IP blocks, the backend service must execute 50 or more consecutive API
calls to fulfill the single UI request. If the cumulative response time for these calls exceeds one minute, the API gateway
drops the connection, resulting in a 504 Gateway timeout.
Workaround: To bypass the timeout and successfully view or release IP allocations, the organization administrator can
use the VCF Automation CLI to manage the resources directly through the Kubernetes API.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation CLI and configure your kubectl context to access the organization.
2. List all IP blocks for the organization by running the following command.
kubectl --context=cci get ipblocks -A
Broadcom 541

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Example output:

:ext-ip-blk2 region1 20.20.1.0/24 External Realized 111m

default-tgw-region1 region1 172.31.0.0/16 Private Realized 109m

3. View the allocation states for a specific IP block. Identify the target IP block from the previous step and use the
get
command to inspect its details. (Example: Viewing IPBlock :ext-ip-blk1)
kubectl --context=cci get ipblockallocationstates :ext-ip-blk1 -o yaml

The Bills page doesn't renew the authorization token
The Bills page on the Administer tab stops working or shows authorization session errors after the user has been on
the page for more than five minutes. This is caused by a short-lived iframe URL token. When the token is not renewed,
subsequent actions on the Bills page run with an expired token and fail until the user leaves or reloads the page.
Workaround: Navigate away from the Bills page and then open Bills again so a new token is fetched and a fresh URL is
loaded.
Broadcom 542

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Namespaces cannot have more than 1,000 shared subnets
When creating or updating a namespace, you cannot assign more than 1,000 shared subnets to the namespace.
No workaround.
The Edit button for namespaces is visible to project administrators even though they do not have the
permissions to perform the action
Project administrators see an active Edit button on the namespace page in the VCF Automation organization UI, even
though they cannot actually edit the namespace.
No workaround.
Lists for VM classes and storage classes on a namespace class only display the first 128 entries
When viewing or editing a namespace class in the VCF Automation organization UI, the interface retrieves available VM
classes and storage classes using a default page size limit. In large-scale environments where the total number of classes
across all associated regions exceeds 128, the list is truncated. Affected users are unable to view or assign classes that
fall outside the initial 128 returned items, even though those classes are valid and present in the underlying system. This
issue occurs in any organization where the combined total of VM classes or storage classes across all regions exceeds
128.
Workaround: If you need to assign a class that does not appear in the truncated list, use one of the following methods:
• Search by name. Use the Add dialog to query and add individual VM classes or storage classes by their specific name.
• Wildcard selection. Use the wildcard * selection, where supported, to include all available classes regardless of the
display limit.
• API update. Use the VCF Automation APIs to update the namespace class directly. This bypasses the UI display limit
and ensures all intended classes are associated correctly.
File upload fails or is canceled when the user navigates away from the content library page
After submitting the upload form for a VM image (tenant) or a content library item (provider content library), the user is
brought to the content library list page. If the user then navigates to another part of the application while the upload is still
in progress, the system cancels all in-flight network requests including the upload. A warning is displayed advising the
user to stay on the page until the upload is complete, which disappears once the upload finishes.
Workaround: Stay on the content library upload page for the entire duration of the upload without navigating away.
The SubnetConnectionBindingMap resource is not captured during namespace capture
When capturing a namespace as a blueprint, the resource is not captured.
SubnetConnectionBindingMap
Workaround: After the namespace capture is complete, add the following resource to the blueprint manually.
subnetConnBindingMap_binding-vlan-1701:
type: CCI.Supervisor.Resource
dependsOn:
- <subnet_1>
- <subnet_2>
properties:
context: ${resource["Namespace"].id}
manifest:
apiVersion: crd.nsx.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: SubnetConnectionBindingMap
metadata:
name: <name>
spec:
subnetName: <subnetName>
targetSubnetName: <targetSubnetName>
vlanTrafficTag: <trafficTag>
When capturing a namespace as a blueprint, the Publish to catalog option might not be enabled due to warnings
related to guest customization
Broadcom 543

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When capturing a namespace as a blueprint, if any of the virtual machines are customized, users see a warning message
that the guest customization will be removed in the generated blueprint. In VCF Automation 9.1, if any warnings are
present, then the Publish to catalog option is not enabled in the UI.
Workaround: Even though the Publish to catalog option is not enabled, user can still generate the blueprint. Once the
blueprint is generated, go to the blueprint, verify it, and manually publish it to catalog. See Publish a Blueprint to the
Catalog in VCF Automation.
During namespace capture, users might see a warning message about a missing mandatory infrastructure policy
When a namespace is created, mandatory infrastructure policies are automatically applied. When capturing a namespace
as a blueprint, however, VCF Automation incorrectly checks for mandatory infrastructure policies and displays a warning
message that the policies are missing.
Workaround: Dismiss the warning message. The namespace capture will succeed and users can successfully go on to
deploy the generated blueprint.
VPC LoadBalancer setting is missing from captured blueprints
When a namespace is captured into a blueprint, the load balancer property of the associated dedicated VPC is not
preserved. This occurs because the blueprint VPC resource schema does not support the load balancer attribute.
Resources deployed from such blueprints, like VMs, fail to receive expected external IP addresses which might lead to
connectivity issues.
Workaround: The organization administrator must perform the following procedure.
1. After the VPC is created in the VCF Automation organization UI, navigate to Manage & Govern > VPC.
2. Toggle on the load balancer setting.
When capturing a blueprint into a project content library, items cannot be renamed in the organization UI
When capturing a namespace as a blueprint in a project content library, the captured images have auto-generated names
that cannot be changed using the VCF Automation UI.
No workaround.
Creating a project content library fails with an internal server error in mixed tenancy mode
After upgrading from VMware Aria Automation 8.x, vCenter cloud accounts are imported as connections in a VCF
Automation VM Apps organization. These connections can be used to create regions assigned to All Apps organizations
so an All Apps organization can have region quota in a supervisor that is managed by the vCenter cloud account used
in the VM Apps organization as a result of the upgrade. However, the connection is not automatically updated to use the
service credentials with the necessary permissions because this is managed in the VM Apps organization. As a result,
users in All Apps organizations cannot create project content libraries that are associated with that region.
Workaround: Add the user account used by the vCenter connection endpoint to the SupervisorProviderAdministrators
group in vCenter, which manages the respective supervisor/region, to give users the ability to create project content
libraries in that particular region.
Project level content library creation fails because of incompatible vCenter and vSphere Supervisor versions
Project content libraries require that both vCenter and the underlying vSphere Supervisor are at version VCF 9.1.
Attempts to create a project content library on a Supervisor that is not upgraded to version 9.1 fail.
Workaround: Upgrade vCenter and vSphere Supervisor to version 9.1.
Updating the name or description of an item in a project content library fails with a timeout error
When you update the name or description of an item in a project content library, the update times out after around 25
minutes and fails. The item ends up in a state.
FAILED
Workaround: After the update times out and fails, refresh the content library to recover the item.

When editing a project content library, users cannot change the storage class used by any of the regions that the content

No workaround.

projects.packages.broadcom.com

Networking Issues
After reloading the bnxtroce driver several times, network traffic might intermittently stop
If for some reason the bnxtroce driver unloads and reloads several times in a sequence, the driver might start dropping
unknown unicast traffic. As a result, the network traffic might intermittently stop. The issue occurs due to a rare race
condition in modifying tagged unicast traffic to unknown unicast address when Promiscuous Mode is active.

vCenter and vSphere Client Issues
You see Service Accounts and Solution Users under Configuration > Users and Groups in the vSphere Client
In VCF 9.0, instead of only accounts with which individuals are signing in, you can also see Service Accounts and
Solution Users under Configuration > Users and Groups in the vSphere Client.
This issue is resolved in this release. With VCF 9.1, you see only the accounts with which individuals are signing in
under Configuration > Users and Groups in the vSphere Client. The full list of the service accounts and solution users
is internal to vCenter and you can retrieve it by using the dir-cli command line tool. For more information, see dir-cli
Command Reference.

In large environments, when remediation operations run in a single batch, you might see intermittent timeout errors during
the host scanning phase. In the vSphere Client, you see errors such as:

The issue occurs not because any task fails, but because the status request waits in the queue longer than the 30-second
threshold.

vSphere Lifecycle Manager Issues
Creating a vSphere Lifecycle Manager image might fail even when the corresponding depots are imported
In rare cases, when multiple offline and online depots are imported into the vSphere Lifecycle Manager, the metadata
of one depot might overwrite the metadata of a previously imported depot and effectively remove the older depot.
As a result, when you try to create a desired image based on the deleted depot, during draft validation, the task
fails. In the logs, you see an error that depends on the depot that is missing, for example:
Software Solution
. This
com.vmware.vsphere-wcp with version 9.0.1.31.6.0-24913416 cannot be found in depot
issue is more likely to occur in VCF environments where the depots imported in the vSphere Lifecycle Manager come
from multiple sources.
vSAN
This document contains the following sections
• vSAN
vSAN
vSAN host crash (PSOD) caused by malformed network packets
Previously, in some enviroments vSAN hosts could crash with a Purple Screen of Death (PSOD) when receiving
malformed or corrupt network packets. The crash occurred in the vSAN Cluster Monitoring, Membership, and Directory
Service (CMMDS) layer, which is responsible for maintaining cluster state and membership across all hosts in a vSAN
cluster.
This has been fixed. vSAN has enhanced the verification of vSAN CMMDS traffic by doing full-payload checksum
verification. This ensures the integrity CMMDS traffic by detecting data corruption or tampering during transmission, which
improves resiliency amd avoids potential PSOD situations.

After upgrading the SDDC Manager appliance from 5.2.2 to 9.0.2, you see a 502 gateway error
The Plan Upgrade wizard displays the NSX appliance build number, rather than the NSX component build number

of the NSX component build number. The displayed build number can then differ before and after the upgrade. This is a
cosmetic issue only, it does not affect the upgrade process.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
An error occurred when validating VMware Cloud Foundation compatibility: File with Compatibility Matrix
Content for Compatibility controller VMWARE_COMPAT is not found. Please refer to error message above and
contact support for more details.
Pre-checks and validations take longer than expected when running VCF Installer and SDDC Manager workflows
in large environments
In VCF 9.0.1, cluster pre-checks perform additional lookups per ESX host through vCenter. In large environments, the
cluster pre-checks scale per host, which may add significant time for an operation to complete. Affected workflows are
add/remove ESX host from cluster, stretch cluster, add / expand / shrink / remove NSX Edge cluster, upgrade readiness
pre-check, converge and synchronize existing virtual infrastructure, and import an existing vCenter.
If ESX hosts are unreachable during a decommission operation, SDDC Manager does not release VMKNIC IP
addresses to the associated network pool
During a host decommission workflow, if the associated ESXi hosts are not reachable during the VMKNIC clean-up phase,
SDDC Manager does not fail the workflow and removes the ESX hosts from the inventory. The VMKNIC IP addresses
associated with the ESX hosts are not returned to the free list in the network pool.
VCF Operations does not display available vSphere Lifecycle Manager images when importing an image from a
vCenter
After you create a vSphere Lifecycle Manager image in vCenter and you attempt to import the image in VCF Operations,
the Import Image dialog box does not display the existing image. This happens because SDDC Manager cannot retrieve
the vCenter image repository.
Validation fails with the following error message:
The uplinks [uplink2, uplink1] used in the NSX
teaming specification are not part of the uplinks defined [<uplink2-custom>, <uplink1-
custom>] in the input specification for the Distributed Virtual Switch <vds-name>
If you edit the uplink names when configuring the vSphere Distributed Switch, those custom names are not applied to the
NSX traffic settings, leading to the validation error.
VCF Operations appliance deployment fails if the password contains "?"
When you deploy a new VCF fleet and specify a password containing a "?" for the VCF Operations appliance or the VCF
Operations collector appliance, the VCF Installer validation does not report an issue, but the deployment fails.
Retrying a failed deployment fails
When you deploy the VCF Installer appliance on one of the ESX hosts that will be used for the management domain and
the deployment of a new VCF fleet or VCF Instance fails, retrying the deployment may fail if you are using vSAN storage.
This issue occurs because the VCF Installer does not clean up the vSAN datastore that gets created on the ESX host
during the initial failed deployment. The domain manager log files will contain an error similar to
The cache disk/s
.
[<vsan-disk-id>] is/are in an invalid state.
Required hosts information for a vSAN OSA datastore does not reflect the deployment model
When you deploy a new VCF fleet or a new VCF Instance and choose vSAN OSA storage, the "Required hosts"
information displayed in the deployment wizard may be misleading if you chose the high availability deployment model.
For example, if you specify "1" for the "Failures to Tolerate" (FTT), the deployment wizard says that three ESX hosts are
required, when high availability requires a minimum of four ESX hosts.
VMware Cloud Foundation deployment fails if the SDDC Manager FQDN includes uppercase letters
Deploying a new VCF fleet or VCF Instance fails when deploying SDDC Manager if the SDDC Manager FQDN includes
uppercase letters. The logs show an error related to .
CS_APPLIANCE_CERT_ALIAS_LOWERCASE
VCF Installer deployment fails when configuring the vSphere cluster
When you deploy VMware Cloud Foundation or VMware vSphere Foundation using the VCF Installer, the deployment can
fail if you specify IP segments that are already in use by other components.
Validation fails in the VCF Installer if any of the vSphere Distributed Switch names include a space or special
character
Broadcom 551

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If you include a space or special character in the name of any vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS), deployment fails at
vSAN Network Connectivity and the error message
A problem has occurred on the server. Please retry
is displayed.
or contact the service provider and provide the reference token.
The VCF Installer UI validations incorrectly allow duplicate FQDN inputs that differ only by letter case
The UI validation for FQDNs incorrectly treats certain entries as unique. For example, Example.com and example.com are
considered distinct. The final validation, which uses the validation API, correctly identifies the FQDNs as duplicates, but
the user must go back and and manually fix the issue.
When you deploy VCF Operations with High Availability, anti-affinity rule is not configured
The anti-affinity rule ensures that all virtual machines associated with it are placed on separate hosts at all times, ensuring
high availability of the VCF Operations cluster. Without the anti-affinity rule, the VCF Operations nodes could end up on a
single host, which could lead to all VCF Operations nodes going down if that host fails.
VCF Installer displays incorrect evaluation period
When you deploy a new VCF fleet and you select the option to configure custom networking for VCF Operations and VCF
Automation, the VCF Installer reports that you must apply a VCF license within the 60-day evaluation period. The actual
evaluation period is 90 days.
VCF Installer validation error
vCenter Server root password must be at least 15 characters
When you use the VCF Installer to deploy a VCF instance or VCF Fleet using an existing vCenter, you will get a validation
error if the vCenter root password is too short. This can happen if the vCenter was upgraded to 9.0 from a previous
version that accepted shorter passwords.
Deploying a new VCF fleet or VCF Instance with an existing vCenter and a new NSX Manager fails
If the existing vCenter has a large number of hosts or clusters, the import task may fail during NSX transport node
creation. The domain manager log shows the following error message:
exceeded request rate of 100 per
.
second
VCF Installer does not support IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking
Validation fails in the VCF Installer if you have dual-stack networking configured on your ESX hosts.

NSX Edge logs spammed with log: Query to /var/run/vmware/edge/dpd.ctl failed with lrouter with the UUID or

Edge log errors triggering alarms in custom vRNI monitoring. There is no functionality impact.
VRF remains in the 'InProgress' state during deletion.

Bare Metal edges run out of memory.
Stale ComputeManager ID references in internal tables might prevent realization of subnets folders/DVPGs.

segments.
Log-ins to NSX Manager are intermittently failing with the following error: Failed to use SAMAccountName,
attempting UserPrincipleName: Invalid credentials.
Unable to log in to NSX Manager.
Post upgrade, proton startup is taking a very long time. The upgrade is unable to progress and fails.
NSX manager upgrade failed on start_manager. Proton startup during an upgrade takes a very long time.
The API to get the cluster certificate is not returning the right certificate.
Compute Manager fails to create its connection with vCenter because it has the wrong cluster certificate.
Rare BGP flaps when the TCP source port is reused for the same source and destination IPs on another VRF.
Unexpected flap for correctly configured BGP session.
After PUB upload, the stage operation fails with NullPointerException.
No impact. Users can stage the upgrade bits post MUB upload and UC upgrade.
Not all vNIC might receive multicast traffic even if the multicast address and ICMP SNOOP are enabled.
Applications that depend on multicast functionality might break.
VMs intermittently lose their IP addresses from NSX security group membership that causes firewall rules to
temporarily stop applying to affected VMs.
VMs experience intermittent network connectivity loss when their IP address is temporarily removed from NSX Group
effective members. Distributed Firewall rules that rely on dynamic group membership may stop matching the affected
VM's traffic during these periods. The issue is intermittent and can affect multiple VMs in production environments.
After replacing the vCenter root CA certificate with a certificate that lacks a Common Name (CN), the "Update
Compute Manager" operation fails because NSX cannot properly identify the root certificate without the CN field.
Compute Manager connectivity remains down, preventing NSX from managing vCenter resources.
Stats for vusb0 interface is throwing an error.
If an ESX node has vusb0 interface, vROP and VRNI are reporting issues with vusb0 stats interface API that cannot be
resolved.
Intents are not going through realization. The realization status gets stuck in IN_PROGRESS when customers try
to create/update/delete tier-1.
None of the network services work.
During host transport nodes upgrade in a scale setup, multiple VMs can face connectivity issues.
For more information, see KB article 413006.
NSX firewall rule drops packets.
Logical-port IP is not realized and it is not present as an effective member in the NSGroup that is being used by the
impacted firewall rule. As a result, the impacted firewall rule drops packets.
When a NAT Rule is deleted by Policy Provider from Corfu during an upgrade because of the data migration,
an issue with CCP's UFO full sync might occur and CCP might not propagate this NAT Rule deletion to the data
plane.
The stale NAT Rule in the data plane cannot be changed or interacted with. As a result, customers are not able to change
the behavior.
Stateless cache enabled ESX host profile does not create a log directory under /scratch.
A host that auto-deploys with the stateless cache enabled host profile causes /var (ramdisk) to be full.
User observes a false alarm.
Broadcom 553

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
User observes a false alarm, remote_logging_server_error, and the false alarm keeps going on and off even if logs can be
redirected to the remote logging-server as expected.
SNMP service crashed in edge node and generated core dump file in some race condition.
SNMP created a core dump and stops working when it loads TCP endpoints for v4 and v6 from the kernel.
Enlarged capacity or updated expiry VCF license with that same allocationId as the previously applied VCF
license fails to sync with NSX.
Changes, such as expiry date and license capacity, in the vCenter's VCF license do not get reflected in the connected
NSX.
Load balancer status is shown incorrect.
When a load balancer instance is enabled -> disabled -> detached -> attached again, then the status of the load balancer
instance is shown as unknown.
Failure to configure the application profile of a load balancer.
If a tier-1 with an attached load balancer has no tier-0 and no tier-1 interface, the application profile of the load balancer
cannot be configured.
After an upgrade, the perf configuration of the load balancer is lost.
The performance of the load balancer degrades after an upgrade.
Load balancer (LB) configuration cannot be loaded into LB nginx as char '"' is configured in the request header
body of the LB HTTP monitor.
The new LB configuration cannot be loaded. After the LB docker restarts with this configuration, LB cannot work and the
LB status is unkown.
High disk usage occurs in/var/log partition of edge node.
This issue is caused by the failed rotation of load balancer debug files. As a result, many of these .tar.gz debug files
persist in the /var/log partition.
NSX Manager reports incorrect load balancer (LB) status.
NSX Manager reports that the load balancer virtual service is down, even though the virtual service is capable of handling
traffic. The issue is observed when multiple monitors are configured in the same LB pool.
Users can delete default load-balancing persistence profiles through the API.
In case the default LB persistence profile is deleted, users would have to manually create custom LB persistence profiles.
Nginx process can crash on NSX Edge when using L7 drop rule in load balancer configuration.
This issue is caused by an nginx coredump that occurs when using the drop rule in an L7 virtual server of the load
balancer, resulting in L7 traffic disruption.
The nginx coredump is found after the source IP persistence feature of the Load Balancer (LB) is deactivated.
The LB traffic is impacted.
NSX Load Balancer status is marked as unknown because the UDP monitor is not configured correctly and LB is
not running properly on the edge.
If the LB is configured with the incorrect UDP monitor in the beginning, the LB on edge cannot provide service and the LB
status is unknown.
If the LB is configured properly in the beginning and the incorrect LB monitor is configured later, the reconfiguration cannot
take effect anymore.

Security Fixes
• This release resolves CVE-2026-41722 and CVE-2026-41723. For more information about these vulnerabilities and
their impact on VMware products, please see VMSA-2026-0004.
• For a list of fixed CVEs, see VCF_Ops_9.1_Fixed_CVEs.
Build
Lifecycle
Unable to download logs from VCF Operations
After upgrading the SDDC management stack, generated support bundles do not download using the VCF Operations
post-deployment "Download Support Bundle" action.
Resource API calls are returning and
resourceHealth=GREY resourceHealthValue=-1
The API call to GET resources by relationship type returns mismatched and
resourceHealth resourceHealthValue
field values. This mismatch impacts the VMware Aria Operations health monitoring value in VMware Aria Suite Lifecycle.
Operate
VCF Health
In VCF Health metrics, you see vCenter Archive Disk usage flagged as Critical, even though it is designed to
operate above the 85% utilization threshold
By design, the vCenter Archive Disk metric keeps an utilization rate above 85%, which is the threshold for Critical status
in VCF Health. As a result, in VCF Health you often see the vCenter Archive Disk metric above the Critical threshold,
which is a false positive.
In VCF 9.1, the vCenter Archive Disk metric is removed from the count of Critical issues.
Log Management
The Log Analysis widget in public shared dashboards fails to load and displays a "Cannot retrieve logs" error.
When accessing a public shared dashboard, the Log Analysis widget may fail to display data and instead show a Cannot
retrieve logs error message. This issue prevented users from viewing critical log metrics in shared environments.
Inaccurate status messages are displayed in the Log Data migration UI when a migration fails due to insufficient storage
space.
Broadcom 555

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When a log data migration fails because the destination nodes have reached storage capacity, specifically within the
/
partition, the user interface incorrectly displays the task as both "Completed" and "Pending 0%."
storage/core
Configuring Log Forwarding using the Raw Protocol prevents the Preview and Create functions from operating.
When configuring Log Forwarding in the VCF Operations UI, selecting the Raw Protocol forwarding method caused the
Preview and Create functionalities to become unresponsive. This issue occurred specifically when switching the input
type from Syslog to Raw, preventing the successful establishment of new log forwarding destinations.
Network Operations
NSX-T latency metric profiles (BFD, Transport Zone, and Latency) accumulate redundant and duplicate entries in
the collector database and in NSX-T due to DIDs/UUIDs appended to profile IDs.
The profile generation logic for NSX-T latency metrics appends unique system identifiers (DIDs/UUIDs) to profile IDs,
causing the system to generate a high volume of redundant and superfluous profiles. This behavior increases internal
state management overhead and degrades overall system efficiency over time. Database clutter accumulates as duplicate
profile entries persist without resolution.
The NSX health widget incorrectly displays "no data available" on the Network Operations page
When navigating to the Network Operations page, the NSX health widget may display a message.
no data available
However, the underlying data is still being collected and is accessible. Clicking View Details under the widget successfully
opens the detailed view displaying all expected metrics.
Custom-named VCF Operations for networks instances do not automatically update to the default "VCF OPS NI"
name after upgrading to version 9.x.
Previously, if a VCF Operations for networks adapter was configured with a custom name in a pre-9.0 release, the custom
name persisted after upgrading to version 9.x. The upgrade process has been corrected to automatically rename any
existing VCF Operations for networks instances to the default "VCF OPS NI" name for consistency across the managed
infrastructure.
The NSX health widget incorrectly displays "no data available" on the Network Operations page
While navigating to the Network Operations page, the NSX health widget may show a 'no data available' message.
However, the underlying data is still being collected and is accessible; clicking "view details" under the widget successfully
opens the detailed view displaying all expected metrics.
Integrations
Auto-discovery for VCF components may fail if a new CA certificate relevant to the VCF endpoint, is manually
imported into VCF Operations
CA certificates imported via the VCF Operations Control Panel's Trusted Certificates section are not being sent to the VCF
adapter. This can potentially cause new service accounts creation to fail for VCF instance sub-components.
Data-grid filters for vMotion reporting incorrectly display options derived from all vCenter instances rather than
the specifically selected instance
In VCF 9.0, vMotion reporting is scoped to a specific vCenter instance within a VCF instance. While the data-grid correctly
renders vMotion events for the selected vCenter instance, the associated filter options are incorrectly constructed using
vMotion data from all vCenter instances across the fleet. This issue is fixed in VCF 9.1.
Inconsistent formatting of Knowledge Base (KB) article links within vCenter Management Pack
recommendations.
Previously, references to Knowledge Base (KB) articles in the vCenter Management Pack recommendations displayed
varying text formats. This issue has been resolved. All KB article references have now been standardized to follow a
uniform format (for example, "See Broadcom KB 1000258").
The "Account Monitoring Notification" message updated with instructions on starting data collection.
Broadcom 556

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The "Account Monitoring Notification" dialog box only stated that data collection does not start automatically. The
message text has been updated to provide administrators with explicit instructions on how to manually start data
collection.
Data collection for the VMware Infrastructure Health adapter may require multiple cycles (3–4) in large scale
environments
The data collection process for the VMware Infrastructure Health adapter was delayed when ESX hosts in the vCenter
environment became unresponsive or disconnected.
vCenter pricing in VCF Operations does not allow you to add a new tag if it uses an existing tag category as an
existing tag with a new tag value, resulting in an error that prevents configuration completion
vCenter pricing enforces a unique tag category in the user interface for Recurring, One-time, and Rate factor tags,
which prevents defining multiple distinct tag values under the same category. Administrators who need several values
within one category for differentiated pricing cannot complete that model through vCenter pricing in the VCF Operations
UI.
The vSAN Cloud account status remains in a "Stopped" state after configuring a VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF)
Cloud account.
When configuring accounts in a specific sequence, the vSAN account may fail to initialize data collection automatically.
This issue occurs when an administrator first creates a vCenter account using a vCenter instance from a VCF domain,
starts data collection, and subsequently creates a VCF account with the "Enable Domain Monitoring on Creation" setting
configured to "True". As a result of this sequence, while all VCF domains are successfully configured and started, the
associated vSAN account defaults to a "Stopped" state, preventing immediate data collection and monitoring of the
storage layer.
ESX Virtual Machine Network Interface Card (VMNIC) status was not accurately reflected in VCF Operations.
In certain cases, when a Virtual Machine Network Interface Card (VMNIC) went down, VCF Operations did not update
its status accordingly and continued to display stale data. This resulted in an incorrect representation of the VMNIC
state compared to vCenter. Due to this inconsistency, users were not able to reliably determine the actual VMNIC status,
impacting monitoring and day-2 operations.
The actions from VCF Operations to vCenter fail to execute
This issue occurs because Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) tasks are not currently whitelisted during the collector’s
initialization phase. While the controller successfully starts adapter instances, the subsequent DRS configuration tasks
are blocked, preventing the necessary communication between VCF Operations and vCenter. Whitelisting the DRS task
ensures that adapter instances are correctly synchronized and operational during the startup sequence.
Administrators are subsequently unable to rename the vCenter adapter instance within the VCF adapter
hierarchy.
Upon configuring the VCF adapter in VCF Operations, existing vCenter, vSAN, and NSX adapters automatically nest
within the VCF adapter hierarchy. Following this integration, administrators are unable to rename the vCenter adapter.
Users are unable to edit or change the configuration of a VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) cloud account when it
is in a stopped state.
When a VCF cloud account is in a stopped state, configuration edits fails and returns the message "SDDC configuration
is not available as adapter instance is not ready." This blocks administrative tasks such as vCenter Server license
management, unless data collection is active, forcing users to start data collection, manage the integration, and then
stop it again. This issue is resolved. Administrators can now modify VCF cloud account configurations in a stopped state,
ensuring consistent operational behavior across all cloud account types.
Inventory
The error dialog box that opens when you use the Actions drop-down in the VCF Operations inventory UI uses an
incorrect graphic and inconsistent style
If you encounter an error when using a functionality from the Actions drop-down menu in the VCF Operations inventory
UI on both the VCF Instance and the VCF domain levels, the error message dialog box displays a graphic and is
inconsistent with the remaining VCF Operations UI error messages.
Broadcom 557

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Application Monitoring
After upgrading VMware Tools to 13.0.5 version, the Service Discovery adapter may stop collecting data
After upgrading VM Tools to version 13.0.5, you may encounter an issue where the credential-less mode fails to collect
data from VMs.
Cost
Links in the Cost Optimization dashboard redirect incorrectly.
The link to the VCF Operations Forrester Total Economic Impact (TEI) documentation has been updated in the Cost
Optimization dashboard in VCF Operations.
Administrators are unable to match the inventory count of virtual machines to the "Windows Server 2016 or later"
license item within the License Cost Driver.
When an administrator lists virtual machines by Guest OS to determine the total count of systems running Windows
Server 2016 or later, the resulting inventory count does not match the total displayed for the "Windows Server 2016 or
later" license item in the License Cost Driver. Virtual machines running the Windows Server 2022 Guest OS are incorrectly
categorized and counted under the "Other OS" classification during cost calculations. This discrepancy prevents accurate
license cost attribution and reconciliation for newer Windows Server operating systems.
The Power and Cooling monthly cost calculated within the Facilities cost driver lacks accuracy because it relies
on a fixed reference value for host energy consumption rather than actual utilization metrics.
There is an hourly energy consumption metric coming from vCenter adapter. It can be utilized for cost calculations.
Currently a fixed monthly energy consumption is utilized for hosts. Using the actual host energy consumption will be more
accurate for calculating cost.
Multiple Additional Cost configurations applied to the same Entity Selection object yield an incorrect "Monthly
Additional Cost" host metric.
When multiple Additional Cost configurations are assigned to the same Entity Selection object (vCenter/ Datacenter/
Cluster Compute Resource/ Host System), the system incorrectly selects a single configuration to calculate the "Monthly
Additional Cost" host metric. To ensure accurate financial modeling and cost calculation, the system must aggregate all
applicable configurations assigned to the object rather than applying only one.
Reports and Views
The Report Templates page contains an obsolete 'Change report font' menu option
The report font customization feature has been deprecated and dropped from the product. However, the menu on the
Report Templates page still displays this option.
The Virtual Machine Utilization Summary view displays an incorrect number of vCPUs
In the out-of-the-box Virtual Machine Utilization Summary view, the vCPU count might not match the actual number of
vCPUs assigned to the virtual machine in vCenter. This occurs because the view incorrectly uses the "
Configuration|
property instead of the
Hardware|Number of virtual sockets Configuration|Hardware|Number of
property to calculate the value.
virtual CPUs
Report generation stops working with new reports remaining stuck in the "In queue" status
During report generation, the system may encounter timeouts while attempting to load and render certain report
pages. When this occurs, an issue in handling these timeouts causes the internal report generation service to become
permanently blocked. Consequently, all subsequent report requests are unable to process, remaining stuck in the "In
queue" status and eventually failing.
Metrics
VCF Operations UI displays deprecated metrics from older releases, metric from End of Life products (such as
VMware Configuration Manager), and inaccurate network metrics.
In previous releases, VCF Operations retained certain metrics from End of Life products, like VMware Configuration
Manager (VCM), as well as some legacy network metrics. To ensure accurate system monitoring and prevent misleading
data, VCF Operations has now permanently deleted the obsolete metrics. Additionally, specific legacy network metrics
have been officially marked as deprecated and will be completely removed in a future release.
Broadcom 558

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Others
Tenant-scoped alerts are missing from the triggered alerts list when no filters are applied.
When viewing the triggered alerts list without any active filters, alerts scoped specifically for tenants fail to appear in the
default view. To see these alerts, users were previously required to manually set the "For Tenants" filter field to "Yes." The
alert filtering mechanism has been updated to ensure tenant-scoped alerts are included in the comprehensive triggered
alerts list by default.
Fixed broken URLs in the VCF Operations UI.
Navigation from the Metrics tab to the Summary tab after selecting an object from Global Search
A user is on the Metrics tab of the Inventory page viewing a specific object and one or more metrics have been added
to the metric chart area on the right of the page for this particular object. When the user opens Global Search, selects
the Object category, and selects another object from the suggestions, the user is shown the Summary tab of the new
object, when they were expecting to remain on the Metrics tab so they could add more metrics to the chart area.
The Custom Groups page displays "No Results Found" after a group deletion.
After deleting a custom group, the Custom Groups page incorrectly displays "No Results Found" even if other groups
exist. Refreshing the browser resolves the issue and displays the remaining custom groups.
The browser's back button navigation does not work correctly after viewing generated reports
While navigating to the Report Templates page under Dashboards & Reports and clicking on a "Generated reports" link,
subsequent use of the browser's back button fails to function as expected. Users may experience incorrect navigation
behavior and be unable to return to their previous screens using the browser's built-in back controls.
Inability to navigate to the Custom Groups page directly from the "Push Categories to vCenter Instances" dialog
box when existing groups are present
The link to create or manage Custom Groups was only visible within the "Push Categories" workflow when no groups had
been defined. This required users to manually exit the Push Categories dialog box and navigate through the main panel to
reach the Custom Groups page. A permanent "Add Custom Group" link, has been added to ensure a seamless navigation
path regardless of whether existing groups are displayed.
The link configured in the Scoreboard widget opens in a new window
The link configured in the Scoreboard widget opens in a new window instead of navigating within the existing page.
The term 'Sustainability' has been updated to 'Green Score' across the product interface
To align with updated terminology guidelines, all references to Sustainability in the user interface have been replaced
with Green Score. This includes updates to menu items and metric grouping names. This is a terminology update only
and does not impact the underlying functionality or calculation of the metrics.
In large-scale VCF Operations instances, the "Appliances Health & Management" section on the VCF Overview
page takes longer than expected to load.
When navigating to the Operate> Home> VCF Overview page in large-scale environments with more than 4,000 ESX
hosts, there might be a delay of over a minute while the widgets in the "Appliances Health & Management" section load.
This delay is caused by the time required to calculate and retrieve health and configuration data for the connected multi-
cloud appliances. With this fix, the load time for these widgets has been reduced to less than 10 seconds.
In the metric chart, the 'Anomalies' option displays all active symptoms for the selected object, rather than
filtering them by the specific metric key
In VCF Operations, when viewing a metric chart, the 'Anomalies' overlay incorrectly displayed all active symptoms for the
selected object instead of filtering them by the chosen metric.
Manage
Fleet Management
Adding LDAP/AD users or groups in identity broker (group or user provisioning) fails; the UI displays the
following error: . Search can hang or display an error when the
Over 1000 group/user DNs are available
directory under the base DN is very large, for example, over 1000 matching groups or users
Broadcom 559

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
With a large LDAP/AD tree, default substring search can return too many matches and hit the 1000-result limit, causing
lookup to fail. The backend now supports an optional prefix search: type only as the first character (for example,
^
) for a narrower, indexed-style match. How quickly results return still depends on your LDAP directory and its
^finance
configuration, but prefix search usually returns a smaller, more focused set of matches than a broad substring search.
Configuration Template validation fails with a missing property error when only a subset of nested options is
selected.
Within the Fleet Management > Configuration Management > Create Configuration Template workflow, administrators can
select a subset of nested configuration keys using the UI checkboxes. However, back-end validation enforces certain child
properties as mandatory once a parent branch is selected (for example, requiring min_length under a password policy).
This mismatch between the UI presentation of optional fields and the strict validation requirements causes template
validation to fail, preventing the successful creation of the configuration template.
When attempting to use a functionality not available in VCF versions older than 9.0 in VCF Operations 9.0 UI, the
view that opens does not provide a link to the relevant documentation.
When attempting to use a functionality not available in VCF versions older than 9.0 in VCF Operations 9.0 UI, such as
Certificates, Passwords, Configuration Drifts, Lifecycle, and Tasks under Fleet Management, the view that opens does
not provide a link to the relevant documentation.
User accounts with usernames that contain the exclamation mark character (!) are unable to authenticate or be
provisioned when using Microsoft Entra ID for Single Sign-On (SSO) with vCenter or VCF 9.0
Authentication failures occur because the identity broker utilizes a strict validation pattern for SCIM user provisioning
that does not include the exclamation mark as a permitted symbol. This issue prevents users with the exclamation mark
character (!) from successfully logging into vCenter via Entra ID federation.
With Photon FIPS mode enabled, replacing the VCF Operations certificate with a certificate that is missing the
serverAuth attribute in its Extended Key Usage (EKU) causes the UI to become unresponsive
When replacing the VCF Operations certificate, the validation workflow does not check whether the
serverAuth
attribute is available in the new certificate's Extended Key Usage (EKU). With FIPS mode enabled on the appliance, the
cryptographic library explicitly requires that any certificate used for a server acting as a TLS endpoint must contain the
value in its EKU. As a result, applying this invalid certificate causes the VCF Operations UI to become
serverAuth
unresponsive.
Show ESX Hosts toggle switch may not be visible depending on screen size
The Show ESX Hosts toggle switch in the VCF Operations certificate management UI is not floating and, depending on
the screen size, may not be visible.
The management vCenter name appears with the prefix vRSLCM_VCF_VC Adapter Instance instead of a clear,
human-readable name in vCenter Linking.
After upgrading VCF Operations, the vCenter Linking UI labels the management vCenter using an internal adapter
instance name, making it hard to recognize. This display issue is isolated to the vCenter Linking workflow and does not
impact underlying product functionality or vCenter operations beyond how the instance is identified in that specific view.
VCF Operations UI shows incorrect password expiration for VCF fleet level component accounts
VCF Operations UI does not show the correct password expiration for VCF fleet level component accounts, even when
there is a set password expiry.

based services on that node.

due to an error. When logs are set to debug mode, you see error messages like

Issues with environments as part of a package
This release introduces fixes to various issues with environments as part of a package.
Carriage return character is replaced when passed as a workflow input through the API
When running a workflow using a script and passing the character as part of a string input, the character is then
"\r"
replaced to in the actual workflow run.
"\n"
Workfow runs fail when using JSON.stringify()
When using on objects that are not Javascript-defined, the workflow run fails.
JSON.stringify()
Refresh token values not applied if VCF Automation or VCF SSO are used for authentication
If an external VCF Operations orchestrator instance is authenticated with either VCF Automation or VCF SSO, the values
set for the refresh token are not applied as configured. For example, you can configure a token duration for 300 seconds
and then continue to use VCF Operations orchestrator even after this limit is exceeded.
VCF Operations orchestrator not detecting usage or dependencies for workflows or actions
The usage and dependency detection sometimes misses references to VCF Operations orchestrator workflows or actions
in scripts in case of multi-line references.
VCF Operations orchestrator page content is not updated after switching between VCF Operations orchestrator
instances
After switching between VCF Operations orchestrator instances, page content is not updated, unless you refresh your
browser.
The VCF Operations orchestrator workflow run is interrupted when the VCF Automation browser session expires.
When performing workflow runs in the embedded VCF Operations orchestrator instance in VCF Automation, expiration of
the browser session stops the workflow run. As a result, the workflow run usually fails with an access denied error.
The VCF Operations orchestrator API allows you to create configuration elements with same attribute name
multiple times
Updating a configuration element with the PUT /configurations/{id} operation allows you to set multiple attributes with
the same name. Performing the same action in the UI is not possible.
The Create a Supervisor Namespace example workflow fails
The example workflow Create a Supervisor Namespace fails even if the namespace is created successfully. This is
caused by the missing annotation.
infrastructure.cci.vmware.com/id
Error with the display prompt for external VCF Operations orchestrator certificate
When an external VCF Operations orchestrator with a self-signed certificate is added to a VCF Automation organization
and the user goes to the Orchestrate tab, the VCF Operations orchestrator UI is not loaded and a spinner is shown until
it times out. This is caused by the certificate not being accepted by the browser. The user still has to accept the certificate,
but the message is fixed.
Bad request when deleting configuration properties in VCF Operations orchestrator
After deleting properties from System Settings -> Configuration Properties, you receive an "A problem occurred while
saving properties. ..." error. The selected properties are still deleted from the server.

Provider Management
When an organization is disabled, all currently logged-in users retain their sessions for up to 5 minutes
Because of the system's in-memory caching, the existing user sessions are not immediately stopped when an
organization is deactivated. The sessions might be active for up to five minutes after the fact. After this time elapses,
users see an error message .
"Server Error: Error: 401 - OK" or "401 UNAUTHORIZED"
Cannot create or delete organization in VCF Automation Provider Management
There are two scenarios for this issue. The first is a scenario where the organization creation process does not complete
and the creation task is left in the running state. This scenario can happen in a situation the organization creation or
deletion process is started in the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal when the Event Broker service is down or
being restarted.
In the second scenario the organization creation or deletion process is marked as failed. This is cause by the Event
Broker service failing to trigger the events associated with the creation or deletion of a organization. In such as case, you
receive an error message similar to
Org creation/deletion task failed. Event processing failed with
.
error :

error{}
When attempting to view utilization metrics, a failure in the metrics API prevents users from switching between the
Project and Namespace pages in the VCF Automation organization UI and can cause the entire interface to crash or
malfunction. This happens when the API fails to return data, resulting in a lack of graceful error handling and the loss of
visible organizational statistics.

manager

Broadcom 562

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In environments with multiple vSphere Distributed Switches (vDS), when querying multiple Distributed Switches

-VDSwitch Get-VDPort
ports or displayed incorrect uplink information.
If you use VCF PowerCLI 9.0 and earlier, upgrade to VCF PowerCLI 9.1.
If you are using an affected version of PowerCLI, you can avoid this issue by querying each Distributed Switch individually
and joining the results.
Instead of running: , use a loop to process each switch
Get-VDPort -VDSwitch VDS-A, VDS-B -Uplink foreach
independently:
$mySwitches = Get-VDSwitch -Name "MS01-vmkernel01-vds", "MS01-nsxm01-cvds"
$allPorts = foreach ($vds in $mySwitches) {
Get-VDPort -VDSwitch $vds -Uplink
}
$allPorts | Format-Table -AutoSize
Alternatively, you can join the results manually:
(Get-VDPort -VDSwitch SwitchA -Uplink) + (Get-VDPort -VDSwitch SwitchB -Uplink) | ft -a

Introduction
Maintenance releases provide bug and security fixes, hardware enablement changes, such as support for servers, CPUs,
devices, driver updates, guest OS support, and backward-compatible new features. They are limited in scope to minimize
the operational impact. You can pick and choose which components to apply based on the impact on your environment
and operational costs. For example, if you run into a critical issue with vCenter, you do not need to apply a patch to ESX
that is irrelevant to your environment. Maintenance releases are synchronized among VCF components with a new Bill Of
Materials.
VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
VCF 9.1.1.0 is a maintenance release that comes with an updated Bill of Materials (BoM). The features it delivers are
mostly focused on improving the supportability of the product.
See the list of updates in the release per component:
• vCenter
• ESX
• vSAN
• NSX

Introduction
VMware vCenter 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25712839
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
• Automated Secure Boot Platform Key (PK) Remediation: To address Microsoft 2011 Secure Boot certificate
expirations, as detailed in Broadcom knowledge base article 423893, VCF 9.1.1.0 introduces three new capabilities to
simplify Platform Key (PK) remediation:
– vCenter Alarm: Proactively warns administrators when Secure Boot-enabled, powered-on virtual machines have
an out-of-date NULL PK. This per-VM alarm is triggered once vCenter and the ESX host are upgraded to 9.1.1.0.
– Silent PK Update in ESX: Automatically updates the out-of-date NULL PK on Secure Boot-enabled virtual
machines that have no virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM) during a guest reboot.
– Capsule PK Update: Enables a secure mechanism to safely update the out-of-date NULL PK on Secure Boot-
enabled, vTPM-enabled Windows virtual machines during a guest reboot without interrupting TPM-based
applications. The Capsule PK update driver triggering the PK update is available starting in VMware Tools 13.1.5
for supported Windows versions, except Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 64-bit 22H2, and 1809, which will
be supported in a future VMware Tools release. For the Capsule PK update, the July 2026 Windows Cumulative
Update or later is required. You must install this cumulative update before installing or upgrading VMware Tools to
version 13.1.5 to allow the installation of the PK update driver, except for Windows Server 2025, Windows 11 25H2,
and 24H2.
• VM-VM anti-affinity and affinity rules through compute policies:
You can use compute policies to create VM-VM anti-affinity rules that distribute VMs across separate hosts for
resiliency, and VM-VM affinity rules that collocate VMs on the same host for low latency. This functionality applies to
traditional virtual machines and to virtual machines created through VM Service. In the VM spec file, you can configure
the strictness of a rule as either required (hard) or preferred (soft) during initial VM placement. However, only the
preferred setting is supported during runtime. For more information, see vSphere Compute Policies.
Broadcom 569

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Photon RPMs are upgraded to the latest versions for improved security.
Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) and High Availability (HA) support for Memory Tiering:
With VCF 9.1.1, Memory Tiering supports DRS and HA. In clusters with Memory Tiering activated, vSphere HA admission
control tracks DRAM as an independent resource alongside total memory to make sure that the cluster retains sufficient
DRAM capacity for virtual machines restart after a host failure. This capability prevents failover operations from silently
failing due to insufficient DRAM. For more information, see Memory Tiering and HA Admission Control.
Product Support Notes
Removal of the lstool script:
The script is removed, because it is only supported on vCenter 6.x and 7.x versions. You can
ls_update_certs.py
use the Lookup Service Doctor (lsdoctor) tool instead, as described in Broadcom knowledge base article 320837.
vCenter enforces MethodActions alarms to run on behalf of the user who configures the alarm:
With VCF 9.1.1, new vCenter alarms configured with the object can only be executed on behalf of
MethodAction
existing users with current, valid permissions. Alarms configured by users who have been deleted or had their privileges
revoked are blocked and a event is posted on the target object.
com.vmware.vc.AlarmMethodActionBlockedEvent
You can control the enforcement behavior by using the Advanced Setting in vCenter
vpxd.alarm.methodActionMode
and selecting a mode, such as :
vpxd.alarm.methodActionMode = flexible | strict | legacy
• flexible (default): Enforces user identity and privilege checks for new alarms. Existing alarms continue to fire without
disruption.
• strict: All require valid user credentials and privilege checks. Blocked actions post a
MethodActions
event.
com.vmware.vc.AlarmMethodActionBlockedEvent
• legacy: Actions run impersonating the vpxd service account. If a is blocked in strict mode, a
MethodAction
event is posted on the target object. Re-save the alarm to
com.vmware.vc.AlarmMethodActionBlockedEvent
register fresh credentials.

You do not see service accounts in the Global Permissions page in the vSphere Client
Since service account permissions are not customer-managed, service accounts are filtered out from the Global
Permissions page in the vSphere Client. The page also excludes VCF reserved groups. You can retrieve all accounts for
auditing or any other purpose by using CLI/API.
Applying password expiry and lockout policies for the vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) administrator account might
affect existing automation and integrations
The vCenter SSO administrator account enforces no password expiration or lockout policies by default. Applying these
security policies globally might affect existing automation, integrations, and day-to-day operations. vCenter 9.1.1.0
introduces an opt-in/opt-out mechanism for the SSO administrator account password policy through a vCenter API
endpoint. By default, the account remains opted out, preserving the existing behavior where no expiration or lockout is
enforced. If you require strict compliance, you can opt in to apply expiry and lockout policies to the account. The VCF
Operations UI does not expose this setting in 9.1.1.0. You can use only the vCenter API.
This issue is resolved in this release. If you opt in for password expiry and lockout policies for the vCenter SSO
administrator account, you can use the following example:
curl -sk -X PATCH \
"https://10.161.46.164/api/identity/admin/administrator/password-policy" \
-H "vmware-api-session-id: ${session}" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
Broadcom 571

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
-d '{"enable_expiry_policy": true, "enable_lockout_policy": true}'
After a VCF certificate refresh, you see stale data for removed hosts in vSphere Configuration Profiles (VCP)
cluster configurations
Following a VCF certificate refresh, the VCP inventory monitoring service loses its cached host association information.
If a host removal event occurs before the cache is rebuilt, the system fails to identify the host association and skips
the necessary configuration cleanup. As a result, stale host-specific and host-override sections remain in the cluster
configuration.
The vSphere Statistics (vstats) service repeatedly logs a false-positive ERROR-level message about a missing
discovery configuration for host-based metrics
The vstats provider orchestrator might incorrectly attempt to register the ESX host metrics provider with the generic
discovery manager, even though host providers use a push-based streaming model and do not require generic discovery.
As a result, the provider reports an error multiple times per minute, generating roughly 5,000 false-positive error events
per day in Log management. The vstats service remains fully functional, only the logging behavior is affected.
Content library synchronization occasionally fails due to a reported missing file, even though the library is fully
in sync and the file exists on the publisher
The pagination queries during a content library sync might not use a fully deterministic sort order. As a result, for libraries
containing more than 100 items, some file records belonging to the same item might be returned in an inconsistent order
across paginated queries. Occasionally, a file that is already present, might be identified as missing and scheduled for
deletion during a subscribed library sync.
The pagination queries used during library-item sync now sort deterministically by item, version, and file identifiers,
ensuring files are consistently accounted for across paginated results.
A vApp does not retain changes to some settings after a restart of vCenter or the VPXD service
Some settings of vApps such as the start order and the IP allocation are not updated in the vCenter database when they
are changed. As a result, they might revert to previous values after a reboot of vCenter or a restart of the VPXD service.
vCenter upgrade from 8.0.x or 9.0.x to 9.1.0 fails during the import of vSphere Lifecycle Manager while attempting
database schema upgrade
Orphaned database records in the vSphere Lifecycle Manager database, specifically in the
pm_recommendation_spec
table, might cause vCenter upgrade from 8.0.x or 9.0.x to 9.1.0 to fail. In the Virtual Appliance Management Interface,
you see an error such as Error attempting Upgrade Database Schema. Please check vcintegrity
migration logs for details.
vCenter 9.1.0.0 introduces a strict foreign key constraint, , to harden database integrity
FK_PM_RECOMMENDATION_SPEC
and the Postgres engine blocks schema changes because existing orphaned data violates the constraint.
Converging vSphere environments to VCF 9.1 might complete with errors due to duplicate DNS servers
In the vCenter Appliance Management Interface (VAMI), you can set duplicate DNS Server settings, which leads to errors
after converging vSphere environments to VCF 9.1.
The fix removes duplicates and prevents error propagation for invalid DNS addresses.
You see an error 'HTTP Error 403: Forbidden' in the vSphere Client while downloading VIBs
Upgrading or remediating ESX hosts might fail with an error in the vSphere Client while
HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
downloading VIBs because of an issue with file permissions.

serviceAccount
after an upgrade to VCF 9.1.

If the machine account password stored in the VMware Directory Service (VMDIR) database does not match the
password used by a given vCenter service, such services fail to start or some vCenter operations fail, but you do not see
a notification or informative error message.

When performing an upgrade precheck targeting VCF version 9.1 either by Reduced Downtime Upgrade (RDU) or regular

machine after the precheck might disrupt operational services such as the vc-ws1a-broker service in vCenter.

failure.
