Introduction
VMware ESX 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25714478
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
Automated Secure Boot Platform Key (PK) Remediation: To address Microsoft 2011 Secure Boot certificate
expirations, as detailed in Broadcom knowledge base article 423893, VCF 9.1.1.0 introduces three new capabilities to
simplify Platform Key (PK) remediation:
• vCenter Alarm: Proactively warns administrators when Secure Boot-enabled, powered-on virtual machines have an
out-of-date NULL PK. This per-VM alarm is triggered once vCenter and the ESX host are upgraded to 9.1.1.0.
• Silent PK Update in ESX: Automatically updates the out-of-date NULL PK on Secure Boot-enabled virtual machines
that have no virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM) during a guest reboot.
• Capsule PK Update: Enables a secure mechanism to safely update the out-of-date NULL PK on Secure Boot-
enabled, vTPM-enabled Windows virtual machines during a guest reboot without interrupting TPM-based applications.
The Capsule PK update driver triggering the PK update is available starting in VMware Tools 13.1.5 for supported
Windows versions, except Windows Server 2016, Windows 10 64-bit 22H2, and 1809, which will be supported in
a future VMware Tools release. For the Capsule PK update, the July 2026 Windows Cumulative Update or later is
required. You must install this cumulative update before installing or upgrading VMware Tools to version 13.1.5 to
allow the installation of the PK update driver, except for Windows Server 2025, Windows 11 25H2, and 24H2.
Getting to 9.1.1

 command namespace. To avoid service disruptions, replace SHA-1 before upgrading to a future scheduled
ipsec
maintenance release.

This patch resolves the following issues:
ESX host might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or
Windows VM
When you use PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or Windows VM, including Nvidia GPUs, the VMs might
not program the MSI/MSIx interrupts correctly during device probe. As a result, the ESX host either powers off the VM or
fails with a purple diagnostic screen.
You see a "Create and Commit draft check" or "Failed to invoke create and commit" error in VCF Operations
When attempting to patch ESX hosts to version 9.1.1, the workflow fails at step Desired State. In the SDDC Manager and
VCF Operations UI, you see errors such as or
Create and Commit draft check Failed to invoke create
Broadcom 579

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If you try to set the vSphere Lifecycle Manager cluster image to 9.1.1 in the vSphere Client, you see the
and commit.
following error:
The /profile/nsx/fabric/transport_node_profile in configuration is not compatible with the
draft image. Remove the incompatible configuration before setting the new desired state.
Workaround: Perform the steps in Broadcom knowledge base article 455572.
On the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client, you see a false warning that the VM network portgroup
does not exist
After a VCF deployment, the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client might incorrectly display the warning
for VMs with network
This VM is attached to a network portgroup undefined that doesn't exist
adapters connected to a Distributed Virtual Switch (DVS) portgroup. This issue occurs due to an underlying check for only
recognized standard virtual switches and not identifying the portgroup for DVS-backed network adapters. As a result, you
see a false-positive warning for every affected VM.
Due to vSAN disk failures, you might not see the vSAN File Service UI widget
vSAN File Service determines its supported version by evaluating the on-disk format versions across all disks in the
cluster. If a disk in the cluster is in a Permanent Device Loss (PDL) state, such as Absent vSAN Disk, the vSAN File
Service query might return an obsolete or inaccurate format version of that disk. As a result, the vSAN File Service might
get an incorrect supported version and due to vSAN disk failures, the vSAN File Service UI widget might not display. This
issue applies to both vSAN Original Storage Architecture (OSA) and vSAN Express Storage Architecture (ESA).
The fix skips PDL disks when calculating lowest disk format version.
Fault Domain Manager (FDM) might fail when vSphere High Availability (HA) is active in environments with Cisco
NFNIC driver
The Cisco NFNIC driver might generate an excessively large volume of stats data and while attempting to retrieve and
process such data, FDM might run out of memory and fail with a core dump at . In the
/var/core/fdm-zdump /var/
file, you see errors such as and under
run/log/fdm.log Unable to allocate memory /var/lib/vmware/
, you see large stats files.
hostd/stats dir
Hot-add operation for an independent nonpersistent disk might fail for virtual machines hosted on vSphere
Virtual Volumes datastores
When you restore VMs on ESX 8.0 Update 1 and later hosts from earlier ESX versions, hot-add operations for some
of the restored disks hosted on vSphere Virtual Volumes datastores might fail due to a mismatch in the virtual volume
namespace versions. The issue is specific for independent nonpersistent disks.
Configuring vSAN File Service with Active Directory domain fails with an error for exception caught when
running preflight check on the file server
In the vSphere Client, when you create a file service domain with AD and click Next, you see an error such as:
Failed to check domain configuration: Exception caught when running preflight check on
file server.
The issue occurs because querying the Active Directory domain for LDAP SRV records returns multiple duplicate entries
for the same Domain Controller hostname. As a result, the pre-flight check script causes an exception and fails the file
service enablement workflow.
A disk-only Storage vMotion operation might accidentally delete an orphaned virtual disk file on the destination
datastore and cause data loss
When you perform a disk-only Storage vMotion, vCenter might not check if an orphaned virtual disk (VMDK) file - for
example, one left behind by an earlier disk detach operation - is already present in the destination folder. As a result, the
new file might get the same name as the existing VMDK and the migration task fails. The cleanup after such a failure
might remove the pre-existing orphaned virtual disk file, and cause loss of that file's data.
Multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen due to a rare race condition in the NFSv4.1 client
On ESX hosts using the NFSv4.1 client, if a competing APD starts during an ongoing APD recovery, the file reclaim
process creates duplicate insertions and causes pointer corruption. As a result, multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen.
Broadcom 580

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VMware Tools Bundling Changes in ESX 9.1.1.0
The following VMware Tools ISO images are bundled with ESX 9.1.1.0:
• windows.iso: VMware Tools 13.1.5 supports 64-bit Windows versions - Windows 7 SP1 or Windows Server 2008 R2
SP1 and later.
The following VMware Tools ISO images are available for download:
• VMware Tools 12.5.4:
– windows.iso: VMware Tools 12.5.4 supports 64-bit Windows versions.
– windows-x86.iso: VMware Tools 12.4.9 supports 32-bit Windows versions.
– linux.iso: VMware Tools 10.3.26 ISO image for Linux OS with glibc 2.11 or later.
• VMware Tools 11.0.6:
– windows.iso: for Windows Vista (SP2) and Windows Server 2008 Service Pack 2 (SP2).
• VMware Tools 10.0.12:
– winPreVista.iso: for Windows 2000, Windows XP, and Windows 2003.
– linuxPreGLibc25.iso: supports Linux guest operating systems earlier than Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 5,
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES) 11, Ubuntu 7.04, and other distributions with glibc version earlier than 2.5.
• solaris.iso: VMware Tools image 10.3.10 for Solaris.
• darwin.iso: Supports Mac OS X versions 10.11 and later.
Follow the procedures listed in the following documents to download VMware Tools for platforms not bundled with ESX:
• VMware Tools 13.1.5 Release Notes
• VMware Tools for hosts provisioned with Auto Deploy
• Upgrading VMware Tools
ESX hosts might experience CPU utilization at around 100% after a port is quiesced in an Enhanced Network
Stack (ENS) environment
When a network port is quiesced, the host network scheduler might fail to correctly update its internal byte counters after
clearing pending packets. This mismatch causes the system to continually check for network traffic even when the queue
is empty, resulting in the transmit (TX) process getting stuck in a loop and consuming up to 100% of CPU resources.
The fix ensures that internal byte counters are accurately updated when packets are dropped.
When using Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), if a physical NIC is down, defined alarms might not
trigger
When you configure an alarm based on Broadcom knowledge base article 378014, the alarm might not trigger in the
vSphere Client if a physical NIC is down.
When resuming virtual machines configured with device groups containing DVX devices, the VMs might fail to
power on
A power-on failure might occur when resuming a VM configured with a device group containing DVX devices.
Uplink gets reenabled before the time defined by the TeamPolicyUpDelay policy passes
The ESX advanced setting sets a time before an uplink is reenabled after the link status
Net.TeamPolicyUpDelay
changes from to . During such a wait period, new ports might be enabled for various reasons, such as migration,
DOWN UP
VM power cycle, or flapping of the network interface inside the guest OS. A newly powered-on vNIC can cause an uplink
in state to reactivate prematurely for all VMs connected to the switch.
TeamPolicyUpDelay
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after powering on
virtual machines when Virtual Machine Identifier (VMID) is enabled
An issue in the Broadcom Emulex lpfc storage driver if VMID is enabled can cause an ESX host to fail with a purple
diagnostic screen immediately after powering on virtual machines. The issue occurs due to an invalid memory access
during Fibre Channel common transport command processing.
If ESX hosts share a LUN, you might overwrite VMFS volumes
Broadcom 581

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If ESX hosts share a LUN and you create a VMFS volume on one of the hosts by using the VMware Host Client, the new
volume might not be immediately visible on the other hosts and another user can create a VMFS volume on the same
LUN from another Host Client session. As a result, the first VMFS datastore path might be overwritten.
The fix makes sure that while listing the available LUNs for new VMFS volumes, latest changes on the LUNs are fetched
and considered.
A rare race condition in the lpfc driver might cause ESXi hosts to fail with a purple diagnostic screen during
reboot or shutdown
On an ESXi host with Emulex LightPulse Fibre Channel adapters, a rare race condition in the lpfc driver can result in
an invalid DMA access. This invalid access can lead to silent memory corruption, resulting in unpredictable system
instability that might cause the ESX host to fail with a purple diagnostic screen, but since the memory corruption only
affects the address range of the lpfc driver, it does not damage user VM data. The race condition only occurs during the
device detachment phase, typically triggered during a reboot or when enabling PCI passthrough, and the probability of
occurrence is low.
ESXi hosts using the lpfc driver do not provide log visibility for certain faulty small form-factor pluggable (SFP)
optics
When an SFP module is present but non-functional, the Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware detects the fault and
reports an error code. The lpfc driver does not capture or log that specific hardware error code into the vmkernel.log,
which makes it difficult to identify and troubleshoot faulty optics.
The fix enhances the driver to properly log SFP hardware errors as they occur.
After an Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware upgrade, ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen
When updating the firmware on certain Broadcom Emulex Fibre Channel adapters, the inbox lpfc driver might incorrectly
handle a change in the internal resource counts during the subsequent host reboot. This mismatch can trigger an
improper memory management condition during driver initialization or cleanup, leading to a purple diagnostic screen on
the ESX host.
Emulex SAN Manager (ESM) does not display encryption details for certain Host Bus Adapters (HBAs)
An issue within the lpfc driver prevents ESM from properly retrieving data from all encryption-capable Emulex Fibre
Channel adapters. This occurs due to a communication mismatch during fabric port initialization and link setup sequences
between the ESX host and the switch.
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or
shutdown due to a race condition
A race condition in the native lpfc driver can occur if a hardware error on an Emulex Host Bus Adapter (HBA) triggers
while the driver is unloading. As a result, the ESXi host fails with a a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or shutdown
with an error such as # .
PF in lpfc_hw_info_setup()
ESX hosts with Emulex Fibre Channel HBAs might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during storage array
upgrades
During the upgrade of certain Fibre Channel storage arrays, the target node IDs might change. As a result, the lpfc driver
interprets the targets as offline and different targets coming online in a short period. Handling such cases might trigger a
race condition in the lpfc driver, leading to failure of the ESX host with a purple diagnostic screen displaying an error such
as .
#PF Exception 14 in world <world_id>:lpfc_path_cl
Scheduling delays when high-priority processes are placed on a busy physical CPU might cause packets drop
When high-priority processes, for example in an Enhanced Network Stack (ENS) context, are placed on a busy physical
CPU, they rely on the virtual CPU migration algorithm to move them to an idle or less busy CPU as appropriate. An
issue with the migration algorithm might cause such processes to stay on the busy CPU for extended periods, causing
significant scheduling delays, or high CPU Ready Time. As a result, you might see packets drop.
Log entries in the dfwpktlogs.log for distributed firewall (DFW) packets might occasionally split across two lines
Some log records for DFW packets might be written as two separate lines instead of one. When the split occurs within the
record timestamp, the second line shows a system-generated timestamp rather than the original. For example
2026-03-11T05:57:28.172Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] 2026-03-11
Broadcom 582

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2026-03-11T05:57:28.176Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] T05:57:28.172Z 4678804c INET6 match PASS
1007 OUT 76 TCP 2001:db8:abcd:12::1001/23557->2001:db8:abcd:12::1501/80 S Cyperf_L4-rule
The issue only affects log formatting, no log data is lost and firewall enforcement is unaffected.You can read the full record
by combining the split line with the partial record on the following line.
In the ESX Host Client, you do not see the option to add Sound Controller for virtual machines
In ESX Host Client version 9.1, under Edit Settings > Virtual Hardware > Add New Device, you do not see the Sound
Controller option to configure audio hardware.
Setting the /Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount advanced configuration option does not correctly
limit the Maximum Unmap LBA Count Per Descriptor for NVMe devices
When the advanced configuration option is set to a non-zero
/Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount
value for the Maximum Deallocate Range Size Limit, ESX incorrectly applies the same limit to the Maximum Unmap LBA
Count Per Descriptor as for the Maximum Unmap Descriptor Count. As a result, the vSphere API for Array Integration
(VAAI) cache reports incorrect UNMAP limits, which might cause UNMAP operations to behave unexpectedly with NVMe
storage arrays.
When Intel SGX Flexible Launch Control (FLC) is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, VMs using vSGX
might fail to power on after a Quick Boot
When SGX FLC is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, and a VM is configured to enable SGX with FLC, the
hypervisor programs the associated FLC Model-Specific Register (MSRs) with guest-provided values. Such values persist
during a Quick Boot, which might cause subsequent MSR uniformity checks to fail during boot. As a result, ESX might
disable SGX on the host if it finds non-uniform values in the FLC MSRs during boot. The issue also impacts Pod VMs
utilizing vSGX, such as the TDX Quote Pod.
Intel Xeon 6 processors utilizing QAT accelerators might see increased boot times on ESX 9.1
On Intel Xeon 6 processors systems using QAT devices, in some cases, the boot time for ESX hosts might increase.
In the VMware Host Client, you do not see vSAN data migration options while entering maintenance mode
When placing a vSAN host into maintenance mode by using the VMware Host Client in version 9.1, you might not see
vSAN data migration options in the dialog box.
In the NSX Manager, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host metrics
In the NSX Manager, when you navigate to System > Fabric > Hosts, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host
metrics, such as , , and . The issue occurs because
Controller Connectivity Tunnel Status PNIC/Bond Status
NSX requests high quality entropy for frequent use and consequently the default HWRNG entropy is exhausted and
causes timeouts. Affected ESX hosts create an opsAgent core dump file: . During heavy
/var/core/opsAgent-zdump
load, multiple ESX hosts might be affected in batches. In the ESX log, , you see log
/var/run/log/nsx-syslog.log
messages such as:
Wa(###) nsx-opsagent[#######]: NSX ######## - [nsx@4413 comp="nsx-esx" subcomp="opsagent"
s2comp="nsx-core" tid="########" level="WARNING"] AsioNsxProvider: (0x##########-2) user
dispatcher blocked since 20 seconds.
The ESX agent hostd might intermittently fail or generate a core dump during gathering device statistics or
socket disconnections
Under conditions of high-concurrency performance queries or unexpected connection drops, synchronization race
conditions can occur. Such timing conflicts might cause internal tracking structures to be cleared prematurely and cause
hostd to terminate unexpectedly.
A very rare race condition might cause an encrypted virtual machine to fail with a core dump
A very rare race condition might cause the VMX process on an ESX host to fail and cause an encrypted virtual machine to
unexpectedly power off. In the file you see an error such as: .
vmware.log PANIC: Unexpected signal: 6
In the VMkernel logs, you see multiple log messages for failed retrieval of ENS uplink distributed statistics
In environments using the Enhanced Network Stack (ENS), the VMkernel creates logs each time it fails to retrieve
distributed statistics for an uplink port, even when the port does not support ENS. The error messages are
Fail to get
Broadcom 583

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
. Such retrieval attempts can fail transiently under normal operating conditions
uplink dist stats for ens port
and do not indicate an actual network problem, but might clutter VMkernel logs and cause unnecessary log noise, CPU
overhead, and affect monitoring.
The fix demotes the error messages to debug-level logging and
Fail to get uplink dist stats for ens port
you do not see such in release builds.
Tunneled SSL from vCenter to ESX fails intermittently
In some cases, such as when traffic goes through a tunnel that terminated inside a guest virtual machine, an SSL
connection from vCenter to the ESX host might intermittently fail.
In Advanced Settings, you do not see an option to configure a time window for consecutive login failures before
locking user accounts
In ESX, user accounts are locked after a configurable number of consecutive login failures without a specific time window
and you cannot configure such a window.
The fix updates the Pluggable Authentication Modules and adds the advanced ESX setting
, which allows you to set a time window for consecutive login failures before
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
locking user accounts. defaults to 15 min, but you can configure the time
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
window accordingly.
IPFIX traffic might be blocked due to a missing route on a DPU ESX host
On a dual-DPU ESX host with offloading enabled, when you configure sending IPFIX data to a VCF Operations for
networks collector but the IP address/netmask of the collector is in a different network that requires a gateway, IPFIX
traffic might be blocked due to a missing route. In a non-DPU environment, you can configure a default gateway for VCF
Operations, but you cannot create a default gateway in a DPU environment.
In rare cases, ESXi hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during VMFS UNMAP operation
Under rare race conditions, ESXi hosts with VMFS datastores supporting UNMAP operations might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen during an UNMAP task.
The esxtop utility reports inflated VMWAIT values
The calculation of VMWAIT, which is the percentage of time a VM waits for a VMkernel activity such as running I/O to
complete before it can continue, uses the CPU WAIT and IDLE values. In some cases, the calculation might overestimate
the CPU IDLE value and as a result, the VMWAIT value is much higher.

The VF link state in NVIDIA NICs remains at "UP" regardless of the PF link state
For NVIDIA NICs, the VF link state does not follow the PF link state and always remains UP, even if the physical port link
state changes to DOWN.
With ESX 9.1.1.0, in the NVIDIA nmlx5 driver you can configure the behavior of the VF link state. You need to download
nmlxcli tools, which is an ESXCLI command line extension available on the NVIDIA website, on the ESXi host to configure
PFs so that VFs follow the PF link state.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Related CVE numbers N/A
This patch resolves the following issues:
ESX host might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or
Windows VM
When you use PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or Windows VM, including Nvidia GPUs, the VMs might
not program the MSI/MSIx interrupts correctly during device probe. As a result, the ESX host either powers off the VM or
fails with a purple diagnostic screen.
On the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client, you see a false warning that the VM network portgroup
does not exist
After a VCF deployment, the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client might incorrectly display the warning
for VMs with network
This VM is attached to a network portgroup undefined that doesn't exist
adapters connected to a Distributed Virtual Switch (DVS) portgroup. This issue occurs due to an underlying check for only
recognized standard virtual switches and not identifying the portgroup for DVS-backed network adapters. As a result, you
see a false-positive warning for every affected VM.
Due to vSAN disk failures, you might not see the vSAN File Service UI widget
vSAN File Service determines its supported version by evaluating the on-disk format versions across all disks in the
cluster. If a disk in the cluster is in a Permanent Device Loss (PDL) state, such as Absent vSAN Disk, the vSAN File
Service query might return an obsolete or inaccurate format version of that disk. As a result, the vSAN File Service might
get an incorrect supported version and due to vSAN disk failures, the vSAN File Service UI widget might not display. This
issue applies to both vSAN Original Storage Architecture (OSA) and vSAN Express Storage Architecture (ESA).
The fix skips PDL disks when calculating lowest disk format version.
Fault Domain Manager (FDM) might fail when vSphere High Availability (HA) is active in environments with Cisco
NFNIC driver
The Cisco NFNIC driver might generate an excessively large volume of stats data and while attempting to retrieve and
process such data, FDM might run out of memory and fail with a core dump at . In the
/var/core/fdm-zdump /var/
file, you see errors such as and under
run/log/fdm.log Unable to allocate memory /var/lib/vmware/
, you see large stats files.
hostd/stats dir
Hot-add operation for an independent nonpersistent disk might fail for virtual machines hosted on vSphere
Virtual Volumes datastores
When you restore VMs on ESX 8.0 Update 1 and later hosts from earlier ESX versions, hot-add operations for some
of the restored disks hosted on vSphere Virtual Volumes datastores might fail due to a mismatch in the virtual volume
namespace versions. The issue is specific for independent nonpersistent disks.
Configuring vSAN File Service with Active Directory domain fails with an error for exception caught when
running preflight check on the file server
In the vSphere Client, when you create a file service domain with AD and click Next, you see an error such as:
Failed to check domain configuration: Exception caught when running preflight check on
file server.
The issue occurs because querying the Active Directory domain for LDAP SRV records returns multiple duplicate entries
for the same Domain Controller hostname. As a result, the pre-flight check script causes an exception and fails the file
service enablement workflow.
A disk-only Storage vMotion operation might accidentally delete an orphaned virtual disk file on the destination
datastore and cause data loss
When you perform a disk-only Storage vMotion, vCenter might not check if an orphaned virtual disk (VMDK) file - for
example, one left behind by an earlier disk detach operation - is already present in the destination folder. As a result, the
new file might get the same name as the existing VMDK and the migration task fails. The cleanup after such a failure
might remove the pre-existing orphaned virtual disk file, and cause loss of that file's data.
Multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen due to a rare race condition in the NFSv4.1 client
Broadcom 590

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
On ESX hosts using the NFSv4.1 client, if a competing APD starts during an ongoing APD recovery, the file reclaim
process creates duplicate insertions and causes pointer corruption. As a result, multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen.
VMware Tools Bundling Changes in ESX 9.1.1.0
The following VMware Tools ISO images are bundled with ESX 9.1.1.0:
• windows.iso: VMware Tools 13.1.5 supports 64-bit Windows versions - Windows 7 SP1 or Windows Server 2008 R2
SP1 and later.
The following VMware Tools ISO images are available for download:
• VMware Tools 12.5.4:
– windows.iso: VMware Tools 12.5.4 supports 64-bit Windows versions.
– windows-x86.iso: VMware Tools 12.4.9 supports 32-bit Windows versions.
– linux.iso: VMware Tools 10.3.26 ISO image for Linux OS with glibc 2.11 or later.
• VMware Tools 11.0.6:
– windows.iso: for Windows Vista (SP2) and Windows Server 2008 Service Pack 2 (SP2).
• VMware Tools 10.0.12:
– winPreVista.iso: for Windows 2000, Windows XP, and Windows 2003.
– linuxPreGLibc25.iso: supports Linux guest operating systems earlier than Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 5,
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES) 11, Ubuntu 7.04, and other distributions with glibc version earlier than 2.5.
• solaris.iso: VMware Tools image 10.3.10 for Solaris.
• darwin.iso: Supports Mac OS X versions 10.11 and later.
Follow the procedures listed in the following documents to download VMware Tools for platforms not bundled with ESX:
• VMware Tools 13.1.5 Release Notes
• VMware Tools for hosts provisioned with Auto Deploy
• Upgrading VMware Tools
ESX hosts might experience CPU utilization at around 100% after a port is quiesced in an Enhanced Network
Stack (ENS) environment
When a network port is quiesced, the host network scheduler might fail to correctly update its internal byte counters after
clearing pending packets. This mismatch causes the system to continually check for network traffic even when the queue
is empty, resulting in the transmit (TX) process getting stuck in a loop and consuming up to 100% of CPU resources.
The fix ensures that internal byte counters are accurately updated when packets are dropped.
When using Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), if a physical NIC is down, defined alarms might not
trigger
When you configure an alarm based on Broadcom knowledge base article 378014, the alarm might not trigger in the
vSphere Client if a physical NIC is down.
When resuming virtual machines configured with device groups containing DVX devices, the VMs might fail to
power on
A power-on failure might occur when resuming a VM configured with a device group containing DVX devices.
Uplink gets reenabled before the time defined by the TeamPolicyUpDelay policy passes
The ESX advanced setting sets a time before an uplink is reenabled after the link status
Net.TeamPolicyUpDelay
changes from to . During such a wait period, new ports might be enabled for various reasons, such as migration,
DOWN UP
VM power cycle, or flapping of the network interface inside the guest OS. A newly powered-on vNIC can cause an uplink
in state to reactivate prematurely for all VMs connected to the switch.
TeamPolicyUpDelay
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after powering on
virtual machines when Virtual Machine Identifier (VMID) is enabled
Broadcom 591

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
An issue in the Broadcom Emulex lpfc storage driver if VMID is enabled can cause an ESX host to fail with a purple
diagnostic screen immediately after powering on virtual machines. The issue occurs due to an invalid memory access
during Fibre Channel common transport command processing.
If ESX hosts share a LUN, you might overwrite VMFS volumes
If ESX hosts share a LUN and you create a VMFS volume on one of the hosts by using the VMware Host Client, the new
volume might not be immediately visible on the other hosts and another user can create a VMFS volume on the same
LUN from another Host Client session. As a result, the first VMFS datastore path might be overwritten.
The fix makes sure that while listing the available LUNs for new VMFS volumes, latest changes on the LUNs are fetched
and considered.
A rare race condition in the lpfc driver might cause ESXi hosts to fail with a purple diagnostic screen during
reboot or shutdown
On an ESXi host with Emulex LightPulse Fibre Channel adapters, a rare race condition in the lpfc driver can result in
an invalid DMA access. This invalid access can lead to silent memory corruption, resulting in unpredictable system
instability that might cause the ESX host to fail with a purple diagnostic screen, but since the memory corruption only
affects the address range of the lpfc driver, it does not damage user VM data. The race condition only occurs during the
device detachment phase, typically triggered during a reboot or when enabling PCI passthrough, and the probability of
occurrence is low.
ESXi hosts using the lpfc driver do not provide log visibility for certain faulty small form-factor pluggable (SFP)
optics
When an SFP module is present but non-functional, the Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware detects the fault and
reports an error code. The lpfc driver does not capture or log that specific hardware error code into the vmkernel.log,
which makes it difficult to identify and troubleshoot faulty optics.
The fix enhances the driver to properly log SFP hardware errors as they occur.
After an Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware upgrade, ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen
When updating the firmware on certain Broadcom Emulex Fibre Channel adapters, the inbox lpfc driver might incorrectly
handle a change in the internal resource counts during the subsequent host reboot. This mismatch can trigger an
improper memory management condition during driver initialization or cleanup, leading to a purple diagnostic screen on
the ESX host.
Emulex SAN Manager (ESM) does not display encryption details for certain Host Bus Adapters (HBAs)
An issue within the lpfc driver prevents ESM from properly retrieving data from all encryption-capable Emulex Fibre
Channel adapters. This occurs due to a communication mismatch during fabric port initialization and link setup sequences
between the ESX host and the switch.
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or
shutdown due to a race condition
A race condition in the native lpfc driver can occur if a hardware error on an Emulex Host Bus Adapter (HBA) triggers
while the driver is unloading. As a result, the ESXi host fails with a a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or shutdown
with an error such as # .
PF in lpfc_hw_info_setup()
ESX hosts with Emulex Fibre Channel HBAs might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during storage array
upgrades
During the upgrade of certain Fibre Channel storage arrays, the target node IDs might change. As a result, the lpfc driver
interprets the targets as offline and different targets coming online in a short period. Handling such cases might trigger a
race condition in the lpfc driver, leading to failure of the ESX host with a purple diagnostic screen displaying an error such
as .
#PF Exception 14 in world <world_id>:lpfc_path_cl
Scheduling delays when high-priority processes are placed on a busy physical CPU might cause packets drop
When high-priority processes, for example in an Enhanced Network Stack (ENS) context, are placed on a busy physical
CPU, they rely on the virtual CPU migration algorithm to move them to an idle or less busy CPU as appropriate. An
issue with the migration algorithm might cause such processes to stay on the busy CPU for extended periods, causing
significant scheduling delays, or high CPU Ready Time. As a result, you might see packets drop.
Broadcom 592

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Log entries in the dfwpktlogs.log for distributed firewall (DFW) packets might occasionally split across two lines
Some log records for DFW packets might be written as two separate lines instead of one. When the split occurs within the
record timestamp, the second line shows a system-generated timestamp rather than the original. For example
2026-03-11T05:57:28.172Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] 2026-03-11
2026-03-11T05:57:28.176Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] T05:57:28.172Z 4678804c INET6 match PASS
1007 OUT 76 TCP 2001:db8:abcd:12::1001/23557->2001:db8:abcd:12::1501/80 S Cyperf_L4-rule
The issue only affects log formatting, no log data is lost and firewall enforcement is unaffected.You can read the full record
by combining the split line with the partial record on the following line.
In the ESX Host Client, you do not see the option to add Sound Controller for virtual machines
In ESX Host Client version 9.1, under Edit Settings > Virtual Hardware > Add New Device, you do not see the Sound
Controller option to configure audio hardware.
Setting the /Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount advanced configuration option does not correctly
limit the Maximum Unmap LBA Count Per Descriptor for NVMe devices
When the advanced configuration option is set to a non-zero
/Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount
value for the Maximum Deallocate Range Size Limit, ESX incorrectly applies the same limit to the Maximum Unmap LBA
Count Per Descriptor as for the Maximum Unmap Descriptor Count. As a result, the vSphere API for Array Integration
(VAAI) cache reports incorrect UNMAP limits, which might cause UNMAP operations to behave unexpectedly with NVMe
storage arrays.
When Intel SGX Flexible Launch Control (FLC) is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, VMs using vSGX
might fail to power on after a Quick Boot
When SGX FLC is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, and a VM is configured to enable SGX with FLC, the
hypervisor programs the associated FLC Model-Specific Register (MSRs) with guest-provided values. Such values persist
during a Quick Boot, which might cause subsequent MSR uniformity checks to fail during boot. As a result, ESX might
disable SGX on the host if it finds non-uniform values in the FLC MSRs during boot. The issue also impacts Pod VMs
utilizing vSGX, such as the TDX Quote Pod.
Intel Xeon 6 processors utilizing QAT accelerators might see increased boot times on ESX 9.1
On Intel Xeon 6 processors systems using QAT devices, in some cases, the boot time for ESX hosts might increase.
In the VMware Host Client, you do not see vSAN data migration options while entering maintenance mode
When placing a vSAN host into maintenance mode by using the VMware Host Client in version 9.1, you might not see
vSAN data migration options in the dialog box.
In the NSX Manager, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host metrics
In the NSX Manager, when you navigate to System > Fabric > Hosts, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host
metrics, such as , , and . The issue occurs because
Controller Connectivity Tunnel Status PNIC/Bond Status
NSX requests high quality entropy for frequent use and consequently the default HWRNG entropy is exhausted and
causes timeouts. Affected ESX hosts create an opsAgent core dump file: . During heavy
/var/core/opsAgent-zdump
load, multiple ESX hosts might be affected in batches. In the ESX log, , you see log
/var/run/log/nsx-syslog.log
messages such as:
Wa(###) nsx-opsagent[#######]: NSX ######## - [nsx@4413 comp="nsx-esx" subcomp="opsagent"
s2comp="nsx-core" tid="########" level="WARNING"] AsioNsxProvider: (0x##########-2) user
dispatcher blocked since 20 seconds.
The ESX agent hostd might intermittently fail or generate a core dump during gathering device statistics or
socket disconnections
Under conditions of high-concurrency performance queries or unexpected connection drops, synchronization race
conditions can occur. Such timing conflicts might cause internal tracking structures to be cleared prematurely and cause
hostd to terminate unexpectedly.
A very rare race condition might cause an encrypted virtual machine to fail with a core dump
Broadcom 593

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
A very rare race condition might cause the VMX process on an ESX host to fail and cause an encrypted virtual machine to
unexpectedly power off. In the file you see an error such as: .
vmware.log PANIC: Unexpected signal: 6
In the VMkernel logs, you see multiple log messages for failed retrieval of ENS uplink distributed statistics
In environments using the Enhanced Network Stack (ENS), the VMkernel creates logs each time it fails to retrieve
distributed statistics for an uplink port, even when the port does not support ENS. The error messages are
Fail to get
. Such retrieval attempts can fail transiently under normal operating conditions
uplink dist stats for ens port
and do not indicate an actual network problem, but might clutter VMkernel logs and cause unnecessary log noise, CPU
overhead, and affect monitoring.
The fix demotes the error messages to debug-level logging and
Fail to get uplink dist stats for ens port
you do not see such in release builds.
Tunneled SSL from vCenter to ESX fails intermittently
In some cases, such as when traffic goes through a tunnel that terminated inside a guest virtual machine, an SSL
connection from vCenter to the ESX host might intermittently fail.
In Advanced Settings, you do not see an option to configure a time window for consecutive login failures before
locking user accounts
In ESX, user accounts are locked after a configurable number of consecutive login failures without a specific time window
and you cannot configure such a window.
The fix updates the Pluggable Authentication Modules and adds the advanced ESX setting
, which allows you to set a time window for consecutive login failures before
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
locking user accounts. defaults to 15 min, but you can configure the time
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
window accordingly.
IPFIX traffic might be blocked due to a missing route on a DPU ESX host
On a dual-DPU ESX host with offloading enabled, when you configure sending IPFIX data to a VCF Operations for
networks collector but the IP address/netmask of the collector is in a different network that requires a gateway, IPFIX
traffic might be blocked due to a missing route. In a non-DPU environment, you can configure a default gateway for VCF
Operations, but you cannot create a default gateway in a DPU environment.
In rare cases, ESXi hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during VMFS UNMAP operation
Under rare race conditions, ESXi hosts with VMFS datastores supporting UNMAP operations might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen during an UNMAP task.
The esxtop utility reports inflated VMWAIT values
The calculation of VMWAIT, which is the percentage of time a VM waits for a VMkernel activity such as running I/O to
complete before it can continue, uses the CPU WAIT and IDLE values. In some cases, the calculation might overestimate
the CPU IDLE value and as a result, the VMWAIT value is much higher.
Broadcom 594

The VF link state in NVIDIA NICs remains at "UP" regardless of the PF link state
For NVIDIA NICs, the VF link state does not follow the PF link state and always remains UP, even if the physical port link
state changes to DOWN.
With ESX 9.1.1.0, in the NVIDIA nmlx5 driver you can configure the behavior of the VF link state. You need to download
nmlxcli tools, which is an ESXCLI command line extension available on the NVIDIA website, on the ESXi host to configure
PFs so that VFs follow the PF link state.
ESXi-9.1.1.0-25714478-no-tools

This patch resolves the following issues:
ESX host might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or
Windows VM
When you use PCI passthrough on a PCI/PCIe device to a Linux or Windows VM, including Nvidia GPUs, the VMs might
not program the MSI/MSIx interrupts correctly during device probe. As a result, the ESX host either powers off the VM or
fails with a purple diagnostic screen.
On the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client, you see a false warning that the VM network portgroup
does not exist
After a VCF deployment, the VM Summary page in the VMware Host Client might incorrectly display the warning
This VM is attached to a network portgroup undefined that doesn't exist  for VMs with network
Broadcom 599

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
adapters connected to a Distributed Virtual Switch (DVS) portgroup. This issue occurs due to an underlying check for only
recognized standard virtual switches and not identifying the portgroup for DVS-backed network adapters. As a result, you
see a false-positive warning for every affected VM.
Due to vSAN disk failures, you might not see the vSAN File Service UI widget
vSAN File Service determines its supported version by evaluating the on-disk format versions across all disks in the
cluster. If a disk in the cluster is in a Permanent Device Loss (PDL) state, such as Absent vSAN Disk, the vSAN File
Service query might return an obsolete or inaccurate format version of that disk. As a result, the vSAN File Service might
get an incorrect supported version and due to vSAN disk failures, the vSAN File Service UI widget might not display. This
issue applies to both vSAN Original Storage Architecture (OSA) and vSAN Express Storage Architecture (ESA).
The fix skips PDL disks when calculating lowest disk format version.
Fault Domain Manager (FDM) might fail when vSphere High Availability (HA) is active in environments with Cisco
NFNIC driver
The Cisco NFNIC driver might generate an excessively large volume of stats data and while attempting to retrieve and
process such data, FDM might run out of memory and fail with a core dump at . In the
/var/core/fdm-zdump /var/
file, you see errors such as and under
run/log/fdm.log Unable to allocate memory /var/lib/vmware/
, you see large stats files.
hostd/stats dir
Hot-add operation for an independent nonpersistent disk might fail for virtual machines hosted on vSphere
Virtual Volumes datastores
When you restore VMs on ESX 8.0 Update 1 and later hosts from earlier ESX versions, hot-add operations for some
of the restored disks hosted on vSphere Virtual Volumes datastores might fail due to a mismatch in the virtual volume
namespace versions. The issue is specific for independent nonpersistent disks.
Configuring vSAN File Service with Active Directory domain fails with an error for exception caught when
running preflight check on the file server
In the vSphere Client, when you create a file service domain with AD and click Next, you see an error such as:
Failed to check domain configuration: Exception caught when running preflight check on
file server.
The issue occurs because querying the Active Directory domain for LDAP SRV records returns multiple duplicate entries
for the same Domain Controller hostname. As a result, the pre-flight check script causes an exception and fails the file
service enablement workflow.
A disk-only Storage vMotion operation might accidentally delete an orphaned virtual disk file on the destination
datastore and cause data loss
When you perform a disk-only Storage vMotion, vCenter might not check if an orphaned virtual disk (VMDK) file - for
example, one left behind by an earlier disk detach operation - is already present in the destination folder. As a result, the
new file might get the same name as the existing VMDK and the migration task fails. The cleanup after such a failure
might remove the pre-existing orphaned virtual disk file, and cause loss of that file's data.
Multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen due to a rare race condition in the NFSv4.1 client
On ESX hosts using the NFSv4.1 client, if a competing APD starts during an ongoing APD recovery, the file reclaim
process creates duplicate insertions and causes pointer corruption. As a result, multiple ESX hosts might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen.
ESX hosts might experience CPU utilization at around 100% after a port is quiesced in an Enhanced Network
Stack (ENS) environment
When a network port is quiesced, the host network scheduler might fail to correctly update its internal byte counters after
clearing pending packets. This mismatch causes the system to continually check for network traffic even when the queue
is empty, resulting in the transmit (TX) process getting stuck in a loop and consuming up to 100% of CPU resources.
The fix ensures that internal byte counters are accurately updated when packets are dropped.
When using Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), if a physical NIC is down, defined alarms might not
trigger
Broadcom 600

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When you configure an alarm based on Broadcom knowledge base article 378014, the alarm might not trigger in the
vSphere Client if a physical NIC is down.
When resuming virtual machines configured with device groups containing DVX devices, the VMs might fail to
power on
A power-on failure might occur when resuming a VM configured with a device group containing DVX devices.
Uplink gets reenabled before the time defined by the TeamPolicyUpDelay policy passes
The ESX advanced setting sets a time before an uplink is reenabled after the link status
Net.TeamPolicyUpDelay
changes from to . During such a wait period, new ports might be enabled for various reasons, such as migration,
DOWN UP
VM power cycle, or flapping of the network interface inside the guest OS. A newly powered-on vNIC can cause an uplink
in state to reactivate prematurely for all VMs connected to the switch.
TeamPolicyUpDelay
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen after powering on
virtual machines when Virtual Machine Identifier (VMID) is enabled
An issue in the Broadcom Emulex lpfc storage driver if VMID is enabled can cause an ESX host to fail with a purple
diagnostic screen immediately after powering on virtual machines. The issue occurs due to an invalid memory access
during Fibre Channel common transport command processing.
If ESX hosts share a LUN, you might overwrite VMFS volumes
If ESX hosts share a LUN and you create a VMFS volume on one of the hosts by using the VMware Host Client, the new
volume might not be immediately visible on the other hosts and another user can create a VMFS volume on the same
LUN from another Host Client session. As a result, the first VMFS datastore path might be overwritten.
The fix makes sure that while listing the available LUNs for new VMFS volumes, latest changes on the LUNs are fetched
and considered.
A rare race condition in the lpfc driver might cause ESXi hosts to fail with a purple diagnostic screen during
reboot or shutdown
On an ESXi host with Emulex LightPulse Fibre Channel adapters, a rare race condition in the lpfc driver can result in
an invalid DMA access. This invalid access can lead to silent memory corruption, resulting in unpredictable system
instability that might cause the ESX host to fail with a purple diagnostic screen, but since the memory corruption only
affects the address range of the lpfc driver, it does not damage user VM data. The race condition only occurs during the
device detachment phase, typically triggered during a reboot or when enabling PCI passthrough, and the probability of
occurrence is low.
ESXi hosts using the lpfc driver do not provide log visibility for certain faulty small form-factor pluggable (SFP)
optics
When an SFP module is present but non-functional, the Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware detects the fault and
reports an error code. The lpfc driver does not capture or log that specific hardware error code into the vmkernel.log,
which makes it difficult to identify and troubleshoot faulty optics.
The fix enhances the driver to properly log SFP hardware errors as they occur.
After an Emulex Fibre Channel adapter firmware upgrade, ESX hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen
When updating the firmware on certain Broadcom Emulex Fibre Channel adapters, the inbox lpfc driver might incorrectly
handle a change in the internal resource counts during the subsequent host reboot. This mismatch can trigger an
improper memory management condition during driver initialization or cleanup, leading to a purple diagnostic screen on
the ESX host.
Emulex SAN Manager (ESM) does not display encryption details for certain Host Bus Adapters (HBAs)
An issue within the lpfc driver prevents ESM from properly retrieving data from all encryption-capable Emulex Fibre
Channel adapters. This occurs due to a communication mismatch during fabric port initialization and link setup sequences
between the ESX host and the switch.
ESX hosts using Emulex Fibre Channel adapters might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or
shutdown due to a race condition
Broadcom 601

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
A race condition in the native lpfc driver can occur if a hardware error on an Emulex Host Bus Adapter (HBA) triggers
while the driver is unloading. As a result, the ESXi host fails with a a purple diagnostic screen during reboot or shutdown
with an error such as # .
PF in lpfc_hw_info_setup()
ESX hosts with Emulex Fibre Channel HBAs might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during storage array
upgrades
During the upgrade of certain Fibre Channel storage arrays, the target node IDs might change. As a result, the lpfc driver
interprets the targets as offline and different targets coming online in a short period. Handling such cases might trigger a
race condition in the lpfc driver, leading to failure of the ESX host with a purple diagnostic screen displaying an error such
as .
#PF Exception 14 in world <world_id>:lpfc_path_cl
Scheduling delays when high-priority processes are placed on a busy physical CPU might cause packets drop
When high-priority processes, for example in an Enhanced Network Stack (ENS) context, are placed on a busy physical
CPU, they rely on the virtual CPU migration algorithm to move them to an idle or less busy CPU as appropriate. An
issue with the migration algorithm might cause such processes to stay on the busy CPU for extended periods, causing
significant scheduling delays, or high CPU Ready Time. As a result, you might see packets drop.
Log entries in the dfwpktlogs.log for distributed firewall (DFW) packets might occasionally split across two lines
Some log records for DFW packets might be written as two separate lines instead of one. When the split occurs within the
record timestamp, the second line shows a system-generated timestamp rather than the original. For example
2026-03-11T05:57:28.172Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] 2026-03-11
2026-03-11T05:57:28.176Z -NOTICE FIREWALL-PKTLOG 2100407 [nsx@4413] T05:57:28.172Z 4678804c INET6 match PASS
1007 OUT 76 TCP 2001:db8:abcd:12::1001/23557->2001:db8:abcd:12::1501/80 S Cyperf_L4-rule
The issue only affects log formatting, no log data is lost and firewall enforcement is unaffected.You can read the full record
by combining the split line with the partial record on the following line.
In the ESX Host Client, you do not see the option to add Sound Controller for virtual machines
In ESX Host Client version 9.1, under Edit Settings > Virtual Hardware > Add New Device, you do not see the Sound
Controller option to configure audio hardware.
Setting the /Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount advanced configuration option does not correctly
limit the Maximum Unmap LBA Count Per Descriptor for NVMe devices
When the advanced configuration option is set to a non-zero
/Scsi/NvmeMaxUnmapBlockDescriptorLbaCount
value for the Maximum Deallocate Range Size Limit, ESX incorrectly applies the same limit to the Maximum Unmap LBA
Count Per Descriptor as for the Maximum Unmap Descriptor Count. As a result, the vSphere API for Array Integration
(VAAI) cache reports incorrect UNMAP limits, which might cause UNMAP operations to behave unexpectedly with NVMe
storage arrays.
When Intel SGX Flexible Launch Control (FLC) is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, VMs using vSGX
might fail to power on after a Quick Boot
When SGX FLC is set to unlocked in the ESX host firmware, and a VM is configured to enable SGX with FLC, the
hypervisor programs the associated FLC Model-Specific Register (MSRs) with guest-provided values. Such values persist
during a Quick Boot, which might cause subsequent MSR uniformity checks to fail during boot. As a result, ESX might
disable SGX on the host if it finds non-uniform values in the FLC MSRs during boot. The issue also impacts Pod VMs
utilizing vSGX, such as the TDX Quote Pod.
Intel Xeon 6 processors utilizing QAT accelerators might see increased boot times on ESX 9.1
On Intel Xeon 6 processors systems using QAT devices, in some cases, the boot time for ESX hosts might increase.
In the VMware Host Client, you do not see vSAN data migration options while entering maintenance mode
When placing a vSAN host into maintenance mode by using the VMware Host Client in version 9.1, you might not see
vSAN data migration options in the dialog box.
In the NSX Manager, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host metrics
In the NSX Manager, when you navigate to System > Fabric > Hosts, you see unknown status for multiple ESX host
metrics, such as , , and . The issue occurs because
Controller Connectivity Tunnel Status PNIC/Bond Status
Broadcom 602

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
NSX requests high quality entropy for frequent use and consequently the default HWRNG entropy is exhausted and
causes timeouts. Affected ESX hosts create an opsAgent core dump file: . During heavy
/var/core/opsAgent-zdump
load, multiple ESX hosts might be affected in batches. In the ESX log, , you see log
/var/run/log/nsx-syslog.log
messages such as:
Wa(###) nsx-opsagent[#######]: NSX ######## - [nsx@4413 comp="nsx-esx" subcomp="opsagent"
s2comp="nsx-core" tid="########" level="WARNING"] AsioNsxProvider: (0x##########-2) user
dispatcher blocked since 20 seconds.
The ESX agent hostd might intermittently fail or generate a core dump during gathering device statistics or
socket disconnections
Under conditions of high-concurrency performance queries or unexpected connection drops, synchronization race
conditions can occur. Such timing conflicts might cause internal tracking structures to be cleared prematurely and cause
hostd to terminate unexpectedly.
A very rare race condition might cause an encrypted virtual machine to fail with a core dump
A very rare race condition might cause the VMX process on an ESX host to fail and cause an encrypted virtual machine to
unexpectedly power off. In the file you see an error such as: .
vmware.log PANIC: Unexpected signal: 6
In the VMkernel logs, you see multiple log messages for failed retrieval of ENS uplink distributed statistics
In environments using the Enhanced Network Stack (ENS), the VMkernel creates logs each time it fails to retrieve
distributed statistics for an uplink port, even when the port does not support ENS. The error messages are
Fail to get
. Such retrieval attempts can fail transiently under normal operating conditions
uplink dist stats for ens port
and do not indicate an actual network problem, but might clutter VMkernel logs and cause unnecessary log noise, CPU
overhead, and affect monitoring.
The fix demotes the error messages to debug-level logging and
Fail to get uplink dist stats for ens port
you do not see such in release builds.
Tunneled SSL from vCenter to ESX fails intermittently
In some cases, such as when traffic goes through a tunnel that terminated inside a guest virtual machine, an SSL
connection from vCenter to the ESX host might intermittently fail.
In Advanced Settings, you do not see an option to configure a time window for consecutive login failures before
locking user accounts
In ESX, user accounts are locked after a configurable number of consecutive login failures without a specific time window
and you cannot configure such a window.
The fix updates the Pluggable Authentication Modules and adds the advanced ESX setting
, which allows you to set a time window for consecutive login failures before
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
locking user accounts. defaults to 15 min, but you can configure the time
Security.AccountLockFailInterval
window accordingly.
IPFIX traffic might be blocked due to a missing route on a DPU ESX host
On a dual-DPU ESX host with offloading enabled, when you configure sending IPFIX data to a VCF Operations for
networks collector but the IP address/netmask of the collector is in a different network that requires a gateway, IPFIX
traffic might be blocked due to a missing route. In a non-DPU environment, you can configure a default gateway for VCF
Operations, but you cannot create a default gateway in a DPU environment.
In rare cases, ESXi hosts might fail with a purple diagnostic screen during VMFS UNMAP operation
Under rare race conditions, ESXi hosts with VMFS datastores supporting UNMAP operations might fail with a purple
diagnostic screen during an UNMAP task.
The esxtop utility reports inflated VMWAIT values
The calculation of VMWAIT, which is the percentage of time a VM waits for a VMkernel activity such as running I/O to
complete before it can continue, uses the CPU WAIT and IDLE values. In some cases, the calculation might overestimate
the CPU IDLE value and as a result, the VMWAIT value is much higher.
Broadcom 603

The VF link state in NVIDIA NICs remains at "UP" regardless of the PF link state
For NVIDIA NICs, the VF link state does not follow the PF link state and always remains UP, even if the physical port link
state changes to DOWN.
With ESX 9.1.1.0, in the NVIDIA nmlx5 driver you can configure the behavior of the VF link state. You need to download
nmlxcli tools, which is an ESXCLI command line extension available on the NVIDIA website, on the ESXi host to configure
PFs so that VFs follow the PF link state.
Known Issues
CLI and API Issues
The AcquireTicket API returns a ticket containing empty sslThumbprint and third-party solutions might fail to
open a VM console
As part of security hardening in VCF 9.1.1.0, ESX no longer supports SHA1 and the   field that contains
sslThumbprint
the SHA1 thumbprint of the SSL certificate of the ESX host issuing the ticket is empty by default. Setting the advanced
| option  |     |     |  to include SHA1 as a thumbprint type is also not  |     |     |     |
| ------- | --- | --- | -------------------------------------------------- | --- | --- | --- |
Config.HostAgent.ticketing.thumbprintTypes
supported. As a result, third-party VM console solutions that are not updated to support SHA256 might fail to open a VM
console. The changes does not affect opening a VM console by using the ESX Host Client, the vSphere Client, or the
VMware Remote Console (VMRC). You can also use PowerCLI after updating your environment to 9.1.1.0.
Workaround: None. Instead of the   field, use the   field, which contains the full
|     |     | sslThumbprint |     | sslCertificate |     |     |
| --- | --- | ------------- | --- | -------------- | --- | --- |
PEM-encoded SSL certificate. If a thumbprint is required, the   field contains at least one entry
certThumbprintList
representing the SHA256 thumbprint of the SSL certificate of the host issuing the ticket.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Introduction
VMware vSAN 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 |
VMware vSAN ESA Witness 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25714474
VMware vSAN OSA Witness 9.1.0.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25714473
VMware vSAN File Services 9.1.1.0200 | 26 OCT 2026 | Build 25846901
vSAN File Services 9.1.1.0200 substitutes all previous 9.1.x releases of vSAN File Services.
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
vSAN Topologies support in CNS - Qualification/Validation
In VCF 9.1.1, VMware Cloud Foundation Automation makes cloud management simple for both administrators and
developers by providing fully validated core services across various vSAN storage topologies, allowing users to
seamlessly run traditional and cloud-native applications.
VCF Native Object Store - 9.1.1 Tech Preview
VCF 9.1.1 introduces a Tech Preview of native, S3-compatible object storage built directly into vSAN. By eliminating the
need for third-party add-ons, native object storage provides a unified, scalable, and multi-tenant object storage platform
for modern workloads.
Getting to 9.1.1
For information about deploying, converging, upgrading or patching your environment to 9.1.1, see Getting to 9.1.1.
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
Resolved Issues
UpdateDatastoreSource API fails for Cross vCenter service account password reset
In a Cross-vCenter environment, attempting to reset the service account password for a server vCenter by invoking the
UpdateDatastoreSource API on the client vCenter would fail.
This issue occured when a client cluster mounted a remote vSAN datastore managed by a separate vCenter instance,
and that remote datastore's owner vCenter was running version 9.1.0.0 EP2.
This has been fixed.
The vSAN File Service with vSAN RDMA enabled went to an unhealthy state after upgrading from vSAN 7.x to
vSAN 8.x
After upgrading vSAN environment to 8.x, the vSAN File Service was in an unhealthy state, with vSAN RDMA enabled.
This issue no longer occurs after upgrading to VCF 9.1.1.
The vSAN File Service temporarily returned incorrect file-size in metadata over NFS.
The vSAN File Service was temporarily returning incorrect file-sizes in metadata over NFS. This issue occurred rarely
when multiple writes were being sent from an NFS client, with the writes causing the file size to increase. After the
metadata cache expires or was correctly updated, however, the NFS server started returning correct metadata.
This issue has been fixed.
Known Issues
Applying Host Profiles containing vSAN OSA or ESA configuration deltas to ESXi hosts fails with a generic
'vim.fault.HostConfigFailed' or 'ClusterUUID MethodFault' error.
When remediating a host profile with vSAN configuration differences across hosts in a cluster, the batch remediation task
fails on all target hosts. This issue applies to both vSAN ESA and vSAN OSA.
The vSphere Client UI reports a non-descriptive error summary displaying Error: 'ClusterUUID'. Individual per-host
applyHostConfig tasks fail with an error status, while log entries indicate access denials to vSAN VSI nodes.
Broadcom 609

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
This issue prevents users from being able to standardize vSAN cluster configurations or apply host profiles when vSAN
configuration differences exist between the profile and target hosts.
Non-vSAN settings can only be remediated if vSAN configuration deltas are completely eliminated prior to profile
application.
Workaround:
To apply non-vSAN configuration changes via host profiles, ensure there is no delta in the vSAN configuration by disabling
or aligning the vSAN sub-profile settings prior to remediation. While applying the non-vSAN configuration through host
profile, de-select the vSAN configuration.
For managing and standardizing vSAN cluster settings, use vSphere Configuration Profiles (VCP) or the vSAN Cluster
QuickStart -> Configuration wizard.
vSAN File Service — upgrade order requirement for 172.17.x.x subnet users
If you use IP addresses in the 172.17.x.x subnet for vSAN File Service domains or shares, upgrade the ESX host to
version 9.1.1 before upgrading the FSVM. Upgrading the FSVM ahead of the ESX host can cause the FSVM's internal
Docker bridge network to reclaim the 172.17.0.0/16 range, conflicting with File Service domain/share IPs in that subnet.
NSX 9.1.1.0 Release Notes
This document contains the following sections
• Introduction
• What's New
• Getting to 9.1.1
• Known Issues
• Resolved Issues
Introduction
NSX 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25691509
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
This release contains various security enhancements and the following new features.
• Introduces an Active/Active (A/A) deployment option for EVPN Route Controllers in Distributed Transit Gateway
(DTGW) topologies. All active Route Controller nodes establish independent BGP sessions directly to external EVPN
gateways (BGWs), which increases resiliency and availability during failure and maintenance scenarios.
• Starting with this release, the Distributed VXLAN Connectivity model supports EVPN-VXLAN Direct Prefix Routing.
This feature optimizes traffic forwarding and reduces packet processing overhead on the EVPN gateway by
establishing a direct VXLAN tunnel between the ESXi VTEP and the physical VXLAN leaf switch VTEP. The feature is
configurable per external connection on the Distributed VXLAN connection and creates a hybrid forwarding mode by
letting the designated latency-sensitive storage traffic (such as NFS and S3/object storage) bypass the EVPN gateway
and letting other traffic continue using the standard EVPN Gateway path.
• Administrators can now reallocate CPU cores on NSX Edge nodes from services to the packet data path for greater
performance and improved tuning. This feature provides optimized throughput during peak demand while maintaining
flexibility in resource allocation. Predefined CPU allocation profiles are available for both VM and bare metal NSX Edge
nodes.
• This release extends advanced networking services (such as NAT, load balancing, and DHCP relay) to support EVPN-
VXLAN distributed connectivity in VMware Cloud Foundation, enabling critical multi-tenant and external connectivity
capabilities at the VPC and transit gateway levels for key customer deployments. To enable support for this feature
follow the procedure in Enable Advanced Networking Services for Distributed VXLAN Connections.
• Multi-tenant EVPN-VXLAN distributed external connectivity is supported for VCF Automation and vSphere Supervisor.
Provider admins can create VXLAN external connections and allocate them to target organizations, allowing org
admins to seamlessly attach them to their Transit Gateways.
Broadcom 610

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Introduces vSphere Distributed Switch sharing across multiple clusters in a VCF domain, reducing switch provisioning
overhead and ensuring consistent network configuration and policies across clusters.
• This release introduces support for DHCP Relay in distributed VPC environments with EVPN-VXLAN and VLAN
external connectivity. This feature simplifies IP address management by allowing workloads across VPCs to obtain
IP addresses from external for NSX DHCP servers while leveraging distributed external connectivity. DHCP Relay is
supported for VPC public subnets only; private subnets are not supported.
• Introduces a new predefined role, Cloud Partner Auditor, for Microsoft Azure VMware Solution (AVS). This role is
specifically designed for cloud partners that require less access than Cloud Partner Admin to networking and security
services.
• Administrators can use the NSX API to change the host_switch_mode of host transport nodes between Legacy and
Standard without having to place the ESX host in maintenance mode.
• This release introduces support for a VLAN-backed VPC (networking model without TEPs) under the Distributed
Transit Gateway. In a VLAN-backed VPC model, all traffic flows directly on physical VLANs without the overlay
encapsulation. It does not support private subnets as the IP scheme is limited to the CIDRs backed by physical
VLANs. This is the default model during a VCF import.

On NSX Edges with dynamic BGP neighbors configured, customers might observe NSX Edge CLI commands
such as ‘get route’ hanging or timing out, and routing/FIB convergence failures logged as repeated EDG0100012
("Waiting for RT stack flush start... ignore FIB update") errors in the edge logs. The edge's routing state stops
updating, new and withdrawn routes are not reflected in the forwarding table, and any new configuration pushed
to the affected edge from NSX Manager (for example, new BGP neighbors, route-maps, static routes, VRF
changes) is also not realized until the affected process is manually restarted.
Edges using only statically configured BGP neighbors are not exposed to this issue.
On edges with dynamic BGP neighbors configured, once the RCPM deadlock is triggered, the affected tier-0 Service
Router's routing control plane stops converging and routes learned or withdrawn after the deadlock begins are not
propagated to the dataplane. This causes stale forwarding behavior for prefixes that change after the onset. In addition,
configuration changes made from NSX Manager after the deadlock begins will not take effect on the affected edge. The
condition does not self-recover; it persists until RCPM (and in some cases nsxa) is restarted during which time routing
updates for the affected edge are not processed. Edge CLI-based troubleshooting (such as get route) might also be
unresponsive during the affected window.
Workaround:
Restart the RCPM service (and nsxa, if it has also stopped processing updates) on the affected edge to clear the
deadlocked state and restore routing convergence. As a preventive measure, edges that do not require dynamic BGP
neighbors can avoid exposure to this issue by using static BGP neighbor configuration only.

fabric status, creates a false impression of full DFW configuration. Management plane connectivity and other host services

Broadcom 612

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Sometimes these frequent DB updates lead to the stale revision exception which triggers CCP retry logic which

Since the groups are not updating quickly, Distributed Firewall (DFW) rules end up using outdated information. This can
cause traffic to be incorrectly allowed or blocked, which disrupts a customer's security policies.
Customers see consistent warnings and intermittent "Discovery Failed" errors when running Security
Intelligence policy recommendations.
Automated policy generation is halted that stalls micro-segmentation projects. Applications intended to be protected by
these policies remain exposed to security risks until the issue is manually worked around.
Following a floating IP or EgressIP failover event, network traffic continues to route to the former IP owner
causing a data path disruption. Checking the logical switch ARP table reveals stale MAC addresses mapped to
the active IP address. These invalid records persist indefinitely in the host's NestDB and cannot be cleared by
restarting the host-side cfgagent or opsagent services.
This issue results in a production platform outage, which misroutes application traffic and disrupts end-user access to
impacted cluster services. The communication failure affects all ESX hosts shared to the specific controller node holding
the stale record.
Host live upgrades fail with a traceback RunCommandError: Output from command ... exceeds 1048576 bytes.
Memory usage in net-vdl2 increases linearly during the backup loop, and BFD multipliers may reset to 0, causing
session flapping.
Lifecycle upgrades fail completely in scale environments with over 1,000 BFD sessions requiring manual host reboots or
recovery steps. This extends maintenance windows and increases administrative overhead.
The original code checked only the most recent 1024-byte PTY read chunk against the prompt regex; if the kernel
delivered "sftp> " split across two or more reads, the prompt was never matched. This left the sftp subprocess
waiting for input that never came. Because support bundle generation internally invoked the Backup List API
(which lists all backup files over SFTP), the hang/slowness surfaced as support bundle generation taking
excessively long or appearing stuck, especially with many existing backups.
Support bundle collection could hang or take a very long time to complete on NSX Manager nodes with SFTP-based
backup configured delaying troubleshooting/case data collection. No data loss or corruption occurs. This is an availability
and a latency impact on the backup and support-bundle workflows only.
The BgpNeighborState runbook does not collect any stats if the BGP peer is in the ESTABLISHED state.
No functional impact, but customers want to check their setup health in general by running the ODS runbook diagnostics
like ping test, packet captures and traceroute.
During a brief IPsec/IKE session flap (for example, triggered by a missed IKE rekey and hard-lifetime expiry),
the tunnel is torn down and re-established within the same second with no real data-plane impact. However, the
L2VPN_session_DOWN alarm raised at the moment of the flap does not clear immediately. It persists for roughly
two minutes before the alarm-resolution logic finally catches up, because the retry timer needed to detect the
recovered/UP state was not being (re)armed in all conditions.
Monitoring and alerting systems report a false L2VPN outage of around two minutes even though the tunnel actually
recovered instantly with no observed traffic loss.
Workload VMs experience packet drops when co-located on the same ESX host as the edge node. The issue
persists when i) the Edge Uplink Profile transport VLAN is unset or set to 0. ii) The Edge VTEP fastpath (fp-
ethx) interface is connected to a non-trunk Distributed Virtual Port Group (DVPG). iii) Both the Edge VTEP and
management/VLAN Host Switch interfaces are connected to VLAN-tagged DVPGs.
Customers using the specific configuration described above will experience datapath traffic interruptions due to packet
drops for workload VMs residing on the same host as the edge node.
Edge Services DHCP opened port 1167 for DHCP leases sync. It used four ciphers for handshake in which two
non-AEAD ciphers are identified as weak, but are not excluded.
Customers are exposed to cryptographic vulnerabilities (specifically non-AEAD cipher risks) on the DHCP HA sync port
that potentially compromises the security of Edge Services.

Broadcom 614

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Introduction
VCF Installer / SDDC Manager 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25713928
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
Reduced resource footprint for VCF management services
VCF management services now require less compute and memory resources for all deployment sizes. For sizing details,
see the VCF 9.1.1 Planning and Preparation Workbook. To reduce the footprint on environments patched to version 9.1.1,
see Broadcom knowledge base article 455842.
New default deployment size selection
When you deploy a new VCF fleet or VCF Instance, the VCF Installer UI defaults to a starting deployment size of
small, replacing the previous default of medium. The small deployment size provides full capability and is optimized for
production environments that require High Availability. To match your scale size, during deployment, you can change the
default setting.
VCF Operations must now reside in the management domain of the first VCF Instance
Starting with VCF 9.1.1, it is required that VCF Operations resides in the management domain of the first VCF Instance in
the VCF fleet. This is mandated by all VCF Installer workflows.
Getting to 9.1.1
For information about deploying, converging, upgrading or patching your environment to 9.1.1, see Getting to 9.1.1.
Resolved Issues
Hosts with NIC speed lower than 10Gbit used only for management are blocked and deployment of VCF
management and workload domains fails.
With VCF 9.1.1 and later, ESX hosts with 1Gbit NIC are supported and no longer require the following conditions:
• In the management domain or workload domain creation workflow, on the Network settings page, for VM
Management Network, the Use a separate, dedicated network option is selected.
• The vSphere Distributed Switch with the 1Gbit+ NIC is used for ESX management traffic only.
• A separate vSphere Distributed Switch for vSAN, vMotion, and NSX Traffic uses one or more 10Gbit NICs.
