Known Issues
When upgrading SDDC Manager from 9.0.x , the upgrade fails with error
Timed out or the process exited
.
without updating status while waiting for upgrade to finish
On SDDC Manager 9.0.x appliances, a Photon OS background job periodically refreshes package update information
and holds the package manager lock while it attempts to contact the package repository. On networks that silently drop
outbound traffic to the repository, the job holds the the package manager lock for approximately 48 minutes. The upgrade
needs the same the package manager lock to install packages, waits for it to become available, and times out after 25
minutes.
Before starting the upgrade, stop the background job on the SDDC Manager appliance as root:
systemctl stop tdnf-cache-updateinfo.timer tdnf-cache-updateinfo.service
Broadcom 615

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Verify that both units report inactive:
systemctl is-active tdnf-cache-updateinfo.timer tdnf-cache-updateinfo.service
This stops the update-check job until the next reboot. Run the command again if the appliance is rebooted before the
upgrade starts.
If an upgrade attempt has already failed, check for a leftover script:
pgrep -af cap_platform_setup
Run the stop command so the leftover script can finish, wait until shows no output, then retry the upgrade.
pgrep
Submitting a component-scoped patch plan causes previously patched components to incorrectly display a
status.
VERSION_DRIFT
After upgrading to a major release and patching a component, submitting a new component-scoped patch plan, such as
patching only VC or NSX, causes other already patched components to fall back to the base BoM version in the release
manifest rather than their current version. This leads to an incorrect report on the Component Version
VERSION_DRIFT
page. The issue compounds across sequential single-component patches, because each new plan save discards the prior
plan's per-component targets. The display issue is cosmetic only and does not affect the actual component versions or
patch operations.
Delete the current patch plan or successfully complete its application. Either action clears the incorrect
VERSION_DRIFT
status display on the Component Version page.
When invalid vCenter Single Sign-On credentials are provided, VCF Installer fails on the Validate & Deploy page
During the Deployment Specification validation phase, the exception handler in the validator catches an authentication
failure and misattributes it to a missing DVS network configuration. Since this validator
vim.fault.InvalidLogin
encounters the error first, the validation process halts before the dedicated credential check runs and displays the
correct authentication error message. As a result, even when the vCenter VM is already attached to a Distributed Virtual
Switch, VCF Installer displays the following error message:
vCenter VM must be connected to a Distributed
Virtual Switch.
Workaround: In the deployment specification, enter the correct vCenter Single Sign-On administrator credentials and retry
the deployment.
After upgrading SDDC Manager to version 9.1.1, in the offline depot settings, the VCF Operations UI displays
Hostname, Port, and Username instead of the Depot URL.
An offline depot that you configured before the upgrade stores its address as separate hostname and port values in the
backend record. The upgrade does not migrate this legacy record to the new URL field format, which stores the depot
address as a single URL. As a result, the read-only depot settings continue to show the legacy fields.
Workaround: Perform one of the following tasks.
• Disconnect the offline depot and reconnect it by using the URL format.
• In the offline depot settings, click Edit -> Save.

steps display NSX-Overlay traffic type and overlay Transport Zone labels, even though the deployment is TEP-less.
When you select VLAN backed VPC on the NSX Manager step, the Distributed Switch selection screen lists
NSX-
in the Supported Traffic Type column, and the Review screen displays ,
Overlay NSX-Overlay Traffic Overlay
, and a transport zone. The IP Assignment (TEP) field correctly shows . The overlay transport zone is
Networking None
created internally as part of the VLAN-backed VPC configuration and is required by NSX. The overlay labels are graphical
artifacts, non-functional, and do not indicate that the deployment uses overlay networking or TEPs. The VLAN-backed
VPC configuration is operational and there is no functional impact.
None. The overlay transport zone labels do not affect the TEP-less VLAN-backed VPC configuration.

When you deploy a new VCF Instance by using the VCF Installer UI and select VLAN-backed VPC, the VLAN

of required VLANs.
When selecting a port group in VCF Installer, the Select port group dialog lists multiple entries with the same
name and without distinguishing information, as a result you might select a wrong port group
The port group picker lists all port groups from the specified vCenter Server instance, without filtering or additional context.
Selecting an incorrect port group can cause operation failure or completing an operation with the management networks
attached to the wrong network backing.
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
1. In the vSphere Client, locate the cluster on which the vCenter appliance VM runs and note its data center. The port
group you must select is the one attached to a Distributed Switch in that data center and attached to that cluster.
2. Rename that port group so that its name is unique across all data centers and Distributed Switches in the vCenter
instance.
3. Return to VCF Installer, open the Select port group dialog, and select the port group by its new, unique name.
Adding a new cluster to a VLAN-backed virtual private cloud (VPC) workload domain has no network span or
transit gateway associated with it, resulting in an incomplete network configuration. Adding a new cluster to a
tepless Workload Domain results in a tepless cluster with no network span defined.
When you add a new cluster to a workload domain that uses a VLAN-backed VPC configuration, SDDC Manager creates
the cluster in TEP-less mode but does not associate a network span or configure a transit gateway. The workflow neither
inherits the parent domain's network span. For existing vSphere clusters imported to or synced with SDDC Manager,
the import and sync workflows associate all VLAN-backed VPC clusters under a vCenter with the same network span
and transit gateway, but if the VLAN configuration differs or the vSphere Distributed Switch is not shared, the clusters
experience connectivity issues.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 454415.
When performing parallel upgrade of VCF components, VCF Operations upgrade fails
When you upgrade VCF components to version 9.1.1 and upgrade VCF Operations in parallel, the upgrade fails due to
race conditions.
Workaround: Upgrade VCF Operations separately from other VCF components. Before proceeding with upgrading other
VCF components, verify that the upgrade is completed successfully.
SDDC Manager allows upgrades of VCF core components before VCF Operations is upgraded to or above the
target version
SDDC Manager permits core components upgrades, such as vCenter, ESX, and SDDC Manager itself, while VCF
Operations still runs on an earlier version. Upgrading the core components before upgrading VCF Operations can cause
environmental issues.
Workaround: Before proceeding with any VCF core component upgrades, verify that VCF Operations is at or above the
target version.
Inventory sync for an out-of-band workload domain fails at the
Update or create with given network span
step
Inventory sync for an out-of-band workload domain fails at the Update or create with given network span step with the
error
Invalid Configuration: Transit Gateway path=[/orgs/default/projects/default/transit-
.
gateways/default] network stack cannot be changed from FULL_STACK_VPC to VLAN_BACKED_VPC
This issue occurs when you add a cluster to a workload domain that shares an automatically deployed NSX instance in
a converged environment and then trigger an inventory sync. SDDC Manager attempts to reuse the NSX default transit
gateway (TGW) for the new cluster, which uses VLAN-backed configuration. If the default TGW already serves virtual
private clouds (VPCs) that use the full stack VPC configuration, NSX rejects the reconfiguration because a TGW network
stack cannot change from a full stack VPC to VLAN-backed VPC while VPCs are attached.
See Broadcom knowledge base article 452453.
When importing a vCenter instance in a scaled setup requires more than 60 seconds, the import validation
operation fails or timeout with HTTP 504 error
Broadcom 617

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When importing an existing vCenter instance in a scaled setup, if API validations response acknowledgment has not
returned in 60 seconds, the VCF Operations UI closes or times out the connection and UI displays HTTP 504 error that
indicates the operation has failed or was interrupted. Validation process continues to run in the background.
Workaround: Use the SDDC Manager API to import the instance. You can run the APIs from the SDDC API explorer or
from the command prompt.
1. By using the import vCenter payload, initiate a validation.
POST /v1/sddcs/imports/validations
2. To check the validation progress, poll the task ID received from the previous request.
GET /v1/sddcs/imports/{taskId}
3. After the validation succeeds, perform the import.
POST /v1/sddcs/imports
When upgrading to VCF 9.1.1 by using the Optimized upgrade sequence, the NSX pre-check or upgrade fails
After the vCenter preparation phase ends, initiating the NSX Manager upgrade or pre-check immediately from the
Upgrades tab, results in the following UI error message:
Invalid upgrade spec, nsxtld passed as null.
Workaround: Refresh the browser page and retry the upgrade.
When configuring upgrades in an environment with vLCM and VUM clusters, an error occurs
In an environment that contains both vLCM and VUM clusters, configuring an upgrade for one cluster type and then
configuring an upgrade for the other cluster type may cause the Configure Upgrade wizard to retain stale cluster selection
state. As a result, the wizard may display stale clusters, leading to an incorrect upgrade specification being submitted and
the upgrade request failing.
Workaround: Refresh the browser page and configure the upgrade.

What's New
Operate
Changes to the SDDC Manager Log Configuration
Log collection across all VCF components is now fully managed within VCF Operations. This update extends automated
log configuration to SDDC Manager, eliminating manual setup. Users can now enable, disable, filter, and control log
volume to suit their environment. For more information, see Managing Collection from Log Sources.
Outbound Network Proxy Settings for cloud proxy deployment
Starting with VCF 9.1.1.0, when you deploy a new cloud proxy using the cloud proxy OVA, you can set up Outbound
Network Proxy Settings to route external traffic (for example: Broadcom Portal) through a dedicated proxy. For more
information, see Configuring Cloud Proxies in VCF Operations.
VMware Salt for VCF Components API
The VMware Salt for VCF Components API is now available. Based on VMware Salt, this new API lets you
programmatically manage designated configuration settings across the VCF stack. Using native Salt constructs, you can
implement and maintain desired state consistently across VCF Components.
Manage
On-demand lookup
You can now search AD users and groups on-demand using identity broker, with real-time authentication based on group
membership and privileges at login. For more information, see Configure Active Directory as an Identity Provider Using
AD/LDAP, (Optional) Assign VCF Roles to Groups and Users using On-Demand Lookup, and Managing VCF Single Sign-
On.
VCF Roles
Starting from vCenter 9.1.1.0, the VCF admin role and any custom VCF role that includes the vCenter admin role are
automatically mapped to the local vCenter Administrators group. For more information, see Managing VCF Roles.
Broadcom 619

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Improved user experience with licensing
Error messages now provide more extensive information about the issue and remediation guidance.
License Server IPv6 Support
Starting with version 9.1.1.0, the license server supports IPv6 networking that uses static addressing, or DHCPv6/
SLAAC. For more information, see License Server Networking.
Password Management
• VCF Operations now manages additional OS and application accounts, including the vCenter
account, SDDC Manager , , and accounts.
administrator@vsphere.local root admin@local vcf
• VCF Automation, VCF Operations for networks and cloud proxy now support password policy management through
VCF Operations.
• VCF Operations now displays the last password update date for all managed accounts.
• You can now remove password policy from selected VCF Instances. When you remove a password policy from a
VCF instance the instance falls back to the fleet policy, if one is configured, or to the component's own password
requirements.
• All local account-related operations are audited, including account creation, successful and failed logins, password
updates, password policy updates, and account lockouts.
• You can update the password for a locked or expired account from VCF Operations. Password update does not
change the lockout state of the account.
For more information, see Managing Passwords for VCF Components.
Certificate Management
• VCF Operations now manages certificates for additional components, including NSX (all appliances), cloud proxy,
license server, VCF Operations for networks collector node, Security Token Service (STS), vSphere Supervisor
certificates, vSAN storage certificates, and VCF Automation.
• You can replace certificates that are signed by a configured or a non-configured CA with VMCA-signed certificates
before they expire.
• VCF Operations generates expiry alarms for all certificates across VCF components, including certificates that are not
managed by VCF Operations.
• VCF Operations detects and displays self-signed CA certificates as self-signed in the VCF Operations UI.
For more information, see Managing Certificates in VCF.
VCF Operations APIs for Tag Management
VCF Operations now exposes APIs through which administrators can manage VCF tags across a VCF Fleet.
Service Provider Metadata Re-Import Recommended for SAML Customers
Starting with identity broker 9.1.1.0, the service provider (SP) metadata published by the identity broker includes a
new EncryptionMethod hint that signals enterprise identity providers to use RSA-OAEP with SHA-256 for SAML assertion
encryption. This replaces the previous behavior where no algorithm hint was provided, and which caused some identity
providers to default to SHA-1 OAEP.
If you have SAML federation configured with an enterprise identity provider such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID,
PingFederate, or ADFS, it is recommended that you re-import the identity broker service provider metadata into your
identity provider after you upgrade to 9.1.1.0. Re-importing ensures your identity provider reads the new encryption hint
and switches to SHA-256 OAEP for all subsequent SAML assertion encryption.
SAML login continues to work without re-importing since the identity broker retains a SHA-1 OAEP fallback in 9.1.1.0
while telemetry data is collected to confirm broad fleet adoption. The fallback will be removed in a future release and at
that point, SP metadata re-import will become mandatory.
For more information, see Configure Okta as an Identity Provider using SAML, Configure Ping Identity as an Identity
Provider Using SAML, Configure Microsoft Entra ID as an Identity Provider Using SAML, Configure Microsoft ADFS as an
Identity Provider Using SAML, Configure an Identity Provider using Generic SAML 2.0.
Non-vIDM Authentication Support for Shared Sessions for the VCF Operations Orchestrator Plug-in for VCF
Automation for VM apps
Broadcom 620

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Operations Orchestrator Plug-in for VCF Automation for VM apps supports use API token authentication, which
allows use of the plug-in in environments that configured without VMware Identity Manager when using a shared session.

Product Support Notes
Deprecation Notes
Deprecation announcement for Windows Server 2008 SP2 in VCF Operations HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM)
Removed support for Windows Server 2008 SP2 in VCF Operations HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM).
Deprecation announcement for support of VMware Cloud Director (VCD) as a destination in VCF Operations HCX
9.1.1.0
VMware Cloud Director (VCD) is no longer available as a destination in VCF Operations HCX 9.1.1.0.
Data collection results and Topology Graph widgets are marked as deprecated
Deprecation of low-usage widgets based on telemetry analysis. A deprecated warning icon appears on the corresponding
widget card.
Other Notes
Removal of AWS and Azure data source support in VCF Operations for networks
Starting with VCF 9.1.1.0, VCF Operations for networks removes support for AWS and Azure as data sources. In new
deployments, you cannot add AWS or Azure public clouds as data sources. If you upgrade an existing deployment that
has AWS or Azure public cloud data sources to VCF 9.1.1.0, VCF Operations for networks disables those data sources
and ceases data collection. However, you can continue to view and query data collected from AWS and Azure data
sources before the VCF 9.1.1.0 upgrade until you remove the data sources. For more information, see Adding a Data
Source in VCF Operations for networks.
Removal of the geo map within the VCF Operations UI
To ensure adherence to local laws, the geo map has been removed from the following areas within the VCF Operations
UI:
• Overview section of the Home page: The Inventory card no longer includes a map.
• Widget removal: The Geo widget is no longer available in the widget list during dashboard creation.
• Existing Dashboards: Existing dashboards containing a Geo widget (such as those that were imported or upgraded)
now show a 'Map view is no longer supported' message in the widget preview.
• Inventory Management (Manage Tags): The wrench control for managing geo locations on the map has been
removed.
• Sustainability: For Physical Data Centers, the map view has been removed, leaving only the list view available.
• Adding a Physical Data Center: The map, coordinates, and map-based location selection flow are no longer part of
the Physical Data Center addition process.
• Physical Data Center Details/Selection:The map has been removed from the selection screen, leaving only the
associated accounts visible.
Broadcom 621

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Removal of the Additional Storage Required metric and its associated symptoms, alerts, and dashboards.
In previous releases, the Additional Storage Required metric within the Log Management Health dashboard could
erroneously report a storage shortfall on clusters where log partitions were left at their default settings (without a user-
defined retention period). This non-zero value appeared even when ingestion rates were low and ample disk space
was available, inadvertently misleading users into believing they needed to provision more storage. Because this metric
does not accurately reflect a true storage deficit in the absence of a defined retention contract, the metric, along with any
symptoms, alerts, and dashboards that depend on it, has been removed in version 9.1.1.0.
Server Side Encryption field removed from the Add New Storage UI
The setting has been removed from the Add New Storage configuration UI. For AWS S3
serverSideEncryption
destinations, this option is no longer required because AWS now enforces AES-256 encryption on all buckets by default.
For non-AWS S3-compatible storage solutions, such as MinIO or Ceph, you must now enable default bucket-level auto-
encryption directly on their storage servers. If you previously relied on this UI setting to manage encryption, you must now
ensure that encryption policies are configured natively on your destination storage server.

Creating a vCenter cloud account using the default collector group fails with an unhandled error message when a
collector in the group is offline.
If a collector within the default collector group is offline or unavailable, the system fails to create a vCenter cloud account.
The operation fails because the assigned collector cannot process tasks. The user interface surfaces an unhandled
internal log message instead of a standard failure warning, providing no actionable information.
Updating an existing application monitoring service via the SuiteAPI PUT endpoint fails with a "Configuration
already used." error.
When using the SuiteAPI PUT endpoint /api/applications/agents/{id}/services to modify an existing application monitoring
service — such as setting isActivated to false to disable the service — the request returns HTTP 422 with API error code
1508. The error incorrectly reports a conflict between the service name and an existing configuration on the same VM,
even when no actual conflict exists. This failure affects all service update operations on existing application resources.
The content upgrade status for product-managed Telegraf agents intermittently displays as "Failed" despite the
agent upgrading successfully
When a content upgrade also upgrades the Salt minion, a separate synchronous Salt call used to verify/restore the
agent's running status could be issued while the minion was briefly offline during the minion swap, causing it to fail with
"Minion did not return" and incorrectly marking the whole content upgrade as failed — most noticeable on Application
Monitoring HA-enabled collector groups.
On Windows VMs running a non-English (localized) system language, the Telegraf agent status incorrectly
reports as unhealthy
The agent queries Windows services via using , which routes output
sc.exe subprocess.Popen with shell=True
through and its OEM code page. On localized Windows builds, for example, Polish, service display names
cmd.exe

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
containing non-ASCII characters cannot be decoded as UTF-8/ANSI, causing a that crashes the
UnicodeDecodeError
service-status check and marks the agent unhealthy.
The agent status on Windows machines intermittently appears as unhealthy
The UCP minion's service monitor periodically collects per-process CPU statistics to assess health. If a target
process exits between the time its PID is sampled and the time attempts to read its stats, raises a
psutil psutil
originating from the underlying OpenProcess Windows API call. Because this
NoSuchProcess/ProcessLookupError
exception is unhandled, the health and statistics collection fails, causing the agent's status to flip to unhealthy despite no
actual issue. This is a race condition triggered by short-lived or recently exited processes on Windows.
If a report contains text with a symbol that has no corresponding glyph in the font that is used, an exception is

An exception is thrown when a report contains the U+202F (narrow no-break space) Unicode character, which has no

When exporting a report to PDF, configured metric colorization does not render in the generated file
You encounter this issue in VCF 9.1.x when generating a PDF report from a view that has "Ranges for metric coloring"
configured. Although the metric colors display correctly within the user interface, they fail to pass through to the exported
PDF report.
When attempting to navigate from Inventory to another IP using Global Search, the page fails to redirect and

While viewing an object on the Inventory page, a user may need to navigate to another object that is not visible in the
current view or is difficult to access. To work around this, the user enters the target object's IP address in Global Search to
navigate to it directly. However, this does not work as expected and the page remains on the current view.

When a webhook notification template uses a JSON array as the root payload format, dynamic placeholders such as

Sticky bit not set for temporary directories created by the 'yarn' user.
Files created by the 'yarn' user in a temporary directory could be deleted by any user. This behavior was flagged as a

Git sync, check-in, or check-out operations fail for Configuration templates after a service restart.

The VMware Cloud (VMC) SDDC group dashboard does not display route tables and SDDC information, and

Manage
API calls allowed VCF single-sign configuration on component vCenter and NSX instances even when VCF single
sign-on for that VCF Instance was already managed (at least one vCenter or NSX instance already had VCF single
sign-on configured) by a different VCF Operations
API calls did not perform eligibility checks on component vCenter and NSX instances when the VCF single sign-on of
those components was managed by a different VCF Operations instance. As a result, users could configure VCF single
sign-on using API.
When a vCenter instance has multiple v8 license keys of the same product family, host, socket, and core counts
are doubled in Cost Driver > License, resulting in doubled host costs.
During v8 license discovery, discovered OS types are accumulated in a list instead of a set. When a vCenter instance
has more than one VCF License of the same product family (such as two VCF or two VVF keys), the same OS type is
appended multiple times. Each server is then registered against that license once per duplicate entry, causing vmCount,
socketCount, and coreCount totals to be multiplied by the number of duplicate license keys.
After removing all user-assigned license mappings from Custom License Assignment for a host, the Monthly
Host OS License Total Cost metric continues to include the cost of all the removed license mappings.
When all user-assigned host licenses are unmapped from Custom License Assignment, leaving the User Assigned
column empty, the expected result is the reduction of OS license cost for that host. However, the cost calculation engine
continues to factor in all previously assigned license costs in the Monthly Host OS License Total Cost metric even after the
mappings are cleared.
When the License cost driver is configured with an Enterprise License Agreement (ELA) fixed cost, running a
cost calculation does not apply the ELA costs to hosts. The Host License Cost metric remains unchanged.
When a user selects the ELA cost option in the License cost driver, saves an amount, and runs a cost calculation, the
Host License Cost metric does not update with the new ELA costs across applicable hosts. This issue occurs only when
the License cost driver is the sole cost driver with a fixed cost enabled. If any other cost driver also has a fixed cost
configured, the issue does not manifest.
When exporting the Server Hardware: Hyperconverged cost driver data from the cost driver summary page, the
exported Excel file contains traditional server data instead of hyperconverged server data.
Steps to Reproduce
When a user navigates to the cost driver summary page and exports the Server Hardware: Hyperconverged data as an
Excel file, the export incorrectly populates with a list of traditional servers instead of hyperconverged servers.
When the allocation cost model is enabled and "Cluster Usable Capacity after HA and Buffer" calculation model
is selected, the Cluster CPU Base Rate is computed using Total Capacity (cores) instead of Usable Capacity
(cores), causing VM cost metrics to be lower than expected.
When a cluster has vSphere HA enabled, the allocation cost model is configured and Cluster Usable Capacity after HA
and Buffer calculation model selected, the Cluster CPU Base Rate should be derived from the usable CPU core count
after HA fail over reservations are subtracted. However, the cost engine uses the total physical core count of the cluster,
ignoring HA-reserved capacity. This results in a lower-than-expected CPU Base Rate and cost metrics that do not reflect
the configured allocation model.

when inspecting cluster metrics.
vCenter instances integrated through the VCF Management Pack are classified as "Hybrid Cloud" environments. The cost

VCF Services Runtime
During identity broker upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1, the upgrade process might stop responding at the backup stage
for up to 120 minutes and display only a generic timeout error
Broadcom 625

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
This behavior affects administrators performing the upgrade and can cause uncertainty about whether the upgrade is
progressing or has failed. This issue is fixed in this release and upgrade fails fast on a backup failure and displays a clear
error.
Entering a hostname or FQDN in mixed case caused failures in install, upgrade, import, and other operations of
VCF management services or VCF Automation
Issue occurs due to case-sensitive Domain Name System (DNS) and certificate matching. This issue is fixed in this
release and all FQDNs can use mixed case.
When you power on a VCF management services or VCF Automation cluster, some services might fail to resume
After a shutdown or a power-cycle of the cluster, one or more services could fail to start automatically and required
manual recovery. This issue is fixed in this release and services recover automatically after power-on.
VCF services runtime can accumulate log buffers, which results in the logger disk to fill up and health-check
failures
Fluentd log buffers and retained backup chunks can accumulate on the logging disk until available disk space is
exhausted. When the logging disk reaches capacity, platform health checks fail and block platform operations. This issue
is fixed in this release and logging buffer is improved.
Known Issues
Build
Duplicate error messages appear on failed fleet lifecycle tasks
Some fleet lifecycle tasks automatically retry upon failure to improve overall task reliability. However, this change causes
duplicate error messages to appear when a task fails and is retried. Users may observe repeated error entries for a single
failed task, which can make troubleshooting more difficult.
Workaround: None
Component installation can fail during VCF service runtime node rotation
Fleet lifecycle services run on a single node. During a VCF services runtime platform node rotation operation, an in-
progress component installation can fail. Fleet lifecycle automatically retries the installation of the component. In the worst
case, the retry does not succeed and the installation task fails, requiring you to retry the task manually.
Workaround: If the component installation task fails, retry the task.
Scaling a VCF services runtime component can fail with a misleading task status after a transient network
interruption
When you scale a VCF services runtime component, such as from Small to Large, a transient network
vsp-platform
or infrastructure interruption can cause the orchestrator to lose track of the task status polling loop in
sddc-build-
. The underlying scale operation completes successfully on the component, but the orchestrator times out while
service
waiting for a status update and retries the scaling request. The retry request is rejected by a guard validation that prevents
no-op configuration updates, so the workflow task is marked FAILED even though the component reached the requested
scale size. If you retry the same operation from the UI or from the API client, you will encounter the same no-op guard
because the internal VSP task is already scaled to Large.
Workaround: This issue causes no functional impact, data loss, or service downtime. To verify that the component has
been scaled to the target size, check the component size displayed in the fleet lifecycle UI. If the component reflects
the updated target size, such as Large, no further action or retry is necessary and the failed task notification can be
disregarded.
Successful tasks show failing sub-tasks
When an internal workflow contains sub-workflows that fail initially, the VCF Operation UI displays the failed attempts as
errors, even though subsequent retries succeed and the task completes successfully. This behavior is expected and is
caused by detailed task progress tracking, which now records failed sub-task attempts.
Workaround: None.
Broadcom 626

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Scaling VCF Management Services runtime from Small to Small (High Availability) fails with the error "An
error occurred while updating config for component with ID:xxxx" and the SDDC Lifecycle log shows the error
message "Unexpected value 'small_ha'."
VCF Management Services runtime scaling from Small to Small (High Availability) fails when Fleet Lifecycle is upgraded
to 9.1.1 but SDDC Lifecycle remains on 9.1.0. The Small (High Availability) functionality is introduced in both Fleet
Lifecycle and SDDC Lifecycle 9.1.1, so you can use the functionality only after both components are upgraded to 9.1.1.
Workaround: Use one of the following workarounds:
• Upgrade SDDC Lifecycle to 9.1.1 along with the Fleet Lifecycle upgrade, and then perform the scale operation from
Small to Small (High Availability).
• Scale to another size, such as Medium or Large, based on the available resources.
When creating or updating the backup configuration for a VCF management services, the operation fails and the
UI displays a generic error message
When creating or configuring a backup for VCF management services in the VCF Operations UI, the backup configuration
task can fail for either of the following reasons.
• SFTP connectivity failure. VCF services runtime cannot reach or authenticate against the configured SFTP server.
• Multi-cluster inconsistency. In an environment with VCF Automation deployed, the backup configuration can succeed
on one VCF services runtime cluster and fail on another.
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
1. Verify network connectivity, host key trust, and credentials between VCF services runtime cluster and the SFTP server.
2. If the failure persists, file a Support Request (SR) with Broadcom Support and attach the VCF Services Runtime
support bundle.
When you install Real-time metrics, Log Management, and VCF Operations for networks in parallel, the Real-
time metrics installation fails and the VCF Operations for networks installation appears stuck for more than three
hours before eventually failing.
When you trigger the installation of Real-time metrics, Log Management, and VCF Operations for networks in parallel, a
simultaneous platform node replacement can transiently disrupt platform health. The Real-time metrics installation detects
the disruption and fails immediately with a platform health-check error. The VCF Operations for networks installation does
not detect the disruption, so it continues to run without progress or error until the installation workflow times out after three
hours.
Workaround: Avoid installing VCF Operations for Networks in parallel with components that can trigger VCF Services
Runtime platform node scaling, such as Log Management. Install these components sequentially instead. If the installation
is stuck, you must wait for the installation workflow's three-hour timeout to fail the task, after which you can retry the
installation.
Onboarding and deploy steps on extra-large scale vCenter instances may time out with a 504 Gateway Timeout
error.
On extra-large scale vCenter environments, for example 2,000 or more hosts and 30,000 or more virtual machines,
validation and cluster selection steps during VVVF or VCF onboarding in the installer, converge, or import workflow may
take over an hour to complete. Clicking Deploy may trigger a transient 504 Gateway Timeout error before the deployment
starts.
Workaround: Retry the Deploy operation. The 504 Gateway Timeout error is transient, and the deployment proceeds
on retry. If the problem persists, use the APIs in the VMware Cloud Foundation® Operations fleet management
developer center. Run the Validation API followed by the Import API. For more information, see the VCF Operations fleet
management API reference.
The VCF Operations upgrade precheck shows raw, unresolved resource-bundle keys and JSON instead of
human-readable text for the Management Pack compatibility check
When you run the VCF Operations 9.1 to 9.1.1.0 upgrade precheck from the VCF Operations fleet management UI, the
"Validating Management Pack Compatibility with VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1.1" precheck correctly detects
and reports incompatible Management Packs, but the Message and Resolution fields display raw, unresolved resource-
Broadcom 627

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
bundle keys and JSON instead of human-readable text. The separately downloaded APUAT support bundle HTML report
renders the same result correctly.
Workaround: Download the APUAT support bundle HTML report from the same precheck run. The report renders the
Management Pack compatibility check results correctly, including the full message and recommendation text.
The Small deployment size is missing for the High Availability deployment model in the Deploy deferred
components workflow.
When you deploy VCF Operations and VCF Automation using a custom network through the Deploy deferred
components option in the VCF Installer, the deployment size selector for the High Availability model shows only Medium
and Large. Small is not available, so you cannot select it for a high availability deployment in this workflow.
Workaround: Use one of the following workarounds:
• Use the existing high availability deployment sizes, Medium or Large.
• Use the JSON input option and pass the VCF Operations master and replica node details with appliance size set
to Small.
• Use the simple deployment model with Small size, complete the deployment, and then deploy the replica node for the
VCF Operations component in the VCF Operations fleet management UI and enable high availability.
A joined VCF Instance does not appear on the Integration/Registrations page in VCF Operations after the join
task reports success.
A transient disruption affects a service that VCF Operations depends on internally (for example VCF Operations for
networks), while VCF Operations registers the newly joined VCF Instance. If the disruption lasts longer than the automatic
retry window, the registration does not complete on the VCF Operations side, but the join task in VCF Operations fleet
management still reports success. No error or failure appears in the VCF Operations fleet management UI or task history,
so the issue can go unnoticed unless you check the Integration/Registrations page after the join operation.
Workaround: If a VCF Instance does not appear on the Integration/Registrations page in VCF Operations after a join
operation reports success, manually add the VCF Instance from the UI.
Deploying to a VSP cluster by using the VCF Operations load balancer FQDN fails with an error that the
hostname does not match the address of any of the VCF cluster nodes
When deploying to a VSP cluster, the deployment workflow prompts for either the VCF Operations load balancer FQDN
or the master node hostname. If you provide the VCF Operations load balancer FQDN, the workflow reports that the
hostname does not match the address of any of the VCF cluster nodes, and the installation cannot start. This issue occurs
only when the load balancer FQDN is provided as the target hostname.
Workaround: Provide the hostname of the VCF Operations master node instead of the VCF Operations load balancer
FQDN, and restart the installation process.
Management packs created with the Management Pack Builder break after VCF Operations is upgraded to
version 9.1.1
Upgrading VCF Operations to version 9.1.1 also upgrades the Management Pack Builder, causing custom management
packs built with a previous version of the Management Pack Builder to stop functioning correctly after the upgrade.
Workaround: Recreate the affected management packs using the updated Management Pack Builder after VCF
Operations has been upgraded to version 9.1.1. For more information, see KB 454434.
Operate
When you deploy a secondary VCF Instance at a newer version than the existing VCF Operations instance,
the SDDC Manager of the secondary VCF Instance does not appear as a VCF Adapter on the Administration ->
Integrations tab in VCF Operations UI
The cloud proxy deployed for a secondary VCF Instance must match the exact version of the VCF Operations cluster that
it connects to. If the secondary instance runs a newer version, its cloud proxy fails to register, and the secondary instance
never appears on the Integration tab, even when the rest of the deployment completes without error. When you add an
instance to an existing fleet, VCF Installer validates only version compatibility between cloud proxy and
major.minor
VCF Operations instead of the exact version match that cloud proxy requires.
Broadcom 628

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: Upgrade VCF Operations to the same version as the secondary VCF Instance and perform one of the
following tasks, that matches the current state of the VCF Adapter.
• If cloud proxy is already registered and the VCF Adapter instance exists in an error state and cannot start because of
the version mismatch, the VCF Adapter instance recovers after the VCF Operations upgrade.
• If the VCF Adapter instance was not created, add the secondary VCF Instance after the upgrade.
Note: To avoid this issue, before you deploy a secondary VCF Instance, upgrade VCF Operations to the desired target
version or deploy the secondary VCF Instance at a version that matches the current VCF Operations version.
Operations for Logs Agent 8.18.x installation fails on Linux systems after a failed 9.1.0.0 installation attempt
On Linux operating systems with OpenSSL versions earlier than 3.0 (for example, Ubuntu 18.04), installing Operations
for Logs Agent 9.1.0.0 fails because the OpenSSL version does not meet the minimum requirement. If you then attempt
to install an earlier agent version, such as 8.18.5 or 8.18.6, which does not depend on OpenSSL 3.0, the installation fails
with a package conflict error similar to:
dpkg: regarding VMware-Log-Insight-Agent-8.18.5-24965621.deb containing vmware-log-insight-agent:
operations-logs-agent conflicts with vmware-log-insight-agent
dpkg: error processing archive VMware-Log-Insight-Agent-8.18.5-24965621.deb (--install):
conflicting packages - not installing vmware-log-insight-agent
This occurs because remnants of the failed 9.1.0.0 package remain on the system and
operations-logs-agent
conflict with the earlier package.
vmware-log-insight-agent
Workaround:
Before installing the earlier agent version, remove the leftover 9.1.0.0 agent package by running:
sudo dpkg -P operations-logs-agent
Then proceed with installing the desired earlier agent version (for example, 8.18.5 or 8.18.6).
Log Management Disaster Recovery displays an error after restoration
Log Management Disaster Recovery (DR) requires manual intervention to be fully functional. The Operations UI in the Log
Analysis page currently displays the following error, after restoration, which prevents it from being fully operational:
Unable to access logs due to user permissions.
Workaround: If you encounter this issue, perform a service restart of the log management service via Fleet LCM using
the component Stop / Start action.
After a new service instance is added to a product managed Telegraf agent, the service instance cannot be
reliably edited or deleted
Impact:
• Avoid adding new service instances on a product-managed Telegraf agent in VCF Operations 9.1.1.0, because they
cannot be reliably edited or deleted afterward.
• Data collection for existing and newly added service instances continues to work normally.
Workaround: If you have already added a new service instance in 9.1.1.0 and need to edit or delete it, the only
remediation is to reinstall the Telegraf agent without retaining the existing Telegraf configuration, then re-add all service
instances from scratch. Manually editing the file does not work.
.conf

may stop collecting data and move to a Not Existing state, even though the Supervisor Cluster itself is healthy.
The Supervisor adapter depends on connection/trust information from the associated vCenter adapter instance rather

collection failures that can eventually cause the resource to be marked .
Not Existing
This can occur even if the certificate rotation happens on only one domain (for example, the management domain). The
resulting collection failure can affect Supervisor adapter instances across all domains, not just the domain where the
rotation occurred.

– Start the Supervisor adapter instance again.

– If the Supervisor adapter instance shows , confirm that the vCenter adapter instance is
No Data Receiving
collecting successfully post-rotation.

ID

retrieved above.
– Once the vCenter adapter instance is confirmed healthy, no further action is needed. The vCenter adapter will
automatically recreate the Supervisor adapter instance as part of its regular collection interval.
Workload domain accounts remain in Stopped state after configuring a VCF account in VCF Operations 9.1 or
later
When a VCF 5.2.1 account is configured, or an existing VCF cloud account is upgraded to VCF Operations 9.1 or later,
workload domain sub-accounts (vCenter and NSX) may remain in a Stopped status and fail to collect data. When you
attempt to edit an affected workload domain account, the following UI issues are observed:
• The vCenter hostname field does not pre-populate in the Edit wizard.
• Clicking Validate Connection returns a generic Error trying to establish connection failure with no diagnostic detail.
• The NSX tab within the Edit wizard renders as a blank form with no input fields.
These accounts appear assigned to the default legacy collector instead of the configured cloud proxy, causing collection
to never start.
Workaround: Manually re-save each workload domain account to rebind it to the correct cloud proxy and activate
collection. For more information, see Configuring a Standalone VCF Account in VCF Operations.
Platform nodes in a VCF Operations for networks cluster do not appear simultaneously on the agent listing page.
Instead, their entries toggle or overwrite one another
When deploying or running a multi-node VCF Operations for networks cluster, the VCF Operations for logs agent
instances on each platform node generate identical cached ID configurations. This shared ID conflict causes the agent
listing page to constantly overwrite node entries rather than displaying all active cluster nodes at the same time.
Workaround:
To resolve the ID collision across the cluster:
1. SSH into Platform 1 of the VCF Operations for networks clustered deployment (or the single-node deployment) using
the support user.
2. Switch to the ubuntu user:
ub
3. Stop the VCF Operations for logs agent service across all nodes:
./run_all.sh sudo service liagentd stop
4. Remove the cached ID configuration files to force a reset: .
/run_all.sh sudo rm -r /var/lib/loginsight-
agent/storage
5. Restart the VCF Operations for logs agent service to generate a new, unique ID for each node: .
/run_all.sh sudo
service liagentd start
Broadcom 630

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Manage
After you upgrade a vCenter instance to version 9.1.0.0300, the vCenter instance does not appear on the
Licensing page in VCF Operations
After you upgrade a vCenter instance from version 9.0.x to version 9.1.0.0300, the vCenter instance does not appear
in the VCF Operations UI under Manage > Licensing, so you cannot assign a license to the vCenter instance. In the
vSphere Client, no licenses are displayed on the Administration page. There is no banner to indicate that there are
unlicensed assets.
A stale or orphaned vSphere+ subscription license in the vCenter LDAP database prevents the vCenter instance from
appearing in the VCF Operations UI.
Identify the stale vSphere+ license and manually delete the license from the vCenter LDAP database. For more details,
see Broadcom knowledge base article 455886.
Duplicate completion markers displayed in the Add Plug-in wizard in VCF Operations orchestrator
When a user adds a new plug-in to VCF Operations orchestrator, the Add Plug-in wizard incorrectly displays two
overlapping or duplicate completion markers per step, like incomplete circles or green checkmarks, instead of displaying a
single completion marker.
Workaround: No workaround.
Missing selection column prevents removal of packages and dependencies in the VCF Operations orchestrator
Environment Editor
In VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.1, users might experience an issue where they cannot select and delete existing
packages, dependencies, or key:value pairs within the Environment Editor.
Workaround: If you need to remove a package or dependency, use the corresponding REST API endpoint or command-
line tool to update the environment's configuration. Alternatively, you can create a fresh environment configuration from
scratch containing only your desired dependencies.
After you patch the license server to version 9.1.1, used license capacity might appear higher than the actual
used capacity
After you patch the license server to version 9.1.1, the VCF Operations UI might incorrectly show the used license
capacity as higher than the actual used capacity. A warning message about license overuse might appear, and the system
might prevent license assignment. The issue affects only the information that the VCF Operations shows. Your assigned
licenses, used capacity, and reported usage remain correct on the VCF Business Services console.
Workaround: Perform the following steps to restart the VCF Operations cluster.
1. Ensure that all vCenter instances are running and connected to the license server.
2. Log in to the VCF Operations administration UI at <vcf_operations_fqdn> as the admin local
https:// /admin
user.
a. Take the VCF Operations cluster offline.
b. On the System status page, click Take cluster offline.
3. In the Take cluster offline dialog box, provide the reason for the shutdown and click OK. This operation might take
about an hour to complete.
4. To take the VCF Operations cluster online, on the System status page, click Bring cluster online and wait for the
operation to complete.
vCenter shows "Virtual Machine UEFI Secure Boot Platform Key is out of date." warning for the license server.
After you patch your vCenter from version 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1, you see this message in the issues and alarms section in the
vSphere Client where the license server is deployed. The alarm appears when you have license servers in version 9.1.0.x
or license servers patched to version 9.1.1. This alert is not critical and has no impact on the boot or the functionalities of
your license server.
Workaround: To resolve the alarm, from the vSphere Client, upgrade the compatibility of the license server VM to ESXi
6.7 and later by following the Upgrade the Compatibility of a Virtual Machine Manually procedure.
An update password task is marked as failed in VCF Operations, even though the password update on the target
component succeeds.
Broadcom 631

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When you update the password for an account in VCF Operations, the password is updated on the target component.
If that account is also used by a configured integration, VCF Operations additionally attempts to propagate the updated
password to the credential object associated with that integration. If the credential object is orphaned (no owner assigned
in VCF Operations), this secondary propagation step fails with . The
Operation is not allowed for credential
primary password rotation is not affected. The new password is valid on the target component. Only the propagation to the
orphaned integration credential fails, but the entire update password task is marked as failed.
Configure integrations to use service accounts rather than user-managed credential accounts (avoids the issue entirely).
If an integration's credential is already orphaned, assign it an owner in VCF Operations to restore normal propagation.
Alternatively, manually update the integration's credential with the new password as a one-time step.
While executing the 'Update Password' operation in VCF Operations for a , task timeout
vmware-system-user
triggers an error
An incorrect INVALID_CREDENTIALS error occurs ('the current password provided is incorrect') when the underlying
password-update task times out, despite the password being accurate.
Workaround: None
The password policy page is available in the VCF Operations UI before upgrade of the remaining VCF component
completes
After you upgrade VCF Operations to 9.1.1.0 from Aria Operations 8.18 or VCF Operations 9.0, but before you complete
the upgrade of the remaining VCF components, the password policy page is available in the VCF Operations UI. The
password policy page is introduced in VCF 9.1 and should not be available before all VCF components are upgraded to
version 9.1 and later.
Workaround: None
The VCF Operations UI incorrectly displays "No Expiry" for the vCenter root account even when it has expired.
This issue occurs only when the vCenter version is 9.1 or earlier and VCF Operations is at version 9.1.1.0
For vCenter 9.1 and earlier, the last password change date for an expired root account is incorrectly reset to 0, resulting in
an invalid expiry status.
Workaround: None
The operation fails with the error
Replace with VMware Certificate Authority (VMCA) Failed to
when the certificate signing request (CSR) contains wildcard entries in the
generate certificate from CSR
Subject Alternative Name (SAN) DNS field
VMCA does not support signing certificates with wildcard fully qualified domain name (FQDN) entries in the SAN field.
Workaround: Use wildcard SAN entries to replace the certificate using OpenSSL, Microsoft CA, or an external CA with
an imported certificate instead of VMCA. To use VMCA as the signing CA, provide all SAN FQDNs explicitly in the CSR
without wildcards.
Certificate replacement tasks fail after 2 hours when multiple certificate tasks run concurrently
VCF Operations does not support concurrent certificate rotation. Running multiple rotation operations at the same time
causes instability. When one task briefly restarts a service to apply its certificate, any other task running in parallel
may lose its connection, stall, and eventually time out. The VCF Operation UI already warns against running certificate
operations concurrently.
Workaround: Perform certificate replacements one at a time, and always wait for the active task to finish before starting
the next.
Bulk certificate replacement for NSX fails with the
Unable to obtain CSR ID from NSX for replace
certificate operation, Certificate mismatch detected when connecting to endpoint error
After upgrade to VCF 9.1.1.0, in NSX multi-node cluster environments upgraded from versions earlier than 9.0, bulk
certificate replacement can fail if the VIP certificate is replaced before the cluster node certificate. The updated certificate
may take time to become available, and if the next replacement attempt falls within the same collection window, a
certificate mismatch error occurs.
Workaround: Retry the certificate replacement for the failed component.
Broadcom 632

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Certificate operations fail with after a collector changes due to load balancing or a
Unable to find end point
user-initiated operation
If you perform certificate operations on an endpoint and the collector assigned to that endpoint changes before the
next VMware Infrastructure Management (VIM) adapter collection cycle (every 6 hours), the operations fail with
.
ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND
Workaround:
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. In the left pane, navigate to Administration > Configurations.
3. On the Configurations page, click the Inventory Management card.
4. In the left pane, navigate to Adapter Instances > VMware Infrastructure Management Adapter Instance.
5. For each adapter instance, click Start Maintenance, wait for ten seconds, and click End Maintenance.
After replacing the SSL certificate on an 8.x vCenter instance, attempts to establish or re-establish trust in VCF
Operations fail. Authentication using valid vSphere single sign-on credentials for an existing account is rejected,
and the SDDC Manager UI is inaccessible
The certificate replacement task in VCF Operations fails with the error: Certificate task REPLACE_CERTIFICATE for
vcenter-xxx has failed. Error message: Failed to retrust VCF Ops truststore. Additionally, SDDC Manager fails with the
error: Authorization Error : unauthorized access. As a result, the truststores of both SDDC Manager and VCF Operations
are affected, rendering the SDDC Manager UI inaccessible and disrupting VCF Operations.
Workaround: To resolve the SDDC Manager truststore issue, refer to KB 316056. After SDDC Manager is restored,
delete the VCF integration in VCF Operations and re-add it using the same credentials.
After a certificate is replaced on a VCF management component, VCF Operations might not re-establish trust with
that component until the next inventory synchronization, causing dependent tasks and inventory views to fail
This issue occurs when the periodic inventory synchronization between fleet lifecycle and VCF Operations runs after a
certificate is replaced on a component but before fleet lifecycle retrieves the new certificate. The synchronization workflow
republishes the fleet lifecycle cached certificates for every managed component to VCF Operations. Any component with
a replaced certificate within that interval might have its old certificate replace the new certificate in the VCF Operations
inventory. This prevents VCF Operations from establishing a trusted connection to the component.
Affected tasks fail with a certificate trust error such as
Error occurred while pushing capabilities to VCF
. VCF components might not appear in the lifecycle and certificate management views, or an
Operations for Logs
integration might report a connection failure. The condition persists until the next inventory synchronization publishes
the current certificate and does not affect running workloads or certificates that were already replaced successfully. The
inventory synchronization is scheduled by default to run every 24 hours.
Workaround: Change the synchronization schedule by temporarily setting the property
ops.platform.sync.cron
to in the fleet build service to run hourly. After the synchronization runs successfully, revert the
0 0 * * * *
property to .
ops.platform.sync.cron @daily
vMotion fails if vCenter Server certificate changes before relocate starts and during initiation of vMotion
vMotion fails if the vCenter Server certificate changes before relocate starts and during initiation of vMotion. For example,
storage refresh of vMotion.
The vCenter interface reports a template drift, but selecting the drift view shows no actual drift or discrepancies
This rare issue occurs when duplicate global permission entries exist in the system. Although the vCenter UI typically
prevents duplicate permissions from being created, edge cases can allow a duplicate entry to bypass validation. This
redundant entry triggers false-positive drift alerts while failing to render any visible differences in the comparison view.
Workaround: None
Restoring SDDC Lifecycle task incorrectly reports as failed
The SDDC Lifecycle restore operation in the VCF Operations UI might appear stuck "in progress" and eventually report
a failure, however this is strictly a reporting error. Standalone SDDC Lifecycle and multiple components that include the
SDDC Lifecycle component all restore properly. The underlying back-end process completes successfully, and the target
component boots and functions as expected.
Broadcom 633

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: No corrective action or secondary restore is required. Administrators should manually verify that the target
component is active and functioning, then proceed with standard operations.
Content items cannot be selected in the VCF Operations orchestrator tree view datagrid
Users cannot select one or multiple content items in the VCF Operations orchestrator tree view datagrid. Clicking on rows
fails to highlight them or register a selection, preventing users from performing bulk actions on those items, like moving or
deleting them. Additionally, hovering over item names does not change the cursor to a pointer or show standard hyperlink
styling.
Workaround: To continue managing your content, use the following methods.
• Click the item name directly. While your mouse cursor will not change to a pointer when hovering over the text, clicking
the item will register the action.
• Avoid bulk UI actions.
• For urgent bulk management tasks, like moving multiple workflows to a new category, use the VCF Operations
orchestrator API or CLI.
After upgrading a clustered VCF Operations orchestrator deployment, the salt minion config service might not
start on some of the nodes
After upgrading to a clustered VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.1 deployment, the salt minion config service on port 8061
might not be available on all of the nodes. You can check if the service is active by running the
systemctl status
command on each node.
nginx.service

VCF Operations orchestrator SSO login breaks after vIDB certificate replacement
When a vIDB certificate is replaced with a certificate from a different certificate authority, VCF Operations orchestrator
single sign-on (SSO) breaks and requires re-registration. The VCF Operations orchestrator NDC certificate-replace
endpoint uses a hardcoded URL path that only works with embedded (vCenter-hosted PSC) vIDB deployments. External
(standalone VSP appliance) vIDB deployments return a 404 error which prevents the self-healing certificate rotation from
completing.
Workaround: Reconfigure the authentication for VCF Operations orchestrator. See Configure VCF Operations
Orchestrator for vSphere by Using VCF SSO.
The autocomplete functionality for the script editor in VCF Operations orchestrator does not work
Typing in the script editor in VCF Operations orchestrator does not trigger the completion pop-up which provides a list of
suggestions that match the typed string.
Workaround: No workaround.
Some scripts appear as a hex-encoded string in the workflow script element in VCF Operations orchestrator
In VCF Operations orchestrator, scripts that contain Unicode characters like emojis are encoded upon package export.
When a package with such scripts is imported into a VCF Operations orchestrator instance, the script remains encoded
when viewed in the UI, preventing further edits.
Workaround: Remove characters like emojis from workflow scripts or actions before exporting them in a package.
The workflow selector field in a VCF Operations orchestrator workflow element appears empty
The workflow selector field in a VCF Operations orchestrator workflow element appears empty even when the workflow is
populated.
Workaround: No workaround.
The All Runs button is missing from the workflow editor in VCF Operations orchestrator
In VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.1, users cannot navigate to the historical execution runs of a workflow directly from the
Workflow Editor page because the All Runs button is missing from the action menu.
Workaround: To view your workflow runs, use the following procedure.
1. Copy and save the workflow ID from the URL or editor details of your specific workflow.

3. On the Runs page, enter in the search to isolate the runs for your workflow.
workflowId:<your_workflow_id>
Conditions in the Decision and Switch fields in the VCF Operations orchestrator workflow schema might clear
unexpectedly while the user is typing
In VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.1, when a user adds a Decision or a Switch element to a workflow's schema and
populates the conditions for these elements, the information the user entered might suddenly disappear or reset. While
the user is typing, the page occasionally refreshes in the background which might accidentally clear out any new, unsaved
text.
Workaround: To prevent losing your work, use one of the following methods.
• Save your work immediately after filling out the Decision or Switch field before clicking elsewhere on the page.
• Do not move to other tasks in the VCF Operations orchestrator UI before you are done writing a condition.
• For long or complex conditions, write them in an external application, like Notepad, first. You can then copy and paste
the content in VCF Operations orchestrator and save it immediately.
VCF Operations orchestrator script editor gets stuck when the browser is set to a non-English locale
In VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.1, the script editor fails to load if the user's browser language or locale is set to
anything other than English. The application remains permanently stuck on a loading spinner, preventing users from
viewing or editing scripts.
Workaround: To regain access to the script editor, use one of the following methods.
• Temporarily change the primary browser language or preferred language settings to English.
• If you need to keep your primary browser in a different language for other tasks, create a secondary browser profile or
using an alternative browser specifically configured with an English locale to manage your scripts.
• After updating the language settings, you might need to clear your cache or fully refresh the application page.
After upgrading a clustered VCF Operations orchestrator deployment, the salt-minion-config TLS endpoint is
unavailable
After upgrading a clustered VCF Operations orchestrator deployment to 9.1.1, the TLS endpoint
salt-minion-config
on port 8061 is unavailable on one or more nodes.
Workaround:
1. Run on every node.
systemctl is-active nginx.service
2. If any reports failed, run the following command on that node.
systemctl reset-failed nginx.service
systemctl start nginx.service
3. Verify that the service is active by running .
systemctl is-active nginx.service
If your environment has a VCF Operations HCX manager, the password policy page does not display the VCF
management components row, and applying a password policy fails with a null pointer error
An incorrectly configured VCF Operations HCX adapter prevents VCF Operations from retrieving
the VCF Management components list, so the VCF management components row is missing
from the password policy page. Applying a password policy fails with a null pointer exception in
. The adapter collection status shows
VcfPasswordPolicyManager.getVCFManagementComponentsFromvRops()
as green, so the misconfiguration is not apparent until you attempt to apply a password policy. The error message does
not indicate the adapter configuration as the cause.
Workaround: The user account that VCF Operations uses for the integration with VCF Operations HCX management
pack must exist in vCenter and be a member of the Migration Appliance Administrators and Migration Users user
groups. Remove the misconfigured HCX integration and reconfigure it in VCF Operations. See Management Pack for
HCX.
OSAM migrations fail if HCX Manager is upgraded to 9.1.1 during an active migration
Upgrading the HCX Manager to version 9.1.1.0 while OS Assisted Migrations (OSAM) are in progress may cause those
migrations to fail during the switchover/fixup phase with authentication errors.
Broadcom 635

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Preventative: Ensure all in-progress OSAM migrations are fully completed before upgrading the HCX Manager to 9.1.1.0.
For new migrations, ensure the entire ecosystem (Manager, Interconnect appliances, and Sentinel agents) is running
9.1.1.0.
Recovery for Windows VMs: If a migration fails with authentication errors, upgrade the Sentinel agent on the source VM to
9.1.1.0 and re-invoke the migration.
Recovery for Linux VMs: If a migration fails, upgrade the OSAM data-plane appliances like SRG/SGW/SDR to 9.1.1.0 to
ensure the correct fixup disk is used, then retry the migrationUpgrading the HCX Manager to version 9.1.1.0 while OS
Assisted Migrations (OSAM) are in progress may cause those migrations to fail during the switchover/fixup phase with
authentication errors.
Resolution: Retry the migration after upgrading the OSAM data-plane appliance and sentinel on the VM.
Post HCX upgrade to 9.1.1.0+, data plane appliances need to be redeployed/updated to send logs to the syslog
server
Post HCX upgrade to 9.1.1.0+, data plane appliances stop sending logs to the syslog server.
Workaround: Redeploy or update the data plane appliances to stream the relevant logs to the syslog server.
Unable to modify the "Force Power Off" setting for an active migration if the migration was initiated without a
defined switchover schedule
Unable to modify the "Force Power Off" setting for an active migration if the migration was initiated without a defined
switchover schedule.
Workaround: Temporarily assign a switchover schedule to the migration to force a value update.
The PowerCLI module for HCX Manager (VMware.VimAutomation.Hcx) included in all versions of VCF.PowerCLI
is not compatible with VMware Operations HCX version 9
The PowerCLI module for HCX Manager (VMware.VimAutomation.Hcx) included in all versions of VCF.PowerCLI is
compatible with HCX version 4.11 and no later.
After upgrading HCX Manager to version 9.1.1.0, pending switchovers or newly initiated Bulk and RAV migrations
may fail due to a certificate validation mismatch
Following an upgrade of HCX Manager to version 9.1.1.0, pending switchovers or newly initiated Bulk and
RAV migrations may fail due to a certificate validation mismatch.app logs will display an error similar to:
Caused by: com.vmware.vchs.hybridity.adapters.https.PeerNotVerifiedException: Host
name '172.16.64.204' does not match the certificate subject provided by the peer
(OID.1.2.840.113549.1.9.2="...", CN=VMware vSphere Replication Server, ...)
Workaround: To prevent or resolve this issue, complete all ongoing Bulk and RAV migrations prior to starting the upgrade
process and immediately upgrade or redeploy the photon-based service mesh after upgrading HCX Manager.
After upgrading the HCX Manager to 9.1.1.0, OSAM migrations may fail during the fix-up operation with an
authentication failure if the service meshes which have SGW/SDR/SRG appliances are not upgraded to version
9.1.1.0
OSAM migration fails during the fix-up operation on the migrated VM with the error "Failed to perform fix-up operation on
migrated VM.
Workaround: Upgrade all service meshes with OSAM Interconnect appliances (not just the HCX Manager) to 9.1.1
before triggering OSAM migrations.
VCF Services Runtime
On stretched clusters, VCF management services platform nodes deployed as Day-N operation are not
automatically added to the AZ1 DRS host-affinity rules
New or scaled-out VCF management services and VCF Automation VMs are not automatically assigned to AZ1 DRS
affinity rules on stretched clusters. Consequently, the nodes might run on hosts outside AZ1, which can affect the
expected placement and availability of VCF management services.
Workaround: Manually move the Day-N-deployed node VMs to the AZ1 DRS affinity rule after deployment.
Broadcom 636

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
After VCF management services node VMs are relocated by vMotion to a new resource pool, Day-N deployment
and scale-out operations fail
VCF management services node VMs are created within a pre-specified resource pool. If the VMs are moved directly
in vCenter, the VCF service runtime configuration becomes out-of-sync, which results in issues for subsequent Day-N
component deployment or scale-out operations.
Workaround: Do not move the VCF management services VMs to a different resource pool or folder. If VMs have already
been moved, contact Broadcom Support to reconcile placement.
