Introduction
VCF Automation 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25714559
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
Argo CD as VCF Service
Until VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, Argo CD was available only as a Supervisor Service. With VCF 9.1.1, Argo CD is
available in the following two forms:
• Argo CD Supervisor Service
Deploy and manage the Argo CD Supervisor Service in vCenter. After you deploy the Supervisor Service, use the
CLI to create an Argo CD instance in a vSphere Namespace. An Argo CD instance manages workloads in vSphere
Namespaces and VKS clusters. This capability is available with VCF 9.1.With VCF 9.1.1, Argo CD Supervisor
Service reduces the manual toil and introduced a policy to automatically discover and attach VKS clusters to the
ArgoCD instances enabling quick start managing workloads in VKS clusters. For more information, see Installing and
Configuring Argo CD. The Argo CD version that is currently release is 1.2.0, check the release notes.
• Argo CD as a VCF Service
VCF 9.1.1 introduces installation of the Argo CD service through the Service Management option in the VCF
Automation Provider Management UI. The VCF Automation organization UI enables organization admin to deploy
Argo CD instances to their vSphere Namespaces and then log in to the deployed Argo CD instance by using thier VCF
Automation credentials to quickly start managing workloads in vSphere Namespaces and VKS clusters. See Installing
and Configuring Argo CD.
Note:
In the VCF Automation organization UI, as an organization admin you can use the GitOps Service to deploy Argo
CD instances. You can manage up to 30 vSphere Namespace across all deployed Argo CD instances in the VCF
Automation. For VCF 9.1.1, Argo CD as VCF Service is release as a tech preview.
Broadcom 637

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VKr Support for Argo CD
Argo CD Service support for new Kubernetes minor versions lags VKS by 2–4 months. Based on current upstream
schedules, a June VKr receives Argo CD support in October, an October VKr receives Argo CD support in January, and a
February VKr receives Argo CD support in April.
Support for VLAN-backed VPC
VCF 9.1.1.0 introduces support for VLAN-backed VPCs that are consumed via VCF Automation. In this model, all traffic
flows directly on physical VLANs without overlay encapsulation. It does not support Private networks as the IP scheme is
limited to the CIDRs backed by physical VLANs.
Getting to 9.1.1
For information about deploying, converging, upgrading or patching your environment to 9.1.1, see Getting to 9.1.1.
Product Support Notes
Deprecation of native management capabilities for public cloud resources
Starting with VCF Automation 9.1.1, native management capabilities for public cloud resources, including Amazon Web
Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), are deprecated and disabled by default in VM Apps
organizations.
This deprecation impacts new VCF Automation 9.1.1 installations and environments that were upgraded from earlier
versions. Administrators with the Service Broker Administrator or Assembler Administrator role can restore full public
cloud management functionality using the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 448993.
• If upgrading from VCF Automation 9.0 or 9.1 to version 9.1.1, the procedure to enable full public cloud management
capabilities can be applied before or after upgrade.
• If upgrading from VMware Aria Automation 8.18.x to VCF Automation 9.1.1, the reenablement procedure can only be
applied after upgrade.
After native management capabilities for public cloud resources are enabled in VCF Automation 9.1.1, customers do not
need to reenable the functionality for future VCF releases.
Review the affected functionality and the recommended steps for managing existing deployments.
• Infrastructure management. Create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) operations for the following resources are
restricted: cloud accounts, cloud zones, projects, profiles (image, flavor, network, storage), networks, security groups.
• Deployments and resources.
– Create, update, and delete operations are blocked for deployments that contain public cloud resources.
– Existing deployments are marked as Stale except for deployments that use Terraform configurations.
Note:
The transition of resources to a Stale status after disabling NPC support and the subsequent synchronization
after reenabling NPC support is not immediate. Allow time for these transitions to complete before verifying
resource state.
– All Day 2 actions on deployments are disabled, except for Lease management.
Note:
If a deployment lease expires when NPC support is disabled, VCF Automation attempts to enforce the lease
expiration. After five automatic retry attempts, the system stops retrying. The deployment remains active with an
expired lease and is not deleted. To resume system management of the lease, manually trigger a Change Lease
action.
• Blueprints.
– New blueprints that contain public cloud resources are flagged as Invalid and cannot be versioned or released to
the catalog.
– Existing blueprints display a warning when a user interacts with or modifies them.
Broadcom 638

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
Blueprints that use custom Terraform providers, which execute code in the user's Kubernetes environment, are
not affected by this deprecation.
• Catalog and content sources. Existing catalog items remain visible, but deployment requests that use public cloud
resources fail.
• Onboarding. Onboarding plans that use public cloud resources are blocked during execution.
Deprecation of BYO Velero Package Installation:
Support for bring-your-own (BYO) Velero package installation has been deprecated and will be ended in the next VCF
release. If you use BYO Velero packages, remove the existing packages and enable VKS to deploy the Velero package
that Broadcom supports. For more information, see the Broadcom knowledge base article 428948.
VCF Automation and VCF Operations orchestrator product versions must match
In version 9.1.1, VCF Automation Provider Management has a requirement that requests to endpoints
/cloudapi
must be made with a token containing a newly added scope. Wherever VCF Operations orchestrator makes
vcfa_api
requests to VCF Automation Provider Management endpoints other than the endpoint, for example, , it
/oidc /cloudapi
must use the scope. As a result, the VCF Automation and VCF Operations orchestrator product versions must
vcfa_api
match up to the subminor digit, for example, both must be version 9.1.0.x or both must be version 9.1.1.x and so on. For
more information about compatible versions, check the Product Interoperability Matrix.
Resolved Issues
Provider Management
Storage classes with datastore clusters display incorrect total capacity in regions
When you create a storage class that includes a datastore cluster, the total capacity of the storage class does not include
the datastore cluster capacity. This problem occurs because the vCenter listener ignores storage pod events. As a result,
the datastore table is not populated with the storage pod, and the storage capacity calculations exclude the storage pods.
Region quota update tasks fail with a generic exception when a stale VCF Automation content library is detected
When you modify a region quota for an organization, if the system encounters a stale or missing VCF Automation content
library, the update task fails with an exception. The error log provides only a generic message that does not identify the
specific content library that caused the failure.
Organization Management
Custom forms with drop-down fields populated with VCF Operations orchestrator actions fail validation
After upgrading from VCF Automation 9.0.2 to VCF Automation 9.1.x, submitting custom forms that contain a drop-down
field with a value list populated by VCF Operations orchestrator actions fails to validate. For VCF Operations orchestrator
actions that return Properties objects in a key:value pair format, the backend validation compares the submitted values
against an expected value list that contains null values. In VCF Automation 9.0, action results used the format
[\{"id":
. In VCF Automation 9.1, however, the format changed to
"<key>", "name": "<value>"}] [\{"key": "<key>",
so the validation fails when a user submits a form with incorrectly formatted data.
"value": "<value>"}]
Saving a VCF cloud account associated with a deleted NSX cloud account fails
When deleting a VCF cloud account that uses a NSX cloud account, which is shared between multiple VCF cloud
accounts, the NSX cloud account gets deleted despite still being used by other VCF accounts. When updating
another VCF cloud account associated with the deleted NSX cloud account, saving the updates fails with the error
com.vmware.admiral.vcf.exception.VcfException: Failed to find associated internal NSX
. This causes data corruption for the NSX account that gets deleted and subsequent loss of data.
account for VCF
VCF Services Runtime
During upgrade of VCF Automation from 9.0 to 9.1, the process might stop responding at the backup stage for up
to 120 minutes and display only a generic timeout error
Broadcom 639

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
This behavior affects administrators performing the upgrade and can cause uncertainty about whether the upgrade is
progressing or has failed. This issue is fixed in this release and upgrade fails fast on a backup failure and displays a clear
error.
Entering a hostname or FQDN in mixed case caused failures in install, upgrade, import, and other operations of
VCF Automation
Issue occurs due to case-sensitive Domain Name System (DNS) and certificate matching. This issue is fixed in this
release and all FQDNs can use mixed case.
When you power on a VCF Automation cluster, some services might fail to resume
After a shutdown or a power-cycle of the cluster, one or more services could fail to start automatically and required
manual recovery. This issue is fixed in this release and services recover automatically after power-on.
VCF Automation can accumulate log buffers, which results in the logger disk to fill up and health-check failures
Fluentd log buffers and retained backup chunks can accumulate on the logging disk until available disk space is
exhausted. When the logging disk reaches capacity, platform health checks fail and block platform operations. This issue
is fixed in this release and logging buffer is improved.
Known Issues
Provider Management
Synchronization of a subscribed content library fails with an HTTP 401 error
In the VCF Automation Provider Management UI, when you subscribe a content library to a password-protected vCenter
content library, the subscription and metadata synchronization succeed. However, newly added content library items,
which trigger a fresh file download, are stuck downloading. An HTTP 401 error is thrown when the item's file content is
downloaded. Synchronizing to an unchanged vCenter library or one without password protections is not affected.
Workaround: None.
Creating a subscribed content library fails with an HTTP 401 error
In the VCF Automation Provider Management UI, when you create a subscribed content library by using a subscription
link to a vCenter content library that is protected by a password, the creation fails wit a 401 error.
Workaround: Remove the password from the vCenter content library.
vCenter is wrongly listed as Licensed while in evaluation mode
If a vCenter instance is still in evaluation mode, the main VCF Automation banner displays correct information about
the licensing evaluation period and prompts you to add a licensed instance vCenter 9.0 or later. However, on the
Connections page in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI, the vCenter instance is wrongly listed as
.
Licensed
Workaround: Use the warning banner in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI to monitor your evaluation period
and ensure that you license your vCenter instances before the evaluation expires.
A field validation error incorrectly appears in the New Volume dialog box
When you publish a VM image and you try to add a new volume, a New Volume dialog box opens and immediately
shows a warning about a missing size, even though you have not entered a value for the size of the new volume. Also, if
you enter an invalid name in the respective field, no validation warning appears, but the Create button is deactivated. The
dialog box operates correctly despite the incorrect warnings.
Workaround: None.
A newly created VM class in the vSphere Supervisor is not visible in the VCF Automation Provider Management
UI
Newly created VM classes for a Supervisor might not be visible when you click a region from the Regions panel in the
VCF Automation Provider Management UI, even if you manually refresh the connection to the vCenter instance. The
issue occurs when the vCenter instance supports organizations for VM apps and the Mixed Tenancy Mode feature flag
Broadcom 640

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
is deactivated in Provider Manager. In such cases, new custom VM classes are not detected and displayed in the VCF
Automation Provider Management UI.
Workaround:
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. Navigate to Feature Flags and enable Mixed Tenancy Mode.
Deleting a region quota fails with an error and the region quota remains visible and in a Ready state
When you upgrade VCF Automation from 9.0.x to 9.1.1 and try to delete a region quota that is created before the
upgrade, the delete request is accepted but the operation fails with an error. Region quotas that are created after the VCF
Automation upgrade are not affected.
This issue occurs because during a VCF Automation upgrade, the storage class configuration data that belongs to
existing region quotas is migrated to a new internal format that is introduced in version 9.1.0.0. During the upgrade, the
data is copied, but the old copy is not deleted. As a result, when you attempt to delete region quotas created before the
VCF Automation upgrade, the system encounters the leftover configuration data and the deletion fails.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 453765.
The vksm service installation fails after a VCF Automation upgrade
After a VCF Automation upgrade, the vksm service installation fails with an installation error. The error occurs when the
service upgrade starts on top of a previous version that never completed installation properly, or on a previous installation
that is stuck in uninstallation while still retaining some of its resource custom resources. The new version creates its own
resources instead of transferring the existing ones, and these resources overlap with those from the previous version. The
overlap triggers an validation error, and the installation fails.
already exists
Workaround: Clean up the old version of the service, then reinstall the new version.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, click Service Management.
3. Click VCF Services.
4. On the card of the previous vksm service, click Uninstall.
5. After uninstallation completes, on the card of the service, click Delete.
6. Install the new version of the vksm service.
Partner services does not display resolving status after uploading the service tar file
argocd
When you upload the service tar file in the Partner services section to install the service, the UI does
argocd argocd
not display the resolving status with a loading indicator. Instead, the status remains in an unresolved state. Only the status
indicator is affected; the underlying installation behavior is unchanged. The service resolves after 3-4 minutes and moves
to the VCF Services tab in the state, ready for further user actions.
Not Installed
Workaround: None.
Region creation fails with the
Following zones of the specified supervisors do not have a network
error
stack configured
In VCF Automation 9.1.1, provider administrators must select a network stack when creating a region. The network stack
is fetched from NSX. When creating a region with a VLAN-backed network stack, the region creation might fail with the
error .
Following zones of the specified supervisors don't have a network stack configured
This is caused by an intermittent issue where network stacks for zones are not populated from NSX.
Workaround:
1. Using the VCF Automation Provider Management UI:
a. In the VCF Automation Provider Management UI, select Administration select Connections.
b. Under vCenter, identify the vCenter instances whose supervisors are included in the region.
c. Click the three dots next to the vCenter instance and click Refresh.
Once the refresh finishes, the network stack details for every zone are obtained from NSX.
d. Attempt to create the region again.
2. Using the VCF Automation Provider Management API
Broadcom 641

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
a. Invoke the refresh VC endpoint.
POST https://<vcfa-endpoint>/api/admin/extension/vimServer/<vc-id>/action/refresh
Payload is empty. After a successful refresh, the network stack details for zone are populated and the region is

Organization Management
Pod details not displayed in the VCF Automation organization portal
In the VCF Automation organization, when you navigate to Manage&Govern > Kubernetes Managment > Clusters, you
click a cluster and navigate to the Nodes tab for the cluster, and you click a pod name to see pod details, a blank page is
displayed instead of a pod details page.

/

When saving a network profile or a cloud zone, the user is presented with a Discard Changes dialog
When creating or updating a network profile or a cloud zone in a VCF Automation organization for VM Apps, filling out the
creation/update form so that it is valid, and then saving the form, the user is presented with a Discard Changes dialog.
Workaround: In the dialog, click Discard and navigate to the main Network Profile or Cloud Zone page. Confirm that the
network profile or the cloud zone is available.
Upgrade
VCF Operations orchestrator logs fill disk space on VCF Automation appliances upgraded from VMware Aria
Automation 8.18.x
In environments upgraded from VMware Aria Automation 8.18.x to VCF Automation 9.x, the log deletion policy is missing
so VCF Operations orchestrator logs accumulate and fill the disk space on the VCF Automation appliance nodes. When
disk usage reaches 100%, VCF Automation stops working. When the user runs the kubectl get pods -A command, they
observe a large number of orphaned pods.
Workaround: Follow the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 458715.
Patching the migration service engine component to version 9.1.1 fails and times out after several hours
This problem occurs when you patch migration service engine to version 9.1.1 before you upgrade VCF Automation to
version 9.1.1. Migration service engine 9.1.1 requires updated database capabilities that are only delivered with VCF
Automation 9.1.1. Patching the migration service engine on an earlier VCF Automation platform causes the component to
hang during deployment and ultimately fail with an "Step vmsp_upgrade failed. Reference Code: 85616483." error.
Workaround: Upgrade VCF Automation to version 9.1.1 before you patch the migration service engine component. See
Broadcom knowledge base article 455559.
VCF Automation and migration service engine patches fail with a
com.vmware.vcfms.system.precheck.backup.PackageDeploymentsCompleteWaitTimeout error
If you tried to patch the migration service engine to 9.1.1 before the VCF Automation is patched to 9.1.1, the patching of
both components becomes blocked.
Workaround: To unblock the patch of VCF Automation to 9.1.1, follow the instructions in Broadcom knowledge base
article 455559.
Custom Day-2 actions intermittently disappear and are unavailable from the deployment actions menu in VCF
Automation for VM Apps
In VM Apps organizations in VCF Automation 9.1.1, custom day 2 resource actions, like a custom Deployment Delete
action bound to deployment resources, might intermittently fail to render or populate in the Actions drop-down menu. This
Broadcom 642

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
issue occurs when day 2 policy entitlement evaluations or custom resource action bindings temporarily fail to refresh or
synchronize for active deployments. The issue impacts environments that were upgraded from VMware Aria Automation
8.18.1 to VCF Automation 9.1.1.
Workaround: Follow the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 454245.
Upgrading VCF Automation 9.0.1, 9.0.2.X, or 9.1.0.X to VCF Automation 9.1.1 fails
During upgrade, any custom profiles applied on VCF Automation 9.0.1, 9.0.2.X, or 9.1.0.X cause the upgrade to VCF
Automation 9.1.1 to fail. Custom profiles are drop-in configuration overlays applied to VCF Automation services. During
an upgrade to a version earlier than 9.1.1, the profile artifacts from the source release are not compatible and cause the
upgrade to fail.
Workaround: Follow the steps in Broadcom knowledge base article 451147.
Upgrading VMware Aria Automation 8.18.x to VCF Automation 9.1.1 fails with an internal error
When upgrading VMware Aria Automation 8.18.x to VCF Automation 9.1.1, the system uses name resolution to convert
user-friendly names to IP addresses. Whenever the connection to your DNS server experiences connectivity issues or
resolution does not work as expected, VCF Automation might produce the wrong output when resolving names. Using the
incorrect output further in the upgrade can cause the upgrade to fail with the following error:
ERROR (CC26CB94) com.vmware.vcfms.virtualmachine.VirtualMachineNotFound [VCFMS-VM-002]:
Internal error occurred. Failed to locate virtual machine
;; communications error to <DNS IP address>#53: timed out.
<VM IP address>
Please retry the operation or contact support if the issue persists. ( )
Workaround:
1. Restart the VMware Aria Automation 8.18.x services. See Starting and stopping VMware Aria Automation.
2. Ensure that DNS resolution in the reported DNS works and is stable.
3. Run the upgrade again.
Note:
If the upgrade still fails, use the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 441333 and then run
the upgrade again.
VCF Services Runtime
tenantmanager database disk usage grows significantly due to un-reclaimed space in activity tables
In VCF Automation 9.x, the database size can increase significantly, in some cases exceeding 200
tenantmanager
GB. This growth is primarily driven by tables matching the pattern, which continue to consume allocated disk
activity%
space even after underlying activity records are deleted.
Workaround: Follow the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 436300.
Excessive growth of the audit_trail table in the tenantmanager database causes disk space exhaustion and UI
unavailability
In VCF Automation 9.0.x and 9.1.x versions prior to 9.1.1.0, high-volume audit logging of events
definedEntity
( and ) causes rapid growth of the table in the
accessFullContents modify audit_trail tenantmanager
database. Each event captures the complete entity payload (~36.8 KiB per row), which can
accessFullContents
consume over 95% of total table space during upgrades or high-activity periods. This causes the database partition to
exceed 90% disk usage and switches PostgreSQL into read-only mode, rendering the VCF Automation user interface
down and unavailable. The default 90-day retention cleanup job ( ) does not purge
ActivityLogCleanerJobActivity
records quickly enough to prevent disk fill.
Workaround: Follow the procedure described in Broadcom knowledge base article 453343.
On stretched clusters, VCF Automation platform nodes deployed as Day-N operation are not automatically added
to the AZ1 DRS host-affinity rules
New or scaled-out VCF Automation VMs are not automatically assigned to AZ1 DRS affinity rules on stretched clusters.
Consequently, the nodes might run on hosts outside AZ1, which can affect the expected placement and availability of VCF
Automation.
Broadcom 643

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: Manually move the Day-N-deployed node VMs to the AZ1 DRS affinity rule after deployment.
After VCF Automation node VMs are relocated by vMotion to a new resource pool, Day-N deployment and scale-
out operations fail
VCF Automation node VMs are created within a pre-specified resource pool. If the VMs are moved directly in vCenter,
the VCF Automation configuration becomes out-of-sync, which results in issues for subsequent Day-N component
deployment or scale-out operations.
Workaround: Do not move the VCF Automation VMs to a different resource pool or folder. If VMs have already been
moved, contact Broadcom Support to reconcile placement.

Introduction
VMware Cloud Foundation SDKs 9.1.1.0 | 03 SEP 2026 | Build 25714914
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
What's New
VCF SDK 9.1.1 is a security-focused maintenance release. This release does not introduce any new VCF components,
and no VCF component samples are added or removed.
Security Enhancements
VCF SDK 9.1.1 addresses potential vulnerabilities and strengthens the security of VCF SDKs. Several dependent libraries
are upgraded to make VCF SDK more secure and reduce exposure to known security risks.
What's New in This Release
• No new VCF components are added in VCF 9.1.1.
• No new VCF component samples are added or removed in VCF 9.1.1.
Product Support Notes
VMware Cloud Foundation Java SDK
Java Version Requirements
Java 17 is the minimum requirement for the VCF Java SDK in the 9.1.1.0 release. The SDK is compatible with the
following Java LTS versions: 17, 21, and 25. It is strongly recommended to use one of those versions when integrating the
SDK into custom applications and when running the samples.
Apache CXF Upgrade
The VCF Java SDK modules for the SOAP APIs of vSphere and vSAN — namely vim25, pbm, sms, ssoclient, vslm,
and eam — now use Apache CXF 4.1.7 to provide patches for CVEs and strong security postures for the SDK and the
Broadcom 644

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
applications consuming it. This version of Apache CXF requires Java 17 and is compatible with modern, well-supported
APIs and implementations such as Jakarta EE 10, Spring 6, and Spring Boot 3.
VMware Cloud Foundation Python SDK
Python Version Compatibility
All modules of the VCF Python SDK are compatible with and verified against the supported versions of Python at the time
of their release. Once a Python version reaches End-Of-Life (EOL), it no longer receives security patches. VCF Python
SDK releases that occur after this moment do not provide compatibility guarantees for the EOL-ed Python version. As a
general best practice and for the strongest security posture, use the VCF Python SDK with an actively maintained version
of Python and keep your environment on the latest patch provided by the Python Software Foundation (PSF).
For the VCF 9.1.1.0 release, the supported Python versions are 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.

Resolved collisions where multiple packages defined classes with the same short name (for example, ).

that relied on its lineage.

Introduction
VMware Cloud Foundation PowerCLI 9.1.1.0 | 14 SEP 2026 | Build 25718932
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
VMware Cloud Foundation PowerCLI 9.1.1.0 focuses on delivering a more secure and resilient automation platform
designed to address evolving threat landscapes, including emerging vulnerability risks linked to Mythos frameworks and
modern AI agent environments. This release prioritizes hardened certificate validation, upgraded core dependencies, and
clearer diagnostics for mission-critical automation pipelines.
What's New
Image Builder and lifecycle security
Python 3.14 Support: The Image Builder module now officially supports Python 3.14, enabling customers with strict
compliance rules to continue patching and updating safely.
Important:
In alignment with Python lifecycle policies, support for Python 3.7, 3.8, and 3.9 has been removed. Users must
run Python 3.10 or higher to maintain product support and compatibility.

Patch Releases 9.1.0.x
Patch releases provide time-sensitive fixes to security and catastrophic issues, impacting business operations, that need
to be released between major, minor, and maintenance releases. You can pick and choose which components to apply
based on the impact on your environment and operational costs. Patch releases are not synchronized among all VCF
components and do not require a new implementation of a Bill Of Materials.
Patch release notes cover only newly identified known issues for each release. All known issues documented in earlier
releases remain valid until a subsequent release resolves them. VCF releases are cumulative, so each release includes
all fixes from earlier releases.
For more information, see Lifecycle Management in VMware Cloud Foundation.
To see an АI-generated list of all available patch releases, grouped by release date, click here.

Applying the Patch
Log in to the Broadcom Support Portal to download this patch, depending on your entitlement, VMware vSphere
Foundation or VMware Cloud Foundation.
For download instructions, see Download Broadcom products and software.
See these KBs for details on the authenticated online and offline download: 390121, 390098, and 389276.
For VCF environments, you apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF
Component.
For VMware vSphere Foundation environments, for details on updates and upgrades by using vSphere Lifecycle
Manager, see What is vSphere Lifecycle Manager and vSphere Lifecycle Manager Images and Baselines. You can also
update ESX hosts without the use of vSphere Lifecycle Manager by using an image profile. To do this, you must manually
download the patch offline bundle ZIP file or see the Broadcom knowledge base article How to download ESXi ISO image
for all releases including patch updates.
For more information, see Using ESXCLI for Host Management and the VMware ESX Upgrade guide.
Known Issues
Live patch pre-check fails on vSAN compute clusters causing ESX upgrades to fail
When initiating a live patch ESX upgrade on a vSAN compute cluster, the pre-remediation health check shown in the
vSphere Client fails with the following error:
.
The health check failed to complete
This precheck failure blocks the upgrade process for the ESX hosts in the vSAN compute cluster.
This issue only affects vSAN compute clusters that do not have any local vSAN storage like in vSAN HCI or vSAN
Storage cluster.
Workaround: Disabling the live patch vSAN health checks on vSAN compute clusters allows the process to continue. See
Broadcom knowledge base article 442180.

Known Issues
A reset of the vSphere Lifecycle Manager database might cause data loss in the Supervisor
If the vSphere Lifecycle Manager database in your environment is reset before upgrading vCenter from versions 8.0
Update 3 and later or 9.0.x to 9.1.0 or 9.1.1, the upgrade might cause data loss in the Supervisor. To avoid data loss,
before a vCenter upgrade, you must first check your environment and take mitigation steps, if necessary.
Workaround: See Broadcom knowledge base article 455737 for instructions how to check if your environment is affected
and for mitigation steps.
vCenter backup taken in Ehanced Linked Mode (ELM) cannot be restored after breaking ELM
When a vCenter is in ELM, its Single Sign-On (SSO) domain maintains replication agreements with all partner vCenters.
Backups taken in ELM environments capture such replication agreements. After breaking ELM, linked vCenter instances
are removed from the topology, but the restored backup tries to re-establish SSO sync with them. As a result, the backup
fails to restore with a message such as .
Error Failed to synchronize SSO data with partners
Workaround: After breaking ELM, take new backups to use for vCenter restore.
During vCenter Reduced Downtime Upgrade (RDU), you see a warning that does not correctly display the version
of VCF Operations and the target vCenter version
During RDU from VCF version 9.0.x to 9.1, in the vSphere Client, you might see a precheck warning such as
, in which
Registered VCF Ops's version '%(0)s' is lower than the target vCenter's '%(1)s
versions are not correctly displayed.
Workaround: Ensure that VCF Operations is upgraded before vCenter to a version matching the new desired vCenter
version, for example 9.1. You can ignore the error message.

What's New
This patch includes no changes other than the alignment of build details and does not introduce any resolved or known
issues.
Applying the Patch
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
Related Resolved Issues
VCF Services Runtime 9.1.0.0200 resolves the following issues related to Identity Broker:
• Upgrade of VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation might fail with error VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006
During an upgrade of VCF identity broker or VCF Automation, the process might fail with a generic backup timeout
error VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006. The error does not identify the actual cause: the configured SFTP backup
destination server has insufficient free disk space to accommodate the pre-upgrade backup.
A pre-upgrade validation check now verifies that the SFTP backup server has sufficient free disk space before the
upgrade begins, and returns a descriptive error message if the condition is not met.
• VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails if the 9.0 appliance VMs are not in
the original vCenter folder
When upgrading VCF identity broker or VCF Automation from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, the upgrade might fail if the VMs for the
9.0 appliances are moved out of their original vCenter inventory folder.
VM operations during upgrade now look up VMs by their unique ID rather than by folder path, so the upgrade
succeeds regardless of where appliance VMs are located on the vCenter instance.
• Scheduled backups silently fail after VCF Automation or VCF Identity Broker upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 on
clusters older than 60 days
Following an upgrade of VCF Automation or VCF identity broker from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, scheduled backups complete
without error messages but produce no valid backup data. An SSL certificate hostname mismatch causes the failure:
the upgrade process incorrectly restores stale internal certificate request objects from the pre-upgrade cluster,
preventing the new cluster from generating a valid certificate for internal communication. Backups that depend on this
internal certificate path fail silently. This condition affects only clusters that were in operation for more than 60 days
before the upgrade.
Broadcom 673

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Stale internal certificate request objects from the previous cluster version are no longer restored during upgrade,
allowing the upgraded cluster to generate valid internal certificates and complete scheduled backups successfully.

Resolved Issues
VCF Operations upgrade from 9.0, 9.0.1, and 9.0.2 to 9.1 fails during the post-upgrade script execution phase
This issue occurs while upgrading an environment where a previously imported license has since been deleted. The
deleted license leaves behind a stale record in the database which later violates a new foreign key constraint introduced
during the upgrade process. This constraint violation causes the Postgres database update to fail.
The license server does not work properly and after the appliance boots, in the console you see a black screen
Broadcom 674

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The license server uses the and IP address ranges for internal communications.
172.16.0.0/12 172.17.0.0/16
If you deploy the license server on the network or configure the license server to use a gateway that
172.16.0.0/12
advertises a routable path of , a network conflict occurs. As a result, you see only a black screen in the
172.17.0.0/16
license server console after booting.
Microsoft CA certificates are displayed as external CA signed certificates instead of Microsoft CA signed
certificates
This issue can occur when the root certificate in the Microsoft CA configuration is updated.
After you upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, Microsoft CA certificates appear as EXTERNAL_CA signed certificates
This happens because in VCF 9.0, VCF Fleet Lifecycle Manager appliances stored locker-related information in their
local database. In VCF 9.1, VCF Fleet Lifecycle Manager is deprecated, and all locker contents are migrated to the VCF
Operations locker database.
Certificate replacement with Microsoft CA fails
This issue occurs when the Microsoft CA configuration includes intermediate certificates. In such cases, any certificate
replacement operation triggered with the Microsoft CA fails.

Resolved Issues
The certificate rotation and update API enforces strict Subject Alternative Name (SAN) validation on custom SSL/
TLS certificates after upgrading to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9.1.0.0200.
Starting with VCF 9.1.0.0200, the API actively checks that the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field is present and
correctly populated with the IP addresses of all platform cluster nodes. Certificates missing a SAN, or containing
incomplete cluster IPs, are rejected by the API with an error.
Environments upgraded to VCF 9.1.0.0200 with an active custom certificate that lacks a valid SAN will not experience
disruption to existing session traffic. However, SAN compliance is required for all future certificate updates. Administrators
must audit existing custom certificates and reissue them with the complete list of platform node IPs to maintain
compliance.
Infrastructure nodes experience disk space exhaustion or trigger storage capacity alerts due to retained legacy
Python binaries.
Following system updates, legacy Python versions (such as 3.5, 3.6, and 3.8) remain in the /usr/local/lib directory. These
obsolete binaries consume excessive disk space and are not automatically removed by standard package managers.
Broadcom 675

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Administrators encounter storage capacity warnings when the partition hosting the library directory reaches maximum
utilization.
Antrea flows for VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service 1.35.0 and later clusters are now visible in VMware Cloud
Foundation Operations for networks.
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for networks now successfully discovers VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service
1.35.0 and later clusters. Previously, a discovery failure prevented these clusters and their associated Antrea flows from
appearing in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for networks, as well as in the Operate > Flows section of VMware
Cloud Foundation Operations.

What's New

Applying the Patch

Broadcom 676

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Resolved Issues
VCF Services Runtime 9.1.0.0200 resolves the following issues:
• VCF Services Runtime upgrade fails due to vCenter permission error
During an upgrade of VCF services runtime, the service might fail to apply the updated vCenter roles and permissions
required for VCF 9.1. As a result, the upgrade process either ends with an error or completes in a degraded state,
leaving the cluster with insufficient privileges to perform post-upgrade operations.
VCF services runtime now accepts administrator credentials from the Fleet Lifecycle Manager during upgrade and
applies the required vCenter roles and permissions before the upgrade proceeds.
• VCF upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1 fails due to a DNS check
When upgrading from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, the pre-upgrade health check validates DNS resolution for the VCF Operations
hostname. If that host is no longer in the DNS configuration, the health check reports an error and blocks the upgrade.
The health check now skips the VCF Operations hostname DNS check during upgrade, preventing such errors.
• VCF Automation services fail to recover after cluster restart
A full restart of the VCF Automation cluster might cause one or more VCF Automation services to remain in a non-
running state, requiring manual intervention to restore functionality.
A housekeeping task that was blocking successful restarts is now configured to stop any previously running instances
before starting a new one, and has a maximum allowed runtime so a stuck instance cannot block the system
indefinitely.
• Upgrade of VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation might fail with error VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006
During an upgrade of VCF identity broker or VCF Automation, the process might fail with a generic backup timeout
error . The error does not identify the actual cause: the configured SFTP backup
VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006
destination server has insufficient free disk space to accommodate the pre-upgrade backup.
A pre-upgrade validation check now verifies that the SFTP backup server has sufficient free disk space before the
upgrade begins, and returns a descriptive error message if the condition is not met.
• VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails if the 9.0 appliance VMs are not in
the original vCenter folder
When upgrading VCF identity broker or VCF Automation from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, the upgrade might fail if the VMs for the
9.0 appliances are moved out of their original vCenter inventory folder.
VM operations during upgrade now look up VMs by their unique ID rather than by folder path, so the upgrade
succeeds regardless of where appliance VMs are located on the vCenter instance.
• You see reports for failed VCF Management Services installation even though the cluster is healthy
After completing a VCF management services installation, due to invalid vCenter authentication performed by internal
services, the final status incorrectly reports a failure even though the cluster is fully operational and all services are
running.
Health checks now authenticate correctly against vCenter and succeed on a healthy cluster, fixing the invalid vCenter
authentication by internal services.
• Scheduled backups silently fail after VCF Automation or VCF Identity Broker upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 on
clusters older than 60 days
Following an upgrade of VCF Automation or VCF identity broker from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, scheduled backups complete
without error messages but produce no valid backup data. An SSL certificate hostname mismatch causes the failure:
the upgrade process incorrectly restores stale internal certificate request objects from the pre-upgrade cluster,
preventing the new cluster from generating a valid certificate for internal communication. Backups that depend on this
internal certificate path fail silently. This condition affects only clusters that were in operation for more than 60 days
before the upgrade.
Stale internal certificate request objects from the previous cluster version are no longer restored during upgrade,
allowing the upgraded cluster to generate valid internal certificates and complete scheduled backups successfully.
• VCF Management Services install fails with "unexpected EOF" error when vSphere password contains special
characters
When the vSphere administrator password includes special characters — such as single quotes (') or double quotes
(") — the VCF management services installation might fail. The error message reports an unexpected EOF condition,
which does not identify the special character encoding as the root cause.
Password values are now written using shell-safe encoding.
• VCF Management Services installation might fail due to duplicate vCenter port group names
Broadcom 677

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When two or more vCenter port groups share the same display name across different distributed switches, the VCF
management services provisioning process might fail with an error that the path resolves to multiple networks.
Network lookup now uses the unique network ID directly instead of resolving port groups by name.
• Storage DRS live migration of VCF Services Runtime VMs causes storage failures
When you enable Storage DRS (SDRS) on the datastore cluster that hosts VCF services runtime nodes, vCenter
might automatically migrate VCF services runtime virtual machines to different datastores as part of the storage load
balancing and cause storage failures on the affected nodes.
VCF services runtime now automatically excludes its VMs from Storage DRS, preventing vSphere from migrating
them. Manually migrating VCF services runtime virtual machines is not recommended.
• Overlapping IP pool and Kubernetes internal network ranges cause silent networking failures in VCF Services
Runtime deployment
Deploying a VCF services runtime cluster with an IP pool that overlaps with Kubernetes internal network ranges might
cause silent networking failures and connection issues after deployment.
VCF services runtime now validates IP ranges during deployment and rejects requests with an error message if the
provided IP pool conflicts with internal network ranges. For more information, see
Deploy VCF Management Services and License Server as Part of VCF Upgrade to 9.1.
• Mixed-case hostname or FQDN names cause failures across VCF install, upgrade, and import workflows
When you provide a hostname or fully qualified domain name (FQDN) using mixed-case characters — for example,
MyHost.Example.com — install, upgrade, import, and other operations across the VCF environment might fail,
because DNS resolution and SSL certificate matching are case-sensitive.
FQDNs are now automatically normalized to lowercase at all entry points, preventing case-sensitivity issues across all
workflows.
Known Issues
• You cannot power down or shut down a VCF Services Runtime cluster by using the UI
VCF services runtime does not provide a UI control for powering down or shutting down a cluster. The cluster
shutdown operation is only available through CLI or API.
Workaround: For more information, see Starting Up VMware Cloud Foundation and Shutting Down VMware Cloud
Foundation.
• VCF Management Services or VCF Automation services fail to resume after power-on
When you power on a previously shut-down VCF management services or VCF Automation cluster, some services
might fail to resume. Affected components remain unavailable after power-on and require manual intervention to
restore full service operation.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 440862.
• You cannot change the FQDN for VCF Management Services or VCF Automation after deployment
You cannot change the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for VCF management services or VCF Automation
components after initial deployment. To change the FQDN, you must remove the existing deployment entirely and
redeploy.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 441333.
• You cannot retry a failed VCF Automation upgrade
When a VCF Automation upgrade workflow fails, you cannot retry the operation. Instead, you must delete the
component and restart the upgrade.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 441333.
• VCF Automation upgrade precheck from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails when source and target datastores do not match
The VCF Automation upgrade precheck from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails when the target datastore does not match the source
datastore configuration. The upgrade process stops until you align the datastore configuration between the source and
target environments.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 440045.
• VCF Identity Broker upgrade precheck from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails when target network or datastore configuration
does not match
The VCF identity broker upgrade precheck from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails when the target network or datastore configuration
does not match the source. The upgrade stops until you align both the network and datastore configuration between
the source and target.
Broadcom 678

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 444734.
• If the management domain vCenter certificate rotates twice within 30 minutes, VCF Management Services
loses connection to vCenter
If the management domain vCenter certificate rotates twice within a 30-minute window, VCF management services
might lose connectivity to the vCenter instance. As a result, VM rollout, scaling, and disk resize operations fail and VMs
remain unavailable until you manually restore vCenter connectivity.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 424402.
• After a component disk or volume is resized, the UI might show an incorrect size of 0
After a component disk or volume is resized, the UI might display an incorrect size of 0 instead of the actual disk size.
This error blocks any subsequent resize operations through the UI.
Workaround: For more information, see Broadcom knowledge base article 442600.

What's New
This release contains various security enhancements and delivers fixes as described in the Resolved Issues section.
Applying the Patch

Resolved Issues
Upgrade
VCF Operations upgrade from 9.0, 9.0.1, and 9.0.2 to 9.1 fails during the post-upgrade script execution phase
Broadcom 682

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
This issue occurs while upgrading an environment where a previously imported license has since been deleted. The
deleted license leaves behind a stale record in the database which later violates a new foreign key constraint introduced
during the upgrade process. This constraint violation causes the Postgres database update to fail.
Fleet Management
Replacing vCenter certificates fails when the new certificate includes intermediate certificates in its chain
Replacing vCenter certificates with a new certificate that contains intermediate certificates in its chain fails with the
message: "Certificate replacement operation completed successfully on VCENTER component with FQDN XXXX.
However, automated post-update trust failed with errors." After a certificate replacement operation completes successfully
on a vCenter component, the automated post-update retrust step targeting VCF Automation fails in VCF Operations 9.1
and displays errors.
Certificate Replacement with a Configured CA (Microsoft) operation fails when Microsoft CA is configured as an
Intermediate CA
When Microsoft CA is configured as an intermediate CA, the Certificate Replacement with a Configured CA operation
fails because VCF Certificate Management does not build the full certificate chain which includes intermediate and root
certificates.
After upgrading a multi VCF Instance from 9.0 to 9.1, the 'Choose Deployment Type' step on the SSO
Configuration Overview page remains in an 'In Progress' state, while all other steps displayed as completed
During VCF Operations upgrade from 9.0 to 9.1, the configuration sync converts pre-existing 9.0 single sign-on data into
9.1 single sign-on domain-specific data. During this process, when no identity provider is found, the is
vcfInstanceId
incorrectly retrieved from the component's authsource configuration instead of from the identity broker. Since this does
not always guarantee that the discovered component belongs to the correct VCF Instance, the single sign-on domain was
created with an incorrect VCF Instance ID.
Licensing
VCF Operations 9.1.0.0400 resolves the following issues related to Licensing:
• You do not see informative messages for license assignment failures in VCF Operations
When a license assignment to a vCenter instance fails due to a connectivity failure from VCF Operations to the
vCenter instance or from the vCenter instance to the license server, the message in the task results pane does not
provide sufficient information.
The fix adds informative messages that include the specific reason for failure. You can use the reason details to
diagnose issues such as invalid API keys, DNS failures, or NTP synchronization problems.
• You see only generic alerts when VCF Operations cannot reach a vCenter instance
In VCF Operations, you see generic alerts when VCF Operations cannot reach a vCenter instance, without details
about the failure type.
The fix adds specific alerts and remediation guidance. VCF Operations now displays dedicated alerts with remediation
guidance depending on the failure type, and you can identify whether the root cause is a DNS issue, a network
timeout, a refused connection on port 443, or insufficient permissions.
• No support for Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) requests for license servers
License servers prior to VCF Operations 9.1.0.0400 do not respond to ICMP requests.
Starting with VCF Operations 9.1.0.0400, network administrators can use standard ping diagnostics to verify
license server reachability, which simplifies network monitoring and connectivity troubleshooting for license server
deployments.
• You do not see a warning when the vCenter version is later than the VCF Operations version
You must upgrade VCF Operations before vCenter in any upgrade sequence. When the upgrade order is reversed
and one or more vCenter instances are of version later than the current VCF Operations version, the affected vCenter
instances are not flagged.
The fix adds comparison based on major and minor version numbers. Patch-level differences do not trigger the
warning.
• License assignment fails if the vCenter UUID contains uppercase letters
Broadcom 683

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When the vCenter UUID contains uppercase characters, license assignment fails. The authorization request that VCF
Operations sends to the license server embeds the vCenter UUID directly, and the license server rejects requests
where the UUID casing does not match the expected lowercase format.
VCF Operations now changes the vCenter UUID to lowercase before it builds the authorization request, and license
assignment succeeds regardless of the casing that the source vCenter system uses.
• License server attempts to connect to external Network Time Protocol (NTP) servers for time synchronization
The license server incorrectly attempts to connect to an external NTP server to update its internal clock.
Starting with VCF Operations 9.1.0.0400, time synchronization for the license server is restricted exclusively to the
host system on which the license server virtual machine runs.

Batch precheck of upgrade plan for all VCF management components fails with the validation error
VCF_LCM_FLEET_UPGRADE_400_COMPONENT_NOT_NEEDED_USER_INPUT_SPEC_PROVIDED
This issue occurs when a component's user input specification remains configured after the component has already been
upgraded to its target version. If you then click Run Prechecks (ALL), or use Select All on the VCF Management >
Upgrade page without selecting individual components, the precheck runs against the full upgrade plan. Because the plan
includes a user input spec for a component that no longer requires one, the validation fails and returns the error above.

precheck individually, and then run the prechecks.

Applying the Patch
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
Known Issues
Concurrent software depot component patching causes other component patch operations to fail
Patching software depot takes it temporarily offline. If another component patch from fleet lifecycle runs concurrently,
that patch operation cannot access the required binaries and fails. This issue affects environments where administrators
initiate multiple component patches in parallel.
Workaround: Do not initiate other component patches while the software depot component is being patched. If
concurrent patching already caused failures, wait for the software depot patching process to complete successfully. After
software depot is patched, retry the failed component patches.

Broadcom 688

What's New
This release contains various security enhancements and delivers fixes as described in the Resolved Issues section.
Applying the Patch
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
Resolved Issues
• Creating a Canonical content library fails with an OVF validation error
This issue is caused by the addition of an SBOM in Ubuntu OS images. The following files are present in both the OVA
and the manifest ( ) file but are not actually downloaded because they are not referenced by the OVF:
.mf
–
ubuntu-resolute-26.04-cloudimg.manifest
–
ubuntu-resolute-26.04-cloudimg.sbom.spdx
–
ubuntu-resolute-26.04-cloudimg.filelist
• Users who are added to projects as part of a user group cannot access project resources
This issue occurs in VM Apps and All Apps organizations and includes catalog items, deployments, and, in All Apps
organizations, errors with supervisor resources. The issue is caused by the incorrect use of a filter in the Project
Service when associating users with groups and assigning group project principals' access to namespaces. Instead of
fetching the desired group from VCF Automation Provider Management, the Project Service fetches a page of groups.
When there are more groups than the page size, which is 25, the groups that are left out cannot be handled.
• VCF Operations orchestrator is missing auto token refresh mechanism in HTTP interceptor
If a VCF Automation user stays on the Orchestratortab for longer than the access token lifetime, which is one hour by
default, the user might get a forced logout due to the access token expiring and not being refreshed.
• VCF Automation services fail to recover after cluster restart
A full restart of the VCF Automation cluster might cause one or more VCF Automation services to remain in a non-
running state, requiring manual intervention to restore functionality.
A housekeeping task that was blocking successful restarts is now configured to stop any previously running instances
before starting a new one, and has a maximum allowed runtime so a stuck instance cannot block the system
indefinitely.
• Upgrade of VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation might fail with error VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006
During an upgrade of VCF identity broker or VCF Automation, the process might fail with a generic backup timeout
error . The error does not identify the actual cause: the configured SFTP backup
VCFMS-BACKUP-COMPONENT-006
destination server has insufficient free disk space to accommodate the pre-upgrade backup.
A pre-upgrade validation check now verifies that the SFTP backup server has sufficient free disk space before the
upgrade begins, and returns a descriptive error message if the condition is not met.
• VCF Identity Broker and VCF Automation upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 fails if the 9.0 appliance VMs are not in
the original vCenter folder
When upgrading VCF identity broker or VCF Automation from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, the upgrade might fail if the VMs for the
9.0 appliances are moved out of their original vCenter inventory folder.
VM operations during upgrade now look up VMs by their unique ID rather than by folder path, so the upgrade
succeeds regardless of where appliance VMs are located on the vCenter instance.
• Scheduled backups silently fail after VCF Automation or VCF Identity Broker upgrade from VCF 9.0 to 9.1 on
clusters older than 60 days
Following an upgrade of VCF Automation or VCF identity broker from VCF 9.0 to 9.1, scheduled backups complete
without error messages but produce no valid backup data. An SSL certificate hostname mismatch causes the failure:
the upgrade process incorrectly restores stale internal certificate request objects from the pre-upgrade cluster,
preventing the new cluster from generating a valid certificate for internal communication. Backups that depend on this
internal certificate path fail silently. This condition affects only clusters that were in operation for more than 60 days
before the upgrade.
Stale internal certificate request objects from the previous cluster version are no longer restored during upgrade,
allowing the upgraded cluster to generate valid internal certificates and complete scheduled backups successfully.

Introduction
VCF Installer / SDDC Manager 9.1.1.0200 | 12 OCT 2026 | Build 25801071

Broadcom 695

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
What's New
This release delivers fixes as described in the Resolved Issues section.
IMPORTANT: For upgrading your environment from VCF 5.2.1 to 9.1.1.0200, you must first upgrade from 5.2.1 to 5.2.2 or
5.2.3 and then to 9.1.1.0200.
Applying the Patch
Use the latest available binaries for components when you deploy, upgrade, or patch.
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
Resolved Issues
When configuring DNS or NTP servers with link-local IP addresses during VCF deployment, the VCF Installer
validation rejects the addresses and blocks the deployment from proceeding.
The VCF Installer validation rejects link-local IP addresses, such as those in the range, across all IP
169.254.0.0/16
input fields. This validation is necessary for fields where link-local addresses should not be permitted, such as NSX tunnel
endpoint IPs, vMotion, and management network specifications. However, the same validation also applies to DNS and
NTP server fields, where link-local addresses are valid and sometimes required. In cloud environments, DNS and NTP
services are reachable only through link-local addresses, and the blanket rejection prevents provisioning using native
hyperscaler infrastructure services.
SDDC Manager fails to connect to the online depot through a proxy server with configured SSL/TLS interception
When SDDC Manager validates the online depot FQDN during depot configuration, it does not route the request through
the configured proxy with SSL/TLS interception. In network environments where the depot FQDN is resolvable only
through the proxy, the validation fails because the direct DNS lookup cannot resolve the address. Additionally, the
certificate retrieval step that follows bypasses the proxy entirely, fetching the depot certificate directly instead of through
the proxy connection. The issue occurs even when all required online depot URLs are allowed on the proxy and the
proxy's root CA certificate is imported in the SDDC Manager trust store. This issue prevents SDDC Manager from
retrieving depot certificates, which blocks online depot operations such as patch downloads and bundle retrieval.
When deploying a new VCF or vSphere Foundation instance by using VCF Installer, on the General Information
page, the version drop-down menu is empty and does not pre-load the target version, requiring manual selection
of the version before proceeding
The VCF Installer UI performs an exact version match against the versions returned by the releases API. A mismatch
between the version string sent by the UI and the version string returned by the API prevents the drop-down menu from
automatically populating with the default version.
After SDDC Manager completes an upgrade of the VCF Operations HCX component, the upgrade overview in the
SDDC Manager UI continues to show zero steps completed for 15 minutes or longer, and the component remains
listed as ready to upgrade, even though the upgrade task has succeeded
The VCF Operations HCX upgrade does not update the target version in the SDDC Manager lifecycle management
cache after the upgrade completes. As a result, SDDC Manager relies on the scheduled LCM cache refresh to detect the
completed upgrade, which can delay the status update.
If SDDC Manager cluster creation fails before vCenter creates the cluster object, you cannot remove the cluster
If the cluster creation operation fails before vCenter creates the cluster object, the cluster does not exist in vCenter. When
you attempt to remove the failed cluster from SDDC Manager, the removal operation cannot locate the cluster object in
vCenter and hangs indefinitely.
Upgrading an NSX Manager cluster by using SDDC Manager fails with a error message
During retention evaluation, the automated backup cleanup script skips NSX backups stored under the NSX Manager
Virtual IP (VIP) directory structure. As a result expired backups accumulate indefinitely on the SFTP server. When the
upgrade retrieves the backup history, the accumulated files cause the NSX API to time out, returning the following error:
.
Read timed out
After importing a workload domain whose cluster hosts have individually configured NSX transport nodes,
domain synchronization fails with an error message
Broadcom 696

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If the hosts in an imported workload domain have individually configured transport nodes rather than a Transport Node
Profile, the domain synchronization workflow detects the host-level NSX configuration and attempts to record a warning
for the cluster. An error while recording the warning stops the synchronization and returns the following error message:
.
NSX_TNC_CONFIG_ERROR_GENERICError in configuring transport node collections
Importing an existing vCenter instance deploys NSX Manager on the wrong vCenter and the wrong distributed
virtual port group
If a stale powered-off VM with the same hostname as the vCenter VM exists on the target cluster, SDDC Manager detects
the stale VM instead of the actual vCenter instance. As a result, SDDC Manager deploys NSX Manager to the wrong
vCenter and port group. If there is no connectivity between the NSX Manager VMs and vCenter, the import fails during
Compute Manager registration.
Importing a new workload domain or converging a vCenter with a shared NSX fail with a misleading compatibility
error when the NSX install image bundles are deleted from the SDDC Manager bundle repository, even though the
existing NSX instance is compatible with the target vCenter
When importing a new workload domain or converging a vCenter with a shared NSX instance, the workflow may fail
with an error stating that the existing NSX instance is not compatible with the vCenter, even though the versions are
compatible. This occurs when NSX installation bundles have been removed from the SDDC Manager bundle repository.
After SDDC Manager completes a Quick Patch of the management domain vCenter, the vCenter version displayed
in VCF Operations shows a false version drift, and the vCenter upgrade bundle remains listed as available in
SDDC Manager, even though the upgrade succeeded
SDDC Manager caches the vCenter version per session with no expiry. The cache is removed only if SDDC Manager
disconnects from vCenter or the connection throws an error. A quick patch workflow does not restart vCenter services and
as a result SDDC Manager holds the pre-patch vCenter version persists in the inventory indefinitely. This also corrupts
SDDC Manager upgrade-readiness state, because the vCenter bundle remains listed as available, which can affect
upgrade sequencing and checks for subsequent operations.
After a failed or aborted upgrade attempt, upgrading vCenter to version 9.1 by using the Reduced Downtime
Upgrade workflow fails
When you run pre-checks or upgrade vCenter by using the Reduced Downtime Upgrade workflow, the upgrade fails at
the VCENTER_UPGRADE_PRECHECK stage with the following error message:
vCenter upgrade failed at the
VCENTER_UPGRADE_PRECHECK stage. vCenter set target version - vCenter set target version -
<target_version> failed. Non retriable exception while retrying operation failed.
This issue occurs when the source vCenter version is below 9.1, target vCenter version is 9.1 or later, but after a failed
or aborted upgrade attempt, vCenter Lifecycle Manager is already version 9.1 or later. As a result, SDDC Manager tries
to upgrade vCenter Lifecycle Manager by using a method, that requires vCenter version 9.1 or later. Since the vCenter
version is below 9.1, the pre-check fails.
Upgrading SDDC Manager to version 9.1.1 fails at the SDDC Manager Deployment Drift step
If the password for any SDDC Manager appliance account (such as , , , or ) was changed more
root vcf backup audit
than 90 days ago and the default password policy configuration has been modified, during the SDDC Manager upgrade
procedure, the configuration restore task incorrectly expires the respective accounts and as a result, the upgrade to
version 9.1.1 fails.
Known Issues
When the Binary Management page lists 90 or more bundles, error banners or missing download statuses are
displayed
When the Binary Management page lists 90 or more bundles, the page sends all bundle status requests at once and the
gateway rejects the excess requests with a HTTP 503 error. This issue affects mostly installation binaries on upgraded
setups with large software depot instances, and does not affect bundle downloading, scheduling, or deleting operations.
Workaround: Perform the following tasks.
1. Ignore and close the error banners.
2. If a bundle shows no status, reload the page or switch the binary type and switch back.
Broadcom 697

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. If a bundle you no longer need is listed, such as a bundle for version you have already upgraded to, delete the
bundle.
4. For bulk download, schedule, or delete actions, select less than 90 bundles per action, and verify that the system
created a task for each bundle.

What's New
This release contains various security enhancements and delivers fixes as described in the Resolved Issues section.
Applying the Patch
You apply this patch by using VCF Operations. See Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
When you apply the VCF Operations patch, the cloud proxy and license server components are patched automatically.
Resolved Issues
The vCenter Task Console displays recurring plug-in tasks and vCenter license assignment fails from VCF
Operations.
When a vCenter instance is managed by VCF Operations, the VCF Operations plug-in registers and unregisters
cyclically. As a result, the vCenter Task Console becomes populated with recurring plug-in download, deployment, and
undeployment tasks. Additionally, license assignment to vCenter instances from VCF Operations fails.
An error is displayed on the Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instance page when accessing it with a user scope restricted
only to a specific workload domain
When a user with restricted access to a specific workload domain navigates to the Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instance page,
the page fails to load and displays an error. This issue is triggered by dependency in the scope permissions, and the page
only functions correctly if the assigned scope also explicitly includes access to the management vCenter object. This
dependency limits the ability to effectively restrict per-domain access for users and groups.
Witness and data nodes with a mismatched build version can join the cluster without a compatibility check
In VCF Operations 9.1, the endpoints that enroll witness and data nodes into the cluster do not perform a build-version
compatibility check. As a result, a witness or data node running a newer or older build can be enrolled into the cluster
without being rejected, leaving the cluster in a mixed-build state.
A replica node running a newer or older build can join the cluster without a version compatibility check
In VCF Operations 9.1, the replica node enrollment flow does not perform a build-version compatibility check. As a result,
a replica node deployed on a newer or older build than the primary node can join the cluster without being rejected,
leaving the cluster in a mixed-build state. The inconsistency surfaces later when any subsequent data-node addition is
rejected with HTTP 412, blocking further scale-out and requiring a manual workaround.
vCenter integration settings are not saved when vSAN is not enabled for the cluster.
In VCF Operations 9.1, when vSAN is not enabled for the cluster, the product does not save updates to vCenter
integration settings made from the Integrations page. This blocks routine administrative tasks such as updating the
vCenter password or activating Log Collection.
Upgrading to 9.1.1 causes Telegraf plugin deletion and updates to fail, resulting in orphan configuration blocks
and continued data collection
When updating or deleting Telegraf plugins in version 9.1.1, a status update task unexpectedly bakes a dynamic job ID
(jobId) into the plugin's configuration file marker on the cloud proxy. Because subsequent operations attempt to match
the original marker format (without the job ID), the system fails to locate the marker and cannot remove or edit the plugin
block.
A missing role or authentication failure during Content Management export/import results in a silent failure with
no error message displayed
Broadcom 699

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Single sign-on users without an assigned role experience a silent failure during Content Management export/import
operations, with no error message displayed indicating the failure.
Local user accounts in VCF Operations are locked for an incorrect duration after exceeding the maximum failed
login attempts, conflicting with the configured lockout policy
When a local user account was locked due to exceeding maximum failed login attempts, the lockout expiry duration was
incorrectly calculated using the password expiration setting (in days) directly as seconds, rather than using the configured
lockout duration policy setting.
Note: The 'admin' user account was not affected by this issue.
