After the binaries are successfully transferred to VCF Installer, you are ready to deploy.
Start a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance Deployment by Using the VCF
Installer Deployment Wizard
You can use the VCF Installer deployment wizard to plan, configure, and deploy a new VCF fleet. You can also deploy a
new VCF Instance within an existing fleet.
• Verify that you deployed and configured ESX hosts. See Preparing ESX Hosts for VCF or vSphere Foundation.
• Verify that you deployed VCF Installer version 9.1.1 or later. See Deploy VCF Installer.
• Verify that you downloaded the required binaries for VCF. See Downloading Binaries to VCF Installer.
• Verify that you configured the required FQDNs and IP addresses for deployment. See VCF Components FQDNs and
IP addresses.
Broadcom 2485

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If you plan to use an external load balancer to distribute VCF Operations traffic across the cluster nodes, verify that
the load balancer is deployed and configured. For the supported models and configuration requirements, see VCF
Operations Models.
A VCF fleet refers to an environment consisting of one or more VCF Instances and standalone vCenter instances that are
managed by the same VCF Operations instance.
• When you deploy the first VCF Instance in a VCF fleet, you can deploy a new VCF Operations instance or connect to
an existing one.
• When you deploy a new VCF Instance in an existing VCF fleet, you must connect to your existing VCF Operations
instance.
After you choose a deployment path, you plan and gather all the information required for deployment. By specifying the
scale of the deployment, network, and storage types, you define the required resources for your deployment.
After planning and preparation, you use the VCF Installer deployment workflows to specify deployment information
specific for your environment such as networks, hosts, and other information. As a result, the VMware Cloud Foundation
platform is automatically deployed and configured using the provided information.
This procedure uses the deployment wizard. You can also deploy by using a JSON specification file. See Use a JSON
Specification File to Deploy VMware Cloud Foundation or vSphere Foundation for more information.
VCF Installer allows you to skip VCF Automation during the initial deployment and deploy it as a Day-N operation. See
Deploying VCF Automation as a Day-N Operation.

Management network configuration • VM management network: For core VCF components, such as

• VCF management network: For broader VCF management

• vMotion network IP scheme (IPv4 or IPv6)
• Storage network IP scheme (IPv4 or IPv6)
Dual-stack networking allows communication with components
that support both network protocols, ensuring compatibility and
continuous connectivity. While not all components support IPv6
networking, components that are IPv4 only can still communicate
with the other components.
Note:
The dual-stack networking option is not available, if VCF

Installer wizard are not available.
VPC Network Configuration Full Stack VPC: In version 9.1.1 and later, provides the complete
VPC feature set, including all routing, switching, and gateways,
to manage the virtual network environment. This option uses
TEP-based overlay networking and supports both Distributed
Connectivity and Centralized Connectivity models. Select this
option to use the standard NSX VPC networking model.
VLAN-Backed VPC: In version 9.1.1 and later, provides essential
VPC services without TEPs, prioritizing the existing VLAN
infrastructure. This option enables TEP-less VPC networking,
where NSX provides only the overlay. If you select this option, the
VPC Gateway Connectivity and VNA Cluster Details sections
are not displayed, and Private CIDRs are not required for the
Supervisor configuration.
Broadcom 2489

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VPC Gateway Connectivity • Centralized Connectivity. Routes all north–south traffic
through NSX Edge Nodes for centralized service delivery.
If you select Centralized Connectivity, configure it after the
workload domain is created to make it VPC-ready. See Configure
Centralized Network Connectivity with Edge Clusters.
• Distributed Connectivity. Allows for north–south traffic
routing directly at the hypervisor level using a Transit Gateway
with distributed external connectivity.
If you select Distributed Connectivity, configure it in the Prepare
section of VCF Installer, on the NSX Manager page.
For Distributed Transit Gateways to provide stateful NAT and
load-balancing services, you must later deploy a Virtual Network
Appliance cluster.
Note:
VPC does not support IPv6. For more information about
VPCs, see Managing Virtual Private Clouds in vCenter.
8. Choose a storage type for your management domain.
Your selection determines the initial shared storage type for the default cluster in the management domain. This initial
shared storage type is known as principal storage and the principal storage type for a cluster cannot be changed.
However, you can add more clusters with different principal storage types to the management domain later.
Option Details
vSAN • Select vSAN ESA.
– Allow auto claim of HCL incompatible disks
• Select this option to allow the vSAN ESA automatic
disk-claim process to claim storage devices that VCF
Installer cannot verify against the vSAN Hardware
Compatibility List (HCL). Use this option only for
hardware that you have verified is HCL-certified.
• Select vSAN OSA.
– Select the number of host failures that are tolerated.
– Activate deduplication and compression for this storage
type.
• vSAN Data-in-transit encryption (available for vSAN ESA
and OSA)
– vSAN data-in-transit encryption is a cluster-wide setting.
All data and metadata between hosts in the same cluster
and data and metadata between server and client
clusters is encrypted. The rekey interval sets the time
duration before vSAN automatically regenerates the host-
to-host communication encryption keys. vSAN does not
re-encrypt data at rest or reformat disk after the interval
expires.
VMFS on Fibre Channel (FC) The datastore must already be created and mounted on all ESX
hosts.
NFS v3 The NFS Server must already be created and meet the NFS
Storage Guidelines and Requirements found in the Guidelines
and Requirements for NFS Storage with ESX.
If VCF Installer is deployed on one of the ESX hosts that will
form the management domain, the NFS datastore must be
mounted on the host. See Mount NFS Datastore to an ESX
Host.
• Use the same network configuration as the ESX
management network for the NFS storage network

Alternatively, you can specify non-contiguous IP addresses by using a JSON specification file. See Use a JSON

• NSX Host Overlay Network - dedicated VLAN separation for NSX tunnel endpoint VMkernels. With VCF 9.1.1 and
later, this option is not required for VLAN backed VPCs.
Specify IP inclusion ranges for the VCF management, vMotion, vSAN, and NSX overlay networks of the management
domain. IP addresses from the specified range are automatically assigned to ESX hosts, from vMotion, vSAN and
NSX networks only.
• Ensure that the IP ranges include sufficient IP addresses for the deployment.
• The number of IP addresses must be at least equal to the number of ESX hosts deployed.
• All IPs within the range must be available for use or IP conflicts occur.
• IPs for each network must be part of the VLAN configured with the network's port group.
As an example, if you specify the range start value as 10.11.13.101 and end as 10.11.13.121, a total of 21 IP
addresses would be available. Do not use special IP addresses, such as the network or broadcast address.
MTU determines the largest size of a data packet that can pass through for this traffic type.

16.On the vSphere Distributed Switch page, configure the vSphere Distributed Switch details, configure the network
traffic types, and click Create Distributed Switch.
a) To use a preconfigured profile, select one of the profiles and click Next.
Option Description
Default Configuration Provides a unified fabric for all traffic types using a single vSphere
Distributed Switch.
Storage Traffic Separation This profile creates two vSphere Distributed Switches with
separate physical NICs. One switch is dedicated for storage traffic,
while the other is used for all other traffic.
NSX Traffic Separation This profile creates two vSphere Distributed Switches with
separate physical NICs. One switch is dedicated for NSX (Virtual
Networking) traffic, while the other is used for all other traffic.
Custom Switch Configuration Copy from a preconfigured profile or create a new distributed
switch configuration. Multiple vSphere Distributed Switches can
be configured. Each vSphere Distributed Switch can hold one or
more network traffic configurations.
Some network traffic types are mandatory. Switch configuration is
incomplete until these mandatory traffic types are configured.
VM Management, VCF Management, vMotion, vSAN, and NSX
network types can be configured only once for a cluster.
NSX traffic type can be configured in multiple vSphere Distributed
Switches.
b) To create a custom configuration for the distributed switch, click Create custom configuration.
Option Description
Traffic types for the distributed switch • ESX Management
• VCF Management
This option is not exposed for the default Network setting.
• VM Management
• vMotion
• vSAN
• NSX
Distributed Switch name Enter a name for the distributed switch.
Uplinks / LAG configuration VDS Uplinks represent the individual physical network adapters
(vmnics) on an ESX host connecting to the physical switch. In
this mode, the VDS manages load balancing and failover using
software-based algorithms such as Route Based on Physical NIC
Load or Route Based on the Source of the Port ID. The physical
switch ports do not need to be configured in a bond or channel;
they operate as independent links.
Broadcom 2495

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Description
VDS LAG bundles multiple physical uplinks into a single logical
channel using the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP). This
requires a corresponding LACP configuration on the physical ToR
(Top-of-Rack) switches. The physical switch and VDS negotiate
traffic hashing.
Number of uplinks The number of uplinks dedicated to this distributed switch.
Map uplinks to physical NICs on host Connects your logical virtual network to your physical network
hardware. This mapping pairs a logical uplink (a software object
on the distributed switch, with a physical adapter (hardware on the
ESX host).
c) To configure the traffic types for the distributed switch, turn on the toggle for each traffic type and configure the
settings.
Option Description
Distributed port group name Name of the distributed port group for this traffic type.
Load balancing Route based on the source of the port ID: the
distributed switch maps port IDs to specific uplinks based on the
load balancing source of the NSX uplink profile.
Route Based on Physical NIC Load (Default): the
distributed switch monitors the saturation of the physical uplinks.
If the primary uplinks exceed a set amount of utilization (75%
default) for 30 seconds, the distributed switch moves some VM
traffic to another active uplink.
Route Based on Source MAC Hash: the distributed switch
uses the VM's MAC address and hashes it to an uplink, which
creates even distribution for VMs that might change port IDs but
keep MAC addresses.
Route Based on IP Hash: the distributed switch uses the
source and destination IP address of every packet to decide which
uplink to use. This allows a single VM to use multiple uplinks
simultaneously.
Note:
You must configure LACP (Link Aggregation Control
Protocol) on the physical Top-of-Rack switches.
Use Explicit Failover Order: you define the order in
which uplinks are used in case of failure.
Uplink Active: This traffic type uses the uplink immediately during
normal operation. In case of multiple active uplinks, traffic of this
type is distributed across all active uplinks simultaneously.
Standby: A standby uplink is connected, but no traffic is sent
through it as long as at least one "Active" uplink is healthy. If all
active uplinks fail, the distributed switch moves the standby uplink
to active status.
Unused: Traffic of this type never uses this uplink, regardless of
the status of the remaining uplinks.

configured in the external router (TOR).

Errors Review all failed validations and resolve the issue(s) using the

21.After addressing all validation errors and warnings, click Deploy.
You can monitor the deployment progress. If there are errors, review the failed tasks in the Tasks panel, address the
issue(s), and retry the deployment.
CAUTION:
After deployment completes, do not move the VCF management services or VCF Automation VMs to a different
resource pool or folder. If you move the VMs to a new resource pool or folder, subsequent patching, deployment,
or scale out operations fail.
• License your environment. See Registering VCF Operations and a License Server with the VCF Business Services
Console.
• Click Review Passwords to review the passwords. To review passwords for past deployments, in the VCF Installer
appliance, click the user name at the top-right corner of the window and select Deployments.
Note:
You can also retrieve some of the passwords using the SDDC Manager API and VCF Operations API.
• (Optional) Download the JSON specification file for the deployment.
Note:
The JSON specification file does not include passwords.
• Deploy the remaining VCF platform components that VCF Installer does not deploy automatically. See Completing the
Deployment of Your Platform.
• To cover the platform after a failure, configure file-based backups for SDDC Manager and other management
components. See Configure File-Based Backup Schedule for SDDC Manager.
• If you deployed VCF Operations in High Availability mode, to prevent VCF Operations cluster nodes from running on
the same ESX host, apply a vSphere DRS anti-affinity rule.
• For platform administration tasks such as managing identity and access, certificates, passwords, component lifecycle,
and backup and restore of your VCF platform, see the Fleet Management guide.
• For monitoring and troubleshooting tasks such as configuring alerts, analyzing logs, monitoring dashboards, and
troubleshooting your VCF platform, see the Infrastructure Operations guide.

Start a New vSphere Foundation Deployment by Using the VCF Installer
Deployment Wizard
You can use the VCF Installer deployment wizard to deploy a new VMware vSphere Foundation platform.
• Verify that you deployed and configured ESX hosts. See Preparing ESX Hosts for VCF or vSphere Foundation.
• Verify that you deployed VCF Installer version 9.1.1 or later. See Deploy VCF Installer.
• Verify that you downloaded the required binaries for VMware vSphere Foundation. See Downloading Binaries to VCF
Installer.
• Verify that you configured the required FQDNs and IP addresses for deployment. See vSphere Foundation Platform
FQDNs and IP Addresses in VCF Components FQDNs and IP addresses.
Important:
The VCF Installer deploys vSphere Foundation only with VCF management services. If you want to deploy
vSphere Foundation without VCF management services, you can deploy manually. See Deploying VMware
vSphere Foundation 9.1 Without VCF Management Services.
Plan and gather all the information that is required for deployment. By specifying the network and storage types, you
define the required resources for your VMware vSphere Foundation deployment.
Use the VCF Installer deployment workflows to specify deployment information specific for your environment such
as networks, hosts, and other information. As a result, the VMware vSphere Foundation software components are
automatically deployed and configured using the information provided.
VCF Installer deploys vSphere Foundation in a simple mode with the following component sizes: medium vCenter,
medium VCF Operations, and small VCF management services. To change the component sizes, instead of using this
procedure to deploy vSphere Foundation by using the deployment wizard, you can use a specification file. See Use
JSON
a JSON Specification File to Deploy VMware Cloud Foundation or vSphere Foundation.
To create a VMware vSphere Foundation environment using existing vSphere infrastructure, see Converge a vCenter
Instance and ESX Hosts to vSphere Foundation.
1. In a web browser, log in to the VCF Installer appliance at .
https://installer_appliance_FQDN
Enter the user and password you provided when you deployed the appliance and then click Log In.
admin@local
2. Click Deployment Wizard > VMware vSphere Foundation .
3. Review the introductory information and click Next.
4. Select Deploy new VMware vSphere Foundation.
5. Do not select any existing components.
To use an existing vCenter to create a VMware vSphere Foundation environment, see Converge a vCenter Instance
and ESX Hosts to vSphere Foundation.

as vCenter and ESX. You can share this network with the ESX
management network or use a dedicated network.
• VCF management network: For broader VCF management
components, such as VCF Operations. You can share this

• vMotion network IP scheme (IPv4 or IPv6)
• Storage network IP scheme (IPv4 or IPv6)
Dual-stack networking allows communication with components
that support both network protocols, ensuring compatibility and
continuous connectivity. While not all components support IPv6
networking, components that are IPv4 only can still communicate
with the other components.
Note:
The dual-stack networking option is not available, if VCF
Installer does not have IPv4 and IPv6 configured. For
more information, see Configure the Network on the ESX
Hosts and Deploy VCF Installer.

Your selection determines the initial shared storage type for the default cluster in the management domain. This initial
shared storage type is known as principal storage and the principal storage type for a cluster cannot be changed.
However, you can add additional clusters with different principal storage types to the management domain later.
Option Details
vSAN • Select vSAN ESA.

Compatibility List (HCL). Use this option only for
hardware that you have verified is HCL-certified.
• Select vSAN OSA.
– Select the number of host failures that are tolerated.
– Activate deduplication and compression for this storage
type.
• vSAN Data-in-transit encryption (available for vSAN ESA
and OSA)
– vSAN data-in-transit encryption is a cluster-wide setting.
All data and metadata between hosts in the same cluster
and data and metadata between server and client
clusters is encrypted. The rekey interval sets the time
duration before vSAN automatically regenerates the host-
to-host communication encryption keys. vSAN does not
re-encrypt data at rest or reformat disk after the interval
expires.

• vSAN Network or NFS Network - distributed port group separation for ESX Host storage VMkernels
Specify IP inclusion ranges for the VCF management, vMotion, and vSAN networks of the management domain. IP
addresses from the specified range are automatically assigned to ESX hosts, from vMotion, and vSAN networks only.
• Ensure that the IP ranges include sufficient IP addresses for the deployment.
• The number of IP addresses must be at least equal to the number of ESX hosts deployed.
• All IPs within the range must be available for use or IP conflicts occur.
• IPs for each network must be part of the VLAN configured with the network's port group.
As an example, if you specify the range start value as 10.11.13.101 and end as 10.11.13.121, a total of 21 IP
addresses would be available. Do not use special IP addresses, such as the network or broadcast address.
MTU determines the largest size of a data packet that can pass through for this traffic type.

Deploying VMware vSphere Foundation 9.1 Without VCF Management Services
Deploying VCF management services is not mandatory for VMware vSphere Foundation 9.1. You can build a fully
operational 9.1 environment by deploying and configuring vSphere components manually without using VCF Installer.
Deploying and running vSphere Foundation 9.1 without VCF management services is a supported deployment model. The
following functionalities are available without VCF management services.
• Compute, storage, networking, and administrative operations by using native vSphere management interfaces.
• Running, patching, and upgrading vSphere Foundation by using standard vSphere lifecycle mechanisms.
When using vSphere Foundation without VCF management services, the following functionalities are not available.
• Log management by using the log management component. See Components in VCF and vSphere Foundation.
• Binary management by using the software depot component. See Components in VCF and vSphere Foundation.
• Integrated lifecycle management of VCF Operations.
If you need VCF management services, later you can deploy VCF management services by using VCF Installer. After that
you can deploy log management by using VCF Operations. See Deploy VCF Management Services and License Server
for the vSphere Foundation Upgrade and Deploy Log Management.
Manual vSphere Foundation 9.1 Deployment
• Verify that you deployed and configured ESX hosts. See Installing and Setting Up ESX.

Troubleshooting VMware Cloud Foundation or vSphere Foundation Deployments
If you encounter errors during deployment, you can use the support bundle, log files, and the Supportability and
Serviceability (SoS) Utility to help with troubleshooting.
Generate and Download a Support Bundle
If your current attempt to deploy a new VCF or VMware vSphere Foundation instance is not successful, you can generate
and download a support bundle. The support bundle includes support logs from the components that you specified for the
deployment.
1. In a web browser, log in to the VCF Installer appliance at .
https://installer_appliance_FQDN
2. Enter the user and password that you provided when you deployed the appliance and then click Log
admin@local
In.
3. Click the user name at the top-right corner of the window and select Support Bundle.
Broadcom 2509

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Select the components to include in the bundle and click GENERATE NEW SUPPORT BUNDLE.
5. After the support bundle generation is completed, click DOWNLOAD.
Access Domain Manager Logs on the VCF Installer Appliance
If you experience validation or deployment failures, check the log files for the domain manager service on the VCF
Installer appliance.
1. Log in to the VCF Installer appliance as vcf by using a Secure Shell (SSH) client or the vSphere Web Console.
2. Run the command to switch to root account.
su
3. Access the domain manager service log at .
/var/log/vmware/vcf/domainmanager/domainmanager.log
Recover Access to a Locked VCF Installer Appliance Account
If your local account is locked, you can recover access by restarting the service.
commonsvcs
1. Log in to the VCF Installer appliance as by using a Secure Shell (SSH) client or the vSphere Web Console.
root
2. Restart the service by running the command.
commonsvcs systemctl restart commonsvcs
3. Wait approximately 5 minutes for the service to fully boot.
Retrieve VCF Management Services Passwords
After deploying the VCF management services components, you can retrieve the components' password.
1. Log in to SDDC Manager as by using a Secure Shell (SSH) client.
vcf
2. Run the command to switch to root account.
su
3. Turn on HTTP access to the domain manager’s vault and restart the service.
echo vcf.vault.http-access=true >> /etc/vmware/vcf/domainmanager/application.properties && systemctl
restart domainmanager
4. Obtain the UUID of the deployment task.
a. Log in to SDDC Manager UI with a user assigned the Administrator role.
b. At the bottom of the page, expand the Tasks bar.
c. Click the Deploy VCF Management Components task.
d. Copy the UUID from the address bar of your Internet browser. For example,
9ccad9fd-
.
a179-4538-822c-8bf6149ebc7d
5. Log back in to SDDC Manager as by using a Secure Shell (SSH) client.
vcf
6. Use the UUID to copy the data for the deployment workflow into a temporary file.
UUID
curl -X GET http://localhost/domainmanager/internal/vault/ | json_pp > /tmp/workflow.json
7. Obtain the password from the file.
systemUserPassword /tmp/workflow.json
8. Delete the temporary file immediately after retrieving the password.
shred -u /tmp/workflow.json
9. Turn off HTTP access to the domain manager’s vault and restart the service.
sed -i '/vcf.vault.http-access=true/d' /etc/vmware/vcf/domainmanager/application.properties && systemctl
restart domainmanager
Supportability and Serviceability (SoS) Utility
You can run the SoS Utility on the VCF Installer and SDDC Manager appliances to perform health checks and collect
logs for troubleshooting. After a successful deployment, run the SoS Utility from the SDDC Manager appliance. The
SDDC Manager appliance supports a broader set of options than the VCF Installer appliance, including Fix-It-Up options,
additional health checks, and additional log collection options. To see the options supported on a specific appliance,
connect to it by SSH and run the command.
/opt/vmware/sddc-support/sos --help
Note:
The SoS Utility is not a debug tool. It provides health check and log collection operations that you can use to
facilitate troubleshooting.
Broadcom 2510

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To run the SoS Utility, SSH in to the appliance using the account and then enter to switch to the root user.
vcf su
Navigate to the directory and type followed by the options that are required for
/opt/vmware/sddc-support ./sos
your desired operation.
--option-1 --option-2 --option-n
./sos ...
In VCF Installer, the SoS Utility can collect support logs only for components from the latest deployment. The utility does
not support logs from the following components: cloud proxy, VCF Operations for networks, telemetry, and license server.
Bootstrap virtual machine logs for VCF management services and VCF Automation are collected only if a failure occurs.

SoS Utility Health Check Options
The SoS Utility can be used to perform health checks on various components, including connectivity, compute, and
storage. Health checks do not include VCF management services, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations.
Note:
SoS Utility operations on the VCF Installer appliance are strictly intended for troubleshooting during initial
deployment. Once deployment is complete, execute all SoS health checks and operations from the SDDC
Manager appliance only. Running the SoS Utility from VCF Installer in a Day-N environment may lead to
unexpected results, as VCF Installer is unaware of post-deployment configuration changes.

--storage-health Performs a check on the vSAN disk health of the ESX hosts and • SDDC Manager
vSphere clusters. Can be combined with --run-vsan-checks.
--run-vsan-checks Runs a VM creation test to verify the vSAN cluster health. Running • SDDC Manager
the test creates a virtual machine on each host in the vSAN cluster.
This option cannot be run on its own and must be combined with --
health-check or --services-health.
--dns-health Performs a forward and reverse DNS health check. • SDDC Manager
--get-inventory-info Retrieves inventory details for SDDC Manager, such as vCenter, • SDDC Manager
NSX, SDDC Manager, and ESX hosts.
Optionally, add the flag --domain-name ALL to return details
for all workload domains.
--password-health Checks password expiry status for components. • SDDC Manager
--version-health Checks the version of bill of materials (BOM) components. • SDDC Manager
Compares the SDDC Manager inventory, the actual installed BOM
component version, and the BOM component versions to detect any
drift.
--json-output-dir Writes health check results to a JSON file in the specified JSONDIR • SDDC Manager
JSONDIR directory.
Deploying Deferred Components on Custom Networking
If you did not deploy VCF Operations and VCF Automation during the initial deployment of a VCF Instance, you can use
the VCF Installer UI or the VCF Installer API to complete their deployment process to a custom network. Besides VCF
Operations and VCF Automation, the workflow deploys cloud proxy and license server. You can use custom networking to
separate user-facing networks from management networks to meet regulatory and security requirements.
By default, VCF Installer configures all VCF Operations and VCF Automation nodes to use the same distributed port
group as the vCenter instance. By selecting the Deploy VCF Operations and VCF Automation to a specific vSphere
distributed switch or NSX segment option you skip the deployment of these components when deploying a new VCF
fleet.
Later, to deploy VCF Operations and VCF Automation on custom networking and complete the deployment of the
management domain, you can create a separate network that is backed by a distributed port group or NSX segment and
use this network to deploy the VCF components. After you complete the custom networking configuration, you select the
Deploy deferred components option from the VCF Installer UI and complete the deployment process. Alternatively, you
can complete the deployment by using the VCF Installer API.
For information about the network deployment locations, see Network Deployment Options for VCF Components.
You can deploy the VCF management components to the following custom networks:
• Deploy Deferred Components on the Shared Management Network
Broadcom 2514

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Deploy Deferred Components on a Dedicated Management Network
• Deploy Deferred Components on NSX Overlay Segments
Deploy Deferred Components on the Shared Management Network
If you skipped deploying VCF Operations and VCF Automation during the initial deployment of a VCF Instance, you can
use the VCF Installer user interface or the VCF Installer API to deploy these components on the same distributed port
group as the VCF core components.
• Review Design Guide. See VCF Management Shared VLAN Network Model.
• Verify that you deployed VCF Installer version 9.1.1 or later. See Deploy VCF Installer.
• Download binaries for the VCF management components to VCF Installer. See Downloading Binaries to VCF Installer.
• Verify that the initial VCF fleet deployment is complete.
• If you plan to use a load balancer in your VCF environment, verify it is deployed and configured.
• Verify that you configured the required FQDNs and IP addresses for deployment. See VCF Components FQDNs and
IP addresses.
• (API only) Verify that you have a machine with installed and , and network access to the VCF Installer
curl jq
appliance.
Follow this procedure to configure VCF Operations, VCF Automation, cloud proxy, and license server to use the same
distributed port group as the VCF core components - usually the vCenter instance.
VCF Installer UI 1. In a web browser, log in to the VCF Installer appliance at https://
installer_appliance_FQDN.
Note:
Enter the admin@local user and password you provided when you deployed the appliance and
then click Log In.
2. Click Deployment Wizard > VMware Cloud Foundation.
3. Review the introductory information and click Next.
4. Select Deploy deferred components.
5. Enter the details of the existing SDDC Manager and click Connect.
6. Confirm the certificate thumbprints.
Broadcom 2515

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
7. Select a deployment model, scale for your VCF Instance, and DNS and NTP servers.
Deployment model You can choose the deployment model for new
appliances that get deployed. High Availability is
recommended for production environments.
Note:
The deployment model that you select does
not impact existing appliances that you are
using in your VCF fleet or VCF Instance.
See the VMware Cloud Foundation Design
documentation for more information.
Note:
New appliances that get deployed are
automatically configured to comply with
Federal Information Processing Standards
(FIPS).
Size You can choose the scale of the components in your
VCF Instance.
• Small
– In VCF 9.1, this is the only available option
for the simple deployment model.
– In VCF 9.1.1 and later, this is the default
option for the simple and HA deployment
models.
• Medium
– In VCF 9.1, this is the default option for the
HA deployment model.
– In VCF 9.1.1 and later, this is an option for
the HA deployment model.
• Large
– In VCF 9.1 and later, this is an option for the
HA deployment model.
For more information about deployment sizes, see
VCF Fleet Sizing Models.
Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) Select an option to activate or deactivate CEIP
across all deployed components.
VMware's Customer Experience Improvement
Program (CEIP) collects technical information from
participating customers to provide better support.
See Customer Experience Improvement Program
for more information.
Autogenerate passwords Starting with VCF 9.1, select this option to let VCF
Installer generate secure passwords for all deployed
components. You can retrieve the passwords after
the deployment begins. If you do not select this
option, you must provide each password manually.
Skip VCF Automation In VCF 9.1.1 and later, select this option to skip the
deployment of VCF Automation during the deferred
components workflow. If you select this option, the
UI does not prompt for VCF Automation FQDNs
or IP addresses. You can deploy VCF Automation
later as a Day-N operation. See Deploying VCF
Automation as a Day-N Operation.
8. Provide networking details.
a. Select the same distributed port group that the VCF core components use.
Broadcom 2516

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
The VCF Management components network traffic will run on this port group.
b. Enter the network gateway address.
c. Enter IP details for VCF Automation.
If you chose to deploy VCF Automation later as a Day-N operation, this option is not displayed.
• For deployments version 9.1.0.0 through 9.1.0.300, you specify a contiguous IP range for the
VCF Automation nodes with 5 IP addresses.
• For deployments version 9.1.0.400 and later, you specify 6 IP addresses as contiguous or non-
contiguous IP range.
Note:
The sixth additional IP address is requested by the UI but is not consumed by the deployment.
9. Enter the details for the VCF management components.
Table 967: VCF Management Configuration Details
Each Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) must point to a unique IP address.
Note:
For VCF components that support the dual-stack model, the FQDNs must resolve to
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. See Dual Stack IP Addressing Model.
Component Field Description
VCF Operations Primary node Enter the FQDN of the VCF Operations primary node.
FQDN

Data node FQDN Enter the FQDN of the VCF Operations data node. This field
appears only when deploying VCF in High Availability mode
with a Medium or Large deployment size.
Load Balancer Load balancer (Optional) Enter the FQDN of the load balancer that distributes
FQDN the VCF Operations traffic. This field appears only when
deploying VCF in High Availability mode.
Cloud Proxy Cloud Proxy FQDN Enter the FQDN of the cloud proxy. Cloud proxy collects and
monitors data locally in a VCF Instance.
License Server License Server Enter the FQDN of the license server. A license server is
FQDN added to a VCF Operations instance to store the licenses
you want to assign from this VCF Operations instance. You
must add at least one license server to each VCF Operations
instance that you use for license management.
You can deploy license server as IPv4 only. In VCF 9.1.1 and
later, after the deployment, you can change the networking
configuration to IPv6. See Configure IPv6 on a License Server.
VCF Automation * VCF Automation Enter the FQDN to assign to the VCF Automation instance.
FQDN Later, you use it to access the VCF Automation user interface.
Note:
Do not use capital letters in the FQDN.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Component Field Description

-d @deferred-components.json
4. Check the response of the validation.
curl -k -s -X GET \
https://$vcfInstallerFqdn/v1/sddcs/validations/latest \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $vcfInstallerToken" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
| jq '{executionStatus: .executionStatus, resultStatus: .resultStatus, failed:
[.validationChecks[] | select(.resultStatus == "FAILED")]}'
5. Deploy the VCF management components.
curl -k -X POST \
https://$vcfInstallerFqdn/v1/sddcs \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $vcfInstallerToken" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d @deferred-components.json
6. (Optional) Monitor the deployment.
curl -k -X GET \
https://$vcfInstallerFqdn/v1/sddcs \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $vcfInstallerToken" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
7. When the deployment completes, open the VCF Operations UI to apply licensing and perform other
post-deployment configuration.

Completing the Deployment of Your Platform
After the automated VCF Installer deployment of components for your VMware Cloud Foundation or vSphere Foundation
platform, you must deploy the remaining components to complete the platform. You deploy VCF Operations orchestrator
manually for both VCF and vSphere Foundation. For VCF, you deploy the remaining components by using automation that
is provided by VCF Operations.
Note:
If deployment of a component fails and the component appears listed in the UI, there is no option to delete the
listing. To remove the component from the UI, see Broadcom knowledge base article 441333.
If you did not deploy VCF Automation by using the VCF Installer workflows, see Deploying VCF Automation as a Day-N
Operation.

Important:
After deployment of any VCF services runtime components, note the following guidelines:
• For automatic backups during management component patching and upgrading, configure SFTP after the
management services installation completes. See Configure an External SFTP Server for VCF Management
Services and VCF Automation Backups.
• VCF management services uses the VCF services runtime template to deploy VMs during scale and
remediation operations. Do not remove the VCF services runtime template.
• Do not rename or delete datastores, network objects, folders, or VMs associated with VCF services runtime
directly in vCenter. These modifications are not supported and cause synchronization failures.

Log management collects, analyzes, and visualizes logs across your VMware Cloud Foundation platform. The component
is now part of VCF management services and you deploy it from VCF Operations. You also use this procedure for
scenarios where a redeployment is required for VCF 5.2.x to 9.1 upgrade.

Deploy VCF Operations for Networks
VCF Operations for networks provides a comprehensive overview of your VMware Cloud Foundation platform network
health, issues, and operations.
Initially, you deploy a single platform node and a single collector node. After deployment, you can scale up or down the
node size, see Scaling VCF Management Components. Also, you can scale out the deployment by adding platform and
collector nodes, see Add Nodes in VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks.
You must allocate a static IP for every VCF Operations for networks node you deploy.
You size your VCF Operations for networks deployment based on the size of your VCF fleet. See VCF Operations for
Networks System Recommendations and Requirements.
After deployment of VCF Operations for networks, the platform and collector VM names contain their respective IP
addresses. The VM names are not specified during deployment. Do not change the names of the VMs manually, they are
managed by VCF Operations.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Build.
3. In the left pane, click Lifecycle.
4. Click VCF Management and click the Components tab.

The Add VCF Operations for Networks wizard opens.
6. Deploy VCF Operations for networks.

Deploy Real-Time Metrics
Real-time metrics allows you to collect the real-time, granular data from your core VCF infrastructure, such as vCenter,
ESX, NSX, and vSAN. As part of the deployment the real-time metrics store component is also deployed.
The real-time metrics component collects performance data directly from vCenter, ESX, NSX, and vSAN. This outbound
connection originates from the real-time metrics component that is operating within VCF management services and goes
to both the vCenter instance and the ESX hosts. To facilitate access to the ESX hosts, verify that network connectivity is
established through port 443 over HTTPS.
Perform the following steps to deploy the real-time metrics component.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. (Optional) If integrating VCF instances with shared NSX components, verify that System Managed Credential is
enabled to ensure that real-time metrics data collection succeeds.
a) Navigate to Operate > Administration > Integrations.
b) On the Accounts tab, expand the VMware Cloud Foundation section.
c) Expand your VCF instance and click the domain.
d) On the domain page, click the NSX tab.
e) If System Managed Credential is unchecked, click it on.
3. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management > Add Components.
4. On the Components tab, select Real-Time Metrics.
a) Provide the information required for deployment.
• Version: Select the version of the Real-time metrics component.
Broadcom 2535

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VCF Instance: All VCF Instances managed by SDDC Manager instances that run version 9.1 are selected for
installation by default. To customize the selection, click Change Selection and deselect any VCF Instances
where you do not want real-time metrics installed.
b) Click Install to start the real-time metrics component deployment.
The deployment configures the adapter and invokes data collection from core components such as vCenter, ESX, NSX,
and vSAN. When the deployment completes, the real-time metrics appear on the observability workbench for the selected
inventory object.
Note:
If real-time metrics is not enabled, some charts that are displayed in dashboards and consume aggregated
metrics from real-time metrics have empty values.
When you add VCF Instances to your fleet, repeat the procedure to install the component on the new instances.
Deploy VCF Operations Orchestrator
Before you can access the VCF Operations orchestrator content in your VCF environment, deploy the VCF Operations
orchestrator appliance.
• Verify that the host on which you are deploying the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance meets the minimum
hardware requirements.
– 4 CPUs
– 12 GB memory
– 200 GB storage
Note:
Do not reduce the default memory size, because the VCF Operations orchestrator server requires at least 8 GB of
free memory.
• Download the file for the appliance from the Broadcom Support portal.
.ova
– If you plan to create a cluster, download and deploy three standalone instances.

Format Description
Thick Provisioned Lazy Zeroed Creates a virtual disk in a default thick format. The space
required for the virtual disk is allocated when the virtual disk
is created. If any data remains on the physical device, it is not
erased during creation, but is zeroed out on demand later on
first write from the virtual machine.
Thick Provisioned Eager Zeroed Supports clustering features such as Fault Tolerance. The space
required for the virtual disk is allocated when the virtual disk is
created. If any data remains on the physical device, it is zeroed

Configure VCF Operations Orchestrator for VCF Automation All Apps Organizations
As a provider administrator, you integrate a VCF Automation for All Apps organization with VCF Operations orchestrator
so that the organization administrator and project users can use VCF Operations orchestrator workflows in VCF
Automation.
In a VCF Automation for All Apps organization, a single external VCF Operations orchestrator instance is deployed,
configured, and added as an integration by the provider administrator on a per-request basis. Other VCF Operations
orchestrator instances cannot be added. If the organization already has a VCF Operations orchestrator integration, you
must first delete the existing integration before you can add a different one.
The external instance you configure is restricted and registered to that VCF Automation All Apps organization only. The
registered VCF Operations orchestrator instance cannot be registered to other organizations even if the initial organization
is deleted.
Note:
When configuring VCF Automation as the authentication provider for VCF Operations orchestrator, ensure that
the VCF Automation and VCF Operations orchestrator versions match up to the subminor digit, for example, both
are version 9.1.0.x or both are version 9.1.1.x and so on.
Step 1. Configure Authentication for a VCF Operations orchestrator Integration in VCF Automation for All Apps
When you configure an authentication provider for VCF Operations orchestrator, that VCF Operations orchestrator
instance is restricted to the respective VCF Automation organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance as .
root
2. Configure the authentication provider.
PROVIDER_ADMINISTRATOR_ACCOUNT FQDN_VCF_AUTOMATION
vracli vro authentication set -p tm -u -hn https:// --
ALL_APPS_ORGANIZATION_NAME
tenant
3. Redeploy the VCF Operations orchestrator pods.
/opt/scripts/deploy.sh
The VCF Operations orchestrator instance is configured and associated with the All Apps organization. The configuration
process can take up to several minutes to complete.
Note:
You can unregister the current authentication provider by running the
vracli vro authentication unregister
command from the command-line interface.
Step 2. Add a VCF Operations orchestrator Integration in VCF Automation for All Apps
You integrate VCF Operations orchestrator with your All Apps organization to use it for extensibility automation tasks.
Only one external VCF Operations orchestrator instance can be integrated with the organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal with system administrator credentials.
2. Navigate to your target organization and select Launch Organization Portal.
3. In the organization UI, navigate to Administer > Connections > Integrations and select Add Integration.
4. Select Orchestrator.
5. Enter a name and description for the VCF Operations orchestrator integration.
6. Under VCF Operations Orchestrator URL, enter the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of your external VCF
Operations orchestrator instance.
For example, .
https://my_Orchestrator_FQDN.com:443
Note:
If you have a clustered VCF Operations orchestrator environment, enter the URL of the load balancer.
Broadcom 2538

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
7. To validate the integration, click Validate.
8. When prompted to confirm the certificate, review the certificate and click Accept.
9. Click Add.
The VCF Operations orchestrator integration is saved.
10.To verify that the integration is configured and that the workflows are added, navigate to the Orchestrate tab.
The VCF Operations orchestrator instance is ready and you can now enable extensibility with VCF Operations
orchestrator for the organization. To access VCF Operations orchestrator, select the Orchestrate tab in the VCF
Automation organization UI.
After you configure VCF Operations orchestrator for the organization, VCF Operations orchestrator starts to perform
periodic data collection for the integration after about 10 minutes.
Step 3. Enable VCF Operations orchestrator for the VCF Automation All Apps Organization
To enable extensibility through VCF Operations orchestrator for the VCF Automation organization, you must publish the
Orchestrator rights bundle to that organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal with system administrator credentials.
2. Navigate to Administration > Access Control > Rights Bundles.
3. Select the Orchestrator Rights Bundle.
4. On the Orchestrator Rights Bundle page, click Publish.
5. Select the target organization and click Save.
6. Verify that the organization is added by navigating to Administration > Access Control > Rights Bundles and
checking the link in the Published To list of the Orchestrator Rights Bundle tab.
You have registered VCF Operations orchestrator for use in your organization. Next, the organization administrator can
manage extensibility with VCF Operations orchestrator-related authorizations for users in that organization.
Using the VCF Operations orchestrator Plug-Ins
VCF Operations orchestrator provides a standard set of preinstalled plug-ins, including plug-ins for vCenter and VCF
Automation for All Apps, to allow you to orchestrate tasks in the different environments that the plug-ins expose. For more
information, go to Using the VCF Operations orchestrator Plug-ins.
Note:
If your VCF Operations orchestrator integration authenticates with VCF Automation, when using the vCenter plug-
in, you must use shared session and not session per user. For more information, go to Configure the Connection
to a vCenter Instance.
Configure VCF Operations Orchestrator for VCF Automation VM Apps Organizations
As an organization administrator, you integrate a VCF Automation for VM Apps organization with VCF Operations
orchestrator so that you and your project users can use VCF Operations orchestrator workflows in VCF Automation.
In VCF Automation for VM Apps organizations, you can register multiple VCF Operations orchestrator instances with
the organization. Both embedded and external VCF Operations orchestrator instances can be registered with the same
organization.
Important:
If you upgrade an existing VMware Aria Automation 8.x deployment to VCF Automation 9, your organizations are
automatically mapped to VCF Automation for VM Apps organizations.
• If you are upgrading from VMware Aria Automation 8.x, any existing Automation Orchestrator integrations and
their content are preserved as-is in the VCF Automation for the VM Apps organization.
• Any external Automation Orchestrator instances must be upgraded after first upgrading VMware Aria
Automation 8.x to VCF Automation. The integrations are then available in the corresponding target VM apps
organizations.
Broadcom 2539

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Before you begin
• You are the organization administrator of a VM Apps organization in VCF Automation. For more information on VCF
Automation user roles, see Predefined VCF Automation Roles and Their Rights.
• Users have been imported into your organization. For more information on importing users, see Import Provider Users
to Your VCF Automation.
Note:
When configuring VCF Automation as the authentication provider for VCF Operations orchestrator, ensure that
the VCF Automation and VCF Operations orchestrator versions match up to the subminor digit, for example, both
are version 9.1.0.x or both are version 9.1.1.x and so on.
Step 1. Configure Authentication for a VCF Operations orchestrator Integration in VCF Automation for VM Apps
You configure an authentication provider for VCF Operations orchestrator so that you can integrate it with a VM Apps
organization in VCF Automation.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance as root.
2. Configure the authentication provider.
vracli vro authentication set -p tm -u ORGANIZATION_ADMINISTRATOR_ACCOUNT -hn https://FQDN_VCF_AUTOMATION
--tenant VM_APPS_ORGANIZATION_NAME
3. Redeploy VCF Operations orchestrator pods.
/opt/scripts/deploy.sh
The VCF Operations orchestrator instance is configured and associated with the VM Apps organization in VCF
Automation.
Note:
You can unregister the current authentication provider by running the
vracli vro authentication unregister
command from the command-line interface.
Step 2. Add a VCF Operations orchestrator Integration in VCF Automation for VM Apps
You integrate the VCF Operations orchestrator with your VM apps organization to use it for extensibility automation tasks.
1. Log in to the VM Apps organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Infrastructure > Integrations and click Add Integration.
3. Select Orchestration.
4. Enter a name for the VCF Operations orchestrator integration.
5. (Optional) Enter a description for the VCF Operations orchestrator integration.
6. Select your integration type.
– To integrate an external VCF Operations orchestrator, select User-deployed VCF Operations Orchestrator.
– To integrate an embedded VCF Operations orchestrator, select Embedded VCF Operations Orchestrator.
Note:
The embedded VCF Operations orchestrator instance is the default VCF Operations orchestrator instance that is
part of your VCF Automation deployment.
7. Click Add.
The VCF Automation integration is saved. The Integrations page opens.
8. On the Manage page, verify the resource consumption by the embedded VCF Operations orchestrator.
If there is an issue with the resource consumption, the instance appears as shut down.
9. Start data collection so that VCF Operations orchestrator workflows are synchronized with VCF Automation for your
organization.
10.(Optional) Add capability tags.
You use capability tags to distinguish between multiple VCF Operations orchestrator instances and to explicitly direct
calls from the VCF Automation to a specific integration. For more information on capability tags, see Using capability
tags in VCF Automation.
Broadcom 2540

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
11.To verify that the integration is configured and that the workflows are collected, select Orchestrator > Library >
Workflows.
VCF Operations orchestrator is ready to be used for extensibility automation tasks in the VM Apps organization. To access
VCF Operations orchestrator, select the Orchestrator tab in the VCF Automation for VM Apps organization. If you have
multiple VCF Operations orchestrator integrations, you use the drop-down to select the instance you want to work in.
Step 3. Define Authorization Restrictions
1. Log in to the VM Apps organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Infrastructure > Access Control > Users.
3. Select a user to whom you want to assign permissions to design and run workflows and actions for automation tasks in
VCF Operations orchestrator.
4. Click Edit.
5. Under Assigned roles, select the Orchestrator Workflow Designer role.
6. Click Save.
You assigned a VCF Operations orchestrator role to a user in your organization. This user can now create VCF
Operations orchestrator content for automation tasks in your organization.
Configure the VCF Operations orchestrator plug-in for VCF Automation for VM Apps
The VCF Operations orchestrator plug-in for VCF Automation for VM Apps is used to integrate VCF Operations
orchestrator with VCF Automation for VM Apps.
When upgrading from VMware Aria Automation 8.18.1, the plug-in works as expected without additional user action
required. However, if you are using a new deployment, you must manually configure the plug-in.
• For single-tenant environments, configure the plug-in by following the instructions in Broadcom knowledge base article
401216.
• For multi-tenant environments, configure the plug-in by following this procedure:
a. Configure vIDM as the identity provider for VCF Automation Provider Management by following the instructions in
Broadcom knowledge base article 401216.
b. Configure the organization hostname.
Note:
Verify that the hostnames include the tenant identifier. For each tenant that is not the default tenant, DNS records
must be configured. This is required as the behavior remains consistent with VMware Aria Automation 8.x where
the tenant identifier is included in the hostname for tenants as a subdomain. In VCF Automation 9.x, the tenant
should be exposed in the hostname.
# Example of multiple Soft Tenants
# CSP API will work
second-tenant.vcfa.com/csp/gateway/am/api/login?access_token
# CSP API will work
third-tenant.vcfa.com/csp/gateway/am/api/login?access_token
# This will attempt to log into the default tenant. The defaultLoginOrg should be configured in TM as
described in step 2 of the above section: Set Up Default Login Tenant

Broadcom 2541

Step 1. Create an Administrative Group for VCF Operations orchestrator
Users assigned to this group have administrative rights in the VCF Operations orchestrator instance.

3. Under Single Sign On, select Users and Groups.
4. Click the Groups tab.
5. To create a group, click Add.
6. Configure the group.
a. Enter a group name.
b. (Optional) Enter a description.
c. Select the group domain. For local vCenter groups, the group domain is usually .
vsphere.local
7. To add users to the group, search for existing users in the Add Members field, and add them to the group.
8. To create the group, click Add.
Step 2. Configure Authentication for a VCF Operations orchestrator Integration in vSphere
1. Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance as .
root
2. Configure the authentication provider.
Note:
When running the command, you are prompted for the password for
vracli vro authentication set
.
administrator@vsphere.local
vracli vro authentication set -p vsphere \
--hostname https://FQDN_SPHERE \
--username administrator@vsphere.local \

--admin-group Administrators \

command from the command-line interface.
unregister

To manage the inventory of a vSphere instance, you must register vCenter in VCF Operations orchestrator using the

VCF Operations orchestrator workflows to run, to schedule, and to answer user interaction directly from the vSphere
Client.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Orchestrator Plug-in for vSphere Web Client.

Configure VCF Operations Orchestrator for vSphere by Using VCF SSO
VCF Operations orchestrator can be integrated with vSphere by using VCF SSO as the authentication provider for core
infrastructure automation tasks. This scenario covers integrating VCF Operations orchestrator by using VCF SSO as the
authentication provider.
Before You Begin
• You have installed and configured VCF Operations orchestrator. For information on deploying VCF Operations
orchestrator, go to Deploying VCF Operations orchestrator.
• You have installed and configured VCF Operations.
• You have installed and configured a vSphere instance and applied VCF SSO through VCF Operations.
Step 1. Create an OAuth client in VCF Operations
This client is used to configure VCF SSO as authentication provider for the VCF Operations orchestrator instance.
1. Log in to VCF Operations as a VCF Operations administrator.
2. Navigate to Manage > Fleet Management > Identity & Access > VCF SSO Overview > Other Components > Add
Component.
3. Enter a name for the client.
4. Select an identity broker.
5. Leave the redirect URL and post-log out redirect URLs blank.
6. Click Generate OIDC Client.
7. Click Save.
Now you have an OIDC client to use for your VCF Operations orchestrator configuration.
Step 2. Configure VCF SSO as Authentication Provider for VCF Operations orchestrator
You use above OIDC client to configure VCF Operations orchestrator with enough privileges in VCF SSO to request and
renew VCF SSO OAuth tokens.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance as .
root
2. Configure the authentication provider.
vracli vro authentication set -p vidb \
--hostname https://FQDN_IDENTITY_BROKER/acs/t/CUSTOMER \
--client-id 'CLIENT_ID_OF_ABOVE_OIDC_CLIENT' \
--client-secret 'CLIENT_SECRET_OF_ABOVE_OIDC_CLIENT' \
--admin-group O11N_ADMIN_GROUP@DOMAIN
3. Verify the configuration of the authentication provider and check the property values.
vracli vro authentication
4. Redeploy the VCF Operations orchestrator pods.
/opt/scripts/deploy.sh
The VCF Operations orchestrator instance is configured with the same VCF SSO as the vSphere instance you want to
integrate to.
Note:
You can unregister the current authentication provider by running the
vracli vro authentication unregister
command from the command-line interface.
Broadcom 2543

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Step 3. Configure VCF Operations orchestrator plug-ins
To manage the inventory of a vSphere instance, you must register vCenter in VCF Operations orchestrator using the
vCenter plug-in. In addition, the VCF Operations orchestrator plug-in for the vSphere client allows you to directly select
VCF Operations orchestrator workflows to run, to schedule, and to answer user interaction directly from the vSphere
Client.
1. Register vCenter using the vCenter plug-in. See Configuring the vCenter Server Plug-In in VCF Operations
Orchestrator.
2. Configure the VCF Operations orchestrator plug-in for the vSphere client. See Configure the VMware Cloud
Foundation Operations orchestrator Plug-in for vSphere Web Client.
3. Add custom actions on the vCenter inventory objects. See Create a context action.
Configure VCF Operations Orchestrator for VCF Operations
You can integrate VCF Operations orchestrator with VCF Operations by installing the relevant management pack.
Before You Begin
• Verify that your VCF Operations orchestrator instance is authenticated with vSphere or VCF SSO.
Integrating VCF Operations orchestrator by Using a Management Pack
To integrate VCF Operations orchestrator, you must install the relevant management pack in VCF Operations.
Management packs are hosted on the VCF Solutions Catalog (formerly VMware Marketplace) and can either be
downloaded as PAK files or applied directly from Marketplace tab in VCF Operations.
For more information on adding and managing integrations in VCF Operations, go to Adding and Managing Management
Packs. For more information on using the VCF Operations orchestrator management pack, see Configuring Automation
Orchestrator.
Configure a VCF Operations Orchestrator Cluster
You can configure your new VCF Operations orchestrator deployment to run in high availability by deploying three nodes
and connecting them as a cluster.
• Download and deploy three standalone VCF Operations orchestrator instances.
Note:
A clustered VCF Operations orchestrator environment must consist of three nodes.
• Configure a load balancer server to direct the traffic to the VCF Operations orchestrator nodes.
A VCF Operations orchestrator cluster consists of three VCF Operations orchestrator instances.
To create a VCF Operations orchestrator cluster, you must select one VCF Operations orchestrator instance to be the
primary node of the cluster. After configuring the primary node, you join the secondary nodes to it.
The VCF Operations orchestrator cluster you create is pre-configured with automatic failover.
Note:
Failure of the automatic failover can lead to loss of data.
1. Configure the primary node.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator primary node over SSH as root.
b) To configure the cluster load balancer server, run the load_balancer_FQDN
vracli load-balancer set
command.
c) Configure the authentication provider by running the command.
vracli vro authentication set
Optionally, you can add the FQDN address of the load balancer server by adding the parameter to the
--fqdn
command.
vracli authentication set
Broadcom 2544

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Join secondary nodes to primary node.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator secondary node over SSH as root.
b) To join the secondary node to the primary node, run the
vracli cluster join
primary_node_hostname_or_IP command.
c) Enter the root password of the primary node.
d) Repeat the procedure for the other secondary node.
3. Optional: If your primary node uses a custom certificate, you must either set the certificate in the appliance or generate
a new certificate. For more information, go to Generate a custom TLS certificate for VCF Operations orchestrator.
Note:
The file containing the certificate chain must be PEM-encoded.
4. Finish the cluster deployment.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator primary node over SSH as root.
b) To confirm that all nodes are in a ready state, run the command.
kubectl -n prelude get nodes
c) Run the script and wait for the deployment to finish.
/opt/scripts/deploy.sh
You have created a VCF Operations orchestrator cluster. After you create the cluster, you can access your VCF
Operations orchestrator environment only from the FQDN address of your load balancer server.
Note:
You cannot update the configuration of a cluster node if it has a different root password from the password that
is used by the load balancer. To edit the configuration of this node, remove it from the load balancer, edit the
configuration, and add the node back to the load balancer.
To monitor the state of the VCF Operations orchestrator cluster, log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator client and
navigate to the System tab of the dashboard.
Note:
If you are unable to access VCF Operations orchestrator, you can also monitor the states of your cluster nodes
by running the command from the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance
kubectl get pods -n prelude
command line.
To check the health status of your load balancer, navigate to <load_balancer_FQDN>
https:// /vco/api/
. The health check port is 8008.
healthstatus
Deploy VCF Operations HCX
VCF Operations HCX is a workload mobility platform that simplifies workload migration across data centers. VCF
Operations HCX is an optional component that you can deploy on a VCF Instance domain.
• Verify that the VCF Operations HCX deployment binaries are downloaded to software depot in the VCF Instance where
you want to deploy. See Download Binaries to Software Depot.
• Verify that the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for VCF Operations HCX is resolvable over DNS. The IP address
to which the FQDN resolves must not be already used.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle and select the VCF Instance and domain.
3. On the Component Versions tab, click Manage Components.
4. On the VCF Operations HCX card, click Install to start the installation wizard.
a) On General, select the VCF Operations HCX version to install. Only versions that are compatible with the domain
components are listed.
b) On Deployment Settings, provide the admin and root user passwords for VCF Operations HCX.
• Password length must be greater than 12 characters.
Broadcom 2545

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Password cannot be a palindrome.
• Password must have at least 5 different characters.
• Password must have 1 lower case, 1 upper case, 1 number, 1 special character.
c) Validations check the VCF Operations HCX version compatibility, the FQDN, and the root and admin passwords.
d) On the Summary page, review the VCF Operations HCX deployment configuration.
e) Review the next steps and click Finish.
When the installation wizard completes, the deployment begins.
5. To monitor the progress of the deployment, navigate to Build > Tasks, select the VCF Instance, and click the VCF
Operations HCX deployment task.
On the subtask list that appears, verify the status of each subtask. If any binary download validations fail, you can use
binary management to reinstall the binaries.
VCF Operations HCX is deployed in the same cluster as the target vCenter instance and is automatically configured with
the target NSX and vCenter instances.
After a successful installation, go to the Software Versions tab of the domain. In the Domain Management Components
table, verify that the current version and target version of VCF Operations HCX match.
Import Existing VCF Operations HCX to a VCF Domain
Instead of deploying a new VCF Operations HCX you can import an existing instance for VCF Operations HCX version
9.1 or later. The import version must also be the same or earlier than the version of SDDC Manager.
• Verify that you have the FQDN and admin user password of your existing HCX appliance.
• Verify that you have the IPv4 address and SSL certificate thumbprint, so that you can confirm automatically retrieved
information when HCX Manager is imported into the VCF Domain.
• Verify that the IP address and Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for VCF Operations HCX are resolvable over
DNS.
• Verify that the existing VCF Operations HCX is located either in the management vCenter instance or in the domain
where you plan to import it.
• Verify that you have a valid certificate with Common Names (CN) and Subject Alternative Names (SAN).
Perform the following steps to import VCF Operations HCX to an existing management or workload domain.
Note:
If the VCF Operations HCX admin user password is not compliant with the password policy, you must change the
password in VCF Operations HCX .
After the import operation completes, any custom backup server that is configured in the VCF Operations HCX
instance is overwritten by the backup server settings that are defined in SDDC Manager.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle and select the VCF Instance and domain.
3. On the Component Versions tab, click Manage Components.
4. On the VCF Operations HCX card, click Install.
a) On the General page, select Import an already configured instance.
b) On the Import Settings page, provide the details of your existing VCF Operations HCX :
• Enter the FQDN for VCF Operations HCX .
• Confirm the displayed IP address and SSL thumbprint.
• Enter the admin user password for VCF Operations HCX
c) On the Validations page, verify that there are no validation errors.
Validations include password checks, compatibility checks, and checks for vCenter and NSX configurations, and
reachability.
Broadcom 2546

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
d) On the Summary page, review the VCF Operations HCX import configuration.
e) Review the next step and click Finish.
When the installation wizard completes, the import procedure begins. The procedure for import includes:
• Creation and update of necessary service accounts for HCX to vCenter, SDDC Manager to HCX and HCX to NSX
communications.
• If VCF Operations HCX has a valid self-signed certificate, the certificate is replaced with a new one that is issued
by the Management vCenter VMCA.
Note:
If VCF Operations HCX is assigned a CA signed certificate, VCF Operations HCX does not replace the certificate.
After a successful import, the VCF Operations HCX services are restarted.
5. Optional: To monitor the progress of the import procedure, navigate to Build > Tasks, select the VCF instance, and
click the VCF Operations HCX import task.
On the subtask list that appears, verify the status of each subtask.
After a successful import, go to the Software Versions tab of the domain. In the Domain Management Components
table, verify that the current version and target version of VCF Operations HCX match.
Configuring Advanced Architectures for VCF Operations
VCF Operations supports architectures that are not automated by VCF Installer. You must perform a manual configuration
to achieve the required states.
Configure VCF Operations Cluster for Continuous Availability
VCF Installer supports the deployment of VCF Operations in either simple mode or high availability mode during the initial
VCF deployment. After the initial deployment, the VCF Operations cluster can be converted to a continuous availability
architecture.
Identify three separate fault domains for the installation of the VCF Operations primary node and data nodes, the VCF
Operations primary replica node and data nodes, and the witness node, respectively. The fault domains can be located
in either a different workload domain, a separate availability zone, or a different region. In a continuous availability
architecture, there must be at least one primary node and one data node within the primary fault domain. Additionally, the
replica fault domain should have the same number of nodes as the primary fault domain, and there should be one witness
node in the witness fault domain. The VCF Operations nodes in the primary fault domain, the VCF Operations nodes in
the replica fault domain, and the witness node in the witness fault domain must be able to communicate over the routable
network, despite being in separate fault domains. Consult the VCF Operations sizing guidelines for the sizing and network
latency requirements between the three distinct fault domains.
1. Deploy VCF Operations using VCF Installer in either Simple mode or High Availability mode within the fault domain
designated for the primary node.
2. Deploy the witness node in the fault domain designated for it, by following these steps:
a) Download the VCF Operations ova file from the Broadcom support portal to your local computer. Alternatively, you
can deploy the OVA directly from vCenter.
b) If you have downloaded the OVA to your local computer, upload the VCF Operations ova file to the vCenter, in the
fault domain designated for the witness node.
c) Deploy the VCF Operations OVF template and select Witness as the configuration for deployment.
d) Note down the IP address and the hostname or the FQDN of the witness node.
e) Log in to the VCF Operations administrator interface in the primary fault domain. The administrator interface can be
accessed from .
https://primary-node-name-or-ip-address/admin
f) In the VCF Operations administrator interface, click the + icon in the Nodes in the VCF Operations Cluster
section, to add the witness node. The Add new nodes to cluster wizard opens.
g) Add the newly deployed witness node to the VCF Operations cluster. Enter the Node Name, Node Address
inputs. In the Current Cluster Role option, select Witness Node from the drop-down list. Use the IP address
Broadcom 2547

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
and hostname or the FQDN of the witness node, as recorded in the previous steps. Click SAVE and then after the
thumbprint of the node is displayed, click NEXT.
h) A dialog box with the post-expansion certificate management message is displayed. Select the checkbox to accept
the message, and click NEXT.
i) In the Primary Password step, enter the password of the primary node to add nodes to the cluster. Click FINISH.
The cluster initialization begins.
j) After the cluster initialization completes, click FINISH ADDING NEW NODE(S) in the Cluster Status card. Click OK
in the confirmation dialog box which appears.
3. If VCF Operations was deployed in a High Availability architecture during the initial setup, follow the steps below:
a) Deactivate High Availability in the VCF Operations administrator console

b) The primary replica cluster node is converted into a standard data node within the cluster, which can then be
removed if an extra data node is not needed. The remaining nodes in the cluster maintain their current roles.
c) Ensure that the VCF Operations cluster has at-least one primary node and one data node in the primary fault
domain. Consult the VCF Operations sizing guidelines for the maximum number of data nodes that can be added
in the primary fault domain. Note that the number of VCF Operations nodes in the primary fault domain and the
replica fault domain must be equal.
4. The replica fault domain must contain the same number of data nodes as the primary fault domain to ensure data

a) If the designated replica fault domain is managed by the VCF Operations in the primary fault domain, then use
Add Node capability in Lifecycle, within VCF Operations to add the same number of VCF Operations nodes in
the replica fault domain as in the primary fault domain. You can add replica nodes and data nodes using Lifecycle.
Witness nodes can only be added from vCenter.

domain, ensuring that the selected size matches that of the nodes deployed in the primary fault domain.
d) Note down the IP address and the hostname of the VCF Operations nodes deployed in the replica fault domain.

accessed from .

section, to add the node. The Add new nodes to cluster wizard opens.

Current Cluster Role option, select Data Node from the drop-down list. Use the IP address and hostname or the

SAVE and then after the thumbprint of the node is displayed, click NEXT.

the message, and click NEXT.
i) In the Primary Password step, enter the password of the data node to add nodes to the cluster. Click FINISH. The
cluster initialization begins.
5. Click Activate CA in the VCF Operations admin UI.
6. The Continuous Availability wizard opens. The witness node exists outside the fault domains. The primary node is
already assigned to Fault Domain. Perform the following steps:
a) To pair with the VCF Operations nodes in the primary fault domain, move the VCF Operations data nodes deployed
in the replica fault domain to Fault Domain.
b) Ensure an even distribution of VCF Operations nodes between the primary and replica fault domains to enable
