vSAN Licensing Overview
When you purchase VCF, in addition to your VMware Cloud Foundation (cores) license you receive an equivalent
vSAN license for tebibytes (TiBs) of total raw physical storage. You can also purchase additional storage as a separate
subscription.
• You can assign a vSAN TiB license to a single vCenter instance or multiple vCenter instances.
• vSAN license usage is based on the storage capacity in the vSAN clusters. vSAN pools the capacity of the
subscriptions that you purchased and shares the allocated capacity between multiple vSAN clusters using the vSAN
TiB license.
• You do not need a separate license or subscription for vSAN witness appliances. You can deploy as many vSAN
witness appliances as required. vSAN witness appliances cannot be used to run workloads not related to vSAN
witness.
• Starting with VCF 9.1, you can assign a vSAN TiB license directly to a cluster and override the vCenter license that is
automatically assigned to the cluster. For more information about override licenses, see What is an Override License.
vSAN TiB License
When you assign a vSAN TiB license to vCenter, the vSAN license is automatically applied to all the vSAN clusters that
are managed by the vCenter. To calculate the capacity that you need for your vSAN environment, you must determine the
quantity of TiB licenses required for the total physical device capacity in TiBs on all the ESX hosts in each vSAN cluster.
The vSAN clusters reflect the total raw storage capacity available. For more information about calculating the license
capacity that you need for your environment, see Broadcom knowledge base article 95927.
If you have a bare metal host as a vSAN witness, perform the following:
1. Log in to the witness host.
2. Run the following command:
esxcli vsan witness license set --enable true
3. Reboot the witness host.
vSAN License Capacity in VMware Cloud Foundation
If you have a vSAN cluster with 3 ESX hosts, 1 CPU per host, and each host has 6 physical cores per CPU, you must
purchase the subscription capacity of 16 cores per CPU as it is the required minimum license capacity. For each VCF
cores that you purchase, you receive 1 TiB of vSAN capacity. With a total of 48 (3 * 1 * 16) physical cores per VCF cluster,
you receive 48 TiB vSAN capacity. Similarly, with a total of 144 (3 * 2 * 24) physical cores per VCF cluster, you receive
144 TiB vSAN capacity.

vSAN License Capacity in VMware vSphere Foundation
VMware vSphere Foundation license includes an entitlement of 0.25 tebibyte (TiB) of vSAN raw capacity per licensed
core. To calculate the capacity that you need for your vSAN environment, you need to determine the total number of
licensed CPU cores for each CPU on all the ESX hosts in your environment.
For example, consider a vSAN cluster with 3 ESX hosts, 1 CPU per host, and each host has 8 physical cores per CPU.
You must purchase a vSphere Foundation license with the subscription capacity of 16 cores per CPU because it is the
required minimum license capacity. With a total of 48 licensed cores (3 hosts * 1 CPU * 16 minimum licensed cores per
CPU) , you receive 12 TiBs of included capacity (0.25 TiB *48 licensed cores). Similarly, With a total of 128 licensed cores
(4 hosts * 2 CPUs * 16 minimum licensed cores per CPU), you receive 32 TiBs of capacity.

The 0.25 TiB of vSAN capacity per licensed core pools with any vSAN capacity from other add-ons or VCF purchases.
You can use this capacity to license the vSAN clusters in their vCenter instances, regardless of whether the capacity is
more or less than 0.25 TiB per core.
License Server Overview
A license server is added to a VCF Operations instance to store the licenses you want to assign from this VCF
Operations instance. You must add at least one license server to each VCF Operations instance that you use for license
management.
Licenses for VCF infrastructure and management components are stored on a dedicated license server appliance. The
license server is a protected repository within your environment to keep your licensing data.
A license server is deployed during new VCF or vSphere Foundation deployments, and during upgrades to version 9.1
and later.
You must add at least one license server to each VCF Operations instance that you use for license management. Most
VCF Operations instances only need one license server. In some cases you might need additional license servers. If you
have a vCenter instance that does not have reliable connectivity to your data center, the connectivity latency exceeds 300
ms, you can deploy a license server in that vCenter instance to avoid licensing-related service interruptions. For example,
if you have an edge site with limited connectivity to your management domain, you might not be able to license new hosts
added to your edge site.
Each license server must have a unique license allocation. There must be a connection between the license server and
VCF Operations to complete a license refresh at least once every 180 days. To assign a license to an ESX host, the
vCenter instance that the host is added to must be able to connect to the license server.
You can use a single license server to license your entire fleet, but you cannot share a license server between fleets.
After you add a license server to VCF Operations, you must add licenses to the license server to be able to license your
vCenter systems and other assets in your environment.
License Server Models
• Single license server model. This model provides a single, unified repository for the entire fleet. It is suitable for
deployments where reduced operational overhead is prioritized.
Broadcom 2678

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Multi license server model: This model supports environments that require administrative division for multi-tenancy or
geographic distribution. It ensures local license availability for regional sites that lack reliable connectivity to the central
management domain.
Sizing Requirements and Scale
Sizing requirements:
• 2 vCPUs
• 4-GB RAM
• 8-GB Disk
Scale: 250,000 assets
All licensed vCenter instances, hosts, and vSAN clusters are assets.
Monitoring License Server Health
You can monitor the health of a license server in VCF Operations, on the details page of the specific license server.
For detailed monitoring information, you can view the License Server Health dashboards in VCF Operations. For more
information about using VCF Operations health monitoring dashboards, see Using Predefined Dashboards for Quick
Insights.
License Server Networking
The license server operates within a strictly defined network perimeter and does not communicate with the Internet. There
are no external network requirements for the license server. To ensure reliable operations, the network path must support
a maximum latency of 300 ms.

Internal Network Requirements
For versions 9.1.0.0 and 9.1.0.0100, the license server uses an internal communications network in the 172.16.0.0/12 and
172.17.0.0/16 ranges. To avoid conflicts and allow for normal work of the license server, do not deploy the license server
on the 172.16.0.0/12 network. Also do not configure the license server to use a gateway that advertises a routable path of
172.17.0.0/16.

Starting with version 9.1.0.0200, the license server works with a broader range of IP addresses for the internal
communication. The limitations that are listed above no longer apply.
License Server IPv6 Support
Starting with version 9.1.1, the license server supports IPv6 networking that uses static addressing, or DHCPv6/SLAAC.
The method for configuring IPv6 is different depending on your scenario.
1. New deployment by using VCF Installer. VCF Installer only deploys the license server with IPv4. To configure IPv6 on
the license server, use the vSphere Client. For more information, see Configure IPv6 on a License Server.
2. New deployment by using an OVA file. During the deployment, you can configure the license server for IPv4-only,
IPv6-only, or dual-stack networking. For more information, see Deploy a License Server Version 9.1.1.
3. License servers patched to version 9.1.1. You cannot activate IPv6 on the license server. To use IPv6, you must
deploy a new license server of version 9.1.1 and transfer your licenses to it. For more information, see Deploy a
License Server Version 9.1.1, Register an Additional License Server with the VCF Business Services Console, and
Transfer Licenses After a VCF Operations Upgrade from Version 9.0.x.
Configure IPv6 on a License Server
Starting with version 9.1.1, the license server supports IPv6 networking. You can select a dynamic address allocation
DHCPv6/SLAAC, or you can manually assign a static IPv6 address, prefix length, and default gateway.
• Required privileges: VApp.ApplicationConfig and VApp.InstanceConfig on the license server virtual machine.
• Power off the license server virtual machine.
Note:
If you update a license server from version 9.1.0 to version 9.1.1, you cannot configure IPv6 on that license server
instance. To utilize IPv6 networking, you must deploy a new license server instance of version 9.1.1 and transfer
your licenses to it. For more information, see Deploy a License Server Version 9.1.1, Register an Additional
License Server with the VCF Business Services Console, and Transfer Licenses After a VCF Operations Upgrade
from Version 9.0.x.
The license server supports two IPv6 configuration modes:
• Static. You manually configure the default gateway, prefix length, and IP address.
• DHCP/SLAAC. The default gateway, prefix length, and IP address are configured automatically.
1. Log in to the vSphere Client, and navigate to the license server virtual machine.
2. Select the virtual machine, and click the Configure tab.
3. Under Settings, select vApp Options.
4. Navigate to the Properties section.
5. Select the IPv6 assignment method, and configure the required property values.
• For dynamic addressing, select DHCP/Slaac. The license server automatically obtains its IPv6 address, prefix
length, and default gateway.
• For static addressing, select static. You must manually configure the static network details.

and click OK.

License Server Security
A license server is an inherently sensitive component of any VMware Cloud Foundation deployment. The license server is
hardened and configured to the strictest STIG requirements.
The license server retains a record of licenses and assets to which a license is assigned. The license server retains the
metadata and license data applicable to those licenses and assets and does not retain other data. The license server
does not scan your environment.
The license server communicates through the port and protocols that are listed at VMware Ports and Protocols. All other
inbound and outbound traffic can be blocked.
VCF Operations handles all other licensing-related communication. For example, in connected mode, VCF Operations
periodically communicates aggregated license usage data to Broadcom. In disconnected mode, you must manually
submit that data. For more information, see Updating Licenses and Viewing the License Usage File.
The license server uses the time set on the host which contains the license server virtual machine. To avoid license
assignment failure, ensure that the time on the ESX host which contains the license server virtual machine is
synchronized with the time set on the other VCF components.
The license server does not support SSH connections, and you cannot enable SSH on the license server. Root or other
user accounts are not present on the license server.
License Server Downtime Impact
If the license server is unavailable, you cannot assign licenses, generate license usage reports, or import license files.
The license server does not need to be always online. There is no immediate workload or management operations impact
if the license server becomes unreachable by VCF Operations or vCenter instances. To minimize potential downtime,
ensure that the cluster which contains the license server virtual machine is configured with vSphere High Availability.
While the license server is unavailable to VCF Operations, the following operations are impacted:
• Assigning licenses to new vCenter instances: You can add new vCenter instances in evaluation mode. They are fully
operational during the evaluation period.
Broadcom 2682

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Generating license usage reports: Updated license usage reports cannot be generated until connectivity to the license
server is restored. If VCF Operations is registered in connected mode, the daily automated license usage reports
cannot be generated. After the 180-day update period, the licenses expire.
• Importing license files: You cannot add licenses to the inventory. Prior license usage reports cannot be confirmed and
the license update period cannot be refreshed.
While the license server is unavailable to vCenter , when you add new hosts to the vCenter instance, the hosts cannot be
licensed. You can add new ESX hosts in evaluation mode. They are fully operational during the evaluation period.
While the license server is unavailable to vCenter , when you add new hosts and enable vSAN clusters in the vCenter
instance, the hosts and vSAN clusters cannot be licensed. You can add new ESX hosts and vSAN clusters in evaluation
mode. They are fully operational during the evaluation period.
License Server Recovery
A license server outage does not impact running workloads or management operations until your license usage report due
date expires or a new license assignment is required. Because license assignment data is restored by VCF Operations,
you do not need to perform manual backups or repairs on license servers. If a failure occurs, you can deploy, register, and
transfer your licenses to a new license server. VCF Operations restores all previous license assignment data to the new
license server instance.
Due to integrated security controls, you cannot restore a license server from a backup or a snapshot, and you cannot
clone the license server. To restore the license server and its data:
1. Deploy a new license server appliance and register it with the VCF Business Services console. For more information,
see Deploy a License Server Version 9.1.0.
2. In the VCF Business Services console, delete the unavailable license server registration. For more information, see
Delete a License Server.
3. In the VCF Business Services console, add the licenses that were added to the deleted license server to the newly
deployed license server.
Note:
After you import the license file in VCF Operations, the licenses are automatically reassigned to the same assets
that they were assigned to before you deleted the license server.
Registering VCF Operations and a License Server with the VCF
Business Services Console
You access and manage the licenses for your environment by using VCF Operations, and the VCF Business Services
console. You must register the VCF Operations instance and a license server with the VCF Business Services console.
You must install a VCF Operations instance version 9.1 to manage licenses for VCF components of version 9.1. If you
want to access and manage your 9.1 licenses, and you already have an earlier version of VCF Operations installed, you
must upgrade the instance to version 9.1.
A license server is automatically deployed as part of the installation and upgrade of VCF. Each license server contains
licenses for a specific VCF Operations instance. You can add licenses for different products in the same license server,
and you can add as many licenses to a license server as you need. You can add licenses to the license server at any time
after the initial registration process. For more information, see Add a License to VCF Operations and License Server.
Note:
After the deployment of the license server as part of an upgrade from 9.0.x to 9.1, your licenses are transferred
from the VCF Operations instance to the license server.
If your VCF Operationsinstance is in connected mode, the license server is automatically registered and licenses
are automatically transferred to the license server.
Broadcom 2683

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If your VCF Operationsinstance is in disconnected mode, you must register the license server with the VCF
Business Services console. Licenses are then automatically transferred from VCF Operations to the license
server. For more information, see Transfer Licenses After a VCF Operations Upgrade from Version 9.0.x.
You need at least one license server and a VCF Operations instance to license your environment. If you need another
license server, you can download and install a license server manually. For more information, see Deploy a License
Server Version 9.1.0.
After you deploy or upgrade your VCF Operations instance to version 9.1, it works in evaluation mode for up to 90 days.
During that period you must register VCF Operations and the license server in the VCF Business Services console, and
you must license your environment.
Note:
If you want to use a VCF Operations instance only for monitoring your assets, and not for license management,
you do not need to register it with the VCF Business Services console. A VCF Operations instance that you use
only for monitoring purposes is automatically licensed with the primary license assigned to the vCenter instances
of version 9.0 or 9.1 that are added to the VCF Operations instance. These vCenter instances must be licensed
by a different VCF Operations instance.
You can use specific VCF Operations capabilities based on the primary license that is assigned to each vCenter.
Product VCF Operations Capabilities
VMware Cloud Foundation (includes VCF Edge) License Management, Monitoring, Fleet Management
vSphere Foundation License management, Monitoring
One VCF Operations instance can manage a mix of different license types and licenses for different products. For
example, you can manage both VCF and VMware Foundation primary licenses in the same VCF Operations instance, and
add-on licenses for different product components.
You can choose whether to register your VCF Operations instance in connected or disconnected mode.
• In disconnected mode, to register VCF Operations, you must manually transfer files between the VCF Operations
instance and the VCF Business Services console. After the registration, you must manually transfer files to report
license usage, and to update licenses.
• In connected mode, VCF Operations registration does not require manual transfer of files, the registration is performed
by using an activation code. After the registration, usage reporting is automated, and the update of licenses is
simplified.
CAUTION:
To use VCF Operations for licensing, verify that the Virtual Management Infrastructure (VIM) adapter is running.
By default the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of VCF Operations is prepopulated as a display name when you start
the registration process in the VCF Business Services console. The FQDN is only saved if you do not enter another
display name. If you change the FQDN to another display name, the connectivity between VCF Operations and the VCF
Business Services console is not impacted. You can change the display name at any time after the registration.
If you do not want to include the FQDN of the VCF Operations instance or the hostname of the license server in the
registration details, you can use the following API before you start the registration process:
PUT {VCF_Ops_URI}/suite-api/api/deployment/config/globalsettings/GENERATE_DEFAULT_LICENSE_MANAGER_ASSET_NAME/
false

combination of query string parameters and API parameters. If your VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode,
you must manually download the registration information as a JSON Web Signed (JWS) file. The information provided to
Broadcom for registration is equivalent between connected and disconnected mode, but sent in different formats.

Register VCF Operations and Your License Server in Connected Mode
You must register the VCF Operations instance that you want to use for license management and at least one license
server with the VCF Business Services console. If your environment is connected to the Internet, you can register your
VCF Operations instance in connected mode. Connected mode provides a faster and simplified registration process, and
makes updating your licenses easier. Connected mode is recommended for anyone who has an Internet connection.
• Verify that you have a valid subscription for VCF or vSphere Foundation.
• Verify that your VCF Operations instance is connected to the Internet. If you must configure an Internet proxy,
configure the proxy in VCF Operations, under Global Settings > Network Settings.
• Verify that you have a Broadcom Support Portal role or a VCF Business Services console role with privileges to
register the VCF Operations instance. For more information about the role mappings, see Access Management.
In connected mode, the update of licenses can be fully automated or semi-automated. For more information, see Change
License Updates Mode.
Note:
By default the FQDN of VCF Operations is prepopulated as a display name when you start the registration
process in the VCF Business Services console. The FQDN is only saved if you do not enter another display
name. If you change the FQDN with another display name, the connectivity between VCF Operations and
the VCF Business Services console is not impacted. You can change the display name at any time after the
registration.
If you do not want to include the FQDN in the registration details, you can use the following VCF Operations API
before you start the registration process:
PUT {VCF_Ops_URI}/suite-api/api/deployment/config/globalsettings/
GENERATE_DEFAULT_LICENSE_MANAGER_ASSET_NAME/false

Switch from Connected to Disconnected Mode
You can switch from connected to disconnected mode at any time. In disconnected mode, you must manually submit
license usage reports and update your licenses.

Registration.

The VCF Operations Registration page appears.
4. On the Registration Details tab, next to Reporting Mode, click Switch to Disconnected.
5. In the Switch Reporting Mode dialog box, click Switch to Disconnected.
Your VCF Operations instance operates in disconnected mode. You must manually report license usage, and then upload
license files in VCF Operations. For more information about reporting license usage and updating your licenses, see
Report License Usage and Update Licenses in Disconnected Mode.
Switch from Disconnected to Connected Mode
You can switch from disconnected to connected mode at any time. In connected mode, license usage reports are
submitted automatically, and the update of licenses is easier.
To switch from disconnected to connected mode, verify that your environment is connected to the Internet.
If your VCF Operations instance operates in disconnected mode for more than 180 days, switching from disconnected to
connected connection might fail, and you must generate a new activation code. For information on how to generate a new
activation code, see Register VCF Operations and Your License Server in Connected Mode.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.

Registration.

The VCF Operations Registration page appears.
4. On the Registration Details tab, next to Reporting Mode, click Switch to Connected.
5. In the Switch Reporting Mode dialog box, click Switch to Connected.
Your VCF Operations instance operates in connected mode. License usage is reported automatically. You must update
your licenses on regular intervals. For more information about updating your licenses, see Update Licenses in Connected
Mode.

Managing Licenses in the VCF Business Services Console
Starting with version 9.0, you have one default license per product. You can split the default license into as many licenses
as you need within your total purchased capacity. When you delete a split license, or reduce its capacity, the capacity is
added back to the capacity of the default license. You can rename a license at any time.
User Roles Required for License Management
You must have the required permissions to manage licenses in the VCF Business Services console. For more information
about the roles in the VCF Business Services console, see Access Management.
Split Default Licenses
You can split default licenses into as many licenses as you need. You can allocate part of the default license capacity to
each of the new licenses that you create as a result of the split.
When you create a split license, the capacity you add to it is extracted from the available capacity in the default license.
If the available capacity in the default license is less than the capacity that you want to add to the new split license, you
can reduce the capacity of other split licenses. The capacity that you deduct from split licenses is added back as available
capacity in the default license.
1. In the VCF Business Services console, navigate to Licensing > Licenses.
2. Click the Version 9+ tab.
3. Click Manage Licenses (Split/Merge).
The Manage Licenses wizard appears.
4. From the drop-down menu, select a product for which you want to split the default license.
The default license and all previous split licenses for this product appears.
5. Click Create.
A new line for a split license appears in the table.
6. In the Name column, enter a name for the license.
7. In the New Capacitycolumn, enter the amount of capacity you want to allocate to the new license.
You cannot allocate a higher amount of capacity than what is available in the default license.
8. To create more split licenses, repeat steps 5 through 7.
9. Click Next.
10.On the Summary page, review your changes, and click Finish.
Your newly created license appears in the list of licenses in the VCF Business Services console.
If your default license is added to a VCF Operations instance, you must update the licenses in that VCF Operations
instance after the split. For more information about updating your licenses, see Updating Licenses and Viewing the
License Usage File.
To rename the license, click the vertical ellipsis next to the license, and select Rename.
Merging Licenses
When you delete a split license, or reduce its capacity, the capacity you remove from the split license is merged back into
the default license.
• For more information about deleting a license, see Delete a License.
• For more information about removing license capacity from a split license, see Change License Capacity.
Broadcom 2693

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Change License Capacity
You can change the license capacity of split licenses as many times as you need. You can allocate more capacity or
remove some of the capacity of the split licenses at any time. Any change in the capacity allocated to split licenses affects
the default license.
The capacity that you add to split licenses is extracted from the capacity of the default license. The capacity you remove
from split licenses is added back to the default license. You cannot add more capacity to a split license than the capacity
available in the default license. If you need more capacity than what is available in the default license, you must free up
capacity from the other split licenses which belong to the same product type, or you must purchase more capacity.
You cannot reduce the capacity of a license below the quantity of the license that is currently used. If you try to reduce
the capacity of an assigned license below the used capacity, the operation fails. For example, if you have a license with
capacity of 250 cores, and it is assigned to a vCenter instance, which has 4 ESX hosts added to it, each using 50 cores of
license capacity, you cannot reduce the capacity of the license to less than 200 cores.
Note:
If at a certain point the used capacity of a license is greater than the capacity allocated to the license, you must
allocate more capacity to that license. Until you add more capacity, you cannot assign the over used license to
additional vCenter instances. If a vCenter instance is licensed by a license that is over used, you can only add
new ESX hosts if they are in evaluation mode.
1. In the VCF Business Services console, navigate to Licensing > Licenses.
2. Click the vertical ellipsis next to the split license, and select Change Capacity.
3. In the New Capacitycolumn, enter the new amount of allocated capacity.
For example, if your license has 150 cores of allocated capacity, and you want to add 50 cores, you add 200 in the
New Capacity column.
You cannot assign more capacity than what is available in the default license.
4. Click Next.
5. On the Summary page, review your changes, and click Finish.
The new capacity of the modified license and the default license appear in the list of licenses.

Instance
To remove a license from a license server and not see it in the VCF Operations instance to which the license server is
added, the license must not be assigned to any vCenter instance in your environment.

• If your VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode, report license usage. For more information, see Report
License Usage and Update Licenses in Disconnected Mode.
To complete the license removal, you must update your licenses in VCF Operations. After you remove the license from
VCF Operations, you can add the license to another VCF Operations instance and license server, or you can delete it.
1. Log in to the VCF Business Services console by using your Broadcom Support Portal credentials.
2. Select the Site ID to which you want to register this instance, and click Next.
If you have only one site, it is selected by default.
3. Next to the license you want to remove, click the vertical ellipsis, and click Remove License from License Server.
A dialog box appears.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Click Remove.
5. If your VCF Operations registration is in connected mode, update your licenses in the VCF Operations instance:
a) In the VCF Operations instance, navigate to Licensing > Licenses & Registration.
b) Click Update Licenses.
6. If your VCF Operations registration is in disconnected mode, manually upload the license file in VCF Operations:

Delete a License
You can delete a split license from the VCF Business Services console console if you no longer need it. You cannot delete
a split license if some of its capacity is assigned to a vCenter instance or another asset.
• Verify that the license is not assigned to a vCenter instance or another asset.
• Verify that the license is not added to a license server. For information on how to remove a license from a license
server, see Remove a License from a License Server and the Respective VCF Operations Instance.
1. In the VCF Business Services console, navigate to Licensing > Licenses.
2. Next to the split license, click the vertical ellipsis, and click Delete.
3. In the dialog box which appears, click Delete.
The license is deleted and its capacity is merged with the default license capacity. In connected mode, after the new
license file is automatically imported in the VCF Operations instance, the license that you deleted from the VCF Business
Services console is automatically deleted from VCF Operations. In disconnected mode, you must manually download
the license file from the VCF Business Services console and import it in VCF Operations. The license is then deleted
automatically from VCF Operations.

After you add licenses to your license server, you can assign them to the vCenter instances.

Assign a Primary License to a vCenter Instance
You assign a primary license to a vCenter instance. Your other assets that are connected to that vCenter instance,
including ESX hosts, are then licensed automatically. After you assign a primary license, you can also assign add-on
licenses to license the assets that use add-on license capacity.
• Verify that you have the Licensing > Managepermission assigned in the VCF Operations instance that you use for
license management. The Administrator role has this permission assigned by default.
• Verify that the VCF Operations instance is registered with the VCF Business Services console.
• Verify that at least one primary license is added to this VCF Operations instance.
• If you want to assign a license to a standalone vCenter instance, verify that the vCenter instance is integrated with the
VCF Operations instance registered for license management. For more information about adding a vCenter instance to
VCF Operations, see Configuring a vCenter Account in VCF Operations.
• If you want to assign a license to a vCenter instance that is part of a VCF domain, verify that the VCF Instance is
integrated with the VCF Operations instance registered for license management. For more information about adding a
VCF instance to VCF Operations, see Configuring a Standalone VCF Account in VCF Operations.
Note:
After you integrate a vCenter instance or a VCF Instance with VCF Operations for license management, it takes
up to 20 minutes before the vCenter instance appears on the Licenses tab of VCF Operations.
• Verify that you have the required privileges in the vSphere Client to add a license to the vCenter instance.
– Membership in the LicenseService.Administrators Single Sign-On group.
– Global > Licenses
– Either Certificate Management > Create/ Delete(below Admins Priv), or Certificate Management > Create/
Delete(below Admins Priv).
• Verify that the license has enough capacity to license all ESX hosts of versions 8.x, 9.0 and 9.1 that are added to the
vCenter instance. For more information, see Mixed-Version Environments.
The vCenter instance can be standalone or part of a VCF Instance. You cannot assign a license to a vCenter instance
if it requires more license capacity than the available capacity of the license you want to assign. If you try to assign the
license to a vCenter instance which requires more capacity than the capacity available in the license, the assignment fails.
If you try to add a host to a licensed vCenter instance, and the cores of the host are more than the available capacity left
Broadcom 2696

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
in the license assigned to the vCenter instance, the host is added in evaluation mode. If the host has exceeded the 90-day
evaluation period, you cannot add it to the vCenter instance unless you increase the available capacity of the license.
Note:
If the host is in evaluation mode, it is added to the vCenter instance even if the license capacity is not sufficient.
During the evaluation period of the host, you must add more capacity to the license to license the host.
Alternatively, you can assign an override license to the host. If the host is not licensed when the evaluation
period expires, it is disconnected from the vCenter instance. The virtual machines running on the disconnected
host remain intact. When there is enough available capacity in the license assigned to the vCenter instance, all
disconnected hosts reconnect to the vCenter system.
For example, you add a license with 1000 cores allocated capacity to the VCF Operations instance. You then add
4 vCenter instances to be managed by this VCF Operations instance. The aggregate license consumption of the 4
vCenter instances requires 1500 cores. This means that you cannot assign the license to all of them, as the aggregate
consumption across all vCenter instances cannot exceed 1000 cores. The aggregate consumption includes the total
number of cores of all pre-version 9 and version 9+ hosts adeed to the vCenter instance, and excludes any license
capacity used by ESX hosts licensed with override licenses.
For more information about calculating the license capacity you need for your environment, see Broadcom knowledge
base article 95927.
When a vCenter license expires, your hosts are disconnected from the vCenter instance even if they have override
licenses assigned to them, and you cannot start any workload operations. This is valid for both standalone vCenter
instances and vCenter instances that are part of a VCF Instance. After you assign a valid license to the vCenter instance,
the hosts are automatically reconnected to the vCenter instance unless you added them to another vCenter instance in
the meantime.
If the license assignment to a selected vCenter instance in VCF Operations 9.1 fails with an error message, check the
network connectivity between the vCenter instance and VCF Operations. For more information, see Broadcom Knowledge
base article 424533.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. Select the Version 9+ tab.
4. From the vCenter Systems table, select one or more vCenter instances to which you want to assign a license.
The table contains only vCenter instances of version 9+ managed by the current VCF Operations instance. If a
vCenter instance is added to the VCF Operations instance for monitoring only, it does not appear in this table.
5. Click Assign Primary License.
A list with the primary licenses added to VCF Operations appears. The licenses which you cannot assign appear at the
bottom of the list, and the column Assignable shows No.
6. Select a license to assign, and click Assign.
Note:
You can assign only one primary license to a vCenter instance. If you want to replace the primary license with
another one, see Remove a License from a vCenter Instance.
In the Primary Licenses column of the vCenter Systems table, you can view the licenses that you assigned to the
vCenter instance. If the assignment failed for a vCenter instance, and you want to view the details of the task, refer to the
tooltip message.

Add-on licenses are available for VCF and vSphere Foundation products. You can assign add-on licenses only after you

– Membership in the LicenseService.Administrators Single Sign-On group.
– Global > Licenses

You cannot assign a license to a vCenter instance if that instance requires more license capacity than the available

What is an Override License
When you assign a license to a vCenter instance, it is automatically assigned to all assets of that type in your environment
that are connected to this vCenter instance. If you want to assign a different license to an asset, you can assign it directly
as an override license. Override licenses are available only for assets which use license capacity, such as ESX hosts and
vSAN clusters.
Broadcom 2698

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You cannot assign an override license to a standalone asset, the asset must be added to a vCenter instance before you
can assign the override license. The override license and the vCenter license can be from the same or from different
license servers, if the license servers are added to the same VCF Operations instance.
Note:
You cannot assign override licenses to ESX hosts of versions earlier than 9.0.
When you remove a host from the vCenter instance, the license capacity it uses is added back to the license assigned to
the host. If the host is licensed with an override license, the license capacity is added back to the override license. If the
host is licensed with a vCenter license, the license capacity is added back to the vCenter license.
If the vCenter license expires, you can assign an override license to an ESX host but you must also assign a valid license
to the vCenter instance. If you do not assign a valid license to the vCenter instance, you cannot use the management
capabilities of the vCenter instance and you can only manage the host as a standalone host.
Evaluation Mode and Override Licenses
When you add an ESX host of version 9.0 or later to a vCenter instance of version 9.1, the vCenter license is assigned to
the host automatically if the license capacity is sufficient to license the host. If the license capacity is insufficient, the host
is added in evaluation mode. The evaluation period is 90 days, during that time you can either add more capacity to the
vCenter license, or assign an override license to the host.
Note:
If the evaluation mode for the host has expired before you try to add it to the vCenter instance, you cannot assign
an override license to it. If the vCenter license capacity is insufficient, to add the host, you must increase the
license capacity.
If you add hosts to a vCenter instance when the vCenter instance is in evaluation mode, you must assign a valid license
to the vCenter instance before its evaluation period expires. If you do not assign a valid license to the vCenter instance,
when the evaluation period expires, you cannot use the vCenter instance and all hosts are disconnected from it.
License Compatibility
The override and vCenter license must meet compatibility criteria. Compatibility is checked at the time when you assign a
license. If the compatibility check fails, the license assignment also fails.
When you assign an override license, a compatibility check is performed between the vCenter license and the override
license.
• If a VCF license is assigned to the vCenter instance, you cannot assign a VVF license as an override license.
• If a VVF license is assigned to the vCenter instance, you can assign a VCF license as an override license.
When you assign a vCenter license, a compatibility check is performed between the vCenter license and any override
licenses assigned directly to hosts or clusters.
• If a VCF license is assigned as an override license, you can assign a VVF license to the vCenter instance.
• If a VVF license is assigned as an override license, you cannot assign a VCF license to the vCenter.
Note:
VCF and VCF Edge are equivalent for the purpose of compatibility.
vSAN licenses and vSAN Edge licenses are not compatible.
Assign an Override License to an ESX Host in VCF Operations
Override licenses are available for assets which use license capacity, such as ESX hosts and vSAN clusters.
• Verify that the host is added to a vCenter instance.
• Verify that the override license has sufficient license capacity to license the host.
You cannot assign an override license to a standalone asset, the ESX host must be added to a licensed vCenter instance
before you can assign the override license.
Broadcom 2699

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
You cannot assign override licenses to ESX hosts of versions earlier than 9.0.
The override and vCenter license must meet compatibility criteria. Compatibility is checked at the time when you assign
a license. If the compatibility check fails, the license assignment is unsuccessful. For more information about override
licenses, see What is an Override License.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. Select the Version 9+ tab.
4. From the vCenter Systems table, click the vCenter instance to which the ESX host is added.
The table contains only vCenter instances of version 9+ managed by the current VCF Operations instance. If a
vCenter instance is added to the VCF Operations instance for monitoring only, it does not appear in this table.
5. On the page with the vCenter license details, navigate to Assets, and click ESX Hosts.
6. Select the check box next to the host to which you want to assign an override license, and click Assign Override
License.
7. On the Assign Override License page, select the license that you want to assign to the host, and click Assign.
The license is assigned to the ESX host.
Replace an Override License with a vCenter License
You can replace an override license with the license assigned to the vCenter instance at any time if the vCenter license
has enough available capacity to license the asset.
• Verify that the vCenter license has enough available license capacity to license the asset.
Note:
If a license is assigned as an override license, and you later assign it to the vCenter instance, it is considered a
vCenter license and replaces the override assignment.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. Select the Version 9+ tab.
4. Identify the vCenter instance that contains the asset to which you want to assign an override license.
5. From the vCenter Systems table, click the vCenter instance that contains the asset.
The table contains only vCenter instances of version 9+ managed by the current VCF Operations instance. If a
vCenter instance is added to the VCF Operations instance for monitoring only, it does not appear in this table.
6. On the page with the vCenter license details, navigate to Assets.
7. Assign a vCenter license to an ESX host.
a) Under Assets, click ESX Hosts.
b) Select the check box next to the hosts to which you want to assign an override license, and click Switch to
vCenter License.
A dialog box appears.
c) Click Replace.
The ESX hosts are licensed with the license assigned to the vCenter instance. The License Source column shows
vCenter.

8. Assign a vCenter license to a vSAN cluster.
a) Under Assets, click vSAN Clusters.
b) Select the check box next to the vSAN clusters to which you want to assign an override license, and click Switch
to vCenter License.
A dialog box appears.
c) Click Replace.
The vSAN clusters are licensed with the license assigned to the vCenter instance. The License Source column
shows vCenter.
Reclaim Used Capacity
When you delete an asset, your license capacity is automatically reclaimed and available to assign to a new asset.
If a connectivity issue between the license server and the vCenter instance occurs, the license capacity might not be
automatically added back to the license. If this happens, you can manually reclaim the used capacity.
• Verify that the asset is removed from the vCenter instance.
• If you want to reclaim capacity used by a vCenter instance, verify that the vCenter instance is removed from the
current VCF Operations instance.
To reclaim the license capacity used by a vCenter instance and the assets connected to it, you must first remove the
vCenter instance from the VCF Operations instance. If you want to continue monitoring the vCenter instance from the
VCF Operations instance, you can remove the vCenter instance only from license management.
When you remove the vCenter account from VCF Operations, the license capacity used by assets connected to the
vCenter instance is added back to the license, and the vCenter instance no longer communicates with the license server.
Note:
To avoid service interruption for the vCenter instance, you must add it to a VCF Operations instance, and assign a
license to it.
In some cases, used capacity might not be automatically reclaimed after you remove assets from your environment. For
example, if connectivity between the license server and the vCenter instance is interrupted at the time when you remove
the vCenter instance from VCF Operations, or when you remove an ESX host from vCenter . In such cases you must
manually reclaim the used capacity. You can reclaim used capacity only for assets that are no longer in the inventory, for
example, hosts or clusters that are removed from the vCenter instance, or vCenter instanced that are removed from the
VCF Operations instance.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. In the Registration and License Server Status card, click Manage > License Servers.
The VCF Operations Registration page appears.
4. On the License Servers tab, click the license server which contains the license that is assigned to the removed asset.
5. Under Licensed Assets, select the asset for which you want to reclaim the capacity, and click Reclaim Used
Capacity.
A dialog box appears.
6. Click Reclaim Used Capacity.
The license capacity used by the removed asset is added back to the license as available capacity.
Updating Licenses and Viewing the License Usage File
You must update your licenses in VCF Operations to verify that a usage file has been submitted, or when you make a
license-related change such as subscription capacity changes, renewals, or splitting licenses and changing their capacity.
When you update licenses, you do not need to reassign licenses to the assets.
Broadcom 2701

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If you do not make any license-related changes in the VCF Business Services console, you must still update your licenses
at least once every 6 months (180 days). If license usage data is not submitted within the required reporting time-frame,
and you do not update your licenses, your licenses are treated as expired, your hosts are disconnected from the vCenter
instance, and you cannot start any workload operations.
How to view the detailed contents of your usage file
License usage files contain information on the capacity of each license used by a VCF fleet. VCF Operations creates the
license usage files and sends them to the VCF Business Services console.
You can view your license usage in a ready-to-read usage file that is decompressed and decoded, or you can view the
raw usage file that is created in your VCF Operations instance. The raw usage file is a JSON Web Signed (JWS) file
compressed with gZip.
Note:
• If your VCF Operations instance is in connected mode, usage files are automatically generated and submitted
daily and you can only view the ready-to-read usage file.
• If your VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode, you must manually download and submit usage files
on regular intervals.
The contents of the usage files are identical in connected and disconnected mode.
View a ready-to-read usage file 1. In the VCF Operations instance, navigate to Licensing > Registration.
2. Under File History, download the usage file that you want to view, and
open it.
View the raw usage file in a human-readable format 1. In the VCF Operations instance, navigate to Licensing > Registration, and
click Generate Usage File.
2. Use decompression software that supports gZip decompression to
decompress the content of the usage file.
3. Use a text editor to open the decompressed file, and copy the content.
4. Paste the content of the usage file into a JWT Decoding tool.
After the content is decoded, you can view the collected license usage
information.

Update Licenses in Connected Mode
After any change to your licenses in the VCF Business Services console, to reflect the changes in your on-premise
environment, your licenses must be updated in the VCF Operations instance. In connected mode, the usage file is
submitted automatically on a daily basis. If your licenses update mode is set to manual, you must still update your licenses
in the VCF Operations instance at least once every 180 days to verify that the usage file has been submitted correctly,
and to keep your environment licensed.
You must update your licenses at least once every 6 months (180 days). If license usage data is not submitted within the
required reporting time-frame, and you do not update your licenses, your licenses are treated as expired, your hosts are
disconnected from the vCenter instance, and you cannot start any workload operations. You can update your licenses at
any time to extend your usage reporting refresh period.
Note:
If your licenses update mode is set to automated, your licenses are updated automatically once every 24 hours
and after each change you make to the licenses related to the VCF Operations instance. For more information
about switching to automated licenses update mode, see Change License Updates Mode.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. Optional: To verify that your license usage file was submitted within the last 24 hours, click Manage > Registration
Details, and check the Last Usage Report Generated date.
4. Click Update Licenses.
Your VCF Operations instance is updated with the latest license information available from the VCF Business Services
console.
Change License Updates Mode
If your VCF Operation instance operates in connected mode, you can choose from an automated and a manual update of
licenses. The default license updates mode is automated.
The automated update of licenses happens once every 24 hours and after each change you make to the licenses related
to the VCF Operations instance. The manual update requires that you click a button to update the licenses after each
change and at least once every 180 days. License usage reporting is automated in both the manual and the automated
license update mode because your environment is in connected mode.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. In the Registration and License Server Status card, click Manage > Registration Details.
The VCF Operations Registration page appears.
4. On the Registration Details tab, switch the mode for updating licenses.
• If you want to switch from automated to manual mode, next to Update Licenses Mode, click Switch to Manual.
Broadcom 2704

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If you want to switch from manual to automated mode, next to Update Licenses Mode, click Switch to Automated.
Report License Usage and Update Licenses in Disconnected Mode
When a VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode, you must manually exchange the usage file and the license
file between the VCF Operations instance and the VCF Business Services console.
• Verify that your VCF Operations instance is registered in the VCF Business Services console.
You must update your licenses and submit a license usage file at least once every 6 months (180 days). If license usage
data is not submitted within the required reporting time-frame, and you do not update your licenses, your licenses are
treated as expired, your hosts are disconnected from the vCenter instance, and you cannot start any workload operations.
You can generate a new license file without submitting a usage file as long as it is within your usage reporting due date.
As a best practice, always submit a usage file before you download a new license file.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. Click Generate Usage File, and save the usage file.
4. In the VCF Business Services console, navigate to Licensing > VCF Operations Registrations.
5. Click the VCF Operations instance for which you want to update licenses.
6. In the VCF Operations Details page, click Actions > Upload Usage File.
7. In the Upload Usage File wizard, upload the usage file, and click Upload and Next.
A license file is generated.
8. Click Download, and save the license file.
9. Click Finish.
10.In the VCF Operations instance, navigate to Licensing > Licenses & Registration.
11.In the Registration and License Server Status card, click Manage > Registration Details.
12.Click Import License File.
The Import License File dialog box appears.
13.Click Browse, upload the license file, and click Import.
14.When the license file is imported, click Complete.
A dialog box appears. You can view the licenses and the license servers that are added to this VCF Operation
instance.
Remove a License from a vCenter Instance
To remove a primary license from a vCenter instance, you must replace it with another primary license.
• Verify that you have the Manage Licenses permission assigned.
• Verify that licenses are added to this VCF Operations instance.
• Verify that the license you want to assign to the vCenter instance has sufficient capacity.
If you no longer want to keep the license assigned to a vCenter instance, you can replace it with another primary license.
The used license capacity of the license you replace is freed up and you can assign it to other assets.
When you replace a primary license assigned to a vCenter instance with another primary license, you can choose whether
to update override license assignments. You can replace all override licenses assigned to the hosts in that vCenter
instance with the new primary license or you can keep the override licenses assigned to the hosts. If you want to keep the
override license assignments, license compatibility is checked. For more information about the compatibility matrix, see
What is an Override License.

Delete a License Server
If you want to replace your license server with a new one, and you want to delete the first license server, you must delete
it from the VCF Business Services console and the VCF Operations instance.
To keep your environment licensed, before you delete a license server, you must transfer the licenses added to it to
another license server that is registered with the same VCF Operations instance. Alternatively, you can assign new
licenses to all assets in your environment. The new licenses must be added to a license server that is registered with the
same VCF Operations instance.
You must first delete the license server from the VCF Business Services console, and then you can delete it from the VCF
Operations instance.
Note:
If there are licenses added to the license server, and you delete the license server, the licenses are removed.
As a result, all assets licensed with these licenses become unlicensed. To avoid service interruption, assign new
licenses to the assets.

License Usage Analytics
License usage analytics are available both in the VCF Operations instance that you use for license management, and in
the VCF Business Services console. You can access your license usage data at any time to check the aggregate license
usage per product and per license.
With your subscription for a product, you also receive license keys for version 8.x of the product. You can decide which
version of the product to deploy and license, but your total license usage must not exceed your purchased subscription
capacity. You can use the usage analytics data to monitor license usage and change license capacity.
Note:
If at a certain point the used capacity is higher than the capacity allocated to the assigned licenses, you must
allocate more capacity to the licenses. Before you add more capacity, you cannot assign the over used licenses
to new vCenter instances. To the vCenter instances which are licensed with the over used licenses, you can only
add new ESX hosts that are in evaluation mode.
View License Usage in the VCF Business Services console
In the VCF Business Services console, you can view aggregated data for your complete license usage for all your
products and licenses in the unit of measure for the specific license. You can use the analytics data to monitor license
usage and plan your license management.
License usage is determined based on the vCenter version.
• vCenter 9.1 and later. Version 9.0+ usage combines license usage by hosts of version earlier than 9.0 that use license
keys, and hosts of version 9.0 and later that use license files. When hosts of versions earlier than 9.0 that use license
keys are managed by vCenter instances of version 9.1 or later, the license capacity of these hosts is included in the
version 9+ license usage.
• For vCenter 9.0. License usage is separated into license usage by hosts of version earlier than 9.0 that use license
keys, and hosts of version 9.0 that use license files.
• For vCenter 8.x and earlier. License usage by hosts of version 8.x or earlier that use license keys.

• Pre-Version 9 License Usage. Includes license key usage by pre-9.0 hosts managed by vCenter instances of version
9.0 and license key usage by hosts of version 8.x or earlier managed by vCenter instances of version 8.x.
• Version 9+ License Usage. Includes license usage by hosts managed by vCenter instances of version 9.1 and later.
• Product Aggregate Usage. Presents the total usage of all licenses for each product, derived from the Version 9+
License Usage tab.
You can also export and view the usage analytics data for product aggregate usage, version 9+ license usage, and pre-
version 9 license usage. The export file is available in CSV and JSON formats.

5. If you want to view usage analytics for a specific license, use the Select License drop-down menu.
6. If you want to view usage analytics for a specific vCenter instance, use the Select vCenter drop-down menu.
The list of vCenter instances includes only the instances to which you have assigned licenses from this VCF
Operations instance. If you select a specific license to view data for, the list of vCenter instances contains only the
vCenter instances to which this license is assigned.
7. In the Historical Usage pane, you can view maximum license usage for a specific aggregation period.
Use the filters to view maximum license usage in monthly or daily periods.
License Management for Cloud Services Providers and Hyperscalers
You license your VCF environment by using a VCF Operations instance and the VMware Cloud Foundation Business
Services console (vcf.broadcom.com).
Overview
• To license your environment, you must have entitlements to the VCF products.
• After a commit contract is signed and available in the Broadcom Support Portal, you must create licenses against the
contract serial number and the product in the contract.
• If you and the end customer meet certain requirements, end customers can share licenses for portability with you. For
more information, see License Sharing.
• To license your environment, you must have an installed VCF Operations instance and a license server, register them
in the VCF Business Services console, and add licenses with available capacity to a license server. You can register
VCF Operations to the VCF Business Services console either in connected or in disconnected mode. Connected
registration is recommended for cloud services providers and hyperscalers.
• You must update your licenses at least once every six months. For more information, see Updating Licenses and
Viewing the License Usage File.
• To collect the relevant product usage, you must deploy a VCF usage meter instance. VCF usage meter collects the
licensing data and usage data (for more information, see the guides in the Broadcom Partner Portal Page for VMware
Cloud Service Providers under VCSP Portfolio) in the metered environments and communicates the data to the cloud.
The data is converted to core usage per hour for each license.
• You must register the VCF usage meter instance in the VCF Business Services console. The product usage data is
available in the VCF Business Services console for partners to download and review.
License Management Between Tenants and Sites
You can manage licenses in all the tenants of the sites you belong to. However, you cannot transfer licenses between
tenants. You must register the VCF Operations instance in the same tenant as the licenses you want to add. If you
register the VCF Operations in a wrong tenant, you can deactivate the VCF Operations instance and restart the
registration in the correct tenant. If you have added licenses, the licenses must first be removed before deactivating the
VCF Operations instance.
Licensing Attributes for Providers
On the Licensing tab of the VCF Business Services console, you can see the attributes of the licenses you manage.
Broadcom 2711

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Licensing Attributes
Component Description
Commit Capacity The committed capacity in the signed commit contract. Can be in a number of cores or TiBs.
Total Licenses Total number of the created licenses.
Consumed Capacity The consumed capacity contains data for both non-running and running workloads. If VCF
usage meter manages the environment on a running workload and the consumed capacity
exceeds the commit capacity, you might get billed for over use.
High-Level Provider Licensing Workflow
1. Install a VCF Operations instance version 9.1, or upgrade your existing Aria Operations instance to VCF Operations
9.1.
2. Register your VCF Operations instance with the VCF Business Services console by using one of the two modes.
– Disconnected mode - no Internet connection is required. You must manually exchange registration, verification, and
license files between the VCF Operations instance and the VCF Business Services console.
– Connected mode - Internet connection is required. You use an activation code from the VCF Business Services
console to register your VCF Operations instance and the license servers.
3. Add licenses to the license servers from the VCF Business Services console.
4. Assign licenses to vCenter instances from VCF Operations.
5. Deploy or upgrade a VCF usage meter appliance to version 9.1.
Create Licenses as a Provider
After you purchase a contract serial number and a product, you must create licenses against a contract serial number
combination.
Verify that you are in the correct tenant.
Depending on the type of your contract, you can exceed the commit capacity for the created licenses. The capacity of the
licenses must be between 1 and 100 000 cores.
1. Log in to the VCF Business Services console.
2. Navigate to License Management > Licenses.
3. Click Manage Licenses.
4. From the All Serial Numbers and Products, select the serial number and the product you want to create the new
license against.
You can see all of the licenses previously created for the selected serial number and product with high-level details
for commit contract capacity, the maximum capacity, total number of licenses created, and the total allocated capacity.
You can also see the expiration date and consumed capacity of each license individually.
5. Click Create.
6. Enter a name and capacity for the license and click Next.
7. View the summary and click Finish.
Register VCF Operations as a Provider
If the VCF Operations instance is provider managed, you should register it in connected mode.
Verify that you register the VCF Operations in the correct site and tenant.
The registered VCF Operations instance can be
• fully provider managed
• both customer and provider managed (applicable to white label customers)
Broadcom 2712

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If the VCF Operations is fully provider managed, you register the VCF Operations instance in connected or disconnected
mode and manage all the licenses for the end customers within the tenant.
If both a customer and provider manage the VCF Operations instance, you must start the registration in disconnected
mode and then pass the activation code to the end customer. For more information, see Register VCF Operations and
Your License Server in Connected Mode and Register VCF Operations and Your License Server in Disconnected Mode.
Note:
When you add licenses in the VCF Business Services console, you can only select from existing licenses. Add
only licenses created in the same tenant as the one you register the VCF Operations instance in.
Restart a VCF Operations Registration
If you register the VCF Operations in the wrong site or tenant, you can restart the VCF Operations registration.
Before you restart the VCF Operations registration, you must remove any licenses added to the VCF Operations instance,
delete the VCF Operations instance, and then re-register in the correct tenant. For more information, see Delete a
License.
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. From the navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Licensing > Licenses &
Registration.
3. In the Registration and License Server Status pane, navigate to Manage > Registration details.
The VCF Operations Registration page appears.
4. On the Registration Details tab, navigate to Actions > Restart Registration.
Move a Contract or a Serial Number Between Site IDs
Registration of VCF Operation is linked to a VCF Business Services console tenant and a Broadcom SiteID. The license
allocations are linked to their contracts via serial numbers. If a contract or serial number is moved from one Broadcom
SiteID to another, this impacts existing VCF Operations that are linked to the first SiteID with licenses from that SiteID.
Verify that you have a product or user administrator privileges for the new SiteID.
You cannot move serial numbers, you must contact support and request the move. In some cases, when you expand or
renew a contract, if a new SiteID is added in the ordering process, serial numbers might be moved.
If you must move your serial number from one SiteID to another, you must first submit a usage report from VCF
Operations and download a new license file. You must add licenses again in the new site. You must do this for all VCF
Operations instances with a license from that serial number.
If one of your licenses appears as Inactive but your subscription is not expired, your serial number might have been
moved.
When a serial number is moved, you might observe the following behavior:
1. Existing licenses linked to that serial number become Inactive.
2. Existing assignments appear as over assigned.
3. License updates fail.
4. After 180 days, your license expires, your hosts are disconnected from vCenter, and you cannot start workload
operations.
After the serial number is moved, you must register your VCF Operations instance to the new SiteID and must re-license
your environment.
Broadcom 2713

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Find the licenses and the VCF Operations instances that are related to the serial number.
a) Log in to the VCF Business Services console.
b) Navigate to License Management > Licenses.
c) Use the search box to search for the serial number.
All filtered licenses contain the searched serial number. The search results have a column for VCF Operations Name.
These are the instances that must be re-linked to the new siteID.
2. Generate a license usage file from each VCF Operations instance that is related to the serial number, and update its
licenses.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations instance.
b) Navigate to Licensing > Registration.
c) Update licenses.
• If the VCF Operations instance is in connected mode, verify that your license usage file was submitted within
the last 24 hours by looking at the Last Usage Report Generated date, and click Update Licenses. For more
information, see Update Licenses in Connected Mode.
• If the VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode, generate a license usage file. For more information, see
Report License Usage and Update Licenses in Disconnected Mode.
3. After you move your serial number, for each VCF Operations instance, create your licenses again by splitting the
default license. For more information, see Managing Licenses in the VCF Business Services Console.
As a best practice, allocate the same capacity to the licenses as the capacity from the prior SiteID. Consider also using
a distinct license name from the prior site.
4. Deactivate the VCF Operations instance in the VCF Business Services console. For more information, see Deactivate
a VCF Operations Instance.
You must select the check box I no longer have access to the VCF Operations instance.
5. Restart registration for each VCF Operations instance that is linked to the serial number.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations instance.
b) Navigate to Licensing > Registration.
c) Click Actions > Restart Registration.
Important:
This action does not impact the existing licenses in your environment.
6. Register each VCF Operations instance linked to the serial number with the new SiteID. For more information, see
Registering VCF Operations and a License Server with the VCF Business Services Console.
CAUTION:
During registration, select the new Site ID, and the license you created in step 3.
7. Relicense your environment by assigning the licenses to the vCenter instances. For more information, see Assign a
Primary License to a vCenter Instance.
Both your old and new licenses are displayed in VCF Operations. After your next license update, if the old licenses are
no longer assigned to vCenter instances, they do not appear in VCF Operations.
Update your licenses. For more information, see Updating Licenses and Viewing the License Usage File.
A License Server Does Not Appear in the License Servers Table in VCF
Operations
A license server does not appear in the list of license servers in VCF Operations but appears in the VCF Business
Services console.
If you take a snapshot of VCF Operations before adding a license server to it, when you revert to that snapshot, the
license server is not available in the VCF Operations instance but remains in the VCF Business Services console.
Broadcom 2714

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You cannot reconnect the license server to the VCF Operations instance. You can transfer the licenses from that license
server to a new license server that is connected to the VCF Operations instance, and delete the old license server.
Note:
After you upgrade VCF Operations from version 9.0 to version 9.1, a license server is automatically deployed and
must register it with the VCF Business Services console. After the upgrade, even if you revert to a snapshot of
VCF Operations before the upgrade, you cannot roll back to version 9.0 in the VCF Business Services console.
License-related operations such as license usage reporting might fail.
1. Optional: Transfer the licenses from the license server to a license server that is connected to VCF Operations.
The licenses are automatically assigned to the assets that they were assigned to before the transfer of licenses.
2. Delete the license server from the VCF Business Service console. For more information, see Delete a License Server.
3. Delete the license server virtual machine from the vCenter instance.
Broadcom 2715

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Building Cloud Infrastructure
Use VCF Operations and the vSphere Client as a VI administrator to add and configure infrastructure for consumer and
management workloads in the VCF private cloud after you deploy or converge to a VCF fleet and a VCF Instance with its
management domain.
• You can start adding workload domains to a VCF Instance and individual clusters and hosts to these workload
domains.
VCF Operations deploys the vCenter and NSX Manager instances for the added workload domains. You can also
enable vSphere Supervisor on the default cluster of the workload domain.
• You can import vCenter instances with their managed ESX hosts as workload domains so that they are included in
identity and access management, certificate management, and lifecycle management operations performed centrally in
VCF Operations .
• You can also add NSX network services to the management domain and the workload domains of a VCF Instance by
deploying NSX Edge clusters, transit gateways, and virtual private clouds (VPCs). Then you can configure workloads
to use these network services.
You can place VCF Operations and VCF Automation on NSX overlay or VLAN segments so that they can use the NSX
load balancer, or to support planned migration and disaster recovery, or IP mobility.
You can configure consumer workloads to use the network services either in VCF Automation or directly in the
vSphere Client.
• If you want to implement vSAN stretched clusters in a workload domain, you can use the SDDC Manager API for
automated stretched cluster configuration.
