Configure a Virtual IP Address for a Cluster
To provide fault tolerance and high availability to NSX Manager nodes, assign a virtual IP address (VIP) to the NSX
cluster.
NSX Manager nodes of a cluster become part of an HTTPS group to service API and UI requests. The leader node of the
cluster assumes ownership of the set VIP of the cluster to service any API and UI request. Any API and UI request coming
in from clients is directed to the leader node.
Note:
When assigning Virtual IP, all the NSX Manager VMs in the cluster must be configured in the same subnet. But
if external load balancer is used to configure cluster VIP, then NSX Managers and VIP can belong to a different
subnet.
If the leader node that owns VIP becomes unavailable, NSX elects a new leader. The new leader owns the VIP. It sends
out a gratuitous ARP packet advertising the new VIP to MAC address mapping. After a new leader node is elected, new
API and UI requests are sent to the new leader node.
Broadcom 3967

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Failover of VIP to a new leader node of the cluster might take a few minutes to become functional. If the VIP fails over to a
new leader node because the previous leader node became unavailable, reauthenticate the NSX Manager credentials so
that API requests are directed to the new leader node.
Note:
VIP is not designed to serve as a load-balancer and you cannot use it if you enable the vIDM External Load
Balancer Integration from System > Users > Configuration. Do not set up a VIP if you want to use the External
Load Balancer from vIDM. See Configure VMware Workspace ONE Access Integration in the NSX Administration
Guide for more details.
Important:
If you reset the cluster VIP, then vIDM configurations that are using the VIP is cleared. You will need to
reconfigure vIDM configuration with the new VIP.
1. From a browser, log in with admin privileges to an NSX Manager at https://<nsx-manager-ip-address> or https://<nsx-
manager-fqdn>.
2. Go to System > Appliances.
3. In the Virtual IP field, click Set Virtual IP.
4. Enter the IPv4 and/or IPv6 address to use as VIP for the cluster.
Ensure that VIP is part of the same subnet as the other management nodes. When you deploy a NSX Manager in a
dual stack environment (IPv4 and IPv6), use a valid FQDN address and use the same FQDN address for both IPv4
and IPv6 addresses.
5. Click Save.
6. To verify the cluster status and the API leader of the HTTPS group, enter the NSX Manager CLI command
get
in the NSX Manager console or over SSH.
cluster status verbose
The following is an example output:
Group Type: HTTPS
Group Status: STABLE
Members:
UUID FQDN IP STATUS
cdb93642-ccba-fdf4-8819-90bf018cd727 nsx-manager 192.196.197.84 UP
51a13642-929b-8dfc-3455-109e6cc2a7ae nsx-manager 192.196.198.156 UP
d0de3642-d03f-c909-9cca-312fd22e486b nsx-manager 192.196.198.54 UP
Leaders:
SERVICE LEADER LEASE VERSION
api cdb93642-ccba-fdf4-8819-90bf018cd727 8
7. Verify that the VIP is working correctly.
From a browser, log in to the NSX Manager using the virtual IP address assigned to the cluster at https://<VIP-
address>.
Any API requests to NSX are redirected to the virtual IP address of the cluster, which is owned by the leader node. The
leader node then routes the request forward to the other components of the appliance.
Note:
If you deploy NSX Manager in dual stack mode (IPv4, IPv6) and/or if you plan to configure NSX Manager
deployment with CA-signed certificates, associate the VIP IP address with DNS name. Also, configure reverse
and forward proxy for the VIP IP address on the DNS server. Then access VIP from https://<VIP-dns-name>.
Verify Appliance Proxy Hub on all NSX Manager Nodes are Connected
Appliance Proxy Hub (APH) acts as a communication channel between NSX Manager and a transport node. It runs as a
service on NSX Manager and provides secure connection between a transport node and NSX Manager.
Broadcom 3968

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Before you set a virtual IP (VIP) address for the cluster nodes, ensure the APH running on each NSX Manager cluster
nodes are connected to each other. If APH on all cluster nodes are not connected, you might face issues when configuring
the VIP for the cluster.
1. To verify APH on all the cluster nodes are connected, go to one of the NSX Manager nodes and run the
GET /api/v1/
call.
messaging/cluster-connection/status
{
"results": [
{
"address": "ssl-tcp://192.161.1.52:38522",
"conn_status": "Connected",
"node_id": "e85ceb93-df30-43fa-84d7-32d88f68a2ba",
"node_type": "APPLIANCE_PROXY_HUB"
},
{
"address": "ssl://192.161.1.51:1234",
"conn_status": "Connected",
"node_id": "46cc9a95-6194-4d84-94bd-0744fb46e225",
"node_type": "APPLIANCE_PROXY_HUB"
}
]
2. Repeat Step 1 on the remaining cluster nodes.
3. Wait for 60 seconds before you set the cluster VIP for the cluster.
When APH on all cluster nodes are connected to each other, you can proceed to configure VIP for the cluster.
Set up the cluster VIP address.
Troubleshooting Issues
This chapter provides information about troubleshooting issues related to NSX installation and configuration.
Troubleshooting Installation to check for Basic Infrastructure Services
This section provides information about troubleshooting installation issues.
Basic Infrastructure Services
The following services must be running on the appliances and hypervisors, also on vCenter if it is used as a compute
manager.
• NTP
• DNS
Make sure that firewall is not blocking traffic between NSX components and hypervisors. Make sure that the required
ports are open between the components.
To flush the DNS cache on the NSX Manager, SSH as root to the manager and run the following command:
root@nsx-mgr-01:~# /etc/init.d/resolvconf restart
[ ok ] Restarting resolvconf (via systemctl): resolvconf.service.
You can then check the DNS configuration file.
root@nsx-mgr-01:~# cat /etc/resolv.conf

nameserver 192.168.253.1
search mgt.sg.lab

su admin nsxcli nsxcli

Host Registration Failure
If NSX uses the wrong IP address, host registration will fail. This can happen when a host has multiple IP addresses.
Trying to delete the transport node leaves it in the Orphaned state. To resolve the issue:
• Go to Fabric > Nodes > Hosts, edit the host and remove all IP addresses except the management one.
• Click on the errors and select Resolve.
Configuration Error when Deploying an Edge VM
After deploying an Edge VM, NSX Manager shows the VM's status as configuration error. The manager log has a
message similar to the following:
nsx-manager NSX - FABRIC [nsx@6876 comp="nsx-manager" errorCode="MP16027" subcomp="manager"] Edge
758ad396-0754-11e8-877e-005056abf715 is not ready for configuration error occurred, error detail is NSX Edge
configuration has failed. The host does not support required cpu features: ['aes'].
Restarting the edge datapath service and then the VM should resolve the issue.
Force Removing a Transport Node
You can remove a transport node that is stuck in the Orphaned state by making the following API call:
DELETE https://<NSX Manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<TN ID>?force=true
NSX Manager will not do any validations as to whether you have any active VMs running on the host. You are responsible
for deleting the N-VDS and VIBs. If you have the node added through Compute Manager, delete the Compute Manager
first and then delete the node. The transport node will be deleted as well.

Troubleshoot NSX Manager Cluster
You must configure a three-node NSX Manager cluster and only one of the nodes can fail at any given time for the cluster
to self-heal.
For an NSX Manager cluster to self-recover from a node failure, the majority of nodes must not have failed (the number
of active nodes must be greater than the failed nodes) otherwise the entire cluster becomes unavailable. It means that all
write operations are blocked, all clustering related API/CLIs fail. However, local API/CLI commands continue to work.
NSX Manager logs are written into , directory.
/var/log/syslog
Admin CLI
To activate Admin CLI, log in as an admin to a NSX Manager. But if you login as root, you can run singleton admin CLI
directly from the root shell using the command. You can switch on interactive mode of admin
su admin –c <cmd-to-run>
CLI using the command and then run admin commands.
su admin

A NSX Manager that is manually deployed in vCenter using OVF or OVA file failed to join the NSX Manager cluster.
You used an incorrect thumbprint value to join the new NSX Manager node to the existing NSX Manager cluster. If
NSX VIP is configured, then use the cluster thumbprint command. If external VIP or no VIP is configured, use the API
thumbprint command. Try registering the NSX Manager node with the cluster using correct thumbprint.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

get certificate cluster thumbprint Join management-plane <cluster-vip>
command. The

procedure to join the management node with the cluster is complete. Alternatively, you can use the NSX Manager
thumbprint, as shown in the following steps to join the NSX Manager with the cluster.

command.
username <manager-username> password <manager-pwd> thumbprint <manager-thumbprint>
NSX Manager Cluster status Degraded As Datastore-related Components Are Down
NSX Manager status is degraded due to DATASTORE component and/or CORFU_NONCONFIG component down on
one or more manager nodes member of NSX Cluster.
1. SSH to NSX Manager CLI terminal as an admin.
2. To identify the manager node with components down, run .
get cluster status
3. Verify underlying datastore is available with recommended disk access latency. To get and fix the disk access latency
numbers, see Knowledge Base article 316654: Storage latency causes NSX Manager cluster instability.
Note:
Datastore outage can cause NSX Manager appliance VMs to go into read-only mode. Linux does not provide a
usable utility to recover from this error. Follow the KB, Recover NSX Manager upon storage outage, if appliance
reboot does not fix the issue. Verify backend datastore has fully recovered before rebooting the affected NSX
Manager VM.
4. To verify no disk partition consumed by NSX is full or close-to-full, run ‘get filesystem-stats'.
Note:
Datastore specific logs can be found at and
var/log/corfu/corfu.9000.log /var/log/corfu/
.
tanuki.log
5. Clean up disk space and / or reboot all NSX Manager nodes (after storage issues are resolved) to remove the read-
only mode.
6. If components continue to be down, contact VMware Support.
Important:
With the datastore down, the NSX Manager continues to participate in the cluster if its network connectivity is
up. This state might result in the management plane and control plane to become unavailable. If datastore issue
cannot be resolved, replace the impacted NSX Manager by powering off the impacted NSX Manager (as long as
cluster quorum is maintained by having majority number of nodes up).
7. Remove NSX Manager node from existing NSX Manager Cluster. On the NSX Manager, run
detach node <node-
.
id>
8. Verify the problematic node is not a member of the cluster anymore by running the .
get cluster status
9. Deploy a new NSX Manager node and join it to the existing Manager Cluster.
Manager and HTTPS Services Are Down Frequently Due to Incorrect NAT Configuration
If you incorrectly configured NAT, the Manager and HTTPS service might go down frequently.
Broadcom 3972

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Do not use 0.0.0.0/0, x.0.0.0/8, x.x.0.0/16 subnet ranges in the NAT rules for SNAT Translated IP section (SNAT rule)
and for Destination Network section (DNAT rule).
2. Fix the incorrect NAT configuration.
3. Configure NAT rule where IP address range and count does not exceed 256 for SNAT Translated IP section (SNAT
rule) and for Destination Network section (DNAT rule).
NSX Manager is Slow To Load And Tasks Fail
NSX Manager is slow to load and tasks fail with message or .
server is overloaded too many requests
This issue occurs upon hitting the nsx manager incoming API rate limit. The solution is to either limit the number of
incoming API requests to NSX Manager or modify the default values for Client API rate limit or Client API concurrency
limit or Global API concurrently limit from API or CLI.
1. To view current default values, run as admin or
get cluster api-service GET API /api/v1/cluster/api-
.
service
2. To set a new API rate value, run or
set cluster api-service client-api-rate-limit PUT /api/v1/cluster/
with updated values.
api-service
3. To view logs of incoming API requests, go to directory, .
/var/log/proxy reverse-proxy.log
Note:
Try to avoid configuring the API rate limits. Instead, design your API client to gracefully deal with situations where
limits are exceeded.
NSX Manager UI is not loading even when NSX Clustering is up
NSX Manager is slow to load and tasks fail with message or .
server is overloaded too many requests
1. SSH to one of the NSX Manager that is a member of the cluster.
2. Run admin CLI .
get cluster status
3. If cluster status is stable, run or and verify that the following services
get services get service <service-name>
are running: , , , .
http manager search ui-service
4. To restart or start the stopped service, run .
restart | start service <service-name>
NSX Manager cluster is DOWN or UNAVAILABLE if all nodes part of the NSX Manager cluster
is down or majority nodes are down
NSX Manager is down or unavailable if majority of the nodes in the cluster are down.
NSX Manager UI will fail to load with following error
Some appliance components are not functioning
and clustering
properly. Component health: POLICY:UNKNOWN, MANAGER:UNKNOWN, SEARCH:UNKNOWN, NO
related commands will fail using the CLI and API.
1. SSH to each of the affected NSX Manager nodes and run following commands:
a) Run and verify /config and /image is not 100% full.
get file-system-stats
b) Run to verify no cores have gotten generated in NSX Manager.
get core-dumps
c) Verify there was no datastore outage. See NSX Manager Cluster status Degraded As Datastore-related
Components Are Down.
d) Check logs for out-of-memory errors. See
/var/log/proton/proton-tomcat-wrapper.log
2. To restore clustering and UI, any two nodes in a three node cluster must be up. If you are not able to bring any failed
node back up, but if there is a healthy node available, then do one of the following steps to restore clustering:
• Deploy a new manager node (as 4th member node), join the existing cluster and then detach one of the
failed nodes using CLI cmd or API
detach node <node-uuid> POST /api/v1/cluster/<node-uuid>?
. The commands should be executed from one of the healthy nodes. Alternatively, you can
action=remove_node
follow the next bulleted point to deactivate the cluster.
Broadcom 3973

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Now continue to add the new additional nodes to make a 3-member NSX Manager cluster.
Note:
NSX Manager nodes that are removed from the cluster should be powered off and deleted.

downloading nsx lcp bundle to the host. Error seen is "Failed to download NSX components on host.

/var/log/nsx-syslog

Transport Node Tunnels Down
ESX hosts that are prepared as transport nodes have their tunnel status as .
Down

net-vdl2 –l | more
2. Verify these configuration details are correct: VTEP state is UP, VTEP count is correct, and a valid VTEP addresses is
assigned.
3. To find VTEP BFD tunnel sessions that are down on the ESX transport node, run the CLI command
nsxdp-cli bfd
.
sessions list | grep down
4. For sessions that are down, validate IP connectivity between the TEPs using ICMP ping.
Note:
The TEP interfaces on ESX are instantiated on the vxlan netstack and on the tunnel VRF for NSX Edge nodes.
Therefore, initiate the ping from within the vxlan netstack on ESX and if you have more than one TEP, be sure to
specify the source IP address or interface used for the ping.
5. Run .
ping ++netstack=vxlan <remote address> -I vmk10
6. If ping fails, verify the underlay connectivity of the network.
7. If ping is successful, verify Fabric MTU is configured correctly on the underlay network and within NSX. Use ICMP with
the don’t fragment bit to test proper delivery for large packets.
8. Run .
ping ++netstack=vxlan <remote-vtep-ip=-address> -I vmk10 -d -s 1600
Installation Fails Due to Insufficient Space in Bootbank on ESX Host
NSX installation might fail if there is insufficient space in the bootbank or in the alt-bootbank on an ESX host.
On the ESX host, you might see a similar log ( ) message:
esxupdate.log
20**-**-**T13:37:50Z esxupdate: 5557508: BootBankInstaller.pyc:
ERROR: The pending transaction requires 245 MB free space,
however the maximum supported size is 239 MB.^@
Unused VIBs on the ESX host can be relatively large in size. These unused VIBs can result in insufficient space in the
bootbank or in the alt-bootbank when installing the required VIBs.
• Uninstall the VIBs that are no longer required and free up additional disk space.
For more information on deleting the unused VIBs, see Knowledge Base article 324231: NSX VIBs fail to install/upgrade,
due to insufficient space in bootbank on ESX host.
NSX Agent on ESX Transport Nodes Times Out Communicating with NSX
Manager
In a large-scale environment with many transport nodes and VMs on ESX hosts, NSX agents, which run on ESX hosts,
might time out when communicating with NSX Manager.
Some operations, such as when a VM vnic tries to attach to a logical switch, fail. The
/var/run/log/nsx-
has messages such as:
opsagent.log
level="ERROR" errorCode="MPA41542"] [MP_AddVnicAttachment] RPC call [0e316296-13-14] to NSX management plane
timout
2017-05-15T05:32:13Z nsxa: [nsx@6876 comp="nsx-esx" subcomp="NSXA[VifHandlerThread:-2282640]" tid="1000017079"
level="ERROR" errorCode="MPA42003"] [DoMpVifAttachRpc] MP_AddVnicAttachment() failed: RPC call to NSX
management plane timout
In a large-scale environment, some operations might take longer than usual and fail because the default timeout values
are exceeded.
Broadcom 3978

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Increase the NSX agent timeout (seconds) value.
a) On the ESX host, stop the NSX ops agent with the following command:
On NSX 2.3 or later releases:
/etc/init.d/nsx-opsagent stop
On NSX 2.1 or previous releases:
/etc/init.d/nsxa stop
b) Edit the file and change the value from 25
/etc/vmware/nsx-opsagent/nsxa.json vifOperationTimeout
seconds to, for example, 55 seconds.
"mp" : {
/* timeout for VIF operation */
"vifOperationTimeout" : 25,
Note:
This timeout value must be less than the hostd timeout value that you set in step 2.
c) Start the NSX ops agent with the following command:
/etc/init.d/nsx-opsagent start
2. Increase the hostd timeout (seconds) value.
a) On the ESX host, stop the hostd agent with the following command:
/etc/init.d/hostd stop
b) Edit the file . Under , uncomment the entry for
/etc/vmware/hostd/config.xml <opaqueNetwork>
and change the value from 30 seconds to, for example, 60 seconds.
<taskTimeout>
<opaqueNetwork>
<!-- maximum message size allowed in opaque network manager IPC, in bytes. -->
<!-- <maxMsgSize> 65536 </maxMsgSize> -->
<!-- maximum wait time for opaque network response -->
<!-- <taskTimeout> 30 </taskTimeout> -->
c) Start the hostd agent with the following command:
/etc/init.d/hostd start

the usage of heap memory.
To view edge node high availability status, status changes and reasons for it, run admin cli
get edge-cluster status
and . If the Edge STATE would be DOWN, implying either datapath process is not
get edge-cluster history state

get physical-port <port-name> get physical-port

<interface-name> stats
occurrence of packet loss. Packet loss may be seen if edge is flooded with traffic rate higher rate higher than the
datapath CPUs can process. Packets are first held in input/egress buffer and gets dropped if buffers are full. To check
the current buffer size configuration, use the CLI .
get dataplane | fing ring
5. If dataplane service is stopped, start by issuing cmd (as a temporary workaround).

6. If host switch port is down, start by issuing cmd (as a temporary

workaround).

You can also try to change the rx/tx buffer configuration (to enhance edge interface traffic management capacity)
using the CLI . The supported buffer size range is bytes and
set dataplane ring-size <rx/tx> <size> 128-4096
dataplane service needs to be restarted in order to make the new configuration effective resulting in a downtime of
about seconds.
60

b) . Restart dataplane service for the change to take effect.

restart service dataplane

VMotion of NSX Edge VM may fail in vCenter due to ESX running out of resources from a shared buffer pool.

To fix the issue, increase the P2M buffer slots for all the virtual machines on the host. For more information, see
Knowledge Base article 318766: Configuring P2M Buffer size for virtual machines.

Lifecycle Management
Use VCF Operations as a VI administrator to manage the lifecycle of the management and core components in VCF,
including downloading binaries and updating VCF fleet and VCF Instances.
For VCF, you use VCF Operations for these capabilities. For vSphere Foundation, you perform the supported operations
on the individual management components.
In This Chapter
• Binary Management for VMware Cloud Foundation
• Lifecycle Management of VCF Components
• Upgrading VMware Cloud Foundation Workload Domains to 9.1.x
Getting to Know VCF
To apply this documentation, you must be acquainted with the VCF Product Overview, VCF Design, and VCF Release
Notes.
VCF Component Classification
VCF components are classified based on the level at which they operate. VCF Management components operate on the
fleet level, while VCF core components operate on the instance level.
VCF Management Components VCF Core Components
• VCF Operations • SDDC Manager
– License server • vCenter
– Cloud proxy • NSX Manager
• VCF management services • ESX
• VCF Automation Optional:
• VCF Operations for networks • VCF Operations HCX*
* VCF Operations HCX is an optional component. Lifecycle operations for VCF Operations HCX are performed with VCF
core components.
Broadcom 3987

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Release Types
The VCF release policy defines four distinct release types, each with a specific purpose, scope, and set of lifecycle rules.
Approximate
Type Description
Release Cadence
Major A major release, such as 9.0.0.0 or 10.0.0.0, represents the most significant 3 years
evolution of the VCF platform. It introduces major features and changes that
can redefine the platform's capabilities. This is the only release type that can
introduce breaking changes or remove existing functionality. However, this is
governed by a strict deprecation policy designed to protect enterprise stability:
a feature must be officially announced for deprecation in a prior major release
before it can be removed in a subsequent one.
Major releases are fully synchronized, meaning all VCF components are
upgraded in lockstep as part of a single release. They follow a unified
consumption pattern, requiring a full-stack upgrade.
Minor A minor release, such as 9.1.0.0 or 9.2.0.0, is the primary mechanism for 9 months
delivering new features and enhancements within a major version. These
releases include features and are designed to be functionally additive. Minor
releases aim to be non-disruptive from a compatibility and API perspective.
Like major releases, minor releases are fully synchronized and follow the unified
consumption pattern. The policy that "All components are upgraded in a major
and minor release" applies here, ensuring the entire platform advances to a
new, consistent feature level.
Maintenance A maintenance release, such as 9.0.1.0 or 9.0.2.0, is a scheduled, cumulative 3 months
upgrade, focused on enhancing platform stability and support. Maintenance
releases provide bug and security fixes, hardware enablement changes, such
as support for servers, CPUs, devices, driver updates, guest OS support, and
backward-compatible new features. They are limited in scope to minimize the
operational impact. You can pick and choose which components to apply based
on the impact on your environment and operational costs. For example, if you
run into a critical issue with vCenter, you do not need to apply a patch to ESX
that is irrelevant to your environment. Maintenance releases are synchronized
among VCF components with a new Bill Of Materials.
Express Patch Express patch releases, such as 9.0.1.0100 or 9.0.1.0300, provide component- As needed
level, time-sensitive fixes to security and catastrophic issues, impacting
business operations, that must be released between major, minor, and
maintenance releases.
Express patches are released at the component level only and are not
synchronized across VCF components. Express patches do not require a new
implementation of a Bill of Materials.
Express patch releases for a given component do not always follow a strict
sequence. Each patch release increments the second digit of the fourth
version field (x.y.z.a) but can skip values. For example, the first patch might
be 9.1.0.0100, and the next patch for that component might be 9.1.0.0300 or
9.1.0.0500 and so on.
Hot Patch Hot patch releases, such as 9.0.1.0101 or 9.0.1.0112, provide on-demand, As needed
component-level fixes for issues with limited impact where standard express
patch payloads are not viable.
Hot patches are released at the component level only and are not synchronized
across VCF components. Hot patches do not require a new implementation of a
Bill of Materials.
Hot patches are not cumulative, a higher version number does not include all
previous content. Security fixes are prohibited in hot patches unless the fixes
were already released in a generally available patch.

categories within VCF release types.

VCF Lifecycle Operation Types
VCF defines two types of lifecycle operations to increase your VCF version:
Lifecycle
Description Release Type Version Change
Operation Type
Upgrade An upgrade is defined as a change to the major or minor Major 9.0.0.0000 to 10.0.0.000
version of a VCF component. Upgrades are synchronized
Minor 9.0.0.0000 to 9.1.0.0000
across all VCF components and require a new Bill of
Materials (BoM), meaning the entire platform advances to a
new, consistent feature level in lockstep.
Patch A patch is defined as a change to the maintenance or Maintenance 9.0.0.0000 to 9.0.1.0000
patch version of a VCF component, while the major and
Express Patch 9.0.1.0000 to 9.0.1.0200
minor versions remain unchanged. There is no enforced
patch order for maintenance or patch releases. Any Hot Patch 9.0.1.0000 to 9.0.1.0003
VCF component can be patched independently of other
components. However, specific component dependencies
may apply for certain releases, requiring one component to
be patched before another, as documented in the release
notes.
Lifecycle Management in VCF Operations
VCF Operations provides a comprehensive set of tools for managing the lifecycle of VCF components. You can use VCF
Operations to download and manage upgrade, patch, and install binaries. You can also manage ESX components and
vSphere Lifecycle Manager images and deploy, upgrade, and patch additional VCF components.
For VCF 9.0 and later, VCF Operations manages major, minor, maintenance, and patch releases for your VCF
environment. With the introduction of VCF management services in VCF 9.1, VCF Operations now uses the fleet lifecycle,
SDDC lifecycle, and software depot components to orchestrate lifecycle operations on both fleet and instance-level
components. In addition, the fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle components now replace the VCF Operations fleet
management appliance.
With VCF management services, VCF Operations now uses a declarative lifecycle model. You define a target version for
your VCF environment and VCF Operations orchestrates the upgrade or patch processes, including planning, required
binaries, and additional dependencies. This approach consolidates management resources and ensures high availability
for lifecycle operations.
SDKs, APIs, and CLI for VCF Administration

Administration SDKs, APIs, and CLI.

Binary Management for VMware Cloud Foundation
With VCF 9.1, you perform lifecycle management of VCF components by using the VCF Operations UI and the software
depot component, which handles binaries for all VCF components.
Software Depot Overview
A software depot is VCF 9.1 or later component that serves an internal store for installation, upgrade, patch binaries, and
Open Container Initiative (OCI) images. A software depot can operate on the fleet-level or optionally on an instance-level.
Each VCF Instance can have one software depot instance that is assigned to it.
First Software Depot (Fleet-Level)
Each VCF fleet has a fleet-level software depot that is deployed on the first VCF Instance and can provide binaries for
all VCF Instances in the fleet. When deploying a new VCF Instance version 9.1 or later, the fleet-level software depot is
automatically assigned to the instance. When deploying a new VCF fleet or upgrading an existing one to version 9.1 or
later, the depot settings from VCF Installer or SDDC Manager are transferred to the fleet-level software depot.
Secondary Software Depot (Instance-Level)
If the network latency between the software depot of your first VCF Instance and another VCF Instance exceeds 150 ms,
you can deploy a secondary local software depot within the other VCF Instance. See Deploy a Secondary Software Depot
Instance. After deploying a secondary software depot, assign it to a VCF Instance. See Assign a Software Depot to VCF
Instances.
Offline Depot
If your VCF environment does not have access to the Internet, you can configure an internal web server to host binaries,
and ESX component data. Starting with VCF 9.1.1, you can host also artifacts. By using the VCF Download Tool, the web
server connects to the Broadcom online repository, downloads installation, upgrade, and patch binaries, and hosts them
for use in your environment.
VCF Download Tool
The VCF Download Tool is a command-line utility that is used to download and manage binaries and metadata for
VMware Cloud Foundation platforms in environments without Internet access. The tool provides commands for
downloading, uploading, listing, and cleaning up VCF component and ESX binaries, supporting the management of VCF
components required for VMware Cloud Foundation releases.
Configure a Software Depot Connection Mode
You can configure each software depot instance in one of the three available modes to access binaries, hardware
compatibility data, software interoperability data, and lifecycle metadata. The mode depends on how you access the
Internet in your environment.
• If you plan to use software depot in connected mode, but your environment does not have direct access to the Internet,
verify you configured a proxy server. See Configure a Proxy Server for VCF Management Services Components and
VCF Automation.
Broadcom 3990

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Verify that your VCF Business Services console role has sufficient permissions. See Access Management.
Table 1087: Software Depot Modes
Connection Mode Description
Connected Use this option if your environment has access to the Internet,
either directly or through a proxy server. Register your software
depot with VCF Business Service console to directly download
binaries, hardware compatibility data, software interoperability
data, and lifecycle metadata.
Offline Depot Use this option if your environment cannot connect to the Internet,
but you have a privately owned server that you use as an offline
depot. You use the VCF Download Tool to download the required
binaries to your offline depot. In this mode, software depot
does not download binaries locally. Instead, it proxies requests
from VCF components to the privately owned server. For more
information, see Download Binaries to an Offline Depot by Using
the VCF Download Tool.
Disconnected Use this option if your environment cannot connect to the Internet
and you have no offline depot. You use the VCF Download Tool to
download the required binaries to a computer with Internet access.
You then manually upload the binaries to the software depot. For
more information, see Download Binaries to Software Depot in
Disconnected Mode by Using the VCF Download Tool.
For information about the URLs that must be accessible to download binaries, see Public URLs Required for Online
Functionalities for VCF and vSphere Foundation.

Set Up an Offline Depot
To use VCF Installer or software depot with an offline depot, you must configure an internal web server to host VCF
binaries and ESX component data. You use the VCF Download Tool to connect to the Broadcom depot and download the
binaries to the internal web server.
The offline depot web server must meet the following requirements:
• Operating System: A Linux or Windows virtual machine. For Linux, any distribution is supported (for example, CentOS,
RHEL, Ubuntu). For example, you can use Photon OS. See https://packages.broadcom.com/photon/.
• Storage: A dedicated disk for storing offline depot content. Minimum recommended size: 1 TB.
• Web Server and SSL: A web server to serve the offline depot content over HTTP/HTTPS. For HTTPS, the server must
support TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3. The choice of web server is flexible. For example: Apache HTTP Server, NGINX, and
so on.
• Networking and Access: The virtual machine must have a static IP address. DNS records for the offline depot server
are recommended but not required.
• User Access: A dedicated non-root user on the virtual machine. The user must have read/write access to the offline
depot directory and appropriate permissions to run VCF Download Tool commands.
The following procedure describes how to set up an Apache HTTP Server on a Photon OS 5 virtual machine. Depending
on your environment, you might need to modify some of the commands. For example, if corporate policies require you to
use a different operating system or web server.

Download Binaries to an Offline Depot by Using the VCF Download Tool
You can use the VCF Download Tool to download VCF component binaries and ESX component data to an offline depot
and connect software depot to it.
• Verify that you have configured a web server that serves as an offline depot. See Set Up an Offline Depot.
• Verify that the machine where you plan to download and use VCF Download Tool has Internet connectivity (either
directly or through a proxy) to download the binaries and other required files.
• Verify that the offline depot has TCP keepalive configured in your SSH client to prevent socket connection timeouts
when using the VCF Download Tool for long-running operations.
• Verify that your VCF Business Services console role has sufficient permissions. See Access Management.
The following procedure uses the VCF Download Tool to download VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1 installation, upgrade
binaries, artifacts, ESX binaries, and metadata to software depot in offline depot mode and involves the following steps.
Download the latest version of the VCF Download Tool on a computer with access to the Internet or the offline depot web
server.
• Generate an activation code from the VCF Business Services console.
• Download installation, upgrade, and ESX binaries and metadata.
• If the VCF Download Tool and web server are on separate machines, transfer the downloaded binaries to the offline
depot.
Broadcom 3998

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
For artifacts that contains OCI images, you must upload the artifacts to software depot by using the VCF
Download Tool. See Upload OCI Images When Software Depot Is in Offline Mode.
Important Considerations
• The VCF Download Tool is the only supported method for downloading binaries for VCF 9.1 and later in environments
without Internet access. Do not use third-party tools or other methods to download binaries.
• If you have a vSphere Foundation license, in the following commands, replace with .
--sku VCF --sku VVF
• If the computer hosting the offline depot can only access the Internet using a proxy server, you can use proxy settings
when downloading binaries. See Proxy Server Options.
• VMware Cloud Foundation does not support proxy servers with Kerberos or NTLMv2 authentication.

ode.txt Services Console.

Download Binaries to Software Depot in Disconnected Mode by Using the VCF
Download Tool
If software depot does not have access to an online or offline depot, you can use the VCF Download Tool to download
binaries and ESX component data to a different computer and then upload the binaries and data to software depot.
• A Windows or Linux computer with Internet connectivity (either directly or through a proxy) for downloading the binaries
and other required files.
• Configure TCP keepalive in your SSH client to prevent socket connection timeouts for long-running operations.

Assign a Software Depot to VCF Instances
You can choose which software depot instances are used by the VCF Instances in your environment.
You can assign your first and secondary software depot instances to specific VCF Instances, even when the software
depot instance is not deployed on that VCF Instance. For example, if you deployed a secondary software depot instance
to a VCF Instance, you can assign that software depot instance to another VCF Instance in the same region. Later, if
needed, you can reassign the first software depot instance to any of these VCF instances. For more information about
software depot instances, see Binary Management for VMware Cloud Foundation.
1. Log in to VCF Operations at <vcf_operations_fqdn> with a user assigned the Administrator role.
https://
2. Select Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management.
3. On the Components tab, from the list of components of your first VCF instance, click Software depot.
4. Select Actions > Assign to VCF Instance.
5. In the Assign Sofware Depot to VCF Instance wizard, select the VCF Instances to assign the software depot to.
6. Click Assign.
VCF Download Tool Command Reference Information
The VCF download tool is a command-line utility that you use to download and manage VCF component binaries and
metadata in air-gapped environments. It provides commands for downloading, uploading, listing, and cleaning up binaries
and metadata to help you prepare and maintain VCF artifacts.
The VCF Download Tool provides a suite of commands for downloading, uploading, listing, and cleaning up VCF
component and ESX binaries, enabling efficient management of software components for VMware Cloud Foundation
releases. With its comprehensive features, the VCF Download Tool helps streamline the process of preparing, managing,
and maintaining VCF-related artifacts in your environment.
VCF Download Tool General Options
Use the VCF download tool general options to display help, check the tool version, and manage your Customer
Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) participation and proxy server settings.
Broadcom 4004

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Help Options
Option Description
-h, --help Displays all available VCF Download Tool commands and top-
level options.
binaries -h, binaries --help Displays the options and filters available for downloading, listing,
exporting, and cleaning up VCF component binaries.
depot -h, depot --help Displays the commands available for uploading, listing, and
removing artifacts and binaries in a connected software depot.
metadata -h, metadata --help Displays the options available for downloading and managing VCF
component metadata.
releases -h, releases --help Displays the options available for listing and filtering VCF release
information.
esx -h, esx --help Displays the options available for downloading and managing ESX
binaries and depot configurations.
artifacts -h, artifacts --help Starting with VCF Dowload Tool 9.1.1 and later, this option
displays the options and filters available for downloading, listing,
exporting, and cleaning up workload component artifacts in a local
depot store.
Version Option
Option Description
-v, --version Displays the version of the VCF Download Tool.
Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) Option
The VCF download tool supports the Broadcom Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP), which collects
product usage data to improve the customer experience. You can activate or deactivate CEIP participation at any time.
For more information, see Customer Experience Improvement Program.
Option Description
--ceip ENABLE or --ceip DISABLE Enables or disables participation in CEIP. The first time you run
the VCF Download Tool, you are prompted to choose whether to
participate. The tool saves your selection as the default for future
runs. To change your selection, specify this option again with a
different value.
Broadcom 4005

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Table 1088: Proxy Server Options
If the machine, where VCF Download Tool is installed, can access the Internet only by using a proxy server, use the
following options when using the , , , and tool commands. The command
binaries metadata releases esx depot
cannot use the proxy filter. Staring with VCF Download Tool 9.1.1 and later, you can use these options with the
command.
artifacts
Option Description
--proxy-server, -s Enter the FQDN and port number of the proxy server that the VCF Download Tool uses to
access the Internet. Use the format FQDN:port. The proxy server must be reachable from
the machine where the tool is running.
For example: --proxyServer proxy.example.com:3128.
--proxy-https Specifies that the proxy server uses HTTPS connections. To use this option, add the proxy
certificate to the JRE default trust store of the VCF Download Tool. The exact path to the /
cacerts folder depends on the directory where you extracted the VCF Download Tool tar
file.
For example:
• Unix
/opt/obtu/jre/lin64/bin/keytool -importcert -file ca-bundle.crt -
keystore <tool root>/jre/lin64/lib/security/cacerts
• Windows
/opt/obtu/jre/lin64/bin/keytool -importcert -file ca-bundle.crt -
keystore <tool root>/jre/win32/lib/security/cacerts
--proxy-user, -r Enter the username required to authenticate with the proxy server. Use this option when the
proxy server requires authentication.

r. The file must contain only the password on a single line.

Broadcom 4007

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Description
--component-version ComponentVersion Filters the operation to binaries for a specific component version.
Replace ComponentVersion with the version number to filter
by.
--lifecycle-managed-by lcm Filters the operation to binaries whose lifecycle is managed by
the specified component. Replace lcm with one of the following
values:
• SDDC_MANAGER_VCF (SDDC Manager)
• VRSLCM (VCF Operations fleet management, 9.0 only)
• VCF_FLEET_LCM (Fleet Lifecycle)
• SELF (Self-managed)
--patches-only Filters the operation to binaries for patch versions of components
only.
--sku sku Filters the operation to binaries for the specified product SKU.
Replace sku with VCF for VMware Cloud Foundation or VVF for
VMware vSphere Foundation.
-t type or Filters the operation to binaries of the specified type. Replace
--type type type with INSTALL for installation binaries or UPGRADE for
upgrade binaries.
--upgrades-only Filters the operation to binaries for upgrade versions of
components only.
--vcf-version version[..[end version]] Filters the operation to binaries for a specific VCF version or
version range. You can use the following formats:
Downloads / Lists / Cleans up / Exports binaries for a specific
version versionof VMware Cloud Foundation, or for a range of
versions .
You can enter the version string in the following formats:
• a.b: For example, if you enter 9.0, the tool downloads the
binaries for 9.0.0.0 and any 9.0.x binaries.
• a.b.c: For example, if you enter 9.0.1, the tool downloads all
9.0.1.x binaries.
• a.b.c.d: For example, if you enter 9.0.1.0, the tool only
downloads 9.0.1.0 binaries.
• For a version range, specify start_version..end_ver
sion. The tool includes binaries for both the start and end
versions.
--id bundleIds Filters the operation to one or more specific binaries by bundle
ID. Replace bundleIds with a single bundle ID or a comma-
separated list of bundle IDs.
--download-spec-file downloadSpecFile Filters the download to only the binaries required for a specific
planned upgrade. Replace downloadSpecFile with the path to
the download specification file generated by the create-downl
oad-spec command.
--latest In VCF Download Tool 9.1.1 and later, filters the operation to
only the latest available versions of the binaries (such as the
latest Express Patches for required components). This behavior
is enabled by default. To override this and include all available
versions, specify the --latest false filter option.

Binaries Commands
Command Description
Downloads VCF binaries and metadata, including the unified
download
release manifest, product version catalog, vSAN HCL, and
compatibility data. At least one filter option is required.
When you run the command multiple times against the same
output directory, the tool adds newly downloaded binaries to the
existing content without overwriting it.
Uploads downloaded binaries and metadata to software depot.
upload
Lists all available VCF binaries. At least one filter option is
list
required. For each binary, the command displays the component
name, version number, release date, size, and type. Use this
command to identify relevant binaries before downloading.
Removes unwanted or obsolete binaries from the local depot store
cleanup
while retaining binaries you still need. Run this command on a
machine where you have already downloaded binaries.
Generates a download specification file based on the planned
create-download-spec
upgrades for a specific workload domain. Use the generated file
as input to the download command with --download-spe
c-file to download only the binaries required for the planned
upgrade.
export Archives locally downloaded binaries and metadata into a tar file
for transfer to another system.
With VCF 9.1.1 and later, to reduce storage requirements, for example, when there are multiple express patches for a
VCF component version, only the latest patch for each component is downloaded. To download all the patches, you can
add the false filter option. This option default to true and is applicable to the , , , and
--latest download upload list
commands.
export

Command Description

Broadcom 4011

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Depot Binaries Options
Command Description
upload Uploads metadata and binaries to software depot. Provide either
a tar archive of binaries using --depot-file, or a depot store
path with --depot-store together with filter options to select
which binaries to upload.
cleanup Removes unwanted or obsolete binaries from software depot
while retaining the binaries you still need. Run this command on a
machine that already has binaries downloaded to the depot store.
list Lists all binaries available in software depot. At least one filter
option is required. For each binary, the command displays the
component name, version number, release date, size, and type.
Use this command to assess software depot contents before
downloading or uploading.

Metadata Commands
Command Description
Downloads all metadata required by software depot. in a single
download
operation, including the unified release manifest, product version
catalog, vSAN HCL, and compatibility data. The tool automatically
retrieves all relevant metadata files.
Note:
This command does not download ESX metadata. Use
the esx metadata command for ESX metadata.
Uploads all downloaded metadata to software depot. Before
upload
running this command, transfer the downloaded metadata to a
machine that can reach software depot.
export Archives locally downloaded metadata into a tar file for transfer to
another system.

URLs and enabled host platforms.

VCF Download Tool Artifacts Commands
Starting with VCF Dowload Tool 9.1.1 and later, you can use the commands to list, download, export, and
artifacts

Artifacts Commands
Artifacts are the binary files, OCI images, and associated metadata that is required to install, upgrade, and manage
VCF services such as Supervisor, VKS, and VCF Consumption CLI. Unlike the commands, which download
binaries
VCF core and management component binaries, the commands target workload component artifacts - the
artifacts
software packages that run on top of the VCF platform.
You use the commands to download, list, clean up, and export these files to a local depot store for use in air-
artifacts
gapped environments.
Command Description
download Downloads all workload component artifacts and their associated
metadata. At least one filter option is required. The command
supports filtering to narrow the selection of artifacts based on
the intended operation. When you run the command multiple
times against the same output directory, the tool adds newly
downloaded artifacts to the existing content without overwriting it.
list Lists all available workload component artifacts. At least one
filter option is required. For each artifact, the command displays
the component name, version number, size, and type. Use this
command to identify relevant artifacts before downloading.
cleanup Removes unwanted or obsolete workload component artifacts
from the local depot store while retaining the artifacts you still
need. Run this command on a machine where you have already
downloaded artifacts.
export Exports locally downloaded workload component artifacts into a
tar file for transfer to another system.

Lifecycle Management of VCF Components
Use VCF Operations to upgrade or patch VCF components.
Before you can deploy, upgrade, or patch the VCF management components, you must download the necessary binaries
to software depot See Binary Management for VMware Cloud Foundation.
After downloading the necessary binaries, you can proceed with deployment, upgrade, or patch.
• For deployment, see: Completing the Deployment of Your Platform and Adding or Removing VCF Components Post
Deployment.
• For upgrading to a major or a minor version, see: Upgrading to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x.
• For applying maintenance or patch releases, see Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component.
You can also use software depot to manage ESX components and vSphere Lifecycle Manager images.
Forward-Only Upgrade Requirement
VCF enforces strict upgrade path validation. You can only upgrade your VCF components to a target version that is
released after the release date of your current version. The target version can be a major, minor, or a maintenance
release. In general, you can upgrade directly to a patch release only if you can also upgrade to its parent maintenance
release. For example:
• Supported: VCF 5.2.0 (25 JUN 2024) to VCF 9.1.0 (11 MAY 2026).
• Not supported: VCF 5.2.4 (27 MAY 2026) to VCF 9.1.0 (11 MAY 2026).
• Supported: VCF 5.2.4 (27 MAY 2026) to VCF 9.1.1 (03 SEP 2026).
This is valid for all components in a VCF source BoM. For example:
• Supported upgrade to VCF 9.1.0 (11 MAY 2026): vCenter 8.0 Update 3a (18 JUN 2024) and ESX 8.0 Update 3 (25
JUN 2024), which are part of VCF 5.2.0 BoM.
• Not supported upgrade to VCF 9.1.0 (11 MAY 2026): vCenter 8.0 Update 3j (27 MAY 2026) and ESX 8.0 Update 3j (27
MAY 2026), which are part of VCF 5.2.4 BoM.
• Supported upgrade to VCF 9.1.1 (03 SEP 2026): vCenter 8.0 Update 3j (27 MAY 2026) and ESX 8.0 Update 3j (27
MAY 2026), which are part of VCF 5.2.4 BoM.
VCF components might have further limitations, see VMware Interoperability Matrix.
Broadcom 4025

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

• For workload domain upgrade order, see

component. See VCF Lifecycle Operation Types. instruct you to follow a specific order.
The 9.1.1 maintenance release has specific

from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1.
Maintenance and patch releases do not affect component interoperability. You apply maintenance and patch releases as
per the needs of your organization, unless the release notes explicitly instruct you to follow a specific order.
Before you apply a maintenance or a patch release, plan for possible downtime of certain functionalities performed by the
component and consider the impact on other services in the SDDC. For example, when patching software depot, no other
lifecycle operations can be performed, due to their dependency on the availability of install, upgrade, and patch binaries.
For more information on the functionalities of the components, see Components in VCF and vSphere Foundation.
Patching VCF from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1
VCF 9.1.1 has specific patching dependencies between VCF components:
1. You begin applying the 9.1.1 maintenance release in your 9.1.0.x environment by patching the VCF management
services fleet lifecycle component to 9.1.1 before any other VCF component.
2. After the fleet lifecycle component is at version 9.1.1, you must comply only with the following dependencies:
a. VCF Operations must not be patched in parallel with other components. Before you patch VCF Operations, ensure
that no other lifecycle operations in the environment are in progress. Do not start other lifecycle operations until the
VCF Operations patch process completes.
b. Before you patch ESX hosts from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1.0, you must first patch the VCF Operations instance and the
license servers connected to it.
c. Before you patch an identity broker instance from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1, you must first patch the respective VCF
management services runtime that hosts the identity broker instance.
d. Before you patch Salt RaaS from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1, you must first patch the respective VCF management services
runtime that hosts the Salt RaaS instance.
e. Before you patch the migration service engine component from 9.1.0.x to 9.1.1, you must first patch VCF
Automation.
f. When you patch a software depot instance, patching other components is blocked because the patch binaries are
unavailable until the patch process for the software depot completes.
License Server and Cloud Proxy
The lifecycle management of the license server and the cloud proxy components is bundled with the lifecycle
management of VCF Operations. Upgrading or patching VCF Operations automatically upgrades or patches license
server and cloud proxy.
Shared NSX Instances
For NSX instances that are shared across multiple domains, you must upgrade the NSX, vCenter, and ESX components
in all domains that share the NSX instance. If you cancel the automatically created upgrade plan for a dependent domain,
Broadcom 4026

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
the upgrade plan for all domains that share the NSX instance is also canceled. If the upgrade plan is canceled, you must
create another upgrade plan.
For example, if you create a domain upgrade plan or shared NSX upgrade plan for domain A, you must add and upgrade
the vCenter instance and all ESX hosts in this domain. Before you can finalize the upgrade, you must visit domain B, add
the vCenter and ESX components to the component upgrade plan, and upgrade all three components. After you upgrade
the vCenter, ESX, and NSX components in domain B and all other dependent domains, you can finalize the upgrade in
domain A and the dependent domains.
Note:
If an NSX 9.1 instance is shared between a management domain and workload domain(s), when all other
components are upgraded, you must start the VMware NSX Manager Nodes Upgrade and VMware NSX Edge
Cluster Upgrade and NSX Upgrade Finalize upgrade steps from the management domain only.
VCF Component Version Tracking
To verify the current versions of your VCF components, in VCF Operations, you click Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instance,
then select a VCF domain. The Component Versions tab displays information for supported components, such as
current version, target version, and status for each component. The tab displays version information for cluster hosts
and standalone hosts, and compares installed versions with target versions to identify version drift. For clusters with ESX
hosts that run different versions, a warning appears. The displayed cluster version represents the minimum version across
all hosts in the cluster.
Tracked VCF Components
• SDDC Manager
• vCenter
• NSX Manager
• ESX clusters and hosts
• Standalone ESX hosts
• HCX
Option Description
On Target The current component version matches the target version.
Version Drift The current component version differs from the target version.
Target versions are defined when you create a domain or component upgrade plan. When no target version is configured,
the current version is used as the target, and the status displays as On Target.
Upgrade or Patch an Individual VCF Component
Use VCF Operations to upgrade or apply a patch to an individual VCF component.
• If you are upgrading or patching VCF core components you must download the respective patch binaries. The
method that you use to download binaries depends on how you access the Internet in your environment. See Binary
Management for VMware Cloud Foundation. If you are connected to the online depot, binaries are available in the
patch planner. If you do not have access to an online depot, use the VCF Download Tool to download binaries. See
Download Binaries to an Offline Depot by Using the VCF Download Tool or Download Binaries to Software Depot in
Disconnected Mode by Using the VCF Download Tool.
• Before you upgrade or patch, back up the component. See Component Backup and Restore of VMware Cloud
Foundation.
You can upgrade a single component to a maintenance release. You can apply a patch release to a single component at a
time. If an upgrade or a patch operation is in progress, you cannot upgrade or patch another component.

Managing vSphere Lifecycle Manager Images for VMware Cloud Foundation
VMware Cloud Foundation uses vSphere Lifecycle Manager images to apply software and firmware updates to the ESX
hosts in an SDDC cluster.
You create vSphere Lifecycle Manager images in the vSphere Client and then import them into a VCF Instance using VCF
Operations. You can use imported images when you:
• Upgrade the management domain or a workload domain.
• Create a workload domain.
• Add an SDDC cluster to the management domain or a workload domain.
Clusters can have up to four additional image definitions to make on a single composite image of the cluster.
The base ESX version is static for all additional images and cannot be customized. The vendor addon, firmware, and
components of each image definition can be customized to accommodate clusters with mixed hardware. Each additional
image definition can have a unique hardware support manager (HSM) attached.
You can create a composite image for a cluster that has hosts from different vendors or from the same vendor but different
generations, family, or model. A composite image contains one default image and one or more alternative images. All
images in a composite image contain the same base image and solutions, but may include different vendor or firmware
and driver add-ons.
Additional images can be manually assigned to a subset of hosts in a cluster, or automatically using System BIOS
information including Vendor, Model, OEM String and Family values.
For more information about vSphere Lifecycle Manager images, see Managing Host and Cluster Lifecycle in the vSphere
documentation.
Import a vSphere Lifecycle Manager Image to a VCF Instance
After you create vSphere Lifecycle Manager images in the vSphere Client, you can import those images into VCF
Operations and use them for creating and updating VCF domains and clusters.
Create a vSphere Lifecycle Manager image using the vSphere Client. See How to Use the Image Library in a vCenter
Instance.
• Use the ESX version specified in the VMware Cloud Foundation BOM.
• You can create a composite image for a cluster that has hosts from different vendors or from the same vendor but
different generations, family, or model. A composite image contains one default image and one or more alternative
images. All images in a composite image contain the same base image and solutions, but may include different vendor
or firmware and driver add-ons. When you create alternate images, you also specify the rules that are used to filter the
hosts to which the alternative image is assigned.
• If you plan to use the Import from a file option to import a vSphere Lifecycle Manager image, you must first export the
files from the vSphere Client. See How to Use the Image Library in a vCenter Instance.

To upgrade to a VMware Cloud Foundation workload domain to 9.1.x, all workload domains must be at VMware Cloud

upgrade to 9.1.x.

Getting to Know VCF
To apply this documentation, you must be acquainted with the VCF Product Overview, VCF Design, and VCF Release
Notes.
Deploying or Converging to VCF and Setting Up Cloud Infrastructure
For information about deploying or converging to a VCF fleet or VCF Instance, see Deployment, Convergence, and
Upgrade. For information about adding infrastructure and configuring storage and networking for workloads in VCF
Operations and the vSphere Client as a VI administrator, see Building Cloud Infrastructure.
Managing the Lifecycle of Your VCF Platform
You can manage software binaries and update your VCF fleet and VCF Instance centrally in VCF Operations. See
Lifecycle Management.
SDKs, APIs, and CLI for VCF Administration
You can build, operate, and manage your VCF private cloud by using the VCF SDK and APIs, and VCF PowerCLI. See
Administration SDKs, APIs, and CLI.
Managing Identity and Access With VCF Single Sign-On
Streamline identity and access management across your environment by configuring VCF single sign-on (SSO). This
centralized approach allows you to assign granular permissions for every component using global roles, all from a single
pane of glass. Furthermore, you can manage custom roles across multiple vCenter instances simultaneously, while API
access provides a reliable foundation for your automation workflows.
• To configure and set up VCF single sign-on, see Configuring VCF Single Sign-On.
Broadcom 4032

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• To create custom VCF roles and for more information about built-in VCF roles, see Managing VCF Roles.
• To provision a vCenter custom role to the vCenter instances in a VCF Instance, see Provisioning vCenter Custom
Roles.
• To manage API clients, API tokens, and access tokens, see Managing API Clients and Tokens .
• To migrate VMware Identity Manager to identity broker, see Migrating VMware Identity Manager to Identity Broker.
Configuring VCF Single Sign-On
You can set up VCF single sign-on for VCF to streamline user access with centralized authentication. VCF single sign-
on offers Enterprise admin users the ability to utilize single sign-on and access VCF components such as vCenter,
VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations for networks, VCF Operations orchestrator, VCF Operations HCX,
Salt RaaS, and NSX, with one set of credentials. VCF single sign-on provides a secure login experience with a single
authentication source that you configure from VCF Operations across all VCF components except SDDC Manager and
ESX.
Benefits of VCF Single Sign-On
VCF single sign-on provides multiple benefits:
• Improved user experience as users can log in once and can gain access to the VCF components they have been
granted access to.
• Enhanced security as you reduce password fatigue and strengthen protection against unauthorized access.
• Centralized management as you manage the identity provider configuration and user/group provisioning across VCF
Instances at a central location in VCF Operations.
• Support for multiple identity providers protocols such as OIDC 2.0, SAML 2.0, and directory services such as
OpenLDAP and Active Directory.
Identity Providers and Protocols Supported for VCF Single Sign-On
After you deploy VCF, you can configure VCF single sign-on by using an external identity provider and then sign in to VCF
components by using VCF single sign-on. The identity broker component handles the single sign-on functionality.
Note:
You can configure a single identity provider per identity broker instance.
Identity Providers Supported
You can configure the following identity providers:
• Okta
• Ping Identity
• Microsoft Entra ID
• Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS)
• Symantec Identity Security Platform
• Any SAML 2.0 Identity Providers
• Any OIDC 1.0 Identity Providers
You can configure the following directory services:
• Active Directory over LDAP (AD/LDAP)
• OpenLDAP
Authentication Protocols Supported
• Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML 2.0).
An XML-based protocol where the identity provider issues digitally signed XML-based assertions to the service
provider for user authentication.
• OpenID Connect protocol (OIDC).
Broadcom 4033

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
An authentication protocol built on OAuth 2.0, where the identity provider issues an ID token in JSON format for user
authentication.
User/Group Provisioning
As part of configuring VCF Single Sign-On, you sync users and groups in the identity broker component provisioned from
your identity provider. The following protocols are supported:
1. SCIM 2.0 (System for cross-domain identity management)
2. JIT (Just-In-Time)
a. Just-In-Time Group Provisioning
• Groups are created dynamically based on the SAML assertion or OIDC authentication response when the user
logs in for the first time. You can use group pre-provisioning if you know the group names from the identity
provider that requires entitlements.
b. JIT pre-provisioning of groups
• You create the required groups in advance to perform role assignments. Users will be assigned to these groups
dynamically on their first log in based on SAML assertion or OIDC authentication response. Only the groups
pre-provisioned are available for role assignments before the first log in.
Note:
When Just-In-Time (JIT) user provisioning is enabled, a user object is automatically created upon successful
login, based on the SAML or OIDC authentication response. Group memberships are assigned according to
the group claims in the response. However, based on how JIT provisioning works, if the user later leaves the
organization and is removed from the external identity provider, the JIT-provisioned user is not automatically
deleted from the system.
3. AD/LDAP (Active Directory over LDAP) and on-demand provisioning for AD/LDAP
Users and groups are synced at periodic intervals. The entire directory is not synced, only users and groups that are
specified. Passwords are never synced.
Note:
You can use SAML 2.0 or OIDC as an authentication source and SCIM, JIT, and AD/LDAP as user-group
provisioning.
For operational guidance and prerequisites, see Identity and Access Management, Choosing an Identity Provider Type,
and VCF SSO User and Group Provisioning Options.
VCF Single Sign-On Architecture
VCF allows organizations to configure VCF single sign-on across a fleet of VCF Instances based on your preference for
manageability and availability.
There are one or more potential designs for VCF single sign-on configuration which depend on the deployment of the
identity broker instances across your VCF Instances. For more information, see VCF Single Sign-On Detailed Design.
Deployment Modes of the Identity Broker
When you configure VCF single sign-on, you can implement the identity broker that manages it, as embedded in the
management domain vCenter or you can deploy it as a VCF management services component.
Instance Deployment Mode
The identity broker component is deployed as a VCF management services component within the management domain of
the chosen VCF Instance. Your environment must meet the minimum requirements for the identity broker instance.

Considerations and Prerequisites for VCF Single Sign-On
When you configure VCF single sign-on, it is important that you understand the following important points and ensure that
you carry out the prerequisites.
Points to Consider While Setting Up VCF Single Sign-On
• SDDC Manager UI Client authentication is not compatible with VCF single sign-on
After you configure VCF single sign-on in the management domain vCenter, administrators are no longer able to log in
to the SDDC Manager UI client with VCF single sign-on users.
– SDDC Manager UI supports logins only with local admin accounts such as .
@vsphere.local users
– The SDDC Manager APIs support logins with VCF single sign-on users.
• VCF single sign-on is not compatible with Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM)
Before you configure VCF single sign-on, you must deactivate ELM on all participating vCenter Instances. For more
information, see Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode for Standalone vCenter Instances Using the cmsso-util break-elm
Utililty. If you upgraded from VCF 5.x to 9.0, see Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode for Management and Workload
vCenter Instances Using the SDDC Manager API.
• Manage VCF single sign-on only from VCF Operations and not from the individual components
After you configure VCF single sign-on from VCF Operations, you can no longer configure any identity sources in
vCenter instances that are configured for VCF single sign-on.
• PowerCLI impact
– PowerCLI automations continue to work if the identity provider is configured in the management domain vCenter in
embedded mode.
– If the identity provider is configured in an alternate management domain vCenter or in instance mode, the
integration must be re-performed. Follow the steps in Using VCF Single Sign-On to Access vCenter using
PowerCLI.
Broadcom 4036

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• The users that configures VCF single sign-on in VCF Operations must have access to all objects
The 'All Objects' scope must be assigned in VCF Operations. Navigate to Administration > Control Panel > Access
Control > User Accounts/User Groups and assign the 'All Objects' scope to the required user/group.
• Behavior of identity and access management after setting up VCF single sign-on
– The management layer of VCF single sign-on is always in VCF Operations.
– You can connect a standalone vCenter directly either to an identity provider that is configured within a vCenter or
integrate them as part of VCF single sign-on using the identity broker in VCF Operations. However, after a vCenter
is configured for single sign-on, you must manage its configuration in VCF Operations and not directly in vCenter.
• VCF Components
– vCenter: After you configure VCF single sign-on, any existing identity provider configurations in the participating
vCenter is overridden by the VCF single sign-on configuration. You might be required to perform role assignments
to the required users and groups again to ensure continued access.
Other VCF components: VCF single sign-on is an additional authentication source to the existing authentication
sources such as VMware Identity Manager and the native authentication source of a component. You must
provision users and groups again when you configure VCF single sign-on.
• Single Component Log Out
– VCF single sign-on supports a single component logout mechanism. When you log out, the session ends
exclusively for that particular VCF component within the designated browser.
• Previously configured identity providers
– If you have previously configured an identity provider on a vCenter in the following combinations, the identity
provider configurations are partially imported when you configure single sign-on. The combinations are:
• Active Directory, OpenLDAP, or ADFS
If Active Directory, OpenLDAP, or ADFS is the configured identity provider in vCenter, when configuring VCF
single sign-on, the configuration is partially imported to identity broker. Only the configuration details that are not
imported are required to be additionally configured.
• Okta, Entra, or Ping
The identity provider configuration is retained if the chosen deployment mode is embedded. If the deployment
mode is instance, redo the configuration again.
Note:
The users and groups are not migrated. You must provision the users and groups again even if you have an
existing identity provider configuration in place.
Prerequisites for Configuring VCF Single Sign-On
The identity broker is deployed in the management domain of the VCF Instance. Ensure that the following prerequisites
are met before you configure VCF single sign-on.
Prerequisites for Embedded Identity Broker
For embedded deployment mode, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
• The management domain vCenter must be at version 9.1 or later and must have a VCF license assigned.
• The management domain vCenter must NOT be part of Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM).
Do not activate ELM in the participating vCenter instances after configuring VCF Single Sign-On in embedded mode.
Note:
You can choose instance as the mode of deployment if the preceding criteria are not met. However, the
integration of vCenter with VCF single sign-on is not possible at a later stage without first meeting the preceding
criteria.
Prerequisites for Deploying Identity Broker as Instance
For instance mode, the VCF platform must meet the following minimum requirements:
Broadcom 4037

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• The initial identity broker instance is installed as part of VCF management services on the VCF services runtime
nodes. Any additional identity broker instances that you deploy in additional VCF Instances require more compute
resources to the VCF service runtime.
• The management domain vCenter must be at version 9.1 or later and must have a VCF license assigned.
• The management domain vCenter must not be part of Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM).
Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode for Standalone vCenter Instances Using the cmsso-util break-elm
Utililty
VCF single sign-on is not compatible with vCenter Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM). Before you configure VCF single
sign-on, you must deactivate ELM on all participating vCenter instances. As an administrator, if you want to deactivate
ELM in vCenter Instances, you can do so without causing any loss to existing customer configurations such as global
permissions.
If your vCenter instances are part not part of a VCF Instance, use the utility to deactivate ELM and related features, for
example, vCenter linking and replication. Any shared configurations, such as tags, roles, and permissions that are in ELM,
remain local to individual vCenter instances after you deactivate ELM.
Note:
The new cmsso-util break-elm utility works only if all vCenter instances in the ELM topology are up and running
and vCenter instances are at version 9.0 or later. Back up all vCenter instances before you deactivate ELM.
The only supported backup for vCenter instances in ELM is to take offline snapshots of them which results in
environment downtime.
If your vCenter instances are part of a VCF Instance, see Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode for Management and Workload
vCenter Instances Using the SDDC Manager API.
1. Take an offline backup of the participating vCenter instances in the ELM topology.
This preparatory step requires downtime.
2. Connect over SSH to any vCenter instance that participates in ELM.
3. Run configuration pre-checks and fix any issues.
a) Run
cmsso-util break-elm --mode pre-check --password <default administrator
.
user_password>
b) Fix any issues reported by the pre-check.
Output of the break-elm precheck when successful:
Command:cmsso-util break-elm --mode pre-check --password 'ZSIY+eDe-14dukrW'
Output: Mode: pre-check This operation might take a few minutes to complete.
[Pre-check] Invoking Break ELM topology workflow...
[Pre-check] Fetch the peer nodes details...
[Pre-check] Executing break ELM on local node...
[Pre-check] Executing break ELM on all peer nodes...
Break ELM pre-checks completed successfully.
4. Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode.
a) Run .
cmsso-util break-elm --mode execute --password <administrator_password>
b) Log out from the vSphere Client and log in again for the changes to take effect.
c) In case of a failure, fix the cause of the failure and rerun on all nodes where the failure
cmsso-util break-elm
was reported.
5. After successful validation that the break ELM process is successful, delete the offline backups.
You must resolve the ELM drift. For more information, see Resolve Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM) Drift for Upgraded
vCenter Instances.
Broadcom 4038

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Deactivate Enhanced Link Mode for Management and Workload vCenter Instances Using the SDDC
Manager API
If you upgraded your VCF Instance from 5.2 to 9.1, you must use the SDDC Manager API to deactivate Enhanced Link
Mode (ELM) for upgraded vCenter instances that are part of your VCF fleet, before you can use certain 9.x features.
Minimum required version of the VCF components.
• SDDC Manager 9.0 and later
• vCenter upgraded to 9.0 and later
When you created a workload domain in VCF 5.x, you choose whether to join its vCenter to the management domain's
vCenter single sign-on domain or to create a new vCenter single sign-on domain. If you joined it to the management
domain's vCenter single sign-on domain, the workload domain vCenter was joined to the management domain vCenter in
Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM).
ELM is deprecated in VCF 9.0. Before you can use new features in 9.0, such as VCF single sign-on and vCenter linking,
you must deactivate ELM for all vCenter instances in your VCF Instance.
You can use the SDDC Manager API to remove all the vCenter instances in a VCF Instance from Enhanced Linked Mode
(ELM), creating isolated workload domains.
Note:
This procedure deactivates ELM for all vCenter instances in your VCF Instance. You cannot select a subset of
instances.
If you used the utility to remove some or all of your VCF-managed vCenter instances from
cmsso-util break-elm
ELM, see Resolve Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM) Drift for Upgraded vCenter Instances.
Back up all vCenter instances before you deactivate ELM. The only supported backup for vCenter instances in ELM is to
take offline snapshots of them which results in environment downtime.
1. Take an offline backup of the participating vCenter instances in the ELM topology.
This preparatory step requires downtime.
2. Use the SDDC Manager API to retrieve the management domain ID.
API Description
GET /v1/domains Find the management domain ID in the Response.
3. Acknowledge the offline backup of the participating vCenter instances in the ELM topology.
API Description
PATCH /v1/domains/{domainId} Replace {domainId} with the management domain ID.
In the body parameter, enter:
{
"acknowledgmentSpec": {
"ackThatOfflineBackupsTaken": true
}
}
Broadcom 4039

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Validate the break ELM spec.
API Description
POST /v1/domains/{id}/validations Replace {id} with the management domain ID.
In the body parameter, enter:
{
"breakElmSpec": {
"isReconcileWorkflow": false
}
}
Find the validation ID in the Response.
5. Get the validation response.
Make sure that validation is successful.
API Description
GET /v1/domains/{id}/validations/{validation_id} Replace {id} with the management domain ID.
Replace {validation_id} with the validation ID.
6. Break ELM across all joined domains.
API Description
PATCH /v1/domains/{id} Replace {id} with the management domain ID.
In the body parameter enter:
{
"breakElmSpec": {
"isReconcileWorkflow": false
}
}
Find the task ID in the Response.
7. Monitor the task.
API Description
GET /v1/tasks/{id} Replace {id} with the task ID.
8. After successful validation that the break ELM process is successful, delete the offline backups.

Remove all the vCenter instances in your VCF Instance from ELM using the utility. See
cmsso-util break-elm

1. Use the SDDC Manager API to retrieve the management domain ID.
API Description
GET /v1/domains Find the management domain ID in the Response.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Validate the break ELM reconcile workflow.
API Description
POST /v1/domains/{id}/validations Replace {id} with the management domain ID.
In the body parameter, enter:
