"isReconcileWorkflow": true
}
}
Find the validation ID in the Response.
3. Get the validation response.
Make sure that validation is successful.
API Description
GET /v1/domains/{id}/validations/{validation_id} Replace {id} with the management domain ID.
Replace {validation_id} with the validation ID.
4. Resolve ELM drift across all joined domains.

Configure a New VCF Single Sign-On for a VCF Instance
You can configure VCF single sign-on across components within a single VCF Instance, across a set of VCF Instances,
and across the entire VCF fleet.
Important:
Ensure that you are familiar with the considerations and have completed the prerequisites before you set up VCF
single sign-on. For more information, see Considerations and Prerequisites for VCF Single Sign-On.
Figure 438:
The following flowchart outlines the high-level steps to configure VCF single sign-on.
Broadcom 4041

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Broadcom 4042

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Follow these high-level steps to configure VCF single sign-on:
1. Select the identity broker deployment mode.
Select whether you want to deploy identity broker as embedded or instance. See, Step 1: Choose the Deployment
Mode.
2. Configure the identity provider.
Set up your preferred identity provider using modern or directory-based authentication. See Step 2: Configure an
Identity Provider.
3. Configure VCF single sign-on for NSX and vCenter.
See Step 3: Configure VCF Single Sign-On for NSX and vCenter.
4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role
See Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role.
5. (Optional) Configure VCF single sign-on for VCF Operations and VCF Automation.
Connect the components to the identity broker for single sign-on-based access. See Step 5: (Optional) Configure VCF
Single Sign-On for VCF Operations, VCF Automation Provider, and Salt RaaS.
6. (Optional) Configure VCF single sign-on for other VCF Components.
Connect the components for single sign-on access. See, Step 6: (Optional) Configure VCF Single Sign-On for other
VCF Components.
Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode
Choose a deployment mode for the identity broker configuration. The options available are embedded or instance. For
more information about the VCF single sign-on deployment modes, see Deployment Modes of the Identity Broker.
The identity broker instance is deployed by default in the first VCF Instance of a VCF fleet. For more information, see Start
a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance Deployment by Using the VCF Installer Deployment Wizard.
Procedure
1. Log in to the VCF Operations console at with a user assigned the
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
Administrator role.
2. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity and Access.
3. From the Identity and Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview, and then from the Get Started page on the right, click
the Get Started with SSO tab.
4. In the Get Started with SSO tab, click Configure SSO.
5. In the Prerequisites tab, confirm each check box and click Submit. For more information about the prerequisites, see
Considerations and Prerequisites for VCF Single Sign-On.
6. In the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Choose deployment mode option.
7. Select either Instance (Recommended) or Embedded.
a) If you choose Instance, from the Choose Identity Broker section, select an existing identity broker. To deploy a
new identity broker instance, see Deploy Identity Broker as a Day-N Operation.
b) If you choose Embedded, select a VCF Instance from the Choose VCF Instance section.
Note:
Identity broker embedded will be deprecated in later versions of VCF and you have to migrate to identity broker
instance before identity broker embedded reaches end-of-support. For information about migration, see Migration
of Identity Broker Embedded to Identity Broker Instance.
8. Click Configure.
• While configuring a new VCF single sign-on, you can change the deployment type only if you have not yet
configured an identity provider.
• However, you can change the deployment mode as a Day N operation. For more information see, Change the
Deployment Mode in VCF Single Sign-On.
Broadcom 4043

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Step 2: Configure an Identity Provider
After you select the deployment mode, you must select and configure the identity provider using SAML, OIDC, or LDAP as
the authentication protocol.
For information about supported identity providers and protocols, see Identity Providers and Protocols Supported for VCF
Single Sign-On.
• To configure Okta as an identity provider, see Configure Okta as an Identity Provider.
• To configure Ping Identity as an identity provider, see Configure Ping Identity as an Identity Provider.
• To configure Microsoft Entra ID as an identity provider, see Configure Microsoft Entra ID as an Identity Provider.
• To configure Microsoft ADFS as an identity provider, see Configure Microsoft ADFS as an Identity Provider.
• To configure Symantec Identity Security Platform as an identity provider, see Configure Symantec Identity Security
Platform as an Identity Provider.
• To configure an identity provider using Generic SAML 2.0, see Configure an Identity Provider using Generic SAML 2.0.
• To configure an identity provider using Generic OIDC, see Configure an Identity Provider using Generic OIDC.
• To configure Active Directory as an identity provider using AD/LDAP, see Configure Active Directory as an Identity
Provider Using AD/LDAP.
• To configure OpenLDAP as an identity provider, see Configure OpenLDAP as an Identity Provider.
Note:
For existing deployments, when an identity provider is configured on a vCenter instance, and is configured in the
following combinations, you can use the preselected existing identity provider or choose a new identity provider in
the UI workflows:
• Active Directory, OpenLDAP, or ADFS
• Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or Ping Federate with OIDC
Configure Okta as an Identity Provider
You can configure Okta as an identity provider using SAML 2.0 or OIDC authentication protocols.
• For information about configuring Okta as an identity provider using SAML as the authentication protocol, see
Configure Okta as an Identity Provider Using SAML.
• For information about configuring Okta as an identity provider using OIDC as the authentication protocol, see
Configure Okta as an Identity Provider using OIDC.
Configure Okta as an Identity Provider Using SAML
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Okta as an identity provider
using SAML as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
Broadcom 4044

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
2. From the Choose the identity provider section, select OKTA from the list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) and click Next.
5. In the Service Provider Registration screen, log in to your Okta admin console and follow the steps in Add a private
single sign-on integration to create a SAML 2.0 application in Okta.
While registering Okta, use the metadata provided in the Service Provider Registration screen for the Entity ID/
Metadata URL and Assertion Consumer Service URL options. If the identity provider requires the metadata to be
copy-pasted, it is recommended to download this file to avoid formatting issues.
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. Note that
these claims are case-sensitive:
• userName
• email
• domain
• firstName
• lastName
• groups
6. Click Next.
7. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document containing metadata
about the service provider (identity broker). This metadata includes important
information required for establishing trust and facilitating secure communication
between the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If you have configured VCF single sign-on, after you upgrade to 9.1.1, it is
recommended that you re-import the identity broker service provider metadata
into your identity provider. Re-importing ensures your identity provider reads
the new encryption hint and switches to SHA-256 OAEP for all subsequent
SAML assertion encryption.
Metadata URL Copy the Metadata URL of your identity provider and paste it in this field.
The Metadata URL is used to fetch identity provider metadata. This metadata
includes important information required for establishing trust and facilitating secure
communication between the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If your identity provider is not publicly accessible or if the certificate lacks
a signature from a recognized Certificate Authority (CA), VCF Operations
cannot validate the metadata URL. Provide the metadata in XML format
instead.
Name ID format and Name ID value Select the Name ID format and value.
The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify the authenticated
user.
Broadcom 4045

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Description
SAML Context SAML context refers to the method of authentication that VCF requires the identity
provider to support when verifying a user's identity.
• PasswordProtectedTransport: Authentication with a password sent over a secure
transport (For example, HTTPS).
• Password: Authentication using a password without requiring transport security.
• Unspecified: If you don't want to enforce any particular type of authentication
mechanism, you can use this option.
8. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select SCIM and click Next, complete the configuration as follows.
• In the Domain(s) screen, enter the domain that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
b) If you select JIT and click Next, complete the configuration as follows:
• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role assignments. Users
are assigned to these groups dynamically when they log in based on SAML assertion.
Only the pre-provisioned groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the SAML assertion when the user
logs in.
• In the Domain(s) screen, add the domain details that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
• In the Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen, add the groups from each domain that you want to
provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:

provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.

attributes that you view in the SAML response from the identity provider.
You can add additional user attributes if required. In the group attributes section of the workflow you can add a
group attribute to be called for in the SAML request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.
Note:
• If you choose JIT, it is recommended that you automatically disable inactive users.
c) If you select AD/LDAP and click Next, complete the configuration as follows. To learn more about the benefits of

must have permissions to read the Token-Groups-Global-And-Universal (TGGAU)
attribute.

configuration, such as when you 'Delete Single Sign-On'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF

VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component roles.

Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration).
Configure Okta as an Identity Provider using OIDC
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Okta as an identity provider
using OIDC as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisites
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
If you configure VCF single sign-on using identity broker instance, and there are network restrictions that do not allow
outbound public internet access, you must set up a proxy server. For more information, see Configure a Proxy Server
for VCF Management Services Components and VCF Automation.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
If you have an existing identity provider configured in vCenter, see the information below. For a fresh configuration of
the identity provider, continue from Step 6.
For an existing source (existing identity provider configuration)
• Choose either SAML or OIDC as the authentication protocol.
Note:
If you choose SAML, the VCF Single Sign-On configuration is considered as a new authentication source
configuration. Continue from Step. 6.
• If you choose OIDC:
– If you choose the instance deployment mode, and select OIDC, the following fields are prepopulated in the
Identity Provider Configuration screen.
a. Review the details and provide the shared secret and click Next.
• Identity provider name
• Client identifier
• OpenID address
• Update Redirect URI in the Identity provider's OIDC application
• Shared Secret: Paste the client secret of the OIDC application you created in the identity provider.
b. Review the User/Group Provisioning, Domain(s), and Review screens and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM push details and click Done. The identity provider configuration is complete.
Broadcom 4049

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If you choose the embedded deployment mode, and select OIDC:
a. The configuration details of the identity provider configuration are automatically imported from existing
configuration into the identity broker with OIDC as the authentication protocol and SCIM as the user/group
provisioning method.
b. Review the configuration values in the Identity Provider Configuration screen and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM details, click Done, and then click Finish Setup. The identity provider configuration is
complete.
2. For a fresh identity provider configuration, from the Choose the identity provider section, select Okta from the list
and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. These claims
are case-sensitive:
• preferred_username
• email
• family_name
• given_name
• groups
• domain
If the default claims cannot be added, use alternative claim names and map them to the appropriate attributes in
the VCF Operations Identity & Access page to support your JIT configurations.
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select OIDC (OpenID Connect) and click Next.
5. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider. Example, Okta.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity provider for authentication.
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate itself with the identity
provider.
Note:
Client secrets issued by external identity providers typically have expiration dates.
When a client secret expires, it must be regenerated, and the corresponding
OIDC configuration must be updated in VCF to ensure continued authentication
functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration endpoint for initiating the
authentication process.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider sends the authentication response after a user logs
in.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select SCIM and click Next, complete the configuration as follows.
• In the Domain(s) screen, enter the domains that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.

• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role
assignments. Users are assigned to these groups dynamically
when they log in based on OIDC token. Only the pre-provisioned
groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the OIDC token
when the user logs in.
Alternatively, you can use group pre-provisioning if you know the
group names from Active Directory that requires entitlements.
• In the Domain(s) screen, add the domain details that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
• In the Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen, add the groups from each domain that you want to
provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:
The Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen is displayed only if you have chosen groups to be pre-
provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.
• In the Attributes screen, the user attributes section displays a list of mandatory and non-mandatory user
attributes that you view in the OIDC response from the identity provider.
You can add additional user attributes if necessary. In the group attributes section of the workflow you can add a
group attribute to be called for in the OIDC request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.

Configure Ping Identity as an Identity Provider Using SAML
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Ping Identity as an identity
provider using SAML as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
2. From the Choose the identity provider section, select Ping Identity from the list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) and click Next.
5. In the Service Provider Registration screen, log in to your Ping Identity admin console and follow the steps in Ping
Identity to create a SAML 2.0 application in Ping Identity.
While registering Ping Identity, use the metadata provided in the Service Provider Registration screen for the Entity
ID/Metadata URL and Assertion Consumer Service URL options. If the identity provider requires the metadata to be
copy-pasted, it is recommended to download this file to avoid formatting issues.
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. Note that
these claims are case-sensitive:
• userName
• email
• domain
• firstName
• lastName
• groups
Broadcom 4055

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Click Next.
7. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider.
Metadata Select either URL or XML.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document
containing metadata about the service provider (identity broker).
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If you have configured VCF single sign-on, after you
upgrade to 9.1.1, it is recommended that you re-import
the identity broker service provider metadata into your
identity provider. Re-importing ensures your identity
provider reads the new encryption hint and switches
to SHA-256 OAEP for all subsequent SAML assertion
encryption.
Metadata URL Copy the Metadata URL of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata URL is used to fetch identity provider metadata.
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If your identity provider is not publicly accessible or if the
certificate lacks a signature from a recognized Certificate
Authority (CA), VCF Operations cannot validate the
metadata URL. Provide the metadata in XML format
instead.
Name ID format and Name ID value Select the Name ID format and value.
The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify
the authenticated user.
SAML Context SAML context refers to the method of authentication that VCF
requires the identity provider to support when verifying a user's
identity.
• PasswordProtectedTransport: Authentication with a
password sent over a secure transport (For example, HTTPS).
• Password: Authentication using a password without requiring
transport security.
• Unspecified: If you don't want to enforce any particular type of
authentication mechanism, you can use this option.

steps and click Done.
a) If you have chosen SCIM, you see Configure SCIM push in your identity provider instead of Configure User
and Group Provisioning. Use the values listed on the screen to configure the SCIM application in the identity
provider.
• If your identity provider supports authorizing the SCIM application using OAuth grant type, use the client ID,
client secret, and token endpoint. Otherwise, use the SCIM bearer token to authorize this SCIM server in your
identity provider.
• If required, you can regenerate these values after you have configured VCF single sign-on. To regenerate the

click on Identity Source. The SCIM related values are available under Directory Information.

identity provider. Similarly, ensure that the group attributes, group name, and domain are pushed individually as
well.

The attributes in the identity broker directory are mapped to the Active Directory attributes for accurate
synchronization of user information. If the mappings are incorrect, select the correct attribute from the drop-
down list.

Use the Group Provisioning screen to search for the group names and select the corresponding Active
Directory group Distinguished Names (DN) that you want to sync.

groups and want to specify the group names. You can search for

Important:
Important Notes on Backup
It is highly advisable to create a backup of both VCF Operations and the identity broker instance. Furthermore,
it is advisable to perform a similar backup following any substantial modifications to the initial identity source
configuration, such as when you 'Delete single sign-on'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF
Single Sign-On configuration to a recognized and stable state if necessary. You can download the configuration as
a JSON file.
Important Notes on Role Assignment
VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component role.
• As an admin you can assign built-in and custom VCF roles to groups and and users from the Access
Managment tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on configuration, and
then click the Access Management tab).
• As an admin, you can also assign roles in the component console and enable VCF single sign-on from the
Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration).
Configure Ping Identity as an Identity Provider Using OIDC
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Ping Identity as an identity
provider using OIDC as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
• If you configure VCF single sign-on using identity broker instance, and there are network restrictions that do not allow
outbound public internet access, you must set up a proxy server. For more information, see Configure a Proxy Server
for VCF Management Services Components and VCF Automation.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
If you have an existing identity provider configured in vCenter, see the information below. For a fresh configuration of
the identity provider, continue from Step 6.
For an existing source (existing identity provider configuration)
• Choose either SAML or OIDC as the authentication protocol.
Broadcom 4060

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If you choose SAML, the VCF single sign-on configuration is considered as a new authentication source
configuration. Continue from Step. 6.
• If you choose OIDC:
– If you choose the instance deployment mode, and select OIDC, the following fields are prepopulated in the
Identity Provider Configuration screen.
a. Review the details and provide the shared secret and click Next.
• Identity provider name
• Client identifier
• OpenID address
• Update Redirect URI in the Identity provider's OIDC application
• Shared Secret: Paste the client secret of the OIDC application you created in the identity provider.
b. Review the User/Group Provisioning, Domain(s), and Review screens and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM push details and click Done. The identity provider configuration is complete.
• If you choose the embedded deployment mode, and select OIDC:
a. The configuration details of the identity provider configuration are automatically imported from existing
configuration into the identity broker with OIDC as the authentication protocol and SCIM as the user/group
provisioning method.
b. Review the configuration values in the Identity Provider Configuration screen and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM details, click Done, and then click Finish Setup. The identity provider configuration is
complete.
2. For a fresh identity provider configuration, from the Choose Identity Provider section, select Ping Identity from the
list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. These claims
are case-sensitive:
• preferred_username
• email
• family_name
• given_name
• groups
• domain
If the default claims cannot be added, use alternative claim names and map them to the appropriate attributes in
the VCF Operations Identity & Access page to support your JIT configurations.
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select OIDC (OpenID Connect) and click Next.
5. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter the OpenID Connect provider name. Example, Ping Identity.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity
provider for authentication.
Broadcom 4061

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate
itself with the identity provider.
Note:
Client secrets issued by external identity providers
typically have expiration dates. When a client secret
expires, it must be regenerated, and the corresponding
OIDC configuration must be updated in VCF to ensure
continued authentication functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration endpoint for
initiating the authentication process.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider sends the authentication
response after a user logs in.
SSL Certificate A public key certificate to verify the OIDC identity.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select SCIM and click Next, complete the configuration as follows.
• In the Domain(s) screen, enter the domain that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
b) If you select JIT and click Next, complete the configuration as follows:
• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role
assignments. Users are assigned to these groups dynamically
when they log in based on OIDC token. Only the pre-provisioned
groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the OIDC
assertion when the user logs in.
Alternatively, you can use group pre-provisioning if you know the
group names from Active Directory that requires entitlements.
• In the Domain(s) screen, add the domain details that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
• In the Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen, add the groups from each domain that you want to
provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:
The Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen is displayed only if you have chosen groups to be pre-
provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.
• In the Attributes screen, the user attributes section displays a list of mandatory and non-mandatory user
attributes that you view in the OIDC response from the identity provider.
You can add additional user attributes if necessary. In the group attributes section of the workflow you can add a
group attribute to be called for in the OIDC request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.
Note:

• ExternalId

• nickName
• profileUrl
• title
• organization
• costCenter
• department

• managerId
Note:
If you choose JIT, it is recommended that you automatically disable inactive users.

method, see KB 386870.
Note:
The value of the identifier used to uniquely identify a user in your OIDC identity provider must exactly match with
the value from Active Directory. The unique identifier in the identity broker is used to map the two systems.

optimal domain controllers by querying the DNS Service Record.

IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider. For example,

Metadata Select either URL or XML.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document
containing metadata about the service provider (identity broker).
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.

upgrade to 9.1.1, it is recommended that you re-import

Authority (CA), VCF Operations cannot validate the

the authenticated user.
SAML Context SAML context refers to the method of authentication that VCF
requires the identity provider to support when verifying a user's
identity.

password sent over a secure transport (For example, HTTPS).

transport security.

authentication mechanism, you can use this option.

Secondary domain controller A backup domain controller for the identity broker to point to if the
(Displayed when you select the Global Catalog option) primary domain controller is not reachable.
Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify
entries in the directory. For example, uid, sAMAccountName.
Base DN The Distinguished Name (DN) of the top-level entry in the
directory tree from which LDAP queries begin. For example, dc=e
xample, dc=com.
Bind user name The user name of a user account with sufficient permissions to
authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.
Bind user password The password of a user account with sufficient permissions to
authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.
9. In the Review screen, review the details you have added for the configuration and click Finish.
Configure user and group provisioning
10.In the Configure User and Group Provisioning screen, depending on the option you choose, complete the following
steps and click Done.
a) If you have chosen SCIM, you see Configure SCIM push in your identity provider instead of Configure User
and Group Provisioning. Use the values listed on the screen to configure the SCIM application in the identity
provider.
• If your identity provider supports authorizing the SCIM application using OAuth grant type, use the client ID,
client secret, and token endpoint. Otherwise, use the SCIM bearer token to authorize this SCIM server in your
identity provider.
• If required, you can regenerate these values after you have configured VCF single sign-on. To regenerate the
values to configure the SCIM application in the identity provider, navigate to the respective VCF Instance and
click on Identity Source. The SCIM related values are available under Directory Information.
• Ensure that the user attributes, username, and domain are pushed individually from the SCIM application by the
identity provider. Similarly, ensure that the group attributes, group name, and domain are pushed individually as
well.
b) If you have chosen JIT, there is no additional step to be performed under User and Group Provisioning.
c) If you have chosen AD/LDAP, review the directory information such as the domain controller and bind credentials
that you had configured. Complete the following steps:
1. In the Attributes Mappings screen, review the attribute mappings and click Next.
The attributes in the identity broker directory are mapped to the Active Directory attributes for accurate
synchronization of user information. If the mappings are incorrect, select the correct attribute from the drop-
down list.
2. In the Group Provisioning screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Use the Group Provisioning screen to search for the group names and select the corresponding Active
Directory group Distinguished Names (DN) that you want to sync.
Option Description
Specify the Base Group DN Click the Select Base Group DN button if you have nested
groups and want to specify the group names. You can search for
the group name and select the group DNs that you want to sync
from from the list in the datagrid below.
Sync Nested Groups Select Sync Nested Group to sync all the users from the
selected group and its nested group without maintaining the group
hierarchy.
3. From the User Provisioning screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Broadcom 4070

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Use the User Provisioning screen to search for the user names and select the corresponding Active Directory
group Distinguished Names (DN) that you want to sync.
Option Description
Specify the Base User DN Click the Select Base User DN button to specify the user names
that you want to sync. You can search for the user name and
select the user DNs that you want to sync from from the list in
the datagrid below. If you want to sync the users directly from the
group, do not specify a base user DN.
4. From the Review screen, review the configuration details of the identity provider.
5. Click Finish. The sync starts in the background. After the initial sync, the sync is scheduled to run once a week
at a scheduled time.
6. Click Done.
For more information about the various functionalities you can perform as part of the management operations in
Active Directory, see Managing AD/LDAP.
(Optional) Test Login
11.Click Test Login to test the login using your single-sign on credentials.

Important:
Important Notes on Backup
It is highly advisable to create a backup of both VCF Operations and the identity broker instance. Furthermore,
it is advisable to perform a similar backup following any substantial modifications to the initial identity source
configuration, such as when you 'Delete Single Sign-On'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF
single sign-on configuration to a recognized and stable state if necessary. You can download the configuration as
a JSON file.
Important Notes on Role Assignment
VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component role.
• As an admin you can assign built-in and custom VCF roles to groups and and users from the Access
Managment tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on configuration, and
then click the Access Management tab).
• As an admin, you can also assign roles in the component console and enable VCF Single Sign-On from the
Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration tab).

After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Microsoft Entra ID as an
identity provider using OIDC as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Broadcom 4071

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
If you configure VCF single sign-on using identity broker instance, and there are network restrictions that do not allow
outbound public internet access, you must set up a proxy server. For more information, see Configure a Proxy Server
for VCF Management Services Components and VCF Automation.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
If you have an existing identity provider configured in vCenter, see the information below. For a fresh configuration of
the identity provider, continue from Step 6.
For an existing source (existing identity provider configuration)
• Choose either SAML or OIDC as the authentication protocol.
Note:
If you choose SAML, the VCF single sign-on configuration is considered as a new authentication source
configuration. Continue from Step. 6.
• If you choose OIDC:
– If you choose the instance deployment mode, and select OIDC, the following fields are prepopulated in the
Identity Provider Configuration screen.
a. Review the details and provide the shared secret and click Next.
• Identity provider name
• Client identifier
• OpenID address
• Update Redirect URI in the Identity provider's OIDC application
• Shared Secret: Paste the client secret of the OIDC application you created in the identity provider.
b. Review the User/Group Provisioning, Domain(s), and Review screens and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM push details and click Done. The identity provider configuration is complete.
• If you choose the embedded deployment mode, and select OIDC:
a. The configuration details of the identity provider configuration are automatically imported from existing
configuration into the identity broker with OIDC as the authentication protocol and SCIM as the user/group
provisioning method.
b. Review the configuration values in the Identity Provider Configuration screen and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM details, click Done, and then click Finish Setup. The identity provider configuration is
complete.
2. For a fresh identity provider configuration, from the Choose the identity provider section, select Microsoft Entra ID
from the list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. These claims
are case-sensitive:
• preferred_username
• email
• family_name
• given_name
• groups
• domain
If the default claims cannot be added, use alternative claim names and map them to the appropriate attributes in
the VCF Operations Identity & Access page to support your JIT configurations.
Broadcom 4072

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select OIDC (OpenID Connect) and click Next.
5. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter the OpenID Connect provider name. Example, Microsoft
Entra ID.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity
provider, for authentication.
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate
itself with the identity provider.
Note:
Client secrets issued by external identity providers
typically have expiration dates. When a client secret
expires, it must be regenerated, and the corresponding
OIDC configuration must be updated in VCF to ensure
continued authentication functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration endpoint for
initiating the authentication process.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider will send the authentication
response after a user logs in.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• System for Cross-domain Identity Management SCIM, or
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select SCIM and click Next, complete the configuration as follows.
• In the Domain(s) screen, enter the domain that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
b) If you select JIT and click Next, complete the configuration as follows:
• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role
assignments. Users are assigned to these groups dynamically
when they log in based on OIDC token. Only the pre-provisioned
groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the OIDC
assertion when the user logs in.
Alternatively, you can use group pre-provisioning if you know the
group names from Active Directory that requires entitlements.
• In the Domain(s) screen, add the domain details that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
• In the Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen, add the groups from each domain that you want to
provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:
The Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen is displayed only if you have chosen groups to be pre-
provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
Broadcom 4073

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.
• In the Attributes screen,
the user attributes section displays a list of mandatory and non-mandatory user attributes that you view in the
OIDC response from the identity provider.
You can add additional user attributes if necessary. In the group attributes section of the workflow you can add a
group attribute to be called for in the OIDC request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.

Note:
If you choose JIT, it is recommended that you automatically disable inactive users.
c) If you select AD/LDAP, select the Unique Identifier in OIDC Identity Provider and Unique Identifier in VCF
Identity Broker, and click Next. To learn more about the benefits of using AD/LDAP as a provisioning method, KB
386870.
Note:
The value of the identifier used to uniquely identify a user in your OIDC identity provider must exactly match with
the value from Active Directory. The unique identifier in the identity broker is used to map the two systems.
Option Description
Unique Identifier in OIDC Identity Provider An identifier in your OIDC identity provider that is used to identify
a user uniquely. You can select or enter a custom attribute (except
'sub'). For example, name.
Unique Identifier in VCF Identity Broker Select the unique identifier that will be used to map to an attribute
from Active Directory. The value of this identifier must exactly
match the value of the previous field called Unique Identifier in
OIDC Identity Provider.

In the In the Directory Details screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options.
Option Description
Directory name Enter a name for the directory.
DNS Server Location Select this option if you want the identity broker to find and use
optimal domain controllers by querying the DNS Service Record.
Global Catalog Global catalog has a partial read-only replica of all objects across
all domains.
Some of the limitations with selecting the global catalog option
include:

enforcing policies, and storing directory data. For example,
hostname = DC01 for the domain called example.com.
Secondary domain controller A backup domain controller for the identity broker to point to if the
primary domain controller is not reachable.

entries in the directory. For example, uid, sAMAccountName.
Base DN The Distinguished Name (DN) of the top-level entry in the

xample, dc=com.

Procedure

Configure the identity provider

4. In the Authentication Method pane, select SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language).
5. In the Service Provider Registration pane, log in to your Microsoft ADFS admin console and follow the steps in Set
up a SAML 2.0 provider with ADFS to create a SAML 2.0 in Microsoft ADFS.
While registering Microsoft Entra ADFS, use the metadata provided in the Service Provider Registration screen for

are case-sensitive:

6. Click Next.
7. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider.
Metadata Select either URL or XML.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document
containing metadata about the service provider (identity broker).
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If you have configured VCF single sign-on, after you
upgrade to 9.1.1, it is recommended that you re-import
the identity broker service provider metadata into your
identity provider. Re-importing ensures your identity
provider reads the new encryption hint and switches
to SHA-256 OAEP for all subsequent SAML assertion
encryption.
Broadcom 4078

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Metadata URL Copy the Metadata URL of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata URL is used to fetch identity provider metadata.
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If your identity provider is not publicly accessible or if the
certificate lacks a signature from a recognized Certificate
Authority (CA), VCF Operations cannot validate the
metadata URL. Provide the metadata in XML format
instead.
Name ID format and Name ID value Select the Name ID format and value.
The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify
the authenticated user.
SAML Context SAML context refers to the method of authentication that VCF
requires the identity provider to support when verifying a user's
identity.
• PasswordProtectedTransport: Authentication with a
password sent over a secure transport (For example, HTTPS).
• Password: Authentication using a password without requiring
transport security.
• Unspecified: If you don't want to enforce any particular type of
authentication mechanism, you can use this option.

selected group and its nested group without maintaining the group
hierarchy.

group Distinguished Names (DN) that you want to sync.

that you want to sync. You can search for the user name and
select the user DNs that you want to sync from from the list in

Important:
Important Notes on Backup
It is highly advisable to create a backup of both VCF Operations and the identity broker appliance. Furthermore,
it is advisable to perform a similar backup following any substantial modifications to the initial identity source
configuration, such as when you 'Delete Single Sign-On'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF
single sign-on configuration to a recognized and stable state if necessary. You can download the configuration as
a JSON file.
Important Notes on Role Assignment
VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component roles.
• As an admin you can assign built-in and custom VCF roles to groups and and users from the Access
Managment tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on configuration, and
then click the Access Management tab).
• As an admin, you can also assign roles in the component console and enable VCF single sign-on from the
Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration tab).
Configure Microsoft ADFS as an Identity Provider Using OIDC
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure Microsoft ADFS as an identity
provider using OIDC as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test log in if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
• If you configure VCF single sign-on using identity broker instance, and there are network restrictions that do not allow
outbound public internet access, you must set up a proxy server. For more information, see Configure a Proxy Server
for VCF Management Services Components and VCF Automation.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
If you have an existing identity provider configured in vCenter, see the information below. For a fresh configuration of
the identity provider, continue from Step 6.
For an existing source (existing identity provider configuration)
Broadcom 4082

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Choose either SAML or OIDC as the authentication protocol.
Note:
If you choose SAML, the VCF single sign-on configuration is considered as a new authentication source
configuration. Continue from Step. 6.
• If you choose OIDC:
– If you choose the instance deployment mode, and select OIDC, the following fields are prepopulated in the
Identity Provider Configuration screen.
a. Review the details and provide the shared secret and click Next.
• Identity provider name
• Client identifier
• OpenID address
• Update Redirect URI in the Identity provider's OIDC application
• Shared Secret: Paste the client secret of the OIDC application you created in the identity provider.
b. Review the User/Group Provisioning, Domain(s), and Review screens and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM push details and click Done. The identity provider configuration is complete.
• If you choose the embedded deployment mode, and select OIDC:
a. The configuration details of the identity provider configuration are automatically imported from existing
configuration into the identity broker with OIDC as the authentication protocol and SCIM as the user/group
provisioning method.
b. Review the configuration values in the Identity Provider Configuration screen and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM details, click Done, and then click Finish Setup. The identity provider configuration is
complete.
2. For a fresh identity provider configuration, from the Choose the identity provider section, select Microsoft Entra
ADFS from the list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. These claims
are case-sensitive:
• preferred_username
• email
• family_name
• given_name
• groups
• domain
If the default claims cannot be added, use alternative claim names and map them to the appropriate attributes in
the VCF Operations Identity & Access page to support your JIT configurations.
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select OIDC (OpenID Connect) and click Next.
5. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter the OpenID Connect provider name. Example, Microsoft
Entra ADFS.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity
provider, for authentication.
Broadcom 4083

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate
itself with the identity provider.
Note:
Client secrets issued by external identity providers
typically have expiration dates. When a client secret
expires, it must be regenerated, and the corresponding
OIDC configuration must be updated in VCF to ensure
continued authentication functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration end point
for initiating the authentication process.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider will send the authentication
response after a user logs in.
SSL Certificate Public key certificate to verify OIDC identity.
This field is required only if a self-signed certificate is used to sign
the identity provider.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select JIT and click Next, complete the configuration as follows:
• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role
assignments. Users are assigned to these groups dynamically
when they log in based on OIDC token. Only the pre-provisioned
groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the OIDC
assertion when the user logs in.
Alternatively, you can use group pre-provisioning if you know the
group names from Active Directory that requires entitlements.
• In the Domain(s) screen, add the domain details that users from your enterprise will log in with, and click Next.
• In the Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen, add the groups from each domain that you want to
provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:
The Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen is displayed only if you have chosen groups to be pre-
provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.
• In the Attributes screen, the user attributes section displays a list of mandatory and non-mandatory user
attributes that you view in the OIDC response from the identity provider.
You can add additional user attributes if necessary. In the group attributes section of the workflow you can add a
group attribute to be called for in the OIDC request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.
Note:
If you choose JIT, it is recommended that you automatically disable inactive users.
Broadcom 4084

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
b) If you select AD/LDAP, select the Unique Identifier in OIDC Identity Provider and Unique Identifier in VCF
Identity Broker, and click Next. To learn more about the benefits of using AD/LDAP as a provisioning method, see
KB 386870.
Note:
The value of the identifier used to uniquely identify a user in your OIDC identity provider must exactly match with
the value from Active Directory. The unique identifier in the identity broker is used to map the two systems.
Option Description
Unique Identifier in OIDC Identity Provider An identifier in your OIDC identity provider that is used to identify
a user uniquely. You can select or enter a custom attribute (except
'sub'). For example, name.
Unique Identifier in VCF Identity Broker Select the unique identifier that will be used to map to an attribute
from Active Directory. The value of this identifier must exactly
match the value of the previous field called Unique Identifier in
OIDC Identity Provider.
In the In the Directory Details screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options.
Option Description
Directory name Enter a name for the directory.
DNS Server Location Select this option if you want the identity broker to find and use
optimal domain controllers by querying the DNS Service Record.
Global Catalog Global catalog has a partial read-only replica of all objects across
all domains.
Some of the limitations with selecting the global catalog option
include:
• The Active Directory object attributes that are replicated to the
global catalog are identified in the Active Directory schema
as the Partial Attribute Set (PAS). Only these attributes are
available for attribute mapping by the service. If necessary,
edit the schema to add or remove attributes that are stored in
the global catalog.
• The global catalog stores the group membership (the member
attributes) of only universal groups. Only universal groups are
synced to the service. If necessary, change the scope of a
group from a local domain or from global to universal.
• The bind DN account that you define when you configure a
directory in the service must have permissions to read the
Token-Groups-Global-And-Universal (TGGAU) attribute.
Note:
When you use Global catalog with LDAP and multiple
domains, the additional domains are discovered only after
the user/group sync is complete.
Encrypted Connection Activates LDAPs for all the connections to this directory.
(Displayed when you select the DNS server location option)
Certificates for encrypted connection Upload the root certificate(s) required to access the domain
(Displayed when you select the DNS server location and controllers over SSL.

string in the Primary domain controller field) the filename {directory-name}-concatenated.pem
when you save the configuration.

Mail) PEM format and includes the "BEGIN
CERTIFICATE" and "END CERTIFICATE" lines.

Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify
entries in the directory. For example, uid, sAMAccountName.
Primary domain controller A server machine running Active Directory Domain Services (AD
DS) responsible for managing and authenticating user access,
enforcing policies, and storing directory data. For example,
hostname = DC01 for the domain called example.com.
Secondary domain controller A backup domain controller for the identity broker to point to if the
primary domain controller is not reachable.
Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify

xample, dc=com.

Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document containing metadata
about the service provider (identity broker). This metadata includes important
information required for establishing trust and facilitating secure communication
between the service provider and the identity provider.
Entity URL/Metadata URL Copy the Metadata URL of your identity provider and paste it in this field.
The Metadata URL is used to fetch identity provider metadata. This metadata
includes important information required for establishing trust and facilitating secure
communication between the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If your identity provider is not publicly accessible or if the certificate lacks
a signature from a recognized Certificate Authority (CA), VCF Operations
cannot validate the metadata URL. Provide the metadata in XML format
instead.
Name ID format and Name ID value Select the Name ID format and value.
The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify the authenticated
user.

transport (For example, HTTPS).

• Unspecified: If you don't want to enforce any particular type of authentication
mechanism, you can use this option.

3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Authentication Method screen, select OIDC (OpenID Connect) and click Next.
5. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter the OpenID Connect provider name. Example, Ping Identity.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity
provider for authentication.
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate
itself with the identity provider.
Note:
Client secrets that are issued by external identity
providers typically have expiration dates. When a
client secret expires, it must be regenerated, and the
corresponding OIDC configuration must be updated in
VCF to ensure continued authentication functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration endpoint for
initiating the authentication process. For example, https://<h
ostname>/<tenant>/.well-known/openid-configu
ration.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider sends the authentication
response after a user logs in.
List of domains Domains for a user to log in to your company.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the users and groups.
You can select either:
• Just-In-Time Provisioning (JIT), or
• Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (AD/LDAP)
a) If you select JIT and click Next, complete the configuration as follows:
• In the Group Provisioning screen, select your preferred mode of provisioning the groups. The options are
Groups Pre-provisioning or Just-In-Time Group Provisioning and click Next.
Option Description
Groups Pre-Provisioning This option creates the required groups in advance to perform role
assignments. Users are assigned to these groups dynamically
when they log in based on OIDC token. Only the pre-provisioned
groups are available for role assignments.
Just-In-Time Group Provisioning This option creates groups dynamically based on the OIDC token
when the user logs in.
Alternatively, you can use group pre-provisioning if you know the
group names from Active Directory that requires entitlements.

provision in VCF for roles and assignments by clicking the Add Group button, and click Next.
Note:
The Pre-provisioning Domains and Groups screen is displayed only if you have chosen groups to be pre-
provisioned which means that you chose Groups pre-provisioning in the previous screen.
There should be at least one provisioned group added across the domains.

attributes that you view in the OIDC response from the identity provider.

group attribute to be called for in the OIDC request. Attribute names are case-sensitive.

Directory name Enter a name for the directory.

string in the Primary domain controller field) the filename {directory-name}-concatenated.pem

Mail) PEM format and includes the "BEGIN

enforcing policies, and storing directory data. For example,
hostname = DC01 for the domain called example.com.

Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify
entries in the directory. For example, uid, sAMAccountName.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

directory tree from which LDAP queries begin. For example, dc=e
xample, dc=com.

authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.
Bind user password The password of a user account with sufficient permissions to
authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.

Important:
Important Notes on Backup
It is highly advisable to create a backup of both VCF Operations and the identity broker instance. Furthermore,
it is advisable to perform a similar backup following any substantial modifications to the initial identity source
configuration, such as when you 'Delete Single Sign-On'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF
single sign-on configuration to a recognized and stable state if necessary. You can download the configuration as
a JSON file.
Important Notes on Role Assignment
VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component roles.
• As an admin you can assign built-in and custom VCF roles to groups and and users from the Access
Managment tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF Single Sign-On configuration, and
then click the Access Management tab).
• As an admin, you can also assign roles in the component console and enable VCF single sign-on from the
Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single sign-on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration tab).

Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter a friendly name for your identity provider.
Metadata XML Copy the Metadata XML of your identity provider and paste it in
this field.
The Metadata XML is a URL that points to an XML document
containing metadata about the service provider (identity broker).
This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.
Note:
If you have configured VCF single sign-on, after you
upgrade to 9.1.1, it is recommended that you re-import
the identity broker service provider metadata into your
identity provider. Re-importing ensures your identity
provider reads the new encryption hint and switches
to SHA-256 OAEP for all subsequent SAML assertion
encryption.
Metadata URL Copy the Metadata URL of your identity provider and paste it in

This metadata includes important information required for
establishing trust and facilitating secure communication between
the service provider and the identity provider.

If your identity provider is not publicly accessible or uses
a self-signed certificate, VCF Operations cannot validate
the metadata URL. Provide the metadata in XML format
instead.

The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify
the authenticated user.

transport security.

Directory name Enter a name for the directory.

Some of the limitations with selecting the global catalog option
include:
• The Active Directory object attributes that are replicated to the
global catalog are identified in the Active Directory schema
as the Partial Attribute Set (PAS). Only these attributes are
available for attribute mapping by the service. If necessary,

attributes) of only universal groups. Only universal groups are
synced to the service. If necessary, change the scope of a

directory in the service must have permissions to read the

domains, the additional domains are discovered only after
the user/group sync is complete.

10.In the Configure User and Group Provisioning screen, depending on the option you choose, complete the following
steps and click Done.
a) If you have chosen SCIM, you see Configure SCIM push in your identity provider instead of Configure User
and Group Provisioning. Use the values listed on the screen to configure the SCIM application in the identity
provider.
• If your identity provider supports authorizing the SCIM application using OAuth grant type, use the client ID,
client secret, and token endpoint. Otherwise, use the SCIM bearer token to authorize this SCIM server in your
identity provider.
• If required, you can regenerate these values after you have configured VCF single-sign on. To regenerate the
values to configure the SCIM application in the identity provider, navigate to the respective VCF Instance and
click on Identity Source. The SCIM related values are available under Directory Information.
• Ensure that the user attributes, username, and domain are pushed individually from the SCIM application by the
identity provider. Similarly, ensure that the group attributes, group name, and domain are pushed individually as
well.
b) If you have chosen JIT, there is no additional step to be performed under User and Group Provisioning.
c) If you have chosen AD/LDAP, review the directory information such as the domain controller and bind credentials
that you had configured. Complete the following steps:

The attributes in the identity broker directory are mapped to the Active Directory attributes for accurate
synchronization of user information. If the mappings are incorrect, select the correct attribute from the drop-
down list.
2. In the Group Provisioning screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Use the Group Provisioning screen to search for the group names and select the corresponding Active

Option Description
Specify the Base Group DN Click the Select Base Group DN button if you have nested
groups and want to specify the group names. You can search for
the group name and select the group DNs that you want to sync
from from the list in the datagrid below.

selected group and its nested group without maintaining the group
hierarchy.

group, do not specify a base user DN.

at a scheduled time.

For more information about the various functionalities you can perform as part of the management operations in
