Important:
Important Notes on Backup
It is highly advisable to create a backup of both VCF Operations and the identity broker instance. Furthermore,
it is advisable to perform a similar backup following any substantial modifications to the initial identity source
configuration, such as when you 'Delete Single Sign-On'. This practice ensures that you can restore the VCF
single-sign on configuration to a recognized and stable state if necessary. You can download the configuration as
a JSON file.
Important Notes on Role Assignment
VCF roles can be created and mapped to individual component roles.
• As an admin you can assign built-in and custom VCF roles to groups and and users from the Access
Managment tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single-sign on configuration, and
then click the Access Management tab).
• As an admin, you can also assign roles in the component console and enable VCF single-sign on from the
Component Configuration tab (navigate to the VCF SSO Overview page, click on a VCF single-sign on
configuration, and then click the Component Configuration tab).
Configure an Identity Provider using Generic OIDC
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single sign-on, you can configure an identity provider using
Generic OIDC as the authentication protocol.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test login if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
• If you configure VCF single sign-on using identity broker instance, and there are network restrictions that do not allow
outbound public internet access, you must set up a proxy server. For more information, see Configure a Proxy Server
for VCF Management Services Components and VCF Automation.
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
If you have an existing identity provider configured in vCenter, see the information below. For a fresh configuration of
the identity provider, continue from Step 6.
For an existing source (existing identity provider configuration)
Broadcom 4108

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Choose either SAML or OIDC as the authentication protocol.
Note:
If you choose SAML, the VCF Single Sign-On configuration is considered as a new authentication source
configuration. Continue from Step. 6.
• If you choose OIDC:
– If you choose the instance deployment mode, and select OIDC, the following fields are prepopulated in the
Identity Provider Configuration screen.
a. Review the details and provide the shared secret and click Next.
• Identity provider name
• Client identifier
• OpenID address
• Update Redirect URI in the Identity provider's OIDC application
• Shared Secret: Paste the client secret of the OIDC application you created in the identity provider.
b. Review the User/Group Provisioning, Domain(s), and Review screens and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM push details and click Done. The identity provider configuration is complete.
– If you choose the embedded deployment mode, and select OIDC:
a. The configuration details of the identity provider configuration are automatically imported from existing
configuration into the identity broker with OIDC as the authentication protocol and SCIM as the user/group
provisioning method.
b. Review the configuration values in the Identity Provider Configuration screen and click Finish.
c. Review the SCIM details, click Done and then click Finish Setup. The identity provider configuration is
complete.
2. For a fresh identity provider configuration, from the Choose the identity provider section, select OIDC from the list
and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
Note:
Ensure that you add the following default claims when you configure your external identity provider. These claims
are case-sensitive:
• preferred_username
• email
• family_name
• given_name
• groups
• domain
If the default claims cannot be added, use alternative claim names and map them to the appropriate attributes in
the VCF Operations Identity & Access page to support your JIT configurations.
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Identity Provider Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
IDP Display Name Enter the OpenID Connect provider name. Example, Microsoft
Entra ADFS.
Client Identifier A unique ID assigned to your OIDC application by the identity
provider, for authentication.
Broadcom 4109

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Shared secret A confidential key used by your OIDC application to authenticate
itself with the identity provider.
Note:
Client secrets issued by external identity providers
typically have expiration dates. When a client secret
expires, it must be regenerated, and the corresponding
OIDC configuration must be updated in VCF to ensure
continued authentication functionality.
OpenID Address The URL of the identity provider’s OIDC configuration endpoint for
initiating the authentication process.
Redirect URI The URL where the identity provider will send the authentication
response after a user logs in.
List of domains Domains for user to login to your company.
Table 1135: Keycloak Options
Enter the following details if you are configuring Keycloak as an identity provider.
Option Description
Entity ID/Metadata URL Copy the Entity ID/Metadata XML of your identity provider and
paste it in this field.The Entity ID/Metadata XML is a URL that
points to an XML document containing metadata about the service
provider (identity broker). This metadata includes important
information required for establishing trust and facilitating secure
communication between the service provider and the identity
provider.
Assertion Consumer Service URL An endpoint on the Service Provider (identity broker) that is
responsible for receiving and processing the SAML assertions
sent by the identity provider.
Name ID format and Name ID value The Name ID format is the value in the SAML response to identify
the authenticated user.
SAML Context SAML context refers to the type of user authentication that VCF
needs to be mandated in the identity provider.
• PasswordProtectedTransport: Authentication with a
password sent over a secure transport (For example, HTTPS).
• Password: Authentication using a password without requiring
transport security.
• Unspecified: Select this option if you do not want to enforce
any particular type of authentication mechanism.

You can select either:

Managing AD/LDAP
You can integrate Active Directory with VCF single-sign on. After Active Directory is connected, you can perform several
operations to manage the Active Directory connection such as view a list of active directories, add additional directories,
modify sync settings, and view the sync log.
To start managing the AD/LDAP connection, navigate to the corresponding VCF Instance in which VCF single-sign on was
configured. The Identity Source tab contains the relevant information pertaining to the identity provider configuration. If
more than one VCF Instance is connected to the Active Directory, use the link in the Identity Source tab to navigate to
the relevant VCF Instance. Reset VCF single-sign on to manage the Active Directory connection.
Prerequisite
• Configure an identity provider for AD/LDAP before you start managing it. For more information, see Configure Active
Directory as an Identity Provider Using AD/LDAP.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click Configure VCF SSO.
3. In the VCF Overview SSO page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF single-sign on.
4. In the Identity Source tab you see different sections such as Deployment Mode, Authentication Information, and
Directory Information.
The Deployment Mode and Authentication Information sections indicate the type of deployment and connection
respectively.
Directory Information
The datagrid lists the directories that have been configured. You can add, edit, or delete the directories.
Column Name Description
Directory Name User friendly name of the directory that was configured.
Domain The domain name of the domain controller that was configured as part of the directory
configuration.
Synced groups The total number of groups that have been synced from the directory to the identity broker.
For example, as an enterprise admin, if you have selected 10 groups to provision, but only 8
groups were synced, then only 8 groups are displayed.
Synced users The total number of users that have been synced from the directory to the identity broker.
For example, as an enterprise admin, if you have selected 10 groups to provision, but, only 8
groups were synced, then only 8 groups are displayed.
Alerts The number of alert(s) that might have occurred during the last performed successful sync.
Sync on request Click the link to trigger an on-demand sync from the corresponding directory in Active
Directory.
Last sync status The day and time of the last performed successful sync. If the last sync fails, the status
reflects the same. Click on Learn More for more information. See the table about
#unique_2216/unique_2216_Connect_42_id-657241ba-294f-494e-cd00-820752f147dd for
more information about sync failure errors and the reasons.
Broadcom 4119

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Sync Failure Messages
Error Message Reason/Remediation
LDAP server is not reachable This could be due to network issues, firewall blocks, an incorrect
host name, or invalid BIND credentials. Verify the configuration
and retry the sync.
An internal error occurred during a sync with the LDAP server. Retry sync.
The users don't have the required object UUID property Ensure that the attribute mapping is correct and all the objects
have the attribute.
The groups don't have the required object UUID property Ensure that the attribute mapping is correct and all the objects
have the attribute.
Group Query Failed The group is not found in Active Directory.
Add Additional Directories
You can add a new directory by clicking on the Add button. You can add a new LDAP-based directory with different
modes of on-demand or pre-provisioning user/group settings. To configure a directory in AD/LDAP, see Configure Active
Directory as an Identity Provider Using AD/LDAP .
Edit Existing Directories
You can edit the directory by clicking on the Edit button. From the Directory Details page, click the Edit button at the top of
each of the following pages to modify the existing configuration details:
• Details
• Attribute mappings
• Group provisioning
• User provisioning
• Sync Settings - For more information, see the section called 'Modify Sync Settings' below.
• Sync Log - For more information, see the section called 'View Sync Log' below.
Note:
After you modify configurations in the Attribute Mappings, Group provisioning, User provisioning, and Sync
Settings screens, you are prompted with an option to trigger an on-demand sync. If you do not trigger the on-
demand sync, changes to users and groups take place in the next scheduled sync.
Modify Sync Settings
Editing the directories includes modifying the sync settings. The sync schedule is set to once per week, however you can
modify the sync schedule by clicking the Edit button in the Sync Settings screen. Sync schedule is configured in UTC.
View Sync Log
The sync log under each directory contains the log of each sync between identity broker. and the configured domain
controller in Active Directory. As part of this sync, users and groups are added or removed. You can view the time at which
the sync was completed, the number of groups and users that were modified because of the sync, the status of the sync,
and alerts. Here is a list of error messages.
Error Message Possible Reason(s)
Invalid group attribute name The group object has an invalid or a missing required attribute
from Active Directory.
Invalid user attribute name The user object has an invalid or missing required attribute from
Active Directory.
Multiple attribute values The attribute that was mapped to the user/group contains more
than one value in Active Directory.
User or Group Query Failed The user/group was not found in Active Directory.

Configure OpenLDAP as an Identity Provider
After installing or upgrading to VCF 9.1, to configure VCF single-sign on, you can configure OpenLDAP as an identity
provider.
To set up an identity provider, you must:
1. Choose an identity provider
2. Configure the identity provider
3. Configure user and group provisioning
4. Test Login
Note:
You can test login if the identity broker is at version 9.1.
Prerequisite
• Verify that you have chosen a deployment mode. For more information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode.
• Ensure that the is activated in the OpenLDAP server. For information about activating
memberOf overlay
, see OpenLDAP Overlays.
memberOf overlay
Procedure
Choose the identity provider
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Configure Identity Provider option.
2. From the Choose the identity provider section, select OpenLDAP from the list and click Next.
Configure the identity provider
3. From the Configure the Identity Provider section, click Configure to configure the identity broker to integrate with
the selected identity provider for user authentication.
4. In the Directory Details screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
Directory name Enter a name for the directory.
Primary domain controller A server machine responsible for managing and authenticating
user access, enforcing policies, and storing directory data.
For example, hostname = DC01 for the domain called
example.com.
Certificate for primary domain controller The root certificate required to access primary domain controller
over SSL.
Note:
Ensure that the certificate is in PEM format and include
the "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" and "END CERTIFICATE"
lines.
Secondary domain controller A backup domain controller for the identity broker to point to if the
primary domain controller is not reachable.
Certificate for secondary domain controller The root certificate required to access secondary domain
controller over SSL.
Note:
Ensure that the certificate is in PEM format and include
the "BEGIN CERTIFICATE" and "END CERTIFICATE"
lines.
Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify
entries in the directory.
Note:
By default 'Custom Attribute' is chosen.
Broadcom 4121

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Custom directory search attribute for Users The LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify users in
the directory.
Custom directory search attribute for Groups The LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify groups in
the directory.
Base DN The Distinguished Name (DN) of the top-level entry in the
directory tree from which LDAP queries begin. For example, dc=e
xample, dc=com.
Bind user name The user name of a user account with sufficient permissions to
authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.
Bind user password The password of a user account with sufficient permissions to
authenticate and perform LDAP operations on the directory.
Note:
An additional OpenLDAP server can be created after the first OpenLDAP server is configured.
5. In the LDAP Configuration screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Option Description
Groups The search filter for obtaining group objects. For example:
(objectClass=group)
Bind user The search filter for obtaining the bind user object, that is, the user
that can bind to the directory. For example: (objectClass=person)
Users The search filter for obtaining users to sync. For example:
(&(objectClass=user)(objectCategory=person))
Object UUID The attribute that is used in your LDAP directory to define the
UUID of a user or group. For example: entryUUID.
6. In the Review screen, review the details you have added for the configuration and click Finish.
Configure user and group provisioning
7. In the Configure User and Group Provisioning screen, click Configure to provision the users and groups from the
identity provider to the identity broker .
8. In the Directory Review Information screen, review the information directory information and click Next.
9. In the Attributes Mappings screen, review the attribute mappings and click Next.
The attributes in the identity broker directory are mapped to the LDAP Directory attributes for accurate synchronization
of user information. If the mappings are incorrect, select the correct attribute from the drop-down list.
10.In the Group Provisioning screen, enter the relevant details or select the required option and click Next.
Option Description
Specify the base group DN Enter the details of the base group DN.
View Groups Click this option if you want to specify the group names.
You can search for the group name and select the group DNs that
you want to sync from from the list in datagrid below.
Note:
You can specify only one Base DN for group searches.
To provision groups from multiple locations within Active
Directory, it is recommended that you set the Base DN
at a higher level in the directory hierarchy that includes
all the required groups such as a parent Organizational
Unit (OU) or domain root and then select the necessary
groups.
Broadcom 4122

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Only groups with a valid DN, a unique identifier, and the required attributes (such as group name and object GUID)
that match the configured directory search attribute are provisioned.
11.From the User Provisioning screen, enter the relevant details or select the required options and click Next.
Use the User Provisioning screen to search for the user names and select the corresponding Active Directory group
Distinguished Names (DN) that you want to sync.
Option Description
Specify the Base User DN Click this option to specify the user names that you want to sync.
You can search for the user name and select the user DNs that
you want to sync from from the datagrid.
Note:
If you want to sync the users directly from the group, do
not specify a base user DN.
View Users Click this option if you want to specify the user names.
You can search for the user name and select the user DNs that
you want to sync from the list in the datagrid below.
12.From the Review screen, review the configuration details of the identity provider.
13.Click Finish. The sync starts in the background. After the initial sync, the sync is scheduled to run once a week at a
scheduled time.
14.Click Done.
(Optional) Test Login
15.Click Test Login to test the login using your single-sign on credentials.
16.Click Next in the identity provider screen.

Step 3: Configure VCF Single Sign-On for NSX and vCenter
After you have configured an identity provider for VCF single-sign on, connect vCenter and NSX components to the
identity broker for single-sign on-based access. You can select only those vCenter and NSX components that belong to
the VCF Instance that hosts the identity broker. In the case of an embedded identity broker, the management domain
vCenter is automatically configured and you cannot configure/unjoin the management domain vCenter.
Prerequisites
• Verify that you have configured the identity provider for VCF single-sign on. For more information, see Step 2:
Configure an Identity Provider.
Procedure
1. In the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the Enable SSO for vCenter and NSX option.
2. In the Enable SSO for vCenter and NSX page, from the grid, select the vCenter or NSX components for which you
want to enable VCF Single Sign-On.
Note:
• Only vCenter or NSX components that are of version 9.0 or later and are not part of the ELM ring are
supported for configuring VCF single-sign on access.
3. Click Configure.
4. In the Confirmation required box, read the information, select the checkbox, and click Finish.
Role Assignments
You can assign VCF roles to the provisioned users and groups from VCF Operations or you can assign roles and
permissions from the individual components.
Broadcom 4125

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Assign VCF roles from VCF Operations. After the components are configured as part of the initial setup, you can
create VCF roles and can assign the VCF roles to users/groups. For information about assigning VCF roles to users/
groups, see Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role. For information about VCF roles, see Managing VCF Roles.
• Assign Roles and Permissions from Individual Components. Alternatively, after the components are configured
as part of the initial setup, log in with the local admin account to each component and assign the necessary roles to
the provisioned users and groups. You can launch the components from the Component Configuration tab. For
information about assigning roles, see Assigning Roles and Permissions from Individual Components.
Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role
As an administrator, when you configure VCF single-sign on in VCF Operations, you can assign VCF roles to provisioned
users and groups from VCF Operations for components such as vCenter, VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF
Operations orchestrator, VCF Operations HCX, and NSX.
Note:
Alternatively, you can also assign the required roles and permissions for users or groups from each individual
component. To assign roles and permissions for users and groups from each individual component, see Assigning
Roles and Permissions from Individual Components.
Procedure
1. From the Configure VCF SSO page, click the Start button against the (Optional) Assign VCF Roles option.
2. In the Assign VCF Roles page, you see a list of users and groups that are provisioned under the Users and Groups
tabs.
3. Select the group and/or user that you would like to assign the role to, and click Assign.
4. In the Assign VCF Roles page, under the section that is called Roles, enter the following details and then click
Apply. If you would like to create roles, see Managing VCF Roles.
Option Description
Scope • All components. All the components configured with the relevant identity broker.
• Individual VCF Instances. You can scope the role assignment to one or more VCF
Instances.
Scoping is applicable to vCenter and NSX components that are part of the VCF Instance.
Note:
As a user, you automatically get access to any new vCenter or NSX instances that
are added.
Role Select a role from the drop-down list.
If you selected VCF Instance as the scope, only roles that contain vCenter or NSX
component roles are listed.
Valid Until • Never Expires. Select this option if you do not want to set an expiry date for the role.
• Custom Date (UTC). Enter a date until when you would like the role to be valid.
Note:
You can add more than one role.
5. Click Assign and Done.
6. In the Configure VCF SSO page, click Finish Setup.
For information about managing VCF role assignments, see Manage VCF Role Assignments After Configuring VCF
Single Sign-On.

Configure VCF Single Sign-On for VCF Operations and VCF Automation Provider
You can connect VCF Operations and/or VCF Automation Provider to an identity broker for single sign-on access.
Configure VCF Single Sign-On for VCF Operations
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. On the VCF SSO Overview page, from the grid under the VCF Management tab, select operations appliance.
4. Click Join VCF SSO.
5. On the Join VCF SSO page, select an identity broker and click Join.
6. Read the information about role assignments and click Finish.
Note:
• Create and assign VCF roles to grant users and groups permissions to individual roles. Role assignments are
required to enable single sign-on for the selected component. For information about creating and managing
VCF roles, see Create a Custom VCF Role and Assign Custom and Built-In VCF Roles.
• Alternatively, you can assign roles from each individual component. For more information, see Assigning Roles
and Permissions from Individual Components.
Configure VCF Single Sign-On for VCF Automation Provider
Procedure
• In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
• In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
• On the VCF SSO Overview page, from the data grid under the VCF Management tab, select Automation appliance.
• Click Join VCF SSO.
• On the Join VCF SSO page, select an identity broker and click Join.
• Read the information about role assignments and click Finish.
Note:
• Create and assign VCF roles that to grant users and groups permissions to individual roles. Role assignments
are required to activate Single Sign-On for the selected component. For information about creating and
managing VCF roles, see Create a Custom VCF Role and Assign Custom and Built-In VCF Roles.
• Alternatively, you can assign roles from each individual component. For more information, see Assigning Roles
and Permissions from Individual Components.

In versions 9.1.1 and later, you can connect Salt RaaS to an identity broker for single sign-on access.
Procedure

Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. On the VCF SSO Overview page, from the grid under the VCF Management tab, select Salt RaaS.
4. Click Join VCF SSO.
5. On the Join VCF SSO page, select an identity broker and click Join. Read the information about role assignments
and click Finish.
• Create and assign VCF roles to grant users and groups permissions to individual roles. Role assignments are required

Step 6: (Optional) Configure VCF Single Sign-On for other VCF Components
Configure VCF single sign-on for other VCF Components such as VCF Operations HCX, VCF Operations for networks,
VCF Operations orchestrator, and VCF Automation tenant.
• To configure VCF single sign-on for VCF Operations HCX, Configure VCF SSO.
• To configure VCF single sign-on for VCF Operations for networks, see Configuring VCF SSO for VCF Operations for
networks.
• To configure VCF single sign-on for CLI tools like PowerCLI, see Using VCF Single Sign-On to Access vCenter using
PowerCLI.
• To configure VCF single sign-on for VCF Automation tenant, see Configure Your VCF Automation Organization to Use
an OpenID Identity Provider.
CAUTION:
• VCF Automation tenant support is restricted to a single segment.
• Multiple VCF Automation instances are unsupported.
• The configured user and group scale must not exceed the published identity broker configuration maximum.
For more information, see identity broker maximum limits.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components is supported in enterprise environments only. Cloud
service provider environments are not supported.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components is limited to the identity broker instance deployment
mode only, and is not supported on identity broker embedded deployment mode.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components, is supported on VCF products only and is not
available for non-VCF products.
Using VCF Single Sign-On to Access vCenter using PowerCLI
You can configure CLI and automation tools like PowerCLI to use VCF single sign-on. You can configure CLI and
automation tools like PowerCLI to access vCenter only, using VCF single sign-on. If you are an existing customer
upgrading to VCF 9.1, existing automation scripts using CLI tools will not be impacted if VCF single sign-on is configured
in the same management domain vCenter in embedded mode. However, if single sign-on is configured in instance mode,
or in an alternate management domain vCenter, a new OAuth client must be generated for PowerCLI.
Prerequisite
Verify that VCF single sign-on is configured for at least one VCF Instance. For more information, see Configure a New
VCF Single Sign-On for a VCF Instance.
1. From the VCF Operations navigation pane, select Fleet Management > Identity & Access > VCF Other
Components.
2. Click Add and enter the following information:
• Name - Custom name for the OIDC client.
Broadcom 4129

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Identity broker - Choose the identity broker with which you want to configure Single Sign-On.
• Redirect URI - The endpoint to which the identity broker needs to redirect after authentication. The URI must follow
the HTTP schema, and be on localhost with a free port on the client machine. For example: "http://localhost:8844/
auth."
• Post logout redirect URI - Not applicable for Single Sign-On with PowerCLI.
3. Click Generate OIDC Client.
4. Copy and store the Client ID, client secret, and Identity Broker issuer URL securely in a safe place.
5. Click Save.
6. Create an OAuth security context object for PowerCLI. For example, see the following script.
$oauthSecContext = New-OAuthSecurityContext -TokenEndpointUrl "https://<vcenter_fqdn>/acs/t/CUSTOMER/
token" -
AuthorizationEndpointUrl "https://<vcenter_fqdn>/acs/t/CUSTOMER/authorize" -RedirectUrl "http://
localhost:8844/auth" -
ClientId "powercli-native" -ClientSecret "<secret_value>"
TokenEndpointUrl
AuthorizationEndpointUrl
RedirectUrl
ClientId
ClientSecret
Note:
The Redirect URL should be the same as the value entered in Step 2 - Redirect URI.
7. Exchange the OAuth 2.0 security context for a SAML security context.
$samlSecContext = New-VISamlSecurityContext -VCenterServer '<vcenter_fqdn>' -OAuthSecurityContext
$oauthSecContext
8. Connect to your vCenter using the SAML security context.
Connect-VIServer -Server '<vcenter_fqdn>' -SamlSecurityContext $samlSecContext
Note:
Single sign-on through CLI tools is possible only through vCenter in VCF 9.1.
Manage VCF Instances after Configuring VCF Single Sign-On
After you have configured VCF single sign-on, you can connect to an existing single sign-on configuration and add a VCF
Instance to the pre-configured identity broker. After you have configured single sign-on from VCF Operations, you can
also choose to change or remove VCF Instances from/to an existing VCF single sign-on Configuration.
• To connect or add a VCF Instances to an existing VCF single sign-on configuration, see Connect VCF Instances to an
Existing VCF Single Sign-On.
• To change or modify VCF Instances in an existing VCF single sign-on configuration, see Modify VCF Instances in an
Existing VCF Single Sign-On Configuration.
• To remove VCF Instances from an existing VCF single sign-on configuration, see Remove VCF Instances from an
Existing VCF Single Sign-On Configuration.
Connect VCF Instances to an Existing VCF Single Sign-On
After you have configured VCF single sign-on from VCF Operations, you can choose to join additional VCF Instances to
an existing VCF single sign-on configuration.
Prerequisites
• Ensure that you have added a VCF Instance. For more information, see Start a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance
Deployment by Using the VCF Installer Deployment Wizard.
Broadcom 4130

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Ensure that you have configured an identity provider for VCF Single Sign-On. For more information, see Step 2:
Configure an Identity Provider.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the grid under VCF Instances, select the VCF Instances that you would like to
add to VCF single sign-on and click Join VCF SSO.
4. In the Join VCF SSO page, follow these steps and click Next:
a) In the grid under Choose SSO, select the identity broker you would like to connect to.
b) In the grid under the Configure Components section, click the drop-down arrow against the relevant VCF
Instances and verify if you want to add all the components that are selected.
Note:
• By default, all the components in the selected VCF Instance are part of the single sign-on configuration.
You can choose to customize the list and de-select the components that you wish to exclude from the
configuration.
• vCenter and NSX 9.0 and later versions are supported and displayed.
5. Read and accept the information about role assignment that is required to activate VCF single sign-on for the selected
components and then click Finish.
You can log in as a local admin to each component and can assign service roles to provisioned users and groups. For
more information about assigning service roles, see Assigning Roles and Permissions from Individual Components.
6. In the Configure VCF SSO Overview page, navigate to the VCF Instances tab to see the VCF Instances you have
added to VCF single sign-on configuration.
Modify VCF Instances in an Existing VCF Single Sign-On Configuration
After you have configured VCF single sign-on from VCF Operations, you can choose to change or modify VCF Instances
in an existing VCF single sign-on.
Prerequisites
• Ensure that you have added a VCF Instance. For more information, see Start a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance
Deployment by Using the VCF Installer Deployment Wizard.
• Ensure that you have configured an identity provider for VCF single sign-on. For more information, see Step 2:
Configure an Identity Provider.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the grid under VCF Instances, select the VCF Instances that you would like to
change in the VCF single sign-on configuration, and then click the horizontal ellipsis > Change VCF SSO option.
4. In the Change VCF SSO page, follow these steps:
a) In the grid under Choose SSO, select a identity broker.
b) In the grid under the Configure Components section, click the drop-down arrow against the relevant VCF
Instances to view the components that were previously configured.
• All previously configured components in the selected VCF Instance are migrated to the new VCF single sign-on
Configuration.
• vCenter and NSX 9.0 and later versions are supported and displayed.
Broadcom 4131

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
c) Click Next and read and confirm the information about role assignments.
Modifying VCF single sign-on removes all role assignments that are scoped to the VCF Instance. To reassign roles,
see Assign VCF Roles After Configuring VCF Single Sign-On.
Remove VCF Instances from an Existing VCF Single Sign-On Configuration
After you have configured VCF single sign-on from VCF Operations, you can choose to remove VCF Instances in an
existing VCF single sign-on.
Prerequisites
• Ensure that you have added a VCF Instance. For more information, see Start a New VCF Fleet or a New VCF Instance
Deployment by Using the VCF Installer Deployment Wizard.
• Ensure that you have configured an identity provider for VCF single sign-on. For more information, see Step 2:
Configure an Identity Provider.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the grid under VCF Instances, select the VCF Instances that you would like to
remove in the VCF single sign-on configuration, and then click the horizontal ellipsis > Unjoin VCF SSO option.
4. Read the message about role assignments and click Unjoin.
If you remove a VCF Instance from an existing VCF single sign-on configuration, all role assignments that are scoped
to the VCF Instance are removed.
Managing VCF Single Sign-On
After you configure and start using VCF single sign-on, you can view the existing identity brokers, reset VCF single
sign-on, change an identity provider, change the deployment mode, edit the configuration of an identity provider, add or
deregister existing component configurations, manage API and access tokens, and so on.
• To view configured identity brokers, see Overview of VCF Single Sign-On Configurations.
• To delete VCF single sign-on, see Delete a VCF Single Sign-On Configuration.
• To change the identity provider in VCF single sign-on, see Change the Identity Provider in VCF Single Sign-On.
• To change the deployment mode, see Change the Deployment Mode in VCF Single Sign-On.
• To change the provisioning method, see Change the Provisioning Method in VCF Single Sign-On.
• To migrate identity broker embedded to identity broker instance, see Migration of Identity Broker Embedded to Identity
Broker Instance.
• To edit the configuration of an identity provider, see Edit the Configuration of an Identity Provider.
• To edit the display name of the identity broker, see Edit the Display Name of the Identity Broker.
• To manage VCF role assignments after configuring VCF Single Sign-On, see Manage VCF Role Assignments After
Configuring VCF Single Sign-On.
• To test login after configuring VCF single sign-on, see Test Login after Configuring VCF Single Sign On.
• To change or remove VCF Operations and VCF Automation components, see Change or Remove VCF Operations
and VCF Automation Components.
• To add, change, or remove other VCF components, see Add, Change, or Remove Other VCF Components.
• To assign roles and permissions from individual components, see Assigning Roles and Permissions from Individual
Components.
• For versions 9.1.1 and later, to search for on-demand users and groups and assign roles, see Search for Users and
Groups Dynamically and Assign Roles using On-Demand Lookup.
• For versions 9.1.1 and later, to verify if on-demand lookup is enabled, see Review Directory Details to Verify if On-
demand Lookup is Enabled.
• For versions 9.1.1 and later, to add a directory for identity providers that are configured using AD/LDAP, see Add a
Directory for Identity Providers that are Configured using AD/LDAP.
Broadcom 4132

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Overview of VCF Single Sign-On Configurations
Use the VCF SSO Overview page for a holistic overview of the VCF fleet that has been configured with VCF single sign-
on.
Multiple VCF instances can participate in a VCF single sign-on configuration managed by a single identity broker. To
view details of a specific VCF single sign-on configuration and its participating VCF Instances, in the VCF Overview SSO
page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have configured for VCF single sign-on.
From the Overview tab, click the VCF Instances tab.
In VCF Operations, you can monitor the status of VCF identity brokers based on parameters such as health and
readiness. Health indicates if the identity broker is up and running or not. Readiness indicates if the identity broker is
ready to accept incoming requests or not. From VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate, and then
navigate to Inventory > Integrations icon > Infrastructure Management > Identity Broker health.
Delete a VCF Single Sign-On Configuration
You can delete a VCF single sign-on configuration that is associated with one or more VCF Instance.
When you delete a VCF single sign-on configuration, the entire VCF single sign-on configuration including the identity
provider configuration, provisioned users/groups, and component configuration are deleted.
Note:
• The delete action cannot be reverted.
• If the user performing the deletion of VCF single sign-on is part of the particular VCF single sign-on
configuration being deleted, then the session terminates immediately post deletion. The user has to log in
again as a local admin account user. You might want to consider logging in as a local admin user to perform
the reset activity.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. From the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF Overview SSO page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF single sign-on.
4. Click Actions > Delete SSO from the top-right corner.
5. Select the following option and click Delete.
I confirm to delete of all SSO-related configurations, including the identity provider configuration, the
provisioned users and groups, and the component configuration.
Note:
If you delete VCF single sign-on for the VCF Instance, you must configure VCF single sign-on again.
6. You are directed to the Configure VCF SSO page from where you can complete the steps to configure VCF single
sign-on. For more information about configuring VCF single sign-on, see, Configure a New VCF Single Sign-On for a
VCF Instance.
Note:
If problems arise after deleting the VCF single sign-on configuration, refer to KB 393161 to restore a clean state.
Broadcom 4133

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Change the Identity Provider in VCF Single Sign-On
If you have configured VCF single sign-on using a certain identity provider and protocol, you can change the identity
provider in the future.
For example, you have configured VCF single sign-on using Active Directory, and wish to change to a modern identity
provider like Okta, Ping Identity, or Microsoft Entra ID. To change the identity provider, you must reset VCF single sign-on
and reconfigure the identity provider.
Note:
Since this is a partial reset, the deployment mode and client component configuration are retained. Therefore, you
do not have to reconfigure the client for vCenter, VCF Operations HCX,, VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF
Operations for networks, or log management to the specific identity broker.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF Overview SSO page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF Single Sign-On.
4. Click Actions > Change the Identity Provider from the top-right corner.
5. In the Change Identity Provider dialog box that is displayed, select the following option and click Change.
I confirm to delete of all SSO-related configurations, including the identity provider configuration, the
provisioned users and groups, and the component configuration.
Note:
The components that are configured against this identity broker are retained. After you configure a new identity
provider, you might need to assign roles to the newly provisioned users and groups. For information about
assigning roles, see Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role.
6. You are directed to the Configure VCF SSO page. In the Configure VCF SSO screen, click the second step,
Configure Identity Provider, to reconfigure the identity provider. For more information, see Step 2: Configure an
Identity Provider.
Change the Deployment Mode in VCF Single Sign-On
If you have configured VCF single sign-on using a certain deployment mode, you can choose another deployment mode
in the future.
For example, you have chosen the identity broker embedded deployment mode to configure VCF single sign-on for a VCF
Instance. If necessary, you can change the deployment mode to identity broker instance for the specific VCF Instance.
Conversely, you can change the deployment mode from identity broker instance to identity broker embedded.
Procedure
Broadcom 4134

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF Single Sign-On.
4. Click Actions > Delete SSO from the top-right corner. For more information about deleting VCF Single Sign-On, see
Delete a VCF Single Sign-On Configuration.
5. Click Delete. The Configure VCF SSO screen is displayed.
6. In the Configure VCF SSO screen, click the Start button against the Choose deployment mode option. For more
information, see Step 1: Choose the Deployment Mode and Configure a New VCF Single Sign-On for a VCF Instance.
Ensure that the users and groups are assigned the required VCF roles after you complete configuring the identity provider.
For information about assigning VCF roles, see Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role.
If you configured VCF Single Sign-On in VCF 9.0 using identity broker embedded and you want to migrate to identity
broker instance, see Migration of Identity Broker Embedded to Identity Broker Instance.
Change the Provisioning Method in VCF Single Sign-On
If you have configured VCF single sign-on using SCIM or JIT as the provisioning method, you can choose to change the
provisoning method to AD/LDAP or JIT.
The following migrations are supported:
• SCIM to LDAP. For more information, see Change the Provisioning Method from SCIM to AD/LDAP.
• SCIM to JIT. For more information, see Change the Provisioning Method from SCIM to JIT.
• JIT to LDAP. For more information, see Change the Provisioning Method from JIT to LDAP.
Change the Provisioning Method from SCIM to AD/LDAP
If you have configured VCF single sign-on with SCIM as the provisioning method, you can change to AD/LDAP
provisioning.
Prerequisites
• Verify that VCF single sign-on was configured using SCIM as the provisioning method.
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF single sign-on.
4. In the Identity Source tab, against Provisioning Method, click Change.
5. In the Pre-read screen, read and understand the information, and then click Next.
6. In the User/Group Provisioning Method screen, click AD/LDAP (Active Directory/Lightweight Directory Access
Protocol), and then click Next.
7. In the LDAP Lookup screen, select the type of domain controller configuration you use in Active Directory. Select one
of the following options, complete the relevant steps, and then click Next.
• Global Catalog, or
• Domain Specific Controller
Broadcom 4135

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
a) If you select Global Catalog, complete the following steps.
In the Directory Configuration screen, enter the following details or select the required options and click Validate
and Next.
Option Description
Directory name Enter a name for the directory.
Global Catalog Global catalog has a partial read-only replica of all objects across all domains.
Some of the limitations with selecting the global catalog option include:
• The Active Directory object attributes that are replicated to the global catalog are
identified in the Active Directory schema as the Partial Attribute Set (PAS). Only
these attributes are available for attribute mapping by the service. If necessary, edit
the schema to add or remove attributes that are stored in the global catalog.
• The global catalog stores the group membership (the member attributes) of only
universal groups. Only universal groups are synced to the service. If necessary,
change the scope of a group from a local domain or from global to universal.
• The bind DN account that you define when you configure a directory in the service
must have permissions to read the Token-Groups-Global-And-Universal (TGGAU)
attribute.
Note:
When you use Global catalog with LDAP and multiple domains, the additional
domains are discovered only after the user/group sync is complete.
Primary domain controller A server machine running Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) responsible for
(Displayed when you select the Global managing and authenticating user access, enforcing policies, and storing directory
Catalog option) data. For example, hostname = DC01 for the domain called example.com.
Secondary domain controller A backup domain controller for the identity broker to point to if the primary domain
(Displayed when you select the Global controller is not reachable.
Catalog option)
Directory search attribute A specific LDAP attribute used in queries to search or identify entries in the directory.
For example, uid, sAMAccountName.
Base DN The Distinguished Name (DN) of the top-level entry in the directory tree from which
LDAP queries begin. For example, dc=example, dc=com.
Bind user name The user name of a user account with sufficient permissions to authenticate and
perform LDAP operations on the directory.
Bind user password The password of a user account with sufficient permissions to authenticate and
perform LDAP operations on the directory.
b) If you select Domain Specific Controllers, complete the following steps:
In the Choose Domains screen, the domains that were identified from the existing configuration are displayed.
• Select the domain/s that you want to retain. Users and groups from the selected domain are retained to support
migration.
Note:
If a domain is not configured, the list of users/groups are deleted permanently and not referenced for migration.
• Click the check box to confirm your understanding, and then click Next.
Broadcom 4136

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
8. In the Choose Directory screen, configure the directory details for each listed domain and click Test Connection. If
successful, click Next.
9. In the Grace Period screen, enter a date. The mismatched users and groups from the existing configuration are
retained till the date specified. The cleanup of the mismatched users and groups begins on or after the date specified.
10.Click Finish and then click Continue. You see that the provisioning method has changed to AD/LDAP in the Identity
Source tab.
If there are mismatched user and groups, you can view them by clicking the View More link in the following banner at
the top of the page: x .
The previously configured users and groups are available for days
Provisioning users and groups
11.In the Identity Source tab, navigate to the Directory Information section. In the data grid under Provisioning
Method, click Setup Provisioning in the required row.
12.In the Review Directory Information page, review the information and click Next.
13.In the Attribute Mappings screen, ensure that the correct attributes have been mapped to the Active Directory
attributes, and then click Next.
14.In the Group Provisioning screen, complete the following steps, and click Next.
1. Sync Nested Group. Click this option if you want all the users from the selected group and its nested group to
sync without maintaining the group hierarchy. Do not select this option for large AD setups and manually select the
required groups.
2. Specify the Base Group DN. Click Add Base DN to select the base groups.
15.In the Users Provisioning screen, specify the base user group DN by clicking the Select Base User DN option to
select the base users, and click Next.
16.In the Review page, review the configuration details of the identity provider and then click Finish.
After the sync is complete, you can view the users and groups that have been provisioned by clicking the View More link
from the banner at the top of the Identity Source tab.

14.In the Review page, review the configuration details of the identity provider and then click Finish.
After the sync is complete, you can view the users and groups that have been provisioned by clicking the View More link
from the banner at the top of the Identity Source tab.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Migration of Identity Broker Embedded to Identity Broker Instance
If you configured VCF single sign-on in VCF 9.0 using identity broker embedded and you want to migrate to identity broker
instance, you can do so seamlessly. This transition ensures no data loss and maintains full access to your components
following the migration.
Prerequisites
• Verify that you configured VCF single sign-on in VCF 9.0 using identity broker embedded.
• Verify that the identity broker embedded is at version 9.1. Identity Broker embedded is updated with the vCenter
instance. For more information, see Upgrading vCenter and NSX Manager.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. From the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF Single Sign-On.
4. Click Actions > Migrate from Embedded to Instance from the top-right corner.
5. Read and accept the information about the impact of migrating identity broker embedded to identity broker instance.
6. From the Identity Broker Instance Target section, in the data grid, select the target identity broker instance that you
wish to migrate to.
Note:
• Only those VCF Instances with identity broker instance deployed are listed in the data grid.
• You can deploy a new identity broker instance if necessary and can use that as the target. For information
about deploying an identity broker instance, see Deploy Identity Broker as a Day-N Operation.
7. Enter the following SFTP details:
Option Description
SFTP Server Host Name Enter the name of the SFTP server host name.
SFTP Port Enter the SFTP port number.
Username Enter the name used to log in using SFTP.
Password Enter the password used to log in using SFTP.
Path Enter the file path where the data should be stored on the SFTP
server. The default value is set to /path.
Note:
For the duration of the data migration, create a dedicated, single-purpose SFTP user account. For security
purposes, this account's permissions must be restricted to access only the specific folder defined for the specific
account and must be deleted after the migration process is successfully completed.
8. Click Pre-check. If the pre-check is successful, click Start Migration.
If there is an error, pre-check displays the error that must be fixed. For example, if the SFTP server is not reachable,
an appropriate error message is displayed.
9. Data transfer follows a series of steps such as data export, import of data from SFTP, and restarting of services.
• During migration, identity provider configuration and user/group provisioning are suspended.
• Data transfer might take some time to complete.
10.Click Confirm to proceed to the next step of migration.
If you click Cancel, the migration process is aborted and configuration is deleted in the identity broker instance.
Broadcom 4140

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
11.In the Update Identity Provider section, copy the configuration details of the identity broker instance, navigate to the
admin console of the identity provider, and update the service provider details.
You can get service provider details from your third-party identity system.
12.Select the check box to confirm that you have updated the configuration details in the admin console of the external
identity provider.
In versions 9.1.1 and later, the Directory Information section displays a list of directories that have been configured.
The column that is called Provisioning Method is visible if Active Directory is configured as an identity provider using
AD/LDAP with on-demand search. The Provisioning Method column indicates whether users and groups are pre-
provisioned or configured through on-demand search.
13.Click Next.
14.In the Test Login section, you can validate log in to your identity provider connection using the Test Login link.
15.Click Next to validate log in to the corporate account using the identity provider details. After a successful login, you
will be directed back to the Change Deployment Mode page.
16.Click Next.
17.In the Update Components section, click Update Components to update the components so that they connect to the
identity broker instance and perform a sanity test. All component configurations are modified.
18.Click Next.
19.In the Summary section, click the check box to confirm that you will carry out the next steps which are:
• Manually update the configuration details for other components such as VCF Operations HCX, log management,
and VCF Operations for networks.
• Manually update the automation scripts that use the API clients.
20.Click Done.
21.In the Overview tab, you see the updated identity broker instance details.

Manage VCF Role Assignments After Configuring VCF Single Sign-On
After you configure VCF single sign-on, you can assign VCF roles, and edit and delete existing VCF roles assignments.

Assign VCF Roles After Configuring VCF Single Sign-On
You can assign custom and built-in VCF roles after you have configured VCF single sign-on. VCF level role functionality is
available starting with VCF 9.1.
Prerequisites
• Verify that you have configured VCF single sign-on.
Note:
• You can also assign component level roles from the associated component. For more information, see
Assigning Roles and Permissions from Individual Components
• Users and groups that have been assigned roles both at the component level and through VCF roles have
privileges that are combined.
Procedure:
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity and Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF Overview SSO page, in the section that is called VCF SSO, click the identity broker that you have
configured for VCF Single Sign-On.
4. In the Access Management tab, you see a list of users and groups that are provisioned. Select the group and/or user
that you would like to assign the role to, and click Assign.
• The list displays only those users and groups that have been provisioned and might not be complete.
• With JIT provisioning, users/groups can be assigned only after the first login.
5. In the Assign VCF Roles page, in the section called Roles, you can scope the role by selecting one of the following
options as the Scope, select a role from the drop drop-down list, and enter the validity of the role, and then click
Apply.
Option Description
Components with SSO Covers all the components that are configured with the relevant
identity broker.
Individual VCF Instances You can scope the role to one or more VCF Instances.
Note:
• You can add more than one role.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If you select Individual VCF Instance as the scope, the VCF Viewer, VCF Administrator, and VCF
Operations Administrator roles are grayed out in the roles drop-down list. These roles apply only to vCenter
and NSX instances that are part of the selected VCF Instance.
6. Click Assign.

on.
Edit VCF Role Assignments

Delete the role assignments

Delete the Custom VCF role

Reset and Assign Role Assignments
You can reset and reassign role assignments to establish a uniform approach to role assignments. All the previous role
assignments for the selected users/groups are reset and overwritten.
Note:
All the previous role assignments for the selected principals are reset and overwritten. To add role assignments to
the selected principals, use the Edit feature instead.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity and Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, under the section that is called VCF SSO, click the relevant identity broker.
4. Click the Access Management tab, you see a list of users and groups that are provisioned.
For Groups
5. From the Groups section, select the required groups, click the horizontal ellipsis next to Assign, and then click Reset
and Reassign from the drop-down options.
6. From the Reset and Reassign page, you see the list of selected groups. Add necessary roles from the Roles section.
7. Click Assign. Updates to the role assignment take place in the next authentication.
For Users

and Reassign from the drop-down options.
9. From the Reset and Reassign page, you see the list of selected users. Add necessary roles from the Roles section.
Note:
If any of the users who are selected are part of a group, you cannot reset and assign the role assignments.
Navigate to the Groups section to reset role assignments. See steps from 5 through 7 in this page.
10.Click Reset and Assign. Updates to the role assignment take place in the next authentication.

Modify or Remove VCF Operations and/or VCF Automation Components in an Existing VCF Single Sign-On
Configuration
You can modify or remove existing VCF Operations and VCF Automation components from the identity broker in an
existing VCF single sign-on configuration.
Note:
If you have configured VCF single sign-on for VCF Operations and/or VCF Automation, you can choose to
change the identity broker for these components. The change deactivates the previous authentication source
and the existing provisioned users and groups cannot be used in VCF Automation. You have to reassign the VCF
Automation and/or VCF Operations roles to the newly provisioned users and groups from the new authentication
source. This action cannot be reverted.
Modify or change VCF Single Sign-On for VCF Operations
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, from the data grid under the VCF Management tab, select operations appliance
and then click the horizontal ellipsis > Change SSO option.
4. In the Change VCF SSO page, select a different identity broker and click Change.
5. From the pop-up box that is displayed, read about role assignments and click Confirm.
Note:
Changing VCF single sign-on might impact user access to the operations appliance. You must review role
assignments and carry out relevant updates.
Modify or change VCF Single Sign-On for VCF Automation
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, from the data grid under the VCF Management tab, select Automation appliance
and then click the horizontal ellipsis > Change SSO option.
4. In the Change VCF SSO page, select a different identity broker and click Change.
5. From the pop-up box that is displayed, read about role assignments and click Confirm.
Note:
Changing VCF single sign-on might impact user access to the Automation appliance. You must review role
assignments and carry out relevant updates.

Add Other VCF Components for Single Sign-On Access
You can add other components such as log management, VCF Operations for networks, VCF Operations HCX, and VCF
Operations orchestrator, to an existing VCF single sign-on Configuration.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity & Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click VCF SSO Overview.
3. In the VCF SSO Overview page, from the grid under the Other Components tab, select the component from the grid
and click Add Component.
4. Use the values generated in the Add Component page in the respective component console to enable VCF single
sign-on.
Note:
The configuration details are exclusive for that component.
5. Click Save.
Note:
Store the configuration details as this information cannot be retrieved at a later date.
CAUTION:
• VCF Automation tenant support is restricted to a single segment.
• The configured user and group scale must not exceed the published identity broker configuration maximum.
For more information, see identity broker maximum limits.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components is supported in enterprise environments only. Cloud
service provider environments are not supported.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components is limited to the identity broker instance deployment
mode only, and is not supported on identity broker embedded deployment mode.
• Configuring VCF single sign-on using other components, is supported on VCF products only and is not
available for non-VCF products.

VCF Automation.

HCX, and NSX. For more information, see Step 4. (Optional) Assign a VCF Role.

Assigning Roles in VCF Operations
After you complete configuring VCF single sign-on in the VCF Operations console, log in to VCF Operations as a local
admin to assign the required roles and permissions for users or groups.
Assign roles in VCF Operations if configured for VCF single sign-on. Roles have to be assigned to the provisioned users/
groups to be able to log in with the configured identity provider to achieve single sign-on between the VCF components.
Without these roles, users will not be able to access the respective component consoles with their enterprise credentials.
Note:
If you had chosen JIT as the user/group provisioning method without specifying any groups, then attempt login
from the the Active Directory domain that was configured while configuring the VCF single sign-on. This is
essential before you can assign the roles.
Procedure
1. Log in to VCF Operations as a local admin.
2. In the navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration > Control Panel,
and then click the Access Control tile.
3. From the Access Control page, navigate to the User Accounts and/or User Groups tabs and click the horizontal
ellipsis next to the Add button, and select Import from Source.
4. From the Import from User Groups and/or Import from Users page, select VCF SSO from the drop-down options
against the Import From field.
5. Use the Search Prefix field to search for users and/or groups and click Finish.
6. After the user and/or group has been added, from the Access Control page, select the User and/or Group, and click
the Vertical ellipsis and click Edit.
7. From the section called Assign Roles and Scope, assign the required roles and scope to the use and/or groups and
click Save.
Assigning Roles in VCF Automation
After you complete configuring VCF single sign-on in VCF Operations, log in to the VCF Automation Provider
Management Portal to assign the required roles and permissions for users or groups.
Assign roles in the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal, if configured for VCF single sign-on. Roles have to be
assigned to the provisioned users/groups to be able to log in with the configured identity provider to achieve single sign-on
between VCF components. Without these roles, users will not be able to access the respective component consoles with
their enterprise credentials.
Note:
If you had chosen JIT as the user/group provisioning method without specifying any groups, then attempt login
from the the Active Directory domain that was configured while configuring the VCF single sign-on for the user
and groups to be dynamically provisioned when you log in. This is essential before you can assign the service
roles.
Procedure
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal with the system organization and admin account.
2. From the left menu, click Access Control.
3. From the Users tab, click the Import Users option.
4. From the Source drop-down options, select VCF SSO.
5. Search for and select the required users. Assign the required roles from the Assign Role option.
Repeat the steps to assign roles for groups.

Managing VCF Roles
VCF roles have been introduced to provide simplified access management for VCF users across VCF components
such as vCenter, NSX, VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations HCX, and VCF Operations orchestrator. As
an admin you can define user access using VCF roles to manage access across the VCF fleet from VCF Operations,
instead of assigning the component roles in each individual component. VCF roles are mapped to the individual VCF
component roles. The two kinds of VCF roles are built-in VCF roles and custom VCF roles. You can continue to assign
the roles/permissions for individual components. VCF roles do not aim to replace the individual components roles or their
Authorization model.
Note:
If a user has VCF roles and component roles assigned, then the overall access is a combination of both, and not
the replacement of one over the other.
Note:
To use VCF roles, the vCenter instance creates local groups and new global permissions to support the intended
VCF role.
CAUTION:
Do not modify the new global permissions that have been added and which are for principals whose names start
with . Modifying global permissions could break your system as it causes VCF authorization
vcf_reserved_
issues.
Benefits of VCF Roles:
As an administrator, you can:
• Visualize VCF roles and the corresponding VCF component roles.
• Assign VCF roles to users and groups that are provisioned from the identity provider.
• Assign VCF roles to API clients.
Broadcom 4152

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Specify expiry date/time-to-live during VCF roles assignments.

Assignments After Configuring VCF Single Sign-On.

Custom VCF Roles
You can create additional VCF roles called custom VCF roles. You can create custom VCF roles from VCF Operations
using components such as vCenter, VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations orchestrator, VCF Operations
HCX, and NSX.
For information about creating custom roles and role assignments, see Create a Custom VCF Role and Assign Custom
and Built-In VCF Roles.
Create a Custom VCF Role and Assign Custom and Built-In VCF Roles
As an administrator, you can create custom VCF roles from VCF Operations using components such as vCenter, VCF
Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations orchestrator, VCF Operations HCX, and NSX.
VCF components that are at 9.1 and later versions support VCF role assignments. For more information about built-in
VCF roles, see Built-In VCF Roles.
For VCF role assignments recommendations, see VCF Role Assignment.
Note:
• You can also assign component level roles from the associated component. For more information, see
Assigning Roles and Permissions from Individual Components.
• If a user has VCF roles and component roles assigned, then the overall access is a combination of both, and
not the replacement of one over the other.
Broadcom 4153

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• When a user or group has object-level permissions that are limited to a specific inventory subset, assigning
them a VCF role overrides that restriction, granting visibility across all objects. Do not assign a VCF role to a
user/group when inventory-level permissions are required.

Single Sign-On

(Optional) Assign a Custom VCF Role

Provisioning Method column indicates whether users and groups are pre-provisioned or configured through on-

Provisioning vCenter Custom Roles
You can choose to provision a vCenter custom role to all the vCenter instances in a VCF Instance. Later, when new
vCenter instances are added to the VCF Instance, the roles are assigned to the new vCenter instance thus streamlining
user access and management. You do not have to log in to the relevant vCenter and assign the required role. This
automatic provisioning also applies to single sign-on (SSO) configurations.
Provision vCenter Custom Roles to vCenter Instances and Remediate Drifts
Procedure
Provision vCenter Custom Roles
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity and Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click vCenter Custom Roles.
3. In the section that is called Provisions for vCenter Roles, click Import & Provision Roles.
4. In the Select Source and Role section, select a source VCF Instance, vCenter , and the role you want to provision.
Note:
Only vCenter instances that are created in VCF 9.1 and later are supported for custom roles and displayed.
5. Click Next.
6. In the Select Target section, select the VCF Instance/s to which you want to assign the custom role.
Note:
• All the vCenter instances that have been created in VCF 9.1 and later in the selected VCF Instance receive the
provisioned vCenter custom role.
• All the VCF Instances are listed as targets. You cannot provision a vCenter custom role to a VCF Instance if
a vCenter custom role was previously provisioned to the VCF Instance. The VCF Instance is unavailable for
selection.
7. Click Next.
A banner is displayed stating that if there are conflicts, the source role overrides the existing vCenter custom roles in
the vCenter instances.
Broadcom 4156

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
8. Click Confirm Role Provision.
If provisioning fails, you see a banner stating that role provisioning has failed or failed partially.
Remediate Drifts for vCenter Custom Roles
9. Click the vCenter custom role that you provisioned. You see the vCenter custom role details, such as, the status which
can be Failed, Provisioned, Drifted, and so on, the provisioned vCenter, and the target VCF Instance.
For vCenter custom roles that have failed provisioning click Retry in the grid.
10.Click Remediate Drifts from the banner above the grid.
11.In the Remediate Drifts page, the current master role definition under VCF Operations is displayed along with the
vCenter custom role/s with a conflict. Select the role that you want to make as master.
• You can continue to override the drift with the master role definition or select one of the role/s that has a conflict
and make it the master.
• After you select the role you want to make as master, the role is assigned to all vCenter instances in the
provisioned VCF Instance/s. The existing role definitions are overwritten.
After you complete provisioning a vCenter custom role to other vCenter instances, you can:
• Manually Remediate Drift. For more information, see Remediate Drifts for vCenter Custom Roles by Manually Running
a Check.
• If there are vCenter custom roles assigned to the VCF Instance you have provisioned, you can de-provision the role.
For more information, see De-provision a vCenter Custom Role from VCF Instances.
• Add more VCF Instances to the provision. For more information, see Provision a vCenter Custom Role to Additional
VCF Instances.
• Delete a VCF custom role if it is part of a role definition. For more information, see Delete a vCenter Custom Role.
• For information about role provisioning scope, see Managing vCenter Role Consistency.
Remediate Drifts for vCenter Custom Roles by Manually Running a Check
At a later date, you can manually remediate drifts for vCenter custom roles that have failed provisioning.
For more information about vCenter custom role drift management, see Managing vCenter Role Consistency.
Prerequisites

Custom Roles.
Procedure
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Manage and in the left navigation pane, click Fleet
Management > Identity and Access.
2. In the Identity & Access pane, click vCenter Custom Roles.
3. Click a vCenter custom role that you provisioned. You see the vCenter custom role details, such as, the status which
can be Failed, Provisioned, Drifted, and so on, the provisioned vCenter, and the target VCF Instance.
4. If drifts are detected, click Remediate Drifts from the banner above the grid.
5. In the Remediate Drifts page, the current master role definition under VCF Operations is displayed along with the
role/s that have a conflict. Select the role that you want to make as master.
• You can continue to override the drift with the master role definition or select one of the role/s that has a conflict
and make it the master.
• After you select the role you want to make as master, the role is assigned to all vCenter instances in the
provisioned VCF Instance/s. The existing role definitions are overwritten.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

You can de-provision a vCenter custom role from multiple VCF Instances. When you de-provision a vCenter custom role,
