Configure Image-Based Backup of VCF Operations and VCF Operations for Networks
To back up VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks, you create full virtual machine image-based backup jobs
by using your VMware vSphere Storage APIs - Data Protection compatible backup solution.
To ensure that all management components are backed up correctly, you must create backup jobs that capture the
state of a set of related components at a common point in time. With some components, simultaneous backups of the
component nodes ensure that you can restore the component to a state where the nodes are logically consistent with
each other and eliminate the necessity for further logical integrity remediation of the component.

2. Create backup jobs by using the configurations from the table above.
3. Schedule the backups to run on a daily basis.
4. Retain each backup for a minimum of three days.
5. Perform an initial on-demand backup to ensure the backups complete successfully.
Configure File-Based Backup Schedules in VMware Cloud Foundation
You can use the native file-based backup capabilities of VCF management services, VCF Automation, SDDC Manager,
vCenter and NSX Manager to schedule regular backups. SDDC Manager configure NSX Manager to backup at 1 hour
intervals during the bring-up process. You must manually configure scheduled file-based backup for VCF management
services, VCF Automation, SDDC Manager and vCenter.
Verify that you have an SFTP server on the network to serve as a target of the file-based backups.

Configure File-Based Backup Schedule for VCF Management Services and VCF Automation
You configure an automated backup schedule per component to ensure the regular backup of VCF components at
predefined intervals. To view the status of backups or backup failures, see the VCF Operations Health dashboard.
The SFTP server must support rsa-sha2-512 or rsa-sha2-256 SSH key algorithms.

• Salt RaaS

On-Demand Backups in VMware Cloud Foundation
Whilst scheduled backups are critical in the recovery of a VMware Cloud Foundation platform, its also possible to run on-
demand backups for other planned activities like pre-upgrades. There are also some elements of the system that should
be backed up for recovery purposes that can not be scheduled and must be run on-demand.
• On-Demand Backup of VCF Management Services and VCF Automation
• On-Demand Backup of SDDC Manager
• On-Demand Backup of SDDC Manager Credential Store
• On-Demand Backup of NSX Manager
• On-Demand Backup of vCenter
• On-Demand Backup of vSphere Distributed Switch Configuration
On-Demand Backup of VCF Management Services and VCF Automation
For critical operations or before performing maintenance activities, such as upgrades, you should initiate manual, on-
demand backups of specific VCF component. This provides an immediate recovery point, offering an extra layer of
protection.

role.

4. Click Backup > Backup Now.

a) Select the component that you want to backup.
b) Click Backup Now.

On-Demand Backup of SDDC Manager Credential Store
If you do not have an external password vault, you must backup the SDDC Manager Credential Store using the SDDC
Manager API.
You should configure a scheduled job using external automation to backup the credential store at least once a day. The
steps below use the SDDC Manager developer center but you can also use the REST API.
1. Log into the SDDC Manager UI as a user with the ADMIN role.
2. Navigate to the developer center.
3. Expand Credentials.
4. Expand GET.
5. Click Execute and download the resulting JSON.
6. Store the JSON in a secure location.
7. Repeat the above steps or leverage the SDDC Manager REST API to backup the credentials store daily.

On-Demand Backup of vSphere Distributed Switch Configuration
The vCenter backup includes the configuration of the entire vCenter instance. To have a backup only of the vSphere
Distributed Switch and distributed port group configurations, you export a configuration file that includes the validated
network configurations. If you want to recover only the vSphere Distributed Switch, you can import this configuration file to
the vCenter instance.
You can use the exported file to create multiple copies of the vSphere Distributed Switch configuration on an existing
deployment, or overwrite the settings of existing vSphere Distributed Switch instances and port groups.
You must backup the configuration of a vSphere Distributed Switch immediately after each change in configuration of that
switch.
1. Log in to the vCenter interface at with a user assigned the Administrator role.
https://<vcenter_fqdn>/ui
2. Select the Networking inventory.
3. In the inventory expand the vCenter and Datacenter.
4. Right click the vSphere Distributed Switch you want to backup, and select Settings > Export Configuration.
5. In the Export configuration dialog box, select Distributed switch and all port groups.
6. In the Description text box enter the date and time of export, and click OK.
7. Copy the backup zip file to a secure location from where you can retrieve the file and use it if a failure of the appliance
occurs.
8. Repeat the procedure for the other vSphere Distributed Switches.
Restoring VMware Cloud Foundation
Recovering your VMware Cloud Foundation platform from an unexpected outage or failure is a critical operation.
Depending on your failure scenario and what components of your environemnt is affected could involve any number of
steps. This section provides guidance across all components of the VMware Cloud Foundation platform
• Image-Based Restore of VCF Operations
• File-Based Restore for SDDC Manager, vCenter, and NSX
• File-Based Restore of VCF Management Services
• File-Based Restore of VCF Automation
Image-Based Restore of VCF Operations
Restore a simple or high availability deployment of VCF Operations by using an image-based backup tool.
• Backup Data Available: Ensure that you have a recent backup of your VCF Operations cluster.
• VCF Operations Cluster Configuration: Ensure you know the details of your VCF Operations cluster configuration,
such as cluster nodes, user credentials.
• Backup Software: Ensure that the backup solution you are using is compatible with your VCF Operations version.
Table 1160: VCF Operations Failure Scenarios
Component Deployment Model Failure Scenario Recovery Process
VCF Operations Primary node lost Restore primary node from image-based backup.
Simple
Cloud proxy lost Restore cloud proxy from image-based backup.
High Availability Primary node lost Restore primary node from image-based backup.
Broadcom 4290

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Data node lost Restore data node from image-based backup.
Cloud proxy lost Restore cloud proxy from image-based backup.
1. If there are existing VCF Operations virtual machines, power them off and rename or delete.
2. Access your backup software interface.
3. Locate the backup taken of the VCF Operations nodes.
4. Initiate the restore process.
5. After the virtual machine is restored, power it on.

https://<vcf-operations-primary-node-fqdn>/admin
with the admin user.
b) On the System Status page, verify that all nodes are in a Running state and their status is Online.
c) Navigate to the Cloud Proxies page and verify that the Health Status for each cloud proxy is Healthy.
2. Verify the VCF Operations integration adapters state.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user
https://<vcf-operations-primary-node-fqdn>/
assigned the Administrator role.
b) Navigate to Administration > Integrations.
c) Expand each integration and ensure that its status is OK.

File-Based Restore for SDDC Manager, vCenter, and NSX
When SDDC Manager, vCenter or NSX Manager in your VMware Cloud Foundation platform fails, you can restore the
component to a fully operational state by using their file-based backups. When an NSX Edge node fails, you redeploy the
node from the NSX Manager instance.
Use this guidance as appropriate based on the exact nature of the failure encountered within your environment.
Sometimes, you can recover localized logical failures by restoring individual components. In more severe cases, such as
a complete and irretrievable hardware failure, to restore the operational status of your VMware Cloud Foundation platform,
you must perform a complex set of manual deployments and restore sequences. In failure scenarios where there is a risk
of data loss, there has already been data loss or where it involves a catastrophic failure, contact Broadcom Support to
review your recovery plan before taking any steps to remediate the situation.
Restore SDDC Manager
If SDDC Manager fails, you can restore it from its file-based backup.
• Power off and rename the failed SDDC Manager instance.
• Verify that you have a valid file-based backup of the failed SDDC Manager instance.
To be valid, the backup must be of the same version as the version of the SDDC Manager appliance on which you plan
to restore the instance.
• Verify that you have the SFTP server details:
– SFTP Server IP
– SFTP Server Username
– SFTP Server Password
– Encryption Password
• The following components must be available before proceeding with the restore of SDDC Manager:
– vCenter
After a successful recovery, securely delete the decrypted backup files.
Decrypting the SDDC Manager Backup
Should you need to decrypt the SDDC Manager, you must download and decrypt the encrypted backup file from the SFTP
server.
• OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later must be available on your Linux machine that you use to access the environment.
• Download the SDDC Manager that corresponds to your VCF version from the Broadcom support portal.
The backup file contains sensitive data about your SDDC Manager instance. As a best practice, you must control access
to the decrypted files and securely delete them after you complete the restore operation.
Note:
The procedures have been written based on the host machine being a Linux-based operating system.
1. Identify the backup file for the restore and download it from the SFTP server to your host machine.
2. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export backupFile='vcf-backup-sfo-vcf01-sfo-rainpole-io-xxxx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx.tar.gz'
export encryptionPassword='***************'
Broadcom 4292

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. On your host machine, open a terminal and extract the content of the backup file.
a) For VCF 9.1.1 decrypt and extract the content of the backup file by running the following command.
tail -c +5 "$backupFile" | OPENSSL_FIPS=1 openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -md sha256 -
pass env:encryptionPassword | tar -xz
a) For VCF 9.1.0 decrypt and extract the content of the backup file by running the following command.
OPENSSL_FIPS=1 openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -md sha256 -in "$backupFile" -pass env:encryptionPassword
2>/dev/null | tar -xz
Restore SDDC Manager from a File-Based Backup

the restore. After that, you restore the file-based backup on the newly deployed SDDC Manager appliance.

click Next.
7. On the Select a compute resource page, click Next.

export backupFile='vcf-backup-sfo-vcf01-sfo-rainpole-io-xxxx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx.tar.gz'
export encryptionPassword='***************'
18.On the host machine, copy the encrypted backup file to the folder on the newly deployed SDDC Manager
/tmp
appliance by running the following command. When prompted, enter the vcf_user_password.
scp $backupFile vcf@$sddcManagerFqdn:$tmpFolderPath
19.Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
20.Create the JSON payload for the restore by running the following command.
sddcRestorePayload=$(jq -n \
--arg file "${tmpFolderPath}${backupFile}" \
--arg pass "${encryptionPassword}" \
'{
"elements": [ { "resourceType": "SDDC_MANAGER" } ],
"backupFile": $file,
"encryption": { "passphrase": $pass }
}' | tee /dev/tty )
21.Perform a restore of the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
restoreId=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/restores/tasks" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data "$sddcRestorePayload" \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
22.Monitor the restore task by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/restores/tasks/${restoreId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
Refresh the SSH keys that are stored in the SDDC Manager inventory. See Broadcom knowledge base article 313210.

/opt/vmware/sddc-support

Restoring a vCenter Instance
If a vCenter instance fails, you can restore it from its file-based backup.
• Power off and rename the failed vCenter instance.
• Verify that you have a valid file-based backup of the failed vCenter instance.
To be valid, the backup must be of the version of the vCenter appliance on which you plan to restore the instance.
• Verify that you have the SFTP server details:
– SFTP Server IP
– SFTP Server Username
– SFTP Server Password
– Encryption Password
Prepare for Restoring a vCenter Instance
Before restoring a vCenter instance, you must retrieve the vCenter build number and deployment details, as well as
vCenter and ESX credentials from the SDDC Manager inventory.
• The following components must be available before proceeding with the restore of vCenter:
– SDDC Manager
Retrieve the vCenter Intance Deployment Details
Before restoring a vCenter instance, you must retrieve the vCenter build number and deployment details from the SDDC
Manager inventory. The vCenter instances in your system might be running different build numbers if the backups are
taken during an upgrade process. You must restore each vCenter instance to its correct version.
Because the management domain vCenter might be unavailable to authenticate the login, you use the SDDC Manager
API via the shell to retrieve this information.
1. Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manager appliance, connect using the user.
vcf
2. Get the list of vCenter instances by running the following command.
curl http://localhost/inventory/vcenters -k | json_pp
3. For each vCenter instance, record the values of these settings.
Setting Value
domainId Id of the domain
vmName VM name of the vCenter instance
hostName FQDN of the vCenter instance
version version_number-build_number
4. Verify that the vCenter version retrieved from SDDC Manager is the same as the version associated with the backup
file that you plan to restore.
Retrieve the Credentials for Restoring a vCenter Instance
Before restoring a vCenter instance, you must retrieve the vCenter root and vCenter Single Sign-On administrator
credentials from the SDDC Manager inventory. Before restoring the management domain vCenter instance, you must also
retrieve the credentials of a healthy management domain ESX host.
Broadcom 4295

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If SDDC Manager is not operational, you can retrieve the required vCenter root, vCenter Single Sign-On
administrator, and ESX root credentials from the file-based backup of SDDC Manager. See Decrypting the SDDC
Manager Backup.
Before you can query the SDDC Manager API, you must obtain an API access token by using admin@local account.
1. Log in to your host machine with access to the SDDC and open a terminal.
2. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
3. Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Retrieve the vCenter root credentials.
a) Retrieve the vCenter root credentials by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/credentials?resourceType=VCENTER&accountType=USER" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
The command returns the vCenter root credentials.
Setting Value
domainName Name of the domain
resourceName FQDN of the vCenter instance
username root
password vcenter_root_password
b) Record the vCenter root credentials.
5. Retrieve the vCenter Single Sign-On administrator credentials.
a) Retrieve the vCenter Single Sign-On administrator credentials by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/credentials?resourceType=PSC" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
The command returns the administrator@vsphere.local credentials.
Setting Value
domainName Name of the domain
resourceName FQDN of the vCenter instance
username administrator@vsphere.local
password vcenter_sso_admin_password
Broadcom 4296

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
b) Record the administrator@vsphere.local credentials.
6. If you plan to restore the management domain vCenter instance, retrieve the credentials for a healthy management
domain ESX host.

curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/credentials?resourceType=ESXI" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
The command returns the ESX root credentials.
Setting Value for first ESX host
domainName management domain name
resourceName FQDN of the first ESX host
username root
password esx_root_password
b) Record the ESX root credentials.
Restore a vCenter Instance from a File-Based Backup
If a vCenter instance fails, you can restore it from its file-based backup. If the management domain vCenter instance
and the workload domain vCenter instance are both in a failed state, you must restore the management domain vCenter
instance before restoring the workload domain vCenter instance.

• If you are recovering a workload domain vCenter instance, verify that the management domain vCenter instance is
available.
You deploy a new vCenter appliance and perform a file-based restore. If you are restoring the management domain
vCenter instance, you deploy the new appliance on a healthy ESX host in the management domain cluster. If you are
restoring the workload domain vCenter instance, you deploy the new appliance in the management domain vCenter
instance.

The restored appliance has new SSH host keys. In addition to SDDC Manager, refresh the stored host key for this

administrator workstations.
Key-based SSH access to the appliance is also lost: the contents of /root/.ssh are not included in a vCenter file-based
backup. Re-provision any authorized keys the failed instance had.
Validate the vCenter Instance State
After restoring a vCenter instance, you must validate the state of the vCenter and vCenter Single Sign-On.
1. Log in to the vCenter interface at with a user assigned the Administrator role.
https://<vcenter_fqdn>/ui
2. In the inventory, click the management domain vCenter inventory, click the Summary tab, and verify that there are no
unexpected vCenter alerts.
3.
Note:
This step only applies to upgraded environments that still have Enhanced Linked Mode (ELM) configured. VCF
9.x deployed vCenter instances do not leverage ELM.
For vCenter instances participating in a shared vCenter Single Sign-On domain, do the following:
a) Click the Linked vCenter systems tab and verify that the list contains all other vCenter instances in the vCenter
Single Sign-On domain.
b) Log in to the recovered vCenter instance by using a Secure Shell (SSH) client.
c) Navigate to the bin directory by running the following command.
cd /usr/lib/vmware-vmdir/bin
d) List the current replication partners of the vCenter instance with the current replication status between the nodes by
running the following command.
vsphere_admin_password
./vdcrepadmin -f showpartnerstatus -h localhost -u administrator -w
Broadcom 4299

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
e) Verify that for each partner, the command output contains ,
vdcrepadmin Host available: Yes Status
, and .
available: Yes Partner is 0 changes behind
f) If you observe significant differences, because the resyncing might take some time, wait five minutes and repeat
this step.
4. Repeat the procedure for the other vCenter instance.
5. Review the restore logs. Check /var/log/vmware/applmgmt/restore.log and /var/log/vmware/applmgmt/
reconciliation.log for ERROR entries. Per-adapter network failures and skipped configuration are recorded here only;
they do not cause the restore to report failure.
6. Verify and re-apply the network configuration. Compare the running configuration against the values recorded during
preparation:
a) ip addr — every address on every adapter, both IPv4 and IPv6. In a dual-stack deployment only one address
family is restored from the backup; the other keeps the value entered when the replacement appliance was
deployed.
b) ip route — static routes are not restored. Re-apply them with appliancesh > networking.routes.add.
c) cat /etc/resolv.conf (or resolvectl status) — DNS servers and the search line. DNS search domains are not
restored. Re-apply them with appliancesh > networking.dns.domains.set, or from the Direct Console User
Interface.
d) Confirm every adapter the failed instance had is present and addressed.
7. Verify time synchronization. Confirm the appliance clock is correct and the configured NTP servers are reachable.
Single Sign-On token validation fails if the clock has drifted.
8. Verify identity sources and Active Directory authentication.
a) Under Administration > Single Sign On > Configuration > Identity Provider, confirm each identity source
connects. If an LDAPS source fails, its certificate may have been renewed after the backup was taken; re-import
the current certificate.
b) If the vCenter is joined to an Active Directory domain, confirm domain authentication works. If it fails, the computer
account password may have rotated since the backup was taken; reset the machine account or rejoin the domain.
c) Log in as administrator@<sso_domain> using the password that was in effect when the backup was taken.
d) Roles, permissions, privileges, tags, and categories are restored with the database. Do not re-create them.
9. Verify SSH access and trust.
a) The appliance has new SSH host keys. Refresh the stored host key wherever this vCenter is reached over SSH.
b) /root/.ssh is not restored. Re-provision any authorized keys.
c) Confirm SDDC Manager and VCF Operations can authenticate to the vCenter. If they cannot, verify the root
password matches the one they hold.
10.Verify certificates.
a) If the VMCA root certificate was replaced or renewed after the backup was taken, the restored vCenter carries the
earlier root and does not trust certificates issued from the newer one. Check for host connection failures reporting
certificate errors and re-issue certificates if required.
11.Reconcile the inventory against the environment.
a) The restored vCenter reflects the environment as it was when the backup was taken. Hosts added after the backup
are absent and must be re-added; virtual machines created after the backup appear as orphaned or unregistered;
cluster membership, resource pool hierarchy, DRS configuration and virtual machine resource settings revert;
storage policy providers registered after the backup must be re-registered. Compare the vSphere Distributed
Switch configuration against the export produced by Export the Configuration of the vSphere Distributed Switches
Broadcom 4300

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
and, if it is newer, restore it using Restore the Configuration of a vSphere Distributed Switch. For the full list, see
Considerations and Limitations for File-Based Backup and Restore in the vSphere documentation.
12.Verify content libraries.
a) The content library service remounts remote storage backings and reconciles its database at startup. Confirm
each library is accessible. Items deleted after the backup are no longer accessible; items created after the backup
remain on the storage backing without a library record.
13.Verify alarms.
a) Alarm definitions and their state are restored. Scripts stored on the appliance and invoked by alarm actions are not
restored unless they reside in a directory included in the backup. Confirm every alarm action that runs a script still
points at a script that exists.
14.Verify vSphere Supervisor, if in use.
a) Confirm the Supervisor cluster reaches a running state. Supervisor control-plane state is restored only if
Supervisors Control Plane was selected when the backup was taken.
15.Redeploy vCenter High Availability, if it was in use.
a) The restore removes the vCenter HA configuration.
16.Re-point and re-run the backup.
a) The restored appliance carries the backup schedule that was in effect when the backup was taken, including its
backup location. Update the backup configuration, then take an on-demand backup immediately so a current
recovery point exists.
17.If ESX root passwords were automatically rotated by SDDC Manager after the backup was taken, or if new hosts were
commissioned, they may appear as "Disconnected" or "Not Responding" in the restored vCenter.
a) In the vCenter UI, check the hosts state. Reconnect any disconnected hosts. You may need to provide the current
root credentials if the passwords have been changed.

Restore an NSX Manager Cluster Node
If an NSX Manager instance fails, you can restore it from its file-based backup.
• Verify that you have a valid file-based backup of the failed NSX Manager instance.
• Verify that you have the SFTP server details:
– SFTP Server IP
– SFTP Server Username
– SFTP Server Password
– Encryption Password
• The following components must be available before proceeding with the restore of NSX Manager:
– vCenter
– SDDC Manager
Prepare for Restoring an NSX Manager Cluster Node
Before restoring an NSX Manager node, you must retrieve the NSX Manager build number and deployment details, as
well as the credentials from the SDDC Manager inventory.
Retrieve the NSX Manager Version
Before restoring a failed NSX Manager instance, you must retrieve its version.
1. Navigate to the secure SFTP location that stores your NSX Manager backups, and determine the backup that you
intend to restore. Normally you will be using the most recent backup.
2. The name of the backup folder is made up of four parts
a) The NSX Manager version, for example, 9.1.0.0.25318227.
b) The IP Address format, for example, IPv4.
c) The UUID of the NSX Manager node, for example, 0e3f2442-1d82-5727-cbaf-5b8894186c59.
d) The IP Address of the NSX Manager node, for example, 10.11.10.72.
3. Ensure you that the source NSX Manager Unified Appliance OVA file matches the version found in Step 2a.
This is what you deploy before restoring the selected backup.
Retrieve the Credentials for Restoring NSX Manager from SDDC Manager
Before restoring a failed NSX Manager instance, you must retrieve the NSX Manager root and admin credentials from
the SDDC Manager inventory.
Before you can query the SDDC Manager API, you must obtain an API access token by using an API service account.
Broadcom 4302

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to your host machine with access to the SDDC and open a terminal.
2. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
3. Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Retrieve the root and admin credentials for the NSX Manager instance.
a) Run the command to retrieve the credentials.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/credentials?resourceType=NSXT_MANAGER" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
b) Save the root and admin credentials for the instance you are restoring.
Restore the First Node of a Failed NSX Manager Cluster
If all three NSX Manager nodes in an NSX Manager cluster are in a failed state, you begin the restore process by
restoring the first cluster node.
Important:
This procedure is not applicable in use cases when there are operational NSX Manager cluster nodes.
• If two of the three NSX Manager nodes in the NSX Manager cluster are in a failed state, you begin the restore
process by deactivating the cluster. See Deactivate the NSX Manager Cluster.
• If only one of the three NSX Manager nodes in the NSX Manager cluster is in a failed state, you directly
restore the failed node to the cluster. See Restore an NSX Manager Node to an Existing NSX Manager
Cluster.

You deploy a new NSX Manager instance by using the configuration of the first NSX Manager cluster node.

See Retrieve the NSX Manager Version.
• Verify that the backup file that you plan to restore is associated with the version of the failed NSX Manager cluster.
•
Note:
The first node that you deploy in the cluster must be the node that was running the NSX Cluster VIP when the
last backup was taken. Retrieve the IP address from the backup folder name on the SFTP server, and restore this
NSX manager node first.

Deactivate the NSX Manager Cluster
If two of the three NSX Manager cluster nodes are in a failed state or if you restored the first node of a failed NSX
Manager cluster, you must deactivate the cluster.
Important:
• This procedure is not applicable in use cases when there are two healthy NSX Manager cluster nodes.
If only one of the three nodes in the NSX Manager cluster is in a failed state, after you prepare for the restore,
you directly restore the failed node to the cluster. See Restore an NSX Manager Node to an Existing NSX
Manager Cluster.
• You must power off and delete the two failed NSX Manager nodes from the inventory before performing with
this procedure.
1. Log in to the vCenter interface at https://<vcenter_fqdn>/ui with a user assigned the Administrator role.
2. Select Menu > VMs and Templates.
3. In the inventory expand vCenter > Datacenter > NSX Folder.
4. Click the VM of the operational NSX Manager node in the cluster, click Launch Web Console, and log in by using
administrator credentials.
Setting Value
User name admin
Password nsx_admin_password

deactivate cluster
6. On the Are you sure you want to remove all other nodes from this cluster? (yes/no)prompt, enter .
yes
You deactivated the cluster.
Restore an NSX Manager Node to an Existing NSX Manager Cluster
If only one of the three NSX Manager cluster nodes is in a failed state, you restore the failed node to the existing cluster. If
two of the three NSX Manager cluster nodes are in a failed state, you repeat this process for each of the failed nodes.

Restoring NSX Edge Cluster Nodes
If one or both NSX Edge cluster nodes fail due to a hardware or software issue, you must redeploy the failed NSX Edge
instances. You do not restore the NSX Edge nodes from a backup.
Redeploy an NSX Edge Cluster for VCF Component Backup and Restore
To restore an NSX Edge cluster, use the NSX API to redeploy the edge nodes.
Redeploy an NSX Edge Node Using The NSX Manager UI
1. From a browser, log in with admin privileges toNSX Manager.
2. SelectSystem > Fabric > Nodes > Edge Transport Nodes.
3. In the list, select the edge node that you want to redeploy.
4. Select Actions > Redeploy Edge
Note:
The Redeploy Edge Node workflow is identical to the Add Edge Node workflow that was originally used to
auto-deploy the node. The editable fields in the Redeploy Edge Node workflow are pre-filled with the existing
configuration settings of the node. You can modify these settings as needed.
5. Proceed through the workflow steps and either accept the existing settings or modify the settings as needed. See
"Create an NSX Edge Transport Node" in the Installation Guide
Important:
You must reenter the CLI credentials for the node VM, as the Credentials fields are left blank for security. Also, do
not modify the Compute Manager setting unless you intend to change the compute manager for the node. Once
you modify the setting, the configuration mappings associated with the original compute manager are cleared and
cannot be retrieved, even if you re-select the original compute manager.
6. a. After finishing the Redeploy Edge Node workflow, allow the node redeployment to proceed and reach completion.
b. Verify the node configuration status and connection status on theEdge Transport Nodespage. Alternatively, you
can verify the transport node status by running theGet edge-cluster-status | get managers | get controllers | get
host-switchCLI command.
c. Perform the postrequisites described later on this page.

File-Based Restore of VCF Management Services
Choose a recovery process depending upon your failure scenario. In-place restoration applies when VMs exist.
Redeployment applies when VMs do not exist and must be redeployed as part of the restoration.
Table 1162: VCF management services Failure Scenarios
Failure Scenario Recovery Process
VCF management services component corruption In Place Restore of VCF Management Services Components
Single node lost • No action required
• The failed node is automatically redeployed
Two nodes lost Redeploy VCF Management Services Cluster and Restore Initial
Components
Three nodes lost Redeploy VCF Management Services Cluster and Restore Initial
Components
Broadcom 4314

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In Place Restore of VCF Management Services Components
The following procedure can be used to perform an in place restore of a VCF management services instance if there is a
failure at the application level of one or more components.
• VCF management services is in a failed state but the virtual machines are still running.
• You must have at least one recent backup of the component that you are restoring.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF management services, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– VCF Operations
– SDDC Manager
Note:
Considerations for restoring Fleet lifecycle or SDDC lifecycle:
• Restoring Fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle interrupts any active tasks and causes them to disappear from the
Tasks panel. In addition, the status of the restoration is not reflected on the Tasks panel after the components
are restored.
• Restore Fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle individually. Do not restore Fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle with
other components.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management.
3. On the VCF Management page, click Backup & Restore > Restore.
4. To restore your VCF component, select the VCF Instance.
5. On the Restore pane, select the VCF component from a specific backup or the latest backup.
• Restore from the latest backup on the cluster.
• Specify the date range to filter the backups available, select the backup and optionally select the restore point by
selecting the incremental backup.
6. Optional: Enter the Encryption passphrase.
7. Click Restore.
8. Monitor the restore task from the Tasks pane.
Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for Component Backup and Restore
Before you can redeploy a services runtime cluster, you must find the current version from the VCF Operations inventory.
You use the VCF Operations API to retrieve the component IDs and versions.
1. Retrieve a VCF Operations access token.
# VCF_OPS_FQDN should be the VCF Operations master node FQDN
# VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD should be the VCF Operations local admin password
export VCF_OPS_FQDN='flt-ops01a.rainpole.io'
export VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD='****************'
OPS_TOKEN=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://$VCF_OPS_FQDN/suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d "{
\"username\": \"admin\",
\"password\": \"$VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\",
\"authSource\": \"local\"
Broadcom 4315

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
}" | jq -r .token)
2. Retrieve a list of component IDs and versions from VCF Operations and save them for later use.
curl -k -s -X GET \
"https://${VCF_OPS_FQDN}/suite-api/internal/components?_no_links=true" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H 'X-Ops-API-use-unsupported: true' \
-H "Authorization: OpsToken ${OPS_TOKEN}" \
| jq '
.components as $all
| ( $all
| map(
select(
(.componentType | ascii_upcase) as $t
| $t == "FLEET_LCM" or $t == "SALT_RAAS" or $t == "VIDB" or $t == "LI"
)
)
) as $filtered
| ( $all
| map(select((.componentType | ascii_upcase) == "VSP"))
| map({
id: .componentUuid,
componentVersion: .componentVersion,
fqdn: .properties.fqdn,
fleetFqdn: .properties.fleetFqdn,
ip: (.properties.ip // .vcfInstance.ip),
instanceName: .vcfInstance.instanceName,
vcfInstanceFqdn: .vcfInstance.fqdn
})
| unique_by(.id)
) as $vsp
| ( $all
| map(select((.componentType | ascii_upcase) == "VCFA"))[0]
| if . then {
fqdn: .properties.fqdn,
componentVersion: .componentVersion,
platformFqdn: .properties.platformFqdn,
vspComponentUuid: .properties.vspComponentUuid
} else null end
) as $vcfa
| {
components: (
$filtered
| map({
componentType,
id: .componentUuid,
componentVersion: .componentVersion,
fqdn: .properties.fqdn
})
),
vsp: $vsp,
vcfa: $vcfa
}
'

Redeploy and Restore VCF Management Services Components
You redeploy when VCF management services VMs do not exist and must be redeployed as part of the restoration
Broadcom 4317

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Extract Services Runtime Configuration from the Services Runtime Backup for VCF Component Backup and
Restore
Using the VCF services runtime backup, you extract the package deployment configuration.
• OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later must be available on your Linux machine that you use to access the environment.
• Download and extract the scripts from Broadcom knowledge base article 443506 to the machine you use to access
your VMware Cloud Foundation platform.
• A linux workstation with access to the SFTP server.
The VCF services runtime package deployment configuration is captured as part of the VCF management services
backup. You use this extracted data in a later step.
1. Browse the SFTP server and locate the VCF management services backup that you plan to use for the restore
operation.
2. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sftpHost='192.168.1.2'
export sftpPort='22'
export sftpDirectory='/media/backups/'
export sftpUsername='svc-vcf-bck'
export sftpPassword='***************'
export sftpEncryptionPassphrase='***************'
export remoteArchive='/media/backups/vcf/backups/5d29166a-780d-4481-81df-59cc3cefb697/9.1.1.0.25714471/
vsp/5d29166a-780d-4481-81df-59cc3cefb697/9.1.1.0.25714471/2026-09-01T14-53-53Z/2026-09-01T14-53-53Z.base.tgz'
# remote-archive should be the path to the vsp backup for the VCF Management Services instance
3. Run the following command to execute the script to extract the configuration from the backup.
./vmsp-backup-sftp-to-yaml.sh \
--sftp-host ${sftpHost} \
--sftp-port ${sftpPort} \
--sftp-user ${sftpUsername} \
--sftp-password ${sftpPassword} \
--sftp-dir ${sftpDirectory} \
--remote-archive ${remoteArchive} \
--passphrase ${sftpEncryptionPassphrase} \
--output-dir "./tmp/backup-yaml"

Prepare to Restore VCF Management Services for Component Backup and Restore
Before you can deploy a new VCF management services instance to restore to, you must delete the existing VCF
management services entry in the SDDC Manager database.
CAUTION:
This procedure should not be used to completely delete a deployed component. To fully delete day 2 deployed
components on VCF management services refer to Broadcom knowledge base article 441333. Only follow either
Step 1 or Step 2 depending on the version of VCF you are recovering.
1. For VCF 9.1.1 and later, follow these steps:
a) Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
b) Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--data "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
c) Export the VCF services runtime cluster of type MANAGEMENT details to the
vcfms-vsp-cluster-
file for later use by running the following command.
details.json
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq '.elements[] | select(.type == "MANAGEMENT")' \
| tee vcfms-vsp-cluster-details.json
d) Retrieve the ID of the VCF services runtime cluster of type MANAGEMENT by running the following command.
vspManagementId=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r '.elements[] | select(.type == "MANAGEMENT") | .id' | tee /dev/tty )
e) Delete the VCF services runtime cluster of type MANAGEMENT, using the id obtained in the previous step by
running the following command.
curl -k -s -X DELETE "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters/${vspManagementId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
2. For VCF 9.1.0, follow these steps:
a) Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manager appliance, connect using the vcf user.
b) Switch to the root user.
su -
c) Connect to the Postgres database by running the following command.
psql -U postgres -h localhost -d platform;
Broadcom 4319

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
d) Query the vsp_cluster table and record the vsp_cluster_id of the entry with type MANAGEMENT by running the
following command.
select * from vsp_cluster;
e) Delete the MANAGEMENT entry by running the following command.
delete from vsp_cluster where type='MANAGEMENT';
f) Delete the corresponding credential by running the following command.
delete from credential where username='vsp/<MANAGEMENT-vsp_cluster_id>/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
For Example
delete from credential where username='vsp/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/svc-sddc-manager-
admin';
Redeploy VCF Management Services Cluster and Restore Initial Components
The following procedure can be used to redeploy and restore a VCF management services instance in case of a failure.
• VCF management services is in a failed state and cannot be restored using the in place procedure.
• Existing VCF management services virtual machines must be deleted from vCenter.
• You must have at least one recent scheduled backup of the components that you are restoring.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF management services, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– SDDC Manager
• VCF Installer with the correct binary versions for the release you are running for VCF services runtime, Fleet lifecycle,
Software depot, SDDC lifecycle, Salt master, Salt RaaS, and Identity broker.
• Retrieve the correct component version using Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for Component
Backup and Restore
To restore VCF management services, you restore the components from the table below depending on your scenario.
VCF Management Services in the First VCF Instance VCF Management Services in an Additional VCF Instance
• VCF services runtime • VCF services runtime
• Fleet lifecycle • SDDC lifecycle
• SDDC lifecycle • Software depot *
• Software depot • Salt master
• Salt RaaS • Identity broker *
• Salt master
• Identity broker
* Optional components in an additional VCF Instance
1. Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manager appliance, connect using the vcf user.
2. Switch to the root user.
su -
3. Retrieve token from SDDC Manager.
# sddcmFQDN should be the FQDN for SDDC Manager
# adminUsername should be a username with the ADMIN role in SDDC Manager
# adminPassword should be the password for the user with the ADMIN role in SDDC Manager
export sddcmFQDN='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export adminUsername='administrator@vsphere.local'
export adminPassword='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
# generate token
token=$(curl -k https://"$sddcmFQDN"/v1/tokens \
-X POST \
Broadcom 4320

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
-H "Content-type:application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"$adminUsername\", \"password\":\"$adminPassword\"}" | jq -r '.accessToken')
4. If SDDC Manager was previously restored, or VCF Management Services was upgraded since initial deployment, then
SDDC Manager will need to be pointed to an offline depot to source binares for the redeployment.
a) To repoint to an offline depot, refer to Repoint SDDC Manager Depot to an Offline Depot for VCF Instance Backup
and Restore
b) To download the required binaries, refer to Download Binaries for VCF Management Services Runtime for VCF
Instance Backup and Restore
5. Deploy a new VCF management services runtime instance.
# Domain id should be the management domain id from SDDC Manager. Retrive using the v1/domains API in the
SDDC Manager developer center
# FQDNs must match the original
# clusterId must match the original retrieved in step 4
# networkMoId must be from the portgroup you are deploying to
curl -k -X POST -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization:
Bearer $token" https://"$sddcmFQDN"/v1/vsp-clusters \
-d '{

7. The restore process will attempt to use the original binary path from the VCF installer to source binaries. If you do
not have the original installer, download the binaries and stage them to the newly deployed services runtime instance
using this process
8. Trust the VCF Installer (or SDDC Manager if the VCF installer was converted to SDDC manager during bringup)
Certificate on the new VCF management services instance
a) Retrieve the VCF Installer Certificate
CERT_DATA=$($echo | openssl s_client -connect <VCF-Installer-FQDN>:443 2>/dev/null | \
openssl x509 -outform pem)
b) Retrieve a VCF management services services runtime token
export VCFMS_SR='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
c) Trust the VCF installer certificate
jq -n --arg cert "$CERT_DATA" '{cert: $cert}' | \
curl -k -X POST "https://sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io/api/v1/system/trusted-certificates?action=add" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFMS_SR_TOKEN" \
-d @-
9. Update SFTP Settings on the new VCF management services Instance.
a) Retrieve the SFTP server fingerprint
ssh-keyscan -p 22 <sftp_server_ip> | ssh-keygen -lf -
# SSH fingerprints of type RSA and ED25519 are supported
# Enter the full fingerprint in the payload of step 9c. Example:
SHA256:yA3FHIQMbiMnansI4+lONYBASLP2IQhGZkGJIMZ2Pi8
b) Retrieve a VCF management services services runtime token
export VCFMS_SR='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \

--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \

10.Retrieve list of backups for VCF management services runtime, fleet lifecycle, software depot, and SDDC lifecycle.
curl -k "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/system/backups" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFMS_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' | \
jq -r '
["vsp", "vcf-fleet-lcm", "vcf-fleet-depot", "vcf-sddc-lcm", "salt", "salt-raas", "vidb", "vcfms-
metrics-store", "vcf-obs-data-platform", "telemetry"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") | fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago"), .path ]
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'

Apply Services Runtime Configuration of VCF Management Services for VCF Component Backup and Restore
To ensure the worker nodes are the correct size, you apply the kubernetes package deployment from the backup.
1. Discover the VCF management services control plane node.
a) SSH to the Services Runtime FQDN e.g. sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io.
b) Find the EXTERNAL-IP address of the control plane node.
sudo su
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
kubectl get nodes -o wide
2. Copy all yaml files from Extract Services Runtime Configuration from the Services Runtime Backup for VCF
Component Backup and Restore to the control plane node.
3. SSH to the control plane node and run the following.
sudo su
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
export YAML_PATH='./'
export WORKER_SIZE=$(awk '/worker:/{f=1} f && /size:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-platform.yaml)
export MACHINE_TYPE=$(awk '/worker:/{f=1} f && /machineType:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-
platform.yaml)
export PROFILE=$(awk '/profiles:/{f=1} f && /name:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-platform.yaml)
kubectl patch packagedeployment vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform \
--type=merge \
-p "$(jq -n \
--arg s "$WORKER_SIZE" \
--arg m "$MACHINE_TYPE" \
--arg p "$PROFILE" \
'{
"spec": {
"values": {
"cluster": {
"worker": {
"size": $s,
"machineType": $m
}
},
"profiles": {
"name": $p
}
}
}
}')"
Broadcom 4327

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Monitor the task.
kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Successful packagedeployment/vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform
--timeout=2h
# Wait for this message
packagedeployment.releases.vmsp.vmware.com/vmsp-platform condition met
kubectl get packagedeployment vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'
# Wait for this message
Successful
The worker nodes will be resized to match their size when the backup was taken. Do not proceed until this step has
completed.
Configure Depot and Download Binaries
To enable the restore of the remaining components, you configure a software depot and download the required binaries.
The binaries show as downloaded in the Binary Management UI, however, the underlying binaries are not restored as part
of the restore of the software depot component.
1. Log in to VCF Operations as a user with the Administrator role.
2. Configure the software depot.
a) Navigate to Build > Software Depot.
b) In the right pane, click Edit.
c) Configure your depot type and click Finish.
3. Download the required binaries.
a) Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Instances and click the VCF Instance name where you are performing the
restore.
b) In the right pane, click Binary Management.
c) In the Binary Management pane, click Install Binaries.
d) On the Install Binaries pane, click the checkbox for the following components, and click Delete Download.
Install Binaries to Download
Identity broker
Telemetry
License Server
Salt RaaS
Salt master
e) On the Install Binaries pane, click the checkbox for the following components, and click Download.
Install Binaries to Download
Identity broker
Telemetry
License Server
Wait for the binaries to download before proceeding.

After you restore the core VCF management services components, if you have the log management component, you can
now restore it.
You must download the required binaries.
Broadcom 4328

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Retrieve a VCF management services fleet lifecycle access token.
export VCFMS_SR='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
2. Retrieve a list of available backups for Log management.
# Retrieve list of backups for log management
curl -k "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/system/backups" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFMS_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' | \
jq -r '
["ops-logs"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
| (
# Replace dashes with colons in the time portion to make it ISO-compliant
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") | fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago"), .path ]
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
3. Perform the restore of Log management.

-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H "Content-type: application/json" \
-d '{
"components": [

ac83-481b-876f-922497eaada7/9.1.0.0.25262140/2026-03-23T17-17-22Z",

File-Based Restore of VCF Automation
Depending on the failure scenario, the recovery process can vary. Use this table to guide you to the process that meets
your scenario.
Table 1163: VCF Automation Failure Scenarios
Failure Scenario Recovery Process
VCF Automation application corruption In Place Restore of VCF Automation
Single node lost • No action required
• The failed node is automatically redeployed
Two nodes lost VCF Automation Redeploy and Restore Tasks for Component
Backup and Restore
Three nodes lost VCF Automation Redeploy and Restore Tasks for Component
Backup and Restore
In Place Restore of VCF Automation
The following procedure can be used to perform an in place restore of a VCF Automation instance if there is a failure at
the application level.
• VCF Automation is in a failed state but the virtual machines are still running.
• You must have at least one recent backup of the component that you are restoring.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF Automation, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– VCF Operations
– VCF management services with Fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle.
Broadcom 4330

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management.
3. On the VCF Management page, click Backup & Restore > Restore.
4. To restore your VCF component, select the VCF Instance.
5. On the Restore pane, select the VCF component from a specific backup or the latest backup.
• Restore from the latest backup on the cluster.
• Specify the date range to filter the backups available, select the backup and optionally select the restore point by
selecting the incremental backup.
6. Optional: Enter the Encryption passphrase.
7. Click Restore.
8. Monitor the restore task from the Tasks pane.
Remediate Passwords for VMware Cloud Foundation Components After a VCF Automation Restore
After a successful restore of VCF Automation, some service accounts might become disconnected.
To manually remediate the VCF Automation service account in vCenter and NSX, use the VCF Automation UI.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation interface at https://<vcf_automation_fqdn> with a user assigned the System
Administrator role.
2. In the left pane, navigate to VCF Instances.
3. On the VCF Instances page, click the vertical ellipsis next to the VCF Instance, and, from the drop-down menu, select
Rotate service account.
VCF Automation deletes and recreates the service account. This task might take a few minutes to complete.

Prepare to Restore VCF Automation for VCF Component Backup and Restore
Before you can deploy a new VCF Automation instance to restore to, you must delete the existing VCF Automation entry
in the SDDC Manager database.
CAUTION:
This procedure should not be used to completely delete a deployed component. To fully delete VCF Automation
refer to this KB441333
1. Open an SSH connnection to the SDDC Manger appliance as the vcf user and switch to the root user.
2. Connect to the Postgres database.
psql -U postgres -h localhost -d platform;
3. Query the vsp_clusters table and record the id of the entry with type CONSUMPTION.
select * from vsp_cluster;
4. Delete the CONSUMPTION entry.
CONSUMPTION
delete from vsp_cluster where type=' ';
5. Delete the corresponding credential.
CONSUMPTION
delete from credential where username='vsp/< -vsp_cluster_id>/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
Example
delete from credential where username='vsp/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
6. Retrieve a token from the Fleet Lifecycle service.
export VCFMS_FC='flt-fc01.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_FC_PASSWORD='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
VCFMS_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_FC/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_FC_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
7. Retrieve and record the component id for the VCF Automation.
curl -k -s "https://$VCFMS_FC/fleet-lcm/v1/components?includeConsumptionVsp=true&includeVcdMigrator=true"
\
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFMS_TOKEN" | jq '.components[] |
if .componentTypeDescription == "VCF services runtime"
then {id, componentTypeDescription, fqdn}

else {id, componentTypeDescription}
end'
Redeploy the VCF Automation Services Runtime Cluster for Component Backup and Restore
You deploy a new VCF Automation services runtime instance using the SDDC Manager API.
• VCF Automation is in a failed state and cannot be restored using the in place procedure.
• VCF Automation VMs must no longer exist in vCenter.
• You must have at least one recent backup of VCF Automation.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF Automation, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– VCF Operations
– SDDC Manager
• The VCF Automation binary must be available in the fleet software depot.
1. Retrieve the sddcLcmId from VCF management services.
a) Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export fleetLifecycleFqdn='flt-fc01.rainpole.io'
export fleetLifecycleUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export fleetLifecyclePassword='***************'
b) Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime instance by running the following command.
fleetLifecycleToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${fleetLifecycleFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=$fleetLifecycleUsername" \
--data-urlencode "password=$fleetLifecyclePassword" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
c) Retrieve the sddcLcmId from VCF management services by running the following command.
sddcLcmId=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${fleetLifecycleFqdn}/fleet-lcm/v1/components?
includeConsumptionVsp=true&includeVcdMigrator=true" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${fleetLifecycleToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r '.components[] | select(.componentType == "VCF_SDDC_LCM") | .id' | tee /dev/tty )
2. Retrieve token from SDDC Manager.
export sddcmFQDN='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export ssoAdminPassword='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
# generate token
token=$(curl -k https://"$sddcmFQDN"/v1/tokens \
-X POST \
-H "Content-type:application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"administrator@vsphere.local\", \"password\":\"$ssoAdminPassword\"}" | jq -r
'.accessToken')
3. Deploy a new VCF Automation services runtime instance.
# Domain id should be the management domain id from SDDC Manager
# FQDNs must match the original
# clusterId must match the original recorded in step 3 of Prepare to Restore VCF Automation for VCF

Restore VCF Automation for VCF Component Backup and Restore
Restore VCF Automation from a file-based backup.
Note:
It is recommended to use backups taken by using a backup schedule. On-demand backups will not have a
corresponding vsp backup. If you have a newer on-demand backup of VCF Automation, use the most recent
available vsp backup along with it.
1. Retrieve a VCF Automation services runtime token
export VCFA_SR='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export VCFA_SR_PASSWORD='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
VCFA_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFA_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
2. Retrieve list of backups for VCF Automation.
curl -k "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/system/backups" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFA_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' | \
jq -r '
["vsp","vcfa","vcd-migrator"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]

| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") | fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago"), .path ]
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
