Backup and Restore VCF Management Services in vSphere Foundation
vSphere Foundation deployments do not include the VCF Operations fleet management UI. Use the fleet lifecycle
component API to perform all backup and restore operations for VCF management services components in a vSphere
Foundation environment.
The VCF management services fleet lifecycle API provides programmatic access to backup configuration, on-demand and
scheduled backup configuration, backup enumeration, and component restoration. All operations authenticate against the
VCF Operations appliance and target the fleet lifecycle component discovered at runtime.
Prerequisites
• Verify that the workstation where you plan to run API calls has SSH access to VCF Operations.
• Verify that the workstation where you plan to run API calls has SSH access to the fleet lifecycle component.
• Verify that curl, jq, and base64 are available on the workstation where you plan to run API calls.
• Verify that you have administrative access to VCF Operations.
Obtain VCF Management Services Bearer Token and Component IDs in VMware vSphere
Foundation
Before configuring backup or performing backup and restore operations, obtain the unique component IDs for the VCF
management services components. This procedure also establishes the session variables and bearer token required by
all subsequent API calls in this workflow.
Acquire a fleet lifecycle bearer token.
1. Log in to the workstation where you are planning to run API calls.
2. Set the environment variables for the VCF Operations appliance.
export OPS_HOST="https://<vcf-operations-fqdn>"
export OPS_USER="admin"
password
export OPS_PASSWORD=' '
3. Encode the credentials as an HTTP Basic authorization value.
BASIC=$(printf '%s:%s' "$OPS_USER" "$OPS_PASSWORD" | base64 | tr -d ' \n')
4. To locate the fleet lifecycle service entry and record its host FQDN, query the endpoint.
casa/services
The endpoint uses HTTP Basic authentication. Locate the entry where
casa/services type == VCF_FLEET_LCM
and record both the key and the FQDN from .
nodes[0].addresses[0].value
Note:
The response inlines PEM certificates with raw new lines, which breaks strict JSON parsers. Strip newlines using
before passing output to jq.
tr -d '\n\r'
curl -k -sS "${OPS_HOST}/casa/services" -H "Authorization: Basic ${BASIC}" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r
'.services[] | select(.type == "VCF_FLEET_LCM") | [.key, .nodes[0].addresses[0].value] | @tsv'
# Example output:
# fleet-lcm fleet-lcm.sfo.example.com
Broadcom 4338

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Set the variable from the FQDN.
FLEET_HOST
export FLEET_HOST="https://<fleet-lcm-fqdn>" # e.g. https://fleet-lcm.sfo.example.com
6. Set the variable from the key returned in the previous output.
FLEET_KEY
The service key identifies the fleet lifecycle service and is required to exchange the VCF Operations token for a fleet
lifecycle JSON Web Token (JWT).
export FLEET_KEY="<fleet-lcm-key>" # e.g. fleet-lcm
7. Acquire a bearer token from the VCF Operations appliance.
The VCF Operations token authenticates against the suite-api endpoints on the VCF Operations appliance. This token
cannot be used directly as a Bearer token against the fleet lifecycle API.
export OPS_TOKEN=$(curl -k -sS -X POST "${OPS_HOST}/suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire?_no_links=true" -H
"Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"username\": \"${OPS_USER}\", \"authSource\":\"LOCAL\", \"password
\": \"${OPS_PASSWORD}\"}" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r '.token')
8. Exchange the VCF Operations token for a fleet lifecycle JWT token.
The fleet lifecycle API does not accept the VCF Operations token directly. Use the
/suite-api/api/auth/token/
endpoint to exchange the VCF Operations token for a JWT token scoped to the fleet lifecycle service. Pass
exchange
the VCF Operations token in the Authorization header using the scheme and include the fleet lifecycle
OpsToken
service key in the request body.
export FLEET_TOKEN=$(curl -k -sS -X POST "${OPS_HOST}/suite-api/api/auth/token/exchange" \
-H "accept: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: OpsToken ${OPS_TOKEN}" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d "{\"serviceKeys\": [\"${FLEET_KEY}\"]}" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r '.jwtToken')
9. Define the authorization header array for reuse in subsequent API calls.
AUTH=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${FLEET_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/json")
List VCF management services components and obtain their IDs.
10.Query the fleet lifecycle endpoint to list all registered VCF management services components and their IDs.
curl -k -sS "${AUTH[@]}" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/components" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r '.components[] |
[.componentType, .id, .fqdn, .version] | @tsv' | column -t
The output lists each component type, its UUID, its FQDN, and its current version. Example output:
OPS-LOGS 655d2c8b-2478-4057-80b2-60405cc45d96 ops-logs.sfo.example.com 9.1.0
FLEET-LCM a1b2c3d4-0000-1111-2222-abcdef012345 fleet-lcm.sfo.example.com 9.1.0
SDDC-LCM e5f6a7b8-3333-4444-5555-fedcba987654 sddc-lcm.sfo.example.com 9.1.0
11.Set the variable to the UUID of the component to back up or restore.
COMPONENT_ID
export COMPONENT_ID="<component-uuid>" # e.g. 655d2c8b-2478-4057-80b2-60405cc45d96
12.Retrieve the for the selected component.
sddcLcmId
This value is required to configure backup settings and initiate backup and restore operations.
export SDDC_LCM_ID=$(curl -k -sS "${AUTH[@]}" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/components/${COMPONENT_ID}"
| tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r '.sddcLcmId')
The session variables , , , , , and are set
OPS_TOKEN FLEET_TOKEN FLEET_HOST AUTH COMPONENT_ID SDDC_LCM_ID
and ready for use in subsequent backup and restore procedures. The bearer token is valid for the duration of the session.
The fleet lifecycle JWT token is valid for the duration of the session. Repeat Step 7 and Step 8 to renew the token if the
token expires before the workflow is completed.
Broadcom 4339

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Configure the SFTP Backup Location for VCF Management Services in VMware vSphere
Foundation
Configure an external SFTP server as the backup target for a VCF management services component. This configuration
is set per component using the obtained in the preceding procedure.
SDDC_LCM_ID
• Verify that you have the IP address or FQDN of the SFTP server.
• Verify that there is SSH access between the VCF management services component and the SFTP server.
1. Log in to the workstation where you are planning to run API calls.
2. Retrieve the SFTP server fingerprint.
Supported SSH fingerprints are of type or .
RSA ED25519
ssh-keyscan -p 22 <sftp_server_ip> | ssh-keygen -lf -
3. Set the SFTP server credentials as environment variables.
export SFTP_PASS='<sftp-password>'
export SFTP_THUMBPRINT='<sftp-host-key-thumbprint>'
4. Send a request to update the backup configuration for the component.
PATCH
curl -k -sS -X PATCH "${AUTH[@]}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-
lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}" -d @- << JSON
{
"backupConfigSpec": {
"storage": {
"sftp": {
"host": "<sftp-server-ip-or-fqdn>",
"port": "22",
"username": "root",
"password": "${SFTP_PASS}",
"directory": "/backup",
"thumbprint": "${SFTP_THUMBPRINT}"
}
}
}
}
JSON
The API returns a response. A successful response body reflects the updated value.
200 OK backupConfigSpec
The SFTP backup location is configured for the specified component. Subsequent on-demand and scheduled backup
operations for this component write backup data to the configured SFTP server and directory.
Back up a VCF Management Services Component in VMware vSphere Foundation
Initiate a backup of a VCF management services component. Two approaches are available: trigger an immediate on-
demand backup or configure a daily scheduled backup with a retention policy. Both approaches use the fleet lifecycle API
and write backup data to the SFTP server configured in the preceding procedure.
• Verify that no backup of the same component is currently in progress. Do not submit a new backup request while
another backup of the same component is running.
• Verify that the necessary environment variables are exported and you have completed the Obtain VCF Management
Services Bearer Token and Component IDs in VMware vSphere Foundation and Configure the SFTP Backup Location
for VCF Management Services in VMware vSphere Foundation procedures.
Trigger an immediate on-demand backup.
Broadcom 4340

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the workstation where you are planning to run API calls.
2. Submit a request to initiate an immediate backup of the specified component.
POST
curl -k -sS -X POST "${AUTH[@]}" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}/backups" \
-d @- << 'JSON'
{"actionType": "ComponentsBackupSpec", "componentIds":["${COMPONENT_ID}"]}
JSON
The response body contains a task object with a field. Record this value to monitor the operation.
taskId
3. Poll the state of the task.
TASK_ID="<task-id-from-previous-response>"
while :; do
S=$(curl -k -sS "${AUTH[@]}" \
"${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/tasks/${TASK_ID}" \
| tr -d '\n\r' \
| jq -r '.status')
echo "$S"
case "$S" in
SUCCEEDED|FAILED|CANCELLED) break ;;
esac
sleep 20
done
Configure a backup schedule.
4. Send a request to set the backup schedule and retention policy.
PATCH
The example configures a daily backup at 02:00 UTC with a maximum retention of seven backups. Adjust
startTime
to a time outside operational hours and to align with your organization's retention policy. Remove days
maxBackups
from the array to exclude specific days of the week.
days
curl -k -sS -X PATCH "${AUTH[@]}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-
lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}" -d @- << JSON
{
"backupConfigSpec": {
"storage": {
"sftp": {
"host": "<sftp-server-ip-or-fqdn>",
"port": "22",
"username": "root",
"password": "${SFTP_PASS}",
"directory": "/backup",
"thumbprint": "${SFTP_THUMBPRINT}"
}
},
"fullSchedule": {
"enabled": true,
"schedule": {
"startTime": "02:00:00Z",
"days": ["MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI", "SAT", "SUN"]
}
},
"retention": {
"maxBackups": 7
}
}
}
Broadcom 4341

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
JSON
5. Submit a task to create the backup schedule.
TASK_ID=$(curl -k -s -X POST "${AUTH[@]}" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}?action=apply" \
-d '{ "spec": { "configuration": { "backups": { "full": { "enable": true, "schedule": "0 2 * * 0" },
"incremental": { "enable": true, "schedule": "0 2 * * 1-6" } } } }, "options": {} }' \
| grep -o '"id":[^,]*' | grep -o '[^"]*$')
# Print the ID to verify it was captured
echo "Submitted Task ID: $TASK_ID"
The API returns a response. The response body reflects the updated schedule and retention values.
200 OK
Restore VCF Management Services Components from Backup in VMware vSphere Foundation
Restore a VCF management services component from a previously created backup stored on the configured SFTP
server. The restore operation is disruptive: the target component is taken offline and its data is replaced with the backup
data. Plan and schedule this procedure during a maintenance window.
• Verify that the necessary environment variables are exported and you have completed the Obtain VCF Management
Services Bearer Token and Component IDs in VMware vSphere Foundation and Configure the SFTP Backup Location
for VCF Management Services in VMware vSphere Foundation procedures.
The restore operation brings the target component down and replaces all component data with the selected backup. This
operation cannot be undone. Ensure that the correct backup path is specified before submitting the restore request.
1. Log in to the workstation where you are planning to run API calls.
2. Query the fleet lifecycle backup endpoint to list all backups available for the specified component.
curl -k -sS "${AUTH[@]}" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}/backups?componentId=
${COMPONENT_ID}" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq '.backups[] | {name, path, componentType, componentVersion, points}'
The response lists each backup with its , , , , and the points array.
name path componentType componentVersion
Each entry in points corresponds to a point-in-time backup and includes the SFTP path required for restore. An
example path has the following format:
sftp://root@<sftp-host>:22/backup/vcf/backups/<component-type>/<component-id>/<timestamp>
3. Export the full SFTP path of the backup to restore.
export BACKUP_PATH="sftp://root@<sftp-host>:22/backup/<path-to-backup>"
4. Submit a POST request to initiate the restore operation for the selected backup.
Replace with the value returned in the backup list (for example, ).
<component-type> componentType OPS-LOGS
Set to the passphrase used when the backup was created, or leave it as an empty string if
encryptionPassphrase
no passphrase was configured.
curl -k -sS -X POST "${AUTH[@]}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/sddc-
lcms/${SDDC_LCM_ID}/backups" -d @- << JSON
{
"actionType": "ComponentsRestoreSpec",
"encryptionPassphrase": "",
"components": [
{
"componentId": "${COMPONENT_ID}",
"componentType": "<component-type>",
"path": "${BACKUP_PATH}"
}
]
}
JSON
Broadcom 4342

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The response body contains a task object with a field. Record this value to monitor the operation.
taskId
5. Poll the state of the task.
TASK_ID="<task-id-from-previous-response>"
while :; do
S=$(curl -k -sS "${AUTH[@]}" "${FLEET_HOST}/fleet-lcm/v1/tasks/${TASK_ID}" | tr -d '\n\r' | jq -r
'.status')
echo "$S"
case "$S" in
SUCCEEDED|FAILED|CANCELLED) break ;;
esac
sleep 20
done
The VCF management services component is restored from the selected backup. The component is restarted
automatically as part of the restore process. Verify that the component is operational and that its services are accessible
before resuming normal operations.
VCF Instance Backup and Restore
VCF Instance Backup and Restore provides guidance on restoring a VCF Instance by performing a complete
reconstruction from a backup.
This guidance contains detailed instructions for both the management domain and workload domains where you must
restore all components.
Example Failure Scenarios
You may need to restore all components in a VCF Instance if one of the following scenarios occurs:
• Complete VCF Instance failure
• Malware or ransomware attack
• Datastore corruption
Supported Topologies
Several topologies of VCF exist according to the number of availability zones and VCF Instances.
The following topologies are supported for restore using this guidance.
Supported Topology Description
• Single VCF fleet
• VCF domains with a single or multiple vSphere clusters
• vSphere clusters with a single or multiple vSphere Distributed
Switches
• vSphere cluster models:
– Single-Rack vSphere Cluster Model
– Multi-Rack Layer 2 vSphere Cluster Model
– Stretched vSphere Cluster Model
• vSAN ESA and vSAN OSA
VCF Components to Back Up
All important data in a VMware Cloud Foundation platform should be backed up and that backup data should survive
the loss of any given site. Include all VMs in the management domain and VMs in workload domains that require data
protection.
After initial deployment, the management domain contains a core set of VMs to manage the VMware Cloud Foundation
platform. When you deploy a workload domain, VCF deploys additional VMs to manage the workload domain.
Broadcom 4343

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If you have other VMs in the management domain that require backup, for example, Microsoft SQL servers,
Microsoft Active Directory servers, backup software VMs, and so on, you should plan to back them up too.
This guidance does not provide information about backing up VMs in workload domains, but your backup plan should also
identify and back up critical VMs in workload domains.
Important:
• In order to capture all the required component data you must use scheduled backups for VCF Management
Services and VCF Automation.
• From VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1 and later, the SDDC Manager credentials database is no longer part
of the SDDC Manager backup. You must use the SDDC Manager credentials API to regularly backup the
credentials database and store it in a secure location. See On-Demand Backup of SDDC Manager Credential
Store
Documenting the System Configuration of VCF
Keeping detailed as-built documentation on the system configuration eases the restore process if a failure in your VMware
Cloud Foundation platform occurs.
Recording and subsequently providing the following information is mandatory when recovering a VCF Instance using the
manual processes included in this guidance. while the automated recovery process recovers much of the following from
the SDDC Manager backup, it is still a good idea to have an up-to-date record of the information. Save this information on
a secure secondary storage.
• Topology diagrams of the VMware Cloud Foundation platform:
– Physical networking
– vSphere Distributed Switch networking
– NSX networking
– VCF domain configuration
– Cluster configuration for each cluster in a VCF domain
– ESX hosts assigned to each cluster
– Custom VIBs installed on ESX hosts
• Networking information:
– ESX host vmnic-to-switch port mappings
– VM virtual NIC to distributed port group mappings
– IP address information of the VMkernel interfaces on the ESX hosts
– IP address information of VMs
– DNS, NTP, AD, and other well-known services used by the VMware Cloud Foundation platform
• vCenter instance configuration — for each vCenter instance:
– Fully qualified domain name (FQDN), and the IP address, prefix length, and default gateway for every configured
network adapter
– DNS servers and DNS search domains
– Static routes, if any are configured
– Number of virtual network adapters attached to the appliance
– vCenter version and build number, from the Summary tab of the vCenter Management Interface
– Deployment size and storage size
– Single Sign-On domain name
– Contents of /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, and any custom scripts stored on the appliance that are referenced by
alarm actions or cron jobs
PowerShell Automation for This Guidance
You can perform the procedures in this guide manually or by running cmdlets in an associated PowerShell module.
Broadcom 4344

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The PowerShell cmdlets are available in an open-source module as code-based alternatives to completing certain
procedures in each SDDC component's user interface. For more information on the PowerShell cmdlets for restore of
VMware Cloud Foundation, see the VMware.CloudFoundation.InstanceRecovery open-source project in GitHub.
Table 1164: Prerequisites for CLI Implementation of VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Prerequisite
• Microsoft Windows 2022 (minimum)
• Microsoft PowerShell 7.5.x (minimum)
• VMware OVF Tool
• OpenSSL lite version 1.0.2g or higher installed and added to the Windows PATH system variable.
• PowerCLI DefaultVIServerMode setting must be configured as Multiple for the all AllUsers scope
• Install the supporting modules from the PowerShell Gallery by running the following commands:
Install-Module -Name VCF.PowerCLI -MinimumVersion 9.1.0 -Scope AllUsers -Force
Install-Module -Name Posh-SSH -RequiredVersion 3.0.8 -Scope AllUsers -Force
Install-Module -Name VMware.CloudFoundation.InstanceRecovery -Scope AllUsers -Force
• Open a new PowerShell console and run the following command to confirm all the prerequisites are installed.
Confirm-VCFInstanceRecoveryPreReqs
Sequence Optimization for Restore of a VCF Instance
When restoring an entire VCF Instance, you can run certain tasks in parallel to minimize the time that is required to
restore it.
Example Restore Timeline for a VCF Instance
To minimize the overall restore time of a VCF instance, you can run multiple restore plans in parallel across VCF domains
with the following guidelines:
1. If you do not use all of the components shown, then you can ignore the associated steps and proceed to the next step
in the respective restore plan.
2. If you want to prioritize workload availability over management and operational components, you can do so.
3. You should not reorder the overall sequence of any given restore plan because that might compromise dependencies.
Important:
Where multiple items exist in a single cell, they may be run in parallel. Items across a single row may also be run
in parallel.
The following timeline is for a sample setup with the following configuration:
• Two VCF domains.
– One management domain (which is also running fleet components for the entire fleet).
– Fleet components are not on an NSX overlay network.
– One workload domain with an isolated vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) domain.
• VCF 9.1.0 and 9.1.1 only.
Attention:
* If fleet components are on an NSX overlay network, then do not start the fleet component restore plan until the
appropriate NSX Edge nodes are redeployed.

** Should there be more than one isolated workload domain, you can start the restore plan for all of them in
parallel.

ESX Configuration Tasks for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Perform these tasks for the configuration of ESX when restoring a VCF Instance.
Prepare Networking on Management ESX Hosts for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
During the VCF Instance restore process, you map network adapters on the new management domain hosts to standard
virtual switches
UI Procedure
1. Connect to the first ESX host in the management domain over SSH.
2. Based on the desired number of vSphere Distributed Switches that existed in the source system, and factoring in the
VLANs that are available on each physical NICs in the new ESX hosts, run the following commands.
# Step 1: Inspect existing NICs and switches
esxcli network nic list
esxcli network vswitch standard list
# Step 2: Update MTU on the existing management vSS
esxcli network vswitch standard set --vswitch-name=vSwitch0 --mtu=9000
# Step 3: Add an additional NIC to the existing management vSS (if applicable)
esxcli network vswitch standard uplink add --vswitch-name=vSwitch0 --uplink-name=vmnic1
# Step 4: Create the vm_mgmt portgroup with the VM_MANAGEMENT VLAN
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup add --vswitch-name=vSwitch0 --portgroup-name="vm_mgmt"
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup set --portgroup-name="vm_mgmt" --vlan-id=<VM_MANAGEMENT_VLAN_ID>
# Step 5: Create a NEW vSS that maps to each non-management VDSes (repeat per additional vSS)
esxcli network vswitch standard add --vswitch-name=vSwitch1 --ports=128
esxcli network vswitch standard set --vswitch-name=vSwitch1 --mtu=9000
Broadcom 4384

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
# Step 6: Add NICs to each new vSS (repeat per additional vSS)
esxcli network vswitch standard uplink add --vswitch-name=vSwitch1 --uplink-name=vmnic2
esxcli network vswitch standard uplink add --vswitch-name=vSwitch1 --uplink-name=vmnic3
3. Repeat on the remaining ESX hosts in the management domain.
PowerShell Equivalent

is part of:
• Management Domain Restore Plan
Add VMkernel Adapters to Management ESX Hosts for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To enable vSphere vMotion and vSAN traffic, add VMkernel network adapters to the new management hosts.
UI Procedure
1. Connect to the first ESX host in the management domain over SSH.
2. Configure VMkernel network adapters on the ESX host, reinstating the documented network addresses for the
vSphere vMotion and vSAN interfaces.
# ==============================
# vMotion VMkernel Configuration
# ==============================
# Step 1: Create the vMotion portgroup with the correct VLAN
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup add --vswitch-name=<VMOTION_VSS> --portgroup-name="vmotion"
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup set --portgroup-name="vmotion" --vlan-id=<VMOTION_VLAN_ID>
# Step 2: Create the vMotion netstack (if it doesn't already exist)
esxcli network ip netstack add --netstack=vmotion
# Step 3: Verify it exists
esxcli network ip netstack list
# Step 4: Add vmk1 on the vmotion netstack
esxcli network ip interface add --interface-name=vmk1 --portgroup-name="vmotion" --mtu=<VMOTION_MTU> --
netstack=vmotion
esxcli network ip interface ipv4 set --interface-name=vmk1 --type=static --ipv4=<HOST_VMOTION_IP> --
netmask=<VMOTION_MASK>
# Step 5: Set the default gateway on the vmotion netstack
esxcli network ip route ipv4 add --netstack=vmotion --network=default --gateway=<VMOTION_GATEWAY>
# ===========================
# vSAN VMkernel Configuration
# ===========================
# Step 1: Create the vSAN portgroup with the correct VLAN
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup add --vswitch-name=<VSAN_VSS> --portgroup-name="vsan"
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup set --portgroup-name="vsan" --vlan-id=<VSAN_VLAN_ID>
# Step 2: Add vmk2 (uses the default netstack)
esxcli network ip interface add --interface-name=vmk2 --portgroup-name="vsan" --mtu=<VSAN_MTU>
esxcli network ip interface ipv4 set --interface-name=vmk2 --type=static --ipv4=<HOST_VSAN_IP> --
netmask=<VSAN_MASK> --gateway=<VSAN_GATEWAY>
Broadcom 4385

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
# Step 3: Enable vSAN traffic on vmk2
esxcli vsan network ipv4 add --interface-name=vmk2
# Step 4: Verify
esxcli network ip interface list
esxcli network ip route ipv4 list --netstack=vmotion
esxcli vsan network list
3. Repeat on the remaining ESX hosts in the management domain.

Create a Single-Host vSAN Datastore for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Create a single-host vSAN datastore to use as a target for the OVA deployments of vCenter, NSX Manager, and SDDC
Manager.
UI Procedure
1. Connect to the first ESX host in the management domain over SSH.
2. If your rebuilt system will use vSAN ESA, run the following commands:
# Step 1: Initialize vSAN ESA
esxcli vsan cluster new --vsanesa
# Step 2: Verify vSAN is enabled
esxcli vsan cluster get
# Step 3: List eligible disks (Look for: IsLocal=true, IsBootDevice=false, deviceType=Direct-Access)
esxcli storage core device list | grep -E "^eui\.|^naa\.|^mpx\.|Size:|Is Boot Device:|Is Local:|Device
Type:|Is SSD:"
# Step 4: Add each eligible disk to the ESA storage pool (repeat per disk)
esxcli vsan storagepool add --disk=<DISK_CANONICAL_NAME>
3. If your rebuilt system will use vSAN OSA, run the following commands:
# Step 1: Initialize vSAN OSA
esxcli vsan cluster new
# Step 2: Verify vSAN is enabled
esxcli vsan cluster get
# Step 3: List eligible disks (Look for: IsLocal=true, IsBootDevice=false, deviceType=Direct-Access)
esxcli storage core device list | grep -E "^eui\.|^naa\.|^mpx\.|Size:|Is Boot Device:|Is Local:|Device
Type:|Is SSD:"
# Step 4: If any CAPACITY disk is an SSD, tag it as capacityFlash first
esxcli vsan storage tag add --disk=<CAPACITY_SSD_CANONICAL_NAME> --tag=capacityFlash
# Step 5: Add each disk group (append --disks parameter for each capacity disk to be added)
esxcli vsan storage add --ssd=<CACHE_DISK_CANONICAL_NAME> --disks=<CAPACITY_DISK_CANONICAL_NAME> --
disks=<CAPACITY_DISK_CANONICAL_NAME>
Broadcom 4386

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
# Step 6: Set FTT to 0 to allow deployment of VMs
esxcli vsan policy setdefault -c vdisk -p '(("hostFailuresToTolerate" i0) ("forceProvisioning" i1))'
esxcli vsan policy setdefault -c vmnamespace -p '(("hostFailuresToTolerate" i0) ("forceProvisioning" i1))'

vCenter Restore Tasks for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Perform these tasks that are related to the restore of vCenter in a VCF Instance.
Deploy a vCenter Appliance from an OVA File for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To restore a vCenter instance, you first deploy a new appliance from an OVA file. You then use this appliance to restore
the management domain or workload domain.
Prerequesites
• Confirm the OVA is from the vCenter build matching the version and build recorded for the failed instance. The
restore fails if the versions differ, and the mismatch is only detected after the appliance is deployed.
• Confirm you have the deployment size and storage size of the failed instance. The replacement appliance must be the
same size or larger; a smaller one fails the restore.
• If the failed vCenter had more than one virtual network adapter, plan to attach the additional adapters to the
replacement appliance before you run the restore.
UI Procedure
Important:
In the case of the management domain vCenter, the target for OVA deployment will always be the first
management ESX host. For workload domains, the target can also be the first management ESX host (if doing
in parallel with management domain recovery) or it can be the management vCenter if the workload domain
recovery is being performed after management domain recovery.
1. Download the vCenter OVA and ensure its available to the workstation where you will be performing the recovery from.
2. Log in to the first management ESX host at as the user.
https://<esx_fqdn>/ui root
3. Right-click the host and select Deploy OVF Template.
a. Step through the wizard populating the fields with data gathered during Gather Information for VCF Instance
Backup and Restore.
OVF Property Source If it is wrong
Host Network Identity (FQDN) Gather Information — FQDN Restore fails: The appliance PNID does
not match the backup PNID.
Host Network IP Address Gather Information — IP address Restore fails: Local machine IP(s) do not
match to any of the PNID resolved IPs.
Host Network Prefix Gather Information — prefix length Not checked. The restore succeeds with
the wrong subnet mask.
Host Network Default Gateway Gather Information — default gateway Not checked. The restore succeeds with
the wrong gateway.
Host Network DNS Servers Gather Information — DNS servers Not checked, and not overwritten by
the restore. The value entered here is the
value the restored vCenter keeps.
Broadcom 4387

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
OVF Property Source If it is wrong
Root Password Gather Information — root user password Not checked. See the note below.
Deployment size / storage size Gather Information — deployment size Restore fails if smaller than the failed
instance. Larger is accepted.
Network / port group As-built documentation The appliance is unreachable and the
restore cannot start.
4. Submit and deploy the OVA.
Note:
This wizard does not read the backup. Unlike the vCenter installer used in Restore a vCenter Instance from a
File-Based Backup, no field here is pre-filled from the backup metadata. Every value must come from Gather
Information for VCF Instance Backup and Restore.
Important:
Set the root password to the password the failed vCenter had when the backup was taken — the value
retrieved in Retrieve the Credentials for Restoring a vCenter Instance. The restore preserves the password you
enter here; it does not restore the original password from the backup. SDDC Manager and VCF Operations store
the original password and fail to connect to the restored vCenter if it differs. If you must change the root password,
do so after the restore completes and update it in SDDC Manager and VCF Operations at the same time.
Note:
The Single Sign-On administrator password behaves differently: it is restored from the backup. After the restore,
administrator@<sso_domain> has the password it had when the backup was taken, regardless of anything
entered during recovery.
Note:
If the failed vCenter had more than one virtual network adapter, attach the additional adapters to the replacement
appliance now, before you run the restore. The restore configures only adapters that already exist; addresses for
missing adapters are dropped and the restore still reports success.

Record the Cluster Settings from the Restored vCenter for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Before you can recover the vSphere clusters in the restored vCenter instance, you must first record the settings so they
can be reapplied to the cluster.
vCenter has been restored and powered on.
1. Log in to the restored vCenter instance at with the
https://<restored_vcenter_fqdn>/ui
user.
administrator@vsphere.local
2. Record the following settings for every cluster in the restored vCenter.
• Virtual machine overrides
• Virtual machine locations

Remove Non-Responsive ESX Hosts from the Inventory for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Before you can repair a failed vSphere cluster, you must first remove the non-responsive hosts from the cluster.
Prerequisites
Ensure you have exported all cluster settings before proceeding.
CAUTION:
Refer to SDDC Manager UI to determine if the cluster being recovered is a vSAN Compute-Only cluster. If so,
ensure that the vSAN Storage cluster it depends on has already been recovered. If the cluster is the primary
cluster in the management domain then by definition it cannot be a vSAN Compute-Only cluster.
UI Procedure
1. In the vSphere Client, browse to the cluster and identify every host whose connection state is Not Responding or
Disconnected. Make a list of their exact display names — you will need them repeatedly in later steps.
2. Note the cluster's MoRef ID (visible in the cluster's URL/managed object browser, or via Get-Cluster | select
ExtensionData.MoRef), and determine the NSX Manager's version.
a. GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/node and note product_version.
Broadcom 4389

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
b. If this call fails or returns no version, stop here — do not proceed until NSX Manager is confirmed healthy and
reachable.
3. Identify the NSX transport nodes that correspond to the non-responsive hosts.
a. GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/ and filter results to entries where resource_type is
TransportNode and node_deployment_info.os_type is ESXI.
b. From that filtered list, match each entry's display_name against the non-responsive host names from step 1, and
record their transport node id values.
4. Identify the cluster's NSX compute collection.
a. GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/fabric/compute-collections.
b. Find the entry whose cm_local_id matches the cluster's MoRef ID from step 2, and record its external_id — this
is the compute collection ID used in the next steps.
5. Remove the non-responsive hosts from vCenter Server inventory.
a. For each host identified in step 1, right-click it in the vSphere Client and select Remove from Inventory
(equivalent to Remove-VMHost -Confirm:$false). Confirm the removal.
b. This step must be completed for all non-responsive hosts before continuing — later steps assume they are already
gone from vCenter Server.
6. Detach the Transport Node Profile from the cluster's compute collection.
a. POST https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/fabric/compute-collections/<compute-collection-id>?
action=remove_nsx.
b. For each transport node ID recorded in step 3, poll GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<id>/
state repeatedly until its state reports orphaned. Do not proceed to step 7 until every affected transport node
reaches this state.
7. Force-delete each stale transport node.
a. For each transport node ID from step 3, DELETE https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<id>?
force=true&unprepare_host=false.
b. unprepare_host=false is required here — the host is gone and unreachable, so NSX cannot attempt to uninstall
its own agents from it; this only removes NSX's bookkeeping record for that node.
8. Wait for the deleted transport nodes to fully flush from NSX Manager's inventory before proceeding.
a. Repeatedly POST https://<nsx-manager>/policy/api/v1/search/aggregate?page_size=50 with body
{"primary": {"resource_type": "HostTransportNode"}}.
b. Keep polling until none of the returned results' display_name values match any of the removed host names from
step 1. This can take some time — do not move on early.
9. Reattach the cluster to its Transport Node Profile so NSX resumes auto-preparing hosts in this cluster.
a. GET https://<nsx-manager>/policy/api/v1/infra/host-transport-node-profiles and find the profile whose
display_name contains the cluster's name.
b. POST https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-node-collections with a body creating a
TransportNodeCollection resource that links the compute collection ID (step 4) to that Transport Node Profile's
ID, for example:
{
"resource_type": "TransportNodeCollection",
"display_name": "<clusterName>",
"description": "<clusterName>",
"compute_collection_id": "<compute-collection-id>",
"transport_node_profile_id": "<transport-node-profile-id>"
}
Result
The non-responsive hosts are removed from both vCenter Server and NSX Manager, and the cluster's
compute collection is once again associated with its Transport Node Profile.

Recreate a vSAN Datastore for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To recreate the vSAN datastore, you claim disks and create a vSAN datastore.
CAUTION:

compute-only clusters.
If the datastore is vSAN ESA, the datastore is recreated automatically. Only Step 5 and Step 6 are required.
UI Procedure
1. Log in to the restored vCenter instance at with the
https://<restored_vcenter_fqdn>/ui
user.
administrator@vsphere.local
2. In the Hosts and clusters inventory, navigate to the cluster and click Configure.
3. Under vSAN, click Disk Management, and click Claim Unused Disks.
4. Select the relevant disks for each tier and click Claim.

Restore NSX Manager from a File-Based Backup for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
You restore the file-based backup of the first NSX Manager cluster node to the newly-deployed NSX Manager instance.
Before you Begin
• Verify that you have the login credentials (username and password or the SSH private key matching the public key
stored on the backup file server) for the backup file server.
• Verify that you have the SSH fingerprint of the backup file server. Support includes key size 256-bit, 384-bit, and 521-
bit. Ensure whatever key size is used at time of backup is used at time of restore.
• Verify that you have the passphrase of the backup file.
• Identify which backup you want to restore. Take note of the IP or FQDN of the NSX appliance that took the backup.
• Ensure the network setup where you are performing the restore has the same set of network connectivity as the
system on which you performed the backup. For example, the same VIPs, DNS, NTP communication,and so on. If
network connectivity is not same, fix the inconsistencies before adding a second or third node to the restored system.
• Familiarize yourself with the Management Plane upgrade process as part of restoring a backup during an upgrade.
UI Procedure
1. Log in to the NSX Manager user interface at with the admin user.
https://<nsx_manager-fqdn>
2. On the main navigation bar, click System.
3. In the left navigation pane, under Lifecycle Management, click Backup & Restore.
4. In the Backup & Restore pane, under SFTP server, click Edit.
5. In the Backup configuration dialog box, enter the details for your backup server, and click Save.
6. Under Backup history, select the source backup, and click Restore.
7. During the restore, when prompted, reject adding NSX Manager nodes by clicking I understand and Resume.
8. If a Confirm CM/VC Connectivity dialog box appears, click I understand the message mentioned above and wish
to proceed, and click Resume.
9. If a fabric node discovery timeout dialog box appears, click Resume to continue the restore operation.

Redeploy Specific NSX Edges in an NSX Edge Cluster
To restore only the NSX Edge nodes that are missing from the vCenter inventory (for example, after a partial cluster
failure), identify which NSX Edge nodes are missing, recreate a placeholder VM shell for each one in vCenter, then use
the NSXNSX API to point NSX Manager at the new VM and redeploy the NSX Edge node.
• Administrator credentials for the NSX Manager that owns the NSX Edge cluster.
Broadcom 4399

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Administrator credentials for the vCenter that hosts the cluster.
• The extracted-sddc-data.json file produced during backup extraction, in case the original management portgroup or
vSphere Distributed Switch can no longer be resolved directly in vCenter.
• Sufficient compute and storage capacity in the target cluster to place new NSX Edge VM shells.
1. Identify all NSX Edge transport nodes associated with the cluster.
a) In NSX Manager, send a GET request to https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/ and note every result
whose node_deployment_info.resource_type is EdgeNode.
b) In vCenter note the MoRef IDs of the cluster's resource pools (excluding the default Resources pool) and of the
cluster object itself.
c) Match each Edge's node_deployment_info.deployment_config.vm_deployment_config.compute_id against
those MoRef IDs to determine which NSX Edge belong to this cluster, and whether each one belongs to a specific
resource pool or directly to the cluster.
2. Determine which of those NSX Edge VMs are missing from vCenter.
a) In the vSphere Client, browse to the cluster and check whether a VM with the same name as each NSX Edge
nodedisplay_name exists in inventory.
b) Make a list of the NSX Edge nodes that have no matching VM — these are the ones that need to be redeployed.
3. For each missing NSX Edge node, retrieve its current placement configuration.
a) Send a GET request to https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<edgenode-id> and
note the vm_deployment_config section — specifically resource_allocation.cpu_count,
resource_allocation.memory_allocation_in_mb, reservation_info.cpu_reservation.reservation_in_shares,
data_network_ids, and management_network_id.
b) In vCenter Server, resolve management_network_id to a distributed portgroup name and VDS name (match it
against the portgroup's MoRef in the Networking inventory view). If it can no longer be resolved (for example, the
Broadcom 4400

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VDS was rebuilt during recovery), instead use the management portgroup and VDS name recorded for this cluster
in extracted-sddc-data.json.
c) Note the cluster's primary datastore.
4. Create a placeholder VM shell for the missing NSX Edge node.
a) In the vSphere Client, right-click the resource pool identified in step 1 (or the cluster, if the NSX Edge node was not
in a resource pool) and select New Virtual Machine.
b) Name the VM exactly the same as the NSX Edge node's display_name from step 3.
c) Place it on any host in the cluster, using the datastore identified in step 3.3.
d) Set the guest OS to a generic Linux 64-bit guest, a 200 GB thin-provisioned disk, and connect its first network
adapter to the management portgroup identified in step 3.2.
e) Do not power on the VM.
5. Set the new VM's resource allocation to match the original NSX Edge node.
a) Edit the VM's resource settings and set the memory reservation to the value from
resource_allocation.memory_allocation_in_mb (step 3.1).
b) Set the CPU shares level (Low/Normal/High) to match reservation_info.cpu_reservation.reservation_in_shares
(step 3.1).
6. Add the NSX Edge node's remaining network adapters.
a) For every network ID in data_network_ids (step 3.1) other than the management network, add a VMXNET3
network adapter to the VM, connected to the matching distributed portgroup, set to connect at power on.
7. Update the NSX Edge node's placement references in NSX Manager .
a) Note the new VM's MoRef ID in vCenter.
b) In the vm_deployment_config JSON retrieved in step 3.1, set storage_id to the datastore's MoRef ID.
c) Build a JSON payload containing vm_id (the new VM's MoRef), the updated vm_deployment_config, and a
node_user_settings object with cli_username set to admin and audit_username set to audit.
d) POST that payload to https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<edgenode-id>?
action=addOrUpdatePlacementReferences.
8. Check the NSX Edge node's deployment state.
a) GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<edgenode-id>/state and check
node_deployment_state.state.
b) If the state is already success, no further action is required for this Edge.
c) If the state is MPA_DISCONNECTED, VM_PLACEMENT_REFRESH_FAILED, or NODE_READY, continue to
step 9.
d) If the state is any other value, do not proceed — review the Edge in NSX Manager before retrying.
9. Redeploy the NSX Edge node.
a) GET https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<edgenode-id> and copy the full JSON response body.
b) POST that same JSON body to https://<nsx-manager>/api/v1/transport-nodes/<edgenode-id>?
action=redeploy.
10.Repeat steps 3 – 9 for each remaining missing Edge.
NSX Manager provisions each redeployed NSX Edge node onto the new VM shell you created and rejoins it to the cluster.
In the NSX Manager UI, monitor the configuration status of each redeployed NSX Edge node until it shows Success.
If an NSX Edge node instead reports that its NSX Edge VM is present in NSX inventory but missing in vCenter go to
Alarms in NSX Manager, select the alarm with Event Type Edge VM Present In NSX Inventory Not Present In vCenter,
choose Resolve, and retry the redeploy step (step 9) for that NSX Edge node.
PowerShell Equivalent
To see the PowerShell equivalent of this process in context, with sample parameters, refer to the following plans this task
is part of:
• Management Domain Restore Plan
Broadcom 4401

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Workload Domain Restore Plan

Update vCenter SSH Keys in the SDDC Manager Backup for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To be able to restore of SDDC Manager in VCF versions earlier than VCF 9.1.1, you must update the SSH keys for the
new management vCenter appliance in the backup archive.
Prerequisites
Verify that the vCenter restore operation is complete.
Manual Procedure
1. Copy the encrypted backup file of SDDC Manager to the folder on the newly-deployed SDDC Manager
/tmp
appliance.
Broadcom 4402

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manager appliance, connect using the vcf user.
3. Switch to the root user and change to the folder.
/tmp
su -
cd /tmp
4. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export tmpFolderPath='/tmp/'
export backupFile='vcf-backup-sfo-vcf01-sfo-rainpole-io-xxxx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx.tar.gz'
export vcenterFqdn='sfo-m01-vc01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export encryptionPassword='VMw@re1!VMw@re1!'
backupFolder="${backupFile%.tar.gz}"
5. In the appliance console, run the following command to extract the backup archive.
tail -c +5 $tmpFolderPath$backupFile | OPENSSL_FIPS=1 openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -md
sha256 | tar -xz
When prompted, enter the .
encryption_password
6. Retrieve the new ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 and ssh-rsa SSH keys for the management vCenter.
ecdsaKey=$(ssh-keyscan -t ecdsa $vcenterFqdn 2>/dev/null | awk '/ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/ {print $3}')
rsaKey=$(ssh-keyscan -t rsa $vcenterFqdn 2>/dev/null | awk '/ssh-rsa/ {print $3}')
7. Replace the existing SSH keys with the new SSH keys for the management vCenter returned in the previous step.
sed -i '/"host": "'"${vcenterFqdn}"'"/ { N; /"keyType": "ssh-rsa"/ { N; s|"key": "[^"]*"|"key":
"'"${rsaKey}"'"|; } }' $backupFolder/appliancemanager_ssh_knownHosts.json
sed -i '/"host": "'"${vcenterFqdn}"'"/ { N; /"keyType": "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256"/ { N; s|"key":
"[^"]*"|"key": "'"${ecdsaKey}"'"|; } }' $backupFolder/appliancemanager_ssh_knownHosts.json
8. Rename the original backup archive.
mv $tmpFolderPath$backupFile $tmpFolder$backupFile.original
9. Re-encrypt the backup folder as an archive using the same archive name.
tar -cz $tmpFolderPath$backupFolder | OPENSSL_FIPS=1 openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -md sha256 -out
$tmpFolderPath$backupFile -pass env:encryptionPassword

To see the PowerShell equivalent of this process in context, with sample parameters, refer to the following plans this task
is part of:
• Management Domain Restore Plan
Restore SDDC Manager from a File-Based Backup for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
You restore the file-based backup on the newly-deployed SDDC Manager appliance.
Manual Procedure
1. If you have not already uploaded the SDDC Manager backup to the folder on the newly-deployed SDDC
/tmp
Manager appliance then do so now
2. Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manager appliance, connect using the vcf user.
3. Switch to the root user.
su -
4. Backup the file.
restore_status.json
cp /opt/vmware/sddc-support/backup/restore_status.json /opt/vmware/sddc-support/backup/
restore_status.json.bak
5. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
export tmpFolderPath='/tmp/'
Broadcom 4403

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
export backupFile='/tmp/vcf-backup-sfo-vcf01-sfo-rainpole-io-xxxx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx.tar.gz'
export encryptionPassword='***************'
6. Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
7. Create the JSON payload for the restore by running the following command.
sddcRestorePayload=$(jq -n \
--arg file "${tmpFolderPath}${backupFile}" \
--arg pass "${encryptionPassword}" \
'{
"elements": [ { "resourceType": "SDDC_MANAGER" } ],
"backupFile": $file,
"encryption": { "passphrase": $pass }
}' | tee /dev/tty )
8. Perform a restore of the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
restoreId=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/restores/tasks" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data "$sddcRestorePayload" \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )

Synchronize the SDDC Manager Service Account on the ESX Hosts for VCF Instance Backup and
Restore
The service account of SDDC Manager on the ESX hosts must be in sync with the SDDC Manager inventory. You must
manually set a new password on each ESX host and perform a password remediate operation in SDDC Manager.
UI Procedure
1. If the service account does not exist, create a service account on the ESX host.
a. Log in to the first ESX host in the cluster using the host client as root.
b. Navigate to Manage > Security & users > Users, and click Add user.
c. Enter the SDDC Manager service user name and password, and click Add.
Note:
The service account user name must be in the svc-vcf-ESX_hostname format.
2. If the service account exists, set a new password on the ESX host.
a. Log in to the first ESX host in the cluster using the host client as root.
b. In the host client on the first ESX host, navigate to Manage > Security & users > Users.
c. Select the SDDC Manager service account svc-vcf-ESX_hostname and click Edit user.
d. Set a new password and click Save.
3. Perform password remediation in SDDC Manager.
a. Log in to SDDC Manager
b. Navigate to Developer Center > Credentials > GET.
c. Enter the ESX FQDN in the resourceName field and click Execute.
d. Locate the service account from Step 1 or Step 2 and expand the output and record the output of the account with
accountType of SERVICE.
e. Construct the following JSON payload using the password you set in step 1 or 2.
{
"elements": [ {
"credentials": [ {
"accountType": "SERVICE",
"credentialType": "SSH",
"password": "************",
"username": "svc-vcf-sfo01-m01-r01-esx02"
} ],
"resourceId": "0f11d65d-1b08-4943-b920-5418c7e43c40",
"resourceName": "sfo01-m01-r01-esx02.sfo.rainpole.io",
"resourceType": "ESXI"
} ],
"operationType": "REMEDIATE"
}
4. Expand /v1/credentials/PATCH and paste the JSON payload into the body field, and click Execute. Wait for the
password remediation to complete.
5. Repeat the steps for all hosts in the workload domain.

Repoint SDDC Manager Depot to an Offline Depot for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To deploy a new VCF management services runtime cluster, you must point SDDC Manager to an offline depot.
UI Procedure
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
export offlineDepotFqdn="depot.rainpole.io"
export offlineDepotPort="443"
export offlineDepotUsername="depotuser"
export offlineDepotPassword="***************"
2. Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--data "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrive the depot service key and export the current configuration details to
original-depotServices-
by running the following command.
config.json
serviceConfigKey=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/services-config" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq . | tee original-depotServices-config.json | jq -r '.services[0].key')
4. Delete the current depot service configuration by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X DELETE "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/services-config/${serviceConfigKey}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json"
5. Retrieve the offline depot certificate to by running the following command.
trusted-cert-spec.json
echo "{ \"certificate\" : $(openssl s_client \
-connect ${offlineDepotFqdn}:${offlineDepotPort} \
2>/dev/null </dev/null \
| sed -ne '/-BEGIN CERTIFICATE-/,/-END CERTIFICATE-/p' \
| jq -sR), \"certificateUsageType\" : \"TRUSTED_FOR_OUTBOUND\"}" \
> trusted-cert-spec.json
6. Trust the offline depot certificate on SDDC Manager by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/sddc-manager/trusted-certificates" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
Broadcom 4406

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @trusted-cert-spec.json
7. Configure the offline depot by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X PUT "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/system/settings/depot" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data "{
\"offlineAccount\": {
\"username\": \"${offlineDepotUsername}\",
\"password\": \"${offlineDepotPassword}\"
},
\"depotConfiguration\": {
\"isOfflineDepot\": true,
\"hostname\": \"${offlineDepotFqdn}\",
\"port\": ${offlineDepotPort}
}
}"

Restore VCF Operations from an Image-Based Backup for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Restore a simple or high availability deployment of VCF Operations by using an image-based backup tool.
• Backup Data Available: Ensure that you have a recent backup of your VCF Operations cluster.
• VCF Operations Cluster Configuration: Ensure you know the details of your VCF Operations cluster configuration,
such as cluster nodes, user credentials.
• Backup Software: Ensure that the backup solution you are using is compatible with your VCF Operations version.

Component Deployment Model Failure Scenario Restore Process
VCF Operations Primary node lost Restore primary node from image-based backup.
Simple
Cloud proxy lost Restore cloud proxy from image-based backup.
High Availability Primary node lost Restore primary node from image-based backup.

1. If the VCF Operations virtual machines are running in the management domain, power them off and rename or delete
them.

Verify VCF Operations State for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
After a successful restore of VCF Operations, you verify the state of the analytics cluster and each integration adapter.
The cluster must be online. Not all integration adapters may be in a collecting state as they may not yet be recovered.
1. Verify the VCF Operations cluster state.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations admin console at
https://<vcf-operations-primary-node-fqdn>/admin
with the admin user.
b) On the System Status page, verify that all nodes are in a Running state and their status is Online.
c) Navigate to the Cloud Proxies page and verify that the Health Status for each cloud proxy is Healthy.
2. Verify the VCF Operations integration adapters state.
a) Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user
https://<vcf-operations-primary-node-fqdn>/
assigned the Administrator role.
b) Navigate to Administration > Integrations.
c) Expand each integration and ensure that its status is OK.

Extract Services Runtime Configuration from the Services Runtime Backup for VCF Instance Backup
and Restore
Using the VCF services runtime backup, you extract the package deployment configuration.
• OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later must be available on your Linux machine that you use to access the environment.
• Download and extract the scripts from Broadcom knowledge base article 443506 to the machine you use to access
your VMware Cloud Foundation platform.
• A linux workstation with access to the SFTP server.
The VCF services runtime package deployment configuration is captured as part of the VCF management services
backup. You use this extracted data in a later step.

operation.
2. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sftpHost='192.168.1.2'

vsp/5d29166a-780d-4481-81df-59cc3cefb697/9.1.1.0.25714471/2026-09-01T14-53-53Z/2026-09-01T14-53-53Z.base.tgz'

--sftp-password ${sftpPassword} \

--output-dir "./tmp/backup-yaml"

Before you can deploy a new VCF management services instance to restore to, you must delete the existing VCF

CAUTION:

1. For VCF 9.1.1 and later, follow these steps:

b) Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--data "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
c) Export the VCF services runtime cluster of type MANAGEMENT details to the

file for later use by running the following command.
details.json

| jq '.elements[] | select(.type == "MANAGEMENT")' \
| tee vcfms-vsp-cluster-details.json
d) Retrieve the ID of the VCF services runtime cluster of type MANAGEMENT by running the following command.

running the following command.
curl -k -s -X DELETE "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters/${vspManagementId}" \

2. For VCF 9.1.0, follow these steps:

b) Switch to the root user.
su -
c) Connect to the Postgres database by running the following command.
psql -U postgres -h localhost -d platform;
d) Query the vsp_cluster table and record the vsp_cluster_id of the entry with type MANAGEMENT by running the
following command.

delete from vsp_cluster where type='MANAGEMENT';

admin';
Redeploy VCF Management Services for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
You deploy a new VCF management services instance using the SDDC Manager API.
• VCF management services is in a failed state and cannot be restored using the in place procedure.
• VCF management services VMs must no longer exist in vCenter.
• You must have at least one recent backup of the component that you are restoring.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF management services, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– VCF Operations
– SDDC Manager
• VCF Installer with the correct binary versions for the release you are running for VCF services runtime, Fleet lifecycle,
Software depot, SDDC lifecycle, Salt master, Salt RaaS, and Identity broker.
Restore the specific components according to your scenario.

Apply SFTP Settings on VCF Management Services for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To enable the restore from SFTP backup, you apply the SFTP server settings on the newly deployed VCF management
services instance.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps. The can be obtained
vspId
from the output of the Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
procedure.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
export sftpHost='192.168.1.2'
export sftpPort='22'
export sftpDirectory='/media/backups/'
export sftpUsername='svc-vcf-bck'
export sftpPassword='***************'
export sftpEncryptionPassphrase='***************'
2. Extract the from the file generated from the Retrieve Component Details
vspId components-ids-versions.json
from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore procedure.
vspId=$(jq -r '.vsp[].id' component-ids-versions.json | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Retrieve the fingerprint of the SFTP server by running the following command.
sftpFingerprint=$(ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 -p $sftpPort $sftpHost 2>/dev/null | ssh-keygen -lf - | awk
'{print $2}' | tee /dev/tty )

sftp-config-payload.json
cat << EOF | tee sftp-config-payload.json
{
"spec": {
"configuration": {
"backups": {
"destination": "sftp",
"encryptionPassphrase": "${sftpEncryptionPassphrase}",
"storage": {
"sftp": {
"directory": "${sftpDirectory}",
"host": "${sftpHost}",
"port": "${sftpPort}",
"username": "${sftpUsername}",
"password": "${sftpPassword}",

}
}
}

},

6. Apply the SFTP server settings but running the following command.
taskId=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/components/${vspId}?action=apply" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @sftp-config-payload.json \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
7. Monitor the task by running the following command.
while true; do
# Capture the filtered JSON output
output=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${taskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq '{id: .id, stages: .stages, status: .status}')
# Extract just the raw status string for evaluation
status=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.status')
# Check if the status matches our looping conditions
if [[ "$status" == "Pending" || "$status" == "Running" ]]; then
echo "Current status is '$status'. Checking again in 60 seconds..."
sleep 60
else
# Stop the loop and print the final JSON payload
echo "Task completed with status: '$status'."
echo "$output"
break
fi
done

Trust VCF Installer Certificate on VCF Management Services for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To enable the restore from backup, you trust the VCF Installer certificate on the newly deployed VCF management
services instance. This enables VCF management services to download binaries from the VCF Installer during the restore
process.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
export vcfInstallerFqdn='sfo-ins01.sfo.rainpole.io'
2. Retrieve the VCF Installer certificate details by running the following command.
vcfInstallerCertData=$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "${vcfInstallerFqdn}:443" 2>/dev/null | openssl
x509 -outform pem | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Trust the VCF Installer certificate by running the following command.
taskId=$(jq -n --arg cert "$vcfInstallerCertData" '{cert: $cert}' | \
curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/trusted-certificates?action=add" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @- | jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
5. Monitor the task by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${taskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq

Before you restore VCF management services components, which include VCF services runtime, Software depot, Fleet

RaaS, Identity broker and Real-Time Metrics by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r '
["TYPE", "VERSION", "NAME", "AGE"],
Broadcom 4420

(
["vsp", "vcf-fleet-lcm", "vcf-fleet-depot", "vcf-sddc-lcm", "salt", "salt-raas", "vidb", "vcfms-
metrics-store", "vcf-obs-data-platform"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") |
fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago") ]
)
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'

Restore VCF management services components, which include VCF services runtime, Software depot, Fleet lifecycle,

servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \

Apply Services Runtime Configuration of VCF Management Services for VCF Instance Backup and
Restore
To ensure the worker nodes are the correct size, you apply the kubernetes package deployment from the backup.
1. Discover the VCF management services control plane node.
a) Open an SSH connection to the VCF services runtime, connect using the vmware-system-user user.
b) Switch the user to administrative access.
sudo su
a) Find the address of the control plane node.
EXTERNAL-IP
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/node-agent.conf
kubectl get nodes -o wide
2. Copy all yaml files from Extract Services Runtime Configuration from the Services Runtime Backup for VCF Instance
Backup and Restore to the control plane node.
3. Open an SSH connection to control plane node, connect using the vmware-system-user user.
4. Switch the user to administrative access.
sudo su
5. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
export YAML_PATH='./'
export WORKER_SIZE=$(awk '/worker:/{f=1} f && /size:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-platform.yaml)
export MACHINE_TYPE=$(awk '/worker:/{f=1} f && /machineType:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-
platform.yaml)
export PROFILE=$(awk '/profiles:/{f=1} f && /name:/{print $2; exit}' $YAML_PATH/vmsp-platform.yaml)
6. Apply the services runtime configuration by running the following command.
kubectl patch packagedeployment vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform \
--type=merge \
-p "$(jq -n \
--arg s "$WORKER_SIZE" \
--arg m "$MACHINE_TYPE" \
--arg p "$PROFILE" \
'{
"spec": {
"values": {
"cluster": {
"worker": {
"size": $s,
"machineType": $m
}
},
"profiles": {
"name": $p
}
}
}

}')"

# Wait for this message
packagedeployment.releases.vmsp.vmware.com/vmsp-platform condition met

completed.
Retrieve a List of Backups for Log Management
If your VMware Cloud Foundation platform included log management as an additional deployed component retrieve a list
of backups for log management to perform the restore.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps. The can be obtained
vspId
from the output of the Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
procedure.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Extract the vspId from the file generated from the Retrieve Component Details
components-ids-versions.json
from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore procedure.
vspId=$(jq -r '.vsp[0].id' component-ids-versions.json | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Retrieve a list of available log management backups from the VCF services runtime by running the following
command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r --arg VSP_ID "$vspId" '
["TYPE", "VERSION", "NAME", "AGE"],
(
["ops-logs"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
# Filter based on the VSP_ID variable passed from the shell
| select(.path | contains("/vcf/backups/" + $VSP_ID))
| (
Broadcom 4424

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") |
fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago") ]
)
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
5. Identity the of the backup job and replace the values in the sample code.
NAME
export backupName='2026-09-01T15-28-34Z'
6. Generate the file by running the following command.
logs-restore-payload.json
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq --arg target "${backupName}" '{
"components": [
.backups[]
| select(.component.type == "ops-logs" and .name == $target)
| {
"point": .name,
"path": .path
}
]
}' | tee logs-restore-payload.json
Restore Log Management for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
After you restore the core VCF management services components, you can restore the log management component if
you have it in your environment.
• Download the required binaries.
• Ensure any NFS mount points used by Log Management are available prior to performing the restore.
Note:
If the NFS mount point is unavailable during restore, it can be remediated later, then click Apply Changes on the
Log management External Storage page to resume use. Alternatively, if the NFS is no longer needed, it can be
removed, a new one added, and click Apply Changes.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime instance by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
3. Perform the restore operation of log management using the file generated in the
logs-restore-payload.json
Retrieve a List of Backups for Log Management procedure by running the following command.
restoreTaskId=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups?action=restore" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
Broadcom 4425

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @logs-restore-payload.json \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Monitor the restore task of log management by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${restoreTaskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
Important:
For VCF 9.1.0 only, after the log management restore operation completes, you must run a script to reconcile the
log management database state. See Broadcom knowledge base article 436904.
Update Log Management State
After the restore operation of log management is complete, you must perform steps to finalize the restore.
1. For VCF 9.1.1 do the following:
a) Log in to VCF Operations as a user with the Administrator role.
b) Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management > Components.
c) Click Log management.
d) From the Actions menu, click Stop Service.
e) Monitor the Stop Service task until it completes and then click Start Service.
f) Monitor the Start Service task until it completes.
2. If the logs UI is not loading in the VCF Operations UI after DR failover, we need to follow these steps:
a) Run following script to delete the Log Management component from Ops and re-registering it.
export KUBECONFIG=<path-to-kubeconfig-for VCF Services Runtime>
./update_registration_in_ops.sh --ops-fqdn "flt-ops01a.rainpole.io" --component-fqdn "flt-
logs01.rainpole.io" --ops-username "admin"
b) If step 2a fails, retry the task by visiting https://<ops-fqdn>/vcf-operations/ui/operate/administration/control-
panel/management-tasks/lcm/tasks and clicking Retry on the failed task. Select the Skip option so that
validations are skipped.
c) After successful deletion of the Log Management component from Ops, navigate to Build > Lifecycle > Tasks to
verify status of the Refresh component Log management task. If that task failed, click Retry.
3. For VCF 9.1.0 do the following:
a) Follow the steps in Broadcom knowledge base article 436904.

Reinstall Telemetry Component When No Scheduled Backup Exists
When no scheduled backup exists, you must reinstall the telemetry component with the same identity.
CAUTION:
This procedure should only be used when no scheduled backup of the telemetry component exists.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Retrieve an access token from theservices runtime instance by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
3. Stage the telemetry binary.
curl "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/components?action=stage" -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer
$servicesRuntimeToken" -k -s -d "{
{
\"repository\": { \"url\": \"<uri>\" },
\"componentNamespace\": \"telemetry\"
}
Broadcom 4428

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

$servicesRuntimeToken" -k -s -d "{
\"type\": \"telemetry-acceptor\",
\"version\": \"${componentVersion}\",
\"id\": \"${componentId}\",
\"spec\": {
\"configuration\": {
\"size\": \"small\"
}
}
}"
VCF Automation Restore Tasks for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Perform these tasks related to restoring VCF Automation.
Prepare to Restore VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Before you can deploy a new VCF Automation instance to restore to, you must delete the existing VCF Automation entry
in the SDDC Manager database.
CAUTION:
This procedure should not be used to completely delete a deployed component. To fully delete day 2 deployed
components on VCF management services refer to Broadcom knowledge base article 441333.
1. For VCF 9.1.1 and newer, follow these steps:
a) Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export sddcManagerFqdn='sfo-vcf01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export sddcManagerUsername='admin@local'
export sddcManagerPassword='***************'
b) Retrieve an access token from the SDDC Manager instance by running the following command.
sddcManagerToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/tokens" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--data "{\"username\":\"${sddcManagerUsername}\", \"password\":\"${sddcManagerPassword}\"}" \
| jq -r '.accessToken' | tee /dev/tty )
c) Export the VCF services runtime cluster of type CONSUMPTION details to the
vcfa-vsp-cluster-
file for later use by running the following command.
details.json
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq '.elements[] | select(.type == "CONSUMPTION")' \
| tee vcfa-vsp-cluster-details.json
d) Retrieve the ID of the VCF services runtime cluster of type CONSUMPTION by running the following command.
vcfaVspManagementId=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r '.elements[] | select(.type == "CONSUMPTION") | .id' | tee /dev/tty )
Broadcom 4429

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
e) Delete the VCF services runtime cluster of type CONSUMPTION, using the id obtained in the previous step by
running the following command.
curl -k -s -X DELETE "https://${sddcManagerFqdn}/v1/vsp-clusters/${vcfaVspManagementId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${sddcManagerToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
2. For VCF 9.1.0, follow these steps:
a) Open an SSH connection to the SDDC Manger appliance as the vcf user and switch to the root user.
b) Connect to the Postgres database.
psql -U postgres -h localhost -d platform;
a) Query the vsp_clusters table and record the vsp_cluster_id of the entry with type CONSUMPTION.
select * from vsp_cluster;
a) Delete the CONSUMPTION entry.
delete from vsp_cluster where type='CONSUMPTION';
a) Delete the corresponding credential.
delete from credential where username='vsp/<CONSUMPTION-vsp_cluster_id>/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
For Example
delete from credential where username='vsp/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/svc-sddc-manager-
admin';

You deploy a new VCF Automation services runtime instance using the SDDC Manager API.
• VCF Automation is in a failed state and cannot be restored using the in place procedure.
• VCF Automation VMs must no longer exist in vCenter.
• You must have at least one recent backup of VCF Automation.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF Automation, the following components must be available:
– vCenter
– VCF Operations
– SDDC Manager
• The VCF Automation binary must be available in the fleet software depot.
