Apply SFTP Settings on VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To enable the restore from SFTP backup, you apply the SFTP server settings on the newly deployed VCF Automation
instance.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps. The can be obtained
vspId
from the output of the Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
procedure.

export vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export vcfaSservicesRuntimePassword='***************'
export sftpHost='192.168.1.2'
export sftpPort='22'
export sftpDirectory='/media/backups/'
export sftpUsername='svc-vcf-bck'
export sftpPassword='***************'
export sftpEncryptionPassphrase='***************'
2. Extract the vspId from the file generated from the Retrieve Component Details
components-ids-versions.json
from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore procedure.
vspId=$(jq -r '.vcfa.vspComponentUuid' component-ids-versions.json | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
vcfaServicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \

--data-urlencode "password=${vcfaSservicesRuntimePassword}" \

4. Retrieve the fingerprint of the SFTP server by running the following command.
sftpFingerprint=$(ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 -p $sftpPort $sftpHost 2>/dev/null | ssh-keygen -lf - | awk
'{print $2}' | tee /dev/tty )
5. Generate the file by running the following command.
sftp-config-payload.json

{
"spec": {

"destination": "sftp",
"encryptionPassphrase": "${sftpEncryptionPassphrase}",
"storage": {

"host": "${sftpHost}",
"port": "${sftpPort}",
"username": "${sftpUsername}",
"password": "${sftpPassword}",
"fingerprint": "${sftpFingerprint}"
}
}
}
}
},
"options": {}

6. Apply the SFTP server settings but running the following command.
taskId=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/components/${vspId}?action=apply" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @sftp-config-payload.json \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
7. Monitor the task by running the following command.
while true; do
# Capture the filtered JSON output
output=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${taskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq '{id: .id, stages: .stages, status: .status}')
# Extract just the raw status string for evaluation
status=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.status')
# Check if the status matches our looping conditions
if [[ "$status" == "Pending" || "$status" == "Running" ]]; then
echo "Current status is '$status'. Checking again in 60 seconds..."
sleep 60

else
# Stop the loop and print the final JSON payload
echo "Task completed with status: '$status'."
echo "$output"
break
fi
done
Trust VCF Installer Certificate on VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To enable the restore from backup, you trust the VCF Installer certificate on the newly deployed VCF Automation instance.
This enables VCF Automation to download binaries from the VCF Installer during the restore process.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export vcfaServicesRuntimePassword='***************'
export vcfInstallerFqdn='sfo-ins01.sfo.rainpole.io'
2. Retrieve the VCF Installer certificate details by running the following command.
vcfInstallerCertData=$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "${vcfInstallerFqdn}:443" 2>/dev/null | openssl
x509 -outform pem | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF Automation by running the following command.
vcfaServicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${vcfaServicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Trust the VCF Installer certificate by running the following command.
taskId=$(jq -n --arg cert "$vcfInstallerCertData" '{cert: $cert}' | \
curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/trusted-certificates?action=add" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @- | jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
5. Monitor the task by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${taskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq
Retrieve a List of Backups for VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Before you restore VCF Automation, you retrieve a list of available backups.
Note:
It is recommended to use backups taken by using a backup schedule. On-demand backups will not have a
corresponding vsp backup. If you have a newer on-demand backup of VCF Automation, use the most recent
available vsp backup along with it.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
Broadcom 4434

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
export vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export vcfaServicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Retrieve an access token from the VCF Automation by running the following command.
vcfaServicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${vcfaServicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve list of backups for VCF Automation by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r '
["TYPE", "VERSION", "NAME", "AGE"],
(
["vsp", "vcfa", "vcd-migrator"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") |
fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago") ]
)
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
4. Identity the of the backup job and replace the values in the sample code.
NAME
export vspBackupName='2026-09-01T14-54-30Z'
export vcfaBackupName='2026-09-01T14-54-40Z'
5. Generate the file by running the following command.
vcfa-restore-payload.json
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq \
--arg vsp "${vspBackupName}" \
--arg vcfa "${vcfaBackupName}" \
'{
"components": [
.backups[]
| select(
(.component.type == "vsp" and .name == $vsp) or
(.component.type == "vcfa" and .name == $vcfa)
)
| {
"point": .name,
"path": .path
}
]
Broadcom 4435

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
}' | tee vcfa-restore-payload.json
Restore VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
Restore VCF Automation from a file-based backup.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export vcfaServicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Retrieve an access token from the VCF Automation by running the following command.
vcfaServicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${vcfaServicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${vcfaServicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
3. Perform the restore operation of VCF Automation using the file generated in the
vcfa-restore-payload.json
Retrieve a List of Backups for VCF Automation for VCF Instance Backup and Restoreprocedure by running the
following command.
restoreTaskId=$(curl -k -X POST "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups?action=restore"
\
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data @vcfa-restore-payload.json \
| jq -r '.id' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Monitor the restore task of VCF Automation by running the following command.
while true; do
# Capture the filtered JSON output
output=$(curl -k -s -X GET "https://${vcfaServicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/tasks/${restoreTaskId}" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${vcfaServicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq '{id: .id, stages: .stages, status: .status, resource: .resource}')
# Extract just the raw status string for evaluation
status=$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.status')
# Check if the status matches the looping conditions
if [[ "$status" == "Pending" || "$status" == "Running" ]]; then
echo "Current status is '$status'. Checking again in 120 seconds..."
sleep 120
else
# Stop the loop and print the final JSON payload
echo "Task completed with status: '$status'."
echo "$output"
break
fi
done

vSphere Supervisor Restore Tasks
Tasks related to the restore of vSphere Supervisor.
Mount the NFS Share for the VKr Content Library for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
If you are using an NFS datastore for the content library with the VMware vSphere Kubernetes releases (VKrs), mount the
relevant NFS share.
Procedure
1. Log into vCenter for the workload domain as a user with the administrator role.
2. In the Hosts and Clusters inventory, right- click the vSphere cluster and select Storage > New Datastore.
3. On the Type page, select NFS and click Next.
4. On the NFS version page, select your NFS version and click Next.
5. On the Name and configuration page, enter the datastore details and click Next.
6. On the Hosts accessibility page, select all hosts in the cluster and click Next.
7. On the Ready to complete page, review the settings and click Finish.
Recreate the Content Library folder on the rebuilt vSAN Datatore
After rebuilding a vSAN Datastore, you must create the folder for any dependent Content Libraries
Create vSAN Folder
1. Log into vCenter for the workload domain as a user with the administrator role
2. In the Content Libraries inventory, select the VKr Content Library and note the moRef of the library in your browser
address bar using he following example for reference
https://<vcenter_fqdn>/ui/app/content-libraries/cl/
urn:vapi:com.vmware.content.Library:<content_library_moref:<vcenter_moref>/summary
3. In the Datastores inventory, select the rebuilt datastore.
4. Select the Files tab.
5. Click New Folder.
6. Enter the name of the folder in the format contentlib-<content_library_moref>
Update the VKr Content Library Datastore Mapping for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
The NFS datastore backing the vSphere content library has a new moref-id. You update the vCenter Content Library
Datastore Mapping in the vCenter database to reflect the change.
Procedure
1. Log in to the vCenter appliance as root over SSH or directly to appliance console.
2. Type shell to switch to the BASH Shell.
3. Connect to the VCDB by running this command.
Broadcom 4437

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
/opt/vmware/vpostgres/current/bin/psql -d VCDB -U postgres
4. Find the id of your content library.
select id from cl_library where name='content-library-name';
5. Find the id of the old datastore that corresponds to the content library id from the previous step.
select * from cl_library_storage;
6. Find the storageuri to be updated with the new datastore details.
select * from cl_storage;
7. Get the storageuri for the new NFS datastore.
a. In a browser, log into the vCenter server where the new NFS datastore is located.
b. Navigate to Inventory > Storage and click on the datastore.
c. In the URL select and copy the following string.
Datastore:datastore-4682698:c7481195-b0a1-4c74-a67f-c5bce8b2145d
8. Update the datastore mapping in the cl_storage table.
update from cl_storage SET storageuri='storageuri-from-step-7' where id='storage-id-from-step-5';
9. Reboot the vCenter server.

Restore the vSphere Supervisor Control Plane for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
You can restore the Supervisors control pane in vCenter from the backup files of the vCenter system itself.
Configure recording the Supervisor state from the vCenter management interface file-based backups.
Restoring the Supervisor control plane in vCenter and restoring the state of vCenter are two different workflows. Restoring
vCenter does not lead to restoring the Supervisor control plane.
1. In the vSphere Client, go to Supervisor Management.
2. Select Supervisors, select the Supervisor to be restored, and click Restore.
3. Enter the backup details.
Option Description
vCenter Select the vCenter system that manages the Supervisor.
Backup selection • Select Browse backup server folder to upload the files that are stored in the root
folder of the backup file server configured with this vCenter system.
• Select Single backup location to upload a particular backup file, and then enter the
URL to that backup file.
• Select Use backup location and user name from vCenter backup schedule
to populate the root folder location and user name for the backup location that are
configured with vCenter.
Location Enter the location of the backup root folder.
Username Enter the user name to access the backups
Password Enter the password for that user name.
Broadcom 4438

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Click Next.
5. Select a backup file to restore from and click Next to start the download of the backup file.
6. Select the Supervisor to restore and click Next.
7. Review the settings and click Finish.
The Supervisor goes back to configuring state and all the control plane VMs are deleted and re-deployed with the data
from the backup file. You can monitor the process by clicking view in the Config Status column.

• Restore Stateless and Stateful Workloads on a vSphere Supervisor Cluster. See Backing Up and Restoring VKS
Cluster Workloads.
• Restore VM Service VMs on a vSphere Supervisor cluster. See Backing Up and Restoring VM Service VMs in vSphere
Supervisor.
Remediate vSphere Supervisor Nodes for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
To ensure the vSphere Supervisor spherelet configuration and certificate are pushed to each ESX host, you must remove
and add again each host as a Supervisor node.
1. Retrieve the Supervisor root password from vCenter.
a) Open an SSH connection to vCenter as the root user.
b) Run the following command.
/usr/lib/vmware-wcp/decryptK8Pwd.py
2. Using the root password from the previous step, open an SSH connection to the Supervisor.
3. List the Supervisor nodes that are in a Not Ready state by running the following command.
kubectl get nodes
4. Check to see if the supervisor-admin has the necessary priviledges.
kubectl auth can-i delete nodes
5. If the result is No, then temporarily grant permissions
kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf create clusterrolebinding supervisor-admin-cluster-admin \
--clusterrole=cluster-admin \
--user=supervisor-admin
6. For each ESX host that is in Not Ready state
a) In the vSphere Client, place the host in the list into maintenance mode.
b) In the SSH session to the Supervisor, run the following command.
kubectl delete node <esx-fqdn>
c) Return to the vSphere Client and exit the host from maintenance mode.
7. If you had to grant temporary permissions to delete the nodes, then revoke the permission
kubectl --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf delete clusterrolebinding supervisor-admin-cluster-admin
Recreate the NSX NCP Pods for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
If the NSX NCP Pods are in a crashed state after the Supervisor restore, you must restore them back to running state.
Procedure
1. Retrieve the Supervisor root password from vCenter.
a. Open an SSH connection to vCenter as the root user.
b. Run the following command.
/usr/lib/vmware-wcp/decryptK8Pwd.py
Broadcom 4439

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Using the root password from the previous step, open an SSH connection to the Supervisor.
3. List the NSX-NCP Pod by running the following command.
kubectl get pods -n vmware-system-nsx | grep nsx-ncp
4. If a pod is in a Not Ready state, then restart it NSX-NCP Pod by deleting it.
When you delete an NSX-NCP Pod, it is automatically recreated.
kubectl delete pod <nsx-ncp pod name> -n vmware-system-nsx
5. After the NSX-NCP Pod is recreated, confirm it is now in a state:
Running
kubectl get pods -n vmware-system-nsx | grep nsx-ncp
6. Repeat these steps for all NSX-NCP Pods.

VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
This VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery guide provides the ability to handle a failure of the VCF Instance or a site and recover
VCF fleet components in another location within the same VCF fleet, where that location is typically outside metro radius.
Important:
Use this VCF fleet disaster recovery process together with the design elements of the VCF Fleet Disaster
Recovery blueprint. The VCF fleet disaster recovery process outlines the workflow to recover critical VCF
fleet components on another VCF Instance within the same fleet, covering both failover and failback of these
components.
Table 1168: Plans in this Guide
The VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery guide includes structured, runbook-style plans featuring PowerShell cmdlets, manual
task links, and supporting documentation for key steps.
Plan Description
Protection and Recovery Implementation Plan for VCF Fleet Deployment and configuration guidance for protection and
Disaster Recovery recovery, including setting up recovery plans and configuring
failover for VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks.
Failover Plan for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery Step-by-step guidance to failover VCF fleet level components to
another VCF Instance or site.
Failback Plan for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery Step-by-step guidance to fail back VCF fleet level components to
another VCF Instance or site.

where available.

Configuration for Recovered
Components
Disaster Recovery Task Library
A hierarchy of tasks that are associated with fleet disaster recovery, sorted by component, or functional area.
CAUTION:
The order in which tasks are listed in the library is not necessarily the order in which they should be performed.
Refer to the relevant restore plan to see the sequence of tasks appropriate to the elements you are restoring.
Prerequisites for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
Before you implement the VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery guidance, your environment must meet certain requirements for
networking and component deployments.
When you prepare your environment for disaster recovery, you must determine which of your two VCF Instances functions
as the protected site and which one as the recovery site.
• The protected site hosts the business-critical SDDC services.
• The recovery site is an alternative location to which these applications migrate to if a disaster occurs.
In this guide, the protected site is referred to as the protected VCF Instance and the recovery site is referred to as the
recovery VCF Instance.
Prerequisites
To complete the implementation of Fleet Disaster Recovery for VMware Cloud Foundation, verify that your system fulfills
the following prerequisites.
Broadcom 4456

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Table 1170: Prerequisites for Implementation of Fleet Disaster Recovery for VMware Cloud Foundation
Category Prerequisite
Environment • Verify that your VCF version is 9.1.x on the protected and recovery sites.
• Verify that you have sufficient resources on the recovery site to run the recovered management
components.
• Verify that the chosen recovery site does not have a running instance of any of the components
you plan to recover, such as Identity broker or software depot.
Domain Name Service • Verify that the required DNS entries are created in the DNS server for the associated forward
and reverse zones.
• Verify that all components to be failed over have the DNS servers from the protected and
recovery sites configured.
• Reserve IP addresses in the DNS server for the fleet components that will be failed over.
Network • Verify that you have satisfied the IP mobility requirements between VCF Instances.
• Verify that your VCF Instances have connectivity between each other and that the connection
supports jumbo frames and Layer 3 routing.
• Verify that all uplinks, port channels, and VLANs that carry overlay and Protection and Recovery
traffic are configured for jumbo frames.
• Verify that your environment supports the maximum supported latency between VCF instances.
• Verify that sufficient bandwidth is available for replication traffic. See the Protection and Recovery
Calculator.
Software • Download the Protection and Recovery .ova image and mount it on the machine that you use
to access the vSphere Client.
License • Verify that you have obtained a Protection and Recovery license with a quantity that fulfills the
requirements of your design.
Implementation Tasks for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
Library of tasks used to implement VCF fleet disaster recovery.
Deploy Protection and Recovery for Fleet Disaster Recovery for VMware Cloud Foundation
To manage virtual machine replication, protection, and recovery, deploy the protection and recovery appliance in the
protected and recovery instances.
For the protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance procedure, use the VMware Cloud Foundation Planning and
Preparation Workbook.
Procedure
1. Log in to the management domain vCenter at in the protected
https://<management_vcenter_fqdn>/ui
instance as administrator@vsphere.local.
2. In the Hosts and clusters inventory, expand the management domain vCenter tree and expand the management
domain data center.
3. Deploy the new protection and recovery appliance.
a. Right-click the default management cluster and select Deploy OVF template.
b. On the Select an OVF template page, select Local file, click Upload files, and click Next.
Protection-and-recovery-9.1.x.0.XXXXXXXX.ova
c. On the Select a name and folder page, in the Virtual machine name text box, enter a virtual machine name
according to your VMware Cloud Foundation Planning and Preparation Workbook, and click Next.
d. On the Select a compute resource page, select the default management cluster and click Next.
e. On the Review details page, click Next.
Broadcom 4457

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
f. On the License agreements page, accept the license agreement and click Next.
g. On the Select storage page, select the management domain vSAN datastore and click Next.
h. On the Select networks page, select the management network and click Next.
i. On the Customize template page, configure the following settings and configure the remaining settings according
to your VMware Cloud Foundation Planning and Preparation Workbook, and click Next.

Fleet Component Recovery Tasks
Broadcom 4468

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Modify DNS Entries for Fleet Component VIPs Before Recovery
Before you can recover VCF Management Services fleet components to a new instance you must update the DNS entry
for each fleet component VIP to use an IP from the recovery site VCF Management Services VLAN.
To recover the VCF Management Services fleet components, you must maintain their VIP FQDNs. This process is
required when the source and target VCF Management Services instances are using different VLAN/subnets to allow the
recovery of the fleet components using different IPs.
Modify DNS for the following FQDNs to point to a free IP in the same VLAN/subnet that the VCF Management Services
instance on the recovery site is using.
• Fleet Components FQDN
• Identity Broker FQDN
• Log Management FQDN
• VCF Automation FQDN
• VCF Automation services runtime FQDN
Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations
Before you can restore the fleet components across sites, you must retrieve the component IDs from VCF Operations.
You use the VCF Operations API to retrieve the component IDs and versions.
1. Retrieve a VCF Operations access token.
# VCF_OPS_FQDN should be the VCF Operations master node FQDN
# VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD should be the VCF Operations local admin password
export VCF_OPS_FQDN='flt-ops01a.rainpole.io'
export VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD='****************'
OPS_TOKEN=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://$VCF_OPS_FQDN/suite-api/api/auth/token/acquire" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d "{
\"username\": \"admin\",
\"password\": \"$VCF_OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\",
\"authSource\": \"local\"
}" | jq -r .token)
2. Retrieve a list of component IDs and versions from VCF Operations and save them for later use.
curl -k -s -X GET \
"https://${VCF_OPS_FQDN}/suite-api/internal/components?_no_links=true" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H 'X-Ops-API-use-unsupported: true' \
-H "Authorization: OpsToken ${OPS_TOKEN}" \
| jq '
.components as $all
| ( $all
| map(
select(
(.componentType | ascii_upcase) as $t

Extract Fleet VIP Address Configuration from the Source Services Runtime Backup
Using the services runtime backup from the source site, you extract the fleet component configuration.
• OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later must be available on your Linux machine that you use to access the environment.
• Download and extract the scripts from Broadcom knowledge base article 443506 to the machine you use to access
your VCF environment.
• A linux workstation with access to the SFTP server
The fleet component configuration is captured as part of the VCF management services runtime backup. You use this
extracted data in a later step.
1. Browse the SFTP server and locate the VCF management services runtime backup that you plan to use for the restore
operation.

Scale the Recovery Site VCF Management Services Instance for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
To support restoring components to the recovery site, the target VCF Management Services instance must be the same
size profile. You use this process to scale it up if necessary.
This task is only required if the target VCF Management Services instance is smaller than the protected site instance.
You use the YAML files that are generated in Extract Fleet VIP Address Configuration from the Source Services Runtime
Backup
1. Scale the target cluster.
a) On a workstation with access to the KUBECONFIG for the recovery VCF Management Services instance and the
extracted backup YAML files, run the following commands
export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig
export WORKER_SIZE=$(awk '/worker:/{f=1} f && /size:/{print $2; exit}' ./<path-to-yaml-files>/vmsp-
platform.yaml)
export PROFILE=$(awk '/profiles:/{f=1} f && /name:/{print $2; exit}' ./<path-to-yaml-files>/vmsp-
platform.yaml)
kubectl patch packagedeployment vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform \
--type=merge \
-p "$(jq -n --arg s "$WORKER_SIZE" --arg p "$PROFILE" '
Broadcom 4472

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
{
"spec": {
"values": {
"cluster": {
"worker": {
"size": $s
}
},
"profiles": {
"name": $p
}
}
}
}')"
2. Monitor the task.
kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Successful packagedeployment/vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform
--timeout=2h
# Wait for this message
packagedeployment.releases.vmsp.vmware.com/vmsp-platform condition met
kubectl get packagedeployment vmsp-platform -n vmsp-platform -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'
# Wait for this message
Successful
The worker nodes will be resized to match the size from the protected site when the backup was taken. Do not proceed
until this step has completed.
Disable Log Management Integration on Recovery VCF Management Services Instance
You temporarily disable log management integration on the recovery site VCF Management Services Instance as log
management is unavailable until it is restored.
Disable logging on the target VCF Management Services instance
Flush log buffer on fluentd on the target VCF Management Services instance
Scale down & up fluentd pod
1. Disable logging on the target VCF Management Services instance.
a) Retrieve a token from the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site.
export VCFMS_SR='lax-sr01.lax.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
b) Query the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site for a list of existing components.
curl -ks "https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/components" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" | jq '.components[] | {type, id, status}'
c) Disable logging on the target VCF Management Services instance.
# VSP_COMP_ID should be the id for the VSP component from the previous step

-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" \

}

},

"precheck": true,

# Poll task until complete
curl -ks "https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/tasks/${TASK_ID}" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" | jq

a) SSH to the control plane node of the target VCF Management Services instance and run the following:

kubectl -n vmsp-platform rollout status sts/logging-operator-fluentd

delete

Apply Fleet VIP on Recovery VCF Management Services Instance
You apply the fleet component VIP configuration you extracted form the backup in an earlier step.
Broadcom 4474

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You must have access to the KUBECONFIG for the recovery VCF Management Services instance. The KUBECONFIG is
located on the control plane node at /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf.
Applying the configuration from the extracted backup configures the fleet FQDN and associated certificates and secrets
on the recovery VCF Management Services instance.
1. Apply the configuration from the backup.
a) On a workstation with access to the KUBECONFIG for the recovery VCF Management Services instance and the
extracted backup YAML files, run the following commands
export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig
kubectl apply -f ./<path-to-yaml-files>/ingress-fleet-tls.yaml
kubectl apply -f ./<path-to-yaml-files>/ingress-fleet-tls-ndc.yaml
2. Retrieve a token from the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site.
export VCFMS_SR='lax-sr01.lax.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
3. Apply Fleet FQDN and TLS Certificates to the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site.
# VSP_COMP_ID should be the id for the recovery site VSP component from the previous step
# FLEET_FQDN should be the existing fleet components FQDN from the primary site
# FLEET_VIP should be the new IP that was assigned in DNS to the existing fleet FQDN
export VSP_COMP_ID='e319236e-867e-4779-9270-4921bddf4f1f'
export FLEET_FQDN='flt-fc01.rainpole.io'
export FLEET_VIP='10.21.99.20'

"https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/components/${VSP_COMP_ID}?action=apply" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
"spec": {
"configuration": {
"ingress": {
"fleet": {
"fqdn": "'$FLEET_FQDN'",
"vips": {
"ipv4": ["'${FLEET_VIP}'"]
}
}
}
}
},
"options": {
"timeout": "30m"
}
}' | jq -r '.id')

-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" | jq
Retrieve a List of Backups for VCF Management Services Fleet Components
Retrieve list of backups for the VCF Management Services Fleet Components to perform the restore.
You retrieve a list of backup from which to restore from. Once the list is retrieved, it is recommended to browse to the
folder to verify valid backup files exist at each path.
1. Connect to the SFTP server and retrieve a list of backups for the source VCF management services cluster.
SFTP_HOST="192.168.0.2"
SFTP_USER="svc-vcf-bck"
SFTP_PASS="***************"
BASE_DIR="/home/fleet_sftp_user/backup-inst2/vcf/backups/" # parent directory to scan
VSP_ID="9facfd64-c8a0-446e-81fd-ab048c3ad113" # the ID of the source VSP cluster
COMPONENTS=("vcf-fleet-lcm" "vcf-fleet-depot" "salt-raas" "vidb")
curl_ls() {
# Lists a remote dir, returns "<type-char> <name>" per entry, skipping . and ..
local path="$1"
curl -sk --user "${SFTP_USER}:${SFTP_PASS}" "sftp://${SFTP_HOST}${path}/" \
| awk '{print substr($1,1,1), $NF}' \
| grep -Ev ' \.\.?$'
}
for COMPONENT in "${COMPONENTS[@]}"; do
echo "== ${COMPONENT} =="
FOUND=""
# Level 1: VSP_ID/VERSION
while read -r vtype VERSION; do
[[ "$vtype" == d ]] || continue
COMP_PATH="${BASE_DIR}/${VSP_ID}/${VERSION}/${COMPONENT}"
# Level 2: does this COMPONENT exist under this VERSION?
if ! curl -sk --head --user "${SFTP_USER}:${SFTP_PASS}" \
"sftp://${SFTP_HOST}${COMP_PATH}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
continue
fi
# Level 3: COMPONENT/SUB_ID
while read -r stype SUB_ID; do
[[ "$stype" == d ]] || continue
SUB_PATH="${COMP_PATH}/${SUB_ID}"
# Level 4: SUB_ID/VERSION2
while read -r v2type VERSION2; do
[[ "$v2type" == d ]] || continue
V2_PATH="${SUB_PATH}/${VERSION2}"
# Level 5: dated backup folders
while read -r btype BACKUP; do
[[ "$btype" == d ]] || continue
# Prefix with timestamp for chronological sorting
FOUND+="${BACKUP}|${V2_PATH}/${BACKUP}"$'\n'
done < <(curl_ls "$V2_PATH")
done < <(curl_ls "$SUB_PATH")
Broadcom 4476

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
done < <(curl_ls "$COMP_PATH")
done < <(curl_ls "${BASE_DIR}/${VSP_ID}")
# Sort numerically/lexicographically by timestamp (field 1) and grab latest
LATEST_ENTRY=$(printf '%s' "$FOUND" | grep -v '^$' | sort -t'|' -k1,1 | tail -n1)
LATEST="${LATEST_ENTRY#*|}"
if [[ -n "$LATEST" ]]; then
echo "Most recent backup: $(basename "$LATEST")"
echo "Full path: ${LATEST}"
else
echo "No backups found for ${COMPONENT}"
fi
done

To enable the restore of the fleet level components you pre-stage the binaries on the recovery VCF Management Services

Retrieve a List of Backups for Log Management
If your VMware Cloud Foundation platform included log management as an additional deployed component retrieve a list
of backups for log management to perform the restore.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps. The can be obtained
vspId
from the output of the Retrieve Component Details from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore
procedure.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='sfo-sr01.sfo.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Extract the vspId from the file generated from the Retrieve Component Details
components-ids-versions.json
from VCF Operations for VCF Instance Backup and Restore procedure.
vspId=$(jq -r '.vsp[0].id' component-ids-versions.json | tee /dev/tty )
3. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token' | tee /dev/tty )
4. Retrieve a list of available log management backups from the VCF services runtime by running the following
command.
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq -r --arg VSP_ID "$vspId" '
["TYPE", "VERSION", "NAME", "AGE"],
(
["ops-logs"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
Broadcom 4484

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
# Filter based on the VSP_ID variable passed from the shell
| select(.path | contains("/vcf/backups/" + $VSP_ID))
| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") |
fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago") ]
)
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
5. Identity the of the backup job and replace the values in the sample code.
NAME
export backupName='2026-09-01T15-28-34Z'
6. Generate the file by running the following command.
logs-restore-payload.json
curl -k -s -X GET "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/system/backups" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
| jq --arg target "${backupName}" '{
"components": [
.backups[]
| select(.component.type == "ops-logs" and .name == $target)
| {
"point": .name,
"path": .path
}
]
}' | tee logs-restore-payload.json
Restore Log Management
You restore Log Management into the VCF Management Services instance on the recovery site.
• The VCF Management Services instance on the recovery site will be scaled out as appropriate to accommodate the
required number of log management replicas.
• Ensure any NFS mount points used by Log Management are available prior to performing the restore.
Note:
If the NFS mount point is unavailable during restore, it can be remediated later, then click Apply Changes on the
Log management External Storage page to resume use. Alternatively, if the NFS is no longer needed, it can be
removed, a new one added, and click Apply Changes.
1. Retrieve a token from the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site.
export VCFMS_SR='lax-sr01.lax.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')

2. Perform the restore using the JSON payload.
TASK_ID=$(curl -k -X POST "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/system/backups?action=restore" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFMS_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H "Content-type: application/json" \
-d '{
"components": [
{
"path": "/vcf/backups/40e752c7-e940-4a9f-a49c-0f05efa9d915/9.1.1.0.25370367/ops-logs/1769b822-
e28e-455a-bc28-e2711a78d13c/9.1.1.0.25371109/2026-04-27T07-57-25Z/",
"point": "2026-04-27T07-57-25Z"
}
],

}
}
}' | jq -r '.id')
3. Monitor the task until it reports as SUCCEEDED.
curl -ks "https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/tasks/${TASK_ID}" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" | jq

b) Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management > Components.
c) Click Log management.
d) From the Actions menu, click Stop Service.
e) Monitor the Stop Service task until it completes and then click Start Service.
f) Monitor the Start Service task until it completes.

export KUBECONFIG=<path-to-kubeconfig-for VCF Services Runtime>

panel/management-tasks/lcm/tasks and clicking Retry on the failed task. Select the Skip option so that
validations are skipped.

verify status of the Refresh component Log management task. If that task failed, click Retry.
3. For VCF 9.1.0 do the following:
a) Follow the steps in Broadcom knowledge base article 436904.

Log management integration to the VCF Services Runtime in the primary site will fail as that instance is currently

Enable Logging on the Recovery Site VCF Management Services Instance
After a successful restore of log management you enable logging on the VCF Management Services instance on the
recovery site.
1. Enable logging on the target VCF Management Services instance.
a) Retrieve a token from the VCF Management Services instance on the recovery site.
export VCFMS_SR='lax-sr01.lax.rainpole.io'
export VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFMS_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFMS_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFMS_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
b) Query the VCF Management Services cluster on the recovery site for a list of existing components.
curl -ks "https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/components" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" | jq '.components[] | {type, id, status}'
c) Enable logging on the target VCF Management Services instance.
# VSP_COMP_ID should be the id for the VSP component from the previous step
export VSP_COMP_ID='e319236e-867e-4779-9270-4921bddf4f1f'
export VCFMS_SR='lax-sr01.lax.rainpole.io'
export LOG_MANAGEMENT_VIP='flt-logs01.rainpole.io'
TASK_ID=$(curl -ks -X POST "https://${VCFMS_SR}/api/v1/components/${VSP_COMP_ID}?action=apply" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${VCFMS_SR_TOKEN}" \

-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{

}

},

Deploy a VCF Automation Services Runtime Cluster
You deploy a new VCF Automation services runtime instance using the SDDC Manager API.
• VCF Automation should not already exist in the recovery VCF Instance.
• You must have at least one recent backup of VCF Automation.
• Before proceeding with restoration of VCF Automation, the following components must be available:
– VCF Operations
– vCenter
– SDDC Manager
• The VCF Automation binary must be available in the software depot.
1. Retrieve token from SDDC Manager.
# sddcmFQDN should be the recovery site SDDC Manager
export sddcmFQDN='lax-vcf01.lax.rainpole.io'
export ssoAdminPassword='****************'
# generate token
Broadcom 4488

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
token=$(curl -k https://"$sddcmFQDN"/v1/tokens \
-X POST \
-H "Content-type:application/json" \
-d "{\"username\":\"administrator@vsphere.local\", \"password\":\"$ssoAdminPassword\"}" | jq -r
'.accessToken')
2. Deploy a new VCF Automation services runtime instance.
# Domain id should be the management domain id from SDDC Manager
# FQDNs must match the original
# clusterId must match the original
# networkMoId must be from the portgroup you are deploying to

"Authorization: Bearer $token" https://"$sddcmFQDN"/v1/vsp-clusters \

Trust VCF Installer Certificate on VCF Automation
To enable the restore from backup, you trust the VCF installer certificate on the newly deployed VCF Automation instance.
This enables VCF Automation to download binaries from the VCF installer during the restore process.
Trust the VCF Installer certificate on the new VCF Automation instance.
a) Retrieve the VCF Installer certificate.
CERT_DATA=$($echo | openssl s_client -connect sfo-ins01.sfo.rainpole.io:443 2>/dev/null | \
openssl x509 -outform pem)
b) Retrieve a VCF Automation runtime token.
export VCFA_SR='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export VCFA_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFA_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFA_SR_PASSWORD" \
Broadcom 4489

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
| jq -r '.access_token')
c) Trust the VCF installer certificate.
jq -n --arg cert "$CERT_DATA" '{cert: $cert}' | \
curl -k -X POST "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/system/trusted-certificates?action=add" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFA_SR_TOKEN" \
-d @-

Retrieve a List of Backups for VCF Automation
Retrieve list of backups for VCF Automation to perform the restore.
Note:
It is recommended to use backups taken by using a backup schedule. On-demand backups will not have a
corresponding vsp or vcd-migrator backup. If you have a newer on-demand backup of VCF Automation, use the
most recent available vsp and vcd-migrator backup along with it.
1. Retrieve a VCF Automation services runtime token.
export VCFA_SR='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export VCFA_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
VCFA_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFA_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
2. Retrieve list of backups for VCF Automation.
curl -k "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/system/backups" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFA_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' | \
jq -r '
["vsp","vcfa","vcd-migrator"] as $order
| .backups as $all
| $order[] as $current_type
| $all[]
| select(.component.type == $current_type)
| (
(.name | sub("T(?<h>\\d{2})-(?<m>\\d{2})-(?<s>\\d{2})Z"; "T\(.h):\(.m):\(.s)Z") | fromdateiso8601)
) as $timestamp
| ( (now - $timestamp) / 86400 | floor ) as $days_old
| [ $current_type, .component.version, .name, ($days_old | tostring + " days ago"), .path ]
| @tsv' | \
column -t -s $'\t'
3. Create a restore JSON payload using the backup paths from step 2.

{

a5cf-774a6497fa3d/9.1.0.0.25257932/2026-03-23T16-45-31Z",

Stage Binaries for VCF Automation
To enable the restore of VCF Automation you pre-stage the binaries on the recovery services runtime instance.
1. Replace the values in the sample code with your values, these will be used in later steps.
export servicesRuntimeFqdn='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export servicesRuntimeUsername='admin@vsp.local'
export servicesRuntimePassword='***************'
2. Retrieve an access token from the VCF services runtime by running the following command.
servicesRuntimeToken=$(curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode "grant_type=password" \
--data-urlencode "username=${servicesRuntimeUsername}" \
--data-urlencode "password=${servicesRuntimePassword}" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
3. Stage the binary for the vcfa component by running the following command.
curl -k -s -X POST "https://${servicesRuntimeFqdn}/api/v1/components?action=stage" \
--header "Authorization: Bearer ${servicesRuntimeToken}" \
--header "Content-type: application/json" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data-urlencode '{
"type": "vcfa",
"version": "9.1.1.0.25714559",
"repository": {
"url": "https://offline-depot.rainpole.io/PROD/release/depot-manifest-
vcfa-9.1.1.0.25714559.yaml"
},
"options": {
"timeout": "30m"
}
}' \
| jq
Restore VCF Automation for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
Restore VCF Automation from a file-based backup.
1. Retrieve a VCF Automation services runtime token.
export VCFA_SR='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
export VCFA_SR_PASSWORD='****************'
Broadcom 4492

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCFA_SR_TOKEN=$(curl -ks --request POST \
--url "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/identity/token" \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode grant_type=password \
--data-urlencode "username=admin@vsp.local" \
--data-urlencode "password=$VCFA_SR_PASSWORD" \
| jq -r '.access_token')
2. Perform the Restore.
TASK_ID=$(curl -k -X POST "https://$VCFA_SR/api/v1/system/backups?action=restore" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $VCFA_SR_TOKEN" \
-H 'accept: application/json' \
-H "Content-type: application/json" \
-d '{
"components": [
{
"path": "/vcf/backups/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/9.1.1.0.25257932/vsp/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-
a5cf-774a6497fa3d/9.1.1.0.25257932/2026-03-23T16-45-31Z",
"point": "2026-03-23T16-45-31Z"
},
{

"point": "2026-03-23T16-54-12Z"
},
{
"path": "/vcf/backups/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/9.1.1.0.25257932/vcd-
migrator/3d7c01a5-55fb-4b2a-8f0e-c4d24c6d2c03/9.1.1.0.25262128/2026-03-23T16-54-12Z",

Update the VCF Automation VIP Address
After restoring the backup of VCF Automation, you must update it to use the new IP address that is mapped to the VCF
Automation FQDN on the DNS server.
Download and extract the scripts from Broadcom knowledge base article 443506 to the machine you use to access your
VCF environment.
This step is only required if the IP address for the VCF Automation VIP address has been changed on the recovery site.
On your linux workstation, run the following command.
export PLATFORM_URI='https://flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
Broadcom 4493

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
export PASSWORD='****************'
export VCFA_VIP='10.21.99.25'
echo COMPONENT_TYPE='vcfa'
update-component-vip.sh --platform-url $PLATFORM_URI --password $PASSWORD --vips $VCFA_VIP --component-type
$COMPONENT_TYPE
Update VCF Automation Registration to VCF Operations
After a successful recovery of VCF Automation, you update the registration in VCF Operations.
Download and extract the scripts from Broadcom knowledge base article 443506 to the machine you use to access your
VCF environment.
On your linux workstation, run the following command.
export VCFA_RUNTIME_FQDN='flt-vcfa-sr01.rainpole.io'
./update_vcfa_registration.sh --vcfa-runtime-fqdn $VCFA_RUNTIME_FQDN --password <admin@vsp.local passwd>
Update Backup Schedule Configuration for Recovered Components
To ensure the recovered components are backed up according to the schedule that is assigned by the VCF Instance they
currently reside in, you update the backup schedule.
1. Log in to VCF Operations as a user with the ADMIN role.
2. Navigate to Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management > Backup and Restore.
3. Click the vertical elipsis next to the schedule for the VCF Instance where the recovered components currently reside,
and click Edit.
4. On the Edit Schedule page, click Update.
5. Monitor the task on the Tasks pane.

Cleanup the recovered components from the recovery Site VCF Management Services Instance
Before you can failback to the original site, you must cleanup the recovered components from the recovery site.
CAUTION:
This procedure is specific to failing back from a disaster recovery failover and should not be used to completely
delete a deployed component outside of this scenario. To fully delete day 2 deployed components on VCF
Management Services refer to this KB441333
SSH to the control plane node of the target VCF Management Services instance and run the following:
a) Cleanup the recovered components
sudo su
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
kubectl delete component ops-logs salt-raas vidb vcf-fleet-depot vcf-fleet-lcm
b) Remove the recovered components.
# Find leader
export DB_LEADER=`kubectl exec vcf-sddc-lcm-db-0 -n vcf-sddc-lcm -c postgres -- patronictl list | awk -
F'|' '/Leader/ {print $2}' | xargs`
# Cleanup nodes of VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks
kubectl exec $DB_LEADER -n vcf-sddc-lcm -it -- psql -U postgres -d vcfsddclcmdb -c "DELETE FROM node WHERE
component_id IN ( SELECT id FROM component WHERE component_type in ('OPS', 'OPS_NETWORKS');"
# Cleanup component entries in SDDC LCM
kubectl exec $DB_LEADER -n vcf-sddc-lcm -it -- psql -U postgres -d vcfsddclcmdb -c "DELETE FROM component
WHERE component_type IN ('OPS', 'VIDB', 'OPS_LOGS', 'SALT_RAAS', 'VCF_FLEET_LCM', 'VCF_FLEET_DEPOT',
'OPS_NETWORKS');"
Prepare to Fail Back VCF Automation
Before you fail back VCF Automation to the original site, you clean up the SDDC Manager inventory on the recovery site.
1. Open an SSH to the SDDC Manger appliance in the recovery site as the vcf user and elevate to the user.
root
2. Connect to the Postgres database.
psql -U postgres -h localhost -d platform;
3. Query the vsp_clusters table and record the ID of the entry with type CONSUMPTION.
select * from vsp_cluster;
4. Delete the CONSUMPTION entry.
CONSUMPTION
delete from vsp_cluster where type=' ';
Broadcom 4495

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Delete the corresponding credential.
CONSUMPTION
delete from credential where username='vsp/< -vsp_cluster_id>/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
For example:
delete from credential where username='vsp/1f5c79fe-e3aa-41b1-a5cf-774a6497fa3d/svc-sddc-manager-admin';
Failover Tasks
Configure and perform a failover of the management applications in the SDDC from the protected to the recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance. Failing over these applications maintains the operational state of the SDDC. You follow
the step-by-step instructions to perform disaster recovery of management components running within VMware Cloud
Foundation.
You fail over the following management applications:
Table 1171: Support for Failover of the SDDC Management Applications
Management Application Supports Failover
VCF Identity Broker Yes
VCF Automation Yes
VCF Operations Yes
Prerequisites
Prerequisite Value
Compute The compute infrastructure in the recovery VMware Cloud
Foundation instance must mirror the compute infrastructure in the
protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance.
Storage • The storage configuration and capacity in the recovery
VMware Cloud Foundation instance must mirror the storage
configuration and capacity in the protected VMware Cloud
Foundation instance.
• Datastore space on the management cluster with sufficient
capacity must be available for all the virtual machines of VCF
Automation and VCF Operations.
External services Provide the following services in the recovery site.
• Active Directory domain controller for each domain in the
forest. Required for VCF Identity Broker to synchronize users
when a domain controller in the protected site is unavailable.
• DNS
• NTP
• SMTP
• Syslog
Virtual infrastructure • Verify that the VMware Cloud Foundation versions are the
same in both sites.
• Verify that Protection and Recovery are deployed in both
VMware Cloud Foundation instances and paired.
• Verify that the NSX load balancer is deployed and configured
in both VMware Cloud Foundation instances.
• Verify the NSX Edge cluster for North-South routing is
deployed and configured in both VMware Cloud Foundation
instances.
Broadcom 4496

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Failover Checklist for the VCF Management Applications for VMware Cloud Foundation
Use the checklist to verify that you have fulfilled all the requirements to initiate disaster recovery or planned migration of
the SDDC management applications and to complete the configuration of these applications.
Table 1172: Checklist for Failover and Failback in an SDDC
Checklist Tasks
Activation and assessment • Verify that disaster failover or failback is required:
For example, an application failure might not be a cause
for a failover or failback, while an extended VMware Cloud
Foundation instance outage is a valid cause.
• Plan for business continuity events such as scheduled building
maintenance or the probability of a natural disaster.
Approval • Submit the required documentation for approval to the
following roles:
– IT management staff
– CTO
– Business users
– Other stakeholders
Activation logistics • Verify that all the required facilities and personnel are available
for the complete duration of the disaster recovery process.
• Verify that Protection and Recovery is available in the recovery
VMware Cloud Foundation instance.
• Verify the replication status of the SDDC management
components.
• Verify the state of NSX Data Center in the recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance:
– Verify that the NSX Edge nodes are available.
– Verify that the IP addresses for the overlay-backed
networks are correct.
– Verify that the NSX load balancer is correctly configured
according to the design.
Communication, initiation, and failover or failback validation • In case of a planned migration:
– Notify all stakeholders for the planned outage and the
expected duration of the maintenance window.
– At the scheduled time, initiate the failover or failback
process.
• In case of a failover or failback for disaster recovery:
– Before initiating a failover or a failback, notify all
stakeholders for the event.
• After completing a failover or a failback:
– Test applications availability.
– Notify all stakeholders for the completed event.
Broadcom 4497

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Checklist Tasks
Multiple Availability Zones If your environment consists of multiple availability zones, perform
additional configuration for failback for disaster recovery:
• In case of failback for disaster recovery in which the recovery
VMware Cloud Foundation instance remains unavailable, the
vSAN witness appliance might not available too. As a result,
you might be unable to provision the VCF Automation and
VCF Operations virtual machines in the protected VMware
Cloud Foundation instance according to the active vSAN
storage policy. To ensure the recovery of the VCF Automation
and VCF Operations virtual machines, turn on the force-
provisioning option in the storage policy.
• In case of a planned migration in which both the protected
and recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instances are still
operational, the vSAN witness appliance is available and the
active storage policy is satisfied.
Configuration after failover In case of disaster recovery failover, perform additional
configuration:
• Redirect the log data from the failed over or failed back
applications to Log Management in the recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance.
• Complete a post-recovery assessment:
– Note which items worked and which did not work, and
identify improvements that you can include in the recovery
plan.
Perform a Disaster Recovery of the VCF Management Applications for Fleet Disaster Recovery for
VMware Cloud Foundation
If the protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance becomes unavailable, prepare networking in the recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance and perform a failover of the protected components to the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation
instance.
NSX Federation Tasks in the Recovery VMware Cloud Foundation Instance
Perform the following steps if you are using NSX Federation to provide IP mobility between VMware Cloud Foundation
instances.
Assign the Active Role to the NSX Global Manager Instance in the Recovery VMware Cloud Foundation Instance
If the protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance becomes unavailable, you must prepare the network layer in the
recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance for a failover of the management applications. To provide full management
of the network infrastructure in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance, first change the role of the NSX Global
Manager instance in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance.
Procedure
You set the NSX Global Manager instance in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance as active.
1. Log in to NSX Global Manager for the management domain in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance at
as admin.
https://<standby_nsx_gm_fqdn>/login.jsp?local=true
2. On the main navigation bar, click System.
3. In the left navigation pane, under Configuration, click Location manager.
4. In the card for the NSX Global Manager in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance, click Actions and select
Make active.
5. In the Make active dialog box, click Make active.
6. In the Do you still want to continue? dialog box, click Force to active.
7. In the Do you want to force this standby Global Manager to be active? dialog box, click Yes.
Broadcom 4498

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
8. Wait until the NSX Global Manager instance changes from to .
Standby Active
This process takes several minutes to complete.
Reconfigure the NSX Tier-1 Gateway for Dynamic Routing in the Recovery VMware Cloud Foundation Instance
To support dynamic routing in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance, before you initiate a disaster recovery
from the protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance, configure the NSX Tier-1 gateway to set the recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance as primary. This configuration ensures that the management components of the SDDC
continue to communicate using optimal routes in a fault-tolerant network.
1. Log in to NSX Global Manager for the management domain in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance at
as admin.
https://<active_nsx_gm_fqdn>/login.jsp?local=true
2. On the main navigation bar, click Networking.

Synchronize the VCF Operations Fleet Management Inventory for Fleet Disaster Recovery for VMware
Cloud Foundation
If the virtual machines reside in the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance for an extended period of time, to
activate day two operations, such as power on and power off of virtual machines managed by VCF Operations fleet
management, you must update the VCF Operations fleet management inventory to ensure that it synchronizes the new
location of the virtual machines. To update the VCF Operations fleet management inventory with the new location of the
failed over virtual machines, you perform an inventory sync for each component.
Prerequisites
Verify that the virtual machines for each component are powered on.
Procedure
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at https://<vcf_operations_fqdn> with a user assigned the Administrator role.
2. Navigate to Fleet Management > Lifecycle > VCF Management > Components.
3. On the Components page, select the first component to synchronize.
4. On the component tab, click Trigger inventory sync.
5. Monitor the inventory sync request in the Tasks page.
6. If the inventory sync fails when validating the vCenter details, click Retry, enter the FQDN of the vCenter instance
where the virtual machines are currently running, and click Submit.
7. Repeat the procedure for each component.
What to do next
If SDDC Manager in the original protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance is unavailable, when SDDC Manager in the
original protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance becomes available again, repeat the inventory sync procedure.
Reprotection Tasks
After a disaster recovery or planned migration, the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance becomes the protected
instance, but the virtual machines are not yet protected. If the original protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance
becomes operational, you can reverse the direction of protection.
Prerequisites for Reprotection for VCF Fleet Disaster Recovery
During the reprotect operation, after Protection and Recovery reverses the direction of protection, it forces a
synchronization of the storage from the new protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance to the new recovery VMware
Cloud Foundation instance. Forcing data synchronization ensures that the recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance
has a current copy of the protected virtual machines running at the protected VMware Cloud Foundation instance.
Recovery is possible immediately after the reprotect operation finishes.
Prerequisites
To reprotect the virtual machines of the SDDC management applications, your environment must meet certain
requirements for the availability of the original protected region and state of the recovery plans.
• The new recovery VMware Cloud Foundation instance must be available. The vCenter instance, ESX hosts, Protection
and Recovery Server instances, Protection and Recovery, and corresponding databases must all be recovered.
If you cannot restore the original protected region, you must reinstall Protection and Recovery on the protected and
recovery regions.
• Verify that all steps of the failover recovery plan finish successfully.
Broadcom 4503

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

FIPS Configuration for VCF Components
VCF supports the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-3, which specify security requirements for
cryptographic modules.
Many VCF components support the FIPS standard inherently, and cannot be configured in ways that do not meet the
standard. For example, ESX and VMware NSX. Other components might require enablement for FIPS compliance or
have varying behavior depending on how they were deployed.
The following components have FIPS enabled by default:
• ESX
• vCenter
• NSX
• VCF Operations HCX
• Protection and Recovery
• Data Services Manager
• VCF management services
The table below summarizes FIPS enablement for components where FIPS is either not enabled by default or can be
disabled in certain circumstances.
Component FIPS Configuration
SDDC Manager In new VCF 9.x deployments, FIPS compliance in SDDC Manager
is on by default and cannot be turned off.
For deployments upgraded from VCF 5.x, the FIPS setting
remains the same as it was in the original deployment. This setting
cannot be altered after upgrade.
VCF Operations FIPS compliance is off by default.
You can activate FIPS compliance during deployment by selecting
the Activate FIPS Mode option during deployment.
Log management FIPS compliance is off by default.
You can enable FIPS compliance during deployment by selecting
the the On option for FIPS Compliance. See Deploy Log
Management.
VCF Operations for networks VCF Operations for networks uses FIPS compliant cryptographic
algorithms for internal connections. FIPS compliance for external
connections is off by default.
You can enable FIPS compliance for external connections by
navigating to Settings > System Configuration > FIPS Mode for
External Connections and toggling the setting to On.
Cloud Proxy for VCF Operations FIPS compliance is not enabled by default. You can enable
FIPS compliance for cloud proxies after first enabling FIPS
compliance for VCF Operations. For instructions on enabling FIPS
compliance, see Using the Cloud Proxy Command-Line Interface.
Broadcom 4507

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Component FIPS Configuration
VCF Automation In new VCF 9.x deployments, FIPS compliance in VCF
Automation is enabled by default and cannot be turned off.
For deployments upgraded from VMware Aria Operations 18.x,
the FIPS setting remains the same as it was in the original
deployment. This setting cannot be altered after upgrade.
VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service VKS 3.3 and later provide the ability to enable OS FIPS mode by
configuring the osConfiguration cluster class variable. See osConf
iguration for more details.
VMware Virtual Disk Developer Kit (VDDK) By default, VDDK does not enable FIPS. You can configure it by
setting the option vixDiskLib.ssl.enableSslFIPS=1
in the VDDK configuration file. See the instructions provided with
the development kit at https://developer.broadcom.com/sdks/vmw
are-virtual-disk-development-kit-vddk/latest for more information.
FIPS Configuration for VMware vSphere Foundation Components
You can activate Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) for the VCF Operations component of VMware
vSphere Foundation to make your environment FIPS compliant. You can also activate firewall hardening.
Activate FIPS
You can activate FIPS in the VCF Operations cluster at the time of installation or after VCF Operations is up and running.
Adding FIPS at installation is less intrusive because the cluster has not yet started.
If the cluster is running, to activate FIPS, you must take the cluster offline.
FIPS mode is supported in Cloud Proxy. You can continue using your cloud proxy after enabling FIPS for the VCF
Operations cluster.
1. In a Web browser, navigate to the master node administration interface.
https://master-node-name-or-ip-
.
address/admin
2. Enter the VCF Operations administrator credentials and click Log In.
3. Click Administrator Settings.
Note:
The Activate FIPS button is deactivated when the cluster is running.
4. Click Activate FIPS after you take your cluster offline.
Note:
After you activate FIPS, you cannot deactivate the FIPS mode in the current setup. To revert to a FIPS
deactivated setup, you must re-deploy VCF Operations.
5. In the Are you sure you want to activate FIPS dialog box, read the note and provide your consent for enabling FIPS
and then click Yes.
Note:
After you activate FIPS, the cluster restarts and is not be available during this time. The cluster nodes are
rebooted and after the cluster is online, all the nodes are FIPS activated.
Activate Firewall Hardening
Activating firewall hardening restricts network access to internal services in VCF Operations.
1. In a Web browser, navigate to the master node administration interface.
https://master-node-name-or-ip-
.
address/admin
2. Enter the VCF Operations administrator credentials and click Log In.
3. Click Administrator Settings, and then click Security Settings from the Administrator Settings page.
4. Click Activate Firewall Hardening.
Broadcom 4508

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Using the FIPS API to Query FIPS Status of Components
VCF 9.1 includes an API that allows you to retrieve information about the FIPS cryptographic modules used by each
component, including version number, CMVP certificate, and other information.
Note:
The FIPS API is available as a Tech Preview only.
The FIPS API is a read-only API that can be used to retrieve FIPS cryptographic module information about the following
components:
• vCenter
• ESX
• NSX
• HCX
• SDDC Manager
• Data Services Manager
• VCF Automation
• VCF Operations
• VCF Operations for networks
• VMware Live Recovery
Components aggregate information about subcomponents and return that information in the API response. For example, a
query to vCenter returns component information for ESX.
The API returns the following fields.
Field Description
name The official title of the cryptographic module.
version Specifies the version that has undergone FIPS 140 validation.
cmvp_cert The CMVP certificate number for the cryptographic module.
If the CMVP certificate was not issued at the time of release, this
field returns nothing.
cavp_cert The CAVP certificate number for the cryptographic module.
The Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program (CAVP) is a
prerequisite for CMVP validation. A CAVP certificate number
indicates progress in the validation process.
If the CAVP certificate was not issued at the time of release, this
field returns nothing.
component_name Name of the component containing the cryptographic module.
component_id Component id.
component_version Component version.
FIPS API Limitations
• If FIPS has been disabled for a component, the API might return an empty list.
• Parent components silently exclude subcomponents that are at versions below 9.1. For example, consider a vCenter
running 9.1 that is managing a mixture of ESX hosts running versions 9.0 and 9.1. The API query returns information
for the ESX 9.1 hosts, but omits the ESX 9.0 hosts.
Broadcom 4509

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
FIPS API Endpoints
Component Endpoint
ESX /api/esx/crypto/fips/modules
vCenter /api/vcenter/crypto/fips/modules
SDDC Manager /v1/system/security/fips/modules
NSX /api/v1/node/fips/module
HCX Manager /hybridity/api/admin/fips/modules
HCX Photon-based data plane /fips/modules
Data Services Manager /provider/fips/modules
VCF Operations /suite-api/internal/fips/modules
VCF Automation /vcfa/fips/modules
Log Management /api/v2/fips/modules
VCF Operations for networks /api/ni/settings/fips/modules
Querying vCenter
1. Obtain an API token.
userName password <host>
curl -k -X POST -u ' : ' https:// /api/session
2. Use the token obtained in the following command.
curl -k -X GET https:// <host> /api/vcenter/crypto/fips/modules -H "vmware-api-session-id: <token>" -H
'Content-Type: application/json’
Example output:
[
{
"cmvp_cert": "4743",
"component_name": "vCenter",
"name": "VMware's BC-FJA (Bouncy Castle FIPS Java API)",
"version": "2.0.0",
"component_version": "9.1.0"
},
{
"cmvp_cert": "4865",

Configuring Management Components
After deploying VCF Operations, VCF Automation, or VCF management services components, you can update a
component configuration or address issues in a component deployment.

You can perform post-deployment actions on VCF Operations, VCF Automation, VCF Operations for networks, and VCF
management services components. VCF management services components include log management, identity broker,
software depot, real-time metrics, fleet lifecycle, SDDC lifecycle, Salt RaaS, and Salt master. You can also perform most
post-deployment actions on VCF services runtime.
