Scaling VCF Management Components
You can scale up and can scale out your VCF Operations, VCF Operations for networks, VCF Automation, VCF services
runtime, log management, identity broker, Salt RaaS, and Salt master components.
For all components, the scale up procedure begins in the same way. Some components include additional selections:
• For VCF Operations, you increase the size of nodes in your VCF Operations cluster. You also can add disk size and
select a datastore where the new disk is added.
Important:
To scale a VCF Operations cluster for continuous availability, you must:
• Deploy a VCF Operations cluster for continuous availability. See Configure VCF Operations Cluster for
Continuous Availability.
• Log in to the VCF Operations administrator interface in the primary fault domain to specify options and start
the scale up process for VCF Operations.
• For VCF Operations for networks, you select the platform or collector nodes to scale up.
• For log management, you choose the size of your log management deployment and select the number of replica
nodes.
Broadcom 4514

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• For VCF services runtime, you scale up capacity by increasing size and adding IP addresses to the Node IP pool.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Under Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management, click the component that you want to change.
3. Specify the options for your component and start the scale up process.
• For VCF Operations:
1. Under Actions, click Scale.
2. Select the node size: XS, Small, Medium, Large, XL
3. Optionally provide additional disk size in GB to be added to every node in the VCF Operations cluster.
4. Select Advanced Datastore Configuration to select a datastore where the disk is to be added on each node.
5. Review the summary of your request and click Scale.
• For VCF Operations for networks:
1. Under Actions, click Scale Up.
2. Select the platform or collector nodes to scale up.
3. Specify the size, datastore, and additional disk size for the node, and click Confirm.
4. Repeat the process for the collector nodes, as needed.
5. Review the summary of your request and click Scale Up.
• For VCF services runtime:
1. Under Actions, click Scale.
2. For size, the current size is pre-selcted. Specify the new size of the deployment: Small, Medium, Large.
3. (optional) Add IP addresses to the Node IP pool.
4. Review the summary of your request and click Finish.
• For log management:
1. Under Actions, click Scale.
2. For size, the current size is pre-selected. Specify the new size of the deployment: Small, Medium, Large.
3. For number of replicas, the current number is pre-selected. Specify the new number of nodes.
4. Click Scale.
• For VCF Automation, identity broker , and real-time metrics select the size of deployment:
1. Under Actions, click Scale.
2. For size, the current size is pre-selcted. Specify the new size of the deployment: Small, Medium, Large.
3. Acknowledge the possible service disruption and click Scale.
Scale up begins. Click the Tasks tab to check the progress of the scale up task. During the process, the nodes are
restarted and services are not available during the downtime.
Important:
Rolling back to a backup created before scale up will revert the cluster to its earlier size and permanently delete
data from the node added during scale up. After the scale up process completes, take a new backup to avoid data
loss.
Add Nodes in VCF Operations and VCF Operations for networks
For VCF Operations, you add replica or data nodes. For VCF Operations for networks, you add platform nodes or
collector nodes.
Update the VCF Operations certificate to include the FQDN or IP address of the nodes to be added. See Managing
Certificates in VMware Cloud Foundation.
Broadcom 4515

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If you do not update the certificate prior to performing the scale-out operation, the lifecycle management process
will fail. To remediate the failure, see Broadcom knowledge base article 430384.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Under Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management, select the component that you want to update.
3. Under Actions, select the Node Management action that you want to perform.
• To add a replica or data node in VCF Operations:
1. Select the type of node to add.
2. Enter the Fully Qualified Domain Name.
Important:
The VCF Operations certificate must be updated to include the FQDN of the new node.
3. Enter the password for the VCF Operations admin.
4. Enter the password for the new node.
5. After verifying that any necessary changes to the VCF Operations certificate have been made, click ADD to
start the node deployment.
• To add a platform node in VCF Operations for networks:
1. Select Add platform node.
a. Enter the IP address of the new platform node.
Important:
The VCF Operations certificate must be updated to include the IP address of the new node.
b. (optional) To add multiple platform nodes, click Add Another Platform Node and enter additional IP
addresses.
c. Enter the credentials of the platform node or regenerate and consume a new password. The password is
used for the console user and support.
2. To add a node or multiple nodes to the Operations-Network cluster, click ADD.
• To add a collector node in VCF Operations for networks:
1. Select Add collector node.
2. Enter the IP address of the new collector node.
Important:
The VCF Operations certificate must be updated to include the IP address of the new node.
3. Enter the credentials of the collector node or regenerate and consume a new password. The password is used
for the console user and support.
4. Select the VCF Instance where Operations-Collector node should be deployed. The node is deployed on the
Management Domain vCenter of the VCF Instance selected.
5. To add the node to the Operations-Network cluster, click ADD.
Add a Cloud Proxy
Add a cloud proxy to your VCF Operations environment.
• Verify that you have an IP address and an FQDN for the cloud proxy.
Broadcom 4516

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Verify that you have the VCF Operations admin account password.
• Use the following information to verify that you have enough compute resources for the cloud proxy.
Cloud Proxy Type VM Scale Requirements CPU Requirements Memory Requirements
Unified Small Cloud Proxy Up to 16,000 VMs 4 vCPUs 16GB
Unified Standard Cloud Proxy Between 16,000 to 80,000 VMs 8 vCPUs 48 GB
To add a cloud proxy as a post-deployment action, perform the following steps:
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Under Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management, select VCF Operations.
3. Under Actions, select Add cloud proxy.
a) Provide input for the cloud proxy.
• FQDN: Enter the FQDN for the cloud proxy.
• Size: Select a small or standard size for the new cloud proxy. See Broadcom knowledge base article 397782.
• VCF Operations admin password: Enter the admin account password for the VCF Operations instance where
you are adding the cloud proxy.
• Password: Create a password for the cloud proxy.
Note:
Save the password to a secure place for future use.
• VCF Instance: Select the VCF Instance where you want to add the cloud proxy.
b) Click Add.
If you want to start collecting data using the newly added cloud proxy, you must update the integration settings for your
VCF Instance or vCenter.
4. (Optional) After the deployment completes, update the VCF Instance integration to use the new collector for new
workload domains.
a) Select Operate > Administration > Integrations and click Accounts.
b) Expand VMware Cloud Foundation and expand the integration that you want to configure.
c) At the VCF Instance level, click the vertical ellipsis and click Edit.
d) On the Cloud Account Information page, from the Cloud Proxy / Group drop-down menu, select the newly
deployed collector, click Validate Connection, and click Save.
5. (Optional) For the existing domains of the same VCF Instance, update the integrations for all vCenter instances to use
the new collector/collector group.
a) Select Operate > Administration > Integrations and click Accounts.
b) Expand VMware Cloud Foundation and expand the integration that you want to configure.
c) At the domain level, click the vertical ellipsis and click Edit.
d) On the Connect vCenter page, from the Cloud Proxy / Group drop-down menu, select the newly deployed
collector, click Validate Connection, and click Save.
e) Repeat the step for all remaining workload domains in that VCF Instance.
After deploying the cloud proxy, you can monitor the appliance health status and activate data persistence and log assist.
For more information, see Monitoring the Health of Cloud Proxies.
Increase Storage Size for VCF Automation and VCF Management Services Components
Increase storage size increases the storage capacity for different volume groups in your VCF Automation, VCF services
runtime, or VCF Management Services Component deployment.
Broadcom 4517

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Operations interface at as a user assigned the Administrator
https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.
2. Under Build > Lifecycle > VCF Management, select VCF services runtime or the VCF Management Services
component that you want to update.
3. Under Actions, select Increase Storage Size.
4. Update Volume Size values for the various Volume Groups.
Important:
Once increased, storage size cannot be reduced.
• Volume Group Name: Identifies the volume groups that are mapped to specific components.
• Volumes in group: Indicates the number of volumes that are currently assigned to each volume group.
• Volume Size: Displays the current size of each volume in Gigabytes (GB). Use the - and + buttons or manually
enter a value to specify the new, increased size per volume.
• Used/Total Storage Capacity: Displays the current storage usage versus the total available capacity for the group.
The total capacity is calculated by multiplying the number of "Existing Volumes" by the specified "Volume Size".
5. After ensuring that you are ready to irreversibly increase storage size, click Resize.

Configure a Proxy Server for VCF Management Services Components and VCF
Automation
If your VCF Management Services components do not have direct Internet access, you can configure a proxy server. You
configure proxy settings for a VCF services runtime instance. The configuration is then valid for all the components hosted
on that instance. Components hosted on VCF services runtime instances that might connect to the Internet, are software
depot, telemetry, identity broker, and VCF Automation.
• Verify that you have administrative credentials for the VCF Operations primary node.
• Verify that you have configured a proxy server to access the Internet.
• Verify that you have and utilities installed on a machine with management access to your VCF environment.
curl jq
Note:
In environments where SSL/TLS interception is enabled, software depot configured in connected mode might not
establish a trusted connection to the Broadcom authorization server. For more information on adding your proxy's
CA certificate to the truststore of software depot, see Broadcom knowledge base article 442978.
The following procedure allows you to route component traffic through a proxy server for a specific VCF services runtime
instance. The configuration includes TLS settings, authentication credentials, and certificate information.
This procedure includes the following steps.
• Retrieving the service key for the fleet lifecycle component which stores proxy configuration settings for all VCF
services runtime instances in the fleet.
• Obtaining a VCF Operations token that you use to authenticate and authorize API calls to the fleet lifecycle
component.
• Exchanging the VCF Operations token for a bearer token.
• Configuring the VCF services runtime instance configuration with proxy settings.
You must perform this procedure on each VCF services runtime instance, where the component requires the traffic to be
routed through a configured proxy server.
Note:
Alternatively, instead of manually performing the tasks in the procedure below, you can use the
vmsp-
script. The script automates the API calls and includes a menu with options to show, configure,
utility.py

and remove a proxy configuration for a VCF services runtime instance. See Broadcom knowledge base article
442978.

OPS_FQDN is the VCF Operations primary node FQDN and password is the VCF Operations admin user password.
OPS_FQDN

The Basic authorization header contains the base64-encoded username:password. To encode your

printf 'username:password' | base64

--header 'Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46dkFVXk1KNDMjSTBvcGlEUnJZSDQ=' | jq | less
The response contains service information. Locate and record the key value. For example:

https://<vcf_operations_fqdn>
role.

a) Scroll to the Nodes section.

vmware-system-user
.
APPLIANCE_ROOT_PASSWORD

sudo -i

Renaming VCF 9.1 Components After Deployment
After you deploy VMware Cloud Foundation or vSphere Foundation 9.1 or later, you can rename certain vCenter and NSX
components without breaking your SDDC Manager inventory.
VCF 9.1 reduces the number of component names that SDDC Manager persists in its inventory. As a result, renaming
many vCenter objects no longer causes inconsistencies between vCenter, NSX, and SDDC Manager. However, some
components are still subject to restrictions, and renaming outside the supported paths can produce unexpected behavior.

vCenter and NSX Components You Cannot Rename
CAUTION:
The following components are known to have naming dependencies. Do not rename these components.
Component Reason
NSX segment Segment names are referenced in NSX policy objects.
SDDC Manager persists the edge cluster name in its inventory database and uses it for
NSX edge cluster internal Day-2 operations, including password rotation, cluster removal, and consistency
checks. Renaming the edge cluster in NSX Manager breaks these name-based lookups.
VCF services runtime VMs Name modifications in vCenter cause synchronization failures.
VCF services runtime datastores Name modifications in vCenter cause synchronization failures.
VCF services runtime network objects Name modifications in vCenter cause synchronization failures.
VCF services runtime folders Name modifications in vCenter cause synchronization failures.

Infrastructure Operations
Use VCF Operations as a VI administrator to optimize and monitor compute, storage, and network of your VCF
platform. These operational capabilities include performance optimization, visibility and observability of infrastructure and
operations, global configuration management, monitoring, troubleshooting, log analytics, end-to-end network monitoring,
energy efficiency monitoring, and other.
In This Chapter
• Integrating Data Sources with VCF Operations
• Configuring and Managing Policies
• Configuring Alerts and Using Actions
• Managing Inventory
• Configuring Automation Jobs
• Configuring and Analyzing Logs
• Network Operations
• Monitoring Storage Operations
• Using VCF Operations Diagnostics
• Troubleshooting with the Workbench
• Configuring Green Score
• Configuring Dashboards and Widgets
• Using Predefined Dashboards for Quick Insights
• Configuring Reports and Views
• Configuring Super Metrics
• Configuring Administration Settings
• Viewing Metrics and Properties
• Extending Monitoring Capabilities
Getting to Know VCF
To apply this documentation, you must be acquainted with the VCF Product Overview, VCF Design, and VCF Release
Notes.
SDKs, APIs, and CLI for VCF Administration
You can build, operate, and manage your VCF private cloud by using the VCF SDK and APIs, and VCF PowerCLI. See
Administration SDKs, APIs, and CLI.
Integrating Data Sources with VCF Operations
You can extend the monitoring capabilities of VCF Operations by installing and configuring integrations in VCF Operations
to connect to and analyze data from external data sources in your environment. Once connected, you can use VCF
Operations to monitor and manage objects in your environment. These integrations are also referenced as management
packs.
An integration can be a connection to a data source, or include predefined dashboards, widgets, alerts, and views.
Integrations include accounts, dashboards, reports, alerts, and other content. The accounts comprise of adapters, using
which VCF Operations manages communication and integration with other products, applications, and functions. When
an integration is installed and the accounts are configured, you can use the VCF Operations analytics and alerting tools to
manage the objects in your environment.
VMware integrations include native, non-native, and external management packs.
For a new deployment of VCF Operations, the status of integrations is as follows:

The list of activated and available integrations, accounts, and the full repository of integrations are all available from a
central Integrations page in VCF Operations . This page can be accessed from the left menu by clicking Operate >
Administration > Integrations > Repository.
Non-Native Management Packs and Management Pack Builder
If a technology has no native management pack, you can install a non-native pack or can build your own using VCF
Operations Management Pack Builder.
With the Management Pack Builder, you can create custom management packs for use in VCF Operations. This is a no-
code solution for bringing in data from an external API and either creating new resources or extending your VMware and
third party resources with new data, relationships, and events. For more information, see Management Pack Builder.
Upgrade Considerations
The native integrations in VCF Operations are reinstalled if VCF Operations is upgraded.
The Integrations Page in VCF Operations
You can activate integrations, install integrations, add, import, or export accounts from the Integrations page in VCF
Operations. Integrations are also referenced as Management Packs in VCF Operations.
How Integrations Work
Each account contains adapters using which VCF Operations integrates with other products, applications, and monitors
their function and health. Integrations can include dashboards, reports, alerts, and accounts.
Broadcom 4527

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Where You Find Integrations
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations. By default, the Accounts tab opens. Use this tab to add, import, or export accounts. For more information,
see The Accounts Tab.
Click the Repository tab to view the installed and available integrations. You can also install integrations that are
delivered as PAK files. For more information, see The Repository Tab.
Click the Solutions Catalog tab to add and manage VCF Operations management packs from VCF Solutions Catalog.
For more information see, The Solutions Catalog Tab.
Note:
For more information on pre-activated integrations, see Integrating Data Sources with VCF Operations.
Collection Notifications
The Notifications bell icon on the top menu provides quick access to status and critical notifications that are related to
data collections. The icon indicates whether notifications exist, and whether any of them are critical.
The list displays notifications about the data collections that are in progress, and indicates whether any of them have
critical issues. The list groups the data collection notifications that are in progress into a single entry at the bottom of the
list. To view the details about a collection, expand the notification.
Each notification displays the status of the last or current data collection, the associated adapter instance, and the time
since the collection completed or an issue was identified. You can click a notification to open the Integrations page,
where you can see further details, and manage adapter instances.
If problems occur with the data collections, VCF Operations identifies those problems during each 5-minute collection
cycle.
Go to Collection Status to monitor the data collection, for more information, see Monitoring Data Collection .
The Accounts Tab
You can view and add accounts from the Accounts tab on the Integration page in VCF Operations. You can add accounts
for integrations or you can add accounts after activating integrations from the Repository tab.
Where You Find the Accounts tab
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations. The Accounts tab opens by default. The accounts tab lists all the accounts that are configured for the
different integrations available in VCF Operations. You can filter accounts to view accounts specific to an integration type.
What You Can Do in the Accounts tab
You can add and configure accounts that are associated with integrations that are pre-activated or those that you activate
in VCF Operations . After you have configured the account, VCF Operations can collect data from or can send data to the
target system. You can access the accounts page at any time to modify your adapter configurations.

Adding Accounts
You can add and configure accounts associated with integrations that are provided with or that you add to VCF
Operations. After you have configured the account, VCF Operations can communicate with the target system. You can
access the Accounts tab in the Integrations page at any time to modify your adapter configurations.
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations. In the Accounts tab, click Add and select the integration you want to manage. Configure cloud proxies and
activate the integration before adding and configuring accounts. For more information, see Add a Cloud Proxy and The
Repository Tab.
Exporting and Importing Accounts
As a VCF Operations admin, you can back up the adapter configurations before upgrading, export all the adapter
configurations, and import them into a different VCF Operations instance.
Note:
Users with "Export" permission can export and users with "Import" permission can import the adapter
configurations. For more information, see Access Control: Roles Tab.
1. Export the adapter configuration.
Note:
You cannot export default VMware Cloud Foundation and vCenter accounts that were configured in VCF
Operations using the VCF Installer.
a) In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click
Administration > Integrations.
b) In the Accounts tab, select the adapter configuration(s) that you want to export, click the horizontal ellipses, and
select Export.
c) Set up a new password to export data. The password should be at least 14 characters long and must include at
least one numerical character, upper and lower case character, and special character.
d) Click Export.
The adapter configurations are exported in .zip format. A password is used to encrypt the data. Use the same
password while importing this file.
2. Import the adapter configuration.
Note:
Before importing the content, ensure that you have exported the adapter configurations.

a) In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click
Administration > Integrations.
b) Click the horizontal ellipses and select Import.
c) Click Browse to select the file and enter the password that you had set while exporting the content.
.zip
d) If there is a conflict while importing the adapter configurations, you can either overwrite the existing adapter
configurations or skip the import, which is the default option.
e) Click Import to import adapter configurations to the destination setup.
Configuring Credentials in Integrations
Credentials are the user accounts that VCF Operations uses to activate one or more integrations and associated
adapters, and to establish communication with the target data sources. The credentials are supplied when you configure
each adapter. You can create new credentials and modify the credential settings outside the adapter configuration or
during adapter configuration to accommodate changes to your environment.
If you are modifying credentials to accommodate changes based on your password policy, you must validate your
connection so that the adapters configured with these credentials begin using the new user name and password to
communicate between VCF Operations and the target system.
To edit credential settings, from the left menu, click Administration > Integrations. In the Accounts tab, click Credentials
.
By default, the Credential Ownership Enforcement option is activated. When this option is activated, you can view, add,
modify, or delete only the credentials that you created or that were assigned to you. You can view and use unassigned
credentials only if you have the required permissions. You can also deactivate the Credential Ownership Enforcement
option from Global Settings page to be able to modify credentials created and owned by others. For more information,
see List of Global Settings.
Where You Find Credentials
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations. In the Accounts tab, click Credentials.
Table 1177: Credentials Options
Option Description

an adapter. For more information, see Adding Credentials.
Edit/Delete credentials • Click the Vertical Ellipses to perform any one of the following actions on existing
credentials:
– Edit: Modifies the selected credentials, usually when the user name and password
require a change. The change is applied to the current adapter credentials after you
validate the connection and the data source continues to communicate with VCF
Operations.
– Delete: Removes the selected credentials from VCF Operations. Commonly used
to delete misconfigured credentials. You cannot delete a credential in active use. To
remove it, first reconfigure or delete the adapter, then delete the credential.

instance.

The Repository Tab
The repository tab lists all the installed and available integrations in VCF Operations. Integrations are also referenced as
Management Packs and Solutions.
Where You Find the Repository Tab
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations, and then click the Repository tab. The page displays installed and available integrations as clickable cards.
What Can You Do in the Repository Tab
In the Repository tab, when you click an integration card, the details page is displayed.
The management pack details page consists of the following three tabs:
• Overview: Describes the management pack and its purpose.
• Metrics: Displays a list of metrics and properties for the various object types as defined by the adapter.

This list of metrics and properties can display additional metrics and properties after account creation since other
sources can also publish them.
The actual list of published metrics and properties depends from policy customization and monitored environment.
• Content: Displays the content types and the data defined by that management pack.

Adding a Management Pack
Management packs are delivered as PAK files that you upload, license, and install.
How Management Packs Work
When you add a management pack, you configure adapters that manage the communication and integration between
VCF Operations and other products, applications, and functionality.
Where You Add Management Packs
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, click Administration >
Integrations. Click the Repository tab and then click Add to install other management packs.
Add Solutions Wizard Options
The wizard includes three pages where you locate and upload a PAK file, accept the EULA and install, and review the
installation.
Before you install the PAK file, or upgrade your VCF Operations instance, clone any customized content to preserve it.
Customized content can include alert definitions, symptom definitions, recommendations, and views. While upgrading to
the latest version, you can select the Install the PAK file even if it is already installed and the Reset Default Content
options.

The Solutions Catalog Tab
You can add, manage, create, and download management packs in the Solutions Catalog tab in VCF Operations.
About Solutions Catalog
You can use the Solutions Catalog to discover and deploy curated, trusted, and certified solutions in your VCF
environment. From the Solutions Catalog tab, you can:
• View and download available management packs from VCF Solutions Catalog.
• Upload management packs .zip files in VCF Operations.
• Install, upgrade, or delete downloaded or uploaded management packs.
• Create custom management packs in VCF Operations.
If your VCF Operations instance is able to connect to VCF Solutions Catalog (requires outbound Internet connectivity from
VCF Operations), you can view, download, and install available management packs in the Solutions Catalog tab. For more
information, see Adding Management Packs from Solutions Catalog in Connected Mode.
If your VCF Operations instance cannot connect to VCF Solutions Catalog, you can manually upload management
pack .zip files in the Solutions Catalog tab. For more information, see Adding Management Packs from Solutions Catalog
in Disconnected Mode.
If you want to create a custom management pack in VCF Operations, click Create Management Pack on the Solutions
Catalog tab to create one. Once done, you can install it in VCF Operations. For more information, see Management Pack
Builder.
Broadcom 4534

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Migrating Management Packs
When you upgrade to VCF 9.1 from a prior version of VCF Operations, the upgrade migrates the installed management
packs.
• Migration Status:
– Only installed management packs are migrated.
– Downloaded but not installed management packs are removed. They must be re-downloaded and installed after the
upgrade.
• Post-Migration Limitation:
– You cannot view the Content and Resource & Support tabs for migrated management packs.
• Disconnected Mode:
– If VCF Operations is upgraded in disconnected mode, the icons for the migrated management packs will not be
displayed. To resolve this, you must switch to connected mode and either manually sync the management pack
inventories or wait for the scheduled sync which runs every 12 hours.
Adding Management Packs from Solutions Catalog in Connected Mode
If your VCF Operations instance is in connected mode, you can view and download available management packs in the
Solution Catalog tab in VCF Operations.
If your VCF Operations instance can successfully sync with VCF Solutions Catalog, all available management packs that
are associated with VCF Operations are displayed in the Available section of the Solutions Catalog tab.
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, select
Administration > Integrations, and then click the Solutions Catalog tab.
a) (Optional) Select a management pack and click View Details and click the Overview, Resource & Support, and
Tasks tabs to view the management pack details.
Note:
All actions performed on a management pack are displayed in the Tasks tab. You can review execution details for
any task, and access the corresponding error logs in the event of a failure.
On the Solutions Catalog tab, the Available section is displayed by default. All the management packs that are
compatible with the current version of VCF Operations are displayed.
2. Use the version selector to view the available versions and then select the version you want.
Note:
Only compatible versions of the management pack are displayed in the version selector.
3. Click Download, accept the EULA Agreement, and then click Download again.
The management pack is downloaded in VCF Operations. All downloaded management packs are listed in the
Downloaded section of the Solutions Catalog tab.
After you download a management pack in VCF Operations, you need to install it before you can use it. For more
information, see Installing and Uninstalling a Management Pack from Solutions Catalog.
Adding Management Packs from Solutions Catalog in Disconnected Mode
If your VCF Operations instance is in disconnected mode, you can download the management pack from VCF Solutions
Catalog and then upload it manually in the Solution Catalog tab in VCF Operations.
If your VCF Operations instance is unable to connect to VCF Solutions Catalog, no management pack will be displayed
in the Available section of the Solutions Catalog tab. In such cases, you can manually download management packs
and then upload them in VCF Operations. Optionally you can also upload a management pack that is not available in the
Solutions Catalog.
Broadcom 4535

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, select
Administration > Integrations, and then click the Solutions Catalog tab.
2. On the Solutions Catalog tab, click the VCF Solutions Catalog link to open the VCF Solutions Catalog webpage.
3. Manually download the desired management pack for VCF Operations. For more information, see VCF Solutions
Catalog Overview.
a) Log in to VCF Solutions Catalog webpage and then click Download for VCF-OPS to download the management
pack .zip file.
b) Enter the Key.
The Key is the asset key that is used when you download the management pack PAK file from VCF Solutions
Catalog.
The management pack .zip file is downloaded.
4. Unzip the management pack .zip file, return to the Solutions Catalog tab, and then click Upload.
5. Browse and select the management pack .zip file and then enter the Key.
You must enter the same key that you entered at the time of download.
The management pack is uploaded in VCF Operations. All uploaded management packs are listed in the Downloaded
section of the Solutions Catalog tab.
After you upload a management pack in VCF Operations, you must install it. For more information, see Installing and
Uninstalling a Management Pack from Solutions Catalog.
Installing and Uninstalling a Management Pack from Solutions Catalog
After downloading or uploading a management pack in VCF Operations, you must install it.
• Ensure you have downloaded or uploaded the management pack you want to install. For more information, see Adding
Management Packs from Solutions Catalog in Connected Mode and Adding Management Packs from Solutions
Catalog in Disconnected Mode.
To use a management pack, you must install it.
1. In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Operate and in the left navigation pane, select
Administration > Integrations, and then click the Solutions Catalog tab.
2. Click Downloaded to open the Downloaded section to see the list of management packs that have been downloaded
from the solutions catalog.
3. Locate the management pack you want to install and click View Details.
a) (Optional) Click the Overview, Metrics, Content, Resource & Support, and Tasks tabs to review the
management pack details.
Note:
Management packs that were downloaded but not installed before an upgrade are not migrated. If a previously
downloaded management pack does not appear on this page after upgrading to VCF 9.1, you must download it
again.
4.
5. Click Install, verify the Component Confirmation, and then click Install again.
The management pack is installed.
Broadcom 4536

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Optional: Click Sync Installed Solution to sync the management pack inventories on demand. By default, the
inventory in the VCF Operations Repository tab is synced with the VCF Solutions Catalog page every 12 hours.
7. Optional: Click Check for Updates to check for upgrades to previously downloaded management packs.
If an update is available for any management pack, the Upgrade button will become active, allowing you to download
the newer version. Upgrading a management pack will overwrite the old version's content with the new version's
content.
8. Optional: You can uninstall or delete a management pack that is no longer required. Uninstalling or deleting a
management pack, automatically deletes its associated accounts.
• Uninstall: Removes an installed management pack from the environment and moves it back to the Available
section of the Solutions Catalog tab, where it can be installed again. Locate the management pack you want to
uninstall and click Uninstall. Confirm that you want to uninstall the management pack, and then click Uninstall
again. The management pack is uninstalled.
• Delete: Permanently removes a management pack from the Solutions Catalog. Before you can delete a
management pack, you must first uninstall it. Locate the management pack you want to delete and click Delete.
Confirm that you want to delete the management pack, and then click Delete again. The management pack is
deleted.
All installed management packs are displayed on the Administration > Integrations > Repository tab. After installation,
you must add accounts for each management pack. Each account contains adapters using which VCF Operations
integrates with the management pack and monitors their function and health. For more details, see The Repository Tab.
If you delete a management pack from the respository page, only the management pack icon is removed from the
solutions catalog page. To remove the management pack completely from the solutions catalog page, either manually
sync the management pack inventories or wait for the scheduled sync which runs every 12 hours.
Management Pack Builder
The Management Pack Builder enables the creation of custom management packs for use in VCF Operations. This is a
no-code solution for bringing in data from an external API and either creating new resources or extending VCF Operations
and third party objects with new data, relationships, and events.
Backwards Compatibility
In VCF Operations, there is no separate installation required. It is pre-integrated into the VCF Operations platform,
reducing the initial installation time and eliminating compatibility issues.
The Management Pack Builder retains backward compatibility. Existing designs can be imported directly, preserving
previous work while leveraging new efficiencies and improved performance. This ensures a smooth transition for teams
who previously relied on the standalone Management Pack Builder.
Where you find the Management Pack Builder
In the VCF Operations navigation bar at the top, click Build and in the left navigation pane, click Developer Center >
Management Pack Builder.
What Can You Do in the Management Pack Builder page
You can use the Management Pack Builder page to design a new management pack, import or export a design, edit an
existing design, or delete an existing design. After you design a management pack, you can install it.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

• Install: Install the management pack.
To create a new management pack, click Create new design and enter the Name. The name
should only contain alphanumeric characters and spaces. Enter the Description, and select

Before you Start your Design
Before starting, you should make sure you have access to the reference environment including hostname, user
information, and API documentation. It is important to think about what you want to include in it. The main items to
understand are objects, requests, and relationships.
Broadcom 4538

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Things to Consider for designing a Management Pack using HTTP
• Objects: Objects are the core item that we will be adding or updating in VCF Operations . You should think of them
as the nouns of your technology. An example is a network switch. Your nouns for a switch could be the switch, ports,
CPUs, and fans. These would all become objects in your design. For every object, you will provide the metrics and
properties by adding one or more requests. VCF Operations manages metrics by the objects and has limits based
on number of objects and metrics. Please review the sizing guide for the appropriate sizing of VCF Operations when
designing your objects.
You can also extend existing objects in your VCF Operations environment such as VMs, Host Systems, or third-
party resources. By extending those objects, you can add metrics or properties to the existing object allowing custom
information to be used as if it was part of the original resource.
Note:
VCF Operations manages metrics by objects and imposes limits based on the number of objects.
• Requests: These are the API requests used to add metrics and properties. To understand what is available on these
requests, reference the API documentation. In our switch example, the requests to create port objects could include an
interface endpoint that lists all the ports and a stats endpoint that show the performance of the port.
• Relationships: Relationships associate objects to each other in a parent to child relationship. This creates a topology
for your objects allowing VCF Operations to understand the connectivity between your objects. In our switch example,
the switch would be the parent to the ports, CPUs, and fans. You can also add relationships to VCF Operations objects
like hosts, VMs, or third-party resources like data arrays.
• Events: Events represent a message reported by your endpoint pertaining to a VCF Operations object with an
associated severity. Events can be used to impact the health of an object using symptoms. These symptoms also can
be used to create alerts.
Things to Consider for designing a Management Pack using Prometheus
• Objects: Objects are the core item that we will be adding or updating in VCF Operations. You should think of them as
the nouns of your technology. In a Prometheus design, objects are associated with a specific Prometheus job. For
every object type, you will select the Prometheus metrics you would like to include and the labels on those metrics
which will be mapped to identifiers and properties on the object. VCF Operations manages metrics by the objects and
has limits based on number of objects and metrics. Please review the sizing guide for the appropriate sizing of VCF
Operations when designing your objects.
You can also extend existing objects in your environment such as VMs, Host Systems, or third-party resources. By
extending those objects, you can add metrics and properties to the existing object, allowing custom information to be
used as if it was part of the original resource.
Note:
VCF Operations manages metrics by objects and imposes limits based on the number of objects.
• Relationships: Relationships associate objects to each other in a parent to child relationship. This creates a topology
for your objects allowing VCF Operations to understand the connectivity between your objects. You can also add
relationships to objects like hosts, VMs, or third-party resources.
Creating A Regular Expression
A regular expression is a sequence of characters that define a search pattern, mainly for use in string matching.
Management Pack Builder supports Java-style regular expressions. When using a Regular Expression in Management
Pack Builder you can enter in the expression in the Regex field. When the test button is pressed the Sample Value will be
run through the expression and the result will be displayed in the Sample Output.
Regular expressions can be used in the following contexts:
• When defining fields that should match between objects when creating a relationship.
• When defining fields that should match between an event and the object it could be assigned to when creating an
event.
Broadcom 4539

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Variables
Custom authentication allows the user to add custom variables to be used in the advanced section of the source creation.
This is generally used with permanent session tokens, or any variable sent with every request.
Designing a Management Pack using HTTP
VCF Operations offers a wizard that makes it easy for you to design a management pack based on an HTTP API.
Building a new HTTP API-based management pack consists of the following steps. Once you start your design, you can
save your work and pick up from where you left off. You can edit an existing design at any step.
• Define a Data Source: In this initial step, you define the data source from which the management pack will collect
information. This involves specifying the external API or system that the management pack will integrate with, setting
up the necessary connection parameters, and ensuring that the data source is accessible for data retrieval.
• Set up API Requests: Here, you configure the specific API requests or queries that will be used to fetch data from the
defined source. This includes detailing the endpoints, request methods, parameters, and any necessary authentication
details to ensure successful data extraction.
• Define Objects: In this step, you define the objects that represent the data entities retrieved from the source. This
involves mapping the data to meaningful resource types within VCF Operations, specifying their properties, and
determining how they will be represented in the monitoring environment.
• Specify Relationships (Optional): This step focuses on establishing relationships between the defined objects.
By specifying how these objects interrelate, you can create a structured representation of the data, which aids in
understanding dependencies and interactions within the monitored environment.
• Define Events (Optional): Here, you create an event from an API by defining the message, severity, and assoicated
objects. You can configure symptoms and alerts for significant events in VCF Operations after designing the
management pack.
• Verify your Design: In this step, you validate the configurations made in the previous steps. This involves testing the
data collection, ensuring that objects and relationships are correctly defined, and confirming that events trigger as
expected. It’s a crucial step to ensure the management pack functions as intended before deployment.
• Install: This is the final step. After you have reviewed and verified the design, you can install the management pack.
Define a Source
Start by identifying the source system or API from which you intend to pull data. This step includes specifying host name,
connection settings, and authentication protocols.
Sub-sections in Define Source
• Data Source Connections
• Get Session (visible if you turn on session authentication)
• Global Settings
• Release Session (visible if you turn on session authentication)
• Test Connection
Data Source Connections
• Collector: The collector node or cloud proxy from which the Management Pack Builder adapter instance will make API
requests during the design process.
• Host Name:The target you're pulling data from.
• Port:The port to use.
• TLS Configuration: Select from one of the following options:
– Verify: Use TLS and verify the target's certificate.
– No Verify: Use TLS but don't verify the target's certificate.
– No TLS: Do not use TLS at all, for example, HTTP only.
• Base Path: Path to be prepended to all API calls defined in this design including the Session authentication. You can
leave it blank and use the full path for all requests if there is no shared prefix.
Broadcom 4540

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Preview API Path: A preview of your full path.
Authentication Details
Configure the authentication details for your API requests.
Choose between basic authentication, custom authentication, and no authentication. The configuration here is used for
every subsequent call, so you only need to configure authentication once. If you need to create a session token, before
making connection requests, turn on Use Session Authentication.
The Management Pack Builder can use three different authentication source types:
• Basic: Specify a username and password. The header is automatically created.
– Username: The user on reference system that is authorized to query the intended API endpoint.
– Password: User’s password for authentication.
• Custom: Add authentication fields and headers.
– Use custom authentication when you need to add custom variables to be used in the advanced section of the
source creation.
– This is generally used with permanent session tokens or any variable sent with every request if session
authentication is not used.
– It is generally used for login credentials that will be used in POST a post body to get the session token when using
session authenication.
• No Authentication: Use for public and non-secured APIs.
You can next choose to turn on Session Authentication. Session authentication is a method in which a session is
created on login and stores information from the response body and/or headers as defined by the user. Common fields
include a token or a session ID. When running a collection, the session fields are retrieved once, then used on all
subsequent requests. If a release session request is defined, the session is released at the end of the collection.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Get Session
Define the HTTP Method and API Path when using session authentication.
• HTTP Method: Based on the API requirements this will be either a GET, POST, PUT, PATCH.
• API Path: This is the path to the session creation resource as defined by the API documentation.
Next, set up additional request settings, such as headers, query parameters, and body
• HTTP Headers: This is used to assign headers to the request that is used to retrieve the session. This only needs
to be used if the API requires custom values in the header. If using basic credentials, the Authorization header is
automatically added and thus does not need further configuration.
• Query Parameters: This section allows the user to add custom query prompts to the end of the URL request. This is
optional and only necessary if the API documentation calls for it.
• Body: This allows you to create a body to be sent to the session creation request. Some APIs require the body to
contain information like user and password. This is optional and only needs to be used if the API documentation
indicates it.
Click Test to see the test response. VCF Operations displays the Body, Headers and Log.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Global Settings
Define the headers which are used to pass data with every call in the request header. Session data should be put here so
that every call includes the session ID or token information.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Broadcom 4541

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Release Session
Defining a Release Session Request is recommended when using session authentication. This request will log out the
session, reduce session leaks, and improve security.
• HTTP Method: Based on the API requirements this will be either a GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
• API Path: This is the path to the API endpoint you want to use to release the session.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Test Session
In this step, you to define the HTTP Method being used (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH), the API path, and see a preview of
the fully qualified path. Then, you click TEST CONNECTION.
• HTTP Method: Based on the API requirements this will be either a GET, POST, PUT, PATCH.
• API Path: This is the path to test that your defined authentication works for your API.
The test connection confirms that all the source data is set up correctly. If using basic authentication, this will send one
request including the basic authentication header. If using the session, this will make up to three requests to create the
session, make a call to the test endpoint, then make a call to delete the session.
The response section will show the response to the test connection endpoint. You can see the body and headers of the
response as well as the logs generated by the request. You can download the test response as a JSON file.
Once you are done, click SAVE SOURCE.
Add Requests
This is the second step of the wizard. You can add all the API calls used by the design to provide data to the objects and
events. You will need to reference your API documentation to determine the endpoint and settings necessary for this
section.
Add API Request and API Pagination
In the Add API Request section, define the endpoint to be used for the request. Note: the source hostname, port, and
base path will be prepended to this path for the request URL.
• HTTP Method: This is the method used for the request. It will be either a GET, PUT, PATCH, or POST.
• API Path: Endpoint that needs to be call to retrieve the data.
• Name: Name for this request used in future settings in the design.
Advanced (optional)
In this section you can add specific data to the requests body, headers, and query parameters, as defined by the API
documentation.
Once you are done, click SAVE REQUEST.
You can also add paging to your API call in the Add API Pagination section. You must make the request prior to
configuring paging. Management Pack Builder supports two main methods of pagination: offset and pages. Reference
your API documentation to determine whether paging is necessary and, if so, which method to use.
• Paging Parameter: This is the parameter name to use to indicate which page we are requesting.
• Starting Offset: This is the number that represents the beginning of the API's results. Often, "Pages" start at 1 and
"Offset" starts at 0. Confirm the starting number in the API documentation.
• Limit Parameter: This is the parameter name for the number of records per page.
• Limit Value: The number of records returned per page.
• Data List Returned from Paged Request: List of data being returned. When the count of this is less than the limit value,
it means that the end of the data has been reached and no more paged requests will be made.
Chain From Other API Calls
To add a chained request, return to the wizard, go to the Requests step, and select the parent request from requests list,
then select Add Chained.
Broadcom 4542

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• In the Add Chaining section, select a list from the parent request's response which contains the attribute(s) to be used
in the child request.
• System Attributes: For each attribute that you would like to use in the child request, select Add Field. Select the
Attribute. If desired, update the Parameter. The Parameter will be used to define the usage key, so make sure that
it is meaningful in the context of the design. If the parent request had a value for the selected attribute, it will populate
by default. Regardless, you can manually set the value here. This is the value that will be substituted for the usage key
later when testing the child request, so make sure that it is a valid value which will cause the child request to succeed.
• In the Add API Request section, define the child request like any other request, but now you can use the attribute(s)
defined in the previous step. You can insert the usage key in the path, headers, query parameters, and/or body of the
child request. To insert the attribute usage key, click the clipboard icon on the right side of the field, then select the
attribute you want to insert. It will be inserted where the cursor is currently located in the field. When the request is run
via MAKE REQUEST, all usage keys will be replaced with the sample values defined in the previous step.
Once you are done, click SAVE REQUEST.
Add Objects
In the third step, you define the objects that will be part of your custom management pack. You can define new objects or
extend existing objects from VCF Operations with new metrics and properties.
Sub-Sections in Add New and Add Existing Objects
• Object Type
• Attributes from API
• Properties and Metrics
• Name and Identifiers (Section appears only when adding new objects.)
• Object Bindings (Section appears when there is an existing object or when the attribue selections require it)
Object Type
• Add New Object Type: The object type is the user-facing label that will be displayed for this type of object in VCF
Operations when this management pack is installed. Example object types are Switch, Port, etc. You can also choose
the icon that will be used in VCF Operations. Once you are done, click NEXT.
• Add Existing Object: To extend an existing object, choose a resource type to extend from the list of resource types on
your VCF Operations instance. You can filter by the resource type or page through the list of available options.
Attributes from API
From the list of Requests, you select one or more requests to pull into this object. You will then select all the data entries
you want to add to your object from the list. You can search the list of attributes for a specific attribute or scroll through the
list.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Properties and Metrics
Here you will see the metric and property definitions you have attached to the object.
• Label: The name of the metric or property visible in VCF Operations.
• Datatype: Defines how the data is rendered. If you select decimal or one of the counter options and the data cannot be
converted to a number, the data will be discarded.
– String: Returns the value of the attribute as a string. This datatype is allowed only on properties, and not metrics.
– Decimal: Returns the value of the attribute as a number.
– Counter Delta: Calculates the change in the value between collections.
– Counter Rate: Calculates the change in value between collections over time.
• Unit: If applicable, this is where you can define the unit for the data point. This will allow auto-scaling in dashboards
and reports.
• Property: This drop-down list indicates whether the data is a property.
Broadcom 4543

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• KPI: This toggle indicates whether the data will be treated as a KPI. KPIs are key metrics that are used in dashboards
and resource detail pages. They should be metrics that are important to the status, performance, and health of the
object.
• Expanded row view:
• Request: Shows the call and data path from which this metric is pulled.
• List: List in the request response from which the data is pulled.
• Attribute: Name of the attribute in the response being pulled.
• Example: Shows the value of the first returned data point from the request.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Name and Identifiers
Define the identity of the object in this step.
• Object Instance Name: This is the property from the list above that is used as the object's name in VCF Operations.
• Object Identifiers: Define the properties using the smallest set of properties that will accurately and uniquely identify
each object.
Once you are done, click SAVE OBJECT. If you see Attribute Bindings, proceed to the next step.
Attribute Bindings
When combining data from multiple JSON or XML arrays into a single new object, it's necessary to establish a base
array and select a corresponding attribute from each of the other arrays for mapping. You will only see this section if it is
required.
When extending an existing object, all arrays must link to a property or identifier on the existing object in VCF Operations.
• API Attribute: The data from the selected JSON or XML list in the API response that you match to an existing property
or identifier.
• Object Property: A matching property or identifier on the object. For a new object, it is selected from the base list. For
an extended object, it is selected from the identifiers and properties of the existing object.
Best Practices For Metrics and Properties
Follow these best practices when you create objects from new metrics and properties.
Best Practices
• Objects created from new metrics and properties should represent stable objects, not transient objects.
• Metrics should represent measurable performance characteristics. Example: CPU Utilization %, Network Throughput,
etc. Properties should represent relatively stable configuration values. Example: version, power status, etc.
• Properties should have a small number of possible values.
• Property values should not change frequently from collection to collection.
• Opt for defining metrics using reasonable unit sizes and prefix multipliers to avoid publishing excessively large values.
• The depth of the relationships of the objects should not be too deep (for example 100).
• Avoid defining artificial relationships that do not exist in the end-point.
Define Object Relationships
Relationships are a parent to child connection that is used in VCF Operations to define the interaction between
interconnected resources. Parent to child relationships are the only supported type of relationships with the Management
Pack Builder.
Parent and Child object
Define the objects used to create the relationships. Parent objects are higher in the topology.
Broadcom 4544

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Matching Properties
Relationships in Management Pack Builder are created by matching all resources with matching properties. For example,
a Switch has a switch ID property and the Port has a parent switch ID property. The parent object properties and the
properties of any relevant child object(s) will always match, e.g. switch ID with parent switch ID. With multiple matching
sets, all sets of properties must match for the relationship to be created. This can be either case-sensitive or insensitive
and use basic or advanced matching.
Once you are done, click SAVE RELATIONSHIP.
Add New Events
Map events from the target system into the VCF Operations event model. This includes defining event triggers and
mapping severity levels, and linking them to VCF Operations objects.
Sub-sections in this step
• Add Events from API
• Severity
• Related Objects
Add Events from API
• Event Name: The user-friendly name of the event. This will be prefixed on the event message in VCF Operations.
• API Request: This is the request endpoint setup in the Requests section to use to create events.
• Event List: The location of events in the API response.
• Event Message: This is the event message that will show in VCF Operations. Often in APIs this would be the event
description. You can create the message using one or more fields from the response and type any static information
as well. You can also edit the value of the fields using regular expressions. See the section on regular expressions for
further help on this.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Severity
Events in VCF Operations are ranked with a severity from Info to Immediate. Please reference your API documentation for
a list of valid severities they support.
• Event Severity: Define API response fields and static text which form the event severity definition. You can also adjust
the value of the fields using regular expression.
• Map Severities: Add mappings from the VCF event severity (Event Severity) to the corresponding value expected
from the API (API Response Severity). For example, if the API returns "critical," you would map to the VCF "Critical"
severity. Sometimes an API will have a severity that does not directly correspond to a VCF severity. In that case, the
mapping is up to your discretion. For example, if any API returns an event severity of Severe, you must map that to the
VCF severity "Critical," or "Immediate."
• Set all unmatched API response Severities to: Specify a default severity. If an event severity is returned from the API
that does not match one of the mappings you created, the associated event will be set to the default severity specified
here.
Once you are done, click NEXT.
Related Objects
Relate events to objects by matching. Select "All" if you want to related events to more than one object in the case that
multiple related objects match. Select "First" if you only want the first related object to match.
The order defined in this section is the order in which the management pack will evaluate matches.
Add related object: For each related object, first select the object type (Select object) to relate to. By default, you can
choose any object types included in the current design. If you select "All objects", you can also choose from existing
object types in VCF Operations. Next, create a mapping from the object properties to the API response. You can use any
combination of object properties, API response fields, static text, and regular expressions to make the mapping work. In
Broadcom 4545

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
the top-right, you can choose whether the matching logic should be case-sensitive. If you define multiple related objects
and selected "Relate events to objects by matching: First", you can use the arrows on the left to change the order in which
the mappings will be evaluated.
Once you are done, click SAVE EVENT.
Verify your Design
Before final deployment, you can test your design to ensure that the management pack collects the correct data and
accurately represents the target system within VCF Operations.
Perform Collection
Click PERFORM COLLECTION to verify your design.
VCF Operations runs the collection and displays the following information:
• Summary: Displays the Collection Status, Collection Time, Objects Collected, Metrics Collected, Properties
Collected, Relationships Found, and Events Collected.
• Log: Displays the last 1000 lines. You can download the log to view all the lines. You can change the logging level to
see more detailed logs.
• Objects: Displays the details for the objects.
• Events: Displays the events for the objects.
Once you are done, go to the final step, INSTALL.
Install
Once testing is complete, click REVIEW CONFIGURATION or directly click INSTALL. VCF Operations installs the
management pack, making it available for live monitoring.
Designing a Management Pack using Prometheus
VCF Operations offers a wizard that makes it easy for you to design a management pack from Prometheus data.
Building a Prometheus-based management pack consists of the following steps. Once you start your design, you can
save your work and pick up from where you left off. You can edit an existing design at any step.
• Define a Data Source: In this initial step, you define the Prometheus data source from which the management pack will
collect information. You must specify the Prometheus instance that the management pack will integrate with, setting up
the authentication, and ensuring that Prometheus is accessible for data retrieval. For more information, see Define a
Source.
• Define Objects: In this step, you map metrics that are retrieved from Prometheus to meaningful objects and metrics
within VCF Operations. For more information, see Add Objects.
• Specify Relationships: This step focuses on establishing relationships between the defined objects. By specifying
how these objects interrelate, you can create a structured representation of the data, which aids in understanding
dependencies and interactions within the monitored environment. For more information, see Define Object
Relationships.
• Verify your Design: In this step, you validate the configurations that were made in the previous steps. It also involves
testing the data collection and ensuring that objects and relationships are correctly defined. It’s a crucial step to
ensure the management pack functions as intended before deployment. For more information, see Define Object
Relationships.
• Install: As the final step, after you have reviewed and verified the design, you can install the management pack. For
more information, see Install.
Define a Source
Start by identifying the Prometheus instance from which you intend to pull data. This step includes specifying the IP
address or FQDN, API port, TLS configuration, and authentication settings.
Broadcom 4546

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Data Source Connections
• Collector: The collector node or cloud proxy from which the Management Pack Builder adapter instance will make
requests to Prometheus during the design process.
• Prometheus Host: the IP address, hostname, or FQDN for the Prometheus instance that will be used during the design
process.
• Port: The port hosting the Prometheus APIs. The default is 9090.
• TLS Configuration: Select from one of the following options:
– Verify: Use TLS and verify the target's certificate
– No Verify: Use TLS but do not verify the target's certificate
– No TLS: Do not use TLS at all
• Authentication Type: Select from one of the following options:
– Basic: Specify a username and password
– No Authentication: No credentials are required
Once the form is complete, click Test Connection. The test connection confirms that the Prometheus instance is
accessible with the provided configuration information and the API is returning the expected data.
The Test Response section shows you the list of jobs available on the Prometheus instance. In Prometheus, each type
of monitored technology typically corresponds to one job. For example, all Clickhouse-related metrics are defined with the
“clickhouse” job. By default, Prometheus defines its own self-monitoring metrics under the “prometheus” job.
The Test Response section also shows a Log tab, where you can review the test connection logs. If you are seeing a
failed test connection, review the logs to determine the root cause of the failure.
Once you are done, click Save Source.
Add Objects
Next, select Prometheus metrics that you want to convert into VCF Operations metrics and objects. Prometheus metrics
have labels which can be used to uniquely identify objects. Prometheus metrics can be filtered and processed during their
conversion to VCF Operations metrics.
Add New Object Type
1. Object Type:
– Object Type: The type which will be assigned and visible in VCF Operations.
– Prometheus Job: In Prometheus, each type of monitored technology typically corresponds to one job. Select which
type of technology will be associated with this object type.
– Object Icon: Select an icon to represent this object type. By default, all icons are shown. Select a category
to filter the icons shown. After a management pack is installed, custom icons can optionally be uploaded in
Administration > Control Panel > Icons.
2. Prometheus Data: Prometheus metrics related to the job selected previously are shown. Select the metrics that should
comprise the new VCF Operations object type. Use the search bar to filter on metric name and label.
Note:
When defining object identifiers, you will only be able to select labels that are shared across all the selected
metrics. All Prometheus metrics have the “instance” label by default.
3. Identifiers and Name: Select one or more labels to uniquely identify the objects in VCF Operations. You can optionally
update the text that will be shown in the VCF Operations UI.
After the identifying labels are defined, select one of them to be used as the object name.
4. Metrics Mapping: Each Prometheus metric selected previously is shown. A Prometheus metric can be mapped to one
or more VCF Operations metrics on the new object type.
– Metric Label: Optionally update the metric label to be shown in VCF Operations UI.
– Function: The selection for function varies depending on the type of Prometheus metric:
• Gauge metrics always use the Current Total function. This means the VCF Operations metric will report the sum
of the latest values returned.
• Counter and summary metrics can use a Delta or Rate function.

the Prometheus metric.
• Rate: The VCF Operations metric will report the difference between the current value and previous value of
the Prometheus metric, divided by the time elapsed between collections.
– Units: Specify the unit for this metric.

VCF Operations metric calculation. For example, you may want to split an HTTP Response metric into multiple VCF
Operations metrics by filtering on response codes (2xx -> Successes, 4xx -> Failures, etc.).

Importing or Exporting a Design
A JSON file is created when exporting a design. A JSON file can be imported into VCF Operations. The file is verified as a
valid design file and the author and description are shown. Only valid designs can be exported.
Importing a Design
To import a design, click the Import button in the Management Pack Builder page. Browse to the location of the JSON file
in your system. Only one design can be imported at a time.
VCF Operations verifies the validity and displays the name and description of the design. Ensure that another design of
the same name does not exist. The design that you are importing must have a unique name.
After you import the design, it is displayed in the Management Pack Builder page. Verify the information in the Design
Status column. You must provide the reference environment to test the design against. Click the imported design, and in
the Source step of the wizard, specify the required fields.
Exporting a Design
Before you export a design, ensure that it does not contain private information, such as IP addresses, credentials, or IDs,
outside of end-user configurable fields. Before sharing or storing your exported design in an unsecured location, review
the export file to ensure it does not include any private information.
A zip file containing the JSON file is exported. You must extract the JSON file from the zip file before you can import it.
Note:
You can export a design only if its status is Verified or Valid.
Troubleshooting a Design
1. Request Log: Every time you make a test request or perform a test collection in Management Pack Builder, there are
tabs which show the body, headers, and logs. In the case of an error response code, review the logs and headers for
information regarding the cause of the error.
2. Third-party API documentation: ensure that the request you defined complies with the requirements described in the
third-party API documentation.
3. Management Pack Builder Adapter logs: located under on the
$VCOPS_BASE/user/log/adapters/MPBAdapter
node or cloud proxy selected under Source. Review these logs for any additional errors or warnings.
4. If you suspect an error with the Management Pack Builder tool itself, you can open a support case, or review the
server logs at . You can also
/usr/lib/vmware-vcops/user/log/integration-designer-controller.log
review the Suite API logs at .
/usr/lib/vmware-vcops/user/log/suite-api for additional errors
