Supported VMware Cloud Accounts
You can add VMware Cloud on AWS - vCenter account and NSX Manager account in VCF Operations for networks to
monitor your VMware Cloud on AWS network.
Note:
VCF Operations for networks supports many types of NSX Manager accounts such as VMC on AWS NSX
Manager, Azure VMware Solution NSX Manager, and Oracle Cloud VMware Solution NSX Manager.
To add VMware Cloud on AWS - vCenter account and NSX Manager account in VCF Operations for networks as data
source, you must Manually Configure Data Sources for VMware Cloud on AWS.
Manually Configure Data Sources for VMware Cloud on AWS
To monitor your VMware Cloud on AWS environment, you must set up the VCF Operations for networks collector to
collect data from VMware Cloud on AWS, and add VMware Cloud on AWS -vCenter and VMware Cloud on AWS - NSX
Manager as data sources.
Broadcom 4865

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Preparing VCF Operations for networks to add VMware Cloud on AWS
You must setup VCF Operations for networks collector and configure firewall rules in VMware Cloud on AWS for
communication and data collection.
Set up VCF Operations for networks Collector for VMware Cloud on AWS
You must set up the VCF Operations for networks collector to collect data from VMware Cloud on AWS.
Deploy a VCF Operations for networks collector within every SDDC that needs to be added as a data source.
Important:
• Using a VCF Operations for networks collector deployed in one VMware Cloud on AWS SDDC to collect data
from another VMware Cloud on AWS SDDC is not supported.
• You must deploy the VCF Operations for networks collector on a native VMware Cloud on AWS segment.
Deploying a collector on extended segments is not supported.
1. Log in to VCF Operations for networks.
2. Navigate to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Add Collector VM.
3. Copy the contents of the shared secret.
You will require this during the deployment of VCF Operations for networks Collector OVA.
4. Deploy the VCF Operations for networks Collector OVA in the Compute Resource Pool of the VMware Cloud on AWS
vCenter.
Use the shared secret that you have generated.
Note:
For a single node SDDC in VMware Cloud on AWS, CPU resource reservation for the collector VM must be at
least 1251 MHz.
5. Start the collector VM and follow the wizard to pair the collector with the VCF Operations for networks platform.
Note:
During this step, you must configure Web proxies and Firewall rules for VMware Cloud on AWS.
6. Validate that the collector pairs successfully with the platform.
Configuring Web Proxies for VMware Cloud on AWS
Depending on the scenario you are using, you must configure web proxies to connect to other entities (data sources,
cloud service platforms, and so on) when the connection is made over the Internet.
Web Proxy Configuration Scenarios
• Scenario 1: Web Proxy not configured.
You do not need any web proxy configuration.
• Scenario 2: When the Collector is in VMware Cloud on AWS and the Collector is using the web proxy to connect to
.
vmc.vmware.com
You must enable the web proxy through the user interface (UI). To know how to configure web proxy, see Configuring
Web Proxies.
Broadcom 4866

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Scenario 3: When the Platform is on-premises and the Platform is using a web proxy to connect to CSP.
You must use CLI to enable web proxy (HTTP anonymous and basic authentication web proxy only) in the Platform. To
know about enabling web proxy using CLI, see set-web-proxy.
Create VMware Cloud on AWS Firewall Rules for VCF Operations for networks
You must create VMware Cloud on AWS groups and firewall rules to build communication with VCF Operations for
networks.
Prerequisites:
• Deploy VCF Operations for networks platform and collector (for on-premise) or get the valid subscription (for cloud
service).
• You must have required privileges. See Add VMware Cloud on AWS - vCenter and Add VMware Cloud on AWS NSX
Manager.
• Deploy a VMware Cloud on AWS software-defined data center (SDDC) 1.8 and later with NSX-T networking.
• For the port requirements of incoming traffic, see VMware Ports and Protocols.
• Ensure you allow the HTTPS port 443 in the firewall to communicate between the Collector and the following domain:
Broadcom 4867

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
–
*.vmc.vmware.com
• Ensure you allow the HTTPS port 443 in the firewall to communicate between the Platforms and the following domain:
–
console.cloud.vmware.com
Configure Firewall Rules for communication between VCF Operations for networks platform and collector
Configuring firewall rules in VMware Cloud on AWS includes:
• Creating a VMware Cloud on AWS group for VCF Operations for networks collector.
a. Log in to VMware Cloud on AWS at https://vmc.vmware.com.
b. On the Networking & Security tab, click Inventory > Groups.
c. On the Groups card, click COMPUTE GROUPS, then click ADD GROUP and give the group a Name and an
optional Description.
d. Click Set Members to open the Select Members page.
e. Provide the VCF Operations for networks collector VM details.
You use this group in the firewall rules that you create later to allow communication between VMware Cloud on
AWS NSX Manager and VCF Operations for networks.
• Create a firewall rule.
a. Log in to the VMC Console at https://vmc.vmware.com.
b. On the Networking & Security tab, click Gateway Firewall.
c. On the Gateway Firewall card, click Compute Gateway, then click ADD RULE and give the new rule a Name.
d. Enter the parameters for the new rule.
• Sources: Enter the name of the VMware Cloud on AWS group containing the VCF Operations for networks
collector IP address.
• Destinations: Select Any.
• Services: Select HTTPS, DNS, DNS-UDP, NTP, ICMP.
• Action: Select Allow.
• Applied To: Select Internet Interface.
• Logging: Enable logging if required. Else this field is unchanged.
The new rule is enabled by default. Slide the toggle to the left to deactivate it.
e. Click Publish.
Configure Firewall Rules for communication between collector and NSX Manager, and collector and vCenter
1. Log in to the VMC Console at https://vmc.vmware.com.
2. On the Networking & Security tab, click Gateway Firewall.
3. On the Gateway Firewall card, click Management Gateway, then click ADD RULE and give the new rule a Name.
4. Enter the parameters for the new rule.
– Sources: Enter the name of the VMware Cloud on AWS group containing the VCF Operations for networks
collector IP address.
– Destinations: Select System Defined Groups, search for NSX Manager, and then select the NSX Manager entry.

Add Palo Alto Networks Panorama
You can add Palo Alto Networks Panorama as a data source in VCF Operations for networks.
You must ensure that:
• The data source and its version is supported in VCF Operations for networks. For more information, see Supported
Products and Versions.
• The data source follows VMware Ports and Protocols supported in VCF Operations for networks. For more information,
see VMware Ports and Protocols.
• You have admin role with XML API access. For more details, see Palo Alto Firewall.
In the Panorama UI, perform the following steps to add an admin role for XML API.
1. Select Panorama > Admin Roles.
2. Click Add to add a new admin role.
3. In the The Admin Role Profile window, enter the name to the role and select Panorama.
4. Click the Web UI tab and deactivate all entries.
5. Click the XML API tab and deactivate all entries, except Configuration and Operational Requests.
6. Click OK to close the window.
The new admin role appears in the list.

VCF Operations for networks supports the following features of Palo Alto firewall:
• Neighbor Discovery (LLDP)
• Layer 3 Routing (IPv4)
• Virtual Router
• Virtual Wire (Supported only in network assurance and verification)
• Security Policy
• Security Zone
• Virtual System (Not supported in network assurance and verification)
Note:

Products and Versions.
• VCF Operations for networks requires read-only privileges for the Web-API access for fetching most of the Check
Point data. There are few exceptions as follows:
– If a non-VSX physical gateway is attached to the management server, the user should have read-write access
privileges for the Web API. This is required to fetch the gateway routes for using the Web API for the
run script
VM-VM path computation.
– If a VSX gateway is attached to the management server, the user should have the SSH access with the same
password. In addition, the user should have access to the CLI command . This
vsx_util view_vs_conf
command is used to fetch the VSX gateway routes for the VM-VM path computation.
– For MDS server IP as data-source, the user should have the Web API access to all domains including the MDS
domain and the global domain. It is required to fetch rules, policy packages and other data from all the domains.

check box. When you select this option, the tag gets applied to all associated entities. For more details about the

Configuring and Managing Dropped Flow Alerts for Palo Alto and Check Point Firewalls in VCF Operations
You can use VCF Operations to handle any dropped flow alerts that you receive from your Palo Alto or Check Point
firewalls.
• Verify that log management is added as a data source in VCF Operations for networks.
• Verify that log management is configured as Syslog server for the firewalls. For more information, see Update Syslog
server for Check Point and Palo Alto firewalls.
• Verify that port 514 and port 1514 are open. These ports are used to communicate with log management.
When log management reports a dropped flow that is received from a Check Point or a Palo Alto firewall device VCF
Operations sends an alert.
1. Download and install the VMware Cloud Foundation Content Pack for VCF Operations for networks from the VCF
Solutions Catalog.
2. To check for received dropped flow alerts, navigate to Operate > Alerts and expand Log Fallback Object.
3. To identify the cause for the dropped flow, select the alert, and select analyze logs from the Recommendations
section.
The Analyze Logs tab of the Logs page opens. The Stream tab contains the details of the dropped flow alert, which
you can use to troubleshoot the issue.

Enabling Telemetry on Dell OS10 Switches
You can enable streaming telemetry on the Dell OS10 switches to integrate buffer statistics and tracking on Dell switches.
Broadcom 4899

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
After adding Dell OS10 switches as a data source in VCF Operations for networks , you can enable streaming telemetry
on the switches to send buffer related information to the VCF Operations for networks collector.
The VCF Operations for networks collector ingests this telemetry information and extracts the
per-port egress
metric. This metric can be used to diagnose network congestion at a particular switchport
buffer peak utilization
in the network, and to identify application performance issues.
If the peak buffer utilization exceeds a threshold of 10 MB, VCF Operations for networks raises the
Switchport Buffer
alert.
Threshold Exceeded Event
Here is an example on how to configure streaming telemetry on a Dell OS10 switch:
telemetry
enable
!
destination-group dg03
Aria-Ops-for-Networks Collector IP
destination 50000
!
subscription-profile sp03
sensor-group buffer 15000
destination-group dg03
encoding gpb
transport grpc no-tls
source-interface ethernet1/1/1
end
For more information about configuring telemetry, see the Dell EMC User Guide.

Supported Cisco ACI Contracts

• Application EPG to L3Out EPG Contract between VRF
• Intra Ext-EPG Contract

• L3Out to L3Out Contract

Add VCF Operations for logs

are shown in VCF Operations for networks.

Supported DNS Data Providers
VCF Operations for networks supports DNS providers like Infoblox.
Add Infoblox
VCF Operations for networks allows you to add Infoblox Grid as a DNS data provider in VCF Operations for networks.
Broadcom 4915

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You must verify the following information:
• The data source and its version is supported in VCF Operations for networks. For more information, see Supported
Products and Versions.
• The data source follows VMware Ports and Protocols supported in VCF Operations for networks. For more information,
see VMware Ports and Protocols.
Infoblox DNS offers an advanced solution to manage and control DNS. It uses Infoblox Grid to ensure that the DNS is
highly available throughout the network. The DNS data from Infoblox is used only for enriching the flows where either the
source or the destination IP addresses are associated with the physical devices.
The Infoblox DNS data co-exists with the DNS data that is imported by using CSV.
Infoblox does not need a dedicated collector. If you have configured an Infoblox DNS data source on a collector, you can
use the same collector to configure other data sources on it.
Considerations
• VCF Operations for networks supports only single-grid mode for Infoblox in the current release.
• Only A Records are supported in the current release. Shared A Records are not supported currently.
• The DNS enrichment is supported only for the IP addresses that are marked as physical in the current release.
• If there are multiple FQDNs for a single physical IP address, all FQDNs are returned.

Supported CMDBs
VCF Operations for networks supports addition of CMDBs like ServiceNow.
Broadcom 4919

CMDB Concepts
Basically, a CMDB consists of:
• Configuration item: An entity or a component in a system. Example, a computer, a switch, a service, an application, a
server, or a VM.
• Relationship: a link or a type of communication between configuration items. Example: depends on, runs on,
exchanges data.
Each configuration item has a defined schema.
• Configuration Item Class: Each configuration item must be associated with a class, which defines its properties.
• Relationship class: Defines the type of relation between configuration items.
You can extend both the classes to add additional properties or customize the properties.
ServiceNow supports application service, which is a set of interconnected applications and hosts that offer a service.
ServiceNow allows you to create an application service manually, by using an API, or can automatically discover by
Service Mapping. All these applications are stored in ServiceNow CMDB.
When you add a ServiceNow datasource into VCF Operations for networks, VCF Operations for networks fetches the
configurations items and the relationships from the ServiceNow CMDB configuration file.
VCF Operations for networks fetches data in regular intervals, by default.
• The complete data fetch happens every 12 hours, which fetches all the records of the classes defined the CMDB
configuration. Also, the complete fetch happens when you add or update the datasource.
• The delta fetch happens every 2 minutes, which fetches all new, modified, and deleted records of the classes defined
in the CMDB configuration. Approximately, VCF Operations for networks takes around 12 minutes to reflect these
details on the user interface.
VCF Operations for networks fetches the class hierarchy and the relationship types during complete fetch only.

Note:
If you do not have access to tables/APIs marked as Optional, then VCF Operations for networks runs the
application discovery at every 12 hours. And if you have access to tables/APIs marked as Optional, VCF
Operations for networks runs application discovery at every 30 minutes.
With ServiceNow integration, VCF Operations for networks can discover applications available in ServiceNow CMDB to
enable you to directly add them into VCF Operations for networks.
1. From the left navigation pane, go to Settings > Accounts and Data Sources.
2. Click Add Source.
3. Under CMDBs, select ServiceNow.
4. On the Add a new ServiceNow Account or Source page, provide the following details:
Option Action
Collector (Proxy) VM Select a collector VM from the drop-down menu.
Broadcom 4921

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Action
IP Address/FQDN Enter the IP address or the FQDN details.
Username Enter the user name.
Password Enter the password.
Web Proxy (Optional) Select a web proxy from the drop-down menu.
Note:
The Web Proxy (Optional) is visible only if you
have configured a web proxy in VCF Operations for
networks.
5. Click Validate.
6. To add a customized CMDB configuration, do the following:
a) Select Customize CMDB configuration.
b) Click download to download the default configuration file.
c) Update the file properties. See, Customizing the CMDB Configuration.
d) On the Add Data Source page, browse to select the updated JSON file.
Note:
If you add customize CMDB configuration, then VCF Operations for networks validates all the newly added entries
for Required privileges.
7. Optional: In the Nickname text box, enter a nickname.
8. Optional: In the Notes text box, add a note if necessary.
9. Click Submit.
After you add a ServiceNow data source, VCF Operations for networks discovers the applications available in the
ServiceNow CMDB, which you add into VCF Operations for networks. For more information, see Discover Applications.

Customizing the CMDB Configuration
To support various customizations, the ServiceNow and VCF Operations for networks integration supports a generic
configuration. The CMDB configuration must be in the JSON format.
The configuration includes:
• the configuration items
• the relation between the configuration items
• the rules for the dependency graph traversal.
You can customize the CMDB configuration based on your implementations.
Broadcom 4926

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

When you change the configuration, a complete fetch happens and all the applications are recomputed. So, this
process might take at least 30 minutes to appear on the Discovered Application Dashboard.

FAQs on Add ServiceNow as a Data Source
You find all the common frequently asked questions related to adding ServiceNow as a data source in this topic.
How to Assign Privileges to a Role in ServiceNow for adding in VCF Operations for networks?
1. Create a Role in ServiceNow UI.
2. Click System Administrator > Elevate Roles > security_admin > OK.
3. Go to Access Control (ACL), and click New.
4. For API access, do the following:
Option Action
Type Select REST_Endpoint from the drop-down menu.
Operation Select execute from the drop-down menu.
Name From the drop-down menu select the API entry that you want to
add. For list of APIs, see Add a ServiceNow Account topic.
5. For tables, do the following:
Option Action
Type Select record from the drop-down menu.
Operation Select read from the drop-down menu.
Name From the first drop-down menu, select the table entry that you
want to add. From the second drop-down menu, select None. For
list of tables, see Add a ServiceNow Account topic.
Broadcom 4935

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. In the Requires role table, select the role you want to add the access control.
7. Click Submit.
Do I need to Add all the APIs/Tables Mentioned in the Add a ServiceNow Account Topic?
To run application discovery every 30 minutes, you must provide all the required privileges. However, if you have access
to the following table, you can add the data source in VCF Operations for networks and VALIDATE:
APIs Table Permission Type
/stats.do -- Required
/api/now/v1/cimodel/cmdb_ci/fullclasshiera -- Required
rchy
/api/now/v2/table/cmdb_rel_type cmdb_rel_type Required
/api/now/v2/table/cmdb_ci cmdb_ci Required
/api/now/v2/table/cmdb_ci_service_discove cmdb_ci_service_discovered Required
red
/api/now/v2/table/cmdb_rel_ci cmdb_rel_ci Required
VCF Operations for networks validates the required privileges and shows any missing privileges as an error. You can
check the missing privileges, and then get access to the missing privileges and VALIDATE again.
Not able to find in ServiceNow Access Control (ACL),
/api/now/v1/cimodel/cmdb_ci/fullclasshierarchy
How to add the API in ServiceNow ACL?
1. Create a Role in ServiceNow UI.
2. Click System Administrator > Elevate Roles > Security Admin > OK.
3. Go to Access Control (ACL), and click New.
4. For API access, do the following:
Option Action
Type Select REST_Endpoint from the drop-down menu.
Operation Select execute from the drop-down menu.
Name In the first drop-down menu enter CMBD Model API Read.
From the second drop-down menu, select None.
5. In the Requires role table, select the role you want to add the access control.
6. Click Submit.
How to make any role read-only in ServiceNow?
To make a role read-only, you must assign snc_read_only to the role. For details, see Read-only role topic in ServiceNow
Documentation.
I have all the necessary privileges, still I am getting message, what to do?
Missing privileges
In some of the tables you must add another ACL with the same table to provide access to all the attributes by selecting
form the second Name drop-down menu. Also, ensure you have both the ACLs in the system to get the necessary
*
privileges.
Broadcom 4936

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Bulk Add Devices as Data Sources
You can bulk upload network devices, such as routers, switches, load balancers, and firewalls in VCF Operations for
networks and add those uploaded devices as data sources.
To add multiple network devices at once, you need to add the necessary information related to the network devices in a
CSV file and upload the file in VCF Operations for networks.
Download the sample  .csv  file from VCF Operations for networks and add the details mentioned in the  .csv  file. The
sample   file contains all the fields that you need to use to bulk upload your network devices, along with examples for
.csv
each field.
The   file must have information in the following fields:
.CSV
Table 1313: CSV Fields
| Field Name | Description | Importance |
| ---------- | ----------- | ---------- |
datasource_type The type or category of the data source. Mandatory
Note:
See the sample .csv for accepted values.
| ip  | IP address of the data source. | Mandatory |
| --- | ------------------------------ | --------- |
You need to add either IP address or FQDN.
|     | FQDN of the data source. | Mandatory |
| --- | ------------------------ | --------- |
fqdn
You need to add either IP address or FQDN.
| usersname | User name of the device. | Mandatory |
| --------- | ------------------------ | --------- |
|           | Password of the device.  | Mandatory |
password
nickname Any nick name that you want to give to the device. Mandatory
notes Any additional info that you want to add as a note. Optional
| snmp_version | SNMP version that you want to use. | Optional |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | -------- |
Valid entries are v2c, v3.
| snmp_community_string | SNMP v2 community string. | Optional |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | -------- |
If you use SNMP Version as v2c, snmp_community_string is
a mandatory field.
| snmp_username | SNMP user name. | Optional |
| ------------- | --------------- | -------- |
If you use SNMP version as v3, snmp_username is a
mandatory field.
| snmp_context_name | Context name for the SNMP. | Optional |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- | -------- |
| snmp_auth_type    | SNMP Authentication Type.  | Optional |
You can leave this field blank if SNMP Authentication Type is
not available.
Valid entries are MD5, SHA.

Working with Network Discovery
When you have several network devices in your data center, discovering them and adding them manually to VCF
Operations for networks as data sources might be time-consuming and inefficient.
VCF Operations for networks automatically discovers the network devices in your data center and provides the options to
add these discovered devices as data sources or export their details.
Discover Network Devices Using Network Auto Discovery
You can discover network devices such as routers, switches, firewalls, and F5 load balancer within your network. Once
you have discovered these devices in your network, you can then add them to VCF Operations for networks to get deeper
visibility into them.
Discover Network Devices in VCF Operations for networks
You can discover supported routers, switches, firewalls, and F5 Load Balancer.
You must verify the network devices supported in VCF Operations for networks. For more information, see Supported
Products and Versions.
1. From the left navigation pane, go to Settings > Accounts and Data Sources.
2. Click the Device Auto Discovery tab and select Discovery Profiles.
3. To create a new discovery profile, click Create Discovery Profile.
4. Define the scope based on which you want to discover the devices. You can discover devices either using the seed IP
or the IP range.
1. To discover devices based on seed IP, from the Discovery Method drop-down, select Seed IP.
Here, the devices are recursively discovered using the CDP and LLDP protocols up to the discovery depth that you
define.
2. To discover devices based on the IP range, from the Discovery Method drop-down, select Scan IP Range.
The scan IP Range defines the range of IP addresses where network discovery starts a scan.
Note:
Network auto discovery supports only a maximum of 4096 IP addresses per collector.
While adding the IP addresses, you can perform the following actions:
• To add a single IP address, specify the IP address.
• To add multiple IP addresses, use commas.
• To add an IP range, specify the IP entries with the - or / range separator.
• To add an IP range and exclude few IP addresses, click Add Exceptions, enter the exception IPs.
Broadcom 4938

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Provide appropriate access credentials and click Next. Supported access credential types are SSH, SNMP v2,
SNMPv3, and APIs.
To discover F5 Big-IP Load Balancer devices, you must enter your API credentials.
6. Provide a name for saving your discovery profile and set the discovery job schedule.
1. You can schedule discovery jobs to:
– Run once at the specified date and time.
– Or, run periodically such as daily, weekly, monthly, or at your defined custom intervals.
2. Provide a name for saving your discovery profile.
7. Click Submit.
You can bulk add the discovered network devices as data sources to VCF Operations for networks. See Bulk Add
Discovered Devices as Data Sources for more information.
Bulk Add Discovered Devices as Data Sources
You can bulk add the discovered devices as data sources in VCF Operations for networks.
1. From the left navigation pane, go to Settings > Accounts and Data Sources.
2. Click the Device Auto Discovery tab and select Discovered Devices.
The discovered devices are divided in the following tabs:
• All: Displays all the discovered devices.
• Ready to Add: Displays all the devices that are ready to be added as data sources.
• Needs Attention: Displays the devices that have one or more problems and need remediation.
• Excluded: Displays the devices which cannot be added as data sources. You can also select devices from any of
the other tabs and add it to the excluded list. These devices can later be removed from the excluded list and added
as data sources.
3. Select one or more devices from the All or Ready to Add tab and click the Add As Source button.
4. To bulk edit information of the devices before adding them as data sources, select the devices, click the three dots icon
next to Add As Source and click Bulk Edit and Add.
You can edit the following fields.
• Collector VM: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain your existing collector.
– Or, Override existing values to enter a new values.
• Autoinferred Device Name: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain your existing device name.
– Append to existing values to enter new values at the end of the existing values.
– Or, Prepend to existing values to enter new values at the beginning of the existing values.
• Access Credentials: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain your existing credentials.
– Or, Override existing values to provide a new credentials that works across all the data sources.
• Config Polling Intervals: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain the previously configured polling interval.
– Or, Override existing values to provide a new polling interval for the VCF Operations for networks platform to
collect the configuration data from the selected data sources
• SNMP: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain your existing SNMP credentials.
– Or, Override existing values to enter a new values.
• Notes: From the drop-down, select:
– No Change to retain your existing notes.
– Or, Override existing values to enter a new note.
Click Next.
Broadcom 4939

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In the next screen, review the devices and add them as data sources.
Bulk operations may take some time to complete. If the bulk add operation is successful, you will see a notification for the
same.
If the operation fails for one or more data sources, the details of the devices and the details due to which the operation
failed are displayed.
You can fix the errors and retry the operation on the failed devices.

You can generate and run scripts on the VCF Operations for networks Collector CLI to discover devices in your network
automatically and export the details of discovered devices to a file.

Provide your CLI login credentials using the Secure Socket Shell (SSH) client.

java -cp "/home/ubuntu/build-target/common-utils/tools-0.001-SNAPSHOT.jar"

You use this script to perform network discovery.

6. Run the command on the Python script to view the options supported by the script.
help
python3 script.py --help
You can use these options to authenticate your credentials and perform network discovery.
Option Description
--host The IP address of the VCF Operations for networks platform
node1.
--deployment type The type of deployment on which you are performing this
operation. Accepted values are onprem and saas.
The default value is onprem.
--username The user name of the platform user.
Note:
You must always enclose the username in single quotes.
--password The password of the platform user.
Note:
You must always enclose the password in single quotes.
--domain_type The domain type to authenticate user credentials. Accepted
values are LOCAL and LDAP.
--domain_value If the domain type is LDAP, provide your LDAP domain name.
--proxy_ips The IP address of VCF Operations for networks Collector.
--credentials_file_path The location of the credentials file which contains the SSH, SNMP,
or API credentials.
--network_ranges The IP address range to perform network discovery on. You can
specify the IP addresses in the network range format or the CIDR
range format.
--seeds The seed IP addresses or the seed FQDN of network devices to
begin the network discovery process.
Note:
When you run the network discovery script, you begin the
network discovery process with given seed IP addresses
as the starting point.
Each seed's neighbor devices are discovered based
on industry protocols such as CDP and LLDP. Each
discovered device is then used as a seed to recursively
discover other devices in your network until all devices
in your network are discovered or the seed depth is
reached.
Broadcom 4941

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Description
--seed_depth The depth of discovering network devices.
Note:
The seed depth indicates how many levels of neighbors
must be explored from the seed IP address. By default,
the depth of the seed is 0; the depth of the seed’s
neighbors is 1; the depth of the seed’s neighbors’
neighbors is 2 and so on.
If you enter the seed depth as 2, you can discover
devices of the seed, the seed's neighbors, and the seed's
neighbor's neighbors.
--ignored_list The list of IP addresses to exclude from network discovery. You
can specify the IP addresses in the following formats:
• Individual IP address
• FQDN
• Network range
• CIDR range
--download_discovered_devices The option to download the previously discovered devices. Enter
True or False.
--out The name of the CSV output file for successful network discovery.
The default name of the output file is auto_gen_discovered
_devices.csv.
--clear_all The option to erase details of the discovery such as discovery job,
credential profile, job result, and discovered devices. Enter True
or False.
--wait_time_in_secs The maximum wait time (in seconds) to discover devices.

Bulk Edit Data Sources
In VCF Operations for networks, you can enable, deactivate, edit, or delete multiple data sources at once.
You must have added more than one data source into VCF Operations for networks. For more information, see Adding a
Data Source in VCF Operations for networks and Bulk Add Data Sources Using the Python SDK.
1. Go to Settings > Accounts and Data Sources.
2. In the Accounts and Data Sources page, select the data sources on which you want to perform bulk operations.
3. From the Actions drop-down menu, select the bulk operation that you want to perform.
Note:
Bulk operations are asynchronous in nature, which means that when a bulk operation is in progress, updates to
the selected data sources are temporarily deactivated till the operation completes.
Operation Action
Enable Enables data collection on the selected data sources.
Disable Deactivates data collection on the selected data sources.
Edit Allows you to edit the following options:
• Access Credentials - Edit only the user name and password
of the selected data sources.
• Config polling interval - Edit the interval to collect
configuration data from the data sources.
• Notes - Add additional information that the user wants to add,
limited to 150 characters.
In the Edit Sources page, update the required parameters and
click Submit.
Note:
Only the common options across the selected data
sources are displayed for bulk update.
• From the Access Credentials drop-down menu, select:
– No Change to retain your existing credentials.
– Or, Override existing values to provide a new user name
and password that works across all the data sources.
After entering the credentials, click Validate to validate your
credentials against one of the data sources. A successful
validation hints that the credentials are most likely true for
all the selected data sources.
• From the Config Polling Interval drop-down menu, select:
– No Change to retain the previously configured polling
interval.
– Or, Override existing values to provide a new polling
interval for the VCF Operations for networks platform
to collect the configuration data from the selected data
sources.
• From the Notes drop-down menu, select:
– No Change to retain your existing notes.
– Or, Override existing values to enter a new note.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Operation Action
Delete Deletes the selected data sources from VCF Operations for
networks.
If the selected data sources have a dependency on one or more
data sources, do one of the following actions:
• Delete the dependent data sources before deleting the
selected data sources.
• Or, delete the dependent data sources along with the selected
data sources.
Bulk operations may take some time to complete. After the operation completes, if the operation is successfully, VCF
Operations for networks displays a notification indicating that the operation succeeded for all the selected data sources.
If the operation fails for one or more data sources, VCF Operations for networks displays an error notification indicating
the status of the operation. Click the View Details button to view the following details:
• List of data sources for which the operation succeeded.
• List of data sources for which the operation failed, and the reason for failure.
You can fix the errors and retry the operation on the failed data sources.
Migrate Data Sources to a Different Collector
If a collector VM is down or deleted, you can add a new collector VM and migrate data source from the old collector VM to
the new collector VM.
1. Go to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Overview and Updates > Collector VMs section, click the edit icon
next to the collector name in the list.
If the collector VM is down, you see the error message. The Edit Collector page lists all the data sources added to the
collector.
2. To migrate a data source, click Migrate for a particular data source.
3. Enter the required information of the new collector on the Edit Account or Source page.
Table 1314:
Fields Description
Collector VM Name of the new collector VM to which the data source has to be
migrated
IP Address Pre-filled IP/FQDN address of data source
Username Username for the data source
Password Password for the data source
4. Click Validate and then click Submit.
The data source is then deleted in the old collector VM and is added to the new collector VM.
5. Once the migration is successful, you will see the new collector VM against the data source in the Enabled column in
the Accounts and Data Sources page.
Note:
• If you are migrating VMware vCenter to another collector VM, then ensure that you migrate the corresponding
NSX Manager also to the same collector VM.
• When you migrate NSX Manager to another collector VM, the child data providers such as NSX controller and
NSX Edge are also migrated to the new collector VM.
Broadcom 4946

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Delete a Data Source from VCF Operations for networks
If you do not want to view data from a data source or a data source is not in use, you can delete the data source from VCF
Operations for networks.
Note:
If any data source is no longer available in your environment, you must delete that data source form VCF
Operations for networks.
1. Sign in to the VCF Operations for networks web console.
2. Go to Settings > Accounts and Data Sources.
3. Click the Delete Data Source icon next to the data source you want to delete.
The VCF Operations for networks prompts you for confirmation.
4. Click Yes.
Note:
After you remove a data source from the system, you can add the same data provider back only after two or more
hours.
Unregister a Customer
To unregister or delete a customer from VCF Operations for networks, you must first delete all the collectors of that
customer and then contact VMware Support to remove that customer from VCF Operations for networks.

Other Requirements and Considerations
• While editing a data source collector, other data source fields cannot be edited.
• During a fresh installation or upgrade to VCF Operations for networks in VCF 9, the support password will be
equivalent to the root password. To modify the root password, log in to the appliance through SSH using the support
user credentials, elevate to root using the   command, and then update the root file using the
|     |     |     |     | sudo su |     |     |     |     |     | passwd |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ------ |
command.
• The network verification and assurance and flow based application discovery features are available for deployments
using the Extra Large brick size.
• The maximum time skew between the platform nodes has to be lesser than 30 seconds.
• The availability of the NTP service is critical to system operations. Ensure that you do not reboot the platform node or
the collector node when the NTP service is not available.
• When the existing compute resources are completely used by the other processes on the platform, VCF Operations for
networks crashes and does not recover automatically. If the services fail to recover, reboot the platform node.
• If the network latency between platform node and upgrade server is greater than 500ms, the VCF Operations for
networks upgrade might encounter an error. So, the network latency must be less than 500ms.
• The recommended network latency between platform VMs for optimal performance is up to 3ms. The system
performance might degrade beyond the limit.
•
The recommended network latency between platform and collector VMs for optimal performance is up to 150ms. The
system performance might degrade beyond this limit.
Broadcom 4950

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• The recommended disk latency for optimal performance is up to 5ms. If the disk latency is greater than 5ms, the
system performance degrades.
• The recommended disk IOPS is 7500.
• For optimum performance, the recommended bandwidth usage between the collector and the platform is 15
Megabytes per second (MBps) or 120 Megabits per second (Mbps).
Note:
These bandwidth recommendations are made considering the largest collector and the largest platform brick sizes
mentioned in this topic.
• For Network Map, the maximum supported firewall rules per VMware NSXManager (including of DFW and edge rules)
is 5000.
• To use the Assurance and Verification feature in VCF Operations for networks, you must enable Link Layer Discovery
Protocol (LLDP) and Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) (if supported) on the network devices.
• As IPv6 addresses occupy more space in memory and disk, enabling IPv6 flow processing can reduce the platform
and the collector capacity by up to 20%.
Supported TLS Versions
VCF Operations for networks supports Transport Layer Security (TLS) versions 1.2 and 1.3.
Supported Web Browser
• Google Chrome: The latest two versions.
• Mozilla Firefox: The latest two versions.
Recommendations to Support High Availability
You can customize vSphere HA options to enable vSphere high availability.
• Host Failure - Restart VMs
• Host Isolation- Deactivated
• Guest not heartbeating- Deactivated

• Increase RAM, total vCPU and corresponding reservation. To increase RAM, total vCPU and corresponding
reservation, do the following steps that are relevant to your setup:
Option Description
For a single node platform or fresh independent OVA 1. Log in to VMware vCenter.
2. Shutdown the Platform VM using the Shut Down Guest OS

Do not use the Power Off option.
3. Increase RAM, total vCPU and corresponding reservation of
the VM as required to match the target brick size.
4. Power On the Platform VM.

2. Shutdown the Platform VM using the Shut Down Guest OS

Increase the Disk Size
In VCF Operations for networks, you can add additional disk space to a VCF Operations for networks Platform node.
Ensure that the nodes are in the powered-on state, and you have the correct privileges.
If the disk usage on the Platform are high, adding more disk space helps you prevent any unwanted service interruption.
Note:
Do not expand the existing disks available in the VM. You must always add a new disk in the VM.
Note:
Do not reboot any VMs until VCF Operations for networks detects the new disk and the new disk space is added
in the partition.
/var
1. Log in to VMware vCenter using the web client with correct privileges.
2. Right-click the VM, and click Edit Settings.
3. Add a disk of required size.
A cron job runs every 5 minutes and checks for any new disks added to the VM, then automatically expands the
required partition.
Wait for 10-15 minutes for VCF Operations for networks to detect the disk, and then check and ensure that the additional
disk size is visible in the partition.
/var
In case troubleshooting is required, the cron job script location is:
/home/ubuntu/build-target/common-utils/
. You can find the related log file at .
cron.5m/run-expandpart.sh /home/ubuntu/logs/disk_util.log
Create a Support Bundle
You can create a support bundle that collects diagnostic information such as product-specific logs, configuration files of
your setup. When you raise a support request, VMware Technical Support uses this information to troubleshoot your setup
issues.
1. On the Settings page, click Infrastructure and Support > Support.
2. Select the platform VMs and the collector VMs for which you want to create the support bundle.
To select all VMs, click the check box in the header of the platform VMs and the collector VMs tables.
Broadcom 4952

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Click Create Support Bundle.
4. Click Yes to confirm creation of a new support bundle.
VCF Operations for networks takes some time to complete the creation of the bundle.
A new support bundle is created displaying date and time. To initiate the download of support bundle, click the Download
link next to the respective VM.
Note:
• The support bundle creation on a medium sized system can take in excess of fifteen minutes.
• Only two support bundles can be present at one given time. So, while creating a new one, if there are already
two support bundles present, the older one is deleted.
Attach the support bundle to your service request for VMware to access the details.
Viewing System Health
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view the health status of your system. The health of your system is determined
by process lag, indexer lag, and grid usage.
If all these parameters are in the green state, your system health is good. If any one of these three parameters is in the
red state, your system health is bad. The overall health indicator displays the number of irregularities, with a Red light.
The individual irregularities are listed with their details, when the number of problems against overall health, is clicked
on. In case of normal functioning, the health indicator shines a Green light. The Health indicator turns red if any of the
following malfunctioning events occur:
• If the collector stops collecting flow data
• If platform stops processing data due to some reason; for example, insufficient disk space
• If search indexer lags behind, resulting in outdated search result
Note:
VCF Operations for networks might not detect an out-of-sync system clock sometimes. If the clock is not in sync
with NTP, some services may become unhealthy or stop working.
On the Settings page, click Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates.
The health of your system is displayed in the System Health section.
Note:
If your system health is in the bad state for more than six hours, you must contact the VCF Operations for
networks support.
Viewing System Usage
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view and track the use of resources and see how these entities have changed
over time.
The counts of entities used are tracked as metrics and these metrics are tracked once every 24 hours. These metrics
have a data retention period of up to 13 months or up to the data retention interval set in the Data Management tab of
the Settings page. The trending metric graphs show the counts of VMs, hosts, applications, firewall rules, daily flows, and
weekly flows.
To view the metric graphs:
1. Go to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates.
2. On the Infrastructure and Updates page, click Go to Operations for Networks System Dashboard.
3. You can see the metric graphs under the System Usage section of the Overview page.
Understanding Capacity for Collector and Platform Load
VCF Operations for networks provides the approximate capacity and load information of a collector node and a platform.
This limits-based information helps you to prevent the performance and experience issues later.
Broadcom 4953

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Understanding Capacity
There are two kinds of capacity:
• VM capacity: It is defined as the number of discovered VMs that a node or a setup can handle.
• Flow capacity: It is defined as the number of flows that a node or a setup can handle.
The capacity is defined as follows:
• Single platform with one or more collector nodes: The capacity of a collector node or the platform is the number of
discovered VMs that it can handle without the degradation of performance.
• Cluster setup: The capacity of the platform in a cluster setup is the aggregation of all the capacities of all the platform
nodes while the capacity of collector nodes is considered at the level of an individual node.
Accessing the Capacity Information
You can view VM Capacity and Flow Capacity on the Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates page.
For every collector node listed under Collector VMs, only the VM capacity information is provided.
Note:
When the number of discovered VMs from the data sources across the deployment exceed the capacity of either
the system or the collector or both, you will not be allowed to trigger the upgrade.
To view the discovered VMs for a data source:
1. In the Accounts and Data Sources page, you can see the number of VMs that have been discovered for a particular
data source which is already added and currently active. This column will have a value only if the data source is
vCenter or AWS source.
Note:
The discovered VM count includes placeholder and template VMs. So it can be different from the count of VMs in
the product.
View Platform Capacity
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view the platform capacity and usage.
In the Platform Capacity, you see information about VMs, Active Flows, All Flows, and Devices. To view the Platform
Capacity, do the following:
On the Settings page, click Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates.
In the Infrastructure and Updates page, you can see the Platform Capacity.

Manage Disk Utilization
If the disk utilization is high for a platform or a collector, VCF Operations for networks triggers an alert to warn the user to
manage the disk space. VCF Operations for networks also provides a recommendation of how much more disk space is
to be added.
To view the alerts related to disk utilization, navigate to the platform dashboard or the collector dashboard. You can
also view these alerts in the corresponding collector or the platform section in the Infrastructure and Support >
Infrastructure and Updates page.
To add a hard disk to a node, perform the following steps:
Note:
Do not expand the existing hard disk.
1. Log in to VMware vCenter through the Web client with sufficient privileges.
2. Right-click the node and select Edit settings.
3. Add the hard disk as per recommendations provided in the alert.
VCF Operations for networks takes a few minutes to detect the appliance and add it to the partition.
/var
View the Platform and Collector Details
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view the details of each platform node and collector node.
Broadcom 4955

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. To view the details of a particular platform node, go to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and
Updates > Platform VMs and click its name from the list.
The VCF Operations for networks platform dashboard appears.
2. To view the details of a particular collector node, go to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and
Updates > Collector VMs and click its name from the list.
The VCF Operations for networks collector dashboard appears.
Configure Data Retention Interval
In VCF Operations for networks, you can specify the duration for which you want to retain your data.
Note:
VCF Operations for networks supports configurable data management on an enterprise license only. In the
advanced license edition, the data retention defaults to 1 month.
The data is divided into the following categories:
Table 1320:
Category Minimum Value Maximum Value
Alerts 1 month 13 months
Entities and Configuration Data 1 month 3 months
Metrics 1 month 13 months
Flows 1 month 1 month
Miscellaneous Data NA 100 GB of additional disk space
Note:
For all the categories, the minimum value is the default value.
Different policies can be configured and controlled for each category. You can configure the policy as per your
requirement.
To configure data management:
1. Go to Settings and click Data Management.
2. When you log in for the first time, this page shows the default data.
3. Click Edit on the top-right corner of the page to change the data retention period for various categories of data.
4. Click Submit. The Updated information is recorded in the database.
Note:
The retention period for low-resolution metrics is longer than the high-resolution metrics.
Configuring IP Properties and Subnets
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure different IP properties for better security planning and identification.
Import the DNS mapping file
You can upload your DNS mapping file on VCF Operations for networks to provide information about flows between
physical devices. The supported file formats are the Bind and CSV file format. Ensure that you have placed these files in a
single ZIP file.
Note:
VCF Operations for networks does not support password-protected ZIP files.
Broadcom 4956

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Go to Settings > IP Properties and Subnets > Physical IP and DNS Mapping.
2. Click Upload to upload your DNS mapping file. After you select and upload the file, click Validate. The number of DNS
records is displayed after validation.
The Upload operation removes any existing DNS mappings and replaces them with the mappings that are being
imported.
The DNS Mapping file consists of the following fields:
• Host Name
• IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6 address)
• Domain Name
Configure Mapping Between Subnet and a VLAN
You can define a mapping between subnet and a VLAN.
You can use this mapping for the following:
• Enriching the information about the IP entities that are learned from physical to physical flows by adding the source
and destination subnets and the Layer2 networks associated with the flow.
• Planning the network topology based on the subnet and VLAN for physical addresses.
1. Go to Settings > IP Properties and Subnets > Physical Subnets and VLANs.
This page lists all the subnets and the associated VLAN IDs.
2. Click Add to add the subnet and VLAN information.
3. Click Submit.
4. After defining the mapping information, you can only edit the VLAN ID that is associated with the subnet.You cannot
change to the subnet CIDR associated with the VLAN ID. To edit a subnet associated with the VLAN ID, delete the
subnet and create a new subnet VLAN mapping with the updated values.
When the subnet-VLAN mapping information is updated, a new VLAN is created for the specified VLAN ID and the
subnet information is associated with this VLAN.
5. To delete the subnet-VLAN ID mapping, click Delete.
Note:
All VLAN creation, updating, and deletion operations does not happen immediately after the subnet and VLAN
mappings are created. It takes some time for the changes to be propagated and the corresponding VLAN to be
created or modified.
Configuring East-West and North-South IPs
In VCF Operations for networks, you can override IP addresses, IP ranges, and subnets as either private IPs (East-West
IPs) or public IPs (North-South IPs).
East-West IPs and North-South IPs
The IP addresses that are within the range of RFC1918 standard and the IP addresses of the VMs in VCF Operations for
networks are considered as East-West IPs or private IPs.
The IP addresses that are outside RFC1918 are considered as North-South IPs or public IPs.
VCF Operations for networks supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
Configuring East-West and North-South IPs
1. Go to Settings > IP Properties and Subnets > Custom IPs and click Customize.
2. In the East-West IPs text box, enter custom IPs that you want to override as private IPs. Custom IPs can be IP
addresses, IP ranges, or subnets.
3. In the North-South IPs text box, enter custom IPs that you want to override as public IPs.
Broadcom 4957

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Click Save.
While adding the IP addresses, you can do the following actions:
• To add a single IP address, specify the IP address and press Enter.
• To add multiple IP addresses, use commas.
• To add an IP range or a subnet, specify the IP entries and press Enter.
• To add an IP range or a subnet and exclude a few IP addresses, click Add Exceptions, enter the exception IPs, and
click Done.
Note:
You can add IP addresses, IP ranges, and subnets as exceptions. The IP addresses that you add as exceptions
in the East-West IPs text box are considered as North-South IPs and vice versa.
Configuring Alerts and Notifications
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure various types of alerts and notifications. VCF Operations for networks
creates an alert whenever the system meets a preset rule.
Viewing and Editing Alert Definitions
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view various alert definitions and list of alerts related to the alert definitions.
VCF Operations for networks has the following types of alert definitions:
• Problems: Logical or physical problems detected by VCF Operations for networks in the environment. A problem can
be something involving any entity, property, or metric. For example, a router interface failing or percent of packet drops
of an interface crossing a certain threshold can be detected as a problem.
• Changes: Changes that are detected by VCF Operations for networks in the environment for an entity, or properties
and metrics of an entity. Create, update, and delete qualifies as a change.
• Others: Alerts that are generated by external data sources, and not defined by VCF Operations for networks. For
example, NSX-T alerts, Kubernetes alerts, and so on.
To view the alert definitions, on the Settings page, click Alerts and Notification > Alert Definitions.
All the alert definitions of type Problem are displayed in the Problems tab.
Note:
All the alerts of type Problem are also logged into syslog.
All the alert definitions of type Changes are displayed in the Changes tab.
All the alert definitions of type Others are displayed in the Others tab.
When you point the mouse on each alert, you can see the name, the description, alert tags for that alert.
You can perform the following tasks on the alerts:
• Edit an alert
• Deactivate an alert.
• Perform bulk edit, enable, and deactivate
Edit Alert Definitions
You can edit alert definitions and set notifications for the preferred system events.
1. Click the edit icon on the Action column for the problem you want to edit.
2. Change the severity.
Note:
Applicable only for Problem type - Alert Definition.
Broadcom 4958

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Add or remove event tags if required.
Note:
Applicable only for Problem type - Alert Definition.
4. Select Include/Exclude entities if you want the alert to be enabled or deactivated for selected entities.
• To create inclusion rules:
a. Select Include/Exclude entities check box.
b. Click INCLUDE.
c. Specify the entities which you want to include from the drop-down menu.
You can specify multiple entities in the inclusion rule by adding multiple conditions by clicking ADD CONDITION
button.
• To create exclusion rules:
a. Select Include/Exclude entities check box.
b. Click EXCLUDE.
c. Specify the entities which you want to exclude from the drop-down menu.
Note:
• You can create multiple rules in both inclusion and exclusion lists by clicking ADD CONDITION button.
• You can also specify Custom search by writing your own query to include or exclude entities.
Note:
Applicable only for Problem type - Alert Definition.
5. To get alert notification, do the following:
Option Action
If you do not have an email server configured Click Configure Mail Server. To know how to configure a mail
server, see Configure Mail Server.
If you have already configured an email server Select Email immediately, Email daily digest, or both to
specify the frequency at which you want to receive the emails.
If you select Email immediately, you get email notification
immediately when an alert is raised.
If you select Email daily digest, you get email notification at a
pre-select time every day for all the alerts that are raised in the
system.
If you do not have an SNMP trap configured Click Configure SNMP Trap. To know how to configure an
SNMP trap, see Configure SNMP Trap Destination.
If you have already configured an SNMP trap configured Select one or more SNMP trap destinations from Send SNMP
Trap to drop-down menu. You can select up to four SNMP trap
destinations.
6. Click SUBMIT.
Perform a Bulk Edit on an Alert
In VCF Operations for networks, you can edit multiple alert definitions at once.
1. In the Alert Definitions page, select the alerts that you want to edit.
When you select multiple alerts, the options ENABLE, DISABLE, and EDIT appear above the list.
2. Click EDIT, and make the required changes.
Option Action
Severity Select an option from the drop-down menu.
You see the following options:
• No change: Default value
Broadcom 4959

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Option Action
• Override existing values: Overwrites the existing values
and sets the new value as per your selection.
Tags Select an option from the drop-down menu.
You can overwrite existing tags, add new tags, or remove
existing tags.
Email immediately Select an option from the drop-down menu.
If you select Enable, you get email notification immediately
when an alert is raised.
Email daily digest Select an option from the drop-down menu.
If you select Enable, you get email notification at a pre-select
time every day for all the alerts that are raised in the system.
SNMP Trap Select an option from the drop-down menu.
You can enable or deactivate SNMP traps.
3. Click SUBMIT.
Deactivate an Alert
You can deactivate alerts as needed to stop receiving notifications when certain conditions are met.
To deactivate an alert:
1. Select the alert in the Open Problems section of the Homepage. Or, enter Problems in the search bar and select an
alert from the list.
2. In the more option (three vertical dots), click Archive.
3. Select Disable all alerts of this type in future for and select an entity or all entities.
4. Click SAVE.
Note:
The changes made in severity, tags, or inclusion/exclusion rules will reflect for the future alerts. The existing alerts
continue to show the old configuration.
Alert Limitations
This section provides the limitations for the various alerts.
Distributed Firewall Rule Masked by Preceding Rule alert Limitation
This alert has the following limitations:
• This alert is supported only for NSX-T distributed and Edge firewall rules, and NSX-T on VMware Cloud on AWS
firewall rules. Other firewall vendors are not supported.
• The following firewall rule properties are currently supported for masking computation:
– Source
– Destination
– Applied To
– Service protocol and Port ranges
– Packet type
– Layer-7 application IDs
• Rules with source or destination inversion are not supported.
• Deactivated rules are ignored.
• Rules with security groups containing excluded members directly or indirectly in Source/Destination or Applied To is
not supported.
• The masking computation for Source, Destination, and Applied To properties are based on the static membership and
IP range overlap of member IPSets. Dynamic membership of a security group are not considered for masking.

Create a Search-based Alert
In VCF Operations for networks, you can define an alert through the search. Whenever you perform search, you get a
option to create an alert based on your search result.
All the alerts created by users are categorized as Search-based alerts. Search-based alerts were previously know as user
defined events.
Note:
If you are an existing VCF Operations for networks user, and you have configured user-defined events in your
VCF Operations for networks, then when you upgrade to VCF Operations for networks version 6.1, you see all
your user-defined events under the Alert Definitions page. Based on the event type, you can find your events
under either Problem or Change tab in the Alert Definitions page.
1. Click
located in upper-right corner on the search result window.
2. In the Define Alert page, do the following:
Option Action
Name Enter a unique name for the alert.
Search query Shows the search criteria for the alert.
Generate alert when Select when you want to generate the alert.
Definition type Select an alert type.
Severity This field specifies the severity of the alert. You can set it to the
following values:
• Critical
• Moderate
• Warning
• Info
3. To configure how you want to send the notification, select Alert Notification check box and do the following:
Option Action
Email frequency Select how frequently you want to get the notifications.
Email addresses Enter an email address when you want to get the notifications.
SNMP trap destination Select trap destinations from the drop-down.
You can select maximum four trap destinations.
4. Click SUBMIT.

Severity This field specifies the severity of the alert. You can set it to the
following values:
• Critical

Viewing Platform Health Alerts
The Platform Health Alerts page is your one-stop page to view all the alerts that provide details on the overall health of the
system. These alerts might have occurred on a data source or a node in the infrastructure. You can also view these alerts
through search.
Field Description
Name The name of the alert.
Severity The severity of the alert. You cannot change the severity of the
alert.
Type The type of alert. The alert denotes a problem or a change.
Notifications The types of notifications that are sent. The notifications can be
sent as an email, an SNMP trap, or both.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
NSX-T Events
VCF Operations for networks raises several self-computed NSX-T alerts. In addition, all NSX-T generated system alerts
(for NSX-T versions 2.2 to 2.5) and NSX-T Alarms (for NSX-T version 3.0 onwards) are also visible in VCF Operations for
networks.
Note:
Starting from 6.3 release, a few events are optimized for quick notification and are delivered under 5
minutes. See the Optimized for quick notification column in the table.

In addition to NSX-T events, all NSX-T 3.0 alarms are displayed as NSX-T system events in VCF Operations for networks
5.2 and later. You can see the complete list alarms generated by NSX-T at: https://nsx-t_ip_address/nsx/#/app/home/
alarms/alarm-definitions. Here, replace nsx-t_ip_address with the IP address of your NSX-T instance.
Note:
Starting from 6.3 release, all NSX-T system alarms are optimized for quick notification and are delivered before 5
minutes.

Configure Mail Server
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure a mail server to receive alert notifications through mail.
To configure a mail server:
1. Go to Settings > Alerts and Notification > Mail Server > CONFIGURE.
2. In the Configure Mail Server page, enter appropriate values:
| Option |     | Action |
| ------ | --- | ------ |
Sender Email Enter an email address where you want to get the notifications.
SMTP Hostname/IP Address Enter a Hostname or IP address of the SMTP server.
Encryption From the drop-down menu, select an encryption type.
The following encryption options are available: None, Use SSL,
and Support TLS.
SMTP Port Number (Optional) Port number of the SMTP server (default 25).
Note:
To use a Gmail server as the choice of email server, additional configuration settings as listed on Google Support
are required.
Optionally, for additional security, select the Authentication check box, and enter the user name and password.
3. Click SUBMIT to complete the configuration.
Configure SNMP Trap Destination
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure maximum four Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) trap
agents to receive notifications. The product supports the v2c and v3 versions of SNMP:
1. Go to Settings > Alerts and Notification > SNMP Trap Destinations > ADD DESTINATION.
2. In the Add SNMP Trap Destination page, in the Version drop-down box, select SNMPv2c or SNMPv3 protocol.
Note:
SNMP v2c protocol does not require authentication. SNMP v3 protocol supports authentication.
3. In the Destination IP Address/FQDN text box, enter the IP address of the SNMP agent or the Fully Qualified Domain
Name (FQDN).
4. In the Destination Port text box, enter a port number of the SNMP agent.
Broadcom 5014

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Depending on the SNMP version, perform one of the following:
Option Action
For SNMP v2c In the Community String text box, enter a community string.
For SNMP v3 1. In the Username text box, enter the name of the user you
have created in the SNMP agent.
2. Select the Use Authentication check box.
3. Select an authentication protocol, and then enter the
password you had set for the particular user in the SNMP
agent.
4. Select the Use Privacycheck box, and select a privacy
protocol and enter a privacy phrase respectively.
6. In the Nickname field, enter a nick name.
7. To verify whether the configuration is correctly done, click SEND TEST TRAP, and then check whether the trap has
been sent to the SNMP agent.
8. Click SUBMIT.
Delete an SNMP Trap Destination
You can delete an SNMP Trap Destination from VCF Operations for networks. If you have multiple SNMP Trap
Destinations, then when you delete an SNMP Trap Destination, you can migrate all the notification related to that trap
destination to another available trap destination.
1. Click the Delete icon next to the trap destination you want to delete.
A Confirm Action pop-up opens.
2. If you want to migrate the alert from the current trap destination to another trap destination, click Select multiple
destinations drop-down and select the trap destination where you want to migrate the alerts.
3. Click CONFIRM.
Configuring Identity and Access Management
In VCF Operations for networks, you can create users, or configure the access of LDAP users and VMware Identity
Manager users. You can also assign different roles to the users.
User Roles
VCF Operations for networks supports three types of user roles for a user. Users can access VCF Operations for
networks features based on the assigned roles.
• Admin: An administrator has complete access.
• Member: A member user has limited access.
• Auditor: An auditor has read-only access, and restricted from all create, add, edit, or delete actions. Users can only
view the state.

Add Local Users
VCF Operations for networks allows you to add users and assign a role to each user.
1. Go to Settings > Identity & Access Management > User Management .
2. On the User Management page, select the Local Users tab.
3. Click ADD USER and provide the required details.
Properties Description
Name Enter the name of the user.
Email (Login ID) Enter your email or login ID if any.
Role Select the role from drop-down list.
Password Enter the password.
Re-enter new password Re-enter the password for confirmation.
4. Click Add User to save the user information.
Assign Roles to LDAP Users
You can assign roles to any LDAP users to allow access to VCF Operations for networks.
Configure LDAP.
1. Go to Settings > Identity & Access Management.
2. Click User Management and select the LDAP Users tab.
3. Click ADD USER.
4. Provide the login ID of the user to whom you want to assign a role.
5. Select a role from the list. For details, see Configure User Management.
6. Click ADD USER.
Configure Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)
To allow the LDAP users to log into VCF Operations for networks, you must configure the LDAP service in the VCF
Operations for networks platform.
Broadcom 5019

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You must have the Administrator privilege.
Note:
VCF Operations for networks supports the LDAP and LDAPS protocols.
1. Log in to VCF Operations for networks and click Settings.
2. Under Identity & Access Management, select LDAP.
3. Click Configure.
4. Provide the following information.
Field Description
Domain Enter the domain name. This is typically the last part of the user
email address after the '@' sign. Example: For a user logging in
as johndoe@example.com, this field is example.com
LDAP Host URLs Enter the host name. You can specify multiple LDAP Host URLs
separated by commas. The URLs can be of type IPv4, IPv6, or
FQDN.
Examples:
• IPv4: (ldap://192.168.1.1:389)
• IPv6: (ldap://[fc00:192:168:20::e]:389)
• FQDN: (ldap://host:port/ldaps://host:port)
Group based access control Select this option to configure a group and provide a role to the
members of that group.
1. UnderBase DN, type the Base DN, the point from which the
server starts searching for users.
2. Provide the search attribute.
3. Under Group DN, select the role of the user for each group.
If you select the administrator role for a particular group,
then all the members of that group have the administrator
privilege. Similarly, if you select the member role for a
particular group, then all the members of that group have
the member privilege. If this option is not selected, then the
group setting is used to assign the privileges. But other valid
LDAP users who do not belong to the groups that you have
added can log in to the product.
4. Click Add more to add groups in the inclusion list.
5. Select the Restrict access to members of the above
groups only option to allow access to the users only from
the LDAP groups (direct or inherited membership) that you
have added.
Username User with the necessary rights to log in using the settings
provided.
Password Password of the user.
5. Click SUBMIT.
After configuration, you see the LDAP details you have configured.
Import Users from VMware Identity Manager
You can import VMware Identity Manager user accounts to allow them to use VCF Operations for networks and assign
them the roles.
Configure VMware Identity Manager.
Broadcom 5020

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If you are switching your authentication method to VMware Identity Manager from LDAP and the domain used in
VMware Identity Manager is the same as the LDAP authentication source, you must delete all LDAP users and
settings before you switch to VMware Identity Manager.
1. Go to Settings > Identity & Access Management.
2. Click User Management and select the VMware Identity Manager Users tab.
3. Click ADD USER and provide the required details.
Field Name Description
Domain Name Enter the VMware Identity Manager domain name for import.
Search Users/Groups Enter a search string, and select the user account from the
autocomplete list. You can either select a single user or select a
user group. If you select a group, all the members in the group can
access to VCF Operations for networks.
Role Assign a role to the user account. For more information, see
Configure User Management.
4. Click Add User.
Note:
• If you have selected a group, all the members in the group are assigned the same role. If you want to assign a
different role to a specific user in the group, you must add the user individually, and assign the required role.
For example, to assign the Administrator role only to user1 in Mygroup, perform the following steps:
1. Add Mygroup and assign the Member role.
2. Add user1 and assign the Administrator role.
The role assigned to the user overwrites the role assigned to the user as a part of group.
• If a user belongs to multiple groups with different roles, the highest privilege role is assigned to the user.
For example, if a user belongs to Group A that has the Administrator role, and also belongs to Group B and
Group C that have the Member role, the user inherits the Administrator role.
The VMware Identity Manager users or group members can log in to VCF Operations for networks and use the features
based on the assigned role.
