Administrators can authorize VMware Identity Manager users for accessing VCF Operations for networks features based
on their roles.
Register VCF Operations for networks as an OAuth client to the VMware Identity Manager host. For more information see
the VMware Workspace ONE Access Documentation.
1. Log in to VCF Operations for networks and click Settings.
2. Under Identity & Access Management, select VMware Identity Manager.
3. Click Configure.
4. Provide the following information.
Parameter Description
VMware Identity Manager Appliance The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the VMware Identity
Manager host.
OAuth Client ID The ID that is created when registering VCF Operations for
networks to the VMware Identity Manager host.
OAuth Client Secret The secret that is created when registering VCF Operations for
networks to the VMware Identity Manager host.
Broadcom 5021

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Parameter Description
SHA-256 Thumbprint This is an optional field. The certificate thumbprint of the VMware
Identity Manager host. For more information, see Obtain the
Certificate Thumbprint from a vIDM Host.
5. Click Submit.
After configuration, you see the VMware Identity Manager appliance and the client details you have configured.
6. Click the toggle button to enable or deactivate VMware Identity Manager. If you deactivate, you cannot use the
VMware Identity Manager authentication in VCF Operations for networks.
Obtain the Certificate Thumbprint from the VMware Identity Manager Host
For the SSL certificate validation, you can obtain the SHA-256 thumbprint from VMware Identity Manager host.
1. To get the SSL/TLS certificate, run the following command:
openssl s_client -connect <FQDN of vIDM host>:443
Copy the Server Certificate starting from to
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- -----END CERTIFICATE-----
into a file called and save the file.
cert.pem
2. To get the thumbprint, run the following command:
openssl x509 -fingerprint -noout -sha256 -in cert.pem
You see the thumbprint in the following format:
SHA256
Fingerprint=3D:E8:4C:CD:19:D6:AD:23:30:86:E4:A1:72:D5:22:08:F9:72:6D:D3:E7:6E:99:32:C8:C7:3D:F8:E2:91:91:AE
Copy the thumbprint and paste it in the configure VMware Identity Manager page.
Configuring Logs
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view and configure different types of logs.
View and Export Audit Logs
Audit logs capture administrative actions carried out in the system. These actions are regular CRUD operations, and login/
logout alerts. The audit logs capture the actions from the API, the user interface, and the CLI.
• The audit log feature is always on.
• VCF Operations for networks supports the UTC format in the audit logs.
• The audit log is integrated with the syslog. You can configure the syslog collector to collect all the audit logs.
• You can export all the audit log data in a CSV file.
Currently, the following administrative actions are not captured in audit logs:
• SSH login logs. You can find the SSH logs in .
/var/log/auth.log
• Changes in Physical IP and DNS Mapping.
• Changes in Physical Subnets and VLANS.
1. Go to Settings > Logs > Audit Logs.
2. The following details are shown on the Audit Logs page:
Information Description
Date & Time Timestamp of the actual action performed.
IP Address IP address of the client from which the connection is established
such as the CLI or the browser.
User Name User who is performing the action.
Broadcom 5022

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Information Description
Object Type Object on which the action is being performed.
Operation Different actions that the user performs on the object.
Object Identifier Unique identifier for that particular object on which the action is
being performed.
Response Indicator for success or failure of the operation
Details Details of the settings that have been changed such as the
nickname or a property.
3. To allow the collection of information when the user logs in through a browser or CLI, enable Allow collection of
Personally Identifiable Information. This option is deactivated by default.
Note:
The and the columns are blank if this option is deactivated.
IP Address User Name
4. Click Export as CSV to export the audit log data in the CSV format.
Setup Syslog Configuration
You can configure remote syslog servers for VCF Operations for networks by using the Syslog Configuration page.
While every collector can potentially have a different remote syslog server, all the platform servers in a cluster use the
same remote syslog server.
In the current release, the VCF Operations for networks problem alerts and platform or collector syslogs are sent to the
remote syslog server.
Currently, VCF Operations for networks supports only UDP for communication between VCF Operations for networks
servers and remote syslog servers. So ensure that your remote syslog servers are configured to accept syslog traffic over
UDP.
To configure syslogs:
1. In the Settings page, under Logs, click Syslog Configuration.
The Syslog Configuration page has the configured syslog servers and their mappings to the virtual appliances listed.
If you are accessing this page the first time, then the syslog is deactivated by default and the list of servers on this
page does not appear.
2. To add a syslog server:
a. Click Add Server.
b. Enter the IP Address, nickname, and port number of the server. The standard port number for UDP is .
514
The IP address can be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or a fully qualified domain name.
c. To test the configuration, click Send Test Log.
d. Click Submit.
e. If it is the first server that you have added, then enable syslog at the top of the page.
3. To map the server to platforms, alerts, or collectors:
a. Under Source - Server Mapping, individually edit the server for all platforms, alerts, or collectors.
b. Select the syslog server.
c. If you do not want to enable syslog, select the No server option.
d. Click Submit.
Note:
After you make the changes, it can take a few minutes for them to be effective.
Configuring Web Proxies
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure web proxies to connect to other entities (data sources, cloud service
platforms, and so on) when the connection is made over the Internet.
Broadcom 5023

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
You can add, edit, and delete web proxies in VCF Operations for networks.
Note:
This feature is supported for the following data sources:
Data Sources Web Proxy (HTTP) Web Proxy (HTTPS)
Service Now Yes Yes
Amazon Web Services Yes Yes
Microsoft Azure Yes No
VMware Cloud on AWS - NSX Manager Yes Yes
Note:
To enable a web proxy, you must edit the data source and select a web proxy from the Web Proxy (Optional)
drop-down menu.
Supported Web Proxies
In VCF Operations for networks, you can add the following types of web proxies:
• HTTP and HTTPS unauthenticated web proxy
• HTTP and HTTPS authenticated web proxy with the basic authentication
• HTTP web proxy with the NTLM authentication supported through CLI only.
Note:
If you set NTLM authentication-based web proxy using CLI on a platform VM, then the platform VM cannot
communicate with Cloud Service Providers (CSP). This is because currently, we do not support communication
with CSP using NTLM web proxy.
Add a Web Proxy
1. Go to Settings > Web Proxies > ADD WEB PROXY.
2. In the Add Web Proxy window, do the following:
Option Action
Type Select a web proxy type from the drop-down menu.
IP Address/FQDN Enter the IP/FQDN of the web proxy you want to add.
Port Enter the port number used by the web proxy.
Nickname Enter a nick name for the web proxy.
3. Select the Use credentials check box, and provide a username, password, and authentication method.
4. Click SUBMIT.
Edit and Delete a Web Proxy
To Edit a web proxy, do the following:
1. Settings > Web Proxies.
2. In the Web Proxies page, click the edit icon next to the web proxy you want to edit, and modify the information as
required.
3. Click SUBMIT.
Note:
You cannot edit web proxies added using CLI.
To delete a web proxy, do the following:
1. Click the delete icon next to the web proxy you want to delete.
Broadcom 5024

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
Make sure that the web proxy you want to delete has zero Connected Entities. If you have one or more
Connected Entities, then you must migrate the entities to a different web proxy before moving to the next step.
2. In the Confirm Action window, click DELETE.
Collector Migration for Web Proxies
Before migrating collector to version 6.1, if you set a web proxy on the collector using CLI, and if you set the flag
, then all the data sources which were reachable through the web proxy, work seamlessly
isHttpProxyEnabled = TRUE
after the migration to 6.1 as the system auto applies the web proxy details to these data source configurations.

During Collector migration to version 6.1, if you set a web proxy on the collector using CLI, and if you set the flag
then Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure data sources may not work after
isHttpProxyEnabled = FALSE
migration. You have to select a web proxy for both Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure data sources from
the Accounts and Data Sources page. See Supported Public Cloud Accounts for details.
VCF Operations for networks License
The capabilities of VCF Operations for networks are dependent on the license applied to your vCenter instance.
Starting with version 9, product components, including VCF Operations for networks, are licensed automatically after you
license the vCenter instance connected to the component. You no longer license VCF Operations for networks, manually.
For more information, see Licensing Overview.
Note:
After upgrading to VMware vSphere 9, the vSphere deployment will be in evaluation mode. As a result, the
deployment becomes unsupported in VCF Operations for networks, and data collection is paused. After adding a
valid license to your vSphere deployment becomes supported again but data collection must be turned back on
manually.
Configure Auto-Refresh Interval
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure auto-refresh interval for entity pages and dashboards.
VCF Operations for networks provides the auto-refresh feature for the entity dashboards and dashboards. The dashboard
refreshes automatically once in every n minutes specified on the header bar.
You can specify the time interval for which you want all your dashboards to perform an auto refresh. After the specified
time interval (n minutes), all the open widgets on the dashboard will reload automatically.
Note:
• You cannot change the auto-refresh time interval for a particular dashboard.
• Auto-refresh is paused if you select a past time interval in timeline slider.
You can pause auto-refresh if you do not require it for a particular dashboard. On the header bar, set Pause to ON. The
auto-refresh counter resets once you set Pause to OFF.
If you are viewing a dashboard and if another user is making changes to it such as changing the layout of the dashboard,
the auto-refresh feature not only updates the content but also refreshes the entire dashboard. This occurs only if sharing
and collaboration exists between you and the other user.
1. On the Settings page, click My Preferences. Or on the respective dashboard, click Modify next to Auto-Refresh in
the header bar.
2. Click Edit to change the time interval for auto-refresh. Select the time interval from the drop-down menu. Click Save.
3. To deactivate the auto-refresh option, select Disabled from the drop-down menu. All the dashboards are deactivated
from refreshing automatically if you select this option.
Broadcom 5025

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Enabling Support for IPv6 Flow Processing
VCF Operations for networks collects and processes IPv6 flows from VMware vCenter and NSX data sources.
IPv6 is designated by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) as the successor to IPv4 providing the following
benefits:
• Increased address length. The increased address space resolves the problem of address exhaustion and eliminates
the need for network address translation. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses compared with the 32-bit addresses used by
IPv4.
• Ability for improved address autoconfiguration of nodes.
1. On the Settings page, click System Configuration.
Note:
The System Configuration tab is visible only to the .
admin user
2. Switch the IPv6 Flow Processing toggle to true.
Note:
As IPv6 addresses occupy more space in memory and disk, enabling IPv6 flow processing can reduce the
platform and the collector capacity by up to 20%.
After you enable this feature, VCF Operations for networks takes a few minutes to start collecting and processing IPv6
flows.
To view the list of IPv6 flows, from the left navigation, go to Entities > Flows and filter flows by Flow Type.
Configure User Session Timeout
By default, the user session timeout is set to minutes. You can modify this value according to your preference.
15
1. On the Settings page, click System Configuration.
Note:
The System Configuration tab is visible only to the .
admin user
2. To change your preference for the User Session Timeout, click EDIT.
3. Drag the slider bar to set the timeout value for the session. The value ranges from minutes to hours.
15 24
4. You can also view the details on who modified the timeout value and when in the Last Modified field.
5. Click Submit. The Success message appears to confirm that the updated session duration will be effective from the
next login.
Note:
The new value for the user session timeout will come into effect only after you log out and log in again.
Add Google Maps API Key
To get the map view of your SD-WAN deployment, you must add a Google Maps API key in VCF Operations for networks.
Ensure the following:
• You are a member of Google Cloud Platform and billing is enabled in your account.
• You have the Google map API access key for the following API:
– Maps JavaScript API
– Geocoding API
To get the API key, see Get an API key procedure in Google Maps Platform documentation.
• You have restricted the API key to prevent any misuse. To know more, see Restrict the API key in Google Maps
Platform documentation.
Broadcom 5026

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. On the Settings page, click System Configuration.
2. In the Google Maps API Key, enter the API key and click Save.
VCF Operations for networks and FIPS
In VCF Operations for networks enforces FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules for all internal and external
connections. FIPS mode is always enabled and cannot be disabled.
FIPS 140-2 is a U.S. and Canadian government standard that specifies security requirements for cryptographic modules.
VCF Operations for networks uses FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules for all internal and external connections.
The objective of introducing FIPS support in VCF Operations for networks is to simplify compliance with security
requirements in regulated environments..
Note:
Starting with version 9.1, new instances of VCF Operations for networks use FIPS-approved cryptographic
modules by default. No additional configuration is required to enable FIPS compliance. Upon upgrading, all
appliances that were not previously fully FIPS compliant are automatically brought into compliance.
VCF Operations for networks uses the following validated modules:
FIPS Object Module Version Certificate
VMware's OpenSSL 3.0.8 Certificate #4013
BC-FJA (Bouncy Castle FIPS Java API) version 2.0.0 Certificate #37009
You can find more information about the cryptographic modules that VMware has validated against the FIPS 140-2
standard from here: https://www.vmware.com/security/certifications/fips.html.
Configure Security Certificate Validation
When you add a data source, or configure LDAP and VMware Identity Manager (vIDM) in VCF Operations for networks,
all the certificates related to that data source, LDAP, or vIDM are validated. In VCF Operations for networks, you can
configure how you want to validate and accept the certificates.
There are two ways you can configure certificate validation: Automatic Acceptance and Manual Acceptance. In
Automatic Acceptance, system automatically accepts all the detected certificate changes, and in Manual Acceptance,
system show you notification to accept the certificate manually.
1. Go to Settings > System Configurations.
2. From Security Certificate Validation drop-down menu, select one of the validation methods:
• Automatic Acceptance
• Manual Acceptance
3. Click Save.
Note:
If you change the certificate validation method from Manual Acceptance to Automatic Acceptance, you must
accept all the available certificate changes manually before you change the certificate validation method.
If you change the Data Source Certificate Validation from Manual Acceptance to Automatic Acceptance
without accepting the pending detected certificate changes, then you have to delete all the data source with
pending certificate and add them again to get the insight about those data sources.
The security certification validation setting is not applicable to the following data sources: vCenter, NSX-T, and
VCF Operations for logs .
Certificate acceptance for these data sources is handled automatically. If automatic acceptance fails, users must
manually accept the certificate by navigating to the Accounts and Data Sources page.
Broadcom 5027

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
For IPV6-enabled vCenter, NSX-T, and VCF Operations for logs data sources, automatic certificate acceptance is
not supported. In these cases, users must manually accept the certificate by navigating to Settings > Accounts
and Data Sources.
When the certificate of a non-VIP node in an NSX-T cluster is updated using the VCF Operations Console, users
are required to manually accept the new certificate through the same path.
Accept a Data Source Certificate Manually
If you have configured Security Certificate Validation as Manual Acceptance, then you must accept the new certificate
(HTTPS certificate or SSH public key) for each data source whenever the system detects any change in certificate.
When you add a data source in VCF Operations for networks, all the certificates (HTTPs certificates or SSH public
keys) related to that data source are automatically added as a trust on first use. After you add the data source in VCF
Operations for networks, every time there is any change in the certificate, the system validates the certificate.
If you have configured Data Source Certificate Validation as Manual Acceptance, whenever VCF Operations for
networks detects any changes in the certificate, it stops the data source and shows you an alert message notification to
accept the certificate manually. When you accept the certificate, the system starts the data source. You can also see the
certificate change alert in the Accounts and Data Sources page. Use this procedure to accept the certificate.
In the Data source certificate update available alert message notification, click REVIEW.
If the number of certificates update available is up to two: 1. You see a Data Source Certificate window with current
certificate and new certificate details.
2. Review the new certificate and click ACCEPT.
If the number of certificates update available is more than 1. In the Accounts and Data Source page, you see the
two: Certificate update available. Click here
to review and accept

2. Click Click here to review and accept for the data source
you want to review and accept the updated certificate.
3. You see a Data Source Certificate window with the current
certificate and new certificate details.
4. Review the new certificate and click ACCEPT.
When you accept the new certificate, you see message.
Successfully updated the certificate
Accept vIDM and LDAP Certificate Manually
If you have configured Security Certificate Validation as Manual Acceptance, then you need to accept the new
certificate (TLS/SSL X.509) to configure the vIDM or LDAP successfully.
When you configure the vIDM or LDAP in VCF Operations for networks, and configure the Security Certificate
Validation as Manual Acceptance, you see an alert message notification to accept the certificate. You also see the alert
message notification whenever the system detects any changes in the security certificates.
Note:
Only an Admin user can accept a security certificate. If you do not accept the certificate, the vIDM or LDAP users
cannot access VCF Operations for networks.
You can review and accept the security certificate when you see the security alert message notification. To accept the

• For vIDM, when you see the VMware Identity Manager security certificate update alert message notification, click
ACCEPT.
• For LDAPS, when you see the LDAP Security certificate update alert message notification, click ACCEPT.

Join or Leave the Customer Experience Improvement Program
VCF Operations for networks participates in VMware's Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP). This program
provides with information that enables VMware to improve its products and services, correct problems, and advise you on
how best to deploy and use the products.
As part of the CEIP, VMware collects the technical information about your organization's use of the VMware products
and services regularly using your organization's VMware license keys. This information does not personally identify any
individual.
Details regarding the data collected through CEIP and the purposes for which it is used by VMware are set forth in the
Trust & Assurance Center at VMware Products in CEIP Program.
You can join or leave the Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) for VCF Operations for networks.
1. Navigate to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Support.
2. Click Edit next to Customer Experience Improvement Program.
The Customer Experience Improvement Program window opens.
3. To join CEIP, click the Join the VMware Customer Experience Improvement Program check box.
This action activates CEIP and sends data to https://vmware.com.
4. To leave CEIP, deselect the Join the VMware Customer Experience Improvement Program check box.
5. Click Submit.
Configure Login Banners
You can configure Login Banners in VCF Operations for networks to display any text, or you can require that the user
click a check box, for example, to indicate that they accept terms and conditions. You can enable and deactivate the login
banners, and you can require that users click an explicit consent check box.
1. On the Settings page, click System Configuration.
2. Click Edit in the Login Banners row and configure the login banners.
Option Description
Display Banners Click the toggle button to enable or deactivate login banners. You
can change the other fields only if you enable this option.
Login Message Banner In the Description box, enter the message that you want the
users to see when they login to VCF Operations for networks.
User Consent Form Enter the title and enter the content message you want to display.
This requires that the users agree to the consent before logging in
to VCF Operations for networks.
3. Click Submit.
The login banners are configured and displayed when a user logs in to VCF Operations for networks.

  secure-tunnel
This reference includes examples for the syntax information for the  secure-tunnel  command.
To prevent unwanted cyberattack on the insecure inter-platform communication, VCF Operations for networks provides
option to secure the inter-platform communication using IPsec based VPN.
When you enable the secure communication, each platform nodes gets an internal IP addressed assigned from a
/24
subnet. By default, VCF Operations for networks uses  192.168.10.0/24  subnet. You can change the default value
of subnet when enabling the secure communication. The subnet must not conflict with any other IP address used for
configuring VCF Operations for networks. For example, you must not use IPs from   subnet as an SNMP or an SMTP
/24
host configured in VCF Operations for networks.
Note:
After you enable the secure communication, you cannot change the subnet. To change the subnet again, you
must disable the secure communication and enable it again.
Note:
Enabling the secure communication operation can take 15 minutes or more depending size of the cluster. To
avoid session time out, you must use the VM console through VMware vCenter UI to run this command.

Creating and Expanding Clusters
Create Clusters
You can create clusters from the Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates page.
Prerequisites
At least two additional platforms are required. The additional platform VMs should be deployed and powered on.
To create cluster
1. Click CREATE CLUSTER for Platform VMs.
2. On the Create Cluster page, enter the following information:
– IP Address: Enter the IP address of the new platform that you want to add. VCF Operations for networks supports
both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
– Password: Enter the support user password of the platform VM. If you have not changed the password yet, then
refer the Default Login Credentials section in VCF Operations for networks Installation Guide for the password.
3. To keep adding more platforms, click Add more and enter the IP address and the support user password.
4. Click SUBMIT. Click Yes.
5. After creating a cluster, the user needs to log in to the product again.
Broadcom 5045

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
• The CREATE CLUSTER option is enabled only when the platform is of large brick size. All platforms should be
of large brick to create cluster.
• To expand clusters, refer the Expanding a Cluster section in the VCF Operations for networks Installation
Guide.
Expand or Scale Out Clusters
Once the cluster is created, you can expand or scale out the cluster by adding more platform nodes to it.
Note:
• Before you scale up the cluster, you must take a backup of the cluster. For more information about the backup
and restore process, see the KB 55829.
• You must perform the expand cluster operation only from Platform 1 (P1) node.
1. Go to Settings > Infrastructure and Support > Infrastructure and Updates.
2. On the Infrastructure and Updates page, click EXPAND CLUSTER for Platform VMs.
3. The IP addresses of the VMs that are part of the cluster already are listed on the Expand Cluster page. To add one
or more nodes to the existing cluster, provide the IP address (IPv4 or IPv6 address) of the node and the support user
password.
Note:
• Currently, VCF Operations for networks supports 15 nodes in an existing cluster. Once the limit is reached, the
Add more button is deactivated.
• Ensure that all the new nodes do not have license keys applied (non-provisioned) and are reachable through
SSH.
• Ensure that you have taken a backup of the existing platform VMs before you go ahead with the cluster
expansion.
4. Click SUBMIT.
The step-by-step progress is displayed.
5. Once the cluster expansion link is completed, a message indicating success is displayed.
While the cluster expansion is in progress, the application cannot be used for any other operation.
If you are on the Deployment Scenario 2, then you must reconfigure your platform. To reconfigure, on the Infrastructure
and Updates page, under in Platform Capacity section, click the RECONFIGURE button.
Note:
The RECONFIGURE button appears only when your platform needs reconfiguration.
Note:
For information on deployment options and the other system requirements, see System Recommendations and
Requirements.
Configuring VCF SSO for VCF Operations for networks
To use VCF Single-Sign On (SSO) in VCF Operations for networks, you must configure it manually.
As an administrator, you can configure SSO to streamline access to VCF Operations for networks. After configuration, you
can select SSO as you log in method.
1. Log in to VCF Operations for networks with your local account.
2. To begin creating a SSO configuration, click Configure.
The Identity and Access Management page opens.
Broadcom 5046

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Select the VCF SSO option.
4. Enter the identity broker issuer address, client ID, and client secret details.
5. Click Test Connection.
6. To finish configuring SSO, click Submit.
After configuring SSO, you can now log in using this streamline method by selecting the SSO configuration from the
Login Method drop-down. For more information on configuring VCF SSO, see Configuring VCF Single-Sign On in the
fleet management documentation.
Note:
If the IP address is changed, it is recommended that you regenerate the SSO configuration and save the change.
Additionally, if a user is added to SSO group and then that group is deleted, the user can no longer log in to VCF
Operations for networks. To restore access, the administrator must restore the deleted user role.
Network Assessment and Value Analysis
Powered by VCF Operations for networks, the Network Assessment and Value dashboard in VCF Operations allows
you to evaluate and optimize your networking capabilities by adopting VCF networking.
• To use the Flows tab, verify that you have installed VCF Operations for networks. Using the Metrics tab does not
require installing VCF Operations for networks.
• Verify that Network Flow Collection is configured.
By performing a network assessment analysis on your vCenter networking capabilities, you can receive an overview of the
projected benefits of adopting VCF networking capabilities. The benefits of the network assessment include:
• Visualizing the Capital Expenditures (CapEx) and Operational Expenditures (OpEx) savings you can make by
switching to VCF networking.
• Quantify the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) of your networking infrastructure.
• Show the simplification and optimization benefits of VCF networking.
This assessment focuses on deployments with only virtual networking (VDS). Existing VPC networking configuration is not
taken into account in the assessment.
1. Navigate to Operate > Network Inventory and select Network Assessment and Value from the Virtual Networking
widget.
Alternitavely, you can also access this feature in VCF Operations by navigating to Manage > Plan > What-If Analysis.
2. Select Start Network Assessment.
3. Select the vCenter instance which includes your networking resources and click Run Assessment.
Note:
If you have multiple vCenter instances, you must run a seperate assessment for each instance.
You are shown the Network Assessment and Value dashboard. The two tabs on the dashboard, Metrics and Flows,
show an assessment of your current vCenter networking capabilities and the projected improvements that you can expect
if you migrate to VPC networking. Data included in the assessment include:
• The mobility score of your network infrastructure, which indicates the projected capability to move networking
workloads across your data center.
• Compute and memory utilization of your network infrastructure.
• The TCO of your vCenter networking infrastructure and the potential savings of switching to VCF networking.
• Visualization of your current vCenter infrastructure, including VDSs, number of hosts, and clusters and projected
infrastructure converted to NSX VPCs.
When using the dashboard, the following functionality must be considered:
• The Projected Mobility Score is always 100% (not computed), because VPC subnets span across all clusters in the
domain.
Broadcom 5047

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If the current CPU and Memory Utilization is under 50% and there is host reduction opportunity through workload
rearrangement, then projected values are set to 50%. Otherwise, the values remain as they are currently.
• The projected host count is computed at the individual cluster level. Host reduction opportunity across clusters
because of a improved Mobility Score is not considered in the projected host count and Potential Savings calculation.
• Low PNIC Bandwidth Utilization might be displayed as 0% because of a value rounding off.
• Unlike other What-If Analysis items, Network Assessment and Value results cannot be saved.
VPC Planning
After performing a network assessment, you can begin preparing your network infrastructure for migration to VPCs by
performing a VPC planning operation.
You must perform a separate VPC planning operation for each vCenter instance in your environment.
1. Navigate to Operate > Network Inventory and select VPC Planning from the Virtual Networking widget.
Alternatively, you can also access this feature in VCF Operations by navigating to Manage > Plan > What-If Analysis.
2. Select your vCenter instance and click Proceed.
3. Select a Virtual Distributed Switch (VDS) from your vCenter instance and click Proceed to perform the VPC planning
operation.
Note:
You can view detailed information for each Distributed Virtual Port Group (DVPG) in your VDS by selecting the
entry in the Number of Port Groups column.
4. After the operation is complete, you are shown a list of the recommended VPCs, the suggested subnet, Gateway
CIDR IPv4 address, and number of VMs in that subnet.
For more information on VMs in the suggested subnet, select the entry in the Number of VMs column.
5. To export the results of the VPC planning operation, click Export to .CSV File.
About Backing up and Restoring of VCF Operations for Networks Deployment
Data
You can take a backup of the VCF Operations for networks data and restore data in a new deployment when the existing
setup is unrecoverable. And also, you can replicate the setup configuration on multiple deployments.
Starting from the 6.0 release, VCF Operations for networks enables you to take a backup of the following data:
• Configuration defined under Settings option on the UI
– CEIP status
– Data manangement (retention interval)
– IP Properties and Subnet configuration
– Identity and Access management
– Syslog configuration
– Personally Identifiable Information status in Audit logs
– Mail Server and SNMP configuration
– System configurations like User Session Timeout, Certificate Validation, Google Maps API key.
– User preferences like dark theme, dashboard auto refresh.
• Datasources added to the setup, except for Physical Flow Collector (Netflow, sFlow).
• Alerts which includes system alerts, user-defined alerts, platform health
You can store the backup on the local storage, which can store up to five latest backup files. And also you can upload the
backup to SSH or FTP servers.
Note:
• VCF Operations for networks takes a backup of the above mentioned configuration data only, and not the
complete setup data, like flows or application information.
Broadcom 5048

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• You can track any failure in the backup or restore process on the Infrastructure page (Settings >
Infrastructure and Support > Overview and Updates > Infrastructure > Overall Health section ).
• You can also configure an alert notification for the backup failure under Platform Health Alerts.
Backup and Restore of VCF Operations for Networks
In VCF Operations for networks, you can store the backup on the local storage (up to five latest backup files), SSH or FTP
servers. You can start the backup immediately or schedule a periodic backup.
• The backup and restore setups must have identical versions.
• To avoid any inconsistencies, the restore setup must be a fresh deployment. Take the snapshots of the VMs before you
run the restore commands.
• Only Admin and Console users can configure backup and restore through public APIs and CLI commands
respectively. The Auditor user can only see if any backup and restore configuration exists on the setup.

VCF Operations Integration
With VCF Operations, you can see the VCF Operations for networks alerts in VCF Operations. And also, you can see the
network information in VCF Operations from VCF Operations for networks.
VCF Operations consumes a set of VCF Operations for networks APIs and displays lists of alerts on the Alerts
Dashboard. You can identify the VCF Operations for networks alerts with the prefix in the alert names. In addition,
vrni-
you can see the entity on which the alert was triggered.
You can use the Launch-in-context option from the entity pages, such as VMs, Hosts, and NSX-T, so you can view the
dashboard of that particular entity. This enables you to see the network health and to debug a network issue.
For information about supported VCF Operations versions, see VMware Product Interoperability Matrix.
Note:
You must add the VCF Operations user into VCF Operations for networks and provide at least Member privileges
for the user to use this feature in VCF Operations.
Broadcom 5054

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Configuring Flows in VCF Operations for networks
You can use VCF Operations for networks to configure flows to transmit various network data.
Frequently Asked Questions for IPFIX
Familiarize yourself with core concepts of using IPFIX in VCF Operations for networks.
What are the VCF Operations for networks IPFIX configuration limits and requirements?
For information on the VCF Operations for networks IPFIX configuration, see VCF Operations for Networks System
Recommendations and Requirements.
What communication protocols are supported?
VCF Operations for networks IPFIX supports the TCP and UDP protocols. Other protocols, such as ICMP, are not
supported.
Does VCF Operations for networks support de-duplication and aggregation of flows from multiple sources?
Yes, de-duplication and aggregation are supported. The same data reported from multiple sources is de-duplicated and
the best metric among all the sources is considered for flow analysis. Different attributes from multiple sources are also
aggregated and shown in the flow information.
What happens if the TCP handshake Is unsuccessful?
Handshakes are only performed for TCP, UDP does not require this validation. If the handshake is unsuccessful, the flow
is rejected. Currently, VCF Operations for networks only checks for VDS and NSX flows. Other flows do not report TCP
flags and as a result, the check cannot be completed. If VDS reports the TCP handshack as unsuccessful for a specific
flow, the NSX or physical counterpart is also rejected.
What are the outbound flow limits?
The number of connections a client can make in VCF Operations for networks is limited. Flows are dropped if this limit
is exceeded. This is a protection mechanism to make sure any non-flow entities, such as scanners which scan every
machine in the environment, do not overwhelm the total flow limit.
Protocol Type Limit for Allowed Flows Limit for Denied Flows
TCP 1000 50
UDP 500 50
What are the inbound flow limits?
Limit on the number of external flows in the environment. The inbound limit covers the number of external flows in the
environment. This limit ensures that the external flows do not overwhelm the overall flow limit in VCF Operations for
networks . When this limit is exceeded, new incoming flows are aggregated with the following client IPs:
• For allowed external flows: 240.240.240.240
• For denied external flows: 240.240.240.241
Limit Type Limit for Allowed Flows Limit for Denied Flows
Limit per service endpoint 5000 50
Global limit 500000 100000
Broadcom 5055

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
What can cause dropped flows?
Dropped flows are flows that are not picked up by the VCF Operations for networks collector. Flows can be dropped for
the following reasons:
• The wrong reporting point is used. For NSX flows, the flow can be reported from multiple places. VCF Operations for
networks only processes flow data reported from either source or destination of the flow. All other flow records are
ignored.
• The TCP handshake is unsuccessful.
• The outbound or inbound limits are reached.
• Incompatibility between the flow and collector. For example, non-physical flows are directed to a dedicated physical
collector.
Why is port information aggregated?
Port aggregation is built in to aggregate the ephemeral port flows, such as dynamic FTP, Oracle, MS-RPC, and others.
Aggregation helps in reducing the number of flows in the system and provides an summarized view for a large number of
flows that are essentially for the same service.
How does port aggregation work?
Port aggregation is based on the following workflow:
1. For the first three days of having a destination IP be recorded, VCF Operations for networks aggregates the
destination ports of that IP in buckets of 10K and starts building a port profile for the IP.
2. After the intial three day period, port aggregation is started in ranges where the port density is high. High port density
is selected as this is representative of the ephemeral port opening pattern. The ranges can be dyanmic in size (100,
1000, or 10K) and are created depending on how many ports are opened and how widespread they are in the specific
aggregation range. This allows high-port flows to be reported with no aggregation where there is no bulk port open
activity happening. It also allows the application of dynamic aggregation.
Note:
The aggregation range is specific for each server IP address.
3. The profile is continually updated in a time-decayed manner to account for new ports opening up or older ports are not
used anymore.
Why do I see port aggregation for a port where there is no bulk activity?
VCF Operations for networks performs a blanket aggregation of port 1024 when it gets reported for the first time. This
aggregation is done to reduce the number of flows in the system initially. After the port profile is built, this aggregation is
removed, if there is no bulk port opening activity happening.
When is a flow closed?
A specific flow entry is closed when VCF Operations for networks does not receive any IPFIX data for the 5-tuple
parameters (protocol, source IP, source port, destination IP, and destination port) after a time duration of 25 hours.
Can a splitter be used to send flows to multiple collectors?
Yes, if the collector limit is reached, a splitter can be used. You must configure the splitter to ensure that the flow for a 4-
tuple parameters (source IP, source port, destination IP, and destination port) is sent to a specific collector. Sending the
same 4-tuple to different collectors, can cause incorrect metric data to be shown.
How long does it take to see the flow information after adding a data source?
It usually takes three or four hours for flow information for a newly added data source to start being displayed.
Broadcom 5056

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Why do I see stale firewall rules on flows?
Duplicate flows can be caused by the following scenarios:
• When a firewall rule changes from rule 1 to rule 2. When the change occurs, VCF Operations for networks does not
immediately remove the old firewall rule. There is a time window of six hours before the old rule is removed. So, for a
maximum of six hours, you can see both rules. The scope of this temporary duplication can increase if more firewall
rules are changed in a short amount of time.
• For NSX-T Federation, multiple rules can be applied to flow. For example, one by the Global Manager and another by
the Local Manager.
How is the client and server for a flow determined?
The client and server are dependent on the communication protocol which is used.
For TCP:
• DFW: the directionality is already determined by DFW, and the source and destination of the flow are set
corresponding to the client and the server
• VDS: for a TCP connection, the information about the SYN packet sent by the client is reported in a separate IPFIX
flow record by the VDS. This IPFIX flow record is used to decide the client and server for a connection. There might
be a situation when VCF Operations for networks does not receive the IPFIX packet. This can happen if this IPFIX
packet is lost (IPFIX is sent over UDP), or if VCF Operations for networks identifies a long-lived flow which can be
terminated because of a period of inactivity. In this case, VCF Operations for networks determines the client and server
for a connection by using the source and destination port numbers. The client port is assumed to be greater than the
server port.
• OTHERS: for a TCP connection, if the SYN packet sent by the client is reported in a separate IPFIX flow record by
the exporter then same approach as VDS is used. Otherwise, VCF Operations for networks determines the client and
server for a connection by using the source and destination port numbers. The client port is assumed to be greater
than the server port.
For UDP:
• DFW: the directionality is already determined by DFW, and the source and destination of the flow are set
corresponding to the client and the server by DFW.
• OTHERS: if only one direction of IPFIX flow records is found, then consider that direction as the flow direction (source
is the client and the destination is server) Otherwise, VCF Operations for networks determines the client and server
for a connection by using the source and destination port numbers. The client port is assumed to be greater than the
server port.
What is the flow count for a data source page and how is it determined?
The numbers shown on the data source page show the unique flows (4 tuples) seen from the data source in last 24 hours.
The value is updated regularly (every ~5 minutes). The number can change since it only considers flows in the moving
window of the last 24 hours. The count should match the results of the following query:
'count of flows where
reporter = <Data Source>'
How are session counts measured?
If the flow is inactive for more than 2 minutes, then VCF Operations for networks considers that the session is completed
for that 5-tuple. This is done at the 5-tuple level. VCF Operations for networks shows the flow in the UI with an aggregated
4-tuple generated from the 5-tuple (the source port is dropped). If the source port is changed frequently, each 5-tuple is
considered as a separate session. Session counts across a 5-tuple are aggregated to a single 4-tuple.
What is the overall limit on the number of flows?
The overall flow limits are documented in VCF Operations for Networks System Recommendations and Requirements.
If VCF Operations for networks exceeds these limits, the oldest flows are overwritten. Addtionally, if the flow limit is
exceeded on the collector side, then the flow data is dropped on the collector itself until the number of flows goes back to
the defined limit. Exceeding flow limits can cause gaps for existing flow data or missed data on new flows.
Broadcom 5057

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Are flows that are dropped or rejected by DFW supported?
Yes, flows dropped or rejected by DFW are supported.
Why am I not receiving flows even after activating flow collections on the data source or receiving flows after
flow collection is deactivated?
In VCF Operations for networks 9.1 and later, it might take 10 minutes to reflect configuration changes. This delay is valid
for both newly configured flow collections and flow collections that are recently deactivated.
Enabling IPFIX Configuration
IPFIX is an IETF protocol for exporting flow information.
A flow is defined as a set of packets transmitted in a specific timeslot, and sharing the same 5-tuple values - source IP
address, source port, destination IP address, destination port, and protocol. The flow information may include properties
such as timestamps, packets/bytes count, Input/Output interfaces, TCP Flags, VXLAN ID, Encapsulated flow information,
and so on.
Note:
VCF Operations for networks does not display geolocation information included in flows. Contact Broadcom
support for assistance.
IPFIX Configuration on VDS and DVPG
A Virtual Destributed Switch (VDS) in a vSphere environment can be configured to export flow information using IPFIX
Flow monitoring has to be activated on all port groups attached to the VDS. If the packets arrive on port X of a VDS and
exit from port Y, a corresponding flow record is sent if flow monitoring is enabled on port Y.
To analyze the complete information of any session, the IPFIX data about packets in both the directions is required.
Note:
Starting with VCF 9.1, activating uplink DVPG connections is no longer supported. The relevant option in the
IPFIX configuration for vCenter data centers is deactivated.
VCF Operations for networks collector VM has built-in collector/receiver for IPFIX flow information. You can enable the
IPFIX information collection in the VMware vCenter data source settings at various levels of granularity.
Enable IPFIX Configuration on VDS and DVPG
To use IPFIX, you must activate the relevant option for your VMware vCenter data source.
1. Select the Enable NetFlow (IPFIX) on this vCenter check box when you are adding VMware vCenter in VCF
Operations for networks.
Note:
To enable Antrea IPFIX for collection of Supervisor, namespace, and VKS cluster flows, select Enable Antrea
(IPFIX) on this vCenter.
You see list of all the available VDS.
2. Select the VDS for which you want to enable IPFIX from the list of available VDS in VMware vCenter.
3. A notification icon is displayed for the VDS where one of the hosts has unsupported version of ESX. If VCF Operations
for networks has detected that IPFIX is already configured for a VDS with some other IP address apart from VCF
Broadcom 5058

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Operations for networks collector VM, then it displays the Override button. Click Override to view the list of DVPGs
under that VDS.
4. The list of available DVPGs for the selected VDS is displayed. All the DVPGs are selected by default. Turn Manual
Selection on to select specific DVPGs for which you want to enable IPFIX. Select the desired DVPGs and click

Using Antrea IPFIX for VKS Flows
By using Antrea IPFIX, you can collect and analyze data about VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) flows from
your data sources.
• Verify that VCF Operations for networks is deployed.
• Verify that your vCenter data source version is 9.1 or later.
• Verify that your vCenter data source is not added to multiple VCF Operations for networks deployments or that the
Antrea IPFIX management services have a different collector assigned to them from the collector currently configured
in VCF Operations.
• Verify that your VKS version is 3.5.1 or later.
• Verify that the property is activated in the Antrea configuration for each VKS cluster you want to export
AntreaIPFIX
flows from. To activate the property, you must set its value to in either the (VKS 3.5.1) or the
true AntreaConfig
(VKS 3.6.0 or later) file. The following is a sample code for activating the property on a VKS 3.6.0
AddonConfig
cluster:
apiVersion: addons.kubernetes.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: AddonConfig
metadata:
name: ${clustername}-antrea
spec:
addonConfigDefinitionRef:
name: antrea.tanzu.vmware.com.2.5.0---vmware.1-tkg.1
namespace: vmware-system-vks-public
clusterName: ${clustername}
values:
antreaIPFIX:
enable: true
• Verify that you have enabled Enable Antrea (IPFIX) on this vCenter in your vCenter data source in VCF Operations.
Note:
After enabling the IPFIX option in your data source, you can aslo verify that flow collection is enabled by
navigating to the Supervisor cluster in vCenter. Navigate to Network > Management Proxy Configuration and
verify that the netops-vks-api-proxy and netops-antrea-flows management services are available.
VCF Operations for networks allows you to perform an analysis on VKS flows, such as Kubernetes clusters, pods,
and services. You can use this flow information to analyze and troubleshoot your networking infrastructure. For more
information on VKS, see Managing vSphere Kubernetes Service Clusters and Workloads.
Note:
Antrea IPFIX flow collection currently has the following limitations:
• Supervisor VDS Networking stack is not supported.
• Flow collection is stopped if the corresponding NSX data source is not added to VCF Operations for networks.
• The vCenter and NSX data sources associated with the VKS clusters must be added to the same VCF
Operations for networks collector.
• Pod-to-Service flows where the destination VIP is the load balancer IP and not the cluster IP are not
supported.
• IPv6 flows are not supported.
• External-to-Pod flows are not supported.
Broadcom 5059

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. In VCF Operations, navigate to Operate > Flows.
2. Under Scope, you can select the scope of the flow analysis.
3. If you defined to scope of the flow analysis, select the type of VKS flow data, for example, Kubernetes Cluster, which
you want to add to the analysis.
The Network Policy type includes the Antrea cluster network policy, Antrea network policy, and Kubernetes network
policy flows.
4. In the search box, select the VKS flow entities that you want to analyze.
To view the relevant flows for the selected entities, click View All Flows.
5. To collect the flow data for the selected entity types, click Analyze.
The flow data is presented in the Top Talkers, Recent Flows, Network Performance, Pod Network Traffic, Network
Policy, and Node Throughput tabs.
NSX IPFIX Configuration
NSX IPFIX provides network monitoring data similar to that provided by physical devices and gives administrators a clear
view of virtual network conditions.
NSX virtualizes the network by allowing the network administrator the ability to decouple the network from physical
hardware. This functionality makes it easy to grow and shrink the network as needed and making the network transparent
to the applications traversing it.
By using NSX IPFIX in a virtualized network, the network administrators gain visibility into the virtual overlay network. It
provides visibility on the VTEP that is encapsulating the packet, and the details of the VM that generated the inter-host
traffic on an NSX Logical Switch (VXLAN).
The distributed firewall implements stateful tracking of flows. As these tracked flows go through a set of state changes,
IPFIX can be used to export data about the status of that flow.
The tracked alerts include flow creation, flow denial, flow update, and flow teardown. The denied alerts are exported as
syslogs.
Note:
If vCenter is added as compute manager to NSX, VDS does not export TCP flags in IPFIX flow records. VCF
Operations for networks drops such flows.
Starting with VCF 9.1, VDS IPFIX supports TCP retransmission count and round-trip time (RTT) flow metrics for NSX. For
more information, see Flow Metrics.
Enable NSX-T IPFIX
In VCF Operations for networks, you can view DFW or Switch IPFIX flows. For this, you must enable IPFIX flows in the
NSX-T data source.
• Ensure that you have any one of the following privileges:
–
enterprise_admin
–
network_engineer
–
security_engineer
• If you are using Distributed Firewall:
– Ensure that the Distributed (DFW) firewall is enabled.
– Ensure that priority 0 is available for the VCF Operations for networks IPFIX profile. If there is another IPFIX profile
with priority 0, then you have to change it to some other value.
Note:
From VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 or higher, if the DFW license is missing or if DFW is deactivated, then Switch
IPFIX flows will be the default.
• Verify that DFW is activated on each node of your cluster.
Broadcom 5060

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
To receive DFW IPFIX flows, you must have an applicable security license enabled. For more information, see the
vDefend documentation.
To enable NSX-T IPFIX in VCF Operations for networks:
Select Enable IPFIX when adding or editing an NSX-T Manager data source.
After you enable IPFIX, VCF Operations for networks creates its own Operations for Networks Collector profile and
Operations for Networks IPFIX profile on NSX-T. Ensure that you do not modify any of these profiles.
After enabling IPFIX on NSX-T, if the flows are not seen in VCF Operations for networks, then the following events may
occur:
• Operations for Networks Collector Profile is not registered in the NSX-T Manager.
• Operations for Networks IPFIX Profile is not registered in the NSX-T Manager.
• Operations for Networks IPFIX Profile port number has changed.
• Operations for Networks Collector Profile does not match in the Operations for Networks IPFIX profile in the NSX-T
Manager.
Note:
To resolve all the above issues, enable NSX-T IPFIX again.
• Operations for Networks IPFIX Profile priority is not zero in the NSX-T Manager.
To resolve this issue, log into NSX-T Manager and set the priority of Operations for Networks IPFIX Profile to zero.
• Operations for Networks Collector IP cannot be added in existing Operations for Networks Collector Profile in the NSX-
T Manager.
Delete one of the collectors from the Operations for Networks Collector Profile in the NSX-T Manager and re-enable
NSX-T IPFIX from data source page.
• If you are using Distributed Firewall, then check if Distributed Firewall is deactivated in NSX-T Manage.
Log into NSX-T Manager and enable the DFW firewall.
Flow Support for Physical Servers
VCF Operations for networks supports the device that sends the NetFlow data of versions v5, v7, and v9. If the DNS
Mapping and Subnet-VLAN mapping information is provided, VCF Operations for networks can enrich the NetFlow data
with DNS Domains, DNS Host Names, Subnets, and Layer 2 networks. This feature is available for the Enterprise License
users only.
To configure NetFlow in VCF Operations for networks, perform the following steps:
1. Add a Physical Flow Collector for NetFlow and sFlow.
2. Configure the NetFlow collector in the physical devices to receive the flows.
3. Importing the DNS Mapping.
4. Configuring the Physical Subnets and VLANs.
Configure a NetFlow Collector in a Physical Device
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure physical devices manually to send the NetFlow information to the VCF
Operations for networks NetFlow collector.
To configure most of the physical devices, perform the following steps:
1. Create a flow record.
The required fields for a flow record are:
• Mark the following fields as .
Match
–
ipv4 protocol
–
ipv4 source address
–
ipv4 destination address
Broadcom 5061

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
–
transport source-port
–
transport destination-port
–
interface input
• Mark the following fields as .
Collect
–
direction
–
counter bytes
–
counter packets
–
timestamp sys-uptime first
–
timestamp sys-uptime last
• Mark the following field as or . If not, skip it.
Match Collect
–
transport tcp flags
2. Create a flow exporter.
– Provide VCF Operations for networks NetFlow collector IP and port 2055.
3. Configure the flow cache as follows:
– Active timeout: 30 seconds
– Inactive timeout: 60 seconds
4. Create the flow monitor using the created flow record and flow exporter.
5. Configure the monitor on each interface.
The sample steps to configure the physical devices are provided in the following sections:
• Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco 4500 Series Switches
• Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco Nexus 1000v Switches
• Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches
Note:
The steps may vary from version to version and device to device.
Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco 4500 Series Switches
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure a netflow collector for Cisco 4500 series switches.
1. To create the flow record
configure terminal
flow record netflow-original
match ipv4 protocol
match ipv4 source address
match ipv4 destination address
match transport source-port
match transport destination-port
match interface input
collect transport tcp flags
collect counter bytes
collect counter packets
collect timestamp sys-uptime first
collect timestamp sys-uptime last
End
2. To create the flow exporter
configure terminal
flow exporter e1
destination <PROXY_IP>
transport udp 2055
end
3. To create the flow monitor
configure terminal
Broadcom 5062

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
flow monitor m1
record netflow-original
exporter e1
end
4. To configure the timeouts
configure terminal
cache timeout inactive 30
cache timeout active 60
end
5. To configure the flow monitor for each interface on the ingress mode and the egress mode or at least the ingress mode
configure terminal
interface <INTERFACE_NAME>
ip flow monitor m1 unicast input
end
Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco Nexus 1000v Switches
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure a netflow collector for Cisco Nexus 1000v switches.
1. To configure timeouts
configure terminal
Active timeout 60
Inactive timeout 15
end
2. To configure the exporter
configure terminal
flow exporter <EXPORTER_NAME>
destination <PROXY_IP>
transport udp 2055
source <VSM_IP_OR_SUBNET>
end
3. To configure the flow monitor for each interface:
configure terminal
flow monitor <MONITOR_NAME>
record netflow-original
exporter <EXPORTER_NAME>
end
4. To configure the flow monitor for each interface on the ingress mode and the egress mode or at least the ingress
mode.
configure terminal
port-profile type vethernet <IF_NAME>
ip flow monitor <MONITOR_NAME> input
ip flow monitor <MONITOR_NAME> output
.
.
end
Configuring a Netflow Collector for Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches
In VCF Operations for networks, you can configure a netflow collector for Cisco 9000 series switches.
Here are some of the sample device commands for Cisco Nexus 9000:
1. To enable the NetFlow feature
configure terminal
Broadcom 5063

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
feature netflow
end
2. To create flow record
configure terminal
flow record vrni-record
match ipv4 protocol
match ipv4 source address
match ipv4 destination address
match transport source-port
match transport destination-port
match interface input
collect transport tcp flags
collect counter bytes
collect counter packets
collect timestamp sys-uptime first
collect timestamp sys-uptime last
End
3. To create flow exporter
configure terminal
flow exporter vrni-exporter
destination <PROXY_IP>
transport udp 2055
version 9
source <INTERFACE_NAME>
end
4. To create the flow monitor for each interface
configure terminal
flow monitor vrni-monitor
record vrni-record
exporter vrni-exporter
end
5. To configure timeouts
configure terminal
cache timeout inactive 30
cache timeout active 60
end
6. To configure the flow monitor for each interface on the ingress mode and the egress mode or at least the ingress mode
configure terminal
interface <INTERFACE_NAME>
ip flow monitor vrni-monitor input
end
Enriching Flows and IP Endpoints
You can import the DNS mapping and the subnet-VLAN mapping information through the UI.
The flow information is enriched with the following types of information based on the import of the DNS data and the
specification of subnet-VLAN mappings.
• Source DNS Domain
• Source DNS Host Name
• Destination DNS Domain
Broadcom 5064

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Destination DNS Host Name
• Source L2 Network
• Source Subnet network
• Destination L2 Network
• Destination Subnet network
The IP Endpoint information is enriched with the following types of information based on the import of the DNS data and
the specification of subnet-VLAN mappings.
• DNS Domain
• DNS Host Name
• FQDN
• L2 Network
• Subnet network
For more information on enriching flows through the DNS information, refer Import the DNS mapping file.
For more information on enriching flows through the Subnet-VLAN mapping, refer Configure Mapping Between Subnet
and a VLAN.
Note:
• The DNS mapping and subnet information are enhanced only for the physical IPs. No subnet or DNS mapping
information is associated with any vNIC.
• The information is enriched only for flows that have been seen by VCF Operations for networks after this
information has been imported.
Searching Physical to Physical Flows
You can search for the physical to physical flows based on the following attributes:
• Source DNS Host
• Destination DNS Host
• Source DNS Domain
• Destination DNS Domain
• Source Subnet Network
• Destination Subnet Network
You can search for Physical-Physical flows based on the following attributes. A few examples of flow search query using
the enriched DNS and Subnet-VLAN mapping information are as follows:
bytes,Dns Domain,Dns Host,l2 network of flows where flow type = 'Physical-Physical'
bytes,Dns Domain,Dns Host,l2 network of flows where flow type = 'Source is VM' and flow
type = 'Destination is Physical'
bytes,Dns Domain,Dns Host,l2 network of flows where flow type = 'Source is Internet' and
flow type = 'Destination is Physical'
Viewing Blocked and Protected Flows
The NSX-IPFIX integration enables the visibility of the blocked and protected flows in the system.
The basic filters in the Security Planning page are as follows:
• All allowed flows: To see all the flows where firewall rules are set as Allowed, select this option. The All allowed
flows option is the default option.
• Dropped flows: This option helps to detect the dropped flows and planning the security in a better way.
• Protected allowed flows: This option helps to detect all the flows which have a rule other than of the type
associated with it. Such flows are known as protected flows.
any(source)any(dest)any(service)allow
Broadcom 5065

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• All unprotected flows: This option helps to detect all the flows that have the default rules of the type
. Such flows are known as unprotected flows.
any(source)any(dest)any(service)allow
The firewall rules are visible only for the allowed and unprotected flows.
For example, if you are in the planning phase and you want to see the allowed flows in the system, perform the following
steps:
1. On the Micro-Segmentation Planning page, for a particular group, select All Allowed Flows from the drop-down
menu.
2. Click the dropped flows in the topology diagram to see the corresponding recommended firewall rules.
3. Implement those firewall rules by exporting them into the NSX manager.
Network Address Translation (NAT)
VCF Operations for networks supports Static NAT (SNAT), Dynamic NAT (DNAT), reflexive rules in the flows, and the VM-
VM Path for NSX-T Edges, Fortinet, and Check Point.
The NAT flow support in VCF Operations for networks is as follows:
• VCF Operations for networks supports the nested NAT hierarchy for NSX for vSphere and NSX-T, and for physical
devices, VCF Operations for networks supports the single hierarchy (DNAT) for Fortinet only.
Broadcom 5066

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VCF Operations for networks supports the edges and the tier routers with NAT-defined uplinks.
Note:
The NAT rules on the NSX Edge version 5.5 or the previous versions are not supported.
• VCF Operations for networks supports SNAT rules with range. However, DNAT must be one-to-one mapping between
the destination and translated IP addresses (Parity with NSX for vSphere).
• For Check Point, NAT rules both auto or manually generated are supported for both the source and the destination as
network, network-group, or address-range.
Queries
To view NAT rules, use the following queries:
• To view all the NAT rules in NSX-T, use the query.
NSX-T Edge NAT Rule
• To view all the NAT rules in Fortinet, use the query.
Fortinet NAT Rule
• To view all the NAT rules in Check Point, use the query.
Check Point NAT Rule
• To view all the NAT rules, use the query.
NAT Rule
Consideration
• VCF Operations for networks does not support the following use cases:
– In NSX-T, NAT rules can be applied at the service level. For example, in NSX-T, L4 ports set is a type of service and
the associated protocols can be TCP or UDP. So in the VM-VM path, the service level details are not supported.
– Any port level translation is not supported.
– The SNAT match destination address and the DNAT match source address are not supported. Use the SNAT match
destination address as the destination IP address when you specify the SNAT rule. Use the DNAT match source
address as the source IP address when you specify the DNAT rule. For example, if there is a destination IP address
mentioned in the SNAT rule, VCF Operations for networks applies the SNAT rule irrespective of whether the packet
has the destination address as the destination IP address.
– NSX-T Edge firewall has implications for the data path when enabled with the NAT service on the same logical
router. If a flow matches both NAT and Edge firewall, the NAT lookup result takes precedence over firewall. So the
firewall is not applied to that flow. If the flow matches only a firewall rule, then the firewall lookup result is honored
for that flow.
– Service translation is not supported.
– vSEC NAT is not supported.

In this topology, E2, E3, LDRs, VMs (VM1, VM2, VM3, VM4) are part of the NAT domain E1. Anything above E1 such as
uplink of E1 is part of the default NAT domain. This topology consists of the following:
The flow from VM1 to VM2 and VM2 to VM1 is reported in VCF Operations for networks. Similarly the flow from VM3 to
VM4 and VM4 to VM3 is reported.
Example 2
This topology consists of the following:
• VM1 and VM2 are part of the E2 domain.
• VM3 and VM4 are part of the E2 domain.
• The E2 NAT domain and the E3 NAT domain are child domains of the E1 NAT domain.
• E1 is the single child of the default NAT domain.
• VM5 and VM6 are part of the E1 NAT domain.
From example 2, the following flows are reported in VCF Operations for networks:
• Flow from VM5 to VM6
• Flow from (VM1, VM2) to (VM3, VM4).

With Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Flow Logs, you can capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network
interfaces in your VPC.
You can create flow logs through the AWS portal.
1. Sign in to the AWS console.
2. In the Find Servicetext box, enter and select .
CloudWatch
3. Go to Logs > Action > Create log group.
The Create log group window appears.
4. In the Create Group Name field, enter a group name and click Create log group.
Note:
You should set the Retention setting to 1 day. VCF Operations for networks does not retrieve data older than
one day, and setting the retention to 1 day, saves on AWS expenses.
5. In the left navigation pane, click Service and then enter and select .
VPC
6. In the VPC Dashboard page, click Your VPCs.
7. Select the VPC that you want to modify, and click Flow Logs > Create flow log.

Option Action

Destination Select Send to CloudWatch Logs.

The system opens the VPC Flow Logs is requesting permission to use resources in your account page.

a) In the VPC Flow Logs is requesting permission to use resources in your account page, in the IAM Role,
select Create a new IAM Role.

a) Click Allow.

Create a pool of IPFIX Collectors
The BIG-IP system sends IPFIX log messages to a pool of IPFIX collectors.
1. Log in to the F5 console.
2. Click Main > Local Traffic > Pools > Pool Lists > Create.
The New Pool screen opens.
3. In the Name text box, enter a unique name for the pool.
4. In Health Monitors section, select gateway_icmp and move it in the Active box.
5. In the New Member section, configure the collector IP address and click Add.
Option Action
Node Name Enter the Collector IP address.
Service Port 2055
6. Click Finished.
Create an IPFIX Log Destination
Create a log destination to format the logs in IPFIX templates. After the formatting, these logs are sent to the IPFIX
collector.
1. In the F5 console, click Main > System > Logs > Configuration > Log Destinations > Create.
The Log Destinations screen appears.
2. In the Name text box, enter a unique name.
3. In the Type list, click IPFIX.
4. Configure the IPFIX Settings.
Option Action
Protocol Click Netflow V9.
Pool Name Click the pool name you created in the previous step.
Broadcom 5070

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Click Finished.
Create a Log Publisher
To send the logs to a specified log destination, you need to create a log publisher .
1. In the F5 console, click Main > System > Logs > Configuration > Log Publishers > Create.
The Log Publishers screen appears.
2. In the Name field, enter a unique name.
3. In the Destination box, select the log destination you created previously from the Available box, and move it in the
Selected box.
4. Click Finished.
Create iRules
To send the flow information to the configured VCF Operations for networks collector, you must create two iRules. One
iRule for the TCP protocol and another iRule for the UDP protocol.
1. In the F5 console, click Main > Local Traffic > iRules > iRule List > Create.
Local Traffic
The New iRule screen appears.
2. In the Name text box, enter a unique name.
3. In the Definition text box, enter the TCP rules for the TCP protocol and the UDP rule for the UDP protocol. For
information on the rules, see iRules for the TCP and UDP Protocols.
Ensure the iRule points to the publisher created previously.
4. Click Finished.
iRules for the TCP and UDP Protocols
TCP Rule
Use the following rule to create the iRule for TCP protocol:
Note:
Ensure the iRule points to the Log Publisher created previously.
when RULE_INIT {
set static::http_rule1_dest ""
set static::http_rule1_tmplt ""
}
# CLIENT_ACCEPTED event to initiate IPFIX destination and template
when CLIENT_ACCEPTED {
set start [clock clicks -milliseconds]
if { $static::http_rule1_dest == ""} {
# open the logging destination if it has not been opened yet
set static::http_rule1_dest [IPFIX::destination open -publisher /Common/<Log Publisher>]
}
if { $static::http_rule1_tmplt == ""} {
# if the template has not been created yet, create the template
set static::http_rule1_tmplt [IPFIX::template create "flowStartMilliseconds \
sourceIPv4Address \
sourceIPv6Address \
destinationIPv4Address \
destinationIPv6Address \
Broadcom 5071

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
sourceTransportPort \
destinationTransportPort \
protocolIdentifier \
octetTotalCount \
packetTotalCount \
octetDeltaCount \
packetDeltaCount \
postNATSourceIPv4Address \
postNATSourceIPv6Address \
postNATDestinationIPv4Address \
postNATDestinationIPv6Address \
postNAPTSourceTransportPort \
postNAPTDestinationTransportPort \
postOctetTotalCount \
postPacketTotalCount \
postOctetDeltaCount \
postPacketDeltaCount \
flowEndMilliseconds \ "]
}
set rule1_msg1 [IPFIX::msg create $static::http_rule1_tmplt]
}
# SERVER_CONNECTED event to initiate flow data to VCF Operations for networks and populate 5 tuples
when SERVER_CONNECTED {
set client_closed_flag 0
set server_closed_flag 0
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 flowStartMilliseconds $start
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 protocolIdentifier [IP::protocol]
# Clientside
if { [clientside {IP::version}] equals "4" } {
# Client IPv4 address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceIPv4Address [IP::client_addr]
# BIG-IP IPv4 VIP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationIPv4Address [clientside {IP::local_addr}]
} else {
# Client IPv6 address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceIPv6Address [IP::client_addr]
# BIG-IP IPv6 VIP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationIPv6Address [clientside {IP::local_addr}]
}
# Client port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceTransportPort [TCP::client_port]
# BIG-IP VIP port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationTransportPort [clientside {TCP::local_port}]
# Serverside
if { [serverside {IP::version}] equals "4" } {
# BIG-IP IPv4 self IP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATSourceIPv4Address [IP::local_addr]
# Server IPv4 IP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATDestinationIPv4Address [IP::server_addr]
} else {
# BIG-IP IPv6 self IP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATSourceIPv6Address [IP::local_addr]
# Server IPv6 IP address
Broadcom 5072

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATDestinationIPv6Address [IP::server_addr]
}
# BIG-IP self IP port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNAPTSourceTransportPort [TCP::local_port]
# Server port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNAPTDestinationTransportPort [TCP::server_port]
}
# SERVER_CLOSED event to collect IP pkts and bytes count on serverside
when SERVER_CLOSED {
set server_closed_flag 1
# when flow is completed, BIG-IP to server REQUEST pkts and bytes count
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 octetTotalCount [IP::stats bytes out]
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 packetTotalCount [IP::stats pkts out]
# when flow is completed, server to BIG-IP RESPONSE pkts and bytes count
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 octetDeltaCount [IP::stats bytes in]
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 packetDeltaCount [IP::stats pkts in]
IPFIX::destination send $static::http_rule1_dest $rule1_msg1
}
# CLIENT_CLOSED event to collect IP pkts and bytes count on clientside
when CLIENT_CLOSED {
set client_closed_flag 1
# when flow is completed, client to BIG-IP REQUEST pkts and bytes octetDeltaCount
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postOctetTotalCount [IP::stats bytes in]
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postPacketTotalCount [IP::stats pkts in]
# when flow is completed, BIG-IP to client RESPONSE pkts and bytes count
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postOctetDeltaCount [IP::stats bytes out]
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postPacketDeltaCount [IP::stats pkts out]
# record the client closed time in ms
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 flowEndMilliseconds [clock click -milliseconds]
# send the IPFIX log
IPFIX::destination send $static::http_rule1_dest $rule1_msg1
}
UDP Rule
Use the following rule to create the iRule for UDP protocol:
Note:
Ensure the iRule points to the Log Publisher created previously.
when RULE_INIT {
set static::http_rule1_dest ""
set static::http_rule1_tmplt ""
}
# CLIENT_ACCEPTED event to initiate IPFIX destination and template
when CLIENT_ACCEPTED {
set start [clock clicks -milliseconds]
if { $static::http_rule1_dest == ""} {
# open the logging destination if it has not been opened yet
set static::http_rule1_dest [IPFIX::destination open -publisher /Common/<Log Publisher>]
}
if { $static::http_rule1_tmplt == ""} {
# if the template has not been created yet, create the template
set static::http_rule1_tmplt [IPFIX::template create "flowStartMilliseconds \

sourceIPv4Address \
sourceIPv6Address \
destinationIPv4Address \
destinationIPv6Address \
sourceTransportPort \
destinationTransportPort \
protocolIdentifier \
octetTotalCount \
packetTotalCount \
octetDeltaCount \
packetDeltaCount \
postNATSourceIPv4Address \
postNATSourceIPv6Address \
postNATDestinationIPv4Address \
postNATDestinationIPv6Address \
postNAPTSourceTransportPort \
postNAPTDestinationTransportPort \
postOctetTotalCount \
postPacketTotalCount \
postOctetDeltaCount \
postPacketDeltaCount \
flowEndMilliseconds \ "]
}
set rule1_msg1 [IPFIX::msg create $static::http_rule1_tmplt]
}
# SERVER_CONNECTED event to initiate flow data to VCF Operations for networks and populate 5 tuples
when SERVER_CONNECTED {
set client_closed_flag 0
set server_closed_flag 0
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 flowStartMilliseconds $start
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 protocolIdentifier [IP::protocol]
# Clientside
if { [clientside {IP::version}] equals "4" } {
# Client IPv4 address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceIPv4Address [IP::client_addr]
# BIG-IP IPv4 VIP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationIPv4Address [clientside {IP::local_addr}]
} else {
# Client IPv6 address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceIPv6Address [IP::client_addr]
# BIG-IP IPv6 VIP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationIPv6Address [clientside {IP::local_addr}]
}
# Client port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 sourceTransportPort [UDP::client_port]
# BIG-IP VIP port
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 destinationTransportPort [clientside {UDP::local_port}]
# Serverside
if { [serverside {IP::version}] equals "4" } {
# BIG-IP IPv4 self IP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATSourceIPv4Address [IP::local_addr]
# Server IPv4 IP address
IPFIX::msg set $rule1_msg1 postNATDestinationIPv4Address [IP::server_addr]
