| ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Capacity   | Capacity    | Displays the maximum number of units  |
(of the given capacity type) that can be
licensed by this license key.
Disbalance factor (%) Disbalance factor (%) Identifies the state of disbalance in a
VCF Operations cluster and calculates
the disbalance factor (when one or more
nodes have a higher density among all
the nodes in the cluster). Based on the
disbalance percentage of the node, the
following alerts are triggered:
• Warning: If the disbalance factor metric
is equal to or greater than 5%.
• Immediate: If the disbalance factor
metric is equal to or greater than 7%.
• Critical: If the disbalance factor metric
is equal to or greater than 10%.

Cloud Zone Metrics
VCF Automation collects memory, storage, and vCPU limit related metrics at project level on per cloud zone basis.
Cloud Zone Limits Metrics
You can view the memory, storage, and vCPU limit related metrics defined in VCF Automation in VCF Operations. VCF
Operations alerts when the utilisation exceeds configured limits in any of the individual cloud zones.
Note:
The resource limits are configured in VCF Automation. For vCenter objects, limits for all resources - vCPU,
memory, and storage - can be configured. However, for public clouds like AWS, Azure, and GCP only vCPU and
memory limits can be configured.
Table 1592: Cloud Zone Limits Metrics
Property Name Metrics Description
Cloud Zone Limits Memory allocated (KB) This metric displays the total utilized cloud
zone memory.
Memory Limit (KB) This metric displays the limit set on the
cloud zone memory usage.
Broadcom 5897

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Property Name Metrics Description
Memory Utilized (%) This metric displays the percentage of
memory used out of the memory limit set.
Formula ((Memory allocated (KB)/ Memory
Limit (KB))
Storage allocated (GB) This metric displays the total storage
utilized by the cloud zone.
Storage Limit (GB) This metrics displays the limit set on the
cloud zone storage usage.
Storage Utilized (%) This metric displays the percentage of
storage used out of the storage limit set.
Formula (Storage allocated (KB)/ Storage
Limit (KB))
vCPU allocated This metric displays the total vCPU utilized
by the cloud zone.
vCPU Limit This metrics displays the limit set on the
cloud zone vCPU usage.
vCPU Utilized (%) This metric displays the percentage of

(KB))
Summary Metrics for Cloud Zone Centers
Summary metrics provide information about the VM migration as part of workload planning.
Metric Name Description
WLP Displays the VM migration trend as part of workload optimization.
These metrics are deactivated by default. You must activate them
from policies.
• Fail Count: Number of failed VM move attempts in the last daily
cycle.
• Number of runs: The total number of times the WLP was run
during the last daily cycle.
• Success Count: The number of successful VM moves during the
last daily cycle.
Metrics for vSAN
VCF Operations collects metrics for vSAN objects.
From the left menu, click Inventory > Inventory Panel (Detailed View) > Integrations > All Objects > vSAN Adapter,
and then select one of the vSAN adapter objects listed and click the Metrics tab.
Disk I/O and Disk Space Metrics for vSAN Disk Groups
The VCF Operations collects the metrics you use to monitor the performance of your vSAN disk groups.
Disk I/O metrics for the vSAN disk groups include:
• Disk I/O|Reads Per Second (IOPS)
• Disk I/O|Writes Per Second (IOPS
• Disk I/O|Max Observed Reads Per Second (IOPS)
• Disk I/O|Max Observed Writes Per Second (IOPS)
Broadcom 5898

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

• Disk I/O|Throughput Write (bps)
• Disk I/O|Average Read Latency (ms)
• Disk I/O|Average Write Latency (ms)
• Disk I/O|Total Bus Resets
• Disk I/O|Total Commands Aborted per second
The following Disk I/O metrics are disabled by default:
• Disk I/O|Read Count
• Disk I/O|Write Count
• Disk I/O|Average Device Latency
• Disk I/O|Average Device Read Latency
• Disk I/O|Average Device Write Latency
• Disk I/O|Total Number of Errors
Disk space metrics for vSAN disk groups include:

• Disk Space|Used (bytes)
• Disk Space|Usage (%)
Read Cache Metrics for vSAN Disk Groups
The VCF Operations collects metrics and performs capacity trend analysis on a hybrid vSAN read cache. Read Cache
metrics are not collected for a vSAN all-flash configuration.
Read cache metrics for the vSAN disk group include:
• Read Cache|Hit Rate (%)
• Read Cache|Miss Rate Ratio
• Read Cache|Reads Per Second (IOPS)
• Read Cache|Read Latency (ms)
• Read Cache|Writes Per Second (IOPS)
• Read Cache|Write Latency (ms)
The following read cache metrics are disabled by default:
• Read Cache|Read I/O Count
• Read Cache|Write I/O Count
Write Buffer Metrics for vSAN Disk Groups
The VCF Operations collects the metrics you use to monitor the write buffer capacity of your vSAN disk groups.
A reasonably balanced system consumes a significant amount of write buffer. Before placing additional workload on the
vSAN, check the write buffer metrics for the vSAN disk group.
• Write Buffer|Capacity (bytes)
• Write Buffer|Free (%)
• Write Buffer|Usage (%)
• Write Buffer|Used (byte)
• Write Buffer|Reads Per Second (IOPS)
• Write Buffer|Read Latency (ms)
• Write Buffer|Writes Per Second (IOPS)
• Write Buffer|Write Latency (ms)
The following write buffer metrics are disabled by default:
Broadcom 5899

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Write Buffer|Read I/O Count
• Write Buffer|Write I/O Count

Capacity Model for vSAN Objects
The capacity model introduced in VCF Operations 6.7 now extends the support for vSAN objects like, vSAN cluster, Fault
domains, and Cache/Capacity disks. The Capacity tab provides Time Remaining data for the selected vSAN cluster, Fault
domain, Cache/Capacity Disk objects. The information is presented in a graphical format.
Where You Find the Capacity Tab
In the menu, click Environment, then select a group, custom data center, application, or inventory object. The Object
details page appears. Click the Capacity tab.
The VCF Operations defines the capacity model for the following vSAN resource containers:
• vSAN Cluster
– Disk Space
• vSAN Fault Domain
– CPU
– Memory
– Disk Space
• vSAN Cache/Capacity Disk
– Disk Space
Understanding the Capacity Tab
For the selected vSAN resource, the capacity tab lists the capacity used and Time Remaining until the associated CPU,
memory, and disk space resources, respectively, run out.
• If you select the vSAN cluster, the capacity tab lists the capacity used and time remaining until the associated disk
space runs out.
• If you select the vSAN Fault Domain, the capacity tab lists the capacity used and time remaining until the associated
CPU, memory, and disk space resources run out.
• If you select the vSAN Cache/Capacity Disk Space, the capacity tab lists capacity used and time remaining until the
associated disk space runs out.
The available graph depicts - for your choice of CPU, memory, or disk space - the amount of resource used, plotted
against time. A line on the graph shows 100 percent usable capacity and a trend line projects how swiftly resource use is
approaching 100 percent. The time line shows when the selected resource is to reach capacity.

Green Score metrics are collected for virtual machine, host system, cluster compute resource, vSphere World, and

Metric Name Object Type Description
Power|Total Energy (Wh) Virtual Machine Total energy used.

Total Energy (Wh) = Sum(Power|Energy
(Joule))/3600

Formula:
Total Energy (Wh) = Sum(Power|Energy
(Joule))/3600
Sustainability|CO₂ Emission (kg) Cluster Compute Resource Estimated carbon dioxide emissions.
Calculated as power consumption* CO₂
Emission rate

System(Power|Total Energy(Wh)))/1000 *
0.672
Sustainability|CO₂ Emission before Cluster Compute Resource Estimated carbon dioxide emissions
Virtualization (kg) before virtualization, assuming that power
consumption per physical server is 100W,
reflecting a low end hardware specification.

CO₂ Emission before Virtualization (kg) =
Summary|Number of Running VMs * 0.1 *
0.672

(kg) from all idle VMs. Calculated as C O₂
emission rate * Power consumed by
Idle VMs, where the rate is set at cluster
property / 1000.

CO₂ Emission by Idle VMs (kg) =
Sum(VM(Power|Total Energy (Wh)), If

Wasted by Idle VMs (Wh) * 0.672

Metrics for Policies
Each policy is an object in VCF Operations. This allows you to track every change in the policy and create any dashboard,
report, or alert on policy usage distribution.
VCF Operations collects metrics for the object type 'Policy'.
Metric Key Metric Name Description
NumberOfEffectiveObjects Number of Affected Objects Represents the count of objects affected by
the effective policy.
NumberOfVirtualMachines Number of Affected vCenter Virtual Represents the number of vCenter Virtual
Machines Machines associated with a specific policy.
NumberOfCustomGroups Number of Assigned Custom Groups Represents the number of assigned custom
groups for a specific policy.
NumberOfDefaultAssignedObjects Number of Default Assigned Objects Represents the number of objects that are
assigned by default for a specific policy.
This metric value is 0 for all policies except
the default policy.
NumberOfDirectAssignedObjects Number of Directly Assigned Objects Represents the number of objects that are
directly assigned for a specific policy.
NumberOfInheritedObjects Number of Objects Assigned By Scope Represents the count of inherited objects
for a specific policy.
Broadcom 5921

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Property Definitions in VCF Operations
Properties are attributes of objects in the VCF Operations environment. You use properties in symptom definitions. You
can also use properties in dashboards, views, and reports.
VCF Operations uses adapters to collect properties for target objects in your environment. Property definitions for all
objects connected through the vCenter adapter are provided. The properties collected depend on the objects in your
environment.
You can add symptoms based on properties to an alert definition so that you are notified if a change occurs to properties
on your monitored objects. For example, disk space is a hardware property of a virtual machine. You can use disk space
to define a symptom that warns you when the value falls below a certain numeric value.
You can add symptoms based on properties to an alert definition so that you are notified if a change occurs to properties
on your monitored objects. For example, disk space is a hardware property of a virtual machine. You can use disk space
to define a symptom that warns you when the value falls below a certain numeric value. See the VCF Operations User
Guide.
VCF Operations generates Object Type Classification and Subclassification properties for every object. You can use
object type classification properties to identify whether an object is an adapter instance, custom group, application,
tier, or a general object with property values ADAPTER_INSTANCE, GROUP, BUSINESS_SERVICE, TIER, or GENERAL,
respectively.
Properties for vCenter Server Components
The VMware vSphere solution is installed with VCF Operationsand includes the vCenter adapter. VCF Operations uses
the vCenter adapter to collect properties for objects in the vCenter system.
vCenter components are listed in the file for the vCenter adapter. The following example shows the
describe.xml
runtime property or Memory Capacity for the virtual machine in the .
memoryCap describe.xml
<ResourceGroup instanced="false" key="runtime" nameKey="5300" validation="">
<ResourceAttribute key="memoryCap" nameKey="1780" dashboardOrder="200" dataType="float"
defaultMonitored="true" isDiscrete="false" isRate="false" maxVal=""
minVal="" isProperty="true" unit="kb"/>
</ResourceGroup>
The element includes the name of the property that appears in the UI and is documented as a
ResourceAttribute

Broadcom 5929

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Property Key Property Name Description
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Configuired Configuired Size(GB) This property displays the disk space
Size(GB) configured for the virtual disk.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Datastore Datastore This property displays the name of the
datastore where the scsi disk is present. If an
RDM is present, only a pointer to the RDM is
present in the datastore.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Disk Mode Disk Mode This property determines how a virtual disk
is affected by snapshots. The disk mode acts
on each individual VMDK, not on the whole
VM. The available options are Independent
persistent, Persistent, Non-persistent, this
property is disabled by default.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|SCSI Bus Sharing SCSI Bus Sharing This property sets the type of bus sharing
for the VM and determines whether to share
the bus or not. Depending on the type of bus
sharing, the VM can access the same virtual
disk simultaneously on the same server or any
other server. The available options are None,
Physical, Virtual, this property is disabled by
default.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|SCSI Controller SCSI Controller Type This virtual storage controller property
Type connects the virtual and physical disks to
the VM. The available options are LSI SAS/
PVSCSI, this property is disabled by default.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Virtual Disk Sharing Virtual Disk Sharing This property allows VMFS-backed disks to be
shared by multiple VMs. The available options
are Unspecified, No sharing, Multi-Writer. You
can use this option to disable protection for
certain cluster aware applications, where the
applications ensures that simultaneous write
operation from two VMs does not induce data
loss. This property is disabled by default.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Virtual Device Node Virtual Device Node This property determines the virtual device
bus location. The virtual disks are enumerated
starting with the first controller. This property is
disabled by default.
Virtual Disk:scsi0:0|Is RDM Is RDM This property indicates whether the virtual disk
is an RDM or not. This property is enabled by
default.
Virtual Disk|File Name File Name This property is disabled by default.
Virtual Disk|Label Label This property displays the device label.
Virtual Disk:scsi1:1|Compatibility Mode Compatibility Mode This property displays the compatibility mode
for the RDMs. The options are physical
and virtual. Virtual mode specifies the full
virtualization of the mapped device whereas
physical mode specifies minimal SCSI
virtualization of the mapped device. This
property is disabled by default in the base
policy.
Broadcom 5930

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Services Properties
VCF Operations displays the following properties for services.
Table 1659: Services Properties
Property Name Description
Type The name of the service type.
Install Path The install path.
Ports List of service listening ports.
Virtual Machine The name of the parent VM.
Virtual Machine MOID The MOID of the VM.
Version Version of the discovered service.
Is Application Member Indicates that the service is a member of the group of services
forming an application.
Category Category of the service.
Connection Type If there is a remote process that was connected to one of the
listening ports of the given service, then the property's value is set
to Incoming. If not, it is set to Outgoing. If there is no connection to
another service, then the value of the property is set to N/A.
Has Dynamic Port Indicates whether the service has dynamic ports or not.
Status Indicates the status of the service.
Up: The service is running.
Down: The service is unavailable on the monitored VM.
Unavailable: The service is unavailable on a VM that is not being
monitored.
None: The service is not available within 7 days.

Extending Monitoring Capabilities
Installing and Configuring Management Packs in VMware Cloud Foundation
Operations from the Solutions Catalog
Integrations in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations expand your ability to monitor and troubleshoot your software-
defined data center and third-party products. You can install and configure management packs from the Solutions Catalog
to connect physical and virtual layers, providing visibility into performance, capacity, and efficiency.Use these guides
to install integrations in connected or disconnected environments. You can access configuration details for specific
management packs, including AWS, Kubernetes, ServiceNow, and various databases. If you encounter problems, apply
the troubleshooting steps to resolve adapter, installation, and data collection issues.
Getting Started with Integrations for VMware Cloud Foundation Operations
Integrations in VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Operations provide an extensible capability for expanding the monitoring,
troubleshooting, and restoring the functionality of your SDDC and other third-party solutions. Administrators can install and
configure management packs in a VMware Cloud Foundation Operations instance.
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations natively provides an insight into the virtual layer of your data centers. The
Integrations provide the flexibility and customization by allowing you to bring in data from different VMware systems and
environments and see the performance, scalability, redundancy, and efficiency of your stack. To see the vertical in that
stack, you can use management packs.
You can use management packs to relate the physical and application layer objects to the virtual components. This helps
you prioritize visualization and alerts and view your environment in a holistic way. Installing management packs in VCF
Operations enables you to have a logical and structured view of your environment where you can find data with ease. This
allows for capacity planning, crisis management, cost calculations, and root cause analysis.
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for Integrations Index
You can access VCF Operations for Integrations User Guides and Release Notes by browsing through the list on
this page. The User Guide provides information on how you can install, configure, and use the VCF Operations for
Integrations. Release Notes provide details about new features, known issues, and resolved issues with every release.
About VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for Integrations
Management packs in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations provide capability for expanding the monitoring,
troubleshooting, and remediation functionality of SDDC and third party solutions. Administrators can install and configure
management packs in a VMware Cloud Foundation Operations instance.
Download and Installation
If VCF Operations is connected to Internet, you can install Integrations directly from within the product. Alternatively, you
can also download Integrations for VCF Operations from the VCF Solutions Catalog.
Release Notes
The VMware Cloud Foundation Operations for Integrations Release Notes provide details on what's new with every latest
release.

Installing and Configuring Integrations in VMware Cloud Foundation Operations
Follow the respective procedure to install your management pack depending on whether your environment can connect to
the Internet or not.
Installing Integrations in a Connected Environment
Installing a Management Pack in a connected environment, can be done from VCF Operations. All integrations are
available in Solutions Catalog. For information on compatibility between products, see Product Interoperability Matrix.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations user interface with administrator privileges.
2. In the menu, select Administration and in the left pane select Integrations > Solutions Catalog.
3. The Available tab shows all the Management Packs available to be downloaded and installed in VCF Operations.
4. Click Download on the specific Management Pack
5. Accept the EULA and download the Management Pack.
6. After successfull download, the Management Pack is available under the Downloaded tab.
7. Go to the Downloaded tab and click Install on the management pack tile.
8. Once the installation is complete, you can start using the management pack by adding Accounts.
9. In the menu, select Administration and in the left pane select Integrations > Accounts.
10.On the Accounts tab, click Add Account.
11.On the Accounts Types page, click the management pack you have installed.
12.Enter a display name and description for the cloud account.
a) Enter the for the management pack instance as you want it to appear in VCF Operations.
Name
b) Enter the for the management packs with any additional information that helps you manage your
Description
instances.
13.Select the you want to use to sign on to the environment from the drop-down menu. To add new
Credential
credentials to access the management pack, click the plus sign and create a credential.
14.Enter to manage the management pack on VCF Operations. If you have only one account,
Credential/Group
select the Default collector group.
15.Enter the connection information as required to configure the instance of the management pack. Each management
pack has unique settings, configure the settings as prompted to configure that instance of the management pack. For
more information on individual management packs, see List of Management Packs.
16.Click VALIDATE CONNECTION to initiate the authentication request to the CSP authentication service.
17.Configure the Advanced Settings for the management pack.
18.Click ADD.
Verify that the adapter is configured and collecting data by viewing application-related data.
Installing Integrations in a Disconnected Environment
Integrations consist of a PAK file that contains default dashboards for the objects that the management pack identifies.
After installation, configure the integration.
All integrations are available in VCF Solutions Catalog. For information on compatibility between products, see VMware
Product Interoperability Matrix.
• Download the PAK file from VCF Solutions Catalog.
Broadcom 5968

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Save that PAK file to a temporary folder on your local system.
• Before you install the PAK file or upgrade your VCF Operations instance, clone any customized content to preserve it.
Customized content can include alert definitions, symptom definitions, recommendations, and views.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations user interface with administrator privileges.
2. In the menu, select Administration and in the left pane select Integrations > Repository.
3. On the Repository tab, click Add. The Add Solution wizard opens. The wizard includes three pages where you
locate and upload a PAK file, accept the EULA and install, and review the installation.
4. Click Browse to locate the temporary folder and select the PAK file that you downloaded.
5. To upgrade to the latest version of the management pack:
a) Select the Install the PAK file check box even if it is already installed to upgrade the management pack using the
current PAK file even if an older version of the PAK file is already uploaded. Do not overwrite or update the solution
alerts, symptoms, recommendations, and policies and leave all user customizations in place.
b) Select the Reset Default Content, overwriting to a newer version provided by this update. User modifications
to DEFAULT Alert Definitions, Symptoms, Recommendations, Policy Definitions, Views, Dashboards, Widgets,
and Reports is overwritten. If you are installing a product software update, clone or backup the content before you
proceed check box to upgrade the management pack using the current PAK file and overwrite the solution default
alerts, symptoms, recommendations, and policies with the newer versions provided with the current PAK file.
A reset overwrites customized content. Clone your customized content before the upgrade.
6. A warning, The PAK file is unsigned appears if the PAK file is not signed with a digital signature that VMware
provides. The digital signature indicates the original developer or publisher and provides the authenticity of the
management pack. If installing a PAK file from an untrusted source is a concern, check with the management pack
distributor before proceeding with the installation.
7. Click Upload. The upload might take several minutes.
8. Read and accept the EULA, and click Next. Installation details appear in the window during the process.
The installation starts only if all the nodes of the cluster are accessible.
9. Review the installation progress, including the VCF Operations nodes where the adapter was installed. When the
installation is complete, click Finish.
10.In the menu, select Administration and in the left pane select Integrations > Accounts.
11.On the Accounts tab, click Add Account.

Troubleshooting
The troubleshooting section provides guidance on commonly performed activities to troubleshoot problems in VCF
Operations Cloud. You can troubleshoot adapter, installation, data collection, cloud proxy and other issues related to VCF
Operations Cloud.
vSphere Management Pack Issues
You can troubleshoot general problems associated with vSphere and vCenter Management Packs, such as credential
errors, connection errors, collector group errors that might occur when using VCF Operations Cloud.
Wrong Credentials
You might be prompted with incorrect credentials error while accessing vCenter.
Solution: Ensure that the specified user credentials are correct and the user has required permissions to access the target
vCenter.
Note:
The user credentials are case-sensitive. Ensure that you enter the correct values.
No Collector Group Defined
Collector group is not defined for vCenter in VCF Operations Cloud.
Solution: In VCF Operations Cloud, deploy a Cloud Proxy and select it as the collector for the target vCenter. For details,
refer to the Troubleshooting section in the VCF Operations Cloud Getting Started Guide.
No Connection to Target vCenter
No connection is established between VCF Operations Cloud and vCenter.
Solution: Ensure that you validate the connection once you configure a Cloud account.
Note:
FQDN/IP of the target vCenter must be reachable from all the nodes be it VCF Operations on-prem or Cloud
Proxy or VCF Operations Cloud.
Plug-In not Registered
An error message indicates that the plug-in is not registered with vCenter.
Solution: In Management Pack configurations, navigate to Manage Registrations, then unregister and re-register the
Management Pack.
Management Pack Not Collecting Data
vCenter Management Pack might not be collecting all the required data, even though the connection between VCF
Operations Cloud and Management Pack is valid.
Solution:
1. Verify minimum collection credentials. For more information, refer the Knowledge Base article.
2. Add temporarily to verify the collection.
an account with administrative privileges
Metrics Missing After vCenter Upgrade
You might notice that some of the metrics are missing, after you upgrade vCenter.
Solution: Please check vCenter documentation to verify if the statistic has moved to another level. If that is the case, you
must increase the statistics level for said metric on vCenter.
Broadcom 5970

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Management Pack Configuration Issues
You can troubleshoot Management Pack configuration issues like, connection errors, data collection errors, certificate
errors and other issues which occur while using VCF Operations.
Error When Validating Connection
When you try to validate a connection between VCF Operations Cloud and the Management Pack, an error message is
displayed.
Solution:
1. Ensure port 443 is open between the collector and vCenter using telnet.
2. Ensure permissions are adequate. Use an account with administrator privileges.
3. Check file for test connection failures.
collector.log
4. Use to check whether the certificate is OK on vCenter.
openssl s_client -connect
Test Connection Works but Collection Never Starts
You might notice that the test connection works but the Management Pack fails to collect the data.
Solution: Check the Management Pack logs for errors related to user permissions or vCenter session errors. Sometimes
network or vCenter itself can have issues which prevents the Management Pack from starting.
Test Connection Fails due to Multiple Certificates
You might observe that the test connection fails if there are multiple certificates.
Solution: Check for wild card certificates in Administration > Certificates page as VCF Operations Cloud will use these
certificates as default.
Data Collection is Inconsistent
You might observe that the Management Pack starts data collection, but the collected data is inconsistent. Confirm
whether this happens to all vCenter instances or just one instance. If the issue occurs on all vCenter instances, the
problem is with VCF Operations Cloud or network.
If the issue occurs only on one vCenter instance, check the following.
Solution:
1. Check vCenter query time at Management Pack level.
2. Check Tag query time to ensure tags are not causing delay.
3. Check Management Pack logs for hints as to why the collection might be slow.
4. Confirm latency between vCenter> Remote Collector / Cloud Proxy> VCF Operations Cloud is within supported limits.
5. Confirm vCenter itself is sized correctly and has no heap dumps on vCenter. Missing
/var/log/vmware/vapi
metrics.
6. Check the policy and ensure that the metric is enabled.
7. If looking for instanced metrics, ensure is set to enabled for the metric in the policy.
instanced
8. Confirm advanced setting in the Management Pack has not disabled any collection type.
9. Ensure user has permissions.
10.Check vCenter MOB and confirm that the metric is available.
General Management Pack Issues
You can troubleshoot generic Management Pack problems such as, connection errors, collector or collector group errors,
certificate errors and other issues which occur while using VCF Operations Cloud.
Broadcom 5971

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Certificate Expired
VCF Operations Cloud might prompt you with a Certificate Expired or Renew Certificate message when you try to validate
the connection.
Solution:
1. Validate the connection to import the new certificate.
2. You might have to remove the existing certificate.
Incorrect Credentials
You might be prompted with incorrect credentials error message when you validate the connection between VCF
Operations Cloud and the Management Pack.
Solution: Acquire correct credentials for the endpoint.
Unreachable Error
Connection unreachable or connection timeout error is displayed when you try to validate the connection between VCF
Operations and the Management Pack.
Solution: Validate the Operations/CP is responsive to ping and https requests through
ping <endpoint> and curl -
to validate connectivity.
v telnet://<endpoint>:443
Note:
Most end points use port 443 for connection, for more information please refer VCF Operations Cloud
documentation.
Collector or Collector Group Missing
The Management Pack might report collector or collector group missing error, if the collector is offline or the collector is
not assigned to a Management Pack.
Solution: Verify that collector is online and is assigned to the Management Pack.
Management Pack Collection Cycle Issues
You can troubleshoot vCenter Management Pack collection cycle issues such as high latency issue, end point not
processing requests, and other issues which occur while using VCF Operations.
High Latency Issue
You might observe high latency between the collector and the end point.
Solution:
Add Remote Collector /Cloud Proxy on site where endpoint resides (Remote Collector max latency 200ms - Cloud Proxy
max latency 500ms between Remote Collector /Cloud Proxy and analytics nodes). Ping can show latency between
collector and endpoint. ~10-20ms max. This may depend on the amount of data that needs to be collected.
Integrations Configuration Guides
Management Pack for Aggregator
The Management Pack for Aggregator document provides information about the Aggregator feature that is introduced in
VCF Operations.
Broadcom 5972

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Intended Audience
This information is intended for anyone who wants to install the Aggregator. feature to manage distributed deployments of
VCF Operations instances.
Introduction
With Aggregator you can unify your multi-site VCF Operations deployment into a single pane of glass. This single
pane of glass provides a holistic view of the child VCF Operations instance. You can instantiate a deployment of VCF
Operations with the capability of receiving key metrics for specified objects from other VCF Operations deployment in your
environment.
Important:
SDDC Health and Configuration Dashboard is not supported due to the EOGS of SDDC Health management
pack and will be removed from the aggregator management pack in the future release.
The management pack allows you to unlock the following use cases:
• Provide a good set of Executive Dashboards for a worldwide company, without the need to have multiple browser tabs
open for several VCF Operations instances.
• Provide a summary of performance, capacity, and configuration to Senior Executives and Virtual Infrastructure
Administrators across all your vSphere environments.
• Provide a unified view of alerts triggered across the virtual environments into a single pane for making it easier for
NOC or Helpdesk to initiate action.
• Ability to create a data warehouse where user selected set of metrics can be stored for data archiving and report use
cases.
• Ability to provide summarized views of health and configuration of your Software Defined Data Center stack. This
includes core applications such as VMware vCenter, VMware NSX, and VMware vSAN. The solution also covers the
management applications such as VCF Operations, Log management, VCF Automation, VCF Business, and VMware
Site Recovery Manager.
Architecture
The Management Pack for Aggregator follows a simple server-client architecture. This management pack is installed
on the VCF Operations instance, which you have identified as your unified single pane of glass instance. It is highly
recommended that this instance is only used for Aggregator. After you deploy VCF Operations, you can use the
management pack configuration page to add your existing VCF Operations instances to point to this Aggregator instance.
When configuring the management pack, enter the name of a configuration file that stores the information about the
objects and metrics to be fetched from your existing VCF Operations instances into the newly deployed Aggregator
instance.
You can plan your architecture to apply the capabilities of Management Pack for Aggregator.
ACME Corp a Global Manufacturing company has virtual environments spanning across the globe to
meet their regional business requirements. They are leveraging the VMware Software Defined data
center to provide key IT services to line of business. They have an SDDC footprint in Singapore, London,
Johannesburg, and San Jose. As a part of their Capacity Management and Performance Troubleshooting
requirements they are leveraging VCF Operations to help their Operations and Procurement teams. They
currently have an instance of VCF Operations deployed at each of these data center locations. ACME
Corporation is looking to leverage the Management Pack for Aggregator to create a single pane of glass
across all the data center locations. They want to leverage this single pane for their operations, capacity
procurement, and senior executives to provide them with a unified view of their IT landscape. As their London
data center has the largest footprint and low latency connectivity to other data centers, they want to host this
unified instance in their London data center.
Based on the mentioned requirements, ACME Corp must deploy a new global standalone instance of VCF
Operations with the Aggregator Management pack using the following deployment architecture:
Broadcom 5973

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Logical Architecture of the Management Pack for Aggregator for ACME Corp.
Sizing and Collection Time Interval Considerations
The VCF Operations instance hosting the Aggregator management pack should be sized just like any other VCF
Operations instances.
For more information, see the KB article 324340. The following are the best practices.
Broadcom 5974

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Out-of-the-box, Management Pack for Aggregator collects data for objects such as ESX hosts, clusters, datacenters,
datastores, and so on. Virtual machine data is not collected. Based on this, most of the environments can be monitored
with one Extra Large Node.
• The Aggregator instance of VCF Operations should be used only for collecting data from the Aggregator MP. No other
MP on this VCF Operations instance should be configured to collect from any other data sources.
• If you add new objects and metrics to an existing deployment of your Aggregator VCF Operations instance, ensure to
run the sizing calculator to meet the sizing requirements.
• With Management Pack for Aggregator, you can either collect data directly from child VCF Operations instances or use
a remote collector to optimize the collection process. The default collection cycle of Management Pack for Aggregator
is 5 minutes. This time interval works accurately for a centralized VCF Operations collecting data from other child VCF
Operations instances that are located within a short distance. You can also use a remote collector for data collection.
Otherwise, when centralized VCF Operations collects data directly without a remote collector and latency is long, you
can set the collection interval to 15 minutes. This ensures data collection without any gaps.
• As most of the Aggregator use cases are met by collecting data for objects other than virtual machines from your
environment, it is recommended to avoid the collection of virtual machine data as this drastically increases the sizing
requirement for the Aggregator instance in a large-scale environment.
Deploying the Standalone Global Instance
Before you can configure Federation, you must deploy a dedicated VCF Operations instance to serve as the Global Ops
Instance
• Capacity: Determine if you need a specific size. For most global views, a Large or Extra Large node is recommended
to handle the object count from all child sites.
• Network: An IP address and DNS name (e.g., global-ops.corp.local).
• Media: The standard VCF Operations OVA file (same as used for Fleet Ops Instances).
This process converts a blank VCF Operations node into your Global Ops Instance.
1. Deploy the OVF/OVA
a) Log in to your vSphere Client.
b) Right-click the cluster/host and select Deploy OVF Template.
c) Select the file.
VCF Operations .ova
d) Select Deployment Configuration: Choose Large or Extra Large (Federation nodes require significant memory
to map objects from all sites).
e) Network Mapping: Connect to a management network that can reach all regional VCF Operations instances.
f) Customize Template:
• Set the IP address, Gateway, DNS, and Timezone.
• Crucial: Ensure the Timezone matches your Fleet Operations Instances (usually UTC is best practice for all).
Broadcom 5975

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
g) Power on the appliance.
2. Initial Cluster Setup
a) Navigate to https://<Global-IP>/admin in your browser.
b) Select Add New Nodes"Master Node Configuration: You do not need to add Data Nodes or Remote Collectors
immediately unless you have an immense environment (100k+ objects).
c) Set Admin Password: Create a strong root and admin password.
d) Certificate: Install a CA-signed certificate immediately to ensure secure HTTPS handshakes with Fleet Ops
Instances
e) Finish: Allow the cluster to come online (usually 10-20 minutes).
3. "Empty State" Verification
a) Do NOT configure vCenter adapters on this instance.
b) Do NOT install standard management packs (Storage, AWS, etc.).
c) Why? The Global Ops Instance should be kept "clean." Its only job is to aggregate data from other Ops instances.
If you start monitoring local vCenters with it, you will pollute the global view and waste resources.

Configuration File in the Aggregator Management Pack
When you configure an Aggregator adapter instance, you must specify a config file. The config file specifies what kind of
information an adapter instance must collect. Out-of-the-box, the Aggregator Management Pack is shipped with config file
named as .
federation_config
The config file retrieves the following information.
• Resources
• Metrics
• Properties
For example, if you want the adapter to collect information like host system and CPU metrics of that object, then this
information has to be defined in the config file. When these parameters are added, then the adapter instance starts
collecting information pertaining to the required specification. The changes are reflected in the config file only when the
adapter instance is restarted.
With Management Pack for Aggregator, you can retrieve a subset of objects from an object type of a child VCF
Operations. The adapter provides a mechanism to filter the subset by either using properties or tags.
The tag-based filter used is:
<Filter> <Tag category="SOME_CATEGORY" name="SOME_TAG" /> </Filter>
The property-based filter used is:
<Filter> <Property attrkey="SOME_KEY" value="SOME_VALUE"/> </Filter>
Note:
You can use only one filter for a given object type, otherwise, the configuration file validation fails.
To create filters for resource kinds, add the filtering element immediately after the resource kind element in the config file.
For example:
Broadcom 5978

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
<ResourceKind resourceKindKey="...">
<Filter>
<Property attrkey="..." value="..."/>
</Filter>
<Metric ..."/>
<Property .../>
</ResourceKind>
Types of Config Files Used in the Management Pack for Aggregator
Default Config File Management Pack for Aggregator contains a default config file. The Management Pack for Aggregator
dashboards are based on these config files. The default config file contains information of vCenter to host
level and not VM level. The config file also provides information of vCenter operation adapter objects,
VMware SDDC Health Monitoring Solution adapter, and VMware Site Recovery Manager adapter.
Note:
The default federation_config file is aligned with the latest VCF Operations. Ensure that the
desired metrics/properties from the older versions (which no longer exist in the newer versions) are
mentioned in the config file.
Heterogeneous Config You are not limited to using the same config file for all adapter instances when you are configuring multiple
File adapter instances for a separate child of VCF Operations instance. You can collect different data from
different child VCF Operations instances. You can have different level of information in different config files.
Locate Configuration File
The default file has pre-defined objects and metrics, which are collected from the child VCF Operations instances.
Verify that you have installed the Management Pack for Aggregator on your environment.
1. Login to VCF Operations as an administrator.
2. In the menu, click Administration, and in the left pane click Configuration > Metric Configurations.
3. Under Metric Configurations, expand ReskndMetric.
You can see the newly installed file in the list.
federation_config
4. You can view the content of this file by selecting this file from the list.
Best Practices for Configuration File Management
Follow certain best practices to ensure optimal performance of the Management Pack for Aggregator.
• Do not modify the out-of-the-box shipped configuration file. Create a file, copy the content of the out of the box file and
make additions to this new file.
• Do not remove objects or metrics included in the out-of-the-box configuration file as it impacts the content of the out-of-
the-box dashboards.
• Once you have created a configuration file, it is required to stop the collection on the Management Pack for
Aggregator, change the configuration file name to reflect the newly created file and start the collection again. The
Aggregator adapter will now start collecting the additional objects and metrics.
• Version control the configuration files with proper naming conventions and version numbers.
• Avoid adding objects and metrics which are not required to be collected.
• Test your newly created configuration file with a test instance of child VCF Operations instance before applying it to
your production systems.
• The collection of Aggregated metrics from the child VCF Operations monitored by the Management Pack for
Aggregator is not managed in policies. The addition and removal of metrics and properties is managed directly inside
the configuration file. Only the metrics and properties configured in the federation_config file are collected. The
collection of configured metrics and properties can be disabled and re-enabled from policy.

Management Pack for Orchestrator
The guide describes the steps to run Orchestrator workflows from VCF Operations.
The Management Pack for Orchestrator guide describes the process of deploying, configuring and managing the
Management Pack for Orchestrator in your VCF Operations environment.
Intended Audience
The information in this guide is intended for VCF Operations administrators.
Introduction to Management Pack for Orchestrator
Introduction to the Orchestrator
You can run Orchestrator workflows from VCF Operations after you install and configure the Management Pack for
Orchestrator. You can run workflows to remediate alerts in VCF Operations or automate tasks.
Management Pack for Orchestrator supports the following types of workflows:
• Custom vCenter package workflows.
• User defined vCenter workflows in Orchestrator
• Out of the box (OOTB) workflows which ship with the Management Pack for Orchestrator.
You can map these workflows as actions to alerts via recommendations. A Run Action button is displayed when VCF
Operations displays the alerts. Using the Run Action button, you can execute the workflows.
You can map the user-defined workflows from the Orchestrator after you discover them in VCF Operations. If you have
user-defined workflow packages, you can discover the package in VCF Operations and map each workflow in the
package to actions. You can also map custom vCenter workflows.
Management Pack for Orchestrator ships with 15 out of the box workflows. This does not include the python based
actions. They are automatically mapped to the alerts via recommendations.
You can create a new policy or modify an existing policy for automated workflow execution when the vSphere objects
governed by the policy receives alerts. The Reconnect Host workflow is an out of the box workflow which supports
automated execution. To automate the workflow execution, you must apply the policy to a custom group called
Orchestrator Adapter Managed Objects. This group contains the vSphere objects.
Automated workflow execution is possible on workflows which have only one input parameter. The input parameter is the
object name itself. To automate workflows which have more than one input parameter, you can add the input parameter
data inside the action script of the workflow because automated workflow execution supports only one input parameter.
Broadcom 5986

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Using the Orchestrator to Scale Up your Infrastructure
You can use the Orchestrator workflows to scale up your infrastructure and quickly act upon capacity related
alerts.
For example, your VI Admin receives an alert that a VM is low on memory. If the alert is mapped to the
Custom Reconfigure VM workflow with predefined values to increase the RAM in the VM, you can configure
the workflow to be automatically executed. When the alert is received, VCF Operations triggers the action to
reconfigure the VM and the memory is scaled up in the VM against which the alert is received.
Supported Configurations
The Management Pack for Orchestrator supports workflows that are in an external instance of Orchestrator or an instance
of Orchestrator which is embedded in an instance of VCF Automation which is connected to VCF Operations.
The Management Pack for Orchestrator supports running of workflows on vCenter instances that are connected to VCF
Operations. The instance of Orchestrator may be connected to more vCenter instances but you cannot execute workflows
on those instances unless they are connected to VCF Operations.
The VCF Operations may be connected to an external VCF Automation which has an embedded Orchestrator. You can
execute Management Pack for Orchestrator workflows from this instance of Orchestrator as well.
Note:
Since the standalone Management Pack for Orchestrator does not support the VMware Cloud on AWS
authentication, you cannot execute the Management Pack for Orchestrator workflows on VMware Cloud on AWS
vCenters using Management Pack for Orchestrator on VCF Operations.
Overview of Tasks
After you install the Management Pack for Orchestrator, you must perform the required tasks before you can run a
workflow and remediate the alert.

Orchestrator. You must configure the Management Pack for
Orchestrator to connect to a external Orchestrator or an instance
embedded in VCF Automation.

automatically converts all the custom vCenter package
workflows to alert actions.

instance to Orchestrator from VCF Operations.

vCenter user-defined packages or workflows.
Map user defined workflows to resources as actions. You can map user defined workflows to resources, or modify
custom workflows that are already mapped to resources before
you trigger them as actions.
If the user defined workflows are part of a package, you cannot
map the package directly. You can only map workflows in the
package.
Map workflows to alerts. Map the custom workflows, user defined workflows and out of
the box workflows to alerts via recommendations to see the Run
Action button in an alert.
Apply a new policy or modify an existing policy to automate Automate the execution of workflows that have predefined
execution of workflows. parameters by using a policy on the management groups that

Upgrade Management Pack
You can upgrade to a newer version of Management Pack for Orchestrator.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations user interface with admin privileges.
2. From the left menu, click Data Sources > Integrations.
3. Go to the Repository tab in the right pane, and then click Add.
4. Browse to locate the temporary folder and select the PAK file.
5. Select the Install the PAK file even if it is already installed check box.
This selection reloads the PAK file but retains the custom preferences of the user. Also, this selection does not
overwrite or update the solution alerts, symptoms, recommendations, and policies.
6. Select the Reset Default Content, overwriting to a newer version provided by this update check box.
This selection reloads the PAK file and overwrites the existing solution alerts, symptoms, recommendations, and
policies with newer versions provided with the current PAK file.
7. Click Upload.
The upload might take several minutes.
8. Read and accept the EULA, and then click Next.
9. When the upgrade is complete, click Finish.
10.On the Manage Solutions page, click Test Connection to validate the connection.
Import the Apply Host Security Configuration Rules Out of the Box (OOTB) workflow to Orchestrator.

Apply Host Security Configuration Rules workflow to Orchestrator.

Create a Service Account Refresh Token
The user can create an Service Account Refresh Token.
1. Login to VCF Automation Provider Management portal.
2. Navigate to Access Control → Service Accounts → Click on New.
3. Enter the Name.
4. Select the required roles. You can create a new role just with Orchestrator Administrator privileges or use existing
System Administrator with full access.
5. Generate the Software ID by clicking on the magic-wand icon.
6. Click NEXT. Review the information and click on Finish.
7. The Service Accounts table now reflects the newly created Service Account.
8. Edit the newly created Service account to disable / deselect the Requires Rotation Setting and save your changes
9. Expand the service account row to view the Client ID.
10.Create a curl command to perform device authorization by replacing VCFA_TENANT_MANAGER_FQDN and
SERVICE_ACCOUT_CLIENT_ID.
curl -k 'https://<VCFA_TENANT_MANAGER_FQDN>/tm/oauth/
provider/device_authorization' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-
urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'client_id=<SERVICE_ACCOUNT_CLIENT_ID>'
11.Execute the curl command and copy the value of user_code from the response.
{ "device_code":
"k81ANxCMOjaRFxeVZL0gzXwS37LhYkSF2pwhH1IzSIA", "user_code": "5MX5-206H",
"verification_uri": "https://vcfa.10.161.199.184.vcfd.example.com/provider/access-
control/service-accounts", "expires_in": 3600, "interval": 60 }
12.Under Service Accounts, Click on the Review Access Requests tab.
13.Paste the User Code copied from Step 11, and click on the LOOKUP button. Click on the GRANT button to approve
the access request.
14.Copy the value of device_code from the response in Step 13.
15.Create a curl command to generate a Refresh Token by replacing VCFA_TENANT_MANAGER_FQDN,
ORGANIZATION_SERVICE_ACCOUT_CLIENT_ID and DEVICE_CODE_FROM_DEVICE_AUTH_RESPONSE
in
curl -k 'https://<VCFA_TENANT_MANAGER_FQDN>/tm/oauth/provider/token' \ --
header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode
'client_id=<ORGANIZATION_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_CLIENT_ID>' \ --data-urlencode
'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code' \ --data-urlencode
'device_code=<DEVICE_CODE_FROM_DEVICE_AUTH_RESPONSE>'
16.Execute the curl command and copy the refresh_token from the response.
{ "access_token":
"eyJraWQiOiJ1cm46dmNsbhcMqLveEA", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600,
"refresh_token": "aJ4WNSZWmgwOZeg0M5cY9UUehjvicSRg"}
17.Use the refresh_token from Step 16 to configure adapter instance.

Package Discovery
By default, Management Pack for Orchestrator discovers custom vCenter workflows and Management Pack for
Orchestrator Out of the box (OOTB) workflows. You can extend the workflow capability of the Management Pack for
Orchestrator by installing additional packages.
Install and configure the Management Pack for Orchestrator. The Management Pack for Orchestrator must connect to
an external adapter before you install packages related to the adapter. In the Solutions page, verify that the Collection
State column and Collection Status are green under Configured Adapter Instances. The Collection Status displays
Data Receiving after the first collection cycle.
Install additional packages to support workflows related to different adapters.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations instance.
2. From the left menu, click Environment > Inventory, and then click Adapter Instances > VCF Automation
Orchestrator Adapter Instance.
3. Select a Orchestrator adapter instance.
4. Next to the name of the Orchestrator adapter instance in the right pane, click Configure Package Discovery under
Actions.
5. The Configure Package Discovery dialog box opens. Add a list of packages to be discovered in the following format:
<packageName>
6. Click Begin Action.
7. The package discovery task starts. You can view the task ID in the Configure Package Discovery dialog box. Click
OK.
8. To track the progress of the task, go to the Recent Tasks section in the Administration menu. Package discovery
starts after the first content cycle.
Mapping Workflows to Resources as Actions
You can map custom and user-defined workflows to actions. Repeat the task to add one workflow to more than one
resource. You can perform this task for multiple workflows simultaneously within a package by running the same action on
a package resource.
You must discover user-defined workflows them before you can add them as an action to a resource.
Note:
You can only map workflows to the supported target resources.
1. From the left menu, click Environment, and then click Inventory.
2. Click Adapter Instances, and then click VCF Orchestrator Adapter Instance from the list of adapter instances.
3. Select the Orchestrator adapter instance that contains the workflow that you want to run.
A list of all the workflows are displayed on the right pane.
Note:
This action is present at the Adapter instance level, package level, and workflow level. The most recommended is
the package and workflow level.
4. From the right menu, select the workflow that you want to add to a resource.
5. Click the Action icon, and then click Create/Modify Workflow Action on vCenter Resources.
Note:
Ensure that there is at least one input parameter in the workflow, otherwise the action fails when it is run.
Broadcom 5992

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Configure the following properties
Property Option
Workflow Select a workflow from the drop-down menu.
Note:
Do not modify out-of-the-box workflows.
Available on Resource Type If the workflow is already configured as an action in a resource
type, it is displayed here.
Action Target Type If the workflow is already configured as an action in the target
resource type, it is displayed here.
Resource Type Select a resource type from the drop-down menu.
Target Resource Type Select a resource type. The resource type and the target resource
type should be the same.
Operation Choose to add or remove the workflow as an action. Options are
Add and Remove.
With the Management Pack for Orchestrator 3.2, you can map any custom workflow to the parent resource. The
parent object is the Resource Type and the Target Type is the actual vCenter object that the workflow is targeted for.
The workflow accepts the target object as its input parameter. For example, if you want to map a workflow “Change
Ram” to a host system and run the same workflow on multiple virtual machines under it, then select the Resource
Type as Host System and the Target Type as Virtual Machine.
7. Click Begin Action.
A task is added to the task list.
You can verify that the action is available by clicking the Action icon after you select the resource with the required
Adapter Type and Object Type in the right pane. From the list displayed under the Action icon, verify that the workflow
that you added to the resource is available as an action in the list. You must wait one collection cycle before you can
verify. You can monitor the task list to see the status of the task.

After you install and configure the Management Pack for Orchestrator, you can map custom and user defined workflows
(actions) to alerts via recommendations. After you perform this mapping, you can execute the Orchestrator workflow to
remediate issues when VCF Operations displays alerts. Out of the box workflows are automatically mapped to alerts.
Before you map alerts to workflows, review the out of the box workflows and corresponding recommendations and alerts.
See Out of the Box Workflows in the Appendix.

2. Click Actions, and then select Go to Alert Definition.

The Edit Alert Definition dialog box opens.
4. Click the Recommendations tab.
The available recommendation is displayed.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Actions must already be configured in VCF Operations.

Configuring Automatic Remediation
A policy is a set of rules that you define for VCF Operations to use to analyze and display information about the objects
in your environment. You can modify an existing policy or create a new policy and configure it for automatic alert
remediation. To automate the workflow execution, you must apply the policy to a custom group called Orchestrator
Adapter-Managed Objects. This group contains the vSphere objects.
Ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
• You have mapped custom and user-defined workflows to resources as actions. Automated workflow execution is
possible on workflows which have only one input parameter. The only other input parameter is
vrops_alert_id
and it is used to fetch the ID of the alert that triggered the workflow. This input parameter should be of the type String.
To automate workflows which have more than one input parameter, you must create a user-defined workflow and
predefine the input parameters in the workflow.
• You have mapped the action to an alert through a recommendation.
Broadcom 5994

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. From the left menu, click Configure, and then click Policies.
2. Select the current default policy. In the More Actions tab, click Edit.
3. Select Groups and Objects tab in the Default Policy [Edit] window.
4. Click Save.
5. Select the checkbox next to VCF Orchestrator Adapter Managed Objects.
6. Select Alerts and Symptoms tab in the Default Policy [Edit] window.
7. In the Alert Definitions pane, filter by the name of the alert to which you have mapped the action that you want to
automate.
8. Select the alert from the filter results.
a) In the Automate column, select Local.
b) In the State column, select Enabled.
9. Click Save.
The default policy is modified to automatically run the configured action when mapped alerts are displayed.
Import Remediation Package to Orchestrator
After you install and configure the Management Pack for Orchestrator, VCF Operations automatically imports the
remediation package to Orchestrator after the first collection cycle. If you delete the remediation package in Orchestrator,
you see an alert in VCF Operations. You can then re-import the remediation package to Orchestrator.
Verify that you have configured the Management Pack for Orchestrator
1. Log in to the VCF Operations instance.
2. From the left menu, click Environment > Inventory, and then click Adapter Instances > VCF Orchestrator Adapter
Instance.
3. Select a Orchestrator adapter instance.
4. Next to the name of the Orchestrator adapter instance in the right pane, click Import VMware Cloud Foundation
Operations Remediation Package to vRO under Actions.
5. Choose to overwrite package if required.
6. Click Begin Action.
Log on to Orchestrator to verify if the remediation package is available.

Management Pack for Orchestrator Dashboard
Access the Management Pack for Orchestrator Dashboard
The Management Pack for Orchestrator dashboard in the VCF Operations displays information that helps you monitor
workflows.
1. From the left menu of VCF Operations, click Orchestrator Workflows Overview.
The Orchestrator Workflows Overview dashboard displays the following widgets:
• Orchestrator Adapter Instances
• Orchestrator Instance Properties
• vRO Health
• Top-10 Workflows
• Number of Successful and Failed Executions
• Packages
• Workflows
• Number of Execution

2. Click Actions > Set as Home Page, to set this dashboard as one of the default dashboards in the Quick Start page.
OrchestratorWorkflows Overview Dashboard
The Orchestrator Workflows Overview dashboard displays information about the Orchestrator adapter and workflows.
The Orchestrator Workflows Overview dashboard displays the following widgets by default.
Orchestrator Adapter Instances
You can view a list of Orchestrator adapters that you have configured in this widget. The widget displays the name of the
adapter, adapter type, object type, policy applied, collection state, and collection status. Click on an adapter instance to
view the properties of the adapter in the Orchestrator Instance Properties widget.
Orchestrator Instance Properties
Displays the properties of the Orchestrator adapter instances. You can view the adapter instance name and Orchestrator
host settings.
Broadcom 6012

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
vRO Health
Displays the status of the health-related alerts for the Orchestrator adapter instance. The state of the badge is based
on your alert definitions. Click the badge to see the Summary tab for objects or groups configured in the widget. From
the Summary tab you can begin determining what caused the current state. If the widget is configured for an object that
has descendants, you should also check the state of descendants. Child objects might have alerts that do not impact the
parent.
Top 10 Executed Workflows
Displays a count of the top 10 most frequently run workflows. This count includes workflows that have executed both
successfully and unsuccessfully.
Number of Successful and Failed Executions
Displays the number of success and failed workflow executions. You can optionally modify the workflow execution metric
collection time.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations instance.
2. Navigate to the properties file located in the path:
/usr/lib/vmware-vcops/user/plugins/inbound/
.
VMwareAriaAutomationOrchestratorAdapter3/conf /Orchestrator.properties
3. Edit the Orchestrator.properties file and set the value for the key
WORKFLOW_EXEXCUTION_METRIC_COLLECTION_INTERVAL = 720
This value affects the Number of Success and Failed Executions widget in the Orchestrator Workflows Overview
dashboard. The value you specify here decides the rate/frequency at which the workflow execution success/failure
metrics will be updated in VCF Operations. The default value is 720 minutes.
Packages
Displays a data grid with objects in the inventory. The default configuration of the data grid appears in Object List Widget
Options section. You can customize it by adding or removing default columns.
Workflows
Displays a data grid with list of Orchestrator workflows.
Number of Execution
Displays a metric chart of the workflow that you selected in the Top-10 Executed Workflows widget. You can use this
information to monitor the workload of your workflows over time
Workflow Input Parameters
Displays the input parameters which was provided for executed workflows.
Troubleshooting in Management Pack for Orchestrator
An Error Occurs When You Log In After Upgrading Orchestrator from 8.7 to 8.8
From Orchestrator 8.8 onwards, the basic authentication of your Orchestrator deployment is disabled by default.
In certain use cases you must enable this authentication by setting the
com.vmware.o11n.sso.basic-
system property.
authentication.enabled
You can enable basic authentication for your Orchestrator deployment by setting a system property.
1. Log in to the Control Center as root.
2. Select System Properties.
3. Click New.
4. Under Key, enter .
com.vmware.o11n.sso.basic-authentication.enabled
Broadcom 6013

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Under Value, enter .
true
6. (Optional) Enter a description for the new system property.
7. Click Add, and wait for the Orchestrator server to restart.

Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager
The Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager guide provides information about installing and configuring the
Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager. The Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager allows you to
retrieve alerts and findings from VMware Identity Manager to VCF Operations.
Intended Audience
The information in this guide is intended for anyone who wants to install and configure the Management Pack for VMware
Identity Manager.
Installing the Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager
The Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager consists of a PAK file that contains default dashboards for the
objects that the solution identifies.
To install the management pack, download the PAK file from VCF Solutions Catalog to a temporary folder on your local
system. For more information, see Installing and Configuring Integrations in VCF Operations.
Configure an adapter instance for the management pack.
Configuring Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager
After you install the management pack, configure an instance for Management Pack for VMware Identity Manager.
Broadcom 6019

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. In the menu, select Data Sources, and in the left pane select Integrations > Accounts.
2. On the Accounts tab, click Add.
3. On the Accounts Types page, select VMware Identity Manager Adapter.
4. Configure the adapter instance.
Option Description
Display Name The name for the adapter instance.
Description (Optional) The description of the adapter instance.
WSOne Host Enter the FQDN, or the IP address.
Credential Select the credential you want to use to sign on to the
environment from the drop-down menu. To add new credentials
to access the VMware Identity Manager environment, click the
plus sign.
• Credential Name. The name by which you are identifying
the configured credentials.
• User Name. VMware Identity Manager local admin of
system domain user name.
• Password. VMware Identity Manager local admin of system
domain password.
5. Enter Collector/Group to manage the management pack on VCF Operations. If you have only one account, select
Default collector group.
6. Enter the connection information as required to configure the instance of the management pack. Each management
pack has unique settings, configure the settings as prompted to configure that instance of the management pack. For
more information on individual management packs, see List of Management Packs.
7. Click VALIDATE CONNECTION to initiate the authentication request to the CSP authentication service.
8. Click ADD.
Verify that the adapter is configured and collecting data by viewing application-related data.

summary for apps, groups, devices, users, activity, and health for your VMware Identity Manager instance.

Management Pack for VCF Operations HCX
The Management Pack for VCF Operations HCX enables seamless monitoring and centralized management of your HCX
Manager instances directly from VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Operations.
Key Features and Benefits
• Simplified Administration: Streamlines daily administrative tasks, including certificate management, password updates,
and password policy enforcement.
• Comprehensive Data Visualization: Collects and aggregates critical metrics, change events, and resource topology
from across your fleet of HCX Manager instances, visualizing them directly within VCF Operations dashboards.
• Accelerated Troubleshooting: Empowers administrators to rapidly detect, isolate, and resolve performance bottlenecks
within HCX Interconnects and active migration workloads.
• Unified User Experience: Delivers a consistent, end-to-end monitoring interface across both your source and
destination vSphere environments.
System Requirements
Before installing and configuring the Management Pack, ensure your system meets the following requirements.
For compatibility between products, please refer to:
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations Interoperability for HCX.
VCF Operations HCX Requirements
Connection The Management Pack collects data via a REST API
Credentials vCenter username and password
Installing the Management Pack
The Management Pack for VCF Operations HCX is an add-on integration that can be installed in one of the following
ways:
• On top of the core VCF Operations platform using a PAK file available through Customer Connect. See, Installing
Integrations in a Disconnected Environment.
• Through the the VCF Operations UI. See, Installing and Configuring Management Packs in VMware Cloud Foundation
Operations from the Solutions Catalog.
Prerequisites
• Verify that you have access to the latest version of the management pack and the management pack is compatible
with your version of VCF Operations.
• Ensure that you have the privileges to install a management pack.
Configuring the Management Pack
Configure HCX Manager User and Privileges
Before registering with VCF Operations, you must create a user with the appropriate local permissions.
1. Log in to the corresponding vCenter Server and create a new user account for the deployed HCX Manager.
Broadcom 6024

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Add the user account to both the Migration Appliance Administrators and Migration Users groups in vCenter.
This designated user account is responsible for password and certificate management, as well as the collection of
migration metrics from the HCX Manager. Consequently, the assignment of both roles is mandatory.
Alternatively user privileges can be assigned by logging in to the Appliance Management UI, navigating to
Configuration > HCX Role Mapping and Edit, and adding a user name or user groups to the Migration User and
Migration Appliance Admin sections.
Register HCX Manager in VCF Operations
1. Log in to VCF Operations.
2. Navigate to Operate > Administration > Integrations and select VCF Operations HCX.
3. Click Add Account.
4. Enter the HCX Manager hostname and the appropriate user credentials created in the previous section, and click Add.
5. Select the appropriate Cloud Proxy.
6. Click Add.
After successful registration, the HCX instance should appear in the Certificates and Password screens under its specific
domain.
While the Management Pack allows the registration of various HCX Managers, only those imported or deployed via VCF
Operations are compatible with these automated password and certificate management tools.
Validating Data Collection
After you add an adapter instance, you will most likely want to validate the data that it collects in VCF Operations. Wait
until one collection cycle is complete and the Collection Status for the adapter instance on the Solutions page shows as
"Data Receiving".
1. Select the Environment navigation shortcut.
2. Under Inventory Trees, select All Objects, then expand the HCX Adapter objects list.
3. Select a resource from the list, then click the All Metrics tab to select metrics and validate values against the data
source.
Using the Management Pack
The Management Pack for VCF Operations HCX includes the following out-of-the-box features, harnessing the power of
the VCF Operations user interface:
• Resource Kinds
• Dashboards
• Reports
• Alerts
• Metrics
Resource Kinds
The Management Pack for VCF Operations HCX creates Resource Kinds and Relationships (associations) for critical
resources in your VCF Operations HCX environment.
Resource Kinds
Performance, health, and availability data are collected for the following VCF Operations HCX resource kinds:
• Site Connection
• Migration
• vMotion
• Replication Assisted vMotion
• OS Assisted Migration

Management Pack for Microsoft SQL Server
The Management Pack for Microsoft SQL Server is an embedded adapter for VMware Cloud Foundation Operations,
collecting performance data from your Microsoft SQL Server environment and providing predictive analytics and real-time
information about problems in your infrastructure—all within the VCF Operations user interface.
Notable Features
The Management Pack for Microsoft SQL Server includes the following notable features:
• Comprehensive monitoring dashboards
• 250+ collected metrics for Microsoft SQL Server resources
• 30+detailed alerts and notifications for critical and warning conditions
• Capacity definitions for connection limit, CPU demand, memory usage, and disk capacity
• External relationships from your VMware Virtual Machines to SQL Server Instance and Always On Availability
Groups
How the Management Pack Works
The Management Pack for Microsoft SQL Server connects to your Microsoft SQL Server instance via JDBC using the
jTDS driver. SQL queries are executed in order to import health, performance, availability, capacity, and relationships
data for your SQL server resources into VCF Operations.
Getting Started
Wondering where to start? See System Requirements for details.
System Requirements for Management Pack for Microsoft SQL Server
Before installing and configuring the Management Pack, ensure your system meets the following requirements.
For compatibility between products, please refer to:
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations Interoperability for Microsoft SQL Server
-OR-
Third Party Solution Interoperability for Microsoft SQL Server
Broadcom 6026

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Microsoft SQL Server Requirements
Connection Standalone Configuration:
• Hostname (or IPv4 address) of MS SQL Server instance
Clustered Configuration:
• Virtual IP (VIP), or hostname for the VIP, of MS SQL Server
instance
Default Instance Port: 1433 (TCP)
Important:
If using dynamic ports, you will want to change the default
port to SQL Server Browser Service UDP port 1434.
Credentials MS SQL User Name/Password (Active Directory or Local)
• See: Assigning MS SQL User Privileges for information
about creating the least amount of permissions for a MS SQL
monitoring user.
• If using SSL, see: Adding an SSL Certificate to the VMware
Cloud Foundation Operations Truststore.
Important:
The CPU Usage metric for Microsoft SQL Server Instances is not available on MS SQL Server Standard or
Express editions.
Assigning MS SQL User Privileges
This topic contains the minimum MS SQL user permissions needed for an MS SQL Server Management Pack monitoring
user. An automated script is provided below; it can help you create a local LPU user or can be modified for use with a
domain user.
Important:
It is recommended to create your LPU prior to installing and configuring the Management Pack. You should use
your own MS SQL credentials (login), user, and role names.
Required Permissions and Role
To create your MS SQL least-privileged user (LPU), you will need to complete the following general tasks:
1. Grant your MS SQL login credentials the following permissions:
– VIEW SERVER STATE
– VIEW DATABASE STATE
– VIEW ANY DEFINITION
2. Next, to ensure all future-created databases are monitored, create a user that maps to your MS SQL credentials and
has thepublic role on the following databases:
– eachuserdatabase
– msdb database
– model database
Create Local LPU User Script
Run the following script to automate creation of a local MS SQL Server LPU user with the permissions/role mentioned
above:
use master;
CREATE LOGIN sql_lpu WITH PASSWORD = 'your-password';
CREATE USER sql_lpu FOR LOGIN sql_lpu;
Broadcom 6027

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
GRANT CONNECT SQL to sql_lpu;
GRANT VIEW SERVER STATE to sql_lpu;
GRANT VIEW DATABASE STATE TO sql_lpu;
GRANT VIEW ANY DEFINITION TO sql_lpu;
GO
GRANT EXEC on [xp_readerrorlog] to sql_lpu
GO
use model;
CREATE USER sql_lpu FOR LOGIN sql_lpu;
GO
use msdb;
CREATE USER sql_lpu FOR LOGIN sql_lpu;
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[syssessions] TO sql_lpu
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[sysjobhistory] to sql_lpu
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[sysjobsteps] TO sql_lpu
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[sysjobs_view] TO sql_lpu
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[sysjobactivity] TO sql_lpu
ALTER ROLE [SQLAgentReaderRole] ADD MEMBER [sql_lpu]
-- For SQL Server 2008 R2, use: sp_addrolemember [SQLAgentReaderRole], [sql_lpu]
-- Goes through each user database and adds public permissions
DECLARE @name NVARCHAR(MAX)
DECLARE db_cursor CURSOR FOR
SELECT name
FROM MASTER.dbo.sysdatabases
WHERE name NOT IN ('master','model','msdb','tempdb')
OPEN db_cursor
FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @name
WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0
BEGIN
EXECUTE('USE ' + @name + '; CREATE USER sql_lpu FOR LOGIN sql_lpu;' );
FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @name
END
CLOSE db_cursor
DEALLOCATE db_cursor
