VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Configure HCX Role Mapping
Access to VCF Operations HCX requires user authentication at log in, which requires configuration of user roles and
groups.
During VCF Operations HCX configuration and activation, you must configure authentication with the local vCenter Server.
Optionally, you can configure VCF Operations HCX for VMware Cloud Foundation SSO (VCF SSO) authentication.
Regardless of the authentication method, you must assign user groups and roles.
For an overview of VCF Operations HCX user accounts and roles, see User Account and Role Requirements.
1. Log in to the Appliance Management.
2. Select the Configuration tab and navigate to HCX Role Mapping.
3. Select the authentication type and configure the roles and groups:
a) For local authentication, select the vCenter Users tab and click Edit.
Assign the HCX Roles to the vCenter groups and users that are allowed to perform VCF Operations HCX
operations. By default, the Migration Admin role is mapped to the local vSphere administrator group. The Migration
User role is intended for use by Service Providers. Groups assigned to this role cannot add or delete network
profiles.
b) For VCF SSO authentication (if configured), select the VCF SSO Users tab and click Edit.
Assign roles to the groups that are allowed to perform VCF Operations HCX operations. VCF Operations HCX
fetches the list of groups from the configured VCF SSO identify provider. For both the Migration Admin role and the
Migration User role, select a list of groups from the dropdown menu.
4. Click Save.
The assignment of the roles and user groups is now complete. Log in to HCX Manager at
https://hcx-ip-or-
to verify VCF Operations HCX log-in access. If VCF SSO is configured, follow the prompts to the identity
fqdn:443
provider's log in page and enter the VCF SSO credentials. At any time, you can use the dropdown menu on the Log in
page to select local authentication.
Access Bearer Token Authentication for API Access
As a federated SSO user in VCF Operations HCX, you access APIs by generating an API token and then exchanging the
token for an Access Bearer token.
API tokens are generated in VCF Identity Broker, and for ease of access, you can start the process of generating your API
token from the VCF Operations HCX UI.
1. In the VCF Operations HCX UI, click the User Profile icon and select Generate API Token from the dropdown menu.
2. In the VCF Identity Broker page, click Generate.
3. In VCF, exchange the token for an OAuth token, see https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vcf/vcf-9-0-
and-later/9-1/administration-sdks-cli-and-tools/about-vmware-cloud-foundation-development/oauth-token-support-for-
api-and-cli-access.html.
For more information about OAuth token support in VCF, see https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vcf/
vcf-9-0-and-later/9-1/administration-sdks-cli-and-tools/about-vmware-cloud-foundation-development/oauth-token-support-
for-api-and-cli-access.html.
Proprietary Header-Based Authentication Access to HCX APIs
You generate an Authorization token to access the HCX APIs by posting a request to the HCX API server.
Verify that you have the log-in credentials for the registered vCenter Server Single-Sign-On (SSO) user.
Verify that the user group to which the SSO user belongs is mapped to an HCX role.
1. POST a request to the authentication URL to acquire a token.
A successful request returns an "x-hm-authorization" token in the Response Headers that you must include in
subsequent API requests.
Broadcom 6592

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Request header:
a)
POST https://hcx-1.example.com/hybridity/api/sessions
b)
Content-Type: application/json
c)
Accept: application/json
3. Request body in JSON format:
a)
{ "username": "testuser@vsphere.local", "password": "testpassword"}
These credentials should be of the registered vCenter Server SSO user.
4. Response headers:
a)
x-hm-authorization 13956794:e912:4edd:bbee:fea0fa257691
5. The Authorization token is valid for 30 minutes after generation. If the token expires, you must regenerate it.
VCF Operations HCX Pairing Interoperability Policy
You must pair VCF Operations HCX on the source site with VCF Operations HCX on the destination site running the same
major version. For example, pair 9.0 with 9.1, 9.2 with 9.0, and so on.
In cases where a lower minor version is paired with a higher minor version, the functionality of the service mesh is
reduced to the common denominator between versions. For best results and feature set compatibility, run the same minor
version on both the source and the destination sites.
Migrating standalone legacy environments to VCF 9
A legacy environment is considered as an environment running standalone legacy versions of vCenter, vSphere, NSX-V,
NSX-T, or NSX. VCF Operations HCX 9 is able to migrate workloads from legacy environments to VCF 9.
For the specific versions of these legacy environments, see the Interoperability Matrix.
Support of VCF Operations HCX 9 for legacy environments that are included in the Interoperability Matrix is maintained
throughout the lifecycle of VCF 9.
There is a special pairing policy for HCX 9 to assist customers with migration operations from legacy environments to VCF
9.
You deploy and pair VCF Operations HCX 9 on the source (legacy) and destination (VCF 9) sites. After pairing is
complete and HCX 9 is licensed with a VCF 9 entitlement, entitlement inheritance enables VCF Operations HCX 9 on the
source to inherit the entitlement from the licensed VCF Operations HCX 9 on the destination that is deployed within VCF
9. You don’t need to enter a license on the source VCF Operations HCX.
Important:
VCF Operations HCX 9 is the last release that supports migrations of legacy environments.
Migrating between legacy environments using VCF Operations HCX 9
In cases where your destination site is not VCF 9, you can still use VCF Operations HCX 9 on both sites to migrate
workloads.
When you pair VCF Operations HCX 9 across non-VCF 9 sites, you must configure an Entitlement Server on VCF
Operations HCX 9 on one of the sites. An Entitlement Server is a vCenter 9 instance that is deployed and licensed
within VCF 9. Then, through entitlement inheritance, the other VCF Operations HCX 9 inherits the entitlement from the
connected VCF Operations HCX 9.
For the specific versions of environments on the source and destination site, see the Interoperability Matrix.
Important:
VCF Operations HCX 9 is the last release that supports migrations of legacy environments.
Broadcom 6593

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Entitlement Inheritance
For sites that have been activated with different entitlements, the VCF 9 license is the active entitlement on both sites.
For example, if the source site has an HCX Manager in evaluation mode and the destination site has a VCF 9 entitlement
through a VCF 9 depoyment, the VCF license is the active entitlement on both sites.
Entitlement inheritance only works for the duration of the site pairing and is independent for each pairing. Taking from our
example, if the HCX Manager in evaluation mode that inherited the VCF 9 entitlement, is also paired with another HCX
Manager in evaluation mode, this second pairing will remain in evaluation mode until either HCX Manager reaches 90
days after activation.
Migrating environments post-VCF 9
The support policy for the next major releases after VCF 9 is one of long-term support, meaning support for the current
and the LTS release of the previous major version. Under this policy, VCF Operations HCX 9 is the last release that
supports legacy environments.
For legacy environment considerations, see the Interoperability Matrix.
Creating and Managing Site Pairs
This section provides the procedures for creating and managing site pairs.
You create, configure, manage, and view site pair information from the site pairs interface in the HCX Manager.
Understanding Sites
VCF Operations HCX installations, or sites, which are used in site pairing can be vSphere-based or non-vSphere based.
Understanding vSphere-Based Paired Sites
A vSphere-based site is a vSphere installation where VCF Operations HCX has been deployed and activated. For these
sites, VCF Operations HCX supports a full range of management and mobility services when paired with other vSphere-
based sites.
For workload migration within the vCenter instance registered with HCX Manager, VCF Operations HCX provides a local
site.
Some VCF Operations HCX sites serve as the source of mobility and network extension operations while other sites serve
as the target of VCF Operations HCX operations.
For each vSphere site, you must configure a compute profile (CP) and network profile (NP). The CP and NP define the
resources that VCF Operations HCX uses to deploy the appliances for management and data plane connectivity. They
also specify the networks to use for the management and the mobility operations. The CP and NP information is used for
creating the service mesh, which is required for each site pair.
With VCF Operations HCX deployments, site pairing can be unidirectional or bidirectional:
• In unidirectional site pairing, the HCX Manager containing the virtual machine inventory and networks pairs with the
HCX Manager at the destination site. In this type of site pairing, all service mesh operations, Migration, and network
extension operations, including reverse migrations, are always initiated from the source system. In this case, an
administrator might see the message when viewing site pairing from the destination site. This
URL not available
is expected behavior because the site pairing is unidirectional.
• In bidirectional site pairing, network extension from the destination site can only be initiated if there is a service
mesh that is deployed from the destination site. The URLs for the paired sites are visible from either the source or
destination.
Understanding vSphere-Based Local Sites
A local site refers to the vCenter instance that is registered with HCX Manager. VCF Operations HCX supports the HCX-
Assisted vMotion (HAV) service for local site so you can migrate workloads within a single vCenter Server using the
associated HCX Manager. You do not need to configure any other appliances or services to perform a local site migration.
Broadcom 6594

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The HCX-Assisted vMotion (HAV) service is the only service that is enabled for the compute profile and service mesh. The
local site must be selected as both the source and destination site to run HAV migrations.
VCF Operations HCX supports migrations within local sites when vCenter and NSX are registered with HCX Manager.
If the version of the vCenter Server that is registered with HCX Manager is less than 9.0, an entitlement server must be
added to HCX to run HAV migrations for the local site. For information about the VCF Operations HCX pairing policy, see
VCF Operations HCX Pairing Interoperability Policy.
To view local site pair details, navigate to Infrastructure > Site Pairs, and select the Local Site tab.
A single local site pair, with a compute profile, and service mesh are set up by default.
Understanding non-vSphere based sites
Non-vSphere based sites do not run vSphere and VCF Operations HCX is not installed in those environments. Examples
of non-vSphere based sites include sites running on non-vSphere hypervisors like KVM and Hyper-V. A typical scenario
for pairing non-vSphere based sites is when you migrate Guest OS workloads to VMware vSphere-based environments
using OS Assisted Migration (OSAM).
For non-vSphere based sites, the process of adding a site pair generates a "pseudo site" that appears in the site pairs
interface along with any vSphere-based sites. A non-vSphere site has no installed VCF Operations HCX from which
to gather management information, so the site pairs interface provides only limited information about the pseudo-site,
including the site name and type.
Unlike vSphere-based sites, non-vSphere sites require no compute profile or network profile configuration, and site
management operations are not applicable to non-vSphere based sites. Non-vSphere sites are immediately ready for site
pairing.
Important:
The compute profile configuration for any vSphere-based site that is paired with a non-vSphere site must include
OSAM. The service mesh configuration selected for pairing a vSphere-based site with a non-vSphere site must
include the Guest Network. This network is used for migration of the non-vSphere workloads.
Add a Site Pair
A Site Pair establishes the connection that is needed for management, authentication, and orchestration of VCF
Operations HCX services across a source (vSphere or non-vSphere) and destination environment.
• For vSphere sites, VCF Operations HCX is deployed and activated in the source and destination environments.
• Site URL and user roles:
– When the destination is a vSphere-based private cloud, the Site URL refers to the HCX Manager at the target site:
https://hcx-ip-or-fqdn
Provide a user from the destination/target site's local SSO or VCF SSO configuration. The user must be included in
the VCF Operations HCX Role-Mapping Group configuration.
The user is included by default.
administrator@vsphere.local
– When the destination system is a hosted environment, the Site URL can use a trusted domain name pre-created by
the provider or an IP address.
Use the credentials for a user that holds a cloud admin role in your private cloud.
• For vSphere-based site pairs, the destination site URL must use a CA signed trusted certificate or be manually trusted
on the source system. See Managing CA and Self-Signed Certificates.
For vSphere-based sites, site pairing is between a source VCF Operations HCX and destination VCF Operations HCX.
For non-vSphere sites, pairing is between a non-vSphere site and a VCF Operations HCX installation.
Broadcom 6595

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. From the VCF Operations HCX dashboard, navigate to Infrastructure > Sites.
2. Select the Paired Sites tab, and click New Site Pair.
3. Select the Site Type for the remote site:
a) For vSphere-based site pairing, select VMware.
b) For non-vSphere site pairing, select Other.
4. Select the authentication type.
For local authentication with the vCenter Server, select vCenter.
For authentication with the VMware identity Provider as configured for VMware Cloud Foundation, select VCF SSO.
5. Enter the paired site information:
a) For sites with vCenter authentication, enter the remote VCF Operations HCX site URL, username, and password,
and credentials.
For sites with VCF SSO authentication, enter the remote VCF Operations HCX URL, client ID, and client secret set
up when configuring VCF SSO. This should be a different OAuth application to the one configured on the remote
HCX Manager.
b) For non-vSphere site pairing, enter a pseudo-site name and an optional description.
6. Click Create.
7. (Optional) To achieve bidirectional site pairing in vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX installations, repeat this
procedure at both sites.
If all validations succeed, the system displays the remote site with the status "Connected". With bidirectional site pairing,
both sites show up in the list.
When pairing vSphere-to-vSphere sites, the display indicates that the sites are connected with an arrow indicating the
direction of mobility operations is to the destination site. The display includes the destination site URL, location, vCenter,
and NSX server information.
When pairing vSphere with non-vSphere sites, the pseudo-site indicates that the sites are connected with an arrow
indicating the direction of mobility operations is from the non-vSphere site. Because VCF Operations HCX is not deployed
at the non-vSphere site, no other information about the site is available for display.
Broadcom 6596

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Create a network profile and compute profile for each vSphere-based site and then apply a service mesh to the site pair.
See Configuring and Managing the Interconnect.
Delete a Site Pair
To disconnect paired sites, you must delete the site pair.
• Verify that all mobility operations are complete.
• Unextend networks between sites.
• Delete all service meshes associated with the site pair.
Removing a site pair does not affect individual site configurations. The source and the destination sites comprising the site
pair retain compute profile (CP) and network profile (NP) settings.
1. In VCF Operations HCX, click Site Pairs.
2. Select a paired site, and click Delete Site Pair.
3. Click Delete.
Edit a Site Pair
VCF Operations HCX provides an option for editing the credentials of a paired site, including changing the authentication
type.
Editing the site pair credentials has no effect on mobility or network extension operations.
Note:
You cannot edit pseudo sites that are associated with non-vSphere site pairs.
1. In the HCX console, click Sites.
2. Select a paired site, and click Edit Site Pair.
3. (Optional) Change the authentication type: vCenter User or VCF SSO.
The current authentication type is selected by default.
4. Enter the new credentials for destination VCF Operations HCX .
For sites with vCenter authentication, enter the username and password.
For sites with VCF SSO authentication, enter the client ID and client secret setup when configuring VCF SSO. This
should be a different OAuth application than is configured on the remote HCX Manager.
5. Click Edit.
VCF Operations HCX displays a message indicating the update is in progress.
Viewing Site Pair Information
Information regarding site pairs appears in the VCF Operations HCX Dashboard, site pairs interface, and Interconnect
interface.
Broadcom 6597

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
View Site Pair Information in the Dashboard
When you launch VCF Operations HCX, the Dashboard is the default display that opens in the VCF Operations HCX
console. The Dashboard provides at-a-glance visibility into VCF Operations HCX operations, including a summary listing
of paired sites. For more information, Understanding the VCF Operations HCX Dashboard.
View Summary Information for a Site Pair
The site pairs interface displays summary information for HCX Manager indicating the total number of paired sites, the
number of vSphere-based paired sites, non-vSphere paired sites, and associated service meshes. To access the site
pairs interface, navigate to Infrastructure > Site Pairs.
The site pairs interface provides a separate card for each paired site. Each card lists general information about each site
including the Site URL, physical location, registered vCenter version, registered NSX version, Authentication Type, and
number of service meshes established for the Site Pair.
Note:
Because a non-vSphere site has no installed HCX manager from which to gather information, the site pairs
interface provides only limited information about the pseudo-site, including the site name and type.
A directional arrow on each site card indicates the direction of mobility operations relative to the VCF Operations HCX .
Each card includes the connection status between sites: Connected or Disconnected.
Broadcom 6598

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
View the Service Mesh Topology for a Site Pair
For a topology view of the service mesh configuration and connections that are associated with a Site Pair, navigate to
Infrastructure > Interconnect and expand the service mesh selection to display the Topology tab.
Configuring and Managing the Interconnect
The VCF Operations HCX Interconnect provides a secure pipeline for migration and extension between two connected
VCF Operations HCX sites.
Broadcom 6599

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Overview of the Interconnect Services Deployment
VCF Operations HCX services are deployed and managed using the service mesh.
The HCX Interconnect appliance creates and secures connections between paired sites, and deploys the appliances
supporting management, mobility, and network extension operations. All of these connections and appliances are
established and deployed between paired sites using the service mesh.
Configuring the Service Mesh
The service mesh is used to create a secure optimized transport fabric between two paired sites.
The procedures for creating a service mesh vary based on whether the site pairing is between two vSphere-based VCF
Operations HCX installations, or between a vSphere-based site and a non-vSphere site. See About the Service Mesh.
About the Service Mesh
When VCF Operations HCX Migration and network extension services are enabled, HCX Manager deploys the associated
virtual appliances in the source site and corresponding "peer" virtual appliances on the destination site. The service mesh
activates the configuration, deployment, and serviceability of these Interconnect virtual appliance pairs.
Service Mesh Components
The service mesh logic determines the transport fabric and defines what services are associated with a site-pair based on
a number of component factors:
Network Profile Defines what networks are used for connecting virtual appliances and for VCF Operations HCX
management and data plane operations.
Compute Profile Provisions the infrastructure at the source and the destination site. Defines the placement details (Resource
Pool, Datastore) where the system places the virtual appliances.
Note:
The integrated compute profile creation wizard can be used to create the network profiles (or
network profiles can be pre-created).
The service mesh, compute profile, and network profile information is accessible by selecting Interconnect in the HCX
Manager UI.
Broadcom 6600

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Broadcom 6601

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To show additional service mesh selections click the right navigation arrow to expand the display.
You can also click More and select an option from the dropdown menu. The available options depend on your setup.

display for additional details.
Appliances Lists details about the source and destination appliances that are deployed for each service mesh. For
information regarding the management options available after selecting this tab, see Manage Service Mesh
Appliances.
View Tasks Provides a detailed list of tasks associated with service mesh operations.
Run Diagnostics Run data plane diagnostics to troubleshoot issues in your service mesh. See, Understanding Data Plane
Diagnostics.
Migrate Service Mesh Migrate the service mesh to access enhanced services such as support for WAN Optimization and
improved performance for the network extension service. Selecting this option opens the migration wizard
which runs a series of checks, creates a new, enhanced service mesh, migrates the existing network
extensions, and removes the existing service mesh. Migrating the service mesh is possible when HCX
Manager in both the local and remote location is updated to the latest version of VCF Operations HCX.
This option is also accessed by clicking the light bulb icon located on the right side of the pane containing
service meshes that can be migrated.
HA Management Displays information and appliances related to network extension High Availability groups. See,
Understanding Network Extension High Availability.
Sentinel Management Provides options for downloading and managing the Sentinel Agent software, which must be installed
on guest workloads migrated using OS Assisted Migration. This option appears when the OS Assisted
Migration service is selected in the service mesh configuration. See, Sentinel Management.
Creating a Service Mesh
The process for creating a service mesh varies depending on whether the site pairing is with vSphere-based sites or with
non-vSphere sites.
For vSphere-based site pairs, the service mesh is always applied at the source site. Follow these general steps for
creating a service mesh for paired vSphere-based sites:
1. Pair VCF Operations HCX sites. See Creating and Managing Site Pairs.
2. Create a network profile for the source and destination sites. See Create a Network Profile.
3. Create a compute profile for the source and destination sites. See Create a Compute Profile.
4. Create the service mesh for the Site Pair. See Create a Service Mesh for vSphere-Based Site Pairs.
HCX Interconnect service appliances are only deployed when a service mesh is created.
Note:
Installing VCF Operations HCX requires registration with vCenter (source and destination sites) and VMware
NSX Manager (mandatory for the destination site). After VCF Operations HCX installation, configuring the service
mesh deploys the HCX data plane appliances necessary to run VCF Operations HCX services: HCX migration
(HCX-IX) and HCX network extension (HCX-NET-EXT) services.
For non-vSphere site pairs, apply the service mesh at the vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX site for the site pair.
Follow these general steps for creating a service mesh for non-vSphere site pairs:
1. Pair the non-vSphere site. See Creating and Managing Site Pairs.
2. Create a network profile for the vSphere-based site. See Create a Network Profile.
3. Create a compute profile for the vSphere-based site. See Create a Compute Profile.
4. Create the service mesh for the Site Pair. See Create a Service Mesh for Non-vSphere Site Pairs.
Create a Network Profile
The network profile is an abstraction of a distributed port group, standard port group, or NSX Logical Segment, and the
Layer 3 properties of that network. A network profile is a sub-component of a complete compute profile.
Broadcom 6602

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VCF Operations HCX is deployed and configured for each site.
• Use the planned network configurations prepared using the checklist that is described in the Getting Started with VCF
Operations HCX guide.
Create a network profile for each network you intend to use with the VCF Operations HCX services. You select these
network profiles when creating a compute profile.
For information about how VCF Operations HCX interaction with NSX federation might affect your network profile, see
Support for NSX Federation
Note:
Although a network profile can be assigned any of the functions during the compute profile configuration, consider
creating a separate profile for each function as a best practice.
Network Description
Management VCF Operations HCX data plane appliances use this network
to communicate with management systems like HCX Manager,
vCenter, ESX Management, NSX Manager, DNS, and NTP.
Uplink (External) VCF Operations HCX interconnect (HCX-IX) appliances use this
network for WAN communication between source and destination
sites.
vMotion VCF Operations HCX interconnect (HCX-IX) appliances use this
network for the traffic exclusive to vMotion protocol operations.
Note:
Configuring this network does not include the vMotion
NFC traffic. HCX always uses its Management interface
for vMotion NFC traffic.
vSphere Replication (Bulk Migration Service) VCF Operations HCX interconnect (HCX-IX) appliances use this
network for the traffic exclusive to vSphere Replication.
Note:
In deployments where ESX use a dedicated VMkernel
configuration for vSphere Replication services, the
HCX Interconnect appliance uses a network profile
configuration dedicated to the vSphere Replication
traffic. This configuration does not include the vSphere
Replication NFC traffic. VCF Operations HCX always
uses its Management interface for vSphere Replication
NFC traffic.
Sentinel Guest Network (for OS Assisted Migration) The Sentinel Gateway appliances use this vSphere network to
connect with non-vSphere virtual machines.
Important:
When creating a separate network profile for vMotion or vSphere Replication services, although the option is
available to configure a GW as a standard network profile, traffic for those services use only the default GW in
the Management network profile to attempt to access resources in a different subnet. If ESX resources are not
L2 adjacent to the IX appliance on those networks, there is a requirement to configure “Static Routes” as part of
the Advanced Configurations option in the compute profile to ensure traffic is directed to the default GW on those
networks.

Create a Compute Profile
A compute profile contains the compute, storage, and network settings that VCF Operations HCX uses on this site to
deploy the Interconnect-dedicated virtual appliances when creating a service mesh.

• To obtain the optimum system usage, assign resource configurations based on VCF Operations HCX deployment
considerations.
• Use the planned configurations collected using Preparing for General Installation.
• To deploy WAN-OPT, make sure that you are using enhanced service meshes. Enhanced service meshes are created
when VCF Operations HCX and the HCX Manager on both the local and remote site is at version 9.1.0 and later.
• To deploy the HCX NET-EXT appliance in NSX-enabled environments, the NSX Transport Zone must be associated
to all hosts that are part of the deployment cluster. Perform this action in addition to the NSX Overlay or NSX VLAN
network extension configuration part of the Network Containers section.
VMware Operations HCX provides a default compute profile which includes only the HAV service and has all data centers
grouped into a single service boundary. This compute profile, together with a default service mesh is provided to support
local site migration. For more information, see Understanding Sites.
Create a compute profile in both the source and the destination VCF Operations HCX environments using the planned

Create a Service Mesh for vSphere-Based Site Pairs
A service mesh provides the services configuration for a Site Pair. This section describes the procedure for creating a
service mesh for a vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX site pair.
Creating a service mesh requires:
• A connected site pair.
• A valid compute profile at the source and destination site.
• Virtual Switches (for network extension) and network profiles selected in each compute profile must span across all
hosts in every selected deployment cluster. If these objects do not span all hosts, it is possible that the appliances will
Broadcom 6610

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
be deployed in a host missing the needed networks. In this case, the service mesh deployment can fail or services
may not function properly.
Note:
To create a service mesh between a vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX site and a non-vSphere site, see
Create a Service Mesh for Non-vSphere Site Pairs.
VMware Operations HCX provides a default service mesh which includes only the HAV service and has all data centers
grouped into a single service boundary. This service mesh, together with a default compute profile is provided to support
local site migration. For more information, see Understanding Sites.
Adding a service mesh initiates the deployment of HCX Interconnect virtual appliances on both of the sites. A service
mesh is always created on the source site.
Note:
VCF Operations HCX sites require registration with NSX Local Manager at installation time. Selecting a compute
profile for the service mesh requires that network profiles used in compute profile configuration use local
segments. This affects both the network profile and the compute profile, which in turn disrupts service mesh
operations except for service mesh deletion.
You cannot configure the network extension service in the service mesh if one of the VCF Operations HCX sites is
federated.
1. Log in to VCF Operations HCX using an account with Administrator privileges.
2. Navigate to Interconnect > Service Mesh.
3. Click Create Service Mesh.
4. Select a site pair:
a) From the drop-down menu, select a site. The paired site is automatically populated.
b) Click Continue.
5. Select compute profiles:
a) Select a compute profile from the Select Source Compute Profile drop-down menu.
b) Select a compute profile from the Select Remote Compute Profile drop-down menu.
c) Click Continue.
6. Select the services to be activated, and click Continue.
Service meshes created in VCF Operations HCX 9.1 and later display enhanced services.
Broadcom 6611

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Broadcom 6612

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Broadcom 6613

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The WAN Optimization service is only available for enhanced appliances.
The VCF Operations HCX services available for activation are based on your selections in the source and remote site
compute profiles, and based on the service entitlements for each site. In cases where the source and remote sites
have been activated with different entitlements, the service mesh can inherit entitlements from either site. For more
information, see Understanding Service Inheritance.
7. (Optional) Override the default Uplink network profile:
By default, the HCX interconnect appliance uses Uplink network profiles defined in the compute profile for the source
and the destination sites. You can override the default.
a) Select one or more networks from the Select Source Site Uplink Network Profile drop-down menu, and click
Close.
If the service mesh in running in standard mode, it can use up to three Uplinks, adding network path failover and
improving overall resiliency for VCF Operations HCX services. Multiple Uplinks are not aggregated for increased
throughput capacity. The following specific behaviors apply:
• VCF Operations HCX attempts to load balance traffic on the network extension (HCX-NET-EXT) appliance
based on characteristics of the flow and the performance of the uplinks.
• VCF Operations HCX does not load balance migration traffic on the Interconnect (HCX-IX) appliance. Additional
uplinks might or might not be used.
Enhanced service meshes are limited to a single uplink network.
b) Click Select Destination Site Uplink Network Profile, and repeat the selections.
c) Click Continue.
8. (Optional) Modify the uplink path MTU value for the source and destination site, and click Continue.
This sets the MTU value for the Uplink networks. After creating the service mesh, you can test the MTU for the Uplink
networks using Transport Analytics. See Verifying Underlay Network Performance for service mesh Uplinks.
9. Configure the network extension appliances that are deployed per switch or Transport Zone.
VCF Operations HCX creates one network extension appliance minimum for each network container that is configured
in the source compute profile. For example, if the compute profile specifies an NSX Overlay Transport Zone or VLAN
Transport zone as the source containers for network extension, the service mesh will create one network extension
appliance for the Overlay Transport Zone and another for the VLAN Transport Zone.
You can use the advanced configuration settings to deploy additional appliances to distribute or dedicate L2 forwarding
load or when configuring network extension High Availability.
a) In Advanced Configuration - Network Extension Appliance Scale Out, review the default Extension appliances
per network container.
b) For each entry, set the number of network extension appliances that VCF Operations HCX deploys when it
activates the service mesh configuration.
Extended network service can be carried by a single (standalone) network extension appliance at each site, or an
HA group that consists of two network extension appliances at each site. For example, to create a service mesh
that has two non-redundant network extensions and one high-availability network extension, you must set the
number of network extension appliances deployed by the service mesh to 2.
The default setting is 1. This setting restricts the service mesh to deploying one network extension appliance.
Note:
You must configure the network extension Appliance limit in the compute profile at both the source and remote
sites to equal or exceed the number of scale-out appliances set in the service mesh.
For the system resource considerations, see System Requirements.
Broadcom 6614

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
c) In the network extension mode for appliances column, specify whether you want a single extension per vNIC or
multiple extensions per vNIC. Single extension uses a separate port for each network extension. This depends on
your infrastructure and networks, you might want a multiple mode but your infrastructure might not support this.
The option to specify multiple extensions per vNIC is only available if your service mesh has been upgraded to
enhanced mode.
The option to specify a single extension per vNIC is not available when both source and destination transport
zones are Overlay transport zones.
d) In the Configure DHCP profile for network extension column, select Configure to automatically configure your
environment so that DHCP traffic will flow back and forth when you have completed service mesh setup.
Configuring DHCP is not applicable when both source and destination switches are DVS.
e) Click Continue.
10.(Optional) Configure Traffic Engineering features:
Enhanced:
Non-enhanced:
Broadcom 6615

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
a) To create multiple transport tunnels for directing the traffic to a destination site, check Application Path
Resiliency.
Enabling Application Path Resiliency (APR) creates up to eight transport tunnels between each Interconnect and
network extension appliance uplink interface IP address pair between sites. If a few tunnels fail, there is no impact
to the data traffic as one transport tunnel out of eight is always used to provide secure data transfer across the
Wide Area Network (WAN) or Internet connection.
Application Path Resiliency forwards traffic over one tunnel at a time and does not load balance across multiple
paths.
Note:
To view the available tunnels after completing the service mesh configuration, navigate to Interconnect > Service
Mesh > View Appliances and expand the HCX-WAN-IX appliance.
Important:
For additional dynamic tunnel requirement, the source Interconnect (IX) and network extension appliances use a
random source UDP port in the 4500 – 4628 range and target UDP port as 4500 to create a different flow for each
subsequent tunnel. The reverse tunnel originated by target IX/NE appliances have source port as UDP 4500 and
destination ports from same random ports used by source appliances for the forward direction in the range 4500 –
4628.
Ensure the firewall settings on either side allow for that connectivity.
b) To dynamically manage the TCP segment size and optimize the transport performance for the HCX network
extension service traffic, check the TCP MSS Clamping checkbox.
By default, this option is enabled for enhanced service meshes and disabled for standard service meshes, and is
available only after activating the HCX network extension service.
Broadcom 6616

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
c) Select the Generic Receive Offload checkbox to reassemble network extension input packets into larger ones
before delivery to the workloads.
This option is not available for service meshes upgraded to enhanced mode.
d) To activate transport encryption for network extension data between site pairs, select theEncryption for Network
Extension Services checkbox.
Transport encryption to protect network extension data is activated by default. You can deactivate transport
encryption only on Uplink networks that have been verified as secure in the network profile configuration.
e) To activate transport encryption migration traffic between site pairs, select the Encryption for Migration Services
checkbox.
Transport encryption to protect migration traffic is activated by default. You can deactivate transport encryption only
on Uplink networks that have been verified as secure in the network profile configuration.

A service mesh provides the services configuration for a Site Pair. This section describes the procedure for creating a
service mesh between a vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX site and a non-vSphere site.
Creating a service mesh requires:
• A connected Site Pair.
• A compute profile for the vSphere-based site. The compute profile service selections must include OS Assisted
Migration.
Note:
To create a service mesh between two vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX sites, see Create a Service Mesh for
vSphere-Based Site Pairs.
Adding a service mesh initiates the deployment of HCX Sentinel Resource Gateway (SRG) appliance on the vSphere-
based site.

4. From the drop-down menu, select a non-vSphere site.
5. Click Continue.

Managing the Service Mesh
After creating a service mesh, you can perform operations on the service mesh and on the HCX appliances deployed by
the service mesh.
Update and Synchronize the Service Mesh
The service mesh is the effective service configuration between a source and a destination site. It must be kept updated
between the pair following changes in the compute profile, network profile, or service mesh itself.
An update to the compute profile, network profile, or service mesh can have an impact on the system configuration,
including possible downtime. The VCF Operations HCX UI provides two operations for addressing service mesh changes:
Edit and Resync. The Edit operation edits the service mesh. The Resync operation takes changes to the compute profile
and network profile, and applies them to the service mesh.
Broadcom 6618

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If the service mesh configuration includes network extension High Availability (HA) groups, a Resync or Edit operation
reconfigures or redeploys all network extension appliances in the HA group.
To change the service mesh setup, navigate to Interconnect > Service Mesh > Edit, and click Edit . Click Update
Service Mesh to save your changes.
To resync, navigate to Interconnect > Service Mesh > Resync and click Resync.
When the source is a vSphere environment, editing and synchronizing the service mesh is available from the source
site VCF Operations HCX UI where the service mesh was created. These update operations are not available at the
destination site.
When the source is a non-vSphere environment, operations must be done from the destination site HCX manager UI.
Note:
For information about upgrading the service mesh appliances, see Upgrade the HCX Service Mesh Appliances.
Renaming Service Mesh Appliances
You can update the service mesh appliance names in the VCF Operations HCX .
The service mesh, which can comprise the HCX-WAN-IX, HCX-NET-EXT, and OSAM appliances, provides the
interconnect services between paired source and destination sites. You can change the appliance names in your
environment.
Note:
Do not use the same name for appliances in a site pair.
1. Log in to VCF Operations HCX with an account with Administrator privileges.
2. Navigate to Interconnnect > Service Mesh.
3. Click View Appliances.
4. Select an appliance from the list, and click the Rename Appliance tab.
5. Enter the new appliance name, and click Rename.
VCF Operations HCX initiates the name change operation and syncs the changes with the peer site. To monitor the
status of the rename operation, click the Task tab.
Repeat the procedure for any further name changes.
Manage Service Mesh Appliances
Through the Interconnect interface at the local or remote HCX site, you can perform various operations related to
managing the appliances deployed with each service mesh
HCX uses a service called the HCX Mobility Agent, which plays an integral role in the Interconnect (IX) appliance
functionality. This agent facilitates workload migrations in vCenter. As a result, it cannot be patched, serviced or upgraded
using standard ESX tools or images.
The HCX Mobility Agent is displayed in the vCenter inventory as if it were an ESX host, but it is not. The ESX version of
the Mobility Agent displayed in the vCenter inventory matches the version of the ESX host in terms of version/family, for
example 8.x, but the build number shown does not represent a real ESX build number.
Any CVE/VMSA released by Broadcom for ESX is not applicable to these devices. Remediation must be done by
HCX Manager. Any settings, such as vSwitch, Port group or datastore objects related to the ESX host seen in vCenter
Inventory are not genuine configuration and have no practical impact on the underlying infrastructure.
VCF Operations HCX provides the following operations for managing service appliances:
Redeploy Redeploys a specifc appliance at both the source and destination sites. For example, you may need to
redeploy as part of a troubleshooting step.
Note:
VCF Operations HCX automatically redeploys the appliances for a service mesh during an
upgrade procedure. For more information about upgrading appliances, see About Upgrades.
Based on the type of appliance, VCF Operations HCX provides several reployment options.
Broadcom 6619

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Standard: Redeploys Interconnect (HCX-WAN-IX) or network extension (HCX-NET-EXT) appliances
using the same IP address. With this option, VCF Operations HCX disconnects the current appliances
and re-establishes the service tunnels, which can take up to a minute or more.
• In-Service: Available only for HCX-NET-EXT appliances. In-Service upgrades allow for minimally
disruptive redeployment of the appliances as compared to the Standard option by deploying a new
appliance using a separate IP address. For detailed information about this option, see In-Service
Upgrade for Network Extension Appliances.
• High-Availability: Available only for HCX-NET-EXT appliances configured for High Availability (HA).
Redeployment of appliances using the High-Availability option takes advantage of the HA group failover
process to complete the redeploy operation. In this case, the Standby pair is upgraded first. After the
Standby upgrade finishes, a switchover occurs and the Standby pair takes on the Active role. At that
point, the previously Active pair is upgraded and takes on the Standby role. For more information about
network extension HA, see Understanding Network Extension High Availability.
• Force: Forces the reployment operation to proceed if conflicting operations are encountered. If the
HCX-IX appliance is in use - for example, serving migrations - then the appliance redeployment occurs
only if the Force option is applied.
Select this option in conjunction with other selections.
Force-Sync Syncs the appliance configuration in cases where the appliance is not in the expected configured state.
Change Password Updates the password for the deployed appliance.
Rename Appliance Renames the deployed appliance.
Activate High Applies only when selecting network extension appliances.
Availability
Migrate Network Migrate network extensions. Applies to VCF Operations HCX version 9.1 and later.

1. Log in to VCF Operations HCX with an account with Administrator privileges.
2. Click Sites.
3. Identify a service mesh, and click View Appliances.
4. Select the checkbox next to an appliance to view the available management actions.
5. Select an action and respond to any prompts to update the appliance.
Monitor Service Mesh Operations
This section describes how to monitor the status of service mesh-related operations.
1. After initiating a service mesh action, click More and select View Tasks from the dropdown menu.
VCF Operations HCX displays a list of operations that are associated with the service mesh. The most current
operations are listed first. The display includes the operation name, progress, start and stop time, and task description.
2. Expand each entry to view additional tasks associated with the operation.
Understanding Data Plane Diagnostics
VCF Operations HCX provides diagnostic tools that can help you troubleshoot data plane connectivity issues between site
pairs.
Broadcom 6620

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
During the site pairing process, VCF Operations HCX deploys a set of data plane appliances at both the source and
destination sites to support migration and network extension services, including:
• Bulk Migration
• Replication Assisted vMotion Migration
• Cross-cloud vMotion Migration
• OS Assisted Migration
• Network Extension
To perform these services, VCF Operations HCX establishes connections between the appliances using the networks that
are defined in the service mesh, including the Management and External networks.
If VCF Operations HCX detects a connection issue with any of the services deployed for the site pair, a message appears
indicating that the tunnel or connection status is down or degraded. Run data plane diagnostics to troubleshoot.
Note:
For a service mesh with only HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct), data plane diagnostics is unavailable.
Run Data Plane Diagnostics
You can run data plane diagnostics for a service mesh site pair to help troubleshoot data plane connectivity issues or to
better understand connections between services for a site pair. Running diagnostics can take several minutes. While the
diagnostics tests are in progress, all service mesh operations are blocked.
Note:
As a best practice, do not run Transport Analytics while running data plane diagnostics. Running these tests
simultaneously can skew test results.
1. In the VCF Operations HCX Console, next to the site pairing for which you want to run data plane diagnostics, select
Run Diagnostics from the More dropdown menu.
2. Review the report results. See, Viewing the Data Plane Diagnostics Report.
Viewing the Data Plane Diagnostics Report
After running the data plane diagnostics, VCF Operations HCX prepares a report covering the connections from each site
service mesh.
The Data Plane Diagnostics page displays information about the tested service mesh, and the probes that were run on
each site in the service mesh as part of the test.
Select a site to see the probe results for each site.
Viewing Test Results
The test results are grouped by the site. For example, if a service mesh has five network extension appliances, the
test checks the connectivity for the group of those appliances using the management network and the group of those
appliances using the external connectivity (Uplink) network.
You can expand the probe results to see additional details depending on the probe type. For any failed probes, expand
the appliance entry for more information.

Understanding HCX Transport Analytics
You can test and review the underlay network performance as seen by VCF Operations HCX appliances for each uplink
network using HCX Transport Analytics.
Transport Analytics help to characterize the health and performance of the underlay network. Run bandwidth tests on
each uplink network in each service mesh configuration to determine whether the underlay network supporting that
uplink meets the minimum requirements for HCX services. Understanding the underlay network performance can help in
planning migration wave size and in analyzing data transfer and performance issues.
Note:
HCX Transport Analytics test the end-to-end underlay network supporting each uplink, and not the uplink network
itself. The test checks the underlay network between the source and the destination site. Throughout this section,
underlay network results are organized and reported against each uplink network in the service mesh.
To support seamless system operation between sites, network extension and migration operations have minimum
requirements for underlay network bandwidth, latency, and loss. These services all use underlay networks for transporting
data from the source site to the destination site. If the underlay network does not meet the minimum requirements, it can
result in degraded service performance or failure. For a complete description of network underlays and the minimum
requirements for HCX services, see, Network Underlay Minimum Requirements.
Note:
For service meshes upgraded to enhanced mode, measurements are made with the VCF Operations HCX
encapsulations, therefore you might see a difference in the reported numbers. The insights that we provide
regarding minimum requirements are adjusted accordingly.
Verifying Underlay Network Performance for service mesh Uplinks
HCX transport analytics help with monitoring the connectivity health between sites for a service mesh and with
characterizing the underlay network requirements for HCX services.
• If you have changed the Uplink Networks in the compute profile, navigate to Interconnect > Service Mesh, and click
Resync to apply those changes to the Service Mesh.
The Transport Analytics page lists all service mesh configurations for a site pair with a separate card for each service
mesh. Each service mesh card has the same information:
• Connected Sites
• Performance Insights
• Services Overview
• Uplinks Overview
You can use the search option at the top right of the page to find a specific service mesh.
1. In HCX Manager, navigate to Transport Analytics.
The transport analytics page displays the service mesh inventory.
Broadcom 6623

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. For each service mesh, click Test Service Mesh Uplinks.
Note:
It is a best practice to test the service mesh uplinks independent of other tests. Running tests like CCLI perftest in
parallel can skew test results.
3. Review each section of the service mesh card for health details:
Connected Sites Identifies the source and the destination sites for the site pair.
Performance Insights Based on the bandwidth reported by the uplink test and the bandwidth requirement of the HCX service,
(Currently available for HCX calculates the underlay network performance associated with the uplink. From that calculation,
Bulk Migration only) HCX recommends a number of simultaneous migrations that the underlay network can support at the
point when the test was run.
Services Overview Lists the HCX services enabled in the service mesh. Expand each service entry to view the transport
thresholds: Minimum Bandwidth, Maximum Latency, and Maximum Loss. The transport thresholds
reflect the underlay network requirements for each service.
The health of a service relative to the underlay network is indicated by either a checkmark or an
exclamation mark. A checkmark indicates that the underlay network performance meets the minimum
requirements for the service, and the Uplink Network is in a healthy state for the specified HCX service.
An exclamation mark indicates that the Uplink Network is in a degraded state relative to the underlay
network performance, and that Uplink is not recommended to use with the specified HCX service.
Uplinks Overview Provides the transport analysis and the transport monitoring of the underlay network for each Uplink
Network in the service mesh.
Broadcom 6624

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Transport Analysis lists the tested transport thresholds of the underlay network. Expand each Uplink
Network entry to view Available Bandwidth, Latency, and Loss metrics. Select Re-run Test to start a
new test for the selected Uplink Network.
The health of a service relative to the underlay network is indicated by either a checkmark or an
exclamation mark. A checkmark indicates that the service thresholds are met for all the services
configured in the service mesh. An exclamation mark is shown if any one of the service thresholds
are not met for the services configured in the service mesh.
If a new network uplink is added to the service mesh, you must run an initial test on that Uplink to
generate the transport thresholds. Following the initial test, re-run the test to evaluate the current
state of the underlay network.
Note:
Available bandwidth is what is currently available at the time of the test. Transport threshold
metrics are static and are based on the most recent test. To update the metrics for an Uplink
Network, you must re-run the test.
When an Uplink Network is used in multiple service mesh configurations, each service mesh
using that Uplink is updated with new metrics.
• The Transport Monitor provides both path MTU information for each Uplink Network and detailed,
time-series bandwidth, latency, and loss information for each Uplink Network. For more information
related to minimum underlay requirements, see Network Underlay Minimum Requirements.
Path MTU has the following values:
• Discovered: This is the value tested at the Uplink interface. If there is a mismatch between the
Discovered value and the Current value, it is a best practice to update the Path MTU in the service
mesh as a way to improve performance.
Note:
VCF Operations HCX automatically checks the Path MTU value every 15 minutes. If there is a
mismatch with the Current value, VCF Operations HCX displays a message in Interconnect >
Service Mesh display for the affected service mesh.
• Current: This is the value set in the service mesh for the Uplink network. This value overrides the
setting in the network profile. It can be the same as the Configured value.
• Configured: This is the value set in the network profile for the Uplink network.
4. (Optional) To view the detailed metrics, select Transport Monitor for each Uplink Network.
5. For each service mesh card listed under Transport Analytics, review the health details to verify that the underlay
network performance meets the requirements for the HCX services enabled for that service mesh.
If HCX transport analytics indicate that the Uplink Networks are healthy, proceed to using VCF Operations HCX
services. If the Uplink Network status is Degraded, use Transport Monitor to help identify and resolve underlay network
performance issues before using VCF Operations HCX services.
Examining Underlay Network Performance Using Transport Monitor
HCX Transport Monitor provides detailed, time-series throughput, latency, and loss information for the uplink networks in a
service mesh.
Transport Monitor provides a graphical representation of underlay network performance for each uplink network. Transport
Monitor collects the metrics every minute. For each selected uplink, the page provides the same information:
• Metrics selections: Throughput, Latency, Loss
• Duration selections: Real Time, Last Day, Last Week, Custom
• Graphic displays based on selected metrics and duration
In some scenarios, metrics data is not available for an uplink and underlay analytics information is not displayed:
• The service mesh appliance tunnels are down.
• The source environment is using Network Address Translation (NAT).
• The firewall security policies disallow the ICMP traffic.
1. From the Transport Analytics page in the HCX Manager UI, select Transport Monitor.
HCX displays the Transport Monitor page.

mode.

Sentinel Management
You must download and install HCX sentinel on all guest virtual machines requiring migration using HCX OS Assisted
Migration. Sentinel gathers the system configuration from the guest VM and assists with the data replication.
The guest VM information is used by various HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM) service processes. In part, the
information is used to create an inventory of guest VM systems for migration and to help replication processes prepare the
disks on the replica VM for replication and migration.
Sentinel also helps with the data replication by reading data written to the source disks and passing that data to the
Sentinel Data Receiver (SDR) appliance at the destination site.
Download the sentinel software in the Sentinel Management tab. The tab is available for systems that have the OSAM
service selected in the service mesh. For more information about OS Assisted Migration, see Understanding OS Assisted
Migration.
Downloading and Installing Sentinel Agent Software
When performing migrations from non-vSphere virtual machines, you must install the HCX sentinel on all guest virtual
machines requiring migration using HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM). The sentinel agent gathers the system
configuration from the guest virtual machine and assists with the data replication.
The OSAM service must be enabled in VCF Operations HCX service mesh.
Note:
On Linux systems, if the Polkit (PolicyKit) service is running on the virtual machine where Sentinal software is
installed, it can block activation/installation of the sentinel service. In this case, you must disable Polkit, restart the
VM, and reinstall the sentinel software.
1. In the source site VCF Operations HCX , navigate to Interconnect > Service Mesh > Sentinel Management.
Note:
In case of a single-site model, this is the destination site VCF Operations HCX.
VCF Operations HCX displays the sentinel management interface. This interface displays the deployed OSAM
appliance version, the sentinel download options, and the inventory of virtual machine workloads where sentinel
software has been installed. From the sentinel management interface, one can select the virtual machine workloads
and either upgrade or uninstall sentinel. For the list of workloads, you can manage sentinel software upgrades and
perform manual uninstall operations.
Broadcom 6627

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Download the software bundle appropriate for the environment that you are migrating.
The sentinel software bundle is downloaded to the local machine with the name
<SGW-name>-linux-sentinel-
or .
installer.sh <SGW-name>-windows-sentinel-bundle.zip
3. For Linux workloads, install the Linux software on all guest VMs that require migration.
a) Connect to your guest system using SSH.
b) Copy the linux-sentinel-installer.sh file to the guest system.
c) At the terminal, enter the command .
bash linux-sentinel-installer.sh
The software prompts you for permission to start the installation.
d) Enter yes, and press Enter.
4. For Windows workloads, install the Windows sentinel software on all guest VMs that require migration.
a) Log in to the guest system.
b) Copy the file to the guest system.
windows-sentinel-bundle.zip
c) Unzip the bundle.
d) To run the installer, double-click install-sentinel.exe.
e) Click Next to continue.
f) Accept the license agreement and click Next to continue.
g) Choose the location where you to install the software and click Next.
h) Click Finish.
Review the OSAM migration information. See Understanding OS Assisted Migration.

Uninstalling Sentinel Agent Software
The HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM) service automatically uninstalls the sentinel software from the guest system after
a successful migration. Alternatively, you can manually remove the software using the sentinel management interface.
Following a successful migration, the OSAM service automatically sends instructions to the guest virtual machine to power
off and uninstalling the sentinel agent software upon reboot. The OSAM service then removes the VM from the inventory
of non-vSphere virtual machines on VCF Operations HCX .
You can manually uninstall the software from a source VM using the Uninstall button in the sentinel management
interface. The action taken by the OSAM service to uninstall the sentinel software depends on whether the service has
access to the source system:
• OSAM service has a connection to the source VM: OSAM uninstalls the sentinel software from the source VM. Also,
OSAM removes the source VM from the inventory of non-vSphere virtual machines on VCF Operations HCX.
• OSAM service has no connection to the source VM: OSAM removes the source VM from the inventory of non-vSphere
virtual machines on VCF Operations HCX, but the sentinel software remains installed on the source VM. In this case,
if a connection to the source VM is reestablished with the OSAM service, the source VM reappears in the inventory of
non-vSphere virtual machines on VCF Operations HCX. To remove the sentinel agent software and delete the source
VM from the inventory, repeat the uninstall procedure.
Note:
The OSAM service prevents you from uninstalling the HCX sentinel software during the source VM migration.
To uninstall the sentinel agent software manually, use the following procedure.
1. Go to Interconnect > Service Mesh > Sentinel Management.
2. Select the source systems.
3. Click Uninstall.
4. Click Yes.
The OSAM service begins the process of uninstalling the software from the source VM.
5. In the sentinel management interface, verify that the entry is removed from the inventory of non-vSphere virtual
machines.
Upgrading Sentinel Agent Software
To maintain compatibility with OS Assisted Migration (OSAM) service appliances, update the sentinel agent software on
guest virtual machines.
The sentinel appliances are updated to the latest version as described in Upgrade the HCX Service Mesh Appliances.
The VCF Operations HCX upgrade bundle includes the SGW, SDR, and SRG appliance software necessary for upgrade.
It includes the sentinel Windows and Linux client software for downloading on each virtual machine. You must upgrade to
the latest VCF Operations HCX software to get the latest OSAM updates.
1. Navigate to the VCF Operations HCX console, and select Interconnect > Service Mesh > Sentinel Management.
The system displays the inventory of guest virtual machines. Each entry lists the current sentinel software version and
the available software version installed after upgrading the VCF Operations HCX .
2. Select the guest VMs to update:
Update all guest virtual machines to the same version at the same time as a best practice.
• To update all guest VMs, check the box at the top of the Hostname column.
• To update individual VMs, check the box next to each VM.
3. Click Upgrade.
The upgrade begins for the selected guest VMs. For the upgrade status, review the Task Details in the Sentinel
Management page.
Broadcom 6629

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
You can only upgrade the sentinel software when the migration is not in the switchover phase for that guest virtual
machine. An attempt to upgrade sentinel on a guest virtual machine that has a switchover in progress results in
an upgrade request failure.
Extending Networks
Using the network extension service, you can create Layer 2 networks at the destination site and bridge the remote
network to the source network over a multi-gigabit-capable link. The new stretched network is automatically bridged with
the network at the source site data center.
About Network Extension
You can bridge networks between VCF Operations HCX activated data centers using network extension.
With network extension, you can extend the virtual machine networks to a VCF Operations HCX remote site. Virtual
machines that are migrated or created on the extended network at the remote site behave as if on the same L2 network
as virtual machines in the source environment. With network extension, the default gateway for the extended network
is only connected at the source site. Traffic from virtual machines in remote sites that must be routed to a different L3
network flow through the source site gateway.
Using network extension, you can:
• Retain the IP and the MAC addresses of the VM, and honor existing network policies.
• Extend VLAN-tagged networks from a VMware vSphere Distributed Switch.
• Extend NSX segments, NSX VPC subnets, and DVPGs.
Requirements for Network Extension
VCF Operations HCX supports extending networks from VMware vSphere Distributed Switches, NSX segments under
default project, and NSX Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) subnets. HCX also supports extending networks to vSphere DVPG
as the destination.
The following sections list requirements for NSX segments and NSX VPC subnets.
These general requirements apply:
• Never use VCF Operations HCX to extend the vSphere Management network or other VMkernel networks (for
example: vMotion, vSAN, replication) to the remote site.
• The upstream switch for an extended network must be configured to accept (not filter out) RARP (reverse ARP)
packets.
Networks with VMware NSX
Networks with NSX at the source:
Registering NSX with VCF Operations HCX at the source site is optional, except when extending NSX networks or
migrating tags. If NSX is registered, the following requirements apply:
• The NSX Manager must be registered while deploying VCF Operations HCX.
• The NSX Manager must be version 3.2.3 or higher.
The NSX Manager and VCF Operations HCX must be registered with the same vCenter Server.
• The ESX hosts where the NSX segment/VPC subnet originates must be configured as NSX transport nodes.
• NSX Overlay, VPC subnets, and NSX VLAN networks can be extended.
Networks with NSX at the destination:
• Additional network extension appliances are required when extending more than 8 networks. With enhanced service
mesh appliances, additional network extension appliances might be required when extending more than 7 networks.
Broadcom 6630

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Enhanced service mesh appliances can be configured with multiple extensions per vNIC wherein a single vNIC of the
appliance gets used for as many as 128 extensions.
• NSX Overlay and/or NSX VLAN can be configured in the destination vCenter Server or SDDC.
• For those systems that are updated to the most recent version of VCF Operations HCX, multiple extensions per vNIC
mode wherein a single vNIC of an appliance gets used for as many as 128 extensions.
Note:
In addition to the preceding requirements, individual requirements for networks with NSX at the source and
networks with NSX at the destination also apply.
Networks with NSX VPC subnets
Network extension with VPC subnets at the source:
• Extending a VPC subnet requires both VCF Operations HCX and NSX versions to be at least 9.0.0.0 on source sites.
• You can extend VPC subnets to destination sites having an NSX segment or VPC subnet created for extending the
network.
Network extension with VPC subnets at the destination:
• VCF Operations HCX supports Public, Private, and Private Transit Gateway (TGW) access modes when extending to
destination VPC subnet.
• Users can opt to connect to gateway (VPC) when removing the extension irrespective of access mode.
• Extending a network to a destination VPC subnet requires NSX 9.0.0.0 and later on the destination site, and VCF
Operations HCX 9.0.0.0 and later on both paired sites.
– Extending a VPC subnet from the source to an Overlay/VLAN segment requires NSX 9.0 and later on the source
side.
– Extending a VPC subnet from the source to a VPC subnet on the destination site requires NSX 9.0 and later on
both sides.
– Extending a DVPG, VLAN segment, or overlay segment to a VPC subnet only requires NSX 9.0 and later on the
destination site.
Network extension with VPC subnets at the source and the destination:
Network extension from a source NSX VPC subnet to a destination NSX VPC subnet, requires the following preparation in
NSX:
• When creating an NSX Project, make sure that Distributed Firewall Rules do not have DROP or REJECT rules that
can affect traffic for the extension networks.
• Provide "Private" VPC IP CIDR when creating "Private" VPC subnets within the CIDR.
• Provide "Public" VPC IP CIDR in case of creating "Public" VPC subnets within the CIDR
• In the source VPC Service Profile, do not configure distributed DHCP.
Note:
If the source VPC Service Profile is configured with distributed DHCP, VMs connected to the extended network,
either an NSX segment or VPC subnet, do not receive a DHCP IP address from source-side DHCP server.
Restrictions and Limitations for Network Extension
VCF Operations HCX network extension is allowed or prevented under certain conditions.
Detected and Restricted Source Network Types
The VCF Operations HCX network extension service detects and prevents several non-supported network extension
scenarios (items are dimmed in the network extension UI):
• vSphere infrastructure networks (ESX VMkernel networks).
Broadcom 6631

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• VCF Operations HCX network profile networks - distributed port groups or Segments that are selected in a network
profile.
• Untagged distributed port groups - distributed port groups with VLAN type None, ID 0 or NULL.
• Private VLAN (PVLAN) networks.
• vCenter-backed port groups that are configured with ephemeral binding cannot be extended.
• NSX logical switches.
Unsupported Source Configurations
HCX network extension does not support the following source configurations:
• vSphere Standard Switch (VSS) networks.
• Cisco Application Centric Infrastructure (ACI) with VMware Virtual Machine Monitor (VMM).
• Virtual machine networks must only be extended with a single solution. VCF Operations HCX does not support
network extension for networks already extended to the same NSX router by an external solution. For example, either
network extension or NSX L2 VPN can be used to provide connectivity, but both must not be used simultaneously.
Using multiple bridging solutions simultaneously can result in a network outage.
• Virtual machine networks with shared or overlapping VLAN configurations must not be extended to the same
destination router. This can result in a network outage.
• Secondary subnets in a single layer-2 network.
• VCF Operations HCX does not integrate with an NSX Global Manager for extending networks (only the non-Federated
NSX Local Manager is supported). See Support for NSX Federation.
• Network extensions are not supported between non-vSphere VCF Operations HCX site pairs.
Unsupported Destination Configurations
VCF Operations HCX network extension does not support the following destination configurations:
• VCF Operations HCX does not integrate with an NSX Global Manager for extending networks (only the non-Federated
NSX Local Manager is supported). See Support for NSX Federation.
• Mobility Optimized Networking (MON) is not supported when extending networks to a destination NSX VPC subnet,
NSX VLAN segment, or vSphere DVPG.
• NSX DVPG is not supported as a destination segment.
Network Extension in NSX Federated Environments
When the local NSX manager registered with VCF Operations HCX at either the source or destination site is later
integrated with an NSX Global Manager, established network extensions between sites continue to work. However, you
cannot extend a new network or enable/disable Mobility Optimized Networking (MON) for an already extended network.
In such cases, existing network extensions can be impacted if the appliance serving the extensions is upgraded or
redeployed. See, Support for NSX Federation
Additional Considerations
• HCX supports extending the same network to a maximum of 3 distinct destinations or routers.
• One network extension configuration cannot be extended multiple times to the same destination router.
• A network that has been extended to three environments is only supported to the third location if the sites are
physically co-located and traffic does not travel over a Wide Area Network.
– A three-point extension is not supported with source networks that are based on NSX distributed routing.
– A three-point extension can lower end-to-end network performance due to the combined latency and additional
layer of packet and encryption processing.
• One network extension appliance can only connect to one vSphere Distributed Virtual Switch or NSX Transport Zone.
• Networks can only be extended between one appliance pair (source and destination appliances) per site, and multiple
network appliances cannot be used to increase throughput.
• Network extension does not detect or mitigate loops.
• Virtual machine networks that span more than one vCenter Server must not be extended from more than one vCenter
Server to the same destination router to avoid a network outage.
Broadcom 6632

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Network extension does not detect or mitigate IP conflicts.
• Network extension does not detect or mitigate MAC conflicts.
• For a cloud/site pair, a given network can be extended through only one appliance and is subject to the resource and
the performance limitations of that appliance.
• Network extension connects to an existing segment on the target site if it has the same gateway IP and Prefix
configured for the extension, and it disconnects the NSX router interface from the network. If the NSX Tier-1 router
interface was previously connected and in service, all communication to the gateway on the extended network on the
destination site is disrupted.
– For destination VPC Subnet, connection is to an existing VPC Subnet on the target site if it has the same gateway
IP, prefix length, VPC, and Subnet access mode.
– For destination NSX VLAN segment, connection is to an existing segment on the target site if it has same Transport
Zone and VLAN-ID.
– For destination vSphere DVPG, connection is to an existing DVPG on the target site if it has the same vSphere DVS
and VLAN-ID.
• VMware NSX Traceflow does not work with extended networks.
• Extending DVPG/VLAN segments to NSX DVPG at the destination requires the VCF Operations HCX and NSX
versions to be at least 9.1 on both sites.
Extending Networks
Network extension is a layer-two bridging function that is initiated at the source site.
The source and destination site pair are vSphere-based VCF Operations HCX deployments and a service mesh is
deployed between them.
You can extend networks by selecting one or more distributed port groups, NSX overlay or VLAN segments, or NSX VPC
subnets. When you extend a network, a corresponding network is created at the destination site. If the service mesh does
not support extending networks to VLAN-backed segments, see step 9 in this procedure for information about how to
modify a service mesh to deploy NE appliances to support VLAN segments.
Network extension is not supported for non-vSphere site pairs.
For a list of supported networks and requirements for network extension, see Requirements for Network Extension.
For a list of restrictions regarding network extension, see Restrictions and Limitations for Network Extension.
For the operational limits supported with network extension, see Configuration and Service Limits.
1. In HCX Manager, select Network Extension.
The service meshes associated with the local HCX Manager are displayed. Expand a service mesh to view associated
network extensions.

2. At the top of the page, select Extend Networks.
3. Select a service mesh.
If you have only one service mesh, it is selected by default.
4. From the Filters pane, select a network type.
Use the available filters to hide networks that are ineligible for extension, that do not have virtual machines associated
with them, or are networks without extension.
5. In the Networks pane, select one or more source networks to extend.
The network list changes based on the network type. For vSphere clusters, a list of distributed virtual port groups is
displayed. For NSX, NSX segments, VLAN segments, and VPC subnets are displayed.
6. Click Next.
7. To extend a source network to an NSX VLAN network:
a) Select the network extension appliance supporting VLAN.
The network extension appliance information is based on your service mesh configuration. If your service mesh
configuration only supports VLAN, this appliance is selected by default.
b) Enter the destination VLAN ID.
8. To extend a source network to a vSphere DVPG network:
a) Select the network extension appliance supporting VLAN on DVPG.
The network extension appliance information is based on your service mesh configuration. If your service mesh
configuration only supports VLAN, this appliance is selected by default.
b) Enter the destination VLAN ID.

a) Select Destination First Hop Router.
A screen appears with the available NSX Gateway selections.
