Understanding vMotion and Cold Migration
VCF Operations HCX integrates with ESX to perform vMotion migrations for powered on virtual machines, and with Cold
Migration for powered off virtual machines.
vMotion
VCF Operations HCX vMotion can transfer a live virtual machine from a VCF Operations HCX vCenter Server to a VCF
Operations HCX destination site (or from the destination site towards the local site). The vMotion transfer captures the
virtual machine active memory, its execution state, its IP address, and its MAC address. The migration duration depends
on the connectivity, including both the bandwidth available and the latency between the two sites.
Cold Migration
Cold migration uses the same network path as VCF Operations HCX vMotion to transfer a powered-off virtual machine.
During a cold migration, the virtual machine IP address and the MAC address are preserved. Cold migrations must satisfy
the vMotion requirements.
Requirements and Limitations for vMotion and Cold Migration
• HCX Interconnect tunnels must be up/active.
• HCX vMotion requires 150 Mbps or higher throughput capability. See Network Underlay Minimum Requirements.
• The virtual machine hardware version must be at least version 9 or higher.
• The underlying architecture, regardless of OS, must be x86.
• VMs with Raw Disk Mapping in compatibility mode (RDM-V) can only be migrated using Bulk Migration.
• VMware NFC is used as the primary protocol during Cold migration and as a secondary protocol during HCX vMotion.
Note:
The HCX Interconnect appliance uses a network profile configuration that is dedicated to the vMotion traffic.
This configuration does not include the Cold and vMotion NFC traffic. VCF Operations HCX always uses
its Management interface for Cold and vMotion NFC traffic. In deployments where ESX uses a dedicated
Provisioning VMkernel for NFC traffic, VCF Operations HCX continues to route Cold and vMotion NFC traffic
through the Management interface.
• The Migration interface does not display port groups that are VLAN trunks.
For information regarding migration limits, refer to the VMware Configurations Maximums tool.
Virtual Machine Restrictions for vMotion
Virtual machines with the following attributes are not supported for migration.
• Virtual machines cannot be migrated while they are using a shared SCSI bus, flagged for multi-writer, enabled for fault
tolerance, or configured for shared VMDK disk sharing.
• Attached virtual media or ISOs.
• Virtual machine hardware version 8 or earlier.
• Although concurrent vMotion migrations can be initiated up to the vSphere limits, VMware HCX vMotion only supports
serial vMotion migrations between a source and the destination site per the service mesh. For simultaneous migrations
in parallel, select Bulk Migration.
• VCF Operations HCX vMotion defaults to Opportunistic mode for per-VM vMotion Encryption if it is set to Required.
During the migration operation - the mode is changed to Opportunistic during the migration initialization, and then set
back to Required after the migration is completed.
• Virtual Machines with Change Block Tracking (CBT) can be migrated, but HCX deactivates CBT.
• VMware software appliances (including, but not limited to vCenter and NSX Manager) cannot be migrated with HCX
vMotion migration.
• vSphere VM Encryption is not supported.
• Virtual machine workloads with an attached serial port device are not supported. For these workloads, detach such
devices prior to starting the migration.
Broadcom 6666

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
You can use Bulk Migration to migrate workloads with an attached serial port device.
Understanding Replication Assisted vMotion
HCX Replication Assisted vMotion (RAV) uses the HCX along with replication and vMotion technologies to provide large-
scale, parallel migrations with zero downtime.
HCX RAV provides the following benefits:
• Large-scale live mobility: Administrators can submit large sets of VMs for a live migration.
• Switchover window: With RAV, administrators can specify a switchover window.
• Continuous replication: Once a set of VMs is selected for migration, RAV performs an initial sync. After the initial
synchronization is complete, a delta synchronization with two-hour recovery point objective (RPO) occurs while waiting
for the scheduled switchover.
• Concurrency: With RAV, multiple VMs are replicated simultaneously. When the replication phase reaches the
switchover window, a delta vMotion cycle is initiated to do a quick, live switchover. Live switchover happens serially per
service mesh.
• Resiliency: RAV migrations are resilient to latency and varied network and service conditions during the initial sync and
continuous replication sync.
• Switchover larger sets of VMs with a smaller maintenance window: Large chunks of data synchronization by way of
replication allow for smaller delta vMotion cycles.
HCX RAV migration triggers the following events:
1. Replication begins with a full synchronization (replication) of the virtual machine disks to the destination site.
2. Migrated VMs enter a continuous synchronization cycle until a switchover is triggered.
3. Depending upon data churn on the source disk, additional snapshots are created during the RPO cycle. For more
information about RPO cycle/Delta Sync refer to VMware KB 87028.
4. You can have the switchover process start immediately following the initial sync or delay the switchover until a specific
time using the scheduled migration option. If the switchover is scheduled, the synchronization cycle continues until the
switchover begins.
5. The final delta synchronization begins when the switchover phase starts. During this phase, vMotion is engaged for
migrating the disk delta data and virtual machine state.
6. As the final step in the switchover, the source VM is removed, and the migrated VM is connected to the network.
Replication Assisted vMotion creates two folders at the destination site datastore. One folder contains the virtual
machine infrastructure definition, and the other contains the virtual machine disk information. This is normal behavior
for RAV migrations and has no impact on the functionality of the virtual machine at the destination site.
Note:
In some cases, having two folders might impact other applications, such as backup tools, that require access to
the virtual machine folders. If necessary, you can consolidate the contents of these two folders datastore vMotion.
Single vCenter Server Operation
You can use Replication Assisted vMotion (RAV) migration within a single vCenter Server. In this case, HCX appliances
such as HCX Interconnect, are deployed to cater to different clusters within the same VC. Other than deployment within
the same VC, the process for configuring VCF Operations HCX is the same, which means configuring a compute profile
and a service mesh to enable RAV.
Requirements for Replication Assisted vMotion
• Interconnect tunnels must be up/active.
• RAV requires 150 Mbps or higher throughput capability. See Network Underlay Minimum Requirements.
• The virtual machine hardware version must be Version 9 or higher.
• The underlying architecture, regardless of OS, must be x86.
Broadcom 6667

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Hybrid Interconnect and Replication Assisted vMotion services must be activated and in a healthy state in the relevant
service mesh.
• RAV uses vSphere Replication whose potential throughput can vary depending on bandwidth available for migrations,
latency, available CPU/MEM/IOPS, and disk read speed.
• VMware NFC is used as a secondary protocol during Replication Assisted vMotion migration.
Note:
VCF Operations HCX always uses its Management interface for NFC traffic. In deployments where ESX hosts
use a dedicated Provisioning vmkernel for NFC traffic, VCF Operations HCX continues to route NFC traffic
through the Management interface. Provision vmkernels are dedicated network interfaces used for cold migration,
cloning, and snapshot transfers, separate from vMotion.
• When both the source vCenter and HCX Manager versions are 9.1.x or higher the HBR agent must be installed on
source ESXi hosts that are running a version earlier than 9.1.x.
For information regarding the migration limits, refer to the VMware Configurations Maximums tool.
Restrictions for Replication Assisted vMotion
• Virtual machines with the following attributes are not supported for migration.
– Virtual machines cannot be migrated while they are using a shared SCSI bus, flagged for multi-writer, or enabled for
fault tolerance.
– Attached virtual media or ISOs.
– Virtual machine hardware version 8 or earlier.
• Live switchover of concurrent RAV migrations is run serially per service mesh.
• VCF Operations HCX vMotion defaults to Opportunistic mode for per-VM vMotion Encryption if it is set to Required.
During the migration operation, the mode is changed to Opportunistic on the migration initialization, and then set back
to Required after the migration is completed.
• Replication Assisted vMotion does not support the migration of workloads with Independent persistent and
Independent non-persistent disks, as taking a snapshot of such a virtual machine does not produce delta disks, which
are required for the underlying RAV migration technology.
• Virtual machines with Raw Device Mappings (RDM) in Physical Compatibility mode cannot be migrated.
• Virtual machines with Raw Device Mappings in compatibility mode (RDM-V) cannot be migrated using RAV and
vMotion.
• Virtual machines with DirectPath I/O configurations cannot be migrated without first removing the DirectPath device.
• To migrate Fault Tolerance-enabled VMs, temporarily turn off Fault Tolerance, and perform RAV. When this operation is
complete, turn Fault Tolerance back on.
• Migration to or from vVOL datastores is not supported.
• The Migration interface does not display port groups that are VLAN trunks.
• Virtual Machines with Change Block Tracking (CBT) can be migrated, but HCX deactivates CBT.
• RAV migration to VMFS6 target datastores requires the following minimum vSphere version at the target site: vSphere
6.5U3f or vSphere 6.7U3.
• Virtual machines using virtual NVMe (vNVME) controllers cannot be migrated.
• Virtual machine Snapshots cannot be migrated.
• VMware software appliances (including, but not limited to vCenter and NSX Manager) cannot be migrated with HCX
RAV migration.
• vSphere VM Encryption is not supported.
• Virtual machine workloads with an attached serial port device are not supported. For these workloads, detach such
devices prior to starting the migration.
Note:
You can use Bulk Migration to migrate workloads with an attached serial port device.
Understanding HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct)
HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) provides support for VMware vSphere native cross-vCenter vMotion migration.
Broadcom 6668

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
With native cross-vCenter vMotion, a direct data path is established using the underlying management network between
the VMware ESX hosts associated with the source and destination vCenter Servers. In this case, HCX orchestrates
the migration flows between the HCX appliances deployed in each vCenter Server. For more information about native
vSphere vMotion, see Migrating Virtual Machines Between vCenter Systems in the VMware vSphere documentation.
Like other HCX migration types, you enable HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) during the service mesh creation process.
If you configure a site pair with only the HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) migration type, HCX establishes management
plane connectivity between sites, creates a service mesh, and deploys the HCX-IX appliance. In this case, the HCX-IX
appliance is only used for VCF Operations HCX control plane communication and not for migration traffic.
How it Works
The workload migration has the following high-level workflow in HCX:
1. During the service mesh configuration, enable HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct).
2. In the Migration interface, create a mobility group for the selected workloads.
3. Select HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) as the migration type and configure the available transfer, placement, and
extended options.
4. HCX validates the configuration.
5. Start the migration.
6. HCX initiates the migration using native cross-vCenter vMotion.
7. HCX displays the status of the migration operation.
Requirements
• A dedicated vSphere vMotion data path must be set up between the source and the target ESX hosts.
• Standard switches at the source and target clusters must have matching security policies and the teaming and failover
policies.
• The vSphere Distributed Switch version at the source and the destination sites must be the same. See KB 56991.
• The source and target sites are running vSphere 6.7 or later.
• Migrating encrypted virtual machines:
– The Key Management Server (KMS) used to encrypt the source VM is present on the target site for encrypted direct
vMotion to be successful, regardless of the default KMS at either site.
– The name and IP address of the KMS must match between the source and target sites.
– The source and target sites must be running vSphere 7.0 or later.
• Virtual machines must be running Hardware Version 4 or later.
• VMware Tools are installed on the VM.
• Review the port requirements: VMware KB 2106952.
• All the native cross-vCenter vMotion dependencies detailed in KB article 2106952 must be satisfied.
Restrictions
• HCX diagnostics are not available for HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct).
• Virtual machines with mounted ISO images cannot be migrated. The HCX Bulk migration operation can be used for
force unmount ISO images, or you can unmount the ISO images manually.
• Virtual machines cannot be migrated while they are using a shared SCSI bus, flagged for multi-writer, enabled for fault
tolerance, or configured for shared VMDK disk sharing.
• Migration is not supported when the source VM is on an NSX-backed segment.
• Virtual machines with DvFilter configurations are not supported.
• HCX Assisted vMotion (HAV) supports VMs with I/O filters only if a valid I/O filter policy is active on the source VM.
Also the destination environment must have the identical I/O filter provider installed to maintain policy persistence
during migration.
• It is a best practice to avoid scheduling VM hardware upgrade on the source vCenter Server while performing
migration through VCF Operations HCX.
• VCF Operations HCX applies a maximum of 50 concurrent relocation operations per HCX Manager to avoid
overloading the vCenter Server.
Broadcom 6669

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• All the native cross-vCenter vMotion limitations and restrictions related to scale and concurrency apply to HCX
Assisted vMotion migration.
• HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) migrations cannot be performed when the source NIC is in a disconnected state, the
source VM is attached to NSX segment or VPC subnet, and the target network is mapped to either vCenter Distributed
Virtual Port Group (DVPG) or standard VSS network.
• HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) migration is not supported when there is VDS version mismatch between source and
target sites.
• HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct) migration is not supported when the source VM is connected to an NSX segment and
the target network is either an NSX Segment or a VPC subnet. Also, migration is not supported when source VM is
connected to VPC subnet and target network is either an NSX segment or a VPC subnet and the source NIC is in
connected state.
• Adding multiple target datastores on local sites is not supported.
Understanding Supervisor Onboarding for Migrations
When you enable the vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) control plane on vSphere clusters and they become
Supervisors, the Kubernetes control plane is created inside the hypervisor layer. VCF Operations HCX provides the option
to import, or “onboard,” traditional virtual machine workloads into specified Supervisor clusters.
Note:
Supervisor Onboarding supports Bulk migration between vCenter Servers and within a single vCenter Server. For
more information, see Understanding Bulk Migration.
Onboarding workloads to the Supervisor is a two-step process. VCF Operations HCX first bulk migrates workloads from
the source site to a staging area on the destination site defined by the Compute Container setting in the migration
configuration wizard. From the staging area, VCF Operations HCX imports the workloads to the Supervisor namespace
identified in the migration configuration.
How it Works
1. The user creates the migration groups, selects the Supervisor Onboarding option, and provides the necessary
configuration options, including the Supervisor namespace, storage class, and compute container.
2. VCF Operations HCX performs validation checks on the VMs to ensure that they align with the supervisor
environment. For example, the Guest OS running on the VM must be supported by the Supervisor.
3. VCF Operations HCX runs additional validation checks on the VMs to verify they meet the Bulk migration parameters,
such as the HW version and installation of VM Tools. If there is an issue in the validation process, VCF Operations
HCX displays an error. You can address the error and then try the migration again.
4. VCF Operations HCX migrates the VMs to a staging, or layover, area at the destination site.
5. VCF Operations HCX onboards the VMs to the Supervisor and verifies that any applications are running properly.
Note:
If onboarding to the Supervisor is unsuccessful, VCF Operations HCX displays an error and the workload is
retained in the layover area. After addressing the issue, you can manually import the workload from the staging
area.
Requirements and Limitations
• VCF Operations HCX 9.0 or later must be installed at both the source and target.
• VMs must have VMware Tools installed.
• Support is for Bulk migration only.
• Importing a VM to the Supervisor requires a reboot.
CAUTION:
If an application cannot tolerate downtime, it should not be migrated using the Supervisor onboarding process.
• Onboarding Windows-based VMs has additional migration configuration parameters to be provided by users in the UI:
owner name, organization name, computer name, and product key (optional).
Broadcom 6670

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Restrictions
Supervisor onboarding does not support the following:
• Workloads that depend on IPv6 cannot be migrated using Supervisor Onboarding.
• VMs with a Guest OS type that does not support Guest OS Customization (GOSC).
• Migration types: OS Assisted Migration (OSAM), HCX vMotion, Replication Assisted vMotion, Cold, HCX Assisted
vMotion
For the migration process using Supervisor Onboarding, see Migrating Virtual Machines with Mobility Groups.
Understanding OS Assisted Migration
Together with the sentinel appliances deployed at VCF Operations HCX sites, the HCX OS Assisted Migration (OSAM)
service uses the sentinel software that you install on the Linux or Windows-based guest virtual machines to assist with
communication and replication from their guest environment to VCF.
When OSAM is activated in your service mesh, VCF Operations HCX deploys the appropriate sentinel appliance
depending on the Site Pair. For vSphere-based site pairs (multi-site mode), VCF Operations HCX deploys the Sentinel
Gateway (SGW) appliance at the source site and the Sentinel Data Receiver (SDR) appliance at the destination site.
These two appliances work together to migrate workloads from a non-vSphere environment to VCF.
For site pairs where the non-vSphere guest environment is paired directly with an VCF Operations HCX site (single-site
mode), VCF Operations HCX deploys the Sentinel Resource Gateway (SRG) appliance at the destination vSphere-based
site. This appliance alone handles the migration of the guest workloads from the non-vSphere site to the vSphere-based
site.
You must install HCX sentinel agent software on all guest virtual machines requiring migration using HCX OS Assisted
Migration. The software gathers the system configuration from the guest virtual machine and assists with the data
replication. The guest system information is used by various HCX OS Assisted Migration service processes. In part, the
information is used to create an inventory of guest virtual machine systems for migration and to help replication processes
prepare the disks on the replica virtual machine for replication and migration.
After the sentinel agent is installed, a secure connection is established between the guest virtual machines and the
sentinel appliance. You specify the network connections between the guest virtual machines and sentinel appliances by
configuring the Guest network profile setting in the compute profile.
VCF Operations HCX builds an inventory of candidates for migration as the sentinel software is installed on the guest
virtual machines.
An OS Assisted Migration request triggers the following events:
1. Replication begins a full synchronization transfer to the destination site. The guest virtual machine remains online
during replication until the final delta synchronization.
2. Before the final delta synchronization, the OS Assisted Migration service quiesces the guest virtual machine on a best-
effort basis.
For example, it is possible for a Linux service running on the guest virtual machine to start immediately after OS
Assisted Migration has quiesced the services and stopped all known processes. If some process starts after quiescing
the system, it can potentially lead to final synchronization not completing and appear as though the switchover process
is stuck.
Note:
As part of both continuous and final synchronization, the system checks for changed blocks or files and replicates
them.
• On a Windows system, the OS Assisted Migration service reads the entire disk to determine the changed
blocks to replicate. The process of reading the entire disk can be time consuming.
• On a Linux system, the OS Assisted Migration service walks the entire file system to determine the changed
files to replicate.
1. When the delta synchronization finishes, a switchover is triggered. You can have the switchover process start
immediately following the initial sync or delay the switchover until a specific time using the scheduled migration option.
Broadcom 6671

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
By using the scheduled migration option, the switchover can occur during a maintenance window. The final delta
synchronization begins when the switchover phase starts.
During scheduled migrations, HCX sentinel performs continuous synchronization by transferring only the deltas since
the previous sync cycle. For Windows HCX sentinel, this synchronization is achieved by identifying the changed file
system blocks, whereas for Linux HCX sentinel, this synchronization is achieved by monitoring the changed files.
To improve the time it takes to reach that final consistency point for Linux systems, a pre-determined set of files and
directories listed in is excluded from the continuous synchronization.
/opt/vmware/hcx/osam/excluded_paths
If you have additional files that do not require monitoring, you can exclude them from continuous synchronization by
editing the file. Excluding files requires a restart of the sentinel service named using
vmware-hcx-osam-sentinel
service or systemctl commands.
Note:
Excluded files are always synchronized to the target virtual machine during the initial and final synchronization
phases.
2. VCF Operations HCX performs a hardware mapping of the replicated volumes to ensure proper operation, including
updates of the software stack on the replica. This fix-up process includes adding drivers and modifying the OS
configuration files at the destination. The migrated virtual machine reboots during this process.
Note:
When migrating Windows systems, HCX OS Assisted Migration software creates a temporary local user on
the migrated Windows system during the switchover phase. This user gets deleted after the fix-up process is
completed.
Note:
When migrating Linux systems, HCX OS Assisted Migration software uses an independent software stack
residing on a separate disk, called the fix-up disk, for the fix-up process. To fix-up 64-bit workload VMs, VCF
Operations HCX uses the Photon 5.0 version of the fix-up disk. The fix-up boot disk is detached and deleted at
the end of the switchover process.
3. As the final step in the switchover, the source is powered off, the migrated replica is connected to the network, and the
switchover completes.
The vSphere target virtual machine reboots twice during the switchover phase.
For Linux workloads, if the synchronization process fails for any reason, such as a broken network connection, by
default the synchronization is retried for eight hours. To improve the time it takes to reach a final consistency point for
switchover to begin, you can shorten the retry period to as little as one hour by editing the file
/opt/vmware/hcx/
and setting the max_retry_interval from one to eight hours. After setting the interval,
osam/etc/sync.params
restart the sentinel service named using service or systemctl commands.
vmware-hcx-osam-sentinel
For Windows workloads, the synchronization process retries until the synchronization completes or the operation is
canceled.
4. HCX Manager names the replica virtual machine with the host name of the source virtual machine.
5. For Windows workloads, VMware Tools is installed on the migrated virtual machine and migration completes.
6. If the source does not power off, an attempt is made to power off the replica virtual machine.
If the replica virtual machine successfully powers off, it remains connected to the NICs. In this case, you can manually
power off the source and power on the replica. If the replica does not power off, both the guest virtual machine and the
replica remain on, but the replica is not connected to the network. In this case, you activate the NICs manually that are
attached to the replica virtual machine using vCenter, power-off source virtual machine (if not already), and power on
Migrated virtual machine.
Considerations for OSAM Deployment
The OS Assisted Migration (OSAM) service includes several components that work together for connecting and
forwarding guest workloads in the source environment.
Refer to the following considerations when deploying and operating OS Assisted Migration in your environment.
Broadcom 6672

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• The OSAM service converts non-vSphere guests to vSphere virtual machines. This conversion process involves
halting OS services to quiesce the guest virtual machine. The downtime for this conversion process can vary from
minutes to hours depending on a virtual machine size and activity.
• OSAM migrations require a guest network configuration in the compute profile.
• The HCX sentinel agent software encrypts all connections to the Sentinel Gateway. The encryption cannot be
deactivated.
• The HCX sentinel appliance must be deployed in a vSphere environment, and not within KVM or Hyper-V.
• To use network extension with OSAM deployments, VLANs in the non-vSphere environment must also exist on the
source vSphere environment network switches and in vCenter as distributed port groups.
• For vSphere-based site pairs, each service mesh deploys one Sentinel Gateway (SGW) and its peer Sentinel Data
Receiver (SDR), and supports up to 50 active replica disks.
• For non-vSphere site pairs, the service mesh deploys one Sentinel Resource Gateway (SRG) that supports up to 50
active replica disks.
• HCX OSAM deployments support 200 concurrent VM disk migrations across a four service mesh scale-out
deployment. In this service mesh scale-out model for OSAM, the HCX sentinel download operation is presented per
service mesh.
• Guest virtual machines can only be migrated to a datastore that is accessible by the SDR or SRG appliance.
• Redeployment of sentinel appliances is not allowed when any migration is in-progress.
• Only "thin" and "thick" disk provisioning types are supported as the disk provision type for the migrated system. The
"Same as Source" option is not supported.
• OSAM Migration using PowerCLI:
– PowerCLI 11.5 is not supported.
• The OSAM migration service applies the default storage policy to the migrated VMs and their disks. Currently, the
OSAM service does not support a user-selected storage policy.
• Changes to source Guest virtual machine configurations while a migration is in progress might not take effect in
migrated virtual machines and sometimes might lead to migration failure.
• VMs with Linux GuestOS can have up to 15 hard disks attached.
• VMs with Windows GuestOS can have up to 64 volumes or file-systems.
• Migrations of VMs running on vSphere with OSAM are not supported.
For information regarding migration limits, refer to the VMware Configurations Maximums tool.

Guest Operating System Considerations
The OS Assisted Migration service supports a variety of hypervisors and guest operating systems in both Linux and
Windows environments.
General Operating System Considerations
Some service limitations are common to Linux and Windows environments where OS Assisted Migration is deployed.
• The HCX-sentinel agents are installed in the guest operating system and automatically make connections to the HCX
Sentinel Gateway.
• Guest virtual machines with the locale and the UI language other than English US are not supported.
• UEFI-based source systems using legacy BIOS boot mode are not supported.
• Anti-virus software, or any OS application that is actively accessing file systems, can significantly delay the OSAM
switchover phase. Deactivate these types of applications as a best practice before configuring the OSAM migration.
Broadcom 6674

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Network file shares are not supported with OSAM migrations. This includes NFS, SMB, and CIFS, with varying
outcomes:
– Mounted files shares like CIFS may result in migration failures.
– NFS shares are ignored during the fix-up phase and do not result in migration failure.
Linux Specific Considerations
• Block devices (partitions) with unrecognized content are not migrated to the destination.
– Unsupported file systems.
– Unmounted file systems.
– Unknown content with a partition or a block device.
– Encrypted file systems.
– md devices (software RAID).
• Device names for md devices (software RAID) are not retained post migration.
– It is advised to mount the md devices using UUID or Label in .
/etc/fstab
– It is advised to revisit the mdadm.conf and modify the new name and other configuration parameters for the md
devices.
• Statics routes are not supported.
• VLAN interfaces are not supported.
• On RHEL/CentOS 7.0, 7.1, and 7.2, the XFS file system UUID is not restored to the original UUID for the file system
where /boot resides because mkfs.xfs does not support the functionality (-m option). A new random UUID is generated.
Modifying the UUID after the file system is created triggers RHEL bug 1579390.
• /etc/fstab entries for removable media (floppy, CD) are not supported; such entries must be commented out before
migration.
• When migrating Linux systems, the OSAM software uses an independent software stack residing on a separate disk
for the fix-up process. This fix-up boot disk is detached and deleted at the end of the switchover process.
• The configuration files of Linux system services, such as dhcpd, that reference network interface names are not
modified. You must manually modify these files on the migrated system.
• Device names in bonded/teamed interface configuration files are not replaced with the new device names, and this can
lead to the bonded interface not showing as UP. You must make sure that the bonded/teamed interface device names
match the new name after migration. You might encounter this issue if you use Network Manager tools like nmcli to
configure bonded/teamed interfaces.
Windows Specific Considerations
• No support for syncing logical volumes.
• Basic MBR and GPT disk partitions are supported. Dynamic GPT and Dynamic MBR disks partitions are not
supported.
– If the boot disk is dynamic, migration is not supported.
– If the data disks are dynamic, the data on the disks is not migrated, and the disks appear as raw disks on the
migrated system.
• Only NTFS formatted volumes are supported. ESP (EFI system partition) with the FAT32 file system is an exception.
• No support for non-Windows service applications from the system quiescing perspective during the final sync.
• Systems with more than 64 volumes are not supported since vSphere Standard Switch (VSS) allows a maximum of 64
snapshots on a system.
• Any VSS snapshots present on the source Windows system before migration are not usable on the migrated system.
• VLAN interfaces are not supported.
• For Windows systems, in general the pre-requisites for the VMware Tools installation have to be satisfied on the
source system. The pre-requisites for the VMware Tools installation can vary based on the target VCenter Server
and ESX version, and Windows OS version on the source system. For example, if the target ESX version is 6.5.0 (or
higher), VMware Tools version is 10.3.x. To view the list of prerequisites based on different Windows OS versions see
VMware KB 55798.
• When migrating Windows systems, the OS Assisted Migration software creates a temporary local user on the migrated
Windows system during the switchover phase. This user gets deleted after the fix-up process is completed.
Broadcom 6675

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Do not run Windows updates on the source system during a migration. If Windows updates are in progress, the
migration can fail.
• A Windows source system configured as a failover cluster node is not supported.
About Migrating Mobility Groups from Migration Waves
This section describes the process for migrating workloads in migration waves created using VMware Cloud Foundation
Operations for Networks.
Note:
For information related to migrating mobility groups that are not created locally in VCF Operations HCX and do
not use VCF Operations for networks, see Migrating Virtual Machines with Mobility Groups.
For many use cases, the scope of migration operations can involve hundreds or thousands of virtual machines requiring
different migration parameters. Developing a migration plan can help to facilitate the migration of these workloads
efficiently. Establishing a migration plan is a service of VCF Operations for networks. VCF Operations HCX works with the
migration planning functionality in VCF Operations for networks to configure and run the migration wave.
The high-level process of creating a Migration Plan in VCF Operations for networks has these steps:
1. Add the VM migration attributes (optional).
Identify and analyze workloads including application flows within your infrastructure.
2. Define the migration scope.
Create the scope of the migration plan by categorizing workloads based on specific criteria.
3. Create a migration wave.
Group and organize selected workloads into distinct migration waves according to the migration plan scope.
4. Create mobility groups.
Use a mobility group to execute migrations concurrently.
5. Sync to VCF Operations HCX or manually export migration waves from VCF Operations for networks.
Sync migration waves directly to VCF Operations HCX or manually export workload and network CSV files from VCF
Operations for networks..
For complete information regarding the development of the migration plan and associated migration waves, see Create a
Migration Plan and Export Migration Waves.
The high-level process in VCF Operations HCX for implementing the migration plan and migrating workloads that are
defined in the associated migration wave has these steps:
1. Sync from VCF Operations for networks or import a migration wave manually.
Create a migration wave by syncing directly from VCF Operations for networks or by manually importing the workload
and network CSV files.
2. Commit the migration wave (for manual imports).
Validate the workloads in each mobility group in the migration wave and commit those mobility groups for migration.
3. Configure and schedule the mobility groups.
Configure the mobility groups for migration, including setting the migration and placement options, and scheduling the
transfer and switchover windows.
4. Run pre-migration checks.
Run the pre-migration checks to validate workload connectivity and service mesh health.
5. Run migrations.
Run the migrations that are defined in the migration wave and perform post-migration activities.
To begin the process of migrating mobility groups with migrations waves, see Import and Commit Migration Waves.
Broadcom 6676

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Import and Commit Migration Waves
VCF Operations HCX provides two mechanisms for adding migration waves for migration: direct syncing from the VCF
Operations for networks component, and manually by importing the exported CSV files from VCF Operations for networks.
Follow this process to manually import migration waves from CSV files for migration. For an overview of the migration
process using migration waves, see About Migrating Mobility Groups from Migration Waves
Note:
Whether you import a migration wave manually or sync it directly in VCF Operations HCX from the VCF
Operations for networks component, the process requires an initial validation step. The status of the validation
appears in the Migration Planning interface. If validation fails for migration waves synced directly from the VCF
Operations for networks component, you must fix the issues in VCF Operations for networks component. If the
validation step for migration waves synced from VCF Operations for networks is successful, these migration
waves are automatically committed for migration and you can continue to Migrate Mobility Group Workloads in
Migration Waves.
1. In the VCF Operations HCX UI, navigate to Migration.
The Migration Planning screen appears.
Important:
Migration waves synced directly from VCF Operations for networks appear in the display in Committed or
Validation Failed status depending on the outcome of the validation process. For these entries, skip the rest of this
procedure and go directly to Migrate Mobility Group Workloads in Migration Waves.
2. Click .
Import Migration Wave
3. Select the destination HCX Manager that is the target of the mobility operations.
4. Import the CSV files associated with the migration wave.
Exporting a migration wave from VCF Operations for networks generates a zip file with two CSV files that you extract
and upload to VCF Operations HCX.
a) Import the Workload Data File.
This data file contains the information for each workload in the migration wave: vCenter hosting the workload,
migration wave name, and mobility Ggroup for the workload.
The imported file must be from the same vCenter Server where VCF Operations HCX is deployed. For example, if
the source VCF Operations HCX is deployed on vCenter Server 1, the imported wave file must include workloads
from vCenter Server 1. This means workloads in a wave file from vCenter Server 2 will be reported as non-existent
on the VCF Operations HCX.
b) (Optional) Import the Network Dependencies File.
The network dependencies file lists the networks that the workloads connect to in the vCenter Server. The Network
Dependencies file is optional for initially importing the migration wave workloads and can be imported later in the
process.
5. After uploading the files, click Import Migration Wave.
As part of this step, VCF Operations HCX performs various validation checks of the imported migration wave data
against the actual workloads in the vCenter Server.
Following validation, the Migration Planning Screen appears. For migration waves that are imported manually, the
Wave Source column displays CSV.
For migration waves that sync directly from VCF Operations for networks, the Wave Source column displays VCF
Operations for networks.
Broadcom 6677

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Review the Status column.
The status column can have the following values following the import operation. For a complete list of status values,
see Monitoring Migration Waves.
Status
Validating Indicates that validation checks are in progress. For large
migration waves, validation can take several minutes.
Validation Failed VCF Operations HCX performs a number of validations on the
migration wave information in the CSV files against the contents
of the source vCenter Server. A mismatch in the information
can cause a failure. For example, if a workload included in the
migration wave, or a network listed in the network data file are
no longer present in the vCenter Server, a failure can occur.
If a failure occurs, you can modify the migration wave in VCF
Operations for networks and re-import the files.
Ready Indicates that all groups in the migration wave have passed the
validation checks and the wave can be committed for migration.
Committing/Committed Indicates that the migration wave has passed validation, mobility
groups have been created in VCF Operations HCX, and those
groups are ready for configuration. migration waves synced
directly from VCF Operations for networks are automatically set to
Committed state after passing validation.
For migrations waves manually added in VCF Operations HCX
and that are in Ready state, you must take action to commit the
migration wave for migration.
7. For entries in Ready state, click the vertical ellipsis next to the migration wave name and select Commit Migration
Wave.
With this action, mobility groups are created in Draft state once the migration wave commit is successful.
The imported migration wave appears in the Mobility Planning screen. For more information, see Monitoring Migration
Waves.
Next, follow the procedure to configure and schedule the mobility group workloads included in the migration wave and,
when ready, run the migrations. See Migrate Mobility Group Workloads in Migration Waves.
Migrate Mobility Group Workloads in Migration Waves
This section describes the procedure for configuring and migrating mobility groups in migration waves.
• The migration service is activated in both the source and destination site compute profile.
• The migration service is activated in the Service Mesh.
• Information regarding each migration type is reviewed and understood. For more information, see Migration Types.
The process for migrating mobility groups in migrations waves has three high-level steps:
1. For each group in each migration wave, configure the mobility groups.
2. Run the pre-migration checks.
3. Run the migrations.
Follow this procedure to configure and run the migrations.
1. In the VCF Operations HCX UI, navigate to Migration.
The Migration screen appears. Synced migration waves appear in the Wave Source column as VCF Operations for
networks. Manually imported migration waves appear in the Wave Source source column as CSV.
Broadcom 6678

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Review the Status column for each migration wave.
Synced migration waves that have passed validation appear with the status Committed. Manually imported migration
waves that have passed validation appear in the display as Ready.
For a complete list of migration wave states, see Monitoring Migration Waves.
3. For entries in Ready state, click the vertical ellipsis next to the migration wave name and select Commit Migration
Wave.
A pop-up screen prompts you to commit the wave. With this action, the migration wave state changes to Committed.
For either synced or manually imported migration waves, committing these waves creates the mobility groups for
migration and validates they are ready for configuration.
4. (Optional) To review the mobility group and network information for each migration wave, click the verticial ellipsisnext
to the migration wave name and select View Details.
The specific migration wave screen appears with tabs for viewing Migration and network extension data. For more
information, see Monitoring Migration Waves.
5. To configure and schedule mobility groups for migration, click the name of a committed migration wave.
The system displays the list of mobility groups in the migration wave along with the current status of each group and
the number of workloads in each group.
For newly committed migration waves, all groups will appear in Not Configured state.
Broadcom 6679

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
Mobility groups can appear in various states if those groups were subject to prior configuration attempts. For more
information about the mobility group workload status, see Monitoring Mobility Group Activity for Migration Waves.
6. For mobility group entries in Not Configured or Partially Configured state, click the vertical ellipsis and select
Configure Mobility Group.
Note:
The Select VMs for Migration button is not available for migration waves. Once a migration wave is committed
for migration, mobility groups are created and the associated workloads cannot be changed.
7. (Optional) If Supervisor Onboarding is selected, you must configure the Supervisor Namespace and Storage Class.
8. Enter your group Transfer and Placement, Switchover, and Interconnect service mesh selection, along with any
Extended options.
For a group to move to Configured state, all mandatory fields must be completed:
• Destination compute container
• Destination storage
• Migration type (profile)
• Disk provisioning format (Virtual Disk Format)
• Destination network for each VM for migration
These settings, except for the destination network, apply to all members of the group by default. To override the
default settings for specific virtual machines in the group, select and expand the virtual machine entry and set different
options.
For additional information regarding the Extended options, see Additional Migration Settings.
Note:
• For HCX Assisted vMotion (Direct), the Interconnect service mesh selection is not available.
• You can set the Switchover and Transfer schedule for Bulk, Replication Assisted vMotion (RAV), or OS
Assisted Migration (OSAM) migrations. Transfer scheduling is not available for vMotion, HCX Assisted vMotion
(Direct), or Cold migration.
The Transfer schedule identifies the date and time when base synchronization to the destination site begins.
The Switchover schedule defines the date and time when the final data synchronization occurs and the
workload is switched over to the destination site.
• Extended Options provide additional settings.
Broadcom 6680

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
9. Select the destination network for each virtual machine to be migrated:
In most cases, the extended network between the source and destination sites is automatically selected. You can
change this selection as needed.
Important:
VMs connected to standard port groups must be explicitly mapped to the target networks.
a) Expand each virtual machine selection.
b) Next to each guest virtual machine NIC name, click the folder for a list of available target networks.
c) Select the checkbox next to the network that you want the guest virtual machine to map to, and then click Select.
d) (Optional) To specify a new guest OS IP address for the virtual machine at the target network, expand the NIC
entry and enter the new IP address, gateway, and subnet mask.
10.To complete the mobility group configuration, click Save or Close.
Saving the configuration changes the group status to the Partially Configured or Configured state. Groups in
Configured state are ready for validation checking and migration.
Attention:
You do not have to configure every group in the migration wave, but only groups in the Configured state can be
migrated. Other groups in the migration wave can be configured later.
11.When one or more groups in the migration wave is configured, click Continue to Pre-Migration Checks.
The Run Pre-Migration Checks screen appears. The display includes the list of mobility group names and group
status, and number of workloads in each group.
12.For groups in Configured state, click Run Checks.
The system validates the configurations and reports any errors in the Error column along with specific information
about the error. Errors must be resolved before the migration can proceed.
13.When the validation succeeds, click Continue to Run Migrations.
The Run Migration screen appears. The display includes the list of mobility groups, group status, and number of
workloads. If a migration is in progress, it displays information regarding the syncing and Switchover status. For
completed migrations, the screen shows the number of workloads that migrated successfully and the number that
encountered an error.
Mobility groups displaying the Run action, have passed pre-migration checks and are ready for migration.
Broadcom 6681

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
14.To start a group migration, click Run.
The system prompts you to validate the group information.
15.If validation succeeds, click Start Migrations.
The migrations begins and the mobility groups status changes to In-progress.
This completes the process for migrating mobility groups in migration waves.
For information about monitoring mobility groups and migration activity, see Monitoring Mobility Group Activity for
Migration Waves. For information about managing mobility groups, including available group actions, see Managing
Mobility Groups for Migration Waves.
Monitoring Mobility Group Activity for Migration Waves
All mobility group and individual workload migration information for a migration wave is available through the Migration
Planning interface.
Each migration wave is composed of one or more mobility groups. At any point, you can check the status of mobility group
migrations, the status of each group, and the status of individual VMs.
Note:
Migration waves must be in the Committed state before mobility groups are available for migration. For more
information, see Import and Commit Migration Waves.
For a list of actions available for managing mobility groups in a migration wave, see Managing Mobility Groups for
Migration Waves.
Monitor Mobility Group Migrations
To display a summary list of mobility group migration activity for a migration wave, select a migration wave name in the
migration planning screen, and then click Run Migrations.
The display includes the list of mobility groups, group status, and number of workloads. If a migration is in progress,
it displays information regarding the Syncing and Switchover status. For completed migrations, the screen shows the
number of workloads that migrated successfully and the number that encountered an error.
Mobility groups displaying the Run action, are fully configured, have passed pre-migration checks, and are ready for
migration.
To view detailed information regarding migrated workloads that appear in the Errored column, expand the mobility group
and review the VM details. For workloads in a failed state, click the information icon to see details about the failure. For
more information regarding workload status, refer to "Monitor Mobility Group Workloads" in this section.
Monitor Mobility Group Status
To display the list of mobility groups for a committed migration wave, select a migration wave name in the Migration
Planning screen. The list of mobility groups appears in the display along with the group status and number of workloads in
each group of the migration wave.
Broadcom 6682

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Mobility groups can be in one of the following states:
Group Status Description
Not Configured Indicates that no group information has been configured. This
is the initial (draft) state for mobility groups in newly committed
migration waves.
Partially Configured Indicates that the configuration effort for workloads in the
mobility Group has started but is not yet complete, and that the
configuration has been saved for later editing.
Configured Indicates that the mobility group information has been fully
configured.
Queued Indicates that the migration has started, and that scheduled
migrations are pending the start time.
In-Progress Indicates migrations for the group have started.
Completed Indicates that migration is completed for that group.
Error Indicates that one or more workloads in the mobility group have
configuration errors which were detected during the pre-migration
checks. You must edit the mobility group configuration before
migrations can proceed.
Canceled Indicates that the migration operation has been canceled.
To display the migration status for a mobility group, select Run Migrations and expand the mobility group. Then select
the Mobility Group Details tab to see the overall group migration information. This information includes the number of
workloads in the group and the total resource requirements. These details also include the transfer percentage for the
entire group and the number of workloads migrated.
Monitor Mobility Group Workloads
For each mobility group in the migration wave, you can view the current status of each workload in the group. To view the
workload status, expand each mobility group.
The workload display includes the workload name, migration technology (if configured), workload status (Progress),
configured initial sync (transfer) schedule, and switchover schedule.
Broadcom 6683

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Mobility group workloads can be in one of the following states:
Group Workload Status Description
Not Configured Indicates that workload configuration has not started.
Partially Configured Indicates that the workload configuration requires additional setup.
Configured Indicates that the mobility group configuration is complete and
the workloads in the group are ready for migration. Indicates that
the workload configuration is complete. If all the workloads of the
group are configured, then the group status is configured and
ready for migration.
Queued Indicates that the workload is scheduled for migration and pending
the Initial Sync time.
Migration Started Indicates the workload migrations for the group have started.
Migration Parked If the migration is waiting for other migration workloads or tasks, it
Migration Parked with Errors moves to Migration Parked state until resources are available for
the migration to continue.
If some migrations in the mobility group are parked and some
migrations have failed, then the overall status for group becomes
parked with errors.

This can occur due to maintenance at the destination site or

You can retry the migration at another time.

The migration is completed.

You must edit the mobility group configuration before migrations
can proceed.

Monitoring Migration Waves
The migration wave status reflects overall wave status for both pre-commit and post-commit activity.
Migration waves are initially imported either manually as CSV files exported from VCF Operations for networks, or directly
synced from VCF Operations for networks. Migration wave data is validated against the vCenter Server.
If the validation is successful, manually imported migration waves enter a pre-commit, or Ready state, after which these
waves can be committed for migration. Migration waves that are directly synced from VCF Operations for networks can go
to either Committed or Validation Failed state depending on the outcome of the validation process.
Broadcom 6684

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
In the post-commit state, information from the imported migration waves is used to create the mobility groups and
associated workloads for migration.
Each migration wave can have multiple mobility groups. While each mobility group can be configured and migrated
independently of other groups in a migration wave, the status of the migration wave itself is dependent on the combined
status of all mobility groups in the migration wave. For example, the status of a migration wave is not considered complete
until all mobility groups in the wave have reached a terminal state, meaning successful, failed, or canceled migrations.
Migration waves can have the following status:
Migration Wave Status Description
Validation Failed (Pre-commit) Indicates that the imported migration wave did not
pass validation. For manually imported migration waves, the error
must be fixed in the CSV file and then re-imported.
If validation fails for migration waves that are synced from VCF
Operations for networks, you must fix the error in VCF Operations
for networks.
Ready (Pre-commit) Indicates that validation was successful for the
manually imported migration wave files and the wave can be
committed.
Commiting/Commited (Post-commit) Indicates that the migration wave is committed and
the migration groups have been prepared for configuration.
Execution In Progress (Post commit) Indicates the state of migrations in the mobility
groups for the migration wave.
Concluding/Concluded (Post commit) Indicates that all mobility groups operations for the
migration wave have terminated to some state. The migration
wave is no longer available for migrating workloads and is is now
in a read-only mode.
Deleting (Post commit)
Expand a migration wave to see additional details:
Broadcom 6685

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To view mobility group and and network extension information for each migration wave, click the vertical ellipsis next to
each migration wave name and select View Details.
For migration waves in a pre-commit state, the Migrations tab provides summary information about each group in the
wave, including the number of workloads, resource requirements, and validation status. To view information about each
workload in the group, expand the mobility group.
Note:
If the mobility group is in a Validation Failed state, you can expand the group to display workload information that
is related to the failure.
For migration waves in a post-commit state, the Migrations tab displays mobility group information at each point in the
migration wave timeline. In Configure & Schedule Mobility Groups, you can expand a group to see individual workload
information or click the vertical ellipsis to take action on the mobility group. In Run Pre-Migrations Check, you can expand
the group to see summary migration status information for the group and VMs, or click the vertical ellipsis to take action on
the mobility group.
Broadcom 6686

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To display network information for the migration Wave, click the Network Extensions tab. As part of migration wave
validation, the system checks whether the network is present in the vCenter Server and then lists whether the network is
extended or not. If the network validation fails, the system displays a message about the error.
Note:
If validation fails, click the information icon to get details about the issue.

Managing Mobility Groups for Migration Waves
For committed migration waves, you can select from a number of actions to manage mobility groups and individual
workloads.
Managing Mobility Groups for Migration Waves
To display the list of mobility groups for a committed migration wave, click a migration wave name from the Migration
Planning screen. The system displays the list of mobility groups along with the three high-level steps comprising the
migration timeline:

• Run pre-migration checks.

Migrating Virtual Machines with Mobility Groups
You can assemble one or more virtual machines into logical sets, for execution and monitoring of migrations as a group.
• General:
– The migration service is activated in both the source and destination site compute profile.
Broadcom 6689

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
– The migration service is activated in the service mesh.
– Information regarding each migration type is reviewed and understood. For more information, refer to Migration
Types.
– VMware Operations HCX migration of Photon OS-based VMs is not supported.
Note:
For information related to migrating mobility groups that are created as part of a migration wave, see About
Migrating Mobility Groups from Migration Waves.
With mobility groups, you have the flexibility to manage migrations for sets of virtual machines by application, network,
pod, or other aspects of your environment.
Review the following considerations for migrating workloads:
• For paired vSphere-based sites, migrations are always started from the source site. For non-vSphere site pairs,
migrations are always from the non-vSphere site to the destination site.
• The VCF Operations HCX system automatically detects virtual machine disk additions or removals and reconfigures
running migrations to accommodate these changes. These disk changes are honored only if the changes occur before
the migration switchover phase. If disk changes occur during the switchover phase, the changes are not recognized,
which can affect the success of the migration operation. Support for adding or removing disks is available only with
Bulk and Replication Assisted vMotion migrations.
• Taking snapshots of a VM during migration, either manually or using a third-party backup solution, can disrupt the
migration process. To prevent any impact, it is required to stop those services that may create or remove snapshots
during migration. Refer to KB79220 for more information.
• For Bulk, vMotion, and RAV migration types, you can select a service mesh to use for migration operations. For each
site pair, you can have one or more service meshes. Each service mesh configuration has a specific resource and
network configuration. In some cases, you might choose a specific service mesh to use for migrations based on
the mesh configuration. If no service mesh is selected for migration, VCF Operations HCX automatically selects the
service mesh to use. To add a service mesh for a site pair, see Configuring the Service Mesh.
• VCF Operations HCX refreshes the VM inventory every five minutes. When selecting VMs for the mobility group, VCF
Operations HCX provides filters for listing the VMs by cluster, VMs, storage, and networking. The networking filter
displays VMs by the network to which they are attached, including DVPG-backed networks, NSX segments, and VPC
subnets.
• When selecting the destination network in the migration configuration wizard, note that VCF Operations HCX allows
migrations from NSX VPC subnets at the source site to VPC or non-VPC subnets at the destination site. Likewise, you
can migrate VMs from non-VPC subnets at the source site to VPC subnets at the destination site.
Note:
The selectable service mesh option requires that both the source and destination sites run HCX 4.8 or later.
For the operational limits supported with VCF Operations HCX migrations, see Configuration and Service Limits.
1. In the VCF Operations HCX UI, navigate to Migration.
2. Click Create Mobility Group.
3. Select a source site and a destination site for the migration.
VCF Operations HCX displays the inventory of virtual machine workloads that are available for migration and that can

Monitor Mobility Group and Workload Migrations
All mobility group and individual workload migration information, regardless of the source of that migration (migration wave
or non-wave) is available through the Migration interface.
From the Migration interface, you can monitor summary group information, individual group information, and workload-
specific configuration and migration details.
For information related to managing mobility groups, including editing, deleting, canceling and retrying migrations, see
Manage Mobility Groups. For information related to managing group workloads, see Manage Mobility Group Workloads.
Note:
The Migration interface includes an Auto Refresh option which updates mobility group and individual workload
migration status every 30 seconds. This setting persists across all migration management screens and resets only
when moving to other VCF Operations HCX Infrastructure, Services, or Administration operations.

Estimate Migrations with Mobility Groups
Using the VCF Operations HCX predictive estimation feature, you can estimate the migration phase transfer for Bulk and
Replication Assisted vMotion (RAV) migration types, and the relocation phase transfer for vMotion migrations.
Predictive estimation has the following requirements:
• At least 50 successfully completed migrations. Predictive estimates for both forward and reverse migrations requires at
least 50 successful migrations in each direction.
• The mobility group is in Draft state.
• The mobility group has been validated successfully.
• Migration prediction is available only for datastores and HCX-IX appliances that have participated in the previous
migrations to train the machine learning model.
For Bulk and Replication Assisted vMotion (RAV) migrations, VCF Operations HCX can generate real-time estimates
regarding the migration transfer phase. For vMotion migrations, this includes real-time estimates regarding the relocation
phase. Real-time estimation gathers information from the current migration environment. This estimate is based on
sampling the underlying metrics of the environment, such as bytes transferred, rate of transfer, network throughput, and
number of disks. Changes in the underlying metrics can impact the estimate. The interval between estimates varies with
the size of the migrated virtual machine:
Virtual Machine Size Estimate Interval
Less than 50 GB Every 1.5 minutes
Greater than or equal to 50 GB but less than 1 TB Every 5 minutes
Greater than or equal to 1 TB Every 15 minutes
Broadcom 6697

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
The estimate interval begins after the system has gathered the underlying metrics and completed calculations,
meaning there may appear to be a delay in presenting the initial estimate. For relatively small transfers, the
transfer may complete before providing an estimate.
For Bulk and RAV migrations, VCF Operations HCX provides predictive estimates for mobility groups in Draft state.
Predictive estimation uses historical data from completed migrations in combination with machine learning (ML) to
estimate the transfer phase.
To generate and view migration estimate, review these steps:
1. Navigate to Services > Migration.
2. For groups with Bulk, RAV, or vMotion migration types, click a group name.
VCF Operations HCX displays the list of workloads in the group.
3. Expand the Actions menu, and select .
Get Predictions
For Bulk and Replication Assisted vMotion migrations, the Progress column provides a best-effort, real-time estimation
of the time required to complete the transfer phase for a specific virtual machine. For vMotion migrations, the Progress
column provides a real-time estimate to complete the relocation phase.
For each estimate in the Progress column, an information icon provides the prediction details and the estimated time in
minutes and seconds for the most recent prediction.
Viewing Migration Event Details
When migrating content between paired sites, VCF Operations HCX performs a detailed set of actions that are visible in
the system as migration events.
Viewing these events provides diagnostic information about the migration. This information provides the detailed migration
workflow, the state of the migration, how long the migration remains in a certain state, and whether the migration
has succeeded or failed. Understanding what is happening at any point in the migration can provide insight into what
infrastructure or configuration changes might be necessary to address any migration issues that might occur.
HCX displays event information for all migration types.
Events are listed in the order performed. Migration events are separated by the migration phase:
• Transfer Events
• Switchover Events
• Cleanup Events
During the transfer phase, a base synchronization of source VM data takes place with additional transfers over time. The
transfer phase can take time based on the amount of data being transferred and the network performance.
During the Switchover phase, HCX halts mobility operations on the source VM, and performs a final synchronization of the
source data to the destination site.
During the Cleanup phase, HCX completes post migration actions at the source and the destination sites as necessary.
Note:
For migrations older than 30 days, VCF Operations HCX clears the history of events from the system
automatically. For migrations that you archive using the Archive operation, the migration data is saved but the
event history is cleared from the system.

The interface displays a list of workloads associated with the group.

The interface displays the configuration settings and migration events for that virtual machine.

Use the refresh button to update the list of events. Destination events are highlighted. Each event provides an offset
time from the Start event. Events that are more than 24 hours old include a date stamp.
Note:
While the migration is in progress, the system provides options for managing the migration, including scheduling
the migration switchover, canceling the migration, or forcing a power off. For more information about the available
actions, see Managing Migrations.
When migration is complete, cleanup event messages indicate that the source and destination sides of the migration have
been cleaned up and the migration is complete.
Additional Migration Settings
The HCX migration interface provides a set of options that can be used to tailor the behaviors and conditions of the virtual
machine before or after the migration operation.
HCX has several types of optional settings for use when migrating virtual machines: Switchover, Virtual Machine, and
Extended.
Note:
The available options depend on the selected migration type.
Switchover Options
Switchover options are applied during the switchover phase of the migration. Except for the Force Power-Off VM setting,
which can be set on an individual virtual machine (VM) migration, these options are set globally for a group of selected
VMs.
Force Power-Off VM By default, HCX attempts to shut down the virtual machine guest gracefully during the HCX Bulk migration
operation. If the OS interrupts the termination process, the migration operation fails. Checking this option
causes HCX to force the power-off.
Remove Snapshots Causes HCX to consolidate snapshot files during migration of the virtual machine. For more information,
see Understanding Virtual Machine Snapshots During Migrations.
Broadcom 6699

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Force Unmount ISO Causes HCX to remove mounted ISO images before migrating the virtual machine.
Images
Expedited Switchover Reduces migration downtime by bypassing the final offline sync, and immediately recovering the VM at the
(applied during bulk destination after the VM at the source is powered off.
migration only.) Drag the slider to indicate an acceptable data loss. For example, the last 30 minutes of data.
Guest Shutdown Indicates the wait interval for the guest shutdown for bulk migration switchover. Shut down a VM gracefully
Timeout before migrating by specifying an interval of between 5 - 30 minutes.
Virtual Machine Options
The virtual machine (VM) options are available only for individual VM migration.
Enable Seed If a migration is unsuccessful or canceled, Seed Checkpoint retains the target disks that are created at the
Checkpoint target site. Without Seed Checkpoint, the HCX rollback process cleans up the target disks created during
the migration and all transferred data is lost. Seed Checkpoint is available with HCX Bulk Migration and
Replication Assisted vMotion.
Note:
To resume from the migration checkpoint, select Enable Seed Checkpoint when you restart the
migration. If the Seed Checkpoint option is not selected, the migration creates new disks at the
target site and ignores the existing checkpoint.
To use this option, select a specific datastore for migration and not a datastore cluster.
Restarting a Seed Checkpoint migration to a new datastore creates additional target disks on that
datastore, and saves new checkpoint information related to that datastore with the virtual machine data in
HCX.
Extended Options
Extended options customize the characteristics of the migrated virtual machine without having to manually update the
settings after migration. Extended options can be set globally for a group of virtual machines migrations or for an individual
virtual machine.
Retain MAC Causes a virtual machine to keep its current MAC address during HCX Bulk migration operation, allowing
communications to resume gracefully, and honors MAC-based security policies. This option is selected by
default for vMotion and Replication Assisted vMotion migration types and cannot be changed.
Upgrade Virtual Allows HCX to upgrade virtual machine hardware to the latest supported version as part of the migration
Hardware operation, making current virtual machine hardware features immediately available to the migrated virtual
machine.
Upgrade VMware Tools Allows HCX to upgrade VMware Tools to the latest supported version as part of the migration operation,
making current VMware Tools features immediately available to bulk migrated virtual machine.
Deactivate Per Virtual vSphere Enhanced vMotion Compatibility (EVC) ensures that workloads can be live migrated, using
Machine EVC vMotion, between ESX hosts in a cluster that is running different CPU generations. EVC is a cluster level
setting that supports virtual machine mobility within a cluster. For virtual machines implementing per-
VM EVC, the EVC mode becomes an attribute of the virtual machine rather than the specific processor
generation it happens to be booted on in the cluster. If this option is selected then this virtual machine might
not be able to vMotion back to the source site.
Host Name Sets the host name of the migrated virtual machines at the destination site.
Domain Name Sets the domain name for the virtual machine at the destination site. This option is available only with Linux
virtual machines.
Personalization Script Uploads a customization script to a migrated virtual machine. The script runs before and after guest
customization. The customization script cannot exceed 1500 characters.
For Linux VMs, Guest Customization using the Personalization Script option requires VMware Tools version
10.1.0 or later. See VMware KB 74880.

In the VMware Tools configuration, the enable-custom-scripts option is deactivated by default for
