Managing Service Accounts in VCF Automation
You can automate the access of third-party applications to VCF Automation by using service accounts. Service accounts
provide secure, API-based, non-interactive access, which is essential for integrating external systems and running
automated tasks.
Service Account Visibility
If you want to limit the service account information that users can see, you can grant to certain roles only the Service
Account: Simple View right. When a user with only the Service Account: Simple View right makes a GET request on a
service account, the , , , and properties return as . Users with the full
softwareId softwareVersion uri status null
right can see all properties.
Service Account: View
Broadcom 7038

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Authorization Process
To provide automated access to VCF Automation, service accounts use the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC
8628). After the authorization flow completes, the client application receives an OAuth refresh token and an initial access
token (JWT) for its first VCF Automation session. Applications use the refresh token to request new access tokens for
subsequent API calls.
The authorization process steps:
1. The client application sends a device authorization request to the VCF Automation device endpoint and receives a
and a human-readable .
device_code user_code
2. The client application provides the to a system administrator through a separate communication channel,
user_code
such as a secure message or an IT ticket.
3. A user with the right logs in to VCF Automation, navigates to the service account, and
Service Account: Manage
approves or denies the request by confirming the . VCF Automation delivers the resulting refresh token
user_code
exclusively to the client application that initiated the request. The token is not accessible through any management
API, and no other actor, including administrators, can retrieve it.
4. The client application polls the token endpoint with the until the request reaches the state.
device_code GRANTED
5. When the grant is confirmed, the token endpoint issues the OAuth refresh token and an initial access token (JWT) for
immediate use.
6. For subsequent API sessions, the client application exchanges its refresh token for a new access token (JWT) at the
token endpoint.
Managed Service Accounts
You can designate a service account as managed by a parent service account by using the property.
managedBy
Managed service accounts support the JWT Bearer grant ( ),
urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer
which allows the parent service account to obtain tokens for a child account programmatically without an interactive
device flow. Standard service accounts support only the device authorization grant type.
Token Rotation
The property controls token rotation for service account refresh tokens. Unused service account refresh
tokenRotation
tokens never expire unless you explicitly revoke them.
tokenRotation Value Behavior
ALWAYS The refresh token rotates automatically on every use.
NEVER The refresh token never rotates.
ONCE_ON_NEXT_LOGIN The token rotates on the next authentication, and then the setting
automatically resets to NEVER.
NONE The rotation is not configured.
Roles
Service accounts support multiple roles through the roles array property. When registering with the VCF Automation
OAuth endpoint, specify roles in the scope property as space-separated URL-encoded URNs in the format
[roleName].
urn:vcloud:role:
Broadcom 7039

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Service Account Statuses
The status property reflects the state of the OAuth refresh token. This property is visible only to users with the
Service
right.
Account: View
Status Description
CREATED The account is in its initial state after creation. No refresh token
exists and no device authorization requests exist.
REQUESTED One or more device authorization requests are outstanding. No
refresh token exists.
GRANTED An administrator grants an outstanding request. The client
application must poll the token endpoint to retrieve the refresh
token.
ACTIVE The client application retrieves its refresh token and can
authenticate with VCF Automation.
You can use the and actions only when the account is in the state. You can revoke access when
Grant Deny REQUESTED
the account is in the or state.
GRANTED ACTIVE
Restrictions
Because service accounts provide third-party application access, they have restrictions when authenticated:
• Cannot create API tokens. The API token management right is not available to service account sessions.
• Cannot manage arbitrary service accounts. A service account can manage only itself and the service accounts it
directly owns through the property.
managedBy
Create a Service Account Using Your VCF Automation Provider Management UI
You can create an account for automated access to VCF Automation by using the Provider Management UI.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, click Access Control.
3. Click the Service Accounts tab, and click New.
4. Enter a name for the service account.
5. From the Assign Role drop-down menu, select a role for the service account.
The list of available roles comprises the local system organization roles or if you are in another organization, the global
roles published to the organization in addition to any local roles in the organization.
6. Enter a software ID for the service account or generate and enter one using the Generate Software ID button.
Service accounts must have software IDs which are unique identifiers, in UUID format, representing the software that
is connecting to VCF Automation. This ID would be the same for all versions and instances of a piece of software.
For larger solutions, to retain control over the identity of your service accounts, do not use the Generate Software ID
option, and generate your own software ID.
7. Optional: (Optional) Enter the software version of the system using the service account.
The software version is an optional vendor-specified informational piece of metadata that is associated with the service
account. To track when a piece of software changes, VCF Automation uses the software version. The software version
might be useful for identifying a service account.
8. Optional: (Optional) Enter a client URI.

Generate an API Access Token Using Your VCF Automation Provider Management UI
Generate an API access token to authenticate automation against VCF Automation. You can use API access tokens with
your existing authentication methods, including two-factor authentication.
Authenticating with an API token uses the Refreshing an Access Token standard specified in OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749
Section 6 to grant access to VCF Automation as an OAuth application. The API token you generate in this procedure
serves as the refresh token in the OAuth 2.0 exchange. The API returns a new, standard VCF Automation access token.
Client applications use this token to authenticate subsequent API calls to VCF Automation.
To make an OAuth 2.0 RFC-compliant request, familiarize yourself with Request for Comments (RFC) 6749 Section 6
information about refreshing an access token.
Access tokens are artifacts that client applications use to make API requests on behalf of a user. Applications need
access tokens for authentication. When an access token expires, to obtain access tokens, applications can use API
tokens. By default, API tokens expire after 90 days.
Broadcom 7043

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
When using access tokens, applications cannot perform certain tasks.
• Change the user password
• Perform user management tasks
• Create more tokens
• View or revoke other tokens
When accessing VCF Automation by using an API access token, applications have only view rights for the following
resources.
• User
• Group
• Roles
• Global roles
• Rights bundles
Applications accessing VCF Automation by using an API access token do not have the following rights.
• Token: Manage
• Token: Manage All
Similar to generating a user API token, you can create a service account by using the VCF Automation API. The API
request for creating a service account uses the same API endpoint as creating a user API token, but the presence of the
field indicates the intent to create a service account.
software_id

2. In the upper right corner of the navigation bar, click your user name, and click My Account.
3. Under the API Tokens section, click New.
4. Enter a name for the token, and click Create.
The generated API token appears. You must copy the token because it appears only once. After you click OK, you
cannot retrieve this token again, you can only revoke it.
5. Make an OAuth 2.0 RFC-compliant request to the site.cloud.example.com
https:// /oauth/provider/
API endpoint.

Enable Cross-Organization Content Sharing in the VCF Automation Provider
Management UI
You can enable specific organizations to share catalog items, such as blueprints, VCF Operations orchestrator workflows,
and VM images, as well as content library VM images, with other organizations in your VCF Automation environment.
Verify that you have at least one provider content library in your environment. See Create a Content Library.
Broadcom 7045

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI as a system administrator.
2. In the left navigation pane, click Access Control.
3. Click the Rights Bundles tab.
4. Click the Privileged Organization Access Bundle name, and click Publish.
The Privileged Organization Access Bundle includes the Organization: View All Organizations and Share
content with other organizations rights to enable content sharing. Granting the Organization: View All
Organizations right enables an organization to view and list the available set of organizations in VCF Automation.
Granting the Share content with other organizations right, enables the organization to share content. By default,
VCF Automation publishes the Privileged Organization Access Bundle only to the provider consumption
organization, if one exists.
5. Turn on the Publish to Tenants toggle.
6. Select the organizations to which you want to publish the role.
• If you want to publish the bundle to all existing and newly created organizations in your system, select Publish to
All Tenants.
• If you want to publish the bundle to specific organizations in your system, select the organizations individually.
7. Click Save.
To stop an organization from sharing its content with other organizations, deselect the organization from the list of
organizations to which the Privileged Organization Access Bundle is published.
Important:
When you unpublish the rights bundle from an organization with shared items or delete such an organization,
the catalog items are no longer visible to other organizations. The copied VM images remain available to all
organizations because they are copied to the provider content library.
When you log in to an organization by using the Launch Organization Portal button in the Provider Management UI,
even if the organization does not have the necessary rights published, you can see the options to share catalog images
and VM images to other organizations. The options appear because users with system administrator credentials have
all VCF Automation rights, including sharing content across organizations. Because VCF Automation performs rights
bundle validations, you can share only VM images as a system administrator in the organization context. If the rights
bundle is not published to the organization, organization administrators cannot see the options to share catalog images
and VM images to other organizations.

For more information about the terms and components of VCF Automation Provider Management, see Overview of VCF
Automation Provider Management.

You must have the system administrator rights to access the Provider Management UI.

The Provider Management UI URL opens the login screen for the
https://vcfa.example.com/provider

admin
and the password which you set up during the installation.
• After you log in, if there are more than 25 minutes of inactivity, you are automatically logged out of the VCF Automation

• Integrate your VCF Automation with one or more external identity providers (IdPs), and import users and groups to

Quick Start Your VCF Automation Setup
You can go through a simplified wizard for the creation of an organization for all applications with certain predefined
settings. Quick Start is an alternative to manually setting up all aspects of your first organization in VCF Automation.
• Verify that you complete the VMware Cloud Foundation wizard for setting up your vCenter and NSX infrastructure. See
Getting Started with VMware Cloud Foundation.
• Verify that the matching NSX Manager for the Supervisor is registered in your environment. See View and Manage
Your NSX Manager Instances.
• Verify that you have a Tier-0 gateway or Tier-0 VRF gateway created in NSX Manager. For instructions on creating
a Tier-0 gateway, see Add an NSX Tier-0 Gateway. For instructions on creating a Tier-0 VRF gateway, see Step 4 in
Deploy an NSX VRF-Lite with BGP.
Note:
If you want to add a Tier-0 gateway that is backed by a VRF gateway in NSX, you must also create a VRF
gateway that is linked to the Tier-0 gateway.
• Verify that your vCenter instance has a Supervisor with VPC networking enabled. See Deploying Supervisor with VCF
Networking with VPC.
• Verify that you have edge clusters configured and available in your environment.
You have two primary options when setting up your tenant organization:
• The Quick Start is designed for efficiency by automatically creating a fully functional tenant organization along with
all the necessary resources. The Quick Start is the recommended choice for single-tenant setups or exploring and
testing VCF Automation. You can modify the resulting organization for production use.
• The Manual Setup appears as a check list of tasks in the UI and is intended to remind you of the tasks that you must
carry out to realize the full capabilities of the Provider Management UI. When you complete a task, it automatically
turns into a check mark.
Important:
The Quick Start is not applicable to VLAN-backed environments, which are supported in VCF Automation 9.1.1
and later. To use the Quick Start option, you must have a full-stack Supervisor. For VLAN-backed environments,
use the Manual Setup option, see Manually Set Up Your VCF Automation.
Creating an organization by using the Quick Start option does not have any limitations compared to the Manual Setup
and you can change the configuration of the organization after its creation.
You can use the Quick Start option only once. The Quick Start option disappears after you set up the first organization
and region either through the Quick Start or the Manual Setup options. The Quick Start uses the first available tier-0
gateway in NSX, and creates a provider gateway for that tier-0. To create an IP space, VCF Automation uses an IPv4
block with external visibility in NSX. If you want to ensure that VCF Automation uses the tier-0 gateway and IP blocks
generated during the workload domain configuration, do not add any additional tier-0 gateways or IP blocks. When
creating the organization, VCF Automation automatically sets up the organization's quota and networking, including the
transit gateway and VPC.
Broadcom 7047

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. Under Quick Start, click Get Started.
3. Enter a name for your first organization, and click Next.
4. Enter a name for the region, and select a Supervisor.
The list shows all available Supervisors for this NSX Manager instance.
5. Click Next.

The list shows all storage classes across the selected Supervisors.

The Organization Provisioning in Progress dialog opens where you can view and follow the creation process.
8. When the task finishes, click OK.

• To finish setting up the organization, you can use the first user details to log in to the Organization UI by navigating to
FQDN_VCF_Automation. See Organization Management.

• Create content libraries at the provider level or directly within the organization. See Create a Content Library in the
Provider Management guide or Managing Content Libraries in VCF Automation in the Organization Management
guide.

Manually Set Up Your VCF Automation
To realize the full capabilities of the Provider Management UI you must set up VCF Automation.
• Verify that you complete the VMware Cloud Foundation wizard for setting up your vCenter and NSX infrastructure. See
Getting Started with VMware Cloud Foundation.
• Verify that the matching NSX Manager for the Supervisor is registered in your environment.
• To use and configure centralized connections, verify that you have a Tier-0 gateway or Tier-0 VRF gateway created
in NSX Manager. For instructions on creating a Tier-0 gateway, see Add an NSX Tier-0 Gateway. For instructions on
creating a Tier-0 VRF gateway, see Step 4 in Deploy an NSX VRF-Lite with BGP.
Note:
If you want to add a Tier-0 gateway that is backed by a VRF gateway in NSX, you must also create a VRF
gateway that is linked to the Tier-0 gateway.
• To use and configure distributed connections, verify that you have a VLAN configured in your infrastructure.
• Verify that your vCenter instance has a Supervisor with VPC networking enabled. See Deploying Supervisor with VCF
Networking with VPC.
When you set up the necessary infrastructure, Organization Administrators can use the first user credentials, that you

Viewing and Managing Your Infrastructure Resources in VCF Automation
VCF Automation derives its resources from an underlying virtual infrastructure. VCF Automation displays the vCenter and
NSX Manager instances discovered from VCF Operations that you can view and manage.
VCF Automation uses one or more vCenter environments to back its regions. Each vCenter instance must have at least
one Supervisor enabled.
Note:
VCF Automation must manage a vCenter instance, Supervisors, vSphere clusters, and so on, exclusively. When
you use a vCenter instance for VCF Automation and other purposes, a vCenter administrator might accidentally
move VCF Automation resources. This can cause VCF Automation to operate incorrectly, including losing virtual
machines that VCF Automation manages.
Managing Networking Resources
After creating a Tier-0 gateway in NSX Manager, you can make your networking configurations in VCF Automation. As a
Provider Administrator, you can define IP spaces and provider gateways and assign resources to organizations.
As a provider administrator, you can make networking configurations for your organizations. For example, you can define
IP blocks and external connections, which you can later use to assign networking resources to organizations.
View the vCenter Instances in Your VCF Automation
You can see a list of all your vCenter instances, discovered from VCF Operations, and their current connection status.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Administration, click Connections.
3. Click the vCenter tab.
A list of all vCenter instances appears. The list contains the following information for each vCenter instance.
Description
Name The name of the vCenter instance in VCF Automation.
Description Description of the vCenter instance.
State Enabled or Disabled. See Deactivate and Unregister a vCenter Instance in VCF Automation.
Connected Connected or not to VCF Automation. See Reconnect a vCenter Instance to VCF Automation.
Username Username for login to this vCenter instance.
License Status The licensing status of the vCenter instance. Licensed indicates that the vCenter instance
is properly licensed. Not Licensed indicates that the vCenter license is either invalid or
the license is expired.
VCF Instance The VCF Instance managing this vCenter instance.
Deactivate and Unregister a vCenter Instance in VCF Automation
After you delete a workload domain using VCF Operations, you must deactivate and unregister the vCenter instance from
VCF Automation.
1. Decommission a vCenter instance in VCF Operations. See Delete a Workload Domain.
2. Delete the regions created on the vCenter instance. See Create a Region in Your VCF Automation.
Broadcom 7050

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Administration, click Connections.
3. Click the vCenter tab.
4. Click the vertical ellipsis ( ) next to the name of the target vCenter instance, and select Disable.
When you deactivate a vCenter instance, the status of the instance changes to , and you cannot create any
Disabled
regions on it. Existing regions are not affected.
5. When the vCenter instance is deactivated, click the vertical ellipsis ( ) next to the name of the target vCenter
instance, and select Unregister.
Unregistering a vCenter instance, deletes the instance from VCF Automation.
Reconnect a vCenter Instance to VCF Automation
If a vCenter instance appears as disconnected, or if you modified the connection settings, you can try to reset the
connection to VCF Automation.
Note:
During establishing the new connection, the vCenter instance is unavailable for operations.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Administration, click Connections.
3. Click the vCenter tab.
4. Click the vertical ellipsis ( ) next to the name of the target vCenter instance, and select Reconnect.
5. To confirm, click Reconnect.
Refresh a vCenter Instance in VCF Automation
If you make a change to the underlying vCenter infrastructure and you need instant confirmation of the change in VCF
Automation, you can refresh the vCenter instances. By default, VCF Automation performs an automatic refresh of the
vCenter instances every 10 minutes.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Administration, click Connections.
3. Click the vCenter tab.
4. Click the vertical ellipsis ( ) next to the name of the target vCenter instance, and select Refresh.
5. To confirm, click Refresh.
6. If you want to refresh the vCenter storage classes, click the vertical ellipsis, and select Refresh Policies.
7. To confirm, click Refresh.
View Your VMware vSphere Supervisors
You can use the VCF Automation Provider Management UI to view your Supervisors.
A Supervisor is a control plane that spans across one or more zones, each zone has one cluster.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Supervisors.
3. To expand the view and show the full Supervisor details, click the button to the left of the Supervisor name.
Information about the vCenter, Supervisor zones, and Reserved VM classes appears. If the Supervisor is part of a
region in VCF Automation, the region also appears in the details.

For more information about the full-stack and VLAN-backed network stacks, see Supervisor Architecture with VCF
Networking with VPC.
View and Manage Your NSX Manager Instances
You can see a list of all your NSX Manager instances, discovered from VCF Operations, and their current connection

If an NSX Manager instance is not properly registered, it might not appear in the list. You can use the VCF Automation API

Managing Regions in Your VCF Automation
In VCF Automation, a region combines the compute, memory, and networking resources from the underlying
infrastructure.
Region Configuration Requirements
VCF Automation creates a region by grouping one or more Supervisors from one or more vCenter instances, if they are
all configured with the same NSX instance. If the vCenter instances are associated with different NSX instances, you
cannot add their Supervisors to the same region. In a typical VCF Automation deployment, you can use multiple regions to
meet diverse service level requirements, or connect to infrastructure hosted in different VCF Instances within a single VCF
Operations environment.
When you define a region, you must also select the storage classes that you want to make available across all
Supervisors in the region.
Important:
All Supervisors within a region must have a homogeneous configuration including:
• Identical names and configurations for storage classes
• Identical names and configurations for VM classes
• Matching Kubernetes versions
• A consistent set of IaaS services
• Starting with version 9.1.1: Identical network stack type - full-stack or VLAN-backed.
VCF Automation does not support non-homogeneous region configurations for these elements. All specified
classes must be accessible to all zones within the region. Reserved VM classes used for GPUs are an exception
to this requirement and do not need to be homogeneous across the region.
The uniformity of all Supervisors ensures consistent and reliable user experience across the region. When you add a
storage class or VM to a region, you must not rename it in any of the Supervisors.
Regions can contain Supervisors associated with different zones. For example, a region can include one Supervisor in
Zone A and another Supervisor in Zone B.
Broadcom 7052

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To deploy Supervisor Services, VCF CLI plug-ins, and VKS standard packages on VKS clusters in a region, you must
install Regional Harbor to serve as the central container registry for VCF.
Mixed Tenancy Mode and Resource Sharing
Starting with version 9.1, organizations and organizations can share a vCenter instance that has a
VM Apps All Apps
Supervisor with VPC networking enabled. This resource sharing enables customers leveraging VM Apps organizations to
explore modern functionalities without provisioning additional hardware. To activate resource sharing, navigate
All Apps
to the Feature Flags page from the left navigation pane and activate the Mixed Tenancy Mode feature flag.
While the feature flag enables vCenter sharing across organization types, VCF Automation does not enforce strict
resource isolation in this configuration. Specifically, organizations might gain read-only visibility into
VM Apps All Apps
resources. Conversely, organizations remain isolated from resources.
All Apps VM Apps
Beyond visibility concerns, the Mixed Tenancy Mode forces both organizations to share a single NSX or vCenter
instance, creating a risk of API bottlenecks and management-plane contention. Use Mixed Tenancy Mode only for
migration phases or trials where cross-visibility is acceptable. Do not use this configuration for production environments
requiring strict multi-tenancy.
Supervisor VPC Network Stack Types
Starting with version 9.1.1, each zone in a vSphere Supervisor has a property that
supported_networking_stack
indicates the VPC network stack type of the zone. There are two types of VPC network stacks.
• Full-stack VPC
The underlying NSX networking relies on Tunnel Endpoints (TEPs) to create an overlay network.
• VLAN-backed VPC
No overlay is required. All traffic runs directly over VLANs. This configuration is designed for environments running
entirely VLAN-based infrastructure where NSX overlay networking is not available.
For each zone, the VPC network stack type is visible in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
1. Navigate to Infrastructure Overview > Regions and select a region.
2. Click the Zones tab.
The information about the zone includes a network stack column indicating whether the VPC network stack is full-stack
or VLAN-backed.
Note:
You can also view zone network stack details by navigating to Infrastructure > Supervisorsand expanding a
Supervisor to review the zone list.
As a provider administrator, you must know whether a zone is VLAN-backed or full-stack before you assign the zone to an
organization, because all zones per region must have the same network stack type. Mixing VLAN-backed and full-stack
zones in one organization is not supported. Also, you cannot add a zone without a network stack to a region. To prevent
incompatible configurations, zone assignments are automatically validated when you create or modify region quotas.
You can view the supported networking options for each of the network stack types in the following table.
Table 1806: Networking Capabilities per VPC Network Stack
Characteristic Full-stack VPC VLAN-Backed VPC
Public subnets Supported Supported
Private subnets Supported Not supported
VLAN extension subnets Supported Supported
NAT/SNAT Supported Not supported
Private transit gateway IP blocks Supported Not supported
Centralized connections (Tier-0) Supported Not supported
Broadcom 7053

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Characteristic Full-stack VPC VLAN-Backed VPC
Distributed VLAN connections Supported Supported
IPSEC VPN Supported Not supported

Create a Region in Your VCF Automation
To make vSphere compute, memory, and storage resources available to VCF Automation, you must create a region.
• Verify that your vCenter instance has a Supervisor enabled.
• Verify that the following conditions are met across the participating vCenter instances and Supervisors:
– All instances are configured to use the same NSX instance
– All storage classes must:
• Exist on all instances
• Have identical names
• Have the same configuration, for example, the same policies and backing storage.
– All VM classes must:
• Exist on all instances
• Have identical names
• Have consistent configuration, for example, CPU, memory and reservations
• Have consistent zone naming (optional for capacity pooling)
– If you want to group zones across Supervisors into a shared capacity pool:
• The zone names must be the same across all vCenter instances.
– All Supervisors must run the same Kubernetes version to ensure workload compatibility
– The same set of IaaS services, for example, VM Service, Storage Service, Load Balancer Service, must be enabled
and configured consistently across Supervisors.
• If you want to install Supervisor Services, VKS standard packages, and VCF CLI plug-ins, install Harbor. See Install
Regional Harbor Through VCF Automation. Regional Harbor provides a central container registry for VCF and contains
the necessary images to deploy Supervisor Services, VCF CLI plug-ins, and VKS standard packages on VKS clusters.
Important:
VCF Automation does not verify that a storage class or VM class is present in all vCenter instances.
Before creating organizations for your tenants, you must create a region and regional quotas that define the consumption
of resources. Because a region constrains the vSphere capacity and services available to tenants, Provider
Administrators commonly create regions that furnish different classes of service, as measured by performance, capacity,
and features. Tenants can then be provisioned with regional quotas that deliver specific classes of service defined by the
configuration of the backing region. Before you create a region, consider the set of vSphere capabilities that you plan to
offer your tenants.
Important:
If the region uses a vCenter instance version 9.0 or earlier, organization administrators cannot create project
content libraries.
Starting with version 9.1.1, VCF Automation supports VLAN-backed infrastructures. Mixing full-stack and VLAN-backed
zones within a single region is not allowed.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Regions.
3. Click New.
4. Enter a name and, optionally, a description for the region.
5. Select the NSX Manager instance that integrates with the vCenter instances you want to use for the region.
A single NSX Manager instance must be integrated with all vCenter instances within a region.
Broadcom 7054

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Select one or more Supervisors.
The list shows all available Supervisors for this NSX Manager instance.
7. Select one or more storage classes.
The list shows all storage classes across the selected Supervisors.
Important:
The storage classes within a region must be present and have the same names across all vCenter instances
within a region.
VCF Automation does not verify that a storage class or VM class is present in all vCenter instances.
8. Click Submit.
• To view the region details, such as, description, status, Supervisors, NSX Manager instance, VPC networking stack,
and CPU and memory utilization, click the button to the left of the region name to expand the region details pane.
• To view the Supervisors, VM Classes, Storage Classes, and Reserved VM Classes applicable to this region, click
the region name and click the relevant tab in the secondary left navigation pane.
The Zones tab displays the zones from all Supervisors added to the region. If you added two Supervisors with three
zones each, the page displays a total of six zones. If a region includes more than one Supervisor and the zones in the
Supervisors have identical names, VCF Automation displays the combined memory and CPU capacity of the zones with
the same name. To see the zone details and capacity coming from each vCenter, expand the zone view by clicking the
button to the left of the zone name.
The Reserved VM Classes are a special VM class that defines one or more vGPU PCI devices in addition to the CPU
and memory. These VM classes are reserved for each zone in which the Provider Administrator has actual matching GPU
capacity available. You can reserve a VM class in vCenter. VCF Automation detects the reserved counts of these VM
classes per zone and shows them in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI under the Reserved VM Classes
section of a region. The counts of these Reserved VM Classes are further given to organizations through region quotas.
• To edit a region, click the name of the region and click Edit. See Edit a Region.
• Delete a region
a. Remove all region quotas created from the region. See Delete a VCF Automation Region Quota.
b. Click the name of the region and click Delete.
Edit a Region
You can use the Provider Management UI to edit the region settings. You cannot edit the region name and NSX Manager
instance.
If the entire capacity of a region is shared with an organization through a region quota, any changes you make to
the region automatically apply also to the region quota. You can edit a region to remove a storage class, even when
a provider content library uses that storage class to host the published vCenter content library. If namespaces on a
Supervisor originate from a full allocation region quota, you cannot remove that Supervisor by editing the region. If one
or more namespaces use these resources from a full allocation region quota, you cannot remove a storage class or VM
class. You cannot remove the resources from the region until you either remove the namespaces that use the resources
or edit the namespaces so they no longer use these resources.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Regions.
3. Click the name of the region that you want to edit.
4. Click Edit.
5. (Optional) Change the description of the region.
6. (Optional) Increase or decrease the scope of the region by selecting or deselecting Supervisors.
You cannot remove a Supervisor from a region if resources from this Supervisor are already allocated to the
organizations as region quotas. You must delete the region quotas before removing the Supervisor from the region.
Broadcom 7055

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
7. (Optional) Select or deselect the storage classes applicable to the region.
The list shows all storage classes across the selected Supervisors.
Important:
The storage classes within a region must be present and have the same names across all vCenter instances
within a region.
VCF Automation does not verify that a storage class or VM class is present in all vCenter instances.
You cannot remove a storage class from a region if the resources from this storage class are already allocated to the
organizations as region quotas. You must delete the region quotas before removing the storage class from the region
or you must update the region quotas to remove the storage class from it.
8. Click Submit.
Modify the Metadata for a VCF Automation Region
You can use the Provider Management UI to add, edit, and delete metadata for a region in VCF Automation.
To edit or delete metadata, verify that your user account has the Create, update, and delete Regions right. For read
access, your account must have the View Regions right.
You can use metadata to tag, categorize, and automate the management of tenant and provider resources, enabling
policy-driven operations such as billing, compliance, workload placement, and service customization across multi-tenant
environments.
By using metadata, you can associate user-defined pairs with a region. You can use metadata in VCF
key=value

You can edit only the value of an existing metadata item.

2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Regions.
3. Click the name of the region that you want to edit.
4. In the secondary left navigation pane, click Metadata and click Edit.

Create a Content Library
You can use the Provider Management UI to create a provider content library shared with all organizations in this VCF
Automation instance. The provider content libraries are read-only to the users of the organizations.
Create a Region in Your VCF Automation
A VCF Automation provider content library is an abstraction in VCF Automation that provides a single interface for
cloud providers to manage their content across regions. You create a provider content library by selecting one or more
regions and a storage class from each region. To store the actual content in each vCenter taking part in the region, when
you create a provider content library, a content library is also automatically created in vCenter on appropriate storage,
compatible with the selected storage class. The content is automatically synced among all of the backing vCenter content
libraries. For this purpose, one of the vCenter content libraries is randomly picked as a publisher and is set to the
local
type. The rest of the vCenter libraries subscribe to that publisher are set to the type. Because of this
subscribed
underlying synchronization mechanism, you must ensure that the vCenter instances can communicate with each other
and that there is network connectivity between the vCenter instances. The connectivity between the vCenter instances is
critical to the distribution to all vCenter instances of the regions that are part of a VCF Automation provider content library.
From your provider consumption organization, you can promote project-scoped content library images to a provider
content library so that the images become available to all your organizations. See Add a VM Image to a Content Library in
VCF Automation.
Tenant Content Libraries
By default, each tenant project is limited to 200 content libraries. As a service provider, you can use the VCF Automation
API to adjust this threshold for all tenants using the setting. This
contentLibrary.maxLibrariesPerProject
configuration is a global system setting that does not affect provider content libraries.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Content Libraries.
3. On the Content Library tab, click New.
4. Enter a name, and optionally, a description of the content library.
5. To subscribe to an external library, turn on the toggle.
You can subscribe to any content library compliant with the VMware Content Subscription Protocol (VCSP). VCSP is
the underlying communication standard used by VMware Content Libraries to synchronize and share VM templates,
OVA and OVF packages, and ISO images between different vCenter instances.
6. Click Next.
7. If you want to subscribe to an external library, enter the library URL and password, and click Next.
8. Select one or more regions and a corresponding storage class for each region.
Important:
The storage classes within a region must be present and have the same names across all vCenter instances
within a region.
Broadcom 7057

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VCF Automation does not verify that a storage class or VM class is present in all vCenter instances.
9. Click Next.
10.Review the content library settings, and click Confirm.
VCF Automation creates the provider content library in each selected region and shares it with all organizations.
To edit, refresh, or delete a provider content library, click the vertical ellipsis next to the content library name.
• Edit a provider content library by clicking the vertical ellipsis next to the content library name and clicking Edit.
You can edit a VCF Automation provider content library to increase or decrease its scope. For example, you can add
a new region to increase the distribution radius of the content library, alternatively, you can remove a region. You can
also change the storage class of a content library to trigger a migration of content from an old to a new storage.
• Refresh a provider content library by clicking the vertical ellipsis next to the content library name and clicking Refresh.
You can use the refresh option to reconcile changes from underlying vCenter instances. If a new content library item
is added directly in the vCenter content library backing the provider content library, the refresh action propagates this
new item to the provider content library. If an item is directly deleted from a vCenter content library, the refresh option
removes the item from the provider content library.
• Delete a provider content library by clicking the vertical ellipsis next to the content library name and clicking Delete.
Upload a Content Library Item
You can use the Provider Management UI to upload an item to a provider content library that is not subscribed. All items
within a provider content library and the content library itself are automatically shared with all organizations.
Create a Content Library
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Content Libraries.
3. On the Content Library Items tab, click Upload.
4. Upload a source file.
You can upload an OVA, ISO, or an OVF file and all files that the OVF references.
5. From the drop-down menu, select a content library to which to add the item.
6. Enter a name, and optionally, a description for the content library item.
7. Click Submit.
If you want to delete an item, click the vertical ellipsis next to the content library name, and click Delete.
Create an Infrastructure Policy in VCF Automation
You can create an infrastructure policy that defines the VM placement on specific hosts. By adding policy enforcement
criteria, you can target a subset of VMs based on their attributes, ensuring a correct workload placement.
1. vSphere supports the creation of multiple zones. To use them in combination with infrastructure policies, these criteria
must be met:
• Verify that one or more vSphere clusters back each zone.
• Verify that one or more hosts in each vSphere cluster within a single zone have the tags defined in the vCenter
compute policies to ensure the same vCenter compute policy compatibility.
2. In the vSphere Client, create a tag and tag category. See What Are vSphere Tags and How to Use Them.
3. In the vSphere Client, create a VM-Host affinity compute policy.
See Create a VM-Host Affinity Policy.
Broadcom 7058

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
After the creation of a compute policy, the synchronization between the vSphere Client and VCF Automation
might take a few minutes.
Infrastructure policies build upon vCenter compute policies to enforce placement and resource rules in the vSphere
Supervisor context. You can use the Provider Management UI to view the available vCenter compute policies. See View
the vCenter Compute Policies.
After you assign infrastructure policies to a tenant, the tenant can create a namespace, selecting one or more zones.
Namespace creation fails if the selected zones are not compatible with the policies. The system automatically applies all
assigned mandatory policies. The tenant can also select from the available optional policies to meet the requirements of
the namespace.
• VCF Automation does not require a namespace to comply with the policies within a single zone. To meet all policy
requirements, the namespace might span across multiple zones. If a zone has multiple clusters, the infrastructure
policies must be available in all the clusters of that zone. For the infrastructure policy to be available, the vCenter
compute policy defined in the infrastructure policy must be compatible with at least one host in this cluster.
Compatibility requires that the host tag defined in the policy is assigned to that host.
• A VM with multiple policy requirements must have all policies fulfilled within a single zone and a single cluster in that
zone.
• If a single zone cannot fulfill the VM policy requirements, even if the namespace is placed across multiple zones, the
VM placement fails.
• Zones can host a unique combination of available policies. VCF Automation automatically places workloads, such as
VMs, only when you do not provide an explicit zone. For namespaces, you must always provide one or more zones,
and you must ensure the selected zones are compatible with all assigned mandatory and optional infrastructure
policies.
You can dynamically manage the compute capacity within the defined zones.
• You can add additional vSphere clusters to an existing zone.
• To ensure policy consistency for future namespace placement, you must configure new clusters with the same
infrastructure policies as the existing clusters in that zone.
• You must tag at least one host in every vSphere cluster within a zone to match the policies defined for that zone.
vCenter enforces the infrastructure policies using your host tagging.
• When you remove a cluster from a zone and migrate the part of the namespace containing the workloads to another
cluster within the same zone, the destination cluster must be able to satisfy the full set of infrastructure policies that
govern those migrated workloads.
• You can modify the infrastructure policies available in a specific zone by adding new policies for placement. After
adding new policies to a zone, you must update the underlying vCenter configuration by ensuring the corresponding
policy tags are applied to at least one host per cluster in all clusters in that zone.
Note:
You cannot edit the infrastructure policies after their creation.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Infrastructure Policies.
3. Click New.
If there are no infrastructure policies in VCF Automation, click Create Infrastructure Policy.
4. Enter a name for the policy, and optionally, a description.
5. Select a vCenter compute policy to serve as the foundation for the infrastructure policy creation.
6. If you want the policy to be mandatory for the VMs in the namespaces in which the policy is applicable, select the
Make this a mandatory policy when assigned to a region in the organization check box.
If a policy is not mandatory, during the namespace creation process, organization administrators can choose to select
or deselect that policy as applicable to the namespace.
Broadcom 7059

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If existing namespaces are present in a region, you cannot assign mandatory infrastructure policies to the region
quota. You can assign only optional policies for that region. To add mandatory policies, you must do so before
creating any namespaces for the specific region.
7. (Optional) Apply the policy enforcement criteria to the infrastructure policy.
You can add rules to determine which VMs the policy manages. You can define conditions by selecting an attribute,
such as Guest OS, Guest OS Family, or Custom Label, and an operator. You can use the expression preview to
verify the intended rules.
8. Click Submit.
• To view the details of a policy, on the Infrastructure Policies page, click the policy name.
On the details page, the Sync Status column provides information on whether the policy is properly enforced to all the
vCenter instances where VCF Automation detects the vCenter compute policy. You can sync from the vertical ellipsis
in the grid to manually trigger the synchronization in certain cases.
– Deleted vCenter compute policy - If you delete the compute policy in vCenter, the synchronization status for that
vCenter becomes . Manually syncing the infrastructure policy causes the system to clean
PENDING_DELETION
up the vCenter policy object. The synchronization fails if VCF Automation detects that namespaces placed on that
particular vCenter use the infrastructure policy.
– vCenter compute policy added to a new vCenter - If you add the vCenter compute policy to a new vCenter, the
infrastructure policy details show the new vCenter with a synchronization status. When you
PENDING_CREATION
trigger the synchronization operation, the system creates the infrastructure policy object on the new vCenter to sync
the rules and other details from VCF Automation to the new vCenter instance.
•
To delete an infrastructure policy, click the vertical ellipsis ( ) next to the policy name and click Delete. When
you delete a policy, VCF Automation removes it from all namespaces to which it applies. If the vCenter instance is
unavailable, you can force the policy deletion to remove the policy from VCF Automation.
• When you navigate to a namespace, you can see all infrastructure policies that apply to the namespace, including the
mandatory and opt-in policies. You can view the VM details to see its enforced infrastructure policies.
View the vCenter Compute Policies
After you create one or more vCenter compute policies using the vSphere Client, you can view the policies in the VCF
Automation Provider Management UI
You can use vCenter compute policies to define and guide VM placement and resource usage across hosts within a
cluster.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the left navigation pane, under Infrastructure, click Infrastructure Policies.
3. Click the vCenter Compute Policies tab.
Managing Networking Resources in VCF Automation
To leverage the networking capabilities of VCF Automation for organizations for all applications, you add to and manage
your infrastructure and cloud networking resources through the VCF Automation Provider Management UI, and then
assign them to the organizations in your environment.
Managing IP Blocks in VCF Automation
You can use external IP blocks to meet your IP address management needs. Additionally, you can include one or multiple
CIDRs in the IP block, while at the same time exclude one or more IPs from the pool of available IPs. IP blocks provide
a structured approach to allocating public IP addresses to different organizations, enabling connectivity to external
networks.
IP blocks represent IPs used in this local data center, south of the provider gateway. The IP blocks that you define are
used by Organization Administrators as external IP addresses for configuring services and public networks. For example,
Organization Administrators can allocate CIDRs and individual IP addresses for NAT and load balancing. This allocation is
Broadcom 7060

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
subject to the provider-defined quota for the respective organization. Organizations can also create subnets from these IP
blocks to ensure direct workload connectivity without NAT.
As a provider administrator, you create IP blocks and use them for the external connections that you create and configure.
You can assign an IP block to multiple external connections as long as these external connections are not assigned to the
same organization. An IP block consists of a set of CIDR blocks and IP ranges that are reserved and dedicated to VCF.
The IP addresses in an IP block can only be IPv4.
As a provider administrator, you can benefit from an extended set of functionalities that are related to the definition and
usage of external IP blocks.
• You can have up to 10 CIDRs and up to 10 IP ranges inside a single IP block.
• You can specify reserved IP ranges to be excluded from the pool of IP addresses and CIDRs available for allocation.
• You can use existing IP blocks from an external IPAM provided by Infoblox. For more information, see Register
Infoblox NIOS DDI with NSX.
• You can hide the content of the IP block from your organizations and only expose the definition of the objects and the
quotas applying to it.
For example, you can share with an organization an IP block with a quota of 5 IPs without exposing the IP addresses
or CIDRs inside the IP block.
Note:
Quota is defined for all IP blocks, hidden or not.
Starting with version 9.1.1, external IP blocks also work with the distributed VXLAN connection type to provide IPs for
advanced networking services, such as Load Balancer and NAT. When an organization administrator assigns a Load
Balancer VIP or configures NAT, the VIP or NAT IP is allocated as a address from the external IP block that you as
/32
a provider administrator define and assign to the organization. The Route Controller automatically advertises these
/32
service IPs to the physical Border Gateway as BGP EVPN Type-5 routes. No additional routing configuration is required.
Create an External IP Address Block
You can create an IP block, formerly known as an IP Space, to be used by multiple VCF Automation organizations and
you can control organization usage through a quota system. An IP block can only be IPv4.
• Verify that your role includes the System IP Spaces: Manage and System IP Spaces: View rights.
Note:
The System Administrator role has these rights by default.
• Verify that you have a region with more than one Supervisor, see Create a Region in Your VCF Automation.
• To use an external IPAM, verify that connection to Infoblox is configured in NSX Manager, see Register Infoblox NIOS
DDI with NSX.
As a provider administrator, you can add an IP block that can be used by several organizations. The consumption of IP
addresses can be controlled by a quota on the IP block, and optionally, overridden at organization level.
Important:
An IP block can overlap with other IP blocks as long as the overlapping blocks are not assigned to the same
organization.
Starting with version 9.1.1, if you want to create an IP block to support Load Balancer VIPs or NAT IPs for advanced
networking services over a VXLAN external connection, you must observe the following best practices:
• Use a dedicated IP range for service IPs. Avoid mixing Load Balancer VIP and NAT IP ranges with VM subnet ranges,
because the Route Controller advertises Load Balancer VIPs and NAT IPs as host routes.
/32
• Size the IP block to accommodate the expected peak number of concurrent Load Balancer VIPs and NAT IPs across
all organizations that share this IP block.
• After assigning the IP block to an organization, set per-organization quotas to limit VIP and NAT IP consumption.
Broadcom 7061

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Important:
The IP ranges used for Load Balancer VIPs and NAT IPs must be defined as external IP blocks in NSX Manager
before you create the IP block in VCF Automation. Verify that these ranges are reachable from the Border
Gateway before assigning them to an organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the Infrastructure section of the left-hand navigation menu, select Networking > External IP Blocks.
3. Click the New button.
The Create External IP Blocks wizard opens.
4. In the Configure General Settings tile, provide the general configuration for the IP block.

Managing External Connections in VCF Automation
As a VCF Automation provider administrator, you configure external connections to establish external network connectivity
for organizations, for example to the Internet or the data center. After you create an external connection, you assign it to
one or more organizations.
External connections can be of the following types:
• Centralized connections, which leverage VCF networking Tier-0 or Tier-0 VRF gateways, and associate them with IP
addresses from IP blocks that can be advertised from those gateways.
• Distributed VLAN connections, which leverage VLANs.
• Distributed VXLAN connections, which integrate with the physical Ethernet VPN (EVPN)-VXLAN fabric through a
special cluster called a Route Controller, see Create a Route Controller.
Important:
Distributed VXLAN connections are available for version 9.1.1 and later.
Centralized Connections
A centralized external connection in VCF Automation is a Tier-0 gateway integrated with an IP block to manage external
connectivity for your organizations. Centralized connections are backed by existing Tier-0 or Tier-0 VRF gateways in
either in or in mode. Associating IP blocks with a centralized connection provides
Active-Active Active-Standby
control over default service configurations, routing rules, and the dynamic routing configuration. Alternatively, you can
allow organizations to advertise their own private transit gateway IP blocks, in which case the centralized connection does
not require an IP block.
Broadcom 7064

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Centralized connections use edge clusters to get the full set of stateful networking services, including NAT, load balancing,
IPSec VPN, and gateway firewall.
Important:
Starting with version 9.1.1, VCF Automation supports VLAN-backed regions. You cannot use centralized
connections for organizations in VLAN-backed regions.
Distributed VLAN Connections
Using distributed external connections provides organizations with VLAN-based external connectivity and ensures high-
performance distributed routing. Distributed external connections link the organization's transit gateway directly to a VLAN
in the physical infrastructure.
You can add multiple distributed VLAN connections to a single organization configured with a distributed transit gateway.
Also, you can assign a single distributed VLAN connection to multiple organizations. You can also create a dedicated
VLAN connection, which an organization administrator can use to create a VLAN extension subnet directly in their
organization.
Distributed VXLAN Connections
Starting with VCF Automation 9.1.1, you can create a distributed VXLAN connection in the VCF Automation Provider
Management UI. By configuring and using a distributed VXLAN connection, workload VM traffic is routed directly to
gateways in the physical EVPN fabric, eliminating the need for a VLAN spanning the entire physical network.
Distributed VXLAN connections support advanced networking services, such as NAT, Load Balancer VIPs, and Auto
SNAT. These services are delivered through a VNA cluster that you select during organization creation or while setting
up the regional networking of an organization. External IP blocks serve as the source pools for Load Balancer VIPs and
SNAT/DNAT IPs.
Use this type of external connection in environments with an existing EVPN-VXLAN fabric that requires direct VM-to-
physical-network routing without edge nodes.
For more information about distributed VXLAN connections and the Route Controller cluster, see Distributed VXLAN
Connectivity.
Assigning External Connections to Organizations
After you create an external connection, you assign it to one or multiple existing organizations through the regional
networking settings. For more information, see Setting Up Regional Networking for an Organization in VCF Automation.
An organization can use only one connection type per region — centralized, distributed VLAN, or - for version 9.1.1 only -
distributed VXLAN. Mixing connection types within a single region is not supported.
Create a New Centralized Connection
Centralized connections define external network connectivity through NSX Tier-0 or Tier-0 VRF gateway. They provide
connectivity to designated remote networks or a default gateway and facilitate the advertisement of subnets and IPs from
IP blocks associated with this connection. Centralized connections enable a full set of stateful networking services within
organizations, such as NAT, load balancing, IPSEC VPN, and Gateway Firewall.
• Create a Region in Your VCF Automation
• Verify that you have a Tier-0 gateway or Tier-0 VRF gateway created in NSX Manager. For instructions on creating
a Tier-0 gateway, see Add an NSX Tier-0 Gateway. For instructions on creating a Tier-0 VRF gateway, see Step 4 in
Deploy an NSX VRF-Lite with BGP.
Broadcom 7065

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
If you want to add a tier-0 gateway that is backed by a VRF gateway in NSX, you must also create a VRF
gateway that is linked to the tier-0 gateway.
• Verify that you have external IP blocks in your environment, see Managing IP Blocks in VCF Automation.
You can create a centralized connection to serve as an organization's default connection for all external traffic and
connection to the Internet. You can also create and assign additional centralized connections to the organization, for
specific pruposes, such as providing access to a CIDR hosting shared services.
When you create a centralized external connection, you can configure a Source NAT rule directly for the connection. You
can also define inbound remote networks to establish external reachability for the connection. You can create a dedicated
centralized connection, which allows the organization that uses the connection to advertise its own transit gateway IP
blocks up to the connection.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the Infrastructure section of the left-hand navigation menu, select Networking > External Connections.
3. Click the Centralized Connections tab and click New.
4. In the Configure General Settings tile, provide the general configuration for centralized connection.
a) Enter a name and, optionally, a description for the new connection.
b) Select a region from the drop-down menu.
c) Click Next.
5. In the Select T0 Gateway tile, select the Tier-0 gateway for the centralized connection and click Next.
You can only see a list of the available gateways to choose from. The Tier-0 gateways are pre-created and configured
in NSX.
6. In the Associated External IP Blocks tile, select one or multiple IP blocks to become available to the organization
after the connection is associated with an organization, and click Next.
• Select the Allow Organization to advertise their Private TGW networks through the Connection check box to
create a private centralized connection that you do not want to share to multiple organizations.
Important:
Selecting this check box means that the organization that you assign that centralized connection to can advertise
private transit gateway IP blocks through that connection. If you decide to allow the organization to advertise its
private TGW networks, you can skip selecting an IP block from the list.
• Select the Insert Provider Outbound NAT on Centralized Connection check box to use a provider NAT directly
on the connection.
Note:
When you select that option, the transit gateway associated with that connection uses a separate NAT gateway.
7. (Optional) In the Provider Outbound NAT tile, select an IP block for the Provider Outbound NAT and click Next.
• Select the Enable Logging check box to enable logging for the Provider Outbound NAT.
This tile appears only if you select the Insert Provider Outbound NAT on Centralized Connection check box at
Step 6.
The IP block that you select for the Provider outbound NAT can be different from the IP block that you select for the
connection at Step 6.
8. (Optional) In the Remote Networks tile, specify the CIDRs for the remote networks for the centralized connection.
You can have multiple centralized connections associated with a single transit gateway. In such cases, you must
specify the CIDRs to be used for external networks for that particular connection.
Broadcom 7066

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If you only assign one connection to a transit gateway, you do not have to specify CIDRs for remote networks for that
connection. As you start adding more connections to the same transit gateway, you must ensure that the CIDRs for the
remote networks for the different connections do not overlap.
9. In the Review and Complete tile, review the settings for the new distributed connection and click Create.
• To edit the name and description of the centralized connection or to view the connected transit gateways, see Edit a
Centralized External Connection.
• To delete a centralized connection, follow the steps.
a. Verify that no transit gateways are connected to the provider gateway.
b. On the left of the name of the provider gateway you want to delete, click the vertical ellipsis ( ), and click Delete.
Create a New Distributed VLAN Connection
By creating a distributed VLAN connection and then assigning it to your organizations, you can use your existing VLAN
infrastructure to provide external connectivity to your organizations. In the distributed connectivity model, to provide
stateful network services, such as Load Balancer, you must have a VNA cluster set up.
• Create a Region in Your VCF Automation.
• Verify that you have a VLAN configured in your infrastructure.
• Verify that you have external IP blocks created, see Managing IP Blocks in VCF Automation.
Creating distributed connections allows you to connect workloads to networks already existing in the datacenter, for
instance on a VLAN. A distributed VLAN connection can be assigned to multiple organizations. You can also create
a dedicated distributed VLAN connection, which you assign to a single organization. When you dedicate a distributed
VLAN connection to a single organization, the organization administrator can use the dedicated connection and create
VLAN extension subnets directly within the organization. This option gives you more flexibility in the way you design and
configure your network infrastructure.
So, the distributed VLAN connection operates in three modes:
• You use overlay connections and VLAN to advertise the external traffic.
• You create a VLAN subnet and then share it with your organizations.
• You create a dedicated VLAN connection to assign to a single organization, whose organization administrator can
subsequently create a VLAN subnet in the organization VPC.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the Infrastructure section of the left-hand navigation menu, select Networking > External Connections.
3. Click the Distributed Connections tab and click New.
4. In the Configure General Settings tile, provide the general configuration for distributed connection.
a) Enter a name and, optionally, a description for the new connection.
b) Select a region from the drop-down menu.
c) Click Next.
5. In the Connection details tile, enter the VLAN ID and the gateway address in a CIDR format, and click Next.
6. (Optional) Activate the Create a dedicated VLAN toggle to create a VLAN connection that can connect to a single
VPC subnet for bridging.
7. In the Associate External IP Block tile, select the IP block to use with that distributed connection and click Next.
The IP blocks are filtered based on the gateway CIDR that you sepcify at Step 5. The gateway CIDR 5 must be part of
the selected IP block.
The selected IP block is used exclusively for the newly created distributed connection. You cannot use the same IP
block to create another distributed connection.
8. In the Review and Complete tile, review the settings for the new distributed connection and click Create.
The new distributed connection appears in the list of connections.
Broadcom 7067

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Assign the connection to an organization, see Configure the Regional Networking of a VCF Automation Organization.
Create a New Distributed VXLAN Connection for Version 9.1.1
Starting with version 9.1.1, you can create a distributed VXLAN connection and then assign it to your organizations.
Distributed VXLAN connections enable you to use your existing physical EVPN-VXLAN fabric. By using a distributed
VXLAN connection, workload VM traffic routes directly to gateways in the physical EVPN fabric, eliminating the need for a
VLAN spanning the entire physical network.
• Enable support for advanced networking services for distributed VXLAN connections in NSX Manager, see Enable
Advanced Networking Services for Distributed VXLAN Connections.
• Verify that a Route Controller is created in NSX Manager, see Create a Route Controller.
• Verify that the Route Controller cluster VIP is reachable from your BGP EVPN border gateway routers.
• If you require NAT or Load Balancer services over the VXLAN connection, verify that a VNA cluster is available in the
target region.
Important:
vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) requires a Load Balancer.
Unlike a distributed VLAN connection, which maps to a specific physical VLAN, a VXLAN connection uses a Layer 3
VNI to extend connectivity to an EVPN Border Gateway (BGW). The connection integrates with the physical EVPN-
VXLAN fabric through a Route Controller. When you create a distributed VXLAN connection, you specify the Layer 3 VNI,
Route Target (RT), and Route Distinguisher (RD) that identify the tenant VRF on the Route Controller for BGP EVPN
advertisements. For more information about VXLAN connections and the Route Controller cluster, see Distributed VXLAN
Connectivity.
Distributed VXLAN connections support the following advanced networking services:
• NSX Load Balancer VIPs
• Avi Load Balancer in mode
Active-Standby
• Centralized NAT
If you want to enable an organization to use advanced networking services over a VXLAN external connection, you must
assign a VNA cluster to the organization at the time of setting up the regional networking for the organization. Also, you
must configure an external IP block for the load balancer VIPs and NAT IPs. For more information about VNA clusters,
see Managing Edge and VNA Clusters in VCF Automation. For more information about external IP blocks, see Managing
IP Blocks in VCF Automation.
You can add multiple distributed VXLAN connections to a single organization configured with a distributed transit gateway.
Each organization maps to a separate tenant VRF on the Route Controller, identified by the Layer 3 VNI.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the Infrastructure section of the left-hand navigation menu, select Networking > External Connections.
3. Click the Distributed VXLAN Connections tab and click New.
Important:
If support for distributed VXLAN connection is not enabled in NSX Manager, you get an error at Step 3.
Broadcom 7068

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. In the Configure General Settings tile, provide the general configuration for distributed connection.
a) Enter a name and, optionally, a description for the new connection.
b) Select a region from the drop-down menu.
c) Click Next.
5. In the Select Route Controller tile, select a Route Controller from the list and click Next.
6. In the Connection Details tile, enter the VXLAN details and click Next.

7. In the Associate External IP Blocks tile, select an IP block for the connection.
The organizations using that connection use IP addresses from the pool of IPs defined by the selected IP block.
The selected IP block is used exclusively for the newly created distributed connection. You cannot use the same IP
block to create another distributed connection.
8. In the Review and Complete tile, review the settings for the new distributed connection and click Create.
The new distributed VXLAN connection appears on the Distributed VXLAN Connections tab.
Assign the connection to an organization, see Configure the Regional Networking of a VCF Automation Organization.

Managing Edge and VNA Clusters in VCF Automation
Depending on the type of external connection that you want to add to an organization, you specify and use an edge or
VNA cluster to provide stateful networking services to your organization.
Both edge clusters and VNA clusters are NSX constructs. You do not configure or provision edge or VNA clusters within
VCF Automation. VCF Automation simply discovers the available edge and VNA clusters for your environment and lists
them in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
An edge cluster is a grouping of multiple NSX Edge transport nodes that host Tier-0 and Tier-1 gateways. A VNA cluster
is a collection of edge-based virtual network appliances that deliver edge services to VPCs connected with a distributed
transit gateway by enabling service-based traffic redirection.
When you assign a centralized connection to an organization, you must specify an edge cluster to provide stateful
networking services.
When you assign a distributed VLAN or VXLAN connection to an organization, you specify a VNA cluster to provide
stateful networking services, such as NAT and load balancer.
Broadcom 7071

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Important:
NAT is available only in full-stack regions. In VLAN-backed environments, VNA clusters provide load balancer
services only. For more information about full-stack and VLAN-backed regions, see Managing Regions in Your
VCF Automation.
Starting with version 9.1.1, the VNA cluster also hosts the Service VMs that process north-south traffic for advanced
networking services for organizations that use EVPN-VXLAN distributed external connections. When a workload VM in the
VPC must be reached through a load balancer VIP or NAT IP from outside the data center, traffic is routed by the BGW
directly to the ESX host in the VNA cluster where the active Service VM runs.
For more information about edge and VNA clusters, see Create an NSX Edge Cluster and Add Edge Nodes and Create a
Virtual Network Appliance Cluster.
View Details About Edge and VNA Clusters in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI
You can view a list of the available edge and VNA clusters, and you can verify that they are synchronized with NSX.
The list of edge and VNA clusters appears automatically in the VCF Automation Provider Management UI when you
register an NSX Manager. To modify an edge or VNA cluster, you must use NSX and then synchronize VCF Automation
with NSX.
For each edge cluster, you can view the following information:
• Cluster health
• Number of nodes
• Average CPU and memory usage
• Number of organizations that use the respective cluster
• Number of VPCs
• Cluster type
• The region where the cluster can be used
For each VNA cluster, you can view the following information:
• Cluster health
• Number of nodes
• Number of organizations that use the respective VNA cluster
• The region where the cluster can be used
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. In the Infrastructure section of the left-hand navigation menu, select Networking > Edge/VNA Clusters.
In the Edge and VNA Clusters pane, you see two tabs, Edge Clusters and VNA Clusters.
On the Edge Clusters tab, you see a list of all edge clusters in your environment together with essential information
about each edge cluster.
On the VNA Clusters tab, you see a list of all VNA clusters in your environment together with essential information
about each VNA cluster.
3. Select your task.
