Configure Your VCF Automation Organization to Use an OpenID Identity Provider
If you want to import users and groups from an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider to your VCF Automation
organization, you must configure your organization with this OIDC identity provider. Imported users can log in to the
organization with the credentials established in the OIDC identity provider.
OAuth is an open federation standard that delegates user access. OpenID Connect is an authentication layer on top of
the OAuth 2.0 protocol. By using OpenID Connect, clients can receive information about authenticated sessions and end
users. The OAuth authentication endpoint must be reachable from VCF Automation which makes it more suitable when
you use public identity providers or provider-managed ones.
Important:
Endpoint misconfigurations can lead to user inability to complete the SSO logout from VCF Automation. See KB
article 394731.
You can allow organizations to generate and issue API access tokens that applications can use on their behalf.
You can configure VCF Automation to automatically refresh your OIDC key configurations from the JSON Web Key Set
(JWKS) endpoint you provide. You can configure the frequency of the key refresh process and the rotation strategy that
determines whether VCF Automation adds new keys, replaces the old keys with new, or the old keys expire after a certain
period.
To determine the correct values and settings and to ensure proper and accurate configuration, see also the product
documentation of those identity providers.
VCF Automation generates audit events for both successful and failed key refreshes under the event topic
com/vmware/
. The audit events for failed key refreshes include additional information
vcloud/event/oidcSettings/keys/modify
about the failure.

Option Description
Add Add the incoming set of keys to the existing set of keys. All keys in
the merged set are valid and usable.
For example, your existing set of keys includes keys A, B, and D.

key refresh occurs, the new set includes keys A, B, C, and D.
Replace Replace the existing set of keys with the incoming set of keys.
For example, your existing set of keys includes keys A, B, and D.
Your incoming set of keys includes keys B, C, and D. When the
key refresh occurs, key C replaces key A. The incoming keys B,

with the old set.

Option Description

The key refresh runs start at the beginning of every hour. When
the key refresh occurs, VCF Automation tags as expiring the keys
in the existing set of keys that are not included in the incoming
set. At the next key refresh run, VCF Automation stops using the
expiring keys. Only keys included in the incoming set are valid and
usable.
For example, your existing set of keys includes keys A, B, and D.
The incoming set includes keys B, C, and D. If you configure the
existing keys to expire in 1 hour, there is 1 hour of overlap during
which both sets of keys are valid. VCF Automation marks key A
as expiring and until the next key refresh run, keys A, B, C, and
D are usable. At the next run, key A expires and only B, C, and D
continue working.

Managing Predefined User Roles in VCF Automation
Roles assigned to users and groups are an essential part to identity and access management in VCF Automation. You
can leverage identity providers with VCF Automation organizations to enable single sign-on to provision users and groups.
Once the users and groups are added to the VCF Automation organization, they must be assigned roles to enable specific
permissions and access to different features within VCF Automation.
What are User Roles in VCF Automation
VCF Automation has several levels of user roles. These different levels control access to the organization, the projects
that produce or consume the blueprints, catalog items, access to IaaS services, and the ability for users to use or see
individual parts of the user interface. These different levels give organization administrators different tools to apply any
level of granularity that is required by their operational needs.
As the organization administrator, after you configure an identity provider for your organization, you can import users and
groups and manage their role assignments using the Access Control page. There are two types of predefined roles in
VCF Automation: organization roles and project roles. In addition, you can create custom roles for specific use cases.
Predefined Organization Roles
The organization roles are global. The predefined organization-level roles are Organization Administrator, Organization
Auditor, and Organization User.
Broadcom 7128

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Organizational roles define permissions within the organization. Organization administrators can add and manage other
users and create custom roles at the organization level. Custom roles allow you to tailor permissions to specific user
requirements.
Role General permissions
Organization Administrator Can access the organization UI and add users and groups to the
organization.
Organization administrators can:
• Manage projects and project users
• Configure integrations, such as Active Directory, Bitbucket,
GitHub, and GitLab
• Manage blueprints and catalog items
• Manage namespaces and associated resources
• Fully access namespaces that they did not create
• Manage new VPCs and associated resources
• See all projects and all deployments
• Create and manage content libraries
• Create and manage policies on resources and deployments
• Create and manage event subscriptions
Organization User Can log in to the organization UI. Must be added to a project.
Organization Auditor Read-only version of the organization administrator.
Defer to Identity Provider User permissions are determined based on information received
from the identity provider for the organization.
Predefined organization-level roles are managed by the provider administrator in the VCF Automation Provider
Management UI. For a full list of what rights are given to each role, see Predefined VCF Automation Roles and Their
Rights in the Provider Management documentation.
Custom Organization Roles
As an organization administrator, you can create custom roles for your organization.
The custom roles have two categories, view and manage.
• View. A user assigned to a role with this permission can see all the items for all projects across the organization in
the selected sections of the user interface. This role is useful for users who need to see accounts, configurations, or
assigned values.
• Manage. A user assigned to a role with this permission can see all the items and has full add, edit, and delete
permissions for all projects across the organization in the selected sections of the user interface.
These permissions extend the privileges that are granted by the other roles and are not restricted by project membership.
For example, you can expand a project administrator's permissions to manage parts of the infrastructure or give an
organization auditor an ability to review and respond to approvals requests.
For instructions on how to create a custom role, see Create a Custom Role in for All Apps.
Project Roles
In addition to the organizational roles, VCF Automation has project roles. Project members can view and manage project
resources depending on their project role. Project roles include Project Administrator, Project Advanced User, Project
User, and Project Auditor.
Broadcom 7129

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
These roles are assigned automatically on a per-project basis in VCF Automation. The project roles can vary between
projects. The same user can be an administrator in one project and an advanced user in another project.
Role General permissions
Project Administrator Project administrators leverage the infrastructure that is created by the organization
administrator to ensure that their project members have the resources they need for their
development work.
Project administrators can:
• View all content for their project, including namespaces, deployments, and so on
• Perform all Day 2 actions on resources
• Manage users in the project and assign roles
• Manage project-level settings and administrator content
• Create namespaces if the organization administrator set up self-service for the project
• Create resources using the IaaS services console in namespaces they created or have
access to
• Manage catalog approval requests
Project Advanced User Advanced users work within their projects to request catalog items and create resources
using the services console. They can perform day 2 actions on all resources.
Project User Project users can only access the catalog and request catalog items. They can perform day 2
actions on their own deployments. They cannot use the IaaS services console.
Project Auditor Project auditors are restricted to read-only access.
For a full list of what permissions each project role has, see Predefined Roles and Permissions in VCF Automation.
Add Users and Assign Roles in VCF Automation
You can add role assignments for users in VCF Automation.
• Verify that users have been imported from a valid identity provider instance that is associated with your VCF
Automation deployment. See Managing Identity Providers in VCF Automation Organizations.
• Review the VCF Automation organization roles and project roles permissions in Predefined Roles and Permissions in
VCF Automation. You must understand what each user role can see and do.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control.
3. Select the Users tab and click Import Users.
4. From the Source drop-down menu, select your identity provider type.
If you configured only one identity provider, this option is hard-coded.
5. Search for the users you want to assign roles to.
You can import a CSV list.
6. Assign one or more roles to the selected users.
7. If you want the roles of the users to become a combination of all group and assigned roles, turn on the Inherit roles
from groups toggle.
8. Click Save.
• You can edit roles assigned to users that have been imported into VCF Automation at any time. To edit a user's role,
click the vertical ellipsis next to their name on the Users page and click Edit.
Add Group and Assign Roles in VCF Automation
You can add role assignments for groups in VCF Automation.
• Verify that user groups have been imported from a valid identity provider instance that is associated with your VCF
Automation deployment. See Managing Identity Providers in VCF Automation Organizations.
Broadcom 7130

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Review the VCF Automation organization roles and project roles permissions in Predefined Roles and Permissions in
VCF Automation. You must understand what each user role can see and do.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control.
3. Select the Groups tab and click Import Groups.
4. From the Source drop-down menu, select your identity provider type.
If you configured only one identity provider, this option is hard-coded.
5. Use the search function to find the group that you are adding and select it.
6. Assign an organization role.
7. Click Save.
• You can edit roles assigned to groups that have been imported into VCF Automation at any time. To edit a group's role,
click the vertical ellipsis next to the group's name on the Groups page and click Edit.
Disable and Delete Users in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you can disable and/or delete users and user groups from your VCF Automation
organization.
Disabling a user or user group deactivates the user's access to the organization. They are no longer able to log in and
access VCF Automation features. Disabling a user does not remove them from the organization and you can reactivate
their access at a later time.
Deleting a user removes them from the organization. You must import the user again if you want to give them access to
VCF Automation. Before you can delete a user, you must disable their access first.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control > Users.
3. Click vertical ellipsis next to the name of the user you want to delete and then click Disable.
4. Click Disable to confirm.
5. Select Administer > Access Control > Users.
6. Click vertical ellipsis next to the name of the user you want to delete and then click Delete.
7. Click Delete to confirm.
8. Optional: Select the Transfer the user's objects to me checkbox.
Transferring user objects to the administrator ensures that objects are not orphaned when a user is deleted.
9. Click Delete to confirm.
Create a Custom Role in VCF Automation
As a VCF Automation organization administrator, you manage user access using the default organization roles. However,
you might also want to create custom roles so that selected users can perform specific tasks or see content that is outside
of their organization roles.
• Review the custom organization role descriptions so that you know more about how you can refine the permissions for
your users. See Managing Predefined User Roles in VCF Automation.
Broadcom 7131

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control > Roles and click New.
3. Enter a unique name that you can identify when you assign users to the role and, optionally, a description.
4. Select the check boxes that correspond to the permissions you want the users to have over the resources.
5. Click Save.
Assign the custom role to users and groups in your organization. See Add Users and Assign Roles in VCF Automation
Predefined Roles and Permissions in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you assign organization roles and project roles to users in your organization to
determine what they can see and do in the organization. As an organization administrator, you have full permission on all
areas of the user interface.

Create a Service Account in Your VCF Automation Organization
In VCF Automation, you can use service accounts to control access from third-party applications. As the organization
administrator, you create service accounts and you can revoke access at any time.
Service accounts access VCF Automation programatically using an API token that is bound to a device ID. The API token
does not expire and is renewed upon each request.
Service accounts cannot be used to access the VCF Automation organization UI.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control > Service Accounts and click New.
3. Enter a name for the service account.
4. From the Assign Role drop-down menu, select a role for the service account.
The list of available roles comprises global and custom organization roles.
5. Enter a software ID for the service account or generate and enter one using the Generate Software ID button.
Service accounts must have software IDs which are unique identifiers, in UUID format, representing the application
that connects to VCF Automation.
For larger solutions, to retain control over the identity of your service accounts, do not use the Generate Software ID
option, and generate your own software ID.
6. (Optional) Enter the software version of the system using the service account.
The software version is an optional vendor-specified informational piece of metadata that is associated with the service
account. To track when a piece of software changes, VCF Automation uses the software version. The software version
might be useful for identifying a service account.
7. (Optional) Enter a client URI.
The client Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) is a URL to the webpage of the vendor and provides information about the
client.
8. Optional: To keep the refresh token valid, turn off the Require Rotation toggle.
By default, Require Rotation is enabled for service accounts. This means that after each access token request,
the current refresh token becomes invalid. Instead, a new refresh token is provided which then must be used for
subsequent requests.
Broadcom 7140

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Note:
You cannot change this setting later.
9. Click Next.
10.Review the service account information, and click Finish.
Grant Access to a Service Account in Your VCF Automation Organization
After you create a service account and the application requests authorization to receive an access token, you can grant
the token by using the VCF Automation organization UI.
1. Copy the client ID from the service account details.
2. Verify that the application requesting the account makes an OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant RFC-compliant
request to the endpoint.
https://site.cloud.example.com/oauth/provider/device_authorizationAPI
For more information on device authorization requests, see RFC 8628 section 3.1.
Once the application requests access, the service account status changes to Requested. The application receives the
device code, user code, and some additional information.
Run the following curl command to initiate the authorization request. Replace the client_id with your service
account client ID.
<organization-host>
curl --location 'https:// /oauth/tenant/exampleTenant/device_authorization' \
--header 'Accept: application/json;version=40.0' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
<client-id>
--data-urlencode 'client_id= '
The system returns a and a . You use the in the organization to grant access.
user_code device_code user_code
Sample response:
{
<device-code>
"device_code": " ",
<user-code>
"user_code": " ",
<organization-host>
"verification_uri": " /automation/#/administer/access",
"expires_in": 3600,
"interval": 60
}
The device must poll at the frequency that is specified in the above response (in seconds)
/oauth/provider/
as per the RFC. The device must use the device code until it receives the tokens from VCF Automation, or the
token
request times out.
Sample request:
<organization-host>
curl --location 'https:// /oauth/tenant/exampleTenant/token' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode 'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code' \
<client-id>
--data-urlencode 'client_id= ' \
<device-code>
--data-urlencode 'device_code= '
The response includes the . The application must use this token for all subsequent API requests.
access_token
{
<access-token>
"access_token": " ",
"token_type": "Bearer",
"expires_in": 3600,
<refresh-token>
"refresh_token": " "
}
If you do not confirm or deny an access request, the user code times out. The timeout period appears in the response
of the device authorization request.
VCF Automation grants a primary API token to the application only if the application and the administrator use the
device code and user code corresponding to each other.
3. Get the user code from the application. You must enter the code in step 4.
Broadcom 7141

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Administer > Access Control > Service Accounts.
3. Click Review Access Requests.
4. Enter the user code for the application that you obtained in prerequisite 3, click Lookup, and verify the requested
access details.
Тhe user code is valid for one hour.
5. Grant access to the application.
If you deny access to the application, the service account status changes back to .
Created
You can now use the service account to request tokens from VCF Automation.
You can use the access token as bearer token for API requests. The access token expires after one hour and after that
you can use the refresh token to generate a new access token.
The refresh token for service accounts does not expire. However, the refresh token becomes invalid if one access token
was generated and the new refresh token must be used for the next request instead. To disable this behavior, disable
“Require Rotation” as explained in the related section above.
Managing Networking in VCF Automation Organizations
As an organization administrator, you can view what networking infrastructure is assigned to your organization by the
provider administrator and you can manage networking infrastructure within the organization.
VPC Network Stacks
When your provider administrator creates a region, they set a network stack for the region. The network stack of a region
determines which networking features are available. You can view the network stack of a specific zone within the available
regions on the Regions page in your organization.
VCF Automation organizations can use two types of network stacks:
• Full-stack VPC. Workload domains use Tunnel Endpoint (TEP) overlay networking, where traffic between hosts is
encapsulated in VXLAN tunnels. Supports private subnets, private IP address blocks, NAT, and default SNAT.
• VLAN-backed VPC. Workload domains are configured as VLAN-backed, meaning traffic between hosts travels
directly over the physical VLAN fabric without overlay encapsulation. Supports public subnets and VLAN extension
subnets only. No private IP addressing, NAT, or SNAT.
Note:
VCF Automation 9.1.1 introduces support for organizations in VLAN-backed (TEP-less) networking. If your
provider administrator configured your region with VLAN-backed workload domains, your organization uses
VLAN-backed VPC networking.
All zones in a region must use the same network stack, either full-stack VPC or VLAN-backed VPC. Zone types cannot be
mixed within the same organization region.
The following table summarizes the networking capabilities that are available to you depending on the type of network
stack in your organization.
VLAN-backed VPC (VCF Automation
Capability Full-stack VPC (VCF Automation 9.1+)
9.1.1+)
External connections Centralized or Distributed VLAN Distributed VLAN only
Private subnets Supported Not supported
Public subnets Supported Supported
VLAN extension subnets Supported Supported
Private TGW IP blocks Supported Not available
Broadcom 7142

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
VLAN-backed VPC (VCF Automation
Capability Full-stack VPC (VCF Automation 9.1+)
9.1.1+)
Private VPC IP address blocks Supported Not available
NAT (VPC and TGW) Supported Not available
Default SNAT Supported Not available
IPSec VPN Supported (centralized connections only) Not available
External IP address blocks Supported Supported
Load balancing Supported Supported (via Virtual Network Appliances)
For more information about supported workload networking modes, see Workload Connectivity Detailed Design in the
VMware Cloud Foundation Design Guide.
Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs)
A virtual private cloud (VPC) provides an isolated domain of networking resources that can be associated with one or
more namespaces. You can create VPCs for your organization and associate each VPC with one or more namespaces.
You can create a new VPC for each namespace or you can use the same VPC for multiple namespaces.
Important:
VCF Automation is compatible only with supervisors with NSX VPCs. For more information about networking, see
Virtual Private Cloud in the NSX documentation.
Each VPC can leverage three different types of IP blocks that each have different levels of reachability:
• Private CIDRs are local to the VPC and require NAT to connect to any resources outside of the VPC. These CIDRs do
not need to be unique across multiple VPCs.
• Transit gateway (TGW) private IP blocks are only advertised within the VCF Automation organization and its TGW.
The available IP blocks are defined by the organization administrator. Project administrators can allocate subnets
from within the defined IP blocks for use in their VPCs. These IPs have direct reachability to other VPCs within the
organization using the TGW private IP space.
• External IP blocks are managed by the provider administrator. IPs in this space are used for outbound Source NAT to
enable external reachability for workloads using private IPs. Organization administrators can assign subnets within the
external IP blocks by the allocations defined by the provider.
The Network Service can be used to create, update, manage, and delete resources within the VPC by organization
administrators and advanced project users.
Connectivity Profiles
A connectivity profile is a template that allows simplified configuration of new VPCs. A default connectivity profile is
configured by the provider administrator to simplify the initial organization configuration. You can provide one or more
external and private transit gateway IP address blocks that are used by VPCs configured with a specific connectivity
profile.
In full-stack VPC regions, a connectivity profile can include external IPv4 blocks and private TGW IPv4 blocks. In VLAN-
backed VPC regions, only external IPv4 blocks are available.
Transit Gateways (TGWs)
A transit gateway (TGW) provides both inter-VPC communication within the organization and connection to the outside
world through external connections. The provider administrator defines external connections and makes them available to
your organization.
One or more VPCs are connected to the transit gateway, and that connection is defined by a VPC connectivity profile.
Each VPC has connected workloads and, optionally, a private subnet. SNAT rules translate addresses from this private
subnet to a public address in the IP spaces block. This infrastructure enables the organization and its workloads to
connect to external networks.
The type of external connections available to a transit gateway depends on the region's network stack.
Broadcom 7143

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• In full-stack VPC regions, a transit gateway can connect through one of two types of external connections:
– Centralized connections link to an NSX Tier-0 or Tier-0 VRF gateway, with IP addresses advertised from those
gateways.
– Distributed VLAN connections use VLAN fabric for high-performance distributed routing.
A transit gateway can have one or more centralized connections or one or more distributed connections, but cannot
mix centralized and distributed connections on the same gateway.
• In VLAN-backed VPC regions, transit gateways use a distributed VXLAN connection (DVC) for external connectivity
instead of centralized or distributed VLAN connections. A DVC uses EVPN-VXLAN fabric through a Virtual Network
Appliance (VNA) cluster and is provisioned by the provider administrator.
Every organization comes with a default transit gateway per region, created by the provider administrator. Organization
administrators can also create transit gateways as needed. See Create a Transit Gateway in VCF Automation.
You can also manage IP addresses that the provider administrator made available to you and create IP addresses that
are specific to your organization. See IP Address Management in VCF Automation Organizations.
Subnets
A subnet is a subdivision of a VPC that defines a range of IP addresses.
There are three primary subnet types available to organization administrators depending on whether your region uses full-
stack VPC (standard TEP-based) or VLAN-backed VPC (TEP-less) networking.
• Private subnets are scoped to the VPC and routed with other subnets inside the same VPC, they have no direct path
to the outside network. If outside communication is required, you must configure NAT rules on the transit gateway.
Private CIDRs are local to the VPC and do not need to be unique across multiple VPCs. Private subnets that are
scoped to the transit gateway allow inter-VPC connectivity below the transit gateway without NAT. Private subnets are
available in full-stack VPC regions only.
Note:
Private subnets are not available in VLAN-backed VPC regions in VCF Automation 9.1.1. Private IP addressing is
not supported in VLAN-backed mode because the physical VLAN fabric does not allow private IPs.
• Public subnets are accessible from outside the environment, from other VPCs, and also from customers and workloads
above the transit gateway. IP addresses are allocated from external IP blocks managed by the provider administrator
and assigned to the organization's connectivity profile. Public subnets are available in both full-stack VPC and VLAN-
backed VPC regions.
• VLAN extension subnets extend the broadcast domains of the physical fabric directly to the organization so that
organization users can connect their workloads to an existing VLAN without overlay encapsulation. The gateway
resides in the physical network, not inside the VPC. VLAN extension subnets can only be public. VLAN extension
subnets are available in both full-stack VPC and VLAN-backed VPC regions. In VLAN-backed mode, VLAN extension
subnets map directly to a Distributed VXLAN Connection (DVC) and use the DVC's CIDR for IP allocation. The entire
CIDR block is allocated to the subnet.
Subnets can be shared. Organization administrators can create private or public subnets for their organizations and share
them across namespaces, allowing multiple namespaces to access the same network. Provider administrators can create
VLAN extension subnets and share them with multiple organizations.
Project users can use the Network service to create subnets in VPCs that are associated with their namespaces. These
subnets are used for that namespace only.
In VLAN-backed mode, shared subnets serve as the default network for pods and VMs in namespaces. When creating a
namespace in a VLAN-backed VPC region, you must add at least one shared subnet and can optionally designate it as
the default network.
Avi Load Balancer
In VCF Automation organizations that have regions with Avi Load Balancer enabled, each namespace is associated with
a designated Avi service engine group (SEG), which defines how Avi service engines are sized, placed, and made highly
available.
Broadcom 7144

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Depending on requirements, the provider administrator can extend Avi load-balancing capabilities to your VCF Automation
organization by enabling service engine groups for one or multiple regions that are available organization. Service engine
groups allow configuration and management of load-balancing resources for applications.
Each namespace is associated with a SEG. Applications that are deployed within a namespace automatically gain access
to load-balancing capabilities. Project users can deploy load balancers using the Avi Load Balancer service and access
Avi analytics to monitor performance and troubleshoot their applications.
There are two modes in which the organization interacts with SEGs:
• Provider-managed SEGs. The provider administrator creates, manages, and distributes service engine groups to the
organization.
• Organization-managed SEGs. The provider administrator delegates the creation and management of SEGs to the
organization administrator, giving them more control over how resources are allocated. See Create a Service Engine
Group in the Avi Load Balancer for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 guide.
For more information about using the Avi Load Balancer integration with VCF Automation, see the Avi Load Balancer for
VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 guide.
vDefend Firewall
VCF Automation 9.1 integrates with vDefend Firewall. Depending on the organization structure and responsibilities,
the provider administrator manages firewalls for the organization or they can delegate this task to the organization
administrator.
Organization administrators or users with appropriate privileges can then create firewall policies for the following:
• Secure inbound and outbound connectivity to project resources.
• Enforce firewall rules to secure applications between VPCs and within individual VPCs.
• Secure connectivity between applications across VPCs and within a VPC.
• Connect to other organizations or shared services in other organizations.
• Secure connectivity to VPCs across projects.
Organization administrators can configure two types of vDefend Firewall policies.
• vDefend Distributed Firewall policies to control inter- and intra-VPC communications.
• vDefend Gateway Firewall policies on NSX transit gateways and VPCs to control inbound/outbound communication
with the provider gateway.
Project administrators can also configure gateway firewalls for VPCs dedicated to namespaces in their projects.
For more information about using vDefend Firewall in VCF Automation, see the VCF Automation Integration with vDefend
Firewall guide.
Best Practices for Organization Networking
• Effectively using VPCs. VPCs offer networking isolation. As an organization administrator, you can create VPCs and
reserve them for use by certain namespaces and projects or share VPCs with all organization users. You can review
the following sections for examples for effectively using VPCs to fit your organization needs.
– For information about using a single VPC for the entire organization, see Multi-Tenancy Consumption Pattern
1: Resource Isolation with Single VPC for Multiple Businesses in One Supervisor Zone in the VMware Cloud
Foundation Design Guide.
– For information about how each Line of Business, represented as a VCF Automation project, can use a dedicated
VPC, see Multi-Tenancy Consumption Pattern 2: Resource Isolation with Multiple VPCs for Multiple Lines of
Business in One Supervisor Zone in the VMware Cloud Foundation Design Guide.
• Planning for IP blocks and quotas. To learn more about workload networking and how to plan for IP blocks, see
Understanding Workload Networking in the VMware Cloud Foundation Design Guide.
Create a Subnet in a VCF Automation Organization
As an organization administrator, you can create subnets in your organization and share them across namespace so that
multiple namespaces can leverage the same network.
Broadcom 7145

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Review what regions are available to your organization on the Regions page.
• Verify that a connectivity profile is defined for the region in which you want to create the subnet. If the region does not
have a connectivity profile, you can create one at the time of creating the subnet. See Create a Connectivity Profile in
VCF Automation.
• Verify that you have a VPC. See Create a Virtual Private Cloud in VCF Automation.
In addition to the VPC that a namespace is mapped to, each namespace can have subnets created from other VPCs that
might be used across namespaces. While connectivity within the VPC is guaranteed, subnets from multiple VPCs might
not reach one another, which allows workflows involving virtual machines with multiple NICs.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Networking > Subnets and click New Subnet.
3. Select a region.
You can select from regions that the provider administrator made available to your organization.
Important:
If the region you select has VLAN-backed VPC networking, the UI automatically detects VLAN-backed mode. The
networking settings that are available to you change depending on the type of region you selected.
4. Select a VPC from the region.
Based on your VPC selection, a name is generated for the subnet. You can provide a new name.
5. Optional: Change the name that was generated for the subnet.
6. For VLAN-backed regions, leave the VLAN Connection toggle on, select a distributed external connection, and
continue with Step 10b.
If you turn off the VLAN Connection toggle, you configure the subnet manually. Continue with Step 8.
7. Select an access mode to apply to the subnet.
Note:
In VLAN-backed regions in VCF Automation 9.1.1, only public subnets are available.
Option Description
Private - VPC The subnet is scoped to the VPC and routed with other subnets
inside the same VPC, but not to the outside network. If outside
communication is required, you must configure NAT rules. See
Create a NAT Rule for a Transit Gateway in VCF Automation.
Private - Transit Gateway The subnet allows inter-VPC connectivity below the transit
gateway without NAT. If workloads must be reachable to an
outside network, IP translation is required.
Public The subnet is accessible from outside the environment, from
other VPCs, and also from customers and workloads above the
transit gateway.
8. Specify IP blocks.
If there is at least one IP block configured in the selected VPC, by default, the IP block is set to Any, which means
VCF Automation picks any of the available IP blocks based on the allocation mode you select in the next step.
You can also use a specific IP block if you want to ensure the CIDR is picked from that block only.
For public access mode, you can select from IP blocks attached to the connectivity profile of the VPC and VLAN
extension IP blocks that are not related to any VPC. An IP block configured with VLAN extension allocates the entire
CIDR block to the subnet and is intended for VLAN extension use cases.
9. If you want to auto-allocate the IP block, turn on the toggle.
• If you enable automatic IP block allocation, select an IP block size.
Broadcom 7146

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• If you disable automatic IP block allocation, enter the IP CIDR.
10.Configure advanced settings.
a) To enable gateway connectivity, turn on the toggle.
When gateway connectivity is on, the subnet is connected to the VPC gateway.
In scenarios that require fully subnet isolation, turn the gateway connectivity toggle off.
Note:
In VLAN-backed regions in VCF Automation 9.1.1, you cannot change gateway connectivity.
b) To enable static IP allocation, turn on the toggle.
If you do not want to enable static IP allocation, turn off the toggle and specify DHCP settings.
11.Click Create.
• Share the subnet with a namespace. Workloads that are provisioned on the namespace can use the subnet.
– To add the subnet to an existing namespace, see Edit Namespace Settings in VCF Automation.
– To create a new namespace using the subnet, see Create a Namespace in a VCF Automation Project.
• Once you share the subnet with a namespace, verify that the subnet is listed for that namespace. In the Services
section on the Build & Deploy tab, select the namespace, and open the Network service. On the Subnets tab, you
can view a list of associated subnets and can create subnets that are scoped to this namespace only.
• Project users can now use the subnet when provisioning workloads to the namespace.
Create a Connectivity Profile in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you can create, update, and delete VPC connectivity profiles in VCF Automation.
• Review what regions are available to your organization on the Regions page. You create the connectivity profile in a
region that is allocated to your organization.
Your organization comes with а default connectivity profile. As an organization administrator, you can create additional
connectivity profiles to use in your organization if, for example, you need to configure different external and/or private IP
address blocks.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.

If the region you select has VLAN-backed VPC networking, the UI automatically detects VLAN-backed mode. The

Note:

Create a Virtual Private Cloud in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you can create, update, and delete virtual private cloud (VPC) configurations in your
organization.
• Review what regions are available to your organization on the Regions page. You create the VPC in a region that is
allocated to your organization.
• Verify that a connectivity profile is defined for the region in which you want to create the VPC. If the region does not
have a connectivity profile, you can create one at the time of creating the VPC. See Create a Connectivity Profile in
VCF Automation.
• If you want to apply an IP quota to the VPC, verify that you have an IP quota defined. See IP Address Management in
VCF Automation Organizations.
The VPC is associated with a region where namespaces are provisioned. A single VPC can be shared by multiple
namespaces.
In full-stack VPC regions, VPCs use standard TEP overlay networking and support the full range of IP addressing, subnet
types, and network services. When you create a VPC in a full-stack VPC region, you can configure private VPC IPv4
CIDR blocks, private TGW IPv4 blocks, external IPv4 blocks, NAT rules, gateway firewall, static routes, and VPN on the
transit gateway, as well as NAT and gateway firewall on the VPC itself. You can create private subnets, public subnets,
and VLAN extension subnets.
In VLAN-backed VPC region, the available configuration options are restricted because the physical VLAN fabric does not
support private IP addressing or overlay encapsulation. Some fields and services are not available and do not appear in
the UI during VPC creation.
As an organization administrator, you can delegate project administrators the ability to either consume specific VPCs or
create their own VPCs within constraints that you set.
Namespace users can request external IPs for 1:1 NAT in order to have direct external access to a VM.
Your organization comes with a preconfigured VPC and a connectivity profile. You can use these defaults to connect
networking workloads, or you can create new ones using the steps in this procedure.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator or a project administrator with the
necessary permissions.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Networking > Virtual Private Clouds and click New VPC.
3. Enter the VPC name.
4. Select a region.
You can select from regions that the provider administrator made available to your organization.
Broadcom 7148

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
5. Select an existing connectivity profile defined for the region you selected in the previous step, or create a new
connectivity profile.
a) If you choose to create a new connectivity profile, enter a name.
b) Select a transit gateway.
c) Optional: For full-stack VPC regions, select external IPv4 blocks and Private TGW IPv4 blocks.
Note:
Private TGW IPv4 blocks are not available in VLAN-backed VPC regions. Only external IPv4 blocks can be
selected.
6. For full-stack VPC regions, specify private VPC IPv4 CIDR blocks.
Note:
For VLAN-backed VPC regions, skip step 6. Private VPC IPv4 CIDR blocks are not supported.
7. Expand the Advanced Settings section.
8. Optional: Select IP quotas to apply to the VPC.
9. Optional: To enable load balancing for the VPC, turn on the toggle.
If you disable load balancing, you cannot use vSphere Kubernetes Service.
10.Click Create.
To edit existing VPCs, click the vertical ellipsis next to the VPC name and then click Edit.

Create a NAT Rule for a VPC in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you can create NAT rules for VPCs in your organization.
Your organization comes with a default VPC that has a default Source NAT rule. The default NAT is read only, but you can
add new rules for the default VPC.
Broadcom 7149

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Networking > Virtual Private Clouds.
3. On the VPCs tab, select the VPC you want to create the rule for.
4. On the details page, select the NAT tab.
5. Click Add NAT Rule.
6. Enter a name for the rule.
7. Select an action.
Based on the action you select, the infographic on the right changes to visualize the rule.
• SNAT translates a source IP address of outbound packets so that packets appear as originating from a different
network. Supported on Tier-0/Tier-1 gateways running in active-standby mode.
• DNAT translates the destination IP address of inbound packets so that packets are delivered to a target address
into another network.
• Reflexive NAT translates addresses passing through a routing device.
8. To enable the NAT rule, turn on the toggle.
9. In the Source section, enter the source IP and port.
This defines the source network of the packets leaving the network for SNAT, NO SNAT, and Reflexive rules.
10.In the Destination section, enter the destination IP, port, and protocol.
This defines the source network of the packets leaving the network for DNAT and NO DNAT rules.
The destination IP has to be allocated from the external IP block associated with the VPC. You can use an IP block
that was allocated to your organization or you can request a new one.
a) Click Request IP.
The Request IP/CIDR window appears.
b) Select an IP address block to use for allocation.
c) To enable auto-allocation from the IP block, turn on the toggle.
If you disable auto-allocation, manually specify an IP address. Click View IPs to view available IP addresses you
can use.
d) Click Request.
11.In the Translation section, enter an IPv4 address or an IP address range in CIDR format, and port.
12.Expand the Advanced Settings section.
13.To enable logging, turn on the toggle.
Logs are only available to organization administrators.
14.Enter a priority value.
By default, priority is set to 0. A lower value indicates a higher priority.
No SNAT and No DNAT rules must have a higher priority than other rules.
15.Configure a firewall.
You can choose
• Match External Address. Applies the firewall to the external address of the NAT rule.
• Match Internal Address. Applies the firewall to the internal address of the NAT rule.
• Bypass. Policy-based VPN traffic bypasses the NAT rule.
16.Click Create.
You can edit and delete the NAT rules that you created.

Managing Projects in VCF Automation
Projects in VCF Automation organizations provide a logical grouping of users and the infrastructure that they are
assigned. Projects are used to represent real-world teams which are in charge of development or operations. Each project
has one or more namespaces assigned to it. Each namespace is an envelope of resources where applications can be
deployed. Access controls for projects are governed by pre-defined roles.
Project Concepts
Namespaces and Projects. Organization administrators can create and attach one or more namespaces to a project.
Administrators can also delete a namespace at any time, which dissociates the namespace from the project. Every
organization comes with a default project. The default project doesn’t have users or namespaces. The organization
administrator can change the name, description of the default project, and add users and namespaces to the default
project.
If the organization administrator enables namespace self-service for a given project, the project administrators can also
create namespaces in that project. Self-service namespaces have their own view and manage permissions.
Namespace Class. A namespace class is a template that is used to create namespaces. All components of a
namespace, including limits on CPU, memory, and storage utilization, VM classes and storage classes, and content
libraries can be defined as a reusable template. Namespace classes are created and maintained by organization
administrators.
Namespaces and Resource Limits. Infrastructure quota assigned to an organization can be subdivided and assigned
to project teams in the form of namespaces. Namespaces are isolated resource pools in which resources like VMs, VKS
clusters, and volumes can be provisioned. Organization administrators can override the resource limits specified in a
namespace class during namespace creation.
Broadcom 7158

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Namespaces and Zones. The resource limits of a namespace can be satisfied from capacity in one or more vSphere
zones. When creating a namespace, organization administrators can select which zones the namespace can use.
Namespaces and Organization Quotas. Namespaces count towards the organization quota. The sum of resource limits
of all created namespaces cannot exceed the organization quota.
Best Practices for Projects
How many projects and namespaces you create depends on your organization needs.
• Projects. Multiple projects are used when isolation boundaries between project teams are required. Only project
members can access deployments and resources available to a project. Fewer projects are desired when isolation
requirements can be traded off for a simpler operating model. For more information, see Understanding Organizations
and Projects in the VMware Cloud Foundation Design Guide.
• Namespaces. Multiple namespaces are used when strict resource limits are needed for each application.
Namespaces are logical constructs that can be used to define application boundaries. Each application can be
deployed on a namespace with prescribed resource limits for CPU, memory, and storage. For instance, a group of
VMs and VKS clusters that make up an application can be logically grouped in a namespace. For more information,
see Understanding Supervisors, Regions, Zones & vSphere Namespaces in the VMware Cloud Foundation Design
Guide.
Create a Project in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you create a project to which you add users and namespaces so that project members
can deploy VMs and other resources to the associated zones. You can assign a project administrator or you can operate
as the project administrator.
This procedure is based on creating an initial project that includes only the basic configurations. As your application team
deploys their resources, you might modify the project.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Projects and click New.
3. Enter the project name and click Next.
4. (Optional) Add users or user groups and assign roles.
At this stage, you can add, for example, a project administrator only and let them add more users to the project.
User roles based on groups allow users to come and go from your identity provider rather than requiring the project
administrator to constantly update the individual users in the project. For example, if deployment ownership is based
on groups, you can change the ownership of a deployment to the group. Any notifications are sent to all the group
members, allowing anyone to respond.
For more information about user roles, see Organization and Project Role Permissions in for All Apps.
5. Click Next.
6. Review your project and click Create Project.
Add namespaces to your project. Namespaces can be added to a project at any time. See Create a Namespace in a VCF
Automation Project.
Assign Project Roles to Users and Groups in VCF Automation
As an organization administrator, you assign project roles to users in your organization so that they can view and provision
project resources.
• Users and user groups have been imported from a valid identity provider instance that is associated with your VCF
Automation organization. Managing Identity Providers in for All Apps
• Users and user groups have been assigned organization roles. Add Users Role Assignments in for All Apps
• Verify that you have a project. See Create a Project in for All Apps.
• For a more detailed task and role list for various roles, see Organization and Project Role Permissions in for All Apps.
Broadcom 7159

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Projects.
3. Open the project to which you want to add users.
4. On the Users tab, click Add Users or Add Groups.
5. Enter the names or email addresses of the users or groups you want to add.
For example, tony@mycompany.com, sylvia@mycompany.com.
If you are adding users, you can import a CSV list.
6. Assign a role to the users or groups.
7. Click Add.
Managing Namespaces in VCF Automation Projects
In VCF Automation, resources like networks, namespace classes, and namespace services are owned and provisioned by
the organization administrator. Project administrators can consume these shared resources in a self-service manner within
the boundaries of their own project.
In order for project administrators to be able to create namespaces for their projects, the organization administrator
first sets up self-service for the project. The self-service settings govern how a namespace is created by the project
administrator, including what shared resources can be used and what templates are available for them to create their own
resources, like dedicated VPCs.
As an organization administrator, you enable self-service namespace creation in a project. Once self-service is set up
for the project, project administrators can create namespaces within the available limitations. These namespaces can be
captured as blueprints and released to the catalog for project users to deploy.
Project administrators create namespaces for their projects using the allocated resource configurations, like regions,
namespace classes, VPCs, and subnets. They cannot modify the assigned namespace classes, VPCs, and regions.
Project administrators can then capture the namespaces they created for their projects as blueprints and release them to
the VCF Automation catalog.
Project users can request these catalog items to deploy namespaces. Their deployments are also limited to what was
allocated to the project.
Create a Namespace Class in VCF Automation
To enable the creation of new namespaces, you use a namespace class as a parameterized template that defines the
settings and requirements for the namespace. As an organization administrator, you can create namespace classes to
define the settings and requirements for namespaces that you add for your organization.
Review what regions are available to your organization on the Regions page.
The namespace class references the VM classes and storage classes and optional content libraries to attach to the
namespace. When you specify VM classes and storage classes, all the available VM classes and storage classes that are
associated with the selected zones are added to the created namespace.
When your organization is first created, the following namespace classes are created by default.
Namespace Class CPU Limit Memory Limit
small 10 GHz 10 GB (9.77 GB useable)
medium 20 GHz 20 GB (19.53 GB useable)
large 40 GHz 40 GB (39.06 GB useable)
These default namespace classes include all VM classes that are available in the region.
You can use the default namespace classes as they are or you can modify them as needed. You can also create new
namespace classes using the following procedure.
Broadcom 7160

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Namespace Class and click New.
3. Enter a name and, optionally, a description for the namespace class.
4. Click Next.
5. Define CPU and memory limits.
You configure limits and reservations per zone.
To apply resource limits and reservations across all available zones in bulk, select the Add all zones and apply the
same limits and reservations to all zones and enter the respective values.
a) Click Add.
b) Select a zone.
c) For limits, enter the maximum amount of CPU and memory that can be consumed in each namespace.
d) Optional: For reservations, enter the minimum amount of CPU and memory that you want to guarantee for each
namespace.
e) Click Save.
6. Click Next.
7. Add VM classes.
VM classes define how much memory, CPU, or certain capabilities a VM has.
a) In the VM Classes section, click Add.
b) Select the classes that you want to use.
To apply classes in bulk, turn on the Select all available VM classes toggle.
c) Click Add.
8. Add storage classes.
Storage classes define the storage policies and the quota that is assigned in a region.
When you select a storage class, the namespace class is automatically associated with a region that is allocated to
your organization. Later on, when you create a namespace using this namespace class, the region is automatically
selected.
a) In the Storage Classes section, click Add.
b) Select a storage class.
c) Define a storage limit.
d) To apply the storage limit to all available classes in bulk, turn on the Select all available storage classes toggle.
e) Click Add.
9. Click Next.
10.Optional: Add a content library.
A content library is automatically assigned to the namespace class. The namespace class may also specify the names
of configured content libraries that are not automatically attached so that they are also attached.
Organization content libraries can be set to automatically attach to namespaces or not. If there are no content
libraries set to not attach to namespaces, the content library selector is empty. Provider content libraries are always
automatically shared with namespaces and namespace classes.
Broadcom 7161

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
a) Click Add.
b) Select content libraries.
c) Click Add.
11.Click Next.
12.Review your configuration and click Create.
You can now create a namespace using your new namespace class. See Create a Namespace in a VCF Automation
Project.
Enable Namespace Self-Service for Projects in Your VCF Automation
Organization
As an organization administrator, you can allow project administrators to create namespaces in the projects that they
manage. You use a namespace class to define the limits to be applied to a new namespace. Project аdministrators can
then create namespaces using the available resources.
• Review what regions are available to your organization on the Regions page. Namespaces are created in a region that
is allocated to the organization.
• Verify you have the necessary type of networking.
– If you plan to allow the creation of namespace with shared VPCs, verify that you have a VPC. See Create a Virtual
Private Cloud in VCF Automation.
– If you plan to allow the creation of namespaces with dedicated VPCs, verify that you have a connectivity profile. See
Create a Connectivity Profile in VCF Automation.
• Verify that you have a namespace class. See Create a Namespace Class in for All Apps.
• Verify that you have a project. See Create a Project in for All Apps.
• Verify that you assigned a project administrator to the project for which you want to configure self-service.
By giving project administrators the abiity to create namespaces on a self-service basis, you allow them to operate
independently. Namespace self-service is enabled on a project basis.
There is no limit to the number of namespaces that project administrators can create in the project as long as the sum
total of resources used by all namespaces does not exceed the quota for the organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Projects.
3. Select the project for which you want to enable self-service.
4. Click the Namespace Self-Service tab.
5. Click Configure Namespace Self-Service.
6. Select the regions where project administrators can create namespaces and click Next.
7. Select namespace classes that can be used to create namespaces and click Next.
8. Select a networking type and click Next.
You can select one or both options.
a) To allow the usage of shared VPCs in the project, select the check box and then select from the available VPCs.
b) To allow the creation of dedicated VPCs in the project, select the check box and then select from the list of
available connectivity profiles.
9. Optional: Select shared subnets that project workloads can connect to and click Next.
10.Optional: Select infrastructure policies for the namespace and click Next.
Infrastructure policies ensure that VMs provisioned in the namespace are placed appropriately under the underlying
infrastructure to meet specific requirements. Infrastructure policies are created and assigned to your organization by
the provider administrator.
Broadcom 7162

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Project administrators creating namespaces can choose which of the available policies to apply. Project users
provisioning workloads in these namespaces can select which policies to apply to their deployments.
11.Select service engine groups (SEGs) to assign to the project and click Next.
SEGs allow configuration and management of load-balancing resources for applications. Each namespace is
associated with a SEG so applications that are deployed within a namespace automatically gain access to load-
balancing capabilities.
You can configure service engine groups only if the region you selected in Step 6 has Avi Load Balancer enabled.
Otherwise, you don't see the option to configure SEGs.
12.Review your configuration and click Submit.
Project administrators can now create namespaces in this project.

Organization
As an organization administrator, you can configure the self-service namespace settings for projects in your organization.
You assign the resources that project administrators use when creating namespaces which defines the infrastructure
components that are available within the project scope.
When you configure self-service settings for a project, you assign regions, namespace classes, and networking resources
that the project can use. With these settings in place, you create guardrails for all namespaces created within this project,
while giving project administrators flexibility.
You can add multiple resources at a time. When you no longer want a resource to be available, you can remove it.

b) Select namespace classes that can be used to create namespaces.

You can select from VPCs that are available to the regions associated with the project.

In VLAN-backed organizations, only public subnets can be used in VPCs. Because private subnets are unavailable,

Note:
You cannot remove a subnet from a namespace while workloads are using it. To remove a subnet, first remove or

a) Under Associated Subnets, click Add.
b) Select a subnet.

As an organization administrator, you can also set resource limits on individual namespaces. See Edit Namespace

Create a Namespace in a VCF Automation Project
As a project administrator, you can create namespaces in the projects that you manage. You can then publish them as
blueprints to the catalog where users in your project can request and deploy them.
• Verify that your organization administrator enabled self-service namespaces for your project. See Enable Namespace
Self-Service for Projects in Your VCF Automation Organization.
• Review the available resources for your project on the Self-Service Settings tab.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as a project administrator.
2. Select Manage & Govern > Projects.
As an organization administrator, you can select Manage & Govern > Namespaces and click New Namespace. In
this case, you must also select a project to associate with the namespace.
Broadcom 7164

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
3. Select the project for which you want to create a namespace.
4. On the Namespaces tab, click New Namespace.
5. Enter a name and description for the namespace.
A unique suffix is added to the name you enter. For example, if the name you entered is , upon
mynamespace
creation, the namespace might be called .
mynamespace-abcxyz
The name must be up to 63 characters long.
6. Select a namespace class.
The namespace inherits the configuration of the namespace class.
7. Select a region.
The region groups the resources that are allocated to the organization.
Note:
If the region you select has VLAN-backed VPC networking, the UI automatically detects VLAN-backed mode and
hides some of the networking settings.
8. Select at least one zone.
9. Select a networking type.
• Shared VPC. Select a VPC that was created by the organization administrator. The VPC can be shared between
multiple namespaces across the organization. Project administrators can create subnets for namespaces in shared
VPCs.
• Dedicated VPC. Create a VPC that is dedicated only to this namespace. You can edit VPC settings like NAT,
gateway firewall, and static routes. You can also create subnets for namespaces associated with this VPC.
If you want to use a dedicated VPC for this namespace, you must also select a connectivity profile and enter IP
blocks.
Note:
Dedicated VPCs are not available in VLAN-backed organizations. The namespace must use a shared VPC.
10.Optional: Attach shared VPC subnets.
You can share a subnet with the namespace later on as a day 2 action.
Shared subnets are created by the organization administrator in other VPCs and are shared with the project when the
organization administrator configures self-service for the project.
In VLAN-backed VPCs, you must add at least one shared subnet to the namespace. If the Shared Subnets list is
empty, the UI displays the following warning: "Set at least one shared subnet for this TEP-less Namespace, otherwise
workloads in this Namespace will have no networking."
11.Optional: Set default networks.
You can set default subnets so that workloads can be configured without specifying a network. These subnets must
belong to the VPC used by the namespace where workloads are provisioned. You cannot designate a default network
on a subnet that belongs to a different VPC.
• Default VM Network. The subnet the namespace uses by default when a VM is provisioned without an explicit
network.
• Default Pod Network. The subnet the namespace uses by default for pods.
• Default VM and Pod. The subnet serves as both VM and pod default network.

namespace.

SEGs define how the Avi service engines are sized, placed, and made highly available.
14.Review the namespace summary on the right.

In the Services section, you can access all services that are enabled for the namespace, for example, VM Service,
Kubernetes Services, Volume Service, and so on. To access a service, click the respective tile.

Resources.
• To manage a namespace, go to the Build & Deploy tab and select the namespace from the dropdown in the Services
