How do I create an Active Directory integration in VCF Automation for VM Apps
VCF Automation supports integration with Active Directory servers to provide out of the box creation of computer accounts
in a specified Organizational Unit (OU) within an Active Directory server prior to provisioning a virtual machine. Active
Directory supports an LDAP connection to the Active Directory server.
• Active Directory integration requires an LDAP connection to the Active Directory server.
• If you are configuring an integration with Active Directory in the cloud, you must have a Microsoft Azure or Amazon
Web Services account.
• You must have a project configured with appropriate cloud zones, and image and flavor mappings to use with the
Active Directory integration.
• The desired OU on your Active Directory must be pre-created before you associated your Active Directory integration
with a project.
• The user configured for the Active Directory integration must have permissions to create/delete/search for computer
objects in the configured OU.
An Active Directory policy that is associated with a project is applied to all virtual machines provisioned within the scope of
that project. Users can specify one or more tags to selectively apply the policy to virtual machines that are provisioned to
the cloud zones with matching capability tags.
When an Active Directory integration is created, some properties are set during the creation of the computer object in
Active Directory and cannot be changed. In particular, the following default properties cannot be changed:
WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT 0x1000
PASSWD_NOTREQD (No password is required) 0x0020
For on-premises deployments, Active Directory integration enables you to set up a health check feature that shows the
status of the integration and the underlying ABX integration on which it relies, including the required extensibility cloud
proxy. Prior to applying an Active Directory policy, VCF Automation checks the status of the underlying integrations. If
the integration is healthy, VCF Automation creates the deployed computer objects in the specified Active Directory. If the
integration is unhealthy, the deploy operation skips the Active Directory phase during provisioning.
1. Select Infrastructure > Connections > Integrations and then New Integration.
2. Click Active Directory.
3. On the Summary tab, enter the appropriate LDAP host and environment names.
The specified LDAP host is used to validate the Active Directory integration, and it is also used for subsequent
deployments if no alternative hosts are specified and invoked due to errors or unavailability.
4. Enter the name and password for the LDAP server.
5. Enter the appropriate Base DN that specifies the root for the desired Active Directory resources.
Note:
You can specify only one DN per Active Directory integration.
Broadcom 7637

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
6. Click Validate to ensure that the integration is functional.
7. Enter a Name and Description of this integration.
8. Click Save.
9. Click the Project tab to add a project to the Active Directory integration.
On the Add Projects dialog, you must select a project name and a relative DN, which is a DN that exists within the
Base DN specified on the Summary tab.
10.Under the Extended Options selection, provide a comma separated list of Alternate Hosts that will be used if the
initially selected server is unavailable during deployment. The primary server is always used for initial validation of the
integration.
Note:
If the format of the primary host is LDAP, LDAPS is not supported for alternative hosts.
11.Enter the time in seconds to wait for the initial server to respond before trying an alternate server in the Connection
Timeout box.
12.Click Save.
You can now associate the project with Active Directory integration to a cloud template. When a machine is provisioned
using this cloud template, it is pre-staged in the specified Active Directory and Organizational Unit.
Initially, Active Directory integrations are deployed to a default OU with little user restrictions. The OU is set by default
when you map an Active Directory integration to a project. You can add a property called to
FinalRelativeDN
blueprints to change the OU for Active Directory deployments. This property enables you to specify the OU to use with an
Active Directory deployment.
formatVersion: 1
inputs: {}
resources:
Cloud_vSphere_Machine_1:
type: Cloud.vSphere.Machine
properties:
image: CenOS8
flavor: tiny
activeDirectory:
finalRelativeDN: ou=test
securityGroup: TestSecurityGroup
As shown in the preceding YAML example, users can add a property to an Active Directory integration deployment
that adds a computer account to the security group so that appropriate permissions are assigned to access the shared
resource over a network. The Active Directory virtual machine is initially deployed to a fixed OU but when the machine is
ready to release, it is moved to a different OU with the appropriate policy as applicable for users.
If a computer account is moved to a different OU after deployment, VCF Automation attempts to delete the accounts on
the initial OU. Deletion of computer accounts succeeds only in the case of virtual machines moved to a different OU within
the same domain.
You can also implement a tag-based health check for on-premises Active Directory integrations as follows.
1. Create an Active Directory integration as described in the preceding steps.
2. Click the Project tab to add a project to the Active Directory integration.
3. Select a project name and a relative DN on the Add Projects dialog. The relative DN must exist within the specified
base DN.
There are two switches on this dialog that enable you to control Active Directory configuration from cloud templates.
Both switches are off by default.
– Override - This switch enables you to override Active Directory properties, specifically the relative DN in cloud
templates. When switched on, you can change the OU specified in the property in the cloud template.
relativeDN
When provisioned the machine will be added to the OU specified in the property in the cloud
relativeDN
template. The following example shows the cloud template hierarchy in which this property appears.
Broadcom 7638

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
activeDirectory:
relativeDN: OU=ad_integration_machine_override
– Ignore - This switch enables you to ignore the Active Directory configuration for the project. When switched on,
it adds a property to the cloud template called for the associated virtual machine.
ignoreActiveDirectory
When this property is set to true means that the machine is not added to the Active Directory when deployed.
4. Add appropriate tags. These tags are applicable to the cloud zone to which the Active Directory policy may apply.
5. Click Save.
The Status of the Active Directory integration is displayed for each integration on the Infrastructure > Connections >
Integrations page in VCF Automation.
You can associate the project with Active Directory integration with a cloud template. When a machine is provisioned
using this template, it is pre-staged in the specified Active Directory and OU.
Integrating with VCF Operations
VCF Automation can work with VCF Operations to perform advanced workload placement, provide deployment health and
virtual machine metrics, and display pricing.
Number and type of integrations
You can integrate one VCF Automation instance with one VCF Operations instance and eachVCF Operations instance
can only be connected to one VCF Automation instance.
Basic requirements for integration
To integrate with VCF Operations, go to Infrastructure > Connections > Integrations. To add the integration, you need
the VCF Operations URL and credentials for the login account described in the next section. In addition, VCF Automation
and VCF Operations need to manage the same vSphere endpoint.
VCF Operations integration credentials with VCF Automation
This section describes the credentials that are required to integrate with VCF Operations. These credentials are
established and configured in VCF Operations, not in VCF Automation.
Provide a local login account to VCF Operations with the following read privileges.
• Adapter Instance vCenter Adapter > VC Adapter Instance for vCenter-FQDN
Login account for integration
In VCF Operations, you need a local or non-local VCF Operations login account for the integration to use. The account
requires read-only privileges to the vCenter adapter instance for the vSphere endpoint. Note that a non-local account
might need to be imported in VCF Operations and have its read-only role assigned.
For the integration, the username format for non-local account login is username@domain@authenticated-source,
such as .
jdoe@rainpole.local@vIDMAuthSource
Broadcom 7639

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If you are using Workspace ONE Access for source authentication, your account login is username without
any domain information. Authenticated sources are defined during VCF Operations server initial setup.
See the following sections for details. For pricing information, see Using Pricing Cards in VCF Automation.
Advanced workload placement using VCF Operations
VCF Automation and VCF Operations can work together to optimally place deployment workloads.
You enable workload placement at the vSphere based cloud zone level. Only Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS)
enabled clusters of a cloud zone are eligible for advanced placement using VCF Operations.
• VCF Automation placement—The VCF Automation placement engine is application intent based. It considers tag-
based constraints, project membership and the associated cloud zones, and affinity filters related to network, storage,
and compute. Resource placement depends on all of these factors plus the presence of other, related target resources
in the same deployment.
• VCF Operations placement— VCF Operations considers operational intent for optimal placement. Operational intent
can take past workloads and future, what-if predictions into account.
When using advanced workload placement, you must apply VCF Automation tagging in order to implement business
intent decisions, instead of using the VCF Operations business intent options.
When integrating with VCF Operations, VCF Automation continues to follow its application intent model and its related
constraints to filter for target placement. Then, from within those results, it uses the VCF Operations recommendation to
further refine placement.
In the absence of a recommendation
If you enable advanced workload placement, and VCF Operations analysis returns no recommendations, you may
configure VCF Automation to fall back to its default, application intent placement.
Limitations on workload placement
Certain limitations apply when using VCF Operations to place workloads.
• VCF Operations does not support workload placement on resource pools in vCenter Server.
• If VCF Operations is down, the timeout used for workload placement to call VCF Operations might expire.
• Placement doesn't cross multiple cloud zones. VCF Automation sends one cloud zone to VCF Operations for
placement recommendations within that single cloud zone.
How to enable workload placement
To enable workload placement, there are steps to take for vSphere, VCF Operations, and VCF Automation.
1. In VCF Automation, connect to your vCenter cloud account.
The options are under Infrastructure > Connections > Cloud Accounts.
2. In vCenter, verify that DRS enabled clusters exist and are set to fully automated.
3. In VCF Operations, verify that the same vCenter is being managed.
4. In VCF Automation, add the VCF Operations integration.
The options are under Infrastructure > Connections > Integrations.
Broadcom 7640

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To add the integration, you need the VCF Operations primary node URL below, plus the login username and
password.
https://operations-manager-IP-address-or-FQDN/suite-api
After entering the values, click VALIDATE.
5. Synchronize the integration to the vCenter by clicking SYNC.
Also synchronize any time that VCF Automation and VCF Operations begin managing a new vCenter.
6. In VCF Automation, create a cloud zone for the vCenter account.
The options are under Infrastructure > Configure > Cloud Zones.
7. Under the cloud zone Summary tab, set the Placement Policy to ADVANCED.
8. Under the Placement Policy, select whether to have VCF Automation fall back to its default placement if VCF
Operations returns no recommendations.
Troubleshooting workload placement
If VCF Operations isn't recommending workload placements the way that you expect, review the deployment request
details in VCF Automation or VCF Automation.
1. Go to Infrastructure > Activity > Requests, and click the request.
2. In Request Details, look at the allocation phases.
Look for targets that were successfully or unsuccessfully identified.
3. In Request Details, at the upper right, enable Dev Mode.
4. Follow the request path to locate filter blocks.
5. Click a filter block, and review the following section.
filterName: ComputePlacementPolicyAffinityHostFilter
? computeLinksBefore
? computeLinksAfter
? filteredOutHostsReasons
Entry Description
computeLinksBefore List of potential placement hosts based on VCF Automation algorithms.
computeLinksAfter Selected placement host.
filteredOutHostsReasons Messages describing why a host was selected or rejected.
When VCF Operations selects the host, the following message appears.
advance policy filter: Filtered hosts based on recommendation
from vROPS.
Learn more about workload placement
To find the best infrastructure on which to place a deployment, VCF Automation makes several filtering decisions. VCF
Automation integration with VCF Operations may further refine the placement decision.
VCF Operations can help to optimally place workloads provided that you have enabled the Advanced placement policy
option in your vSphere based cloud zones.
In addition, the vSphere cloud accounts for the cloud zones must be monitored by VCF Operations.
Phase 1: Reservation
The VCF Automation reservation phase is the same whether or not you enable Advanced placement with VCF
Operations.
1. Reservation starts with a cloud template linked to a project. That project is in turn linked to cloud zones.
2. The cloud zones consist of compute resource hosts, pools, and clusters, and attached storage.
Initially, any cloud zone in the project may be a potential placement target.
3. VCF Automation filters out cloud zones that don't have enough healthy resources for the deployment.
For example, if too many resources are powered off or in maintenance, that cloud zone is filtered out.
4. VCF Automation filters out cloud zones that can't meet business requirements.
Broadcom 7641

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
For example, the deployment might exceed a pricing or budget limit for the zone.
5. VCF Automation filters out cloud zones that can't meet cluster requirements.
For example, the cloud zone resources might have CPU or memory usage limits that are too low for the deployment.
6. VCF Automation filters out cloud zones that have no affinity with application constraints.
Affinity requires that cloud template or project-level constraint tags match capability tags found somewhere in the cloud
zone resources.
For example, if the cloud template or project includes a storage constraint to use storage tagged , a cloud zone
pci
where none of the storage resources have that capability tag would be filtered out.
7. VCF Automation selects cloud zones with the best provisioning priority.
8. If the project-level placement policy is something other than Default, VCF Automation selects a cloud zone that
supports the non-default placement policy.
In this release, Spread is the only non-default. Spread distributes the load by selecting the cloud zone with the lower
ratio of virtual machines to hosts. Default simply deploys to the first available zone.
The project placement policy is only a factor during the cloud zone reservation phase. It has no effect on, nor relation
to, the cloud zone placement policy in the allocation phase.
When finished, the reservation phase selects one cloud zone and its resources. VCF Automation reserves the first
available zone that remains qualified after passing the preceding filters.
Phase 2: Allocation
VCF Automation inspects the reserved cloud zone compute resources and linked storage.
1. Within the cloud zone, VCF Automation filters out resources that are in a maintenance or powered-off state.
Note that there are still enough healthy resources for the deployment. Otherwise, the entire cloud zone would have
been filtered out during the reservation phase.
2. VCF Automation filters out resources that don't match cluster-level constraints found in the cloud template or project.
For example, a resource in the cloud zone might be tagged under Infrastructure > Resources > Compute.
test
If the cloud template or project includes a constraint tag to use a resource, the resource is filtered out.
dev test
In addition, storage or network profiles in the cloud zone might be tagged in ways that don't match cluster-level storage
or network constraints in the cloud template or project.
3. VCF Automation filters out resources based on affinity settings that are defined in vCenter.
For example, there might be a rule in vCenter where the presence of a virtual machine in one cluster might block
another cluster from being used.
4. VCF Automation filters out resources that don't match any remaining custom constraints found in the cloud template or
project.
For example, if the cloud template includes a constraint to use a tagged image, a cloud zone where none of
ubuntu
the image mappings are tagged would be filtered out.
ubuntu
5. VCF Automation looks for the best possible compute and storage according to the cloud zone placement policy.
VCF Automation engages VCF Operations only when the following two conditions are true:
– The cloud zone placement policy is set to Advanced.
– After filtering through step 4, at least one DRS enabled cluster and the storage linked to it remain qualified.
Otherwise, VCF Automation proceeds with its own placement algorithm without input from VCF Operations.
VCF Operations placement recommendation
If qualified for input from VCF Operations, VCF Automation contacts VCF Operations for a recommendation of the best
possible compute and storage for the deployment. VCF Automation sends the following data to VCF Operations:
• The qualified target DRS enabled clusters and their attached datastores or datastore cluster
• The resource count or cluster size of the deployment
• CPU and memory requirements for the virtual machines in the deployment
• Disk requirements for the virtual machines in the deployment
From the qualified targets, if VCF Operations can return an optimal placement for each of the virtual machines, VCF
Automation allocates compute and storage according to the VCF Operations recommendation.
Broadcom 7642

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
If VCF Operations couldn't find a recommendation, or VCF Automation couldn't find any DRS enabled cluster and storage,
VCF Automation checks the fallback setting of the cloud zone:
• With Fallback
VCF Automation allocates compute and storage that remains qualified even without a VCF Operations
recommendation.
• Without Fallback
VCF Automation cancels the request and does not proceed with provisioning.
Phase 3: Provisioning
VCF Automation deploys the requested virtual machines, storage, and network through the adapter for the placement
target selected at the end of the allocation phase.
The placement target consists of compute hosts, clusters, or resource pools, and attached storage datastore or datastore
cluster.
Continuous optimization using VCF Operations
When you add the VCF Automation adapter in VCF Operations, VCF Operations automatically creates a new custom
datacenter (CDC) for VCF Automation based workloads.
With continuous optimization, you take advantage of workload rebalancing and relocation, and use VCF Automation with
VCF Operations beyond initial workload placement. As virtualization resources move or come under heavier or lighter
load, VCF Automation provisioned workloads can move as needed.
• Continuous optimization automatically creates a new CDC in VCF Operations.
There is one new CDC for each VCF AutomationvSphere cloud zone.
• The newly created CDC contains every VCF Automation managed cluster associated with the cloud zone.
Note:
Do not manually create a mixed CDC of VCF Automation and non- VCF Automation clusters.
• You use VCF Operations to run continuous optimization for the newly created VCF Automation based CDC.
• Workloads can only be rebalanced or relocated within the same cloud zone or CDC.
• Optimization never creates a new VCF Automation or VCF Operations placement violation.
– If you have existing placement violations, optimization can fix VCF Operations operational intent issues.
– If you have existing placement violations, optimization cannot fix VCF Operations business intent issues.
For example, if you used VCF Operations to manually move a virtual machine to a cluster that doesn't support your
constraints, VCF Operations doesn't detect a violation nor try to resolve it.
• This release obeys operational intent at the CDC level. All member VCF Automation clusters are optimized to the
same settings.
To set a different operational intent for clusters, you must configure them in separate VCF Automation CDCs,
associated with separate vSphere cloud zones. Having different test and production clusters might be one example
situation.
• VCF Automation application intent and the constraints defined in VCF Automation are honored during any optimization
rebalance or relocation operations.
• VCF Operations placement tags cannot be applied to VCF Automation provisioned workloads.
In addition, scheduled optimization involving multiple machines is supported. Regularly scheduled optimizations are not
all-or-nothing processes. If conditions interrupt machine movement, successfully relocated machines stay relocated,
and the next VCF Operations cycle attempts to relocate the remainder as is usual for VCF Operations. Such a partially
completed optimization causes no negative effect in VCF Automation.
How to enable continuous optimization
When you add the VCF Automation adapter in VCF Operations, VCF Operations automatically creates a new, dedicated
datacenter for VCF Automation based workloads.
Other than adding the integration within VCF Automation, there are no separate installation steps for continuous
optimization. You may begin configuring and using VCF Operations for workload relocation in the new datacenter. See the
Continuous optimization example .
Broadcom 7643

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Continuous optimization example
The following example shows a rebalancing workflow for VCF Automation continuous optimization with VCF Operations.
1. From the VCF Operations home page, click Workload Optimization.
2. Select the automatically created VCF Automation datacenter.
3. Under Operational Intent, click Edit, and select Balance.
You cannot select or edit Business Intent, which is disabled when the datacenter is for VCF Automation optimization.
4. Under Optimization Recommendation, click Optimize Now.
VCF Operations displays a before-and-after diagram of the proposed operation.
5. Click Next.
6. Click Begin Action.
7. In VCF Automation, monitor the operation in progress by clicking Resources > Deployments and looking at event
status.
When rebalancing finishes, VCF Automation refreshes. The Compute Resources page shows that machines have moved.
In VCF Operations, the next data collection refreshes the display to show that optimization is complete.
In VCF Operations, you can review the operation by clicking Administration > History > Recent Tasks.
Locate VCF Automation managed datacenters
You can use VCF Operations to display only the VCF Automation managed datacenters.
1. From the VCF Operations home page, click Workload Optimization.
2. Near the top right, click the View drop-down.
3. Select only the VCF Automation managed datacenters.
Deployment monitoring based on VCF Operations
VCF Automation can show VCF Operations data about your deployments.
Reviewing the filtered set of metrics directly in VCF Automation saves you the task of accessing or searching VCF
Operations. Although you cannot launch in context to VCF Operations, you are of course free to log in and use VCF
Operations for additional data as needed.
Broadcom 7644

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Enable VCF Operations data
For VCF Automation to show VCF Operations data, specific integrations must be present. The integrations require you to
supply the address and login credentials for VCF Automation, VCF Operations, and vCenter.
1. In VCF Operations, go to Data Sources > Integrations, and verify or add your vCenter account integration.
2. In VCF Automation, go to Infrastructure > Connections > Cloud Accounts, and verify or add your vCenter account.
VCF Operations and VCF Automation must be connected to the same vCenter.
3. In VCF Automation, identify or create a local user with proper permissions, for example, a local user with the
Organization Owner role.
4. In VCF Operations, go to Data Sources > Integrations, and add the VCF Automation for VM Apps organization.
a) Leave the VCF Automation Org ID text box empty.
b) Add the credentials of the local user account that you created in step 3.
5. In VCF Automation, go to Infrastructure > Connections > Integrations, and add the VCF Operations integration.
Enter the VCF Operations address in the following form:
https://operations-manager-IP-address-or-FQDN/suite-api
In VCF Automation, click Resources > Deployments, select a deployment on your vCenter, and verify that the Monitor
tab appears.
Health and alerts provided by VCF Operations
When monitoring is enabled, VCF Automation retrieves VCF Operations Health and associated alerts about your
deployments.
To access monitoring, click a deployment and select the Monitor tab. If the tab is missing, see Enable VCF Operations
data.
To see alerts, highlight the deployment name at the top of the component tree in the left panel.
• You can review the severity and text of the alerts.
• To focus on areas of concern, filter and sort on data in the columns.
• Only Health badges and Health alerts appear. Other alert types such as Efficiency or Risk are not supported.
Metrics provided by VCF Operations
When monitoring is enabled, VCF Automation retrieves VCF Operations metrics about your deployments.
To access monitoring, click a deployment and select the Monitor tab. If the tab is missing, see Enable VCF Operations
data.
To see metrics, expand the component tree on the left, and highlight a virtual machine.
• Metrics are not cached. They come directly from VCF Operations and might take a few moments to load.
• Only virtual machine metrics appear. Metrics from other components such as vCloud Director, Software, or XaaS are
not supported.
• Only vSphere virtual machine metrics appear. Other cloud providers such as AWS or Azure are not supported.
Metrics appear as timeline graphs that show highs and lows for the following measures.
• CPU
• Memory
• Storage IOPS
• Network MBPS
To reveal the specific metric name, click the blue information icon at the upper left corner of the timeline.
Broadcom 7645

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Acting on data provided by VCF Operations
When metrics provided by VCF Operations expose a problem, you can identify trouble areas directly in VCF Automation.
To see metrics provided by VCF Operations, click a deployment and select the Monitor tab. If the tab is missing, see
Enable VCF Operations data.
Metrics for the past day, week, or month are available. To zoom in on an area of concern, select a small area in the lower,
shaded part under any metric timeline:
Resource management and deployment optimization using VCF Operations metrics in VCF Automation
In an integrated VCF Automation and VCF Operations environment, you can access insights and alerts for VCF
Automation objects that are monitored by VCF Operations.
The Insights dashboard and Alerts tab pages provide the real-time capacity and related awareness information that you
need to make management decisions in VCF Automation without needing to open VCF Operations. The information is
supplied by the associated VCF Operations application.
Working with the insights dashboard and with resource alerts
The Insights dashboard conveys information about capacity consumption across all computes within the cloud zone and
grouped by projects. It can also show project deployments that are in need of optimization.
The Alerts pages displays potential capacity and performance concerns for objects such as cloud zones, projects,
deployments, and virtual machines. They also contain information for project owners as to which of their deployments can
be optimized. Each deployment link opens the Optimize tab in the deployment, where specific guidance is provided.
The following diagram illustrates the relationship between VCF Automation resources and deployments, and the data that
the associated VCF Operations application provides in VCF Automation.
Working with the insights dashboard
The Insights dashboard, which is available on each cloud zone page, provides the following VCF Operations metrics:
• CPU, memory, and storage utilization usage as a percentage of capacity
Broadcom 7646

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Capability consumption summary
• CPU and memory demand and usage history
• Consumption across projects
• Reclaimable resource capacity, with cost savings, for deployments and projects in a cloud zone
It also provides an option to alert project owners of deployments that can be optimized.
The Insights dashboard is available for vSphere and VMware Cloud on AWS cloud zones, provided that the cloud
accounts are configured in both VCF Automation and VCF Operations and are being monitored in VCF Operations.
Working with alerts
The Alerts pages provide the following filtering categories. Filtering categories are supplied by the associated VCF
Operations application.
• Severity
• Status
• Impact
• Type
• Subtype
• Resource
Each filter can be further refined using quick filters. For example, the resource filter can be further refined by its quick filter
types of cloud zone, virtual machine, deployment, and project resource.
You use combinations of filters and quick filters to control which alerts are available for display.
Some Alerts provide information about, and a link to, deployments that can be optimized. An individual alert can provide
the option to contact the project owner, examine an Insights dashboard, or take possible actions.
Alerts are available for vSphere and VMware Cloud on AWS resource objects.
Configuring a Provider-Specific External IPAM Integration for VCF Automation for VM Apps
You can use an external IPAM provider to manage IP address assignments for your cloud template deployments. This
tutorial describes how to configure external IPAM integration in VCF Automation using Infoblox as the external IPAM
provider.
In this procedure, you use an existing IPAM provider package, in this case an Infoblox package, and an existing running
environment to build a provider-specific IPAM integration point. You configure an existing network and create a network
profile to support IP address allocation from the external IPAM provider. Finally, you create a cloud template that is
matched to the network and network profile and deploy networked machines using IP values obtained from the external
IPAM provider.
Information about how to obtain and configure the IPAM provider package, and how to configure a running environment
that accesses a cloud extensibility proxy to support the IPAM provider integration, is included as reference.
The values you see in this sample workflow are example values. You won't be able to use them verbatim in your
environment. Think about where you would make your own substitutions to fit your organization's needs.

Send email notifications to users in VCF Automation for VM Apps
As a cloud administrator, you can configure VCF Automation to send users notifications when specific events in VCF
Automation and VCF Automation occur.
• Verify that you configured an outbound email server. See Add an email server in VCF Automation to send notifications.
You can send notifications for several types of events, called scenarios, such as the successful completion of a catalog
request or a required approval.
Email messages are sent to users in the following scenarios.
Scenario Description
Deployment Lease Deletion A deployment lease expired and the deployment is scheduled for
deletion. The message is sent to the deployment owner 15–30
minutes before the deployment is destroyed.
Deployment Lease Expired A deployment lease expired and the deployment is about to be
deleted.
Deployment Lease Expiring A deployment lease expires soon. The message is sent to the
deployment owner three days before the lease expires.
Deployment Request Approved A request is approved. The message is sent to the user who
requested the deployment.
Deployment Request Rejected A request is rejected. The message is sent to the user who
requested the deployment.
Deployment Request Waiting for Approval (Notification sent to A request awaits approval. The message is sent to the user who
requester) requested the deployment.
Pending Approval Request (Notification sent to approver) A request requires approval. The message is sent to the user who
must approve the request.
Pending Work Item (Notification sent to assignees) A request requires user input to proceed. The message is sent to
the user who must provide input.
Pending Work Item (Notification sent to requester) A request requires user input to proceed. The message is sent to
the user who requested the deployment.
Work Item Answered A request that required user input was answered and the
deployment proceeded.
Work Item Rejected A request that required user input was rejected and the
deployment did not proceed.
1. Log in to VCF Automation as an administrator.
2. Select Content and Policies > Notifications > Scenarios.
3. Select one or more events to trigger user notifications.
Users are subscribed to the notifications that you enabled.
When configuring notifications in VCF Automation, consider:
• If a user email is changed in Active Directory, it might take at least 15 minutes before the email address is updated in
VCF Automation. In the meantime, notifications might be sent to the old email address.
• Notification recipients are limited to 100 users per notification. For Active Directory groups, the limit is 10 groups per
notification, where each group consists of a maximum of 500 users. If a group consists of more than 500 users, the
notification is only sent to 500 users, and not to the rest of the users.
Add an email server in VCF Automation to send notifications
As a cloud administrator, you configure an email server if you want to send messages to users about events in VCF
Automation and VCF Automation. The messages are a courtesy that improves the experience of your consumers.
Broadcom 7650

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Verify that you know the credentials required to configure the email server. You must provide the server name and an
email account that you want to be the message sender. If your email server requires authentication, you must also
provide the user name and password.
This email server is for outbound messages only.
Email messages are sent to users in the following scenarios.
• A deployment lease expires soon. The message is sent to the deployment owner three days before the lease expires.
• A deployment lease expired and the deployment is about to be deleted. The message is sent to the deployment owner
15–30 minutes before it is destroyed.
1. Select Content and Policies > Notifications > Email Server.
2. Enter the information for each setting.
If you need assistance on a particular setting, consult the signpost help.
3. To verify the configured settings, click Test Connection.
4. To save, click Create.
As the administrator, monitor the leases to ensure that the messages are sent to the deployment owners at the correct
time.
Customize notifications in VCF Automation
As a cloud administrator, you can customize the email notifications that the users in your organization receive about
events in VCF Automation and VCF Automation.
You can change the text and the branding elements of the email, such as the logo, so that it matches the requirements of
your organization.
Customize the branding of email notifications
As a cloud administrator, you can customize the way that email notifications look.
You can change the background color, edit the text, and add a new logo in the header and the footer of email notifications.
Branding is applied across all notification templates.
In this scenario, you want to replace the default logo and company name in the notifications your users receive with the
logo of your company.
Broadcom 7651

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Select Content and Policies > Notifications > Scenarios.
2. Click Edit shared branding.
3. On the Edit header tab, add the URL of your logo and the name of your organization.
4. To review you changes, click the Preview tab.
5. Click Save.
Customize the subject and body of email notifications
You can edit the subject line and the message body of each notification template and use the deployment attributes that
are available for the scenario.
As a cloud administrator, you want to craft an email notification that informs your developers when a cloud service is
provisioned and provides details about the deployment.
In this scenario, you add the deployment name to the subject of an email notification.
1. Select Content and Policies > Notifications > Scenarios.
2. Click the arrow on the left of the notification scenario you want to customize.
A preview of the notification email appears on the right.
3. Click Customize.
4. On the Edit tab, update the subject line and the message body of the notification as necessary.
a) Click Scenario attributes > properties.
The available attributes are specific to each notification scenario.
Broadcom 7652

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
b) Click the copy icon next to the property.
name(string)
c) Paste the property in the Subject field.
You can also add the dynamic attributes in the message body. Using custom properties is not supported.
5. To review you changes, click the Preview tab.
You see the placeholder text for the deployment name in the subject.
6. Click Save.
7. Optional: Test the updated notification.
a) Click Send test.
b) Enter an email to send the test email to.
c) Click Send test.
Using the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation
The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation® is an integration between VCF Automation (VMware Cloud
Foundation Automation) and the ServiceNow platform.
The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation (henceforth referred to as "Plug-in") imports the VCF Automation
catalog items in the ServiceNow platform. ServiceNow users can use these catalog items to perform various operations in
ServiceNow, including the deployment of virtual machine to various other day-2 operations.
Important:
The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation is supported only for VM Apps organizations in VCF
Automation. You cannot use the plug-in in All Apps organizations.
Broadcom 7653

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Installation Prerequisites
Before you install ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation, make sure that your environment meets the supported
compatibility requirements and the MID server is installed.
Compatibility Matrix
The following table lists the version compatibility between the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation, VCF
Automation, and ServiceNow releases.
Table 1845: ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation Compatibility Matrix
ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for Supported VCF Automation Supported VMware Aria Supported ServiceNow
VCF Automation Version Automation Version Releases
9.0.1 9.0 VM App Orgs only 8.18.1 Yokohama and Zurich
9.0.1 VM App Orgs Only
Note:
• Please follow the steps if you are using ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation on Zurich or
newer version.
• By default, the CMDB schedule job will run only once a day. The schedule period is configurable and you can
configure it based on workload size.
• ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation does not support the ServiceNow on-premises versions.
• ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation only supports VM Apps organizations.
Installation of MID Server
Before installation of ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation, you must configure a MID server. The configured
MID Server acts as a communication bridge between the ServiceNow platform and the VCF Automation.
Refer to the ServiceNow documentation to install a MID Server.
• For the Zurich release, see ServiceNow Zurich Release Documentation.
• For the Yokohama release, see ServiceNow Yokohama Release Documentation.
Note:
• For better performance, use a dedicated MID Server for the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation.
• Please provide role to the MID Server user created while
x_vmw_cloudservice.vra_catalog_admin
installing a MID Server.
MID Server policies setup
ServiceNow has enhanced security with the TLS MID Server certificate check policies. If VCF Automation has an
untrusted certificated connection, the connection will be refused. This procedure modifies the TLS MID Server certificate
check policies and disables the check for untrusted certificates to connect them insecurely.
For security considerations and detailed information, refer to the MID Server TLS or SSL certificate check policy
information.
Configuration of MID Server policies for ServiceNow
This procedure modifies the TLS MID Server certificate check policies and disables the check for untrusted certificates
to connect them insecurely. You do not need to perform the steps provided in this section if the endpoint has CA signed
certificate.
You must be the system administrator in ServiceNow.
Broadcom 7654

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Log in to ServiceNow as a system administrator.
2. In the left pane, search for MID security policy.
3. In the Intranet record, set the Certificate Chain Check to false.
4. Register VCF Automation from the Manage Endpoint. See Register ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation
with VCF Automation / Aria Automation.
Assign Script Writer role to Admin role (mandatory step for Zurich and later versions)
ServiceNow has introduced a new Scripting Governance Tool in Zurich release. This feature enabled a better
control to restrict write access across all script-like fields. To allow the plugin to write catalog client scripts
dynamically, Zurich onwards, ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation would require Admin role to have
"snc_required_script_writer_permission" role assigned.
1. Login with system administrator
2. Search "sys_user_role.LIST" in filter navigation
3. Search for the record with name "admin"
4. Go to the related list "Contains roles"
5. Edit to add "snc_required_script_writer_permission" role
6. Save
Install the user criteria scoped API plug-in
The User Criteria Scoped API plug-in enables you to create, modify, or delete user criteria records using scripts. The User
Criteria Scoped API plug-in is a paid ServiceNow plug-in and requires a subscription. Contact ServiceNow Support for
more information.
You must be the system administrator in ServiceNow.
1. Log in to ServiceNow as the system administrator.
2. Navigate to System Definition > Plug-ins.
3. In the Search box, enter User criteria scoped API to search the plug-in.
The User Criteria Scoped API plug-in dialog box appears.
4. Click Install, and then click Activate.
After the plug-in is installed, the success message appears.
Create a Data Source Choice in ServiceNow
The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation uses Identification and Reconcile Engine which requires to have
discovery source element for the application.
• You must be the system administrator in ServiceNow.
• Set the application scope to .
Global

question_choice

You can install the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation from ServiceNow Store. The installation is free, you

9. Select Install with demo data, and complete the installation.
The application is successfully installed message displays.

Type.
– Expand the System Property and set the Replace on upgrade to True for all the system properties.

upgrading, then the records will fall into Skipped and Skipped Manual Merge. For more information, see

1. Log in to ServiceNow as a system administrator.

Setting Up ServiceNow Groups
The ServiceNow system administrator can add users to the approval and support group. Users in the approval group are
responsible for approving or rejecting the deployment requests made by the users. The incidents created by the failure of
the catalog request submissions are assigned to users of the support group.
• You can add the number of users to the approval group by adding users to the Automation-ApprovalGroup to
approve or reject the requests.
• You can add the number of users to the support group by adding users to the Automation-SupportGroup to approve
or reject the requests.
Note:
If you do not add any users to the approval group, the requests get auto-approved.
Configuration of VCF Automation Endpoint
You must set up an administrative user in VCF Automation. The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation connects
to VCF Automation using the credentials of this user.
This user must have these roles in VCF Automation:
• Organization Member
• Project Member
• Service Broker User
• Assembler Administrator

in the ServiceNow, requests, and corresponding deployments display the ServiceNow user who initiated the
request. This is achieved by correlating the email address from the user records across two systems.
• You must add the integration user to each project as a project admin to use the project in ServiceNow ITSM
Plug-in for VCF Automation
Create Day 2 Policies
Create a day-2 action policy for the integration user. The integration user must be added to the deployment criteria using
the created by condition to limit the policy to integration user. This policy can be used to limit the day-2 actions for the
integration user.
To create policies, see the VCF Automation documentation.
Note:
Use the Deployment Criteria option to limit the day-2 actions for the integration user.
Verify Email Address Mapping
The VCF Automation and ServiceNow can have different Authentication Providers. It is important to set up the users in
both systems with the same email address.
The correlation is required to assign ownership of the deployments and resources.

Fields Inputs

Using the Service Portal
This chapter describes how to use the Service Portal for the ServiceNow plug-in.
Viewing the Deployments
The Deployment List page displays the list of deployments entitled to the user. Users can view the status of the
deployments they own. From the Deployment List page, the user can view the deployment status, expiry date, number of
resources associated with deployment, a project associated with the deployment, owner, and so on.

On the Deployment List page, you can search deployment using the search bar only for the following fields:

• Status

• Project
• Endpoint

one of the following values:

install_status
to on the deployments table based on the absence of the ServiceNow plug-in for Hardware
pending_install
Asset Management. For more information, see KB article.

You can perform actions that are associated with deployments and are entitled to a user. You can perform one action at a
time. If any deployment action is in progress, then a progress bar appears, and all the other day-2 actions are hidden until
the in-progress action is complete. The progress bar shows the status of in-progress action.

ServiceNow User Roles.

Create the User Criteria
The user criteria control the accessibility of categories and catalog items in the Service Catalog. The ServiceNow users
and end-users require user criteria to access projects/catalog items. The ServiceNow system administrator can create
user criteria in the VCF Automation Plugin
• You must create entitlement using the user criteria. To create the user criteria records in the Service Catalog, see
Create User Criteria Record.
• To assign the user criteria to catalog items and projects in the Service Catalog, see Apply User Criteria to Items and
Categories.
• The restrictions for user criteria to view individual projects/catalog items are directly applied by adding items in
Available For or Not Available For related lists in the User Criteria form.
• The system administrator must provide access to projects/ catalog items for a specific user by following the below
steps:
1. Create User Criteria in the Service Catalog.
2. Add Groups and Users in User Criteria.
3. Add the user criteria in Available For if a specific user requires to access a specific project/catalog item.
4. Add the user criteria in Not Available For if the specific user does not want to access a specific project/catalog item.
Note:
The user cannot access the catalog item when the user is on both Available For and Not Available For lists
because the Not Available For settings will override Available For settings.
Advanced Configuration
The ServiceNow system administrators can configure the additional features to enhance the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for
VCF Automation.
Configure and Run Import Jobs
The Configure and Run Import Jobs section describes the jobs that are automatically scheduled at the time of installation.
You can update the default schedule as required. You can also run these jobs manually (on-demand).
However, exercise caution while changing the default configuration or manually running the jobs as data corruption or loss
can occur.
Note:
The Scheduled Jobs and System logs functionality will only be visible to the ServiceNow system administrator.
CAUTION:
Import jobs must be configured and run in the order they appear in the following table. Manual (on-demand)
execution of these jobs must also follow this order. Failure to follow this order can cause the data corruption or
loss.
This table describes the import jobs.
Scheduled Import Jobs Description
Generate API Token Generates an authentication token when VCF Automation is
registered. This job runs automatically and updates the API token.
Import Project Imports project from VCF Automation into ServiceNow as projects.
Import Catalog Imports catalog items from VCF Automation into ServiceNow as
catalog items.
Broadcom 7668

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Scheduled Import Jobs Description
Import Resources and CMDB Imports deployments and resources from VCF Automation into
ServiceNow so that users can view the resources they own on the
portal. By default, the job execution time is set to 23.59.00 PDT at
midnight. The system administrator can change the execution time
as per their requirement. VMware recommends that you must not
run this job frequently and always run it during off-peak hours.
Delete Queue Deletes the scheduled import queues that are older than the
interval specified.
Reconcile Actions While importing the day-2 actions from the VCF Automation
services, if any day-2 actions are removed from VCF Automation
services, then they will be removed from the ServiceNow.
Thread Limit Runs every second to process a limited number of topics from the
Job Queue table. Note that the user need not activate, deactivate,
or run this job manually. This job is automated to activate or
deactivate based on certain conditions.
Thread Limit Maximum By default, the scheduled job runs every Friday at midnight and
can be configured based on requirements. This scheduled job will
maximize the VCF Automation thread limit to the default value of
16 (value set from the system property x_vmw_cloudservice
.ThreadUsed_Maximum) considering less load on the system
during weekends. This allows the customer to avoid configuring
the VCF Automation thread system property manually.
Thread Limit Minimum By default, the scheduled job runs every Sunday at midnight and
can be configured based on requirements. This scheduled job will
minimize the VCF Automation thread limit to the default value of 8
(value set from the system property x_vmw_cloudservice.T
hreadUsed_Minimum) when the system is under normal load.
This allows the customer to avoid configuring the VCF Automation
thread system property manually.
Telemetry Data Push This scheduled job will run only when the user has provided their
consent as Yes in the telemetry pop-up and the “x_vmw_clou
dservice.customer_consent_value” system property
value is true. The scheduled job will import the telemetry data
from ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation. By default,
this scheduled job runs every midnight.
Email and Ticketing Properties
The ServiceNow system administrator or plug-in admin can configure email notification properties and support tickets in
the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation.
The system administrator or plug-in admin can configure the email notification for these functionalities:
• Manage Endpoint: An email is sent to the users responsible to create, update, and delete the endpoint.
• Approval request: If the email settings are configured, then:
– An email is sent to both requester and approval group once the request is created.
– An email is sent to requester if the submitted request is approved or rejected.
– An email is sent to requester if more information is required by the approval group.
• Deployment Requested Items (RITM) to VCF Automation: If the email settings are configured, then:
– An email is sent to requester once the RITM is submitted.
– If the approval group is configured, an email is sent to the approval group once the RITM is submitted.
– An email is sent to requester if RITM is successful.
– An email is sent to requester if RITM is failed and a support ticket is created.
• Day-2 actions: If the email settings are configured, then:
– An email is sent to requester if a Day-2 deployment or resource action is successful.
– An email is sent to requester if a Day-2 deployment or resource action is failed and a support ticket is created.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
The system administrator or plug-in admin can configure the properties to create support tickets:
• A support ticket is created if a RITM request is failed.
• A support ticket is created if a Day-2 deployment or resource action is failed.

Supported and Unsupported Functionality
This section provides information for supported and unsupported functionalities for the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF
Automation.
Catalog Item Support and Limitation
• A single ServiceNow instance supports multiple VCF Automation instances. The Catalog Items from the multiple
instances are consolidated.
• Approval groups to approve or reject the deployment requests are supported.
• Value Picker only supports Properties Array as the return type when the value is fetched from the VCF Automation
Orchestrator Actions.
• Under Custom Resources, for Add Action, the Requires condition must be disabled.
• For Custom forms, field properties such as the Match field are not supported in the Constraints.
• For the Service Portal and Native UI, the placeholder functionality is not supported.
• The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation supports only the following field types in Cloud Template (YAML):
– String
– Integer
– Number
– Boolean
– Object
– Data grid
• The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation does not support the Multi-value Picker field type. When the
Import catalog job runs, it skips the catalog items with the Multi-value Picker field type.
Broadcom 7674

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• In the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation, the dependent fields having minimum and maximum values with
the VCF Automation action are not supported.
• In the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation, the stepwise increment option (stepper) is not supported for
decimal and integer data type constraints.
• The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation does not support the Text Element if fetched from External Source.
• The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation does not support the Deployment Count feature.
• All the functionalities of the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation available on the Service Portal are
supported on the Employee Center.
• In ServiceNow, it is recommended to have numeric values for the version field of the catalog item.
• On vRA, the Date Time field value for Objectfield and Datagrid must be in the UTC time zone.
• For catalog items, the price calculation is not supported for complex datatypes such as Objectfield, Datagrid, Value
Picker, etc.
• If you have created the following field in the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation then while performing
import in ServiceNow, this field will not be created:
– Field ID: project

• Supported Data type Matrix for Day-0
This section provides information on supported data types for Appearance, Default values, and Constraints in
ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation.
– Appearance
Note:
• The support for data types such as Drop down, Multi-select, and Dual list as shown in the below table is also
supported for String, Integer, and Decimal.
• The Conditional visibility and Read-only is supported for the following datatypes using the operators:
– Drop down and Text field using Equals, NotEquals, and Within operators.
– Checkbox using Equals and NotEquals operators.
– Integer and Decimal using Equals, NotEquals, Greater than, Lesser than, Greater than equal to, and
Lesser than equal to.
• The External Source visibility and Read-only can be set by the direct VCF Operations Orchestrator action
and Input in Action inputs as Constant and Field using the following data types: Text field, Text Area,
Decimal, Integer, Drop down, and Check box.

• Custom Categories support:
– The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation supports creating custom categories and linking catalog items to
custom categories.
– To create a new category, go to the filter Navigator, and type Categories> Service Catalog> Maintain Categories.
• To link a newly created category to catalog items, follow the steps:
– In filter Navigator>Catalog items.
– On Catalog items, under the Categories tab, click Edit.
– In Edit Members, search for the newly created categories.
– Add the newly created categories to the Categories List and click Save. The new categories are linked to the
catalog items.
• Support of custom fields for Day-0 catalog item:
– The container for custom fields facilitates you to create a custom field with orders ranging from conditions
10002-10099 under variables.
– You can also change the name of the custom container if required.
– You can create customized client scripts for custom fields.
– You can create a new custom field by clicking the New button under variables, on catalog items in the ServiceNow
ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation.
– While creating new custom fields, if the user changes VCF Automation scope to global scope on catalog items,
then the New button under variables will not be visible to create new custom fields.
– Custom fields can be created only on the Day-0 catalog item.
– You can view the custom fields on RITM. The reference of the RITM number is displayed under requested items by
navigating to deployments and vice versa.
– While creating a client script, in UI type, you must select All so that the script works on both the Native UI and
Service Portal.
– Custom fields cannot be sent to VCF Automation/VMware Aria Automation.
– The Application Scope must be Global for creating a Custom field and Variable set else the catalog items request
will fail in ServiceNow.
–
Note:
The Application Scope must be Global for creating a Custom field and Custom variable set.
• Support for custom variable set for day-0 catalog items:
– The Application Scope must be Global for creating a custom variable set.
Broadcom 7679

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
•
Deployment Name field support:
– You can view the Deployment Name field in the plug-in for both custom form and non-custom form catalog items.
The Deployment Name field displays as a Read-only field and can be enabled or disabled from VCF Automation.
– If the catalog item does not have a Deployment name field in VCF Automation, then the Deployment name will be
displayed after the Version field.
– The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation supports the Deployment name field for external source and
default values.

– Boolean
• Read-only and Default values are not supported for YAML.

Day 2 Action Support and Limitation
• Configuration of email notification for endpoint, entitlement, approval request, RITM request on VCF Automation, day-2
actions, and resource sharing are available.
• A support ticket is created within ServiceNow on the failure of catalog request submission and day-2 action.
• After you have removed the disk from a machine, it takes time to reflect the same in the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for
VCF Automation.
•
The following day-2 actions are available from the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation:
Resource Actions Deployment Actions
Add Disk Change Lease
Compute Relocate Delete
Create Snapshot Power Off

•
You can change the owners of deployments for day-2 actions with the available users displayed in the Owner Type
dropdown only if the same users are available on VCF Automation and ServiceNow :
•
For On-premise, the user_name of users will be displayed if the same user_name is available on vRA and
ServiceNow.
• Adding Groups is not supported in the Owner Type.
• Edit deployment day-2 action does not support changing the icon for a deployment.
• The Run Puppet Task day-2 action is not supported for Puppet deployments.
• Custom day-2 Actions and Custom Resources are supported.

– Deployments
– Built-in Resources
–

– Form-based day-2 actions
– Formless day-2 actions

Supported Cloud Providers

supported.
Other Supported Functionality and Limitations
• Defining the permissions for Admin, Catalog Admin, and User is supported.
• Reconciliation of CMDB to keep the CI item updated is supported.
• The ServiceNow RITM number and Requester email ID or user name will be sent to VCF Automation for Day-0 and
Day-2 catalog requests.
• If the ServiceNow users are not able to view deployments, ensure that the user is using the email address as a user
name in the VCF Automation and it must be the same as the email address of the user in ServiceNow.
• Project Group Entitlements:
– In ServiceNow, on the Project record, under the Users section, you can add multiple groups in the Project Group,
so that all the members of the group can view the deployments and resources related to a particular Project.
– Groups must have  cmdb_read  and  x_vmw_cloudservice.vra_end_user  roles to access deployments and
resources, and also to perform the day-2 actions.
Broadcom 7685

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Telemetry
The telemetry feature facilitates users to provide consent whether to send the data from the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for
VCF Automation to VMwareby Broadcom.
The following data will be sent to VMware by Broadcom after the user provides the consent:
• Organization Id
• Projects
• Deployments
• Catalog items
To provide consent to send data or not, the user must navigate to the Manage Endpoint table and click the existing
endpoint, or while registering a new endpoint, the consent pop-up will be displayed.
• To provide consent, click Yes. The scheduled job will start sending telemetry data to VMware by Broadcom and the
consent pop-up will not be prompted again for the user.
• To not provide consent, click No. The telemetry data will not be sent to VMware by Broadcom and a consent pop-up
will be prompted after every 30 days for further consent.
1. If the user responds to the consent pop-up as Yes but do not wish to send the telemetry data to VMware by Broadcom,
then the user needs to perform the following steps:
a) Navigate to system property.
x_vmw_cloudservice.telemetry_last_trigger
b) Open the system property and in the value option, remove the date and time, and click Update.
c) Search for the system property.
x_wm_cloudservice.customer_consent_value
d) Open the system property and set the value as false.
e) When the next consent pop-up is prompted, click No, so that telemetry data will not be sent to VMware by
Broadcom.
2. If the user responds to the consent pop-up as No but intends to send the telemetry data to VMware, then the user
needs to perform the following steps:
a) Navigate to system property.
x_vmw_cloudservice.telemetry_last_trigger
b) Open the system property and in value, remove the date and time, and click Update.
c) Navigate to the Manage Endpoint table, and open the existing endpoint.
d) When the consent pop-up is prompted, click Yes, so that telemetry data will be sent to VMware by Broadcom.
Known Issues
The following issues are known in the ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation:
• The ServiceNow ITSM Plug-in for VCF Automation displays Boolean type fields as checkboxes in catalog items.
• While deleting an endpoint make sure that data is in the VMware application scope. If not, an error message displays
for the cross scope data deletion post endpoint is deleted and data is removed successfully.
• In the Native UI, if a day-2 action catalog item contains the check box or label fields then ServiceNow displays the
cross-scope info messages while loading day-2 catalog items and also on RITM after submitting the day-2 catalog
items. This is a ServiceNow-known issue.
• On the Service Portal, duplicate data type fields are displayed in the RITM if the catalog item has multiple versions.
• On the Service Portal, for the visibility feature, the Dropdown field list on the catalog item will have an extra empty
option.
Broadcom 7686

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• When day-2 actions for multiple deployments are processed simultaneously, the duplicate variables may be generated
in respective day-2 catalog items. This is a ServiceNow-known issue and occurs rarely.
• In ServiceNow, if you hide all fields under a tab, then the tab will also not be visible even if the visibility condition is
matched.
• The catalog form request with empty fields within property groups will fail after submission because the property
groups are mandatory in VCF Automation.
• In the Data grid, if the input field with type number/integer is empty on the order form, then the catalog request fails
after submitting in ServiceNow.
• In ServiceNow, when you modify the value of any dependent field containing conditional default value and conditional
read-only, then the dependent field will reflect the default value instead of the modified value.
• In ServiceNow, when you perform the price estimate calculations without filling in any mandatory fields in the form, the
price estimate can give an error message that can be viewed in the error logs.
• The “Update” button for price estimate calculations is always active even if any of the field’s inputs are not modified.
• In ServiceNow, if the mandatory field has a default value and conditional read-only, then the read-only condition will not
be applied to the mandatory field.
• For getting an empty value from VCF Operations Orchestrator, make sure your VCF Operations Orchestrator action
script code considers both “Empty” and “Null” conditions while checking the input parameters.
• In the plug-in, the below-mentioned configurations for the Dual List and Multi-Select data type are not recommended:
– Default value is not present in the Value Options.
– Value Options are empty and the default value source is External.
Troubleshoot
The troubleshooting topics provide solutions to potential problems that you might encounter when using ServiceNow ITSM
Plug-in for VCF Automation.
Unable to perform Day-2 Action
ServiceNow users are not able to perform day-2 actions.
From the deployment and resource actions, ServiceNow users are not able to perform day-2 operations.
The registered endpoint is activated after the deactivation in ServiceNow.
Run the import jobs for the deployment and resources. See Configure and Run Import Jobs.
Complete Hover Message or Field Name is not Displayed
Large hover messages or field names are getting truncated.
Not able to see the full value of translated text and Question text.
By default field length of the and is 250 and 255 respectively. If the length is
translated_text question_text
greater than the desired length, the field length will be truncated.
The ServiceNow system administrator must increase the field length for translated_text and question_choice. You must
import the catalog items again after updating the length.
Deployments and Resources are not displayed
The deployments and resources are not visible in ServiceNow.
Even after running the scheduled job, deployments and resources are not displayed in ServiceNow.
This problem occurs as some fields in the table have mandatory conditions.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Workload Orchestration
Use VCF Automation or VCF Operations orchestrator to configure workload orchestration.
In This Chapter
• Managing VMware Cloud Foundation Operations Orchestrator
• Administering VCF Operations Orchestrator
• Developing Workflows with VCF Operations Orchestrator
• Using the VCF Operations orchestrator Plug-ins
Getting to Know VCF
To apply this documentation, you must be acquainted with the VCF Product Overview, VCF Design, and VCF Release
Notes.
Managing VMware Cloud Foundation Operations Orchestrator
VMware Cloud Foundation Operations orchestrator (VCF Operations orchestrator) is a development- and process-
automation platform that provides a library of extensible workflows. VCF Operations orchestrator automates management
and operational tasks of both Broadcom and third-party applications such as service desks, change management
systems, and IT asset management systems.
VCF Operations Orchestrator Overview
VCF Operations orchestrator contains a workflow library and a workflow engine to allow you to create and run workflows
that automate orchestration processes. You run workflows on the objects of different technologies that VCF Operations
orchestrator accesses through a series of plug-ins.
VCF Operations orchestrator provides a standard set of plug-ins to allow you to orchestrate tasks in the different
environments that the plug-ins expose.
VCF Operations orchestrator also presents an open architecture for plugging in external third-party applications to the
orchestration platform. You can run workflows on the objects of the plugged-in technologies that you define yourself.
VCF Operations orchestrator connects to an authentication provider to manage user accounts and to a preconfigured
PostgreSQL database to store information from the workflows that it runs.
Key Features of the VCF Operations Orchestrator Platform
VCF Operations orchestrator is composed of three distinct layers: an orchestration platform that provides the common
features required for an orchestration tool, a plug-in architecture to integrate control of subsystems, and a library of
workflows. VCF Operations orchestrator is an open platform that can be extended with new plug-ins and content, and can
be integrated into larger architectures through a REST API.
VCF Operations orchestrator includes several key features that help with running and managing workflows.
Persistence A production-grade PostgreSQL database is used to store
relevant information, such as processes, workflow states, and the
VCF Operations orchestrator configuration.
Central management VCF Operations orchestrator provides a central tool to manage
your processes. The application server-based platform, with full
version history, can store scripts and process-related primitives in
the same storage location. This way, you can avoid scripts without
versioning and proper change control on your servers.
Broadcom 7694

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Check-pointing Every step of a workflow is saved in the database, which prevents
data-loss if you must restart the server. This feature is especially
useful for long-running processes.
Versioning All VCF Operations orchestrator platform objects have an
associated version history. Version history is useful for basic
change management when distributing processes to project
stages or locations.
Git integration You can integrate a Git repository to further improve version and
source control of your VCF Operations orchestrator content. With
Git, you can manage workflow development across multiple VCF
Operations orchestrator instances.
Scripting engine The Mozilla Rhino JavaScript engine provides a way to create
building blocks for the VCF Operations orchestrator client
platform. The scripting engine is enhanced with basic version
control, variable type checking, name space management, and
exception handling. The engine can be used in the following
building blocks:
• Actions
• Workflows
• Policies
In addition to JavaScript, you can also use Python, Node.js, and
PowerShell/PowerCLI runtimes as a way of creating workflows
and actions.
Workflow engine The workflow engine is used by VCF Operations orchestrator for
core processes such as:
• Processing the workflow schema
• Performs the workflow and action runs
• Manages user interactions
• Creates checkpoints for VCF Operations orchestrator objects
The capabilities to manage VCF Operations orchestrator content
are provided by the Orchestrator platform.
Users, other workflows, schedules, or policies can start workflows.
Policy engine You can use the policy engine to monitor and generate events to
react to changing conditions in the VCF Operations orchestrator
server or a plugged-in technology. Policies can aggregate events
from the platform or the plug-ins, which helps you to handle
changing conditions on any of the integrated technologies.
Development and resources The VCF Operations orchestrator landing page provides quick
access to resources to help you develop your own plug-ins, for
use in VCF Operations orchestrator. You will also find information
about using the VCF Operations orchestrator REST API to send
requests to the VCF Operations orchestrator server.
Security VCF Operations orchestrator provides the following advanced
security functions:
• Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) to sign and encrypt content
imported and exported between servers.
• Digital Rights Management (DRM) to control how exported
content can be viewed, edited, and redistributed.
• Transport Layer Security (TLS) to provide encrypted
communications between the VCF Operations orchestrator
deployment, server, and HTTPS access to the web front end.
• Advanced access rights management to provide control over
access to processes and the objects manipulated by these
processes.
Broadcom 7695

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Encryption VCF Operations orchestrator uses a FIPS-compliant Advanced
Encryption Standard (AES) with a 256-bit cipher key for encryption
of strings. The cipher key is randomly generated and is unique
across appliances that are not part of a cluster. All nodes in a
cluster share a cipher key.
Installing VCF Operations Orchestrator
To install VCF Operations orchestrator, you must deploy it from an OVF template. For more information, see Deploying
VCF Operations orchestrator.
Note:
VCF Automation includes an embedded VCF Operations orchestrator instance which is predeployed. For
more information on the VCF Operations orchestrator deployment in VCF Automation, see VCF Operations
Orchestrator Design.
For more information on configuring a VCF Operations orchestrator cluster, see Configure a VCF Operations Orchestrator
Cluster.
Upgrading VCF Operations Orchestrator
You can upgrade your VMware Aria Automation Orchestrator 8.18.1 deployment to VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1.
For more information on upgrading VMware Aria Automation Orchestrator, see Upgrading VCF Operations Orchestrator
Deployments.
VCF Operations Orchestrator Licensing
The VCF Operations orchestrator deployment license is taken automatically from the authentication provider as part
of the configuration process of the deployment. You do not license VCF Operations orchestrator manually. Supported
authentication providers are VCF Automation, vSphere, and VCF SSO. For more information on VCF licensing, see
Licensing Overview.
Supported VCF Operations Orchestrator Integrations
VCF Operations orchestrator supports the integrations with the following VCF components. Depending on the integration,
you access your VCF Operations orchestrator instance, the objects it exposes, and the VCF Operations orchestrator
workflows differently.

orchestrator

VCF Automation VM Apps Organizations

vSphere or orchestrator deployment

Administering VCF Operations Orchestrator
Use this section to configure, scale, secure, and maintain VCF Operations orchestrator. The tasks are organized
by operational lifecycle so you must complete the initial setup before moving to scaling, access control, or server
configuration topics.
Broadcom 7696

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Before You Begin
Complete the following prerequisites before starting any task in this section.
• VCF Operations orchestrator 9.1 is deployed. For deployment instructions, see Deploying VMware Cloud Foundation
Operations Orchestrator.
• You have network access to the VCF Operations orchestrator server.
• You have administrator credentials for VCF Operations orchestrator.
• The VMware Cloud Foundation environment is operational and you can reach the VCF Automation instance that the
orchestrator is paired with.
Initial VCF Operations Orchestrator Setup
Before you begin automating tasks and managing systems and applications with VCF Operations orchestrator, you must
perform additional configuration tasks such as managing license and certificate information.
Activate or Deactivate SSH Access to VCF Operations Orchestrator
You can activate or deactivate SSH access to VCF Operations orchestrator.
• Download and deploy VCF Operations orchestrator.
• Verify that VCF Operations orchestrator is up and running.
1. Log in to the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance command line as root.
2. To activate SSH access, run the command.
/usr/bin/toggle-ssh enable
3. To deactivate SSH access, run the command.
/usr/bin/toggle-ssh disable
You can configure the SSH settings of the VCF Operations orchestrator appliance by editing the
/etc/ssh/
file. By editing this file, you can remove any ciphers or MACs that you do not consider safe.
sshd_config
Managing Certificates in VCF Operations Orchestrator
Issued for a particular server and containing information about the server public key, the certificate allows you to sign all
elements created in VCF Operations orchestrator and guarantee authenticity. When the client receives an element from
your server, typically a package, the client verifies your identity and decides whether to trust your signature.
You can manage the VCF Operations orchestrator certificates by using the ssl_trust_manager tagged workflows.
Import a certificate to the VCF Operations orchestrator trust store

system (RDBMS), LDAP, Single Sign-On, and other servers. You can import the required TLS certificate from a URL or a
PEM-encoded file. Each time you want to use a TLS connection to a server instance, you must import the corresponding
certificate from the Trusted Certificates tab on the Certificates page and import the corresponding TLS certificate.
You can load the TLS certificate in VCF Operations orchestrator from a URL address or a PEM-encoded file.
