APIs for Service Provider Management
The following topics describe a set of REST commands for setting up a service provider, emphasizing tasks that might be
repeated frequently.
In the context of VCF Automation, a provider offers services to tenant organizations running virtual machines, developing
operations software and microservices, or performing other tasks in a shared computing environment.
The provider interface creates the required organizations and configures underlying infrastructure including regions, IP
spaces, gateways, storage, quotas, and users.
When the VCF Automation UI first starts, it displays an inventory of VCF resources, a series of getting-started steps, and
Overview menus for Infrastructure, Services, and Administration on the left.
Using REST calls, the provider administrator can automate tasks that might be repeated frequently, or tasks that are
easier to accomplish from the command line.
Broadcom 8837

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Advantages of Service Provider Accounts
For production environments with virtual machines and container-based microservices, a service account is
recommended over a normal user account.
VMware introduced service provider accounts in 2022 as an alternative to user accounts, to enable standalone access
for automation plug-ins and third-party applications. Some service provider accounts have system access only through an
API, with no access to a user interface. (VCF Automation provider accounts can access a user interface.)
Service provider accounts have several advantages. They cannot be impersonated by anyone else, assuming their
credentials are kept secret. Provider management accounts authenticate using bearer access tokens, which rotate after
each use. Bearer access tokens typically expire after one hour. They are derived from API refresh tokens, which have a
default lifespan of 90 days but can be revoked earlier and optionally rotated on each access.
When authenticating with a service provider account, applications normally cannot perform user management tasks,
create API refresh tokens, or manage other provider management accounts.
Provider management accounts are created by a system administrator with privileges View Service Accounts and Manage
Service Accounts. System administrators can create provider management accounts either from the VCF Automation user
interface, or with the API using a REST call (POST ... register).
Provider management accounts are like user accounts. If allowed, they can create assets such as virtual machines,
catalogs, templates, media, and automation sequences. Tasks that are initiated by provider accounts are properly
attributed. Provider accounts and user accounts can share assets with each other. System administrators can change
provider account attributes, revoke previously granted access, and delete the provider account – ideally after verifying that
any assets have been transferred as needed.
Before VCF Automation, provider accounts were used for tenant management and the tenant portal in VMware Cloud
Director, which is now discontinued.
Prerequisites for Service Provider Portal
While REST commands exist for attaching a vCenter and registering NSX Managers, these operations are typically
performed using VCF Installer or VCF Operations, by specifying the FQDN of connection endpoints.
You can verify vCenter and NSX Manager status using the VCF Automation UI:
1. Click Connections. The vCenter tab appears initially.
2. Name shows the vCenter endpoint, followed by other information such as License Status.
3. Click the tab for NSX Manager. When the tab appears, Name shows the NSX endpoint.
4. On the left, click Supervisors. The default Supervisor was created by vCenter registration.
The Supervisor displays its Region affiliation. Each NSX Manager (or load-balanced set of NSX Managers) is associated
with a Region, possibly based on geography.
Before it runs any VCF Automation tasks, the provider automation script must sign in to ensure proper authentication and
authorization. See Generating API Tokens for Service Provider Account.
In the following commands, vcfa.vcf.example.com represents the FQDN of the VCF Automation appliance. All REST
commands are assumed to be on a single line, or marked for continuation with backslash (Linux and MacOS shells) or
back-quote (PowerShell).
Generating API Tokens for Service Provider Account
VCF Automation uses OAuth to authenticate REST calls with a short-lived bearer access token. First you obtain an API
refresh token inside the VCF Automation UI, then you ask to exchange it for a bearer access token on the provider token
endpoint.
REST calls require OAuth style HTTP authentication in request headers. The bearer access token is a one-hour expiring
token that is used to authenticate all API calls, including calls made from a Provider management account. To acquire
a bearer access token, you first generate an API refresh token with the VCF Automation interface, then you generate a
bearer access token using the API.
token
Broadcom 8838

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
1. Go to the VCF Automation administrator interface at a URL such as vcfa9.example.com/provider. Enter the
organization name, such as system, and click Continue. If necessary, switch from LDAP to Local authentication.
2. Log in with the service administrator's username and password.
3. In the upper right corner, click ↓ (down arrow) > My Account.
4. On the My Account page, click API Tokens > NEW.
5. In the Create General Token box, type a name after the tool or function using the API refresh, and click CREATE.
Make sure to copy and paste the resulting API refresh token, which looks somewhat like this:
XhWKaESdLzr0Uo7Nd1JBn2AJZvAC0g07.
6. To obtain a bearer access token, use the grant type. The response header from this example Curl
refresh_token
command includes the long (VCLOUD) bearer access token.
curl --location 'https://<vcfa.url>/oauth/provider/token' \
--header 'Accept: application/*' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode 'grant_type=refresh_token' \
--data-urlencode 'refresh_token=<refreshToken>'
7. When you make API calls, provide the bearer access token until it expires. After expiration, you can obtain a new one
if needed.
{
"access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
"token_type": "Bearer"
}
Through the UI, API tokens are created without the rotation option. You can use the same API refresh token to get new
bearer access tokens until the API refresh token expires.
When token rotation is enabled and you make a grant-type call, the response body contains both a new
refresh_token
bearer access token and a new API refresh token. Save the new refresh token – the previous one is invalidated after the
call succeeds.
Create a Region
A Region is a set of one or more supervisors from one or more vCenters, all served by the same NSX Manager, or load
balancing NSX Managers. Regions are often geographically based, for example us-west and us-east. If two vCenters are
associated with different NSX instances, you cannot add their supervisors in the same region.
This REST command associates with an NSX Manager endpoint, including the default Supervisor.
us-west
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/regions
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"name":"us-west","nsxManager:"https://nsx-west.vcf.example.com",
"supervisors":["supervisor"], "storagePolicies":["vSAN Default Storage Policy"]}'
When creating a Region, you must specify its name as a string, the endpoint URL of an NSX Manager, the endpoint URLs
of one or more Supervisors, and one or more storage policies (for example, vSAN ESA Default Storage Policy).
By default, the Region contains a Zone specifying memory and CPU capacity. Zones are aggregated from all supervisors
in a Region. The Region inherits a collection of VM Classes, giving a choice of VM sizes and guaranteed or best-effort
performance. A Region starts with one Storage Class, but you can add more.
Networking Resources
A Provider does not require Internet connectivity, but in most cases connectivity is useful.
For wide area networking, the Provider needs an Edge Cluster, an IP address Space with CIDR blocks (IPv4 only), and a
Provider Gateway associated with the Region. Such a connected Organization is later set to networkingTenancyEnabled.
As a result of associating the Region with NSX, an Edge Cluster is auto-discovered. The Edge Cluster is a logical
grouping (often two) of VCF networking Edge transport nodes, which provide network services and north-south routing for
workloads. This command lists the nodes. Number of pages and page size are mandatory.
Broadcom 8839

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
curl -X GET https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/edgeClusters?page=1&pageSize=128
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
You should know the IP address range that tenant organizations can use for Internet connections. The IP Spaces
command sets that range for internal scope, and a security address for external reach.
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/ipSpaces
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"name:"us-west","externalScopeCidr:"0.0.0.0/0",
"internalScopeCidrBlocks":[{"id":"us-west","name":"us-west","cidr":"23.215.0.0/16"}]}'
Later, you can set quotas for an organization limiting the number of single IPs, the number of CIDRs, and maximum
subnet size. Alternatively, you can leave these unlimited.
After the region is given an IP address space, it must get a Provider Gateway. You specify a name for the gateway, a
region to which it applies, and an available Tier-0 gateway for physical backing.
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/providerGateways
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"name:"us-west","regionRef":{"name":"us-west","id":"us-west"},
"backingRef":{"id":"ContainerT0","name":"containerT0"}}'
Configure NSX Networking with the vSphere UI
As of VCF 9.1, administrators can manage and operate NSX networking though the vSphere user interface. Virtual public
clouds (VPCs) are visible in the vCenter network inventory. Administrators can connect them to each other, or to an
external network, using a transit gateway (TGW).
A virtual private cloud (VPC) is a configurable set of resources that are allocated in a cloud environment, providing
isolation between different organizations sharing a cluster. A VPC is somewhat like a subnet, but a software construct,
and a VPC can itself contain virtual subnets.
A transit gateway (TGW) connects one VPC to another, or to an external network such as the Internet. The external
connection can be centralized (CTGW) going through an edge router, or distributed (DTGW) being directly connected to
multiple VPCs.
The network span is a logical construct that defines which VPC and non-VPC clusters can connect to each other. By
default, all vCenter clusters belong to the default network span. A cluster can belong to multiple network spans. A
span can be made exclusive, so that a cluster set can be dedicated to a workload and not shared across the cloud
environment.
To configure NSX networking with the vSphere Client user interface:
1. In the network view (globe on upper left) click Datacenter > Virtual Private Clouds > ACTIONS > New Transit
Gateway. Enter a gateway name for the TGW. Accept the default span, or choose one that has been established.
Select either None for internal connections, Centralized for CTGW, or Distributed for DTGW. Click SAVE.
2. To establish a network span, click Virtual Private Clouds > Configure > Settings > Network Spans > ADD NETWORK
SPAN. Enter a name, choose Exclusive if desired, and select vSphere clusters in the span. Click SAVE.
3. To configure VPC connectivity policy, click a VPC on the far left, such as Default Transit Gateway. Then click Configure
> Routing and Forwarding > Connectivity Policies > ADD POLICY. Enter a Name, choose a policy Type (Community,
Isolated, Promiscuous), and select VPC Members that are connected to the TGW. Click SAVE.
4. Once you have configured NSX networking, you can troubleshoot VPC connectivity with live traffic analysis. Click
Virtual Private Clouds > Monitor > Troubleshooting > Traceflow.
5. To set up cluster vNetworking, go to the Cluster view (rectangles on upper left). Click Datacenter > Cluster >
Configure > [scroll] vNetworking > Network Configuration. If correctly configured, the cluster is prepared with the
default overlay transport zone for VPC readiness.
Public cloud adapters (AWS, Azure, GCP) are disabled by default in VCF 9.1.1.
Broadcom 8840

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Provisioning a Distributed Transit Gateway
As of VCFA 9.1, organizations that require high-performance distributed routing and VLAN-based connectivity can set up
a distributed transit gateway (DTGW). In VCFA 9.0, organizations had to be configured with a centralized transit gateway
(CTGW).
The service provider administrator can offer a distributed transit gateway (DTGW) as a networking option for organization
tenants. The service provider can assign multiple VLAN connections to the same tenant, ensuring that the connection
span overlaps with the zones that are assigned to the tenant's regional quota. Tenant organizations can then create
multiple DTGWs.
Figure 665: Network diagram with distributed transit gateway
The distributed VLAN connection defines information about the external VLAN attachment that is used by a tenant's
DTGWs, including the external VLAN ID and gateway address.
Regional network settings automatically provision either DTGW or CTGW based on the external connection and
networking infrastructure that the provider assigned to the tenant. If virtual network appliance clusters exist in the region,
a distributed VLAN connection can be selected as default for regional network settings. The provider can add other ones,
but the default distributed VLAN connection cannot be removed or replaced.

Avi Load Balancer Operations
Service providers can perform day 2 operations for load balancing using REST calls to the Avi load balancer (formerly
NSX Advanced load balancer)).
Avi load balancer performs local and global server load balancing, web application firewall security, and ingress services
for container-based environments. Avi load balancer was incorporated into NSX networking years ago, and now it is
incorporated into VMware Cloud Foundation.
When active, VCF Automation discovers Avi controllers and their associations with NSX Manager. VCF Automation also
discovers provider-managed service groups from the Avi controller. Assignment of a service group to a Region is then
determined by the load balancer's association with the NSX manager.
The load balancer service engine (SE) is an appliance that requires an IP address in each virtual service network. Service
engines are created within a group, which defines how SEs are sized, placed, and made available. A service engine group
is a collection of SEs that share properties such as network access and failover. Applications are guaranteed data plane
isolation when deployed in separate SE groups.
To query the discovered Avi controllers, the following GET call returns a paged list of Avi controllers:
curl --request GET \
--url https://<vcfa.ip>:8443/cloudapi/1.0.0/loadBalancer/controllers \
--header 'accept: application/json;version=40.0' \
--header 'authorization: Bearer <token>' \
--header 'content-type: application/json;version=40.0'
[response includes]
"id": "urn:vcloud:loadBalancerController:4887b3c0-7870-492f-8169-7758bc83c76f"
Broadcom 8843

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Once you have the URN of a particular load balancer, you can call again to obtain more information about
controllers
that controller.
GET /1.0.0/loadBalancer/controllers/{aviUrnID}
This call adds and registers an Avi load balancer, given a JSON definition.
POST /1.0.0/loadBalancer/controllers
This call updates an Avi load balancer, given a JSON definition.
PUT /1.0.0/loadBalancer/controllers/<aviUrnID>
This call deletes an Avi load balancer.
DELETE /1.0.0/loadBalancer/controllers/<aviUrnID>
As of VCF 9.1, the Service Engine Group name ( field) in SupervisorNamespace.spec can be updated with
segName
PATCH, after the namespace is created.
Create an Organization
Organization is the VCF Automation term for tenant organization. You can create an organization with the API, or with
Org
the VCF Automation UI. Under Provider Management, click Infrastructure > Organizations > Create Organization.
You can create an organization with the API, or with the VCF Automation UI – under Provider Management, click
Org
Infrastructure > Organizations > Create Organization.
To query organizations that already exist, run the following command. The number of pages and page size are mandatory.
curl -X GET https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/1.0.0/orgs?page=1&pageSize=128
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
To create an organization, specify an org name and its display name. Other optional data parameters include description
and ID, which is auto-filled if not specified.
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/1.0.0/orgs
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"displayName:"Test One","name:"test1"}'
As you would expect, there are also REST commands to get organization details, update details, and delete an
organization. Organization details include canManageOrgs, creationStatus, directlyManagedOrgCount, isClassicTenant,
isEnabled, isProviderConsumptionOrg, managedBy, and maskedEventTaskUsername.
The newly created organization needs a first-user (org admin) with the Organization Administrator role. The first-user is
always local, with appliance-specific password rather than identity provider account. For subsequent users, you call a
REST command that specifies both organization ID (test1) and role.
curl -X POST https://{api_host}/cloudapi/1.0.0/users
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"username":"admin","orgEntityRef":"test1","roleEntityRefs":"OrgAdmin"}'
The organization can be associated with a regional network by assigning a quota policy to it, while specifying the quota
name and the organization ID.
curl -X POST https://{api_host}/cloudapi/1.0.0/quotaPolicies
-H 'Authorization: <value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-d '{"name":"t1q","orgId":"test1","quotaPoolDefinitions":["resourceType":"quota","quota":0]}'
Create an Organization for VM Apps
The most convenient way to create a VM Apps organization is with the VCF Automation UI.
In the UI under Provider Management, click Infrastructure > Organizations > Create Organization > for VM Apps. For
details, see the VMware Cloud Foundation Provider Management guide.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

Infrastructure Compute Policies
Infrastructure policies define requirements and constraints for resource placement and configuration across the regions
and zones that are allocated to your organization. At least one compatible policy must be available to each namespace.
Service providers can list, create, and delete policies with the Policies operations. The REST call
GetAssignments
returns a paginated list of policy assignments, which can be filtered by policy IDs, target names, policy types, project ID,
or assignment phase. The following request body sets compute policy for higher performance virtual
CreatePolicy
machines.
{
"name": "High Performance VM Policy",
"description": "Compute policy for high performance virtual machines",
"vcComputePolicyName": "HighPerformanceVMPolicy",
"isMandatory": true,
"policyRules": [
{ "key": "cpu.cores", "operator": ">=", "values": ["4"] },
{ "key": "vm.class", "operator": "in", "values": ["guaranteed-4xlarge", "guaranteed-8xlarge"] }
]
}
When a role or object refers to a policy that is subsequently removed with , the policy does not go into
DeletePolicy
effect.
Broadcom 8847

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Content Library
The Content Library was introduced in vSphere 6. Content Libraries can contain ISO images, OVF files, VM templates,
vApps, scripts, applications, and other resources. Content Libraries do not store Kubernetes or Docker containers.
Organizations can share Content Libraries, helping reduce storage space and administrator overhead.
Automation is well suited to refreshing and sharing a pre-existing Content Library. To determine what Content Libraries are
accessible to an organization, run this command:
curl -X GET https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/contentLibraries?page=1&pageSize=128
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
To refresh the accessible copy of a distributed catalog, run this command, where cat.vcf.example.com is the URN of the
accessible catalog:
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/1.0.0/catalogs/cat.vcf.example.com/refresh
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
Consumers of provider services are able to access the refreshed Content Library with the REST command Get Catalog
Items. All-apps consumers can also publish, republish, and unpublish existing catalog items.
Administrators are not allowed to upload an image to a Content Library when its status is Partially Ready. Status in the UI
is obvious because the Upload button is grayed out, whereas the API returns only a message.
Forbidden
Blueprints
In addition to the content library, tenants can create their own blueprints. If you have a pre-existing organizational
blueprint, you can enable it for a tenant.
The VCF Automation user interface offers a drag-and-drop method to create blueprints.
Identity Management
VMware Cloud Foundation 9 has unified identity management that permits single sign-on over a wider range of assets
than previously, and offering a decent choice of identity providers.
To help run scheduled updates, the following command begins the LDAP sync task for the identity manager (IDM).
curl -X POST https://vcfa.vcf.example.com/cloudapi/1.0.0/ldap/sync
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
Suppose certain users in an organization prefer to use LDAP instead of SAML authentication. This can be set with the
argument of the Update User REST command, or the similar Update Group REST command. IDM
providerType
choices are: Local, LDAP, SAML, and OAuth.
You can choose from modern identity providers – Okta, Ping ID, Entra ID, ADFS, and SAML – or from directory-based
identity providers such as Active Directory or Open LDAP.
Custom Branding
For a unique look and feel, interface branding may be applied for all tenants of a Provider service.
The VCF Automation user interface (UI) has a Branding page where you can see resources such as logo, title, and
background. Settings can then be assigned as a custom theme to organization pages either shared or private. For details,
see topic "Changing the VCF Automation Portal Branding" in the VCF Provider Management guide.
An API for is also available. To see available themes for an organization, run this command:
brandingThemes
curl -X GET https://vcfa.example.com/cloudapi/vcf/brandingThemes?page=1&pageSize=128
-H 'Authorization: <value>'
To create a branding theme with the API requires two calls. The first call changes the portal branding name but the
branding object remains busy while waiting for the resource Zip to upload. After the second call completes, the branding
theme becomes usable again.

def upload_file_put(url, file_path, content_type='application/octet-stream'):
"""
Uploads a file using an HTTP PUT request.
Args:
url (str): The target URL for the PUT request.
file_path (str): The path to the file to upload.
content_type (str): The Content-Type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg').
"""
# Open the file in binary read mode
with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
# Set the headers, specifically the Content-Type
headers = {'Content-Type': content_type}
# Send the PUT request with the file data in the 'data' parameter
response = requests.put(url, verify=False, data=f, headers=headers)
# Check the response
if response.status_code in [200, 201, 204]:
print(f"File uploaded successfully! Status code: {response.status_code}")
print(response.text)
else:
print(f"File upload failed. Status code: {response.status_code}")
print(response.text)

upload_file_put(url, file_path , file_mime_type)

Metadata Management
As of VCF 9.1, administrators can manage metadata for both provider and tenant resources. You can locate resources by
searching for related metadata, with role-based access control permissions.
Also, legacy VMware Cloud Director (VCD) entities such as a virtual data center (VDC) can transfer metadata to VCF
Automation, as shown in the following table.
VCD to VCFA Resource Migration Method Comments
Organization to Organization Migrate by VcdOrgId Metadata writable by Provider but tenants lack access
to Organization.
Provider VDC to Region Migrate provider VDC Provider only.
Organization VDC to Region Migrate organization VDC Metadata writable by Provider but tenants lack access
Quota to Region Quota.
vApp to Namespace Transfer vApp into Namespace Provider metadata migrated to RegionQuota. Tenant
metadata migrated to Namespace.
VM to VM Service VM Transfer VM into VM Service Provider metadata migrated to RegionQuota. Tenant
metadata migrated to VM.
The metadata REST calls for the service provider follow the same structure as for defined entities. Reference
documentation is available in the API explorer online help.
Retrieve all metadata for the {id} designated entity:
GET https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata
Create a metadata entry in the {id} designated entity:
POST https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata
Replace all metadata entries of the organization with this desired state:
PUT https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata
Retrieve a single metadata entry in the {id} designated entity:
GET https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata/{metadataID}
Update the value of a single key-value metadata entry:
PUT https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata/{metadataID}
Remove a single metadata entry:
DELETE https://{vcfa}/1.0.0/orgs/{id}/metadata/{metadataID}
APIs for All Apps Organization Management
In VCF Automation, the Provider creates services for tenant organizations. These services allow them to run virtual
machines, develop operations software and microservices using containers, and perform other tasks in a shared
computing environment.
Kubernetes and REST commands help automate the creation of projects, supervisor namespaces, virtual machines,
content library items, and so forth. The following sections describe some actions that can be performed with the
kubectl
command line and REST calls.
Administrators of tenant organizations can assign regions for secure boundaries, namespace class for how to allocate
resources, and virtual private clouds (VPC) for network connections that protect regional isolation. Blueprints can be

created so DevOps programmers can easily create an appropriate self-service namespace without having to create to
complicated YAML descriptions.
VCF CLI and Kubernetes Setup
The command-line interface is required to set up the VCF Automation context, cluster plug-in, and cluster
vcf
authentication. You can find it for download on the overview page of the VCF Automation UI, or on the Broadcom support
site.
To download and install the command-line interface, follow this procedure:
vcf
1. Open a browser and navigate to your VCF Automation tenant portal:
https://<vcfa-url>/tenant/<org>/automation/#/overview
2. Log in with your tenant credentials.
3. On the Overview page, click Download VCF CLI. This navigates to the VCF Consumption CLI download page.
– Select your system in the OS dropdown menu: Linux, Windows, or Darwin (macOS).
– Select your CPU architecture in the Arch dropdown menu: AMD64 or ARM64.
– Click Download VCF CLI for <OS> (<Arch>) to download the binary.
– Optionally, click Checksum of VCF CLI to download and verify the SHA256 checksum.
4. Install the binary for your OS and architecture. On MacOS for example:
sudo install vcf-cli-darwin_arm64 /usr/local/bin/vcf
If plug-ins are required to support extended commands, see documentation for VCF Consumption about installing the
VCF CLI plug-in bundle.
If you do not already have the Kubernetes command ( ), it is available using third-party package managers, such
kubectl
as Homebrew for MacOS, Chocolatey for Windows, or RPM for Linux. For example, to download and install on
kubectl
MacOS, type this command:
% brew install kubectl-cli
As of VCF 9.1, the command is no longer available in third-party package managers.
vcf
Generating Tokens for Organization APIs
In the VCF Automation UI, log into the tenant organization account to generate an API refresh token. You can then use
the API refresh token to generate a bearer access token to authorize API calls.
Prerequisite: The VCF Automation service provider should have created a first user (administrator) account for your tenant
organization.
REST calls require OAuth style HTTP authentication in request headers. The bearer access token is a one-hour expiring
token that is used to authenticate all API calls, including calls made from a tenant Organization account. To acquire a
bearer access token, you first generate an API refresh token with the VCF Automation interface, then you generate a
bearer access token using the API.
token
1. Go to the VCF Automation UI at a URL such as vcfa9.example.com/automation. If necessary, enter your organization
name and click Continue. Possibly switch from LDAP to local authentication.
2. Log in with the organization administrator's username and password.
3. In the upper right corner, click ↓ (down arrow) > My Account.
4. On the My Account page, click API Tokens > NEW.
5. In the Create API Token box, type the client name of a tool or function that needs an API refresh token, and click
CREATE. For example, client name could be orgscripts.
Make sure to copy and paste the resulting API refresh token, which looks somewhat like this:
TTMrcIeHoqHuYBkhVXGLy1FurFYj9EDK.
6. To exchange the API refresh token for a bearer access token, use the grant type. You can then use
refresh_token
the bearer access token to authorize API calls. Here is an example Curl command for exchange:
curl --location 'https://<vcfa.url>/oauth/tenant/<vcfaTenant>/token' \
--header 'Accept: application/*' \
Broadcom 8852

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data-urlencode 'grant_type=refresh_token' \
--data-urlencode 'refresh_token=<refreshToken>'
You can use the same API refresh token to keep getting new bearer access tokens until the API refresh token expires.
Then you can obtain a new one from the VCF Automation UI, repeating the steps above.
Initial Setup of Kubernetes Cluster
Access to Kubernetes requires the token obtained above, a certificate for the VCF Automation appliance, and various
designations for namespace and project.
Follow these steps to set up the cluster:
1. Fetch the VCF Automation certificate and send it to a PEM file.
openssl s_client -connect fqdn:443 -showcerts </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -outform PEM > vcfa-
ca-cert.pem
2. Create the VCF Automation context.
vcf context create cci -e fqdn -t cci --api-token <VCF_CLI_API_TOKEN> --tenant-name tenant --ca-
certificate vcfa-ca-cert.pem
Provide Tenant Name: tenant
3. Use the VCF Automation context.
vcf context use cci:namespaceName:projectName
4. Install the VCF CLI cluster plugin.
vcf plugin install cluster
5. Register the Kubernetes cluster JWT authenticator.
vcf cluster register-vcfa-jwt-authenticator <CLUSTER_NAME>
6. Generate the Kubernetes cluster configuration.
vcf cluster kubeconfig get resource.cluster.object.metadata.name --export-file
resource.cluster.object.metadata.name-kubeconfig
Follow these steps to access the cluster:
1. Set environment variable VCF_CLI_VCFA_API_TOKEN with the API token to circumvent interactive mode (avoid
having to copy-paste it repeatedly).
export VCF_CLI_VCFA_API_TOKEN=FlH7L3SXiGAqYZTW784ZcTjQsnvhLlP4
2. Run the Kubernetes control command.
kubectl --kubeconfig resource.cluster.object.metadata.name get namespaces
Note:
Project name should comply with Kubernetes standards. Administrators can change a project name, while the
underlying project ID remains the same.

Before you create a namespace, a namespace class is required. You can either create a custom namespace class, or use

Here is an example that creates a namespace, in the case when the Supervisor Namespace Class Config (e2e-small)
contains a Zones array section:
apiVersion: infrastructure.cci.vmware.com/v1alpha2
kind: SupervisorNamespace
metadata:
generateName: test

Procedure to Create Namespace and Deploy VM
This topic walks you through steps for creating a namespace and deploying a VM with the VCF CLI and Kubernetes CLI,
rather than the UI.
Prerequisites: the and commands must be installed.
vcf kubectl
Get API Token. Create a CCI context using the VCFA endpoint, API token, and tenant name. The CLI initializes its plug-in
cache on first run, which takes a few seconds.
vcf context create vcfa_ctx -e $VCFA_ENDPOINT --api-token $VCFA_API_TOKEN \
--tenant-name $TENANT_NAME --ca-certificate {path_to_cert_file}
Get the Context. List all available contexts to confirm they were saved correctly:
vcf context list --wide
Set Context to Default. Switch to the top-level CCI context before running project or namespace operations:
vcf context use cci
The steps below use against the CCI API to create the project, namespace class, and namespace. All manifests
kubectl
follow the standard Kubernetes YAML structure. The CCI-specific API groups handle the underlying VCF orchestration.
Create a New Project. Set a project name and apply the Project manifest:
PROJECT_NAME=blr-project
cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: project.cci.vmware.com/v1alpha2
kind: Project

name: ${PROJECT_NAME}
spec:
description: This is a demo project

Create Role Bindings for the Project. Role bindings control which users can access a project and at what permission
level. The example below grants admin access to a user named :
fritz
cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: authorization.cci.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ProjectRoleBinding
metadata:
name: cci:user:fritz
namespace: ${PROJECT_NAME}
roleRef:
apiGroup: authorization.cci.vmware.com
kind: ProjectRole
name: admin
subjects:
- kind: User
name: fritz
EOF
The assigned user appears in the project with the correct role permissions.

Developer Self-Service with Virtual Machine Groups
As organization tenants, DevOps programmers can create a virtual machine group, which is useful to associate machines
that can be managed together. For example, a multi-machine application might have a management back end, a
dedicated database, and a web interface front end.
This functionality is similar to the traditional vApp in vSphere.
By creating a virtual machine group, you can perform operations on a set of VMs at an appropriate time. For instance, you
can define the order of power operations so that your user interface does not start prematurely. You can power off all VMs
to synchronize backup of the virtual machine group. You can power off an individual VM without affecting the power state
of other VMs in the group.
You may add existing or new VMs to a VM group. You may create a VM group at the same time as its constituent VMs.
VM groups may include other VM groups. The virtual machine group must have a namespace, it should contain at least
two virtual machines, and the VM Service must be available.
In the YAML definition, a VM group is defined as kind (type) . Affinity and anti-affinity rules
VirtualMachineGroup
are defined in kind . The snapshot details of a virtual machine group for backup, or other
VirtualMachineAffinity
purposes, is defined in kind .
VirtualMachineSnapshotSpec
A new VIM task (or ) was implemented in VCF 9.1 to synchronize the container native
syncVolume CnsSyncVolume
storage (CNS) volumes used for storage by the VM group. It gets called behind the scenes during desired state
operations.
Region VM Class Quotas
Regions are associated with quotas for resource use (CPU, memory, storage), with VM classes based on size, and with
storage classes based on capacity. CPU and memory have both a maximum limit and a minimum reserve allocation.
You can run Kubernetes commands to determine VM class summaries, VM class quotas, and storage class quotas for a
Region.
% kubectl get regions
NAME
paif-region
% kubectl get regionvirtualmachineclasssummaries --field-selector spec.regionName=paif-region
% kubectl get regionvirtualmachineclassquotas --field-selector spec.regionName=paif-region
% kubectl get regionstorageclassquotas --field-selector spec.regionName=paif-region
Networking for All Apps API
Software defined networking with VMware NSX offers a way to increase security and isolation of clients with VCF
Automation All Apps tenancy.
VCF Automation involves three contexts: the Console context of VCF, the Supervisor context created with vCenter, and
the Kubernetes context for Supervisor clusters. Network static routes and subnets are defined as "kinds" of custom
resource definitions (CRD) in the Supervisor context. These are the important ones.
•
networkinfos.crd.nsx.vmware.com
NetworkInfo is used to report the network information for a namespace.
•
subnets.crd.nsx.vmware.com
Subnet is the resource schema for the subnets API. SubnetPortSpec defines the desired state of SubnetPort.
SubnetPortStatus defines the observed state of SubnetPort.
•
subnetsets.crd.nsx.vmware.com
SubnetSet is the resource schema for the API. SubnetSetSpec defines the desired state of SubnetSet.
subnetsets
SubnetSetStatus defines the observed state of SubnetSet.
•
staticroutes.crd.nsx.vmware.com
Broadcom 8858

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
StaticRoute is the resource schema for the API. StaticRouteCondition defines the condition of
staticroutes
StaticRoute. StaticRouteSpec defines static routes configuration on the virtual private cloud. StaticRouteStatus defines
the observed state of StaticRoute.
Virtual private cloud information in VCF is obtained from the NetworkInfo custom resource, which is read-only. This
example shows a Kubernetes command retrieving network information so that subnets and static routes can later be
applied to this network.
# kubectl get networkinfo -o yaml
apiVersion: v1
items:
- apiVersion: crd.nsx.example.com/v1alpha1
kind: NetworkInfo
metadata:
creationTimestamp: "2024-11-04T08:11:13Z"
generation: 2
name: svc-tkg-domain-c10
namespace: svc-tkg-domain-c10
resourceVersion: "10279"
uid: 93ee3688-d6f1-477c-9914-18bdab05b2db
vpcs:
- defaultSNATIP: 192.168.0.4
name: vmware-system-supervisor-services-vpc_ef56697a-4a16-4090-8299-6cdb48caab05
privateIPs:
- 172.17.0.0/16
This example shows a Kubernetes command creating a private subnet that is named served by DHCP
subnet-sample
with 64 nodes.
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: crd.nsx.example.com/v1alpha1
kind: Subnet
metadata:
name: subnet-sample
spec:
accessMode: Private
ipv4SubnetSize: 64
subnetDHCPConfig:
mode: DHCPServer
EOF
Once subnets are created, they can be organized into a subnetSet.
This example shows a Kubernetes command creating a private subnet set named with size 64.
subnetset-sample
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: crd.nsx.example.com/v1alpha1
kind: SubnetSet
metadata:
name: subnetset-sample
spec:
accessMode: Private
ipv4SubnetSize: 64
EOF
This example shows a Kubernetes command creating a 192 private network with static routing through 10.10.0.1 or
10.10.02.
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: crd.nsx.example.com/v1alpha1
kind: StaticRoute
Broadcom 8859

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
metadata:
name: route1
spec:
network: 192.168.2.0/24
nextHops:
- ipAddress: 10.10.0.2
- ipAddress: 10.10.0.1
EOF

CSP APIs are deprecated. For a complete list of Identity API changes, log in as admin to the VCF Automation for VM

• The CMX API is no longer available because the CMX service has been removed.
Formerly CMX service was responsible for Kubernetes integration for deployment and management of Kubernetes
clusters and namespaces. In VCF Automation, these capabilities have been moved from VM Apps to All Apps

• The Migration Assessment and Migration Service API responsible for orchestrating migrations from vRealize
Automation 7.x to Aria Automation 8 has been removed.
VKS integration is available through CCI in the All Apps organization. See VCF Automation and APIs.

How developers use the VCF Automation APIs
To make API service calls, you use a browser application or an HTTP client application to send requests and review
responses. The following open-source applications are commonly used:
• cURL. https://curl.se/
• parser. https://jqlang.org/
jq
• Postman application. https://www.postman.com/
• API Client Bruno. https://www.usebruno.com/
To learn how to use the API, you start by getting an authentication token. Then you can perform steps outlined in the use
cases in this guide. The use cases include commands in request examples. To use the commands, ensure that the
curl
Broadcom 8861

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
command-line JSON processor is installed with . The parser ensures that responses are formatted for optimum
jq curl jq
readability. For information about installation, see https://jqlang.org/download/.
jq
Getting Your Authentication Token
In the REST API, VCF Automation requires an HTTP authentication token in the Authorization request header. Getting
your authentication token is a prerequisite for any use case.
You use an API bearer token to authenticate all API calls. The API bearer token is known as the access token in the
REST API service call examples. To acquire an authentication token, you must:
• Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal to find the name of the VM Apps organization.
• Log in to the VM Apps tenant to get the API token for the organization. The API token for the organization is the refresh
token that is used to get the access token.
• Use the API token to get an access token either by:
– Using an API client such as Postman to create an environment for the VM Apps tenant and get an access token
that expires in one hour by default.
– Registering an OAuth Client, then fetching the API token of the registered client to set an expiration on the access
token.
The default lifespan of an API token is 129600 minutes or 90 days. The default lifespan of an access token is one hour.
If you want to change the default lifespan of the API tokens you create, review the information in Changing the Lifetime
Setting of an API Token before obtaining your refresh token.
Get a Refresh Token for the VM Apps Tenant
To get an API token for the VCF Automation for VM Apps API, you must authenticate against the VM Apps tenant. To get
the name of the organization for the VM Apps tenant, you use the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal. Then
you log in to the VM Apps tenant to get the API token to be used as a refresh token.
Important:
As of VCF 9.0, the Identity Service API functionality has changed and is no longer used to obtain a refresh
token programmatically. To get an API token for the VM Apps organization, you use the VCF Automation UI to
authenticate against the VM Apps tenant.

https://appliance.domain.com

VM Apps organization. See What are the VCF Automation for VM Apps user roles.

•
org_name: {VM_app_tenant_name}

access_token: {API_token_for_VMApps_org}
POST /oauth/tenant/{org_name}/register
Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}
Content-Type: application/json
# Body
{"client_name":"my_client"}

Fetch the API Token of a Registered Client
Use the ID of the registered client to fetch the API bearer token. The new API token in the "refresh_token" field is the API
bearer token that is required to access tenant-specific APIs.
POST /oauth/tenant/org/token
Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
# Body
# take the client id from the previous response
grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer
&client_id=0c72befc-f9a1-4b4e-bffb-2fc08ddfbf3a
&assertion={{access_token}}

# Response
# The new API token will be contained in the refresh_token field
{
"access_token": "new_access_token",
"token_type": "Bearer",
"expires_in": 3600,
"refresh_token": "api_token"
}
Changing the Lifetime Setting of an API Token
The lifespan of an API token is defined by the API token lifetime setting when you create the token and cannot be
changed retroactively. As a best practice, you should change the API token lifetime before creating your token so that
you control its expiration period. Or if you created tokens before changing the API token lifetime, you must revoke the old
tokens before creating tokens again with the changed lifetime setting.
Change the Lifetime Setting
To change the lifespan of the API Token for your organization, log in to the Provider Management Portal, navigate to
General Settings > Timeouts and enter a value for the API token lifetime. Change this setting before getting your refresh
token. See Get a Refresh Token for the VM Apps Tenant.
The default lifespan of the API token is 129600 minutes or 90 days. To change the API token lifetime:
• Enter 0 for an unlimited lifespan.
• Enter an integer value for the lifetime number of minutes.
Broadcom 8868

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Revoke an Existing Token
To change the lifespan of an API token that was previously created, you must revoke it and create it again with the
changed lifetime setting. If you have multiple tokens, you revoke each token separately. You can revoke tokens either
programmatically using the API or from the UI by logging in to the VM Apps or All Apps tenant.
In the following example, the API request deletes the refresh token . If
0c72befc-f9a1-4b4e-bffb-2fc08ddfbf3a
you have multiple refresh tokens, insert each token in the command, and run the delete API request again.
DELETE /cloudapi/1.0.0/tokens/urn:vcloud:token:0c72befc-f9a1-4b4e-bffb-2fc08ddfbf3a

VCF Automation Tutorials
As a VCF Automation administrator, you can use these tutorials to learn how to perform tasks programmatically using the
IaaS APIs.
In addition to the steps in the tutorials, there is additional information in the guide. Links are provided to relevant topics.
Working with tags
As an Organization administrator with the Assembler admin service role, you can use the Tags endpoints to create,
manage, or delete tags in VCF Automation.
Note:
• Tag filters are case-insensitive.
• There is no way to query for unused tags using the IaaS API. However, you can submit a request to check for
tag usage of specific tag IDs.
Prerequisites for working with tags
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
Filtering for tags
You can filter for tags based on a key, value, or origin and the tag filters are case-insensitive.
The following example shows how to filter for a tag with in the key name.
location
curl -X GET \
"$url/iaas/api/tags?$filter=key%20eq%20'location’&apiVersion=$api_version" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" | jq "."
A sample response shows .
"key": "location"
{
"content": [
{
"key": "location",
"value": "MUM",
"id": "9aabbe23-d4bf-3d55-89f7-dc7e67317442"
}
],
"totalElements": 1,
"numberOfElements": 1
}
To filter for the origin of a tag, you specify or for the origin value. The following example
USER_DEFINED DISCOVERED
filters for tags with the origin.
DISCOVERED
curl -X GET \
"$url/iaas/api/tags?$filter=origins.item%20eq%20%27DISCOVERED%27&apiVersion=$api_version" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" | jq "."
Tag origins can also be both and as in the following cases:
USER_DEFINED DISCOVERED
• If a tag's origin is and another tag with the same case-sensitive key/value pair is assigned to an
USER_DEFINED
endpoint resource from which VCF Automation collects data, VCF Automation adds the origin.
DISCOVERED
• If a user assigns a tag with the origin to any VCF Automation resource such as a network profile, VCF
DISCOVERED
Automation also assigns the origin to the tag.
USER_DEFINED

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
Creating tags
You create a tag with a name and an optional value. The following example shows how to create a tag named
with the value that you could add to resources in your production environment.
environment prod
curl -X POST \
"$url/iaas/api/tags?apiVersion=$api_version"
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token"
-d '{
"key" : "environment",
"value" : "prod"
}' | jq "."
The response provides the tag ID.
{
"key": "environment",
"value": "prod",
"id": "ca0ed5ef-72b5-3d9f-bc6d-0707defff540"
}
Listing and deleting tags
To delete a tag, you specify the tag ID. To get the tag ID, you list all tags in your infrastructure.
curl -X GET \
"$url/iaas/api/tags?apiVersion=$api_version"
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token"
}' | jq "."
The response lists all the tag names, values, and IDs as in the following example.
{
"content": [
{
"key": "location",
"value": "MUM",
"id": "9aabbe23-d4bf-3d55-89f7-dc7e67317442"
}
{
"key": "Application",
"value": "testing",
"id": "57ead12-523a-3cd2-9447-06e757dcf382"
}
],
"totalElements": 2,
"numberOfElements": 2
}
Before deleting a tag, a best practice is to check the tag usage of the ID that you plan to delete. The following example
checks for usage of the tag with ID .
9aabbe23-d4bf-3d55-89f7-dc7e67317442
curl -X POST \
"$url/iaas/api/tags/tags-usage?apiVersion=$api_version" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"tagIds" : ["9aabbe23-d4bf-3d55-89f7-dc7e67317442"]
}' | jq "."

How do I retrieve provisioning request details
To validate placement scenarios before deploying a blueprint, you use the IaaS API to retrieve the request graph for a
simulated provisioning request.
Prerequisites for retrieving provisioning request details
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Assign an API version variable for the Blueprint API.
api_version_blueprint='2019-09-12'
Note:
The VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service and the VCF Automation Blueprint service have
different API version values. You set the API version value for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service
(IaaS) service when you satisfied the general prerequisites.
• Verify that you have the ID for the blueprint that you plan to deploy. You can also get the blueprint ID from the UI, by
opening the blueprint listed on Design > Templates and inspecting the ID at the end of the URL.
Broadcom 8879

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x

• Storage limit (GB)

• Provisioning priority

Deploying and Managing Resources
As a VCF Automation administrator, you can use the IaaS APIs to deploy and manage cloud resources.
Create and Deploy a Machine Resource
To create a new resource such as a VM, you can use the resources API to make a POST request with a project ID. The
deployment creates a new resource without using a blueprint.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Assign an API version variable for the Deployment API.
api_version_deployment='2020-08-25'
Note:
The VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service and the VCF Automation Deployment service
have different API version values. You set the API version value for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a
Service (IaaS) service when you satisfied the general prerequisites.
• Verify that you have the ID of the cloud account where you want to deploy the VM. See Adding Cloud Accounts.
• Verify that you know the cloud zone in your cloud account where you want the new VM to be deployed. See Create a
Cloud Zone .
• Verify that you have the ID for a project that includes the cloud zone in your cloud account. See Add a Cloud Zone to
Your Project.
• Verify that the flavor and image for the new VM exist in your cloud account.
Broadcom 8886

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
• Verify that you know the resource type for the AWS machine, GCP machine, vSphere machine, or Azure machine that
you plan to create. For a list of all resource types and request schema, see the link to the schema that's available from
VCF Automation Resource Schema Documentation.
This procedure shows how to provision a VM with a project and a cloud zone assigned to the project. The flavor and
image for the VM must exist in your cloud account.
1. Assign the cloud account ID variable.
your_cloud_account_id
cloud_account_id='< >'
2. Assign the project ID variable.
your_project_id
project_id='< >'
3. List all cloud zones.

zones?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
4. Examine the response for the zone where you want to place your VM.
You use the to filter for fabric flavor and fabric image. You use the cloud zone ID for VM
externalRegionId
placement.

your_external_region_id
external_region_id='< >'
6. Assign the cloud zone placement variable.
your_cloud_zone_id
placement_name='/iaas/api/zone/< >'
7. To list the fabric images in your cloud account and zone, specify the cloud account ID and external region ID in the
request.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
"$url/iaas/api/fabric-images/?apiVersion=$api_version&"\
'$filter'="(((externalRegionId eq '') or (externalRegionId eq '$external_region_id')) \
and ((cloudAccountId ne '*') or cloudAccountId eq '$cloud_account_id')))" | jq "."

9. Assign the fabric image variable.

11.Examine the response to select a fabric flavor.
12.Assign the fabric flavor variable.

Managing IP Addresses
As an VCF Automation administrator, you can reserve IP addresses so that VCF Automation does not use them for
deployment. If you no longer need them, you can release them.
Before reserving IP addresses, you must verify that available IP addresses exist within a network IP range.
Query for IP Addresses
When you use VCF Automation to create a deployment, VCF Automation allocates IP addresses to manage resources.
To identify the IP addresses that have been allocated, you query the network IP range. You can only reserve IP addresses
that have not been allocated.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
You create network IP ranges with a range of IP addresses. The following procedure shows how to determine the IP
addresses in a range that are available.
1. To get the ID of the network range that you want to use, list the internal network IP ranges in your deployment.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
network-ip-ranges?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
Examine the response to find the ID of the network IP range that you want to use.
2. Assign a variable for the network IP range ID.
your_network_ip_range_id
ip_range_id='< >'
3. To query IP ranges associated with a particular network and get information such as IP availability, you can use one of
the following commands:
• If you have the network IP range ID, use:
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/
api/network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
• If you have the network ID, use:
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/
your_network_id
api/networks/< >/network-ip-ranges?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
• If you have the networking fabric ID, use:
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/
your_fabric_network_id
api/fabric-networks/< >/network-ip-ranges?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
• If you have the networking fabric for vSphere ID, use:
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/
your_fabric_network_vsphere_id
api/fabric-networks-vsphere/< >/network-ip-ranges?apiVersion=$api_version"
| jq "."
Examine the response to see the number of allocated and available IP addresses. If the number of available IP
addresses is too low, check another network IP range until you find one with enough IP addresses to fit your needs.
Broadcom 8890

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
4. Use the network IP range ID to query the status of IP addresses within the range.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id/ip-addresses?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
Examine the result. All IP addresses appear with or
"ipAddressStatus": "ALLOCATED" "ipAddressStatus":
and are not available.
"RELEASED"

Allocate IP Addresses
As a cloud administrator, you can use the network IP range API to allocate the IP addresses that you want to reserve and
make them unavailable for deployment by VCF Automation.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have the ID of the network IP range that includes the IP addresses that you want to reserve. See Query
for IP Addresses.
• If you plan to specify the IP addresses from the network IP range, verify that you know the IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
See Query for IP Addresses.
• If you are a cloud administrator and you plan to specify the number of IP addresses from the network IP range, verify
that the number is less than or equal to the number of available IP addresses in the range.
To allocate IP addresses, you submit a request with either:
• A list of specific IP addresses.
• The number of IP addresses.
You can also provide an optional description.
Note:
The following restrictions apply to the request:
• No more than 100 IP addresses can be allocated in a single call.
• If listing specific IP addresses, the addresses must all be of the same type. Mixing IPv4 and IPv6 addresses is
not supported.
1. Assign the variable for the network IP range ID.
ip_range_id='<your_network_ip_range_id>'
Broadcom 8894

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Allocate the IP addresses by providing a list of addresses.
The following request example allocates two IP addresses.
• Specify either IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
• To release additional IP addresses, provide additional addresses in the payload.
curl --location --request POST \
$url/iaas/api/network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id/ip-addresses/allocate?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
your_optional_description
"description":"< >",
"ipAddresses":["<ipv_address_1>", "<ipv_address_2>"]
}'
Examine the response for the self link to track the request.
3. Optional: If you do not list IP addresses, provide the number of IP addresses to allocate.
curl --location --request POST \
$url/iaas/api/network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id/ip-addresses/allocate?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
your_optional_description
"description":"< >",
"numberOfIps": "<number_of_IPs>"
}'
Examine the response for the self link to track the request.
4. Assign the selfLink variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
5. Use the selfLink variable to track the request.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
The IPs are allocated when the response includes and provides a list of allocated
"status": "FINISHED"
resources.
Note:
If you specified the number of IP addresses to allocate, you query for the details of each resource in the response
to get the allocated IP address associated with the resource.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/
api/network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id/ip-addresses/<ip_address_id>?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
Allocate IP addresses within an IP range

• Two IPv6 IP addresses used in this example are:

Release IP Addresses
If you no longer need reserved IP addresses, you can release them so that VCF Automation can use them for
deployment.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have the ID of the network IP range that includes the IP addresses that you want to release. See Query
for IP Addresses.
• Verify that you know the IPv4 or IPv6 addresses that you want to release. The IP addresses must all be the same type.
Releasing a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in the same request is not supported. See Allocate IP Addresses.
This procedure shows how to request specific IP addresses to release.
1. Assign the variable for the network IP range ID.
ip_range_id='<your_network_ip_range_id>'
2. Release the IP addresses.
The following request releases two IP addresses.
• Specify either IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
• To release more IP addresses, provide the IP addresses in the payload.
Note:
No more than 100 IP addresses can be released in a single API call.
curl --location --request POST \
$url/iaas/api/network-ip-ranges/$ip_range_id/ip-addresses/release?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
"ipAddresses":["<ipv_address_1>", "<ipv_address_2>"]
}'
Examine the response for the self link to track the request.
3. Assign the self link variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
4. Use the selfLink variable to track the request.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
The IP addresses are released, when the response includes .
"status": "FINISHED"

-d '{
"ipAddresses":["196.192.2.19", "196.192.2.20"]
}'

Creating and Using a First Class Disk
Using a vSphere Storage Profile that supports First Class Disk (FCD) storage, you can create block device-based storage
that is independent of a VM.
First Class Disks offer many advantages. For example, you can attach an FCD to a VM and take multiple snapshots of the
disk over time. If you find that you do not need certain snapshots, you can delete them. You can also revert an FCD to an
earlier snapshot.
Note:
If you attach an FCD to a VM and then delete the VM, both the FCD and its snapshots are deleted. And if the
FCD is detached from a VM, you cannot delete the FCD without deleting its snapshots first.
Create a First Class Disk
To create a First Class Disk (FCD), you make a POST request using the block device specification. The request body
includes a project ID, disk capacity, persistence setting, and constraints from the vSphere Storage Profile for an FCD
creation.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have added a project and you have the project ID. See Create a Project to use in VCF Automation.
• Know the capacity of the disk and the persistence of the disk that you are creating.
• Verify that you have created a storage profile for an FCD and that you have the and the tags from the
defaultItem
response. See Create a vSphere Storage Profile for a First Class Disk.
1. Assign the project ID variable.
project_id='<your_project_id>'
Broadcom 8899

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Set the capacity and persistence for the disk.
capacity_in_gb=<integer>
persistence=<true|false>
3. Deploy the FCD.
• With set to true, all tags in the must match a storage profile, otherwise provisioning fails.
mandatory expression
• The is the key:value tag pair used to create the storage profile. See Create a vSphere Storage Profile
expression
for a First Class Disk.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"projectId": "'$project_id'",
"name": "FCD-example",
"capacityInGB": "'$capacity_in_gb'",
"persistent" : "'$persistent'",
"constraints": [
{
"mandatory": "true",
"expression": "type:fcd"
}
]
}' | jq "."
The response includes a selfLink value.
{
"progress": 0,
"status": "INPROGRESS",
"name": "Provisioning",
"id": "example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string",
"selfLink": "/iaas/api/request-tracker/example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string"
}
4. Assign the selfLink variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
5. Use the selfLink variable to track the progress of the FCD creation.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
In the list of resources, the response includes block devices with the block device ID in the path.
{
"progress": 100,
"message": "success",
"status": "FINISHED",
"resources": [
"/iaas/api/block-devices/example-blockdevice-alphanumeric-string"
],
...
}
6. Assign the block device ID variable.
block_device_id='example-blockdevice-alphanumeric-string'
Broadcom 8900

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
7. Optional: Retrieve the created block device object.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
block-devices/$block_device_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
8. Optional: Retrieve all the FCD block device types.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
block-devices?%24filter=customProperties.diskType%20eq%20firstClass&apiVersion=$api_version" | jq "."
9. Optional: Delete the FCD block device.
curl -X DELETE -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
block-devices/$block_device_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
Create a First Class Disk
With constraints from a vSphere Storage Profile for FCD storage, use the block device specification to deploy
a First Class Disk for a project ID with a two GB capacity and persistence set to false.
$ url='https://appliance.domain.com'
$ api_version=' 2021-07-15'
$ project_id='f5357a28-df59-47e0-b983-8a562910d0be'
$ capacity_in_gb=2
$ persistent=false
Deploy the FCD.

-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"projectId": "'$project_id'",
"name": "FCD-example",
"capacityInGB": "'$capacity_in_gb'",
"persistent" : "'$persistent'",
"constraints": [
{
"mandatory": "true",
"expression": "type:fcd"
}
]
}' | jq "."

Attach a First Class Disk
To attach a First Class Disk (FCD) to a VM, you make a POST request with the machine ID of the VM. The request body
includes the block device ID that you obtained from creating the FCD.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have created an FCD and you have a block device ID. See Create a First Class Disk.
• Verify that the hardware version of the machine to which you plan to attach the FCD is vmx-13 or later.
1. Assign the block device ID variable.
block_device_id='<your_block_device_id>'
2. Get a list of machines.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
machines?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
3. Examine the response to find the machine that you want to attach the FCD to.
4. Assign a machine ID.
machine_id='<your_machine_id>'
5. Attach the FCD to the machine.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/machines/$machine_id/disks?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"blockDeviceId": "'$block_device_id'"
}' | jq "."
The response includes a selfLink value.
{
"progress": 0,
"status": "INPROGRESS",
"name": "Provisioning",
"id": "example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string",
Broadcom 8902

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
"selfLink": "/iaas/api/request-tracker/example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string"
}
6. Assign the selfLink variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
7. Use the selfLink to track the progress of the FCD attachment.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
Once complete, the response includes a list of resources with a machine that has your machine ID in the path.
{
"progress": 100,
"message": "success",
"status": "FINISHED",
"resources": [
"/iaas/api/machines/your-machine-id"
],
...
}
8. Optional: Detach the FCD.
curl -X DELETE -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
machines/$machine_id/disks/$block_device_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."

iaas/api/machines?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
Examine the response. Identify the machine that you want to attach the FCD to.

Manage First Class Disk Snapshots
To create a snapshot of a First Class Disk (FCD), you make a POST request with the block device ID of the FCD. Using
the snapshot ID created, you can revert an FCD to a snapshot or delete a snapshot of an FCD.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have created an FCD and you have a block device ID. See Create a First Class Disk.
1. Assign the block device ID variable.
block_device_id='<your_block_device_id>'
Broadcom 8904

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
2. Create a snapshot of the FCD.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices/$block_device_id/operations/snapshots?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"description": "example description"
}' | jq "."
The response includes a selfLink value.
{
"progress": 0,
"status": "INPROGRESS",
"name": "Provisioning",
"id": "example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string",
"selfLink": "/iaas/api/request-tracker/example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string"
}
3. Assign the selfLink variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
4. Use the selfLink to track the progress of the FCD snapshot creation.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
The response indicates if the snapshot is successful.
{
"progress": 100,
"message": "success",
"status": "FINISHED",
"resources": [
"/iaas/api/block-devices/your-block-device-id"
],
...
}
5. Optional: To create additional FCD snapshots, repeat Step 2 to Step 4.
6. To get a snapshot ID, list all FCD snapshots.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
block-devices/$block_device_id/snapshots?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
If you created multiple snapshots, the response lists multiple snapshot IDs.
7. Examine the response and select a snapshot ID to assign as a variable.
snapshot_id=<your_snapshot_id_1>
8. Optional: You can list an individual snapshot.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
block-devices/$block_device_id/snapshots/$snapshot_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
9. Optional: You can revert an FCD to a snapshot.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices/$block_device_id/operations/revert?id=$snapshot_id\&apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '' | jq "."
Broadcom 8905

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
To track the progress of the reversion, perform Step 3 and Step 4.
10.Optional: You can delete a snapshot.
curl -X DELETE -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
block-devices/$block_device_id/snapshots/$snapshot_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."

Working with Azure Disk Snapshots
You can use the VCF Automation IaaS API to create or delete snapshots of Azure managed disks. The snapshot provides
a backup of your block device.
Note:
If you create a snapshot of an independent disk and then delete the disk, the snapshot is left behind. So before
deleting a disk from the Azure cloud account, check for snapshots. If snapshots exist, delete them first before
deleting the disk.
Create a Block Device
If you do not already have an Azure managed disk, create a block device to use for your snapshot. To create a block
device, you make a POST request using the block device specification. The request body includes a project ID, disk
capacity, persistence setting, and constraints from the Azure Storage Profile for a managed disk.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have added a project and you have the project ID. See Create a Project to use in VCF Automation.
• Know the capacity of the disk and the persistence of the disk that you are creating.
• Verify that you have created a storage profile for a managed disk and that you have the and the tags
defaultItem
from the response. See Create a Microsoft Azure Storage Profile for a Managed Disk.
1. Assign the project ID variable.
project_id='<your_project_id>'
2. Set the capacity and persistence for the disk.
capacity_in_gb=<integer>
Broadcom 8908

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
persistence=<true|false>
3. Deploy the block device.
• With set to false, tags in the are not required to match tags in an existing storage
mandatory expression
profile for the deployment to succeed. However if tags are provided, VCF Automation will try to match them when
deploying the block device.
• The is the key:value tag pair used to create the storage profile. See Create a vSphere Storage Profile
expression
for a First Class Disk.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"projectId": "'$project_id'",
"name": "block-device-example",
"capacityInGB": "'$capacity_in_gb'",
"persistent" : "'$persistent'",
"constraints": [
{
"mandatory": "false",
"expression": "type:managed"
}
]
}' | jq "."
The response includes a selfLink value.
{
"progress": 0,
"status": "INPROGRESS",
"name": "Provisioning",
"id": "example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string",
"selfLink": "/iaas/api/request-tracker/example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string"
}
4. Assign the selfLink variable.
selfLink_id='example-selfLink-alphanumeric-string'
5. Use the selfLink variable to track the progress of the block device creation.
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
request-tracker/$selfLink_id?apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
In the list of resources, the response includes block devices with the block device ID in the path.
{
"progress": 100,
"message": "success",
"status": "FINISHED",
"resources": [
"/iaas/api/block-devices/example-blockdevice-alphanumeric-string"
],
...
}
6. Optional: If you want to retrieve the ID of an existing block device, use an filter with the block device name in
OData
the request.
block_device_name='<your_block_device_name>'
Broadcom 8909

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.x
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" "$url/iaas/api/
block-devices?apiVersion=$api_version&"'$filter'"=name%20eq%20$block_device_name" | jq "."
7. Assign the block device ID variable.
block_device_id='example-blockdevice-alphanumeric-string'

Create and Manage Azure Disk Snapshots
To create a snapshot of a Azure managed disk, you make a POST request with the block device ID of the managed disk.
Using the snapshot ID created, you can list a snapshot or delete a snapshot of a managed disk.
• Verify that all general prerequisites and prerequisites for the VCF Automation Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) service
have been satisfied. See Prerequisites for API Use Case Examples.
• Verify that you have an Azure managed disk and a block device ID. See Create a Block Device.
1. Assign the block device ID variable.
block_device_id='<your_block_device_id>'
2. Create a snapshot of the managed disk.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices/$block_device_id/operations/snapshots?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"name": "example_name"
}' | jq "."
In addition to the required snapshot name, you can include optional snapshot properties that can be used
independently or combined as in the following example.
curl -X POST \
$url/iaas/api/block-devices/$block_device_id/operations/snapshots?apiVersion=$api_version \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" \
-d '{
"name": "example_name"
"snapshotProperties": {
"incremental": "true",
"resourceGroupName": "newRG",
"encryptionSetId" : "'"$encryption_key"'"
},
}' | jq "."
• To create a snapshot that only consists of changes since the last snapshot, set to true.
incremental
• To specify a target resource group for the snapshot, include the property. You can look up
resourceGroupName
existing resource group names in the Azure portal, or specify a name for a new resource group, If not specified,
VCF Automation creates the snapshot in the same resource group as the block device by default.
• To encrypt the snapshot with a customer-managed key, include the property.
encryptionSetId
To get the property for a particular region ID, use the following API request:
encryptionSetId
curl -X GET -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $access_token" $url/iaas/api/
fabric-azure-disk-encryption-sets?regionId=$region_id&apiVersion=$api_version | jq "."
Examine the response for the as in the following example.
id
